product_title: Life n Soul Bluetooth Headphones
review_headline: Not for those who want simplicity OR user support.
review_body:
Low-end piece of junk. The "User Guide" is printed in faint "microfont" and, hence, unreadable without a microscope. Had to go online to find something legible, and even then, things don't make sense. The "retractable string" (HUH?) referred to in the unreadable manual apparently is the adjustable-width HEADSET. Musta been written by someone not fully literate in English.

The infinitesimally-small "LED indicator lights" are barely visible and don't seem to match what the instructions say I'm SUPPOSED to see under various conditions. Moreover, the device only charges when it's plugged into one of my laptop USB ports. Therefore, it recharges only when my laptop is in use, or so I infer, because no "indicator light" shows when the laptop is hibernating. What happens when I want to charge the device overnight in order to use the device in the morning? (Too cheap to provide a separate charging unit, I suppose.)

I wanted to see if I could use one of my other wall-charging units (for my faithful old Sansa Sandisk MP3 music player, for example) to charge the unit without blowing it up, but guess what? User support is nonexistent. I don't want to create a damned "account" with Life n Soul (giving them my e-mail &etc. for their marketing purposes) in order to communicate with them. I want a "1-800" telephone number or direct e-mail to ask a simple question. No such luck.

After much prodding and guesswork, the device seems to work in conjunction with a Bluetooth transmitter that my wife and I occasionally plug in to use to listen to our family room and bedroom surround-sound TV systems whilst the other is asleep. But in the end, it's a pain-in-the-butt to set up and use. A dedicated set of plug-in wireless headphones would have been a damned sight easier to use, and probably wold have sounded better too.

Think simplicity and buy something else for casual use.

So after scouring through the internet and numerous amazon reviews, I came down to the extra bass Sony Headphones as my choice, until I saw these headphones. Maybe I got a defective piece, but with no real customer support, the brand and this product baffles me. I mean sure it would work perfectly and would be a steal for $80 without the noise isolation, but to have that creates more of a potential for things going wrong down the road and performance is definitely a concern. product_title: Pure i-20 30-Pin iPod/iPhone Speaker Dock
review_body: This is a remarkable product. The sound it puts out has bested some of the DACs in my collection which cost much more (I have this product hooked up to my iPod and run into a preamplifier to power amp to home tower speakers)  It’s simply a much more natural, unprocessed sound.  Don’t believe me? Fine, let the savings go to some other Joe.  Through my audiophile craze years, I have found that money and performance is hardly a direct relationship. This holds true not just for DACs but preamps, power amps, headphones and speakers.  I was previously running my music straight from my PC to a DAC and into my system.  The music sounds cleaner coming from the iPod/ipure combo. it might be owed to the iPod having much less noise and working parts than the computer motherboard.  The sound is however a little colder and more sterile than my aftermarket soundcard. I still prefer my computer DAC , but this is a nice alternative.  I do have one minor gripe, the range on the remote control is poor.

product_title: HDMI-DVI Cables
review_headline: Excellent Quality Cable - Very (too?) tight fit on a 2008 Macbook Pro
review_body: Just installed this cable on the stock output of an older (2008) MacBook Pro DVI output to the HDMI input on a 23 inch HP Monitor  There seems to be better image clarity than using an OEM Apple DVI > HDMI Adapter, which was starting to give me connection / stability issues.  I would have given it 5 stars, but for me the fit was way tighter than my old (cheaper) cable, to the point of being almost impossible to insert into the computer without some delicate forcefulness (oxymoron?).  I had to insert one end at a slight angle, and put some pressure to nudge the female jack on the computer into allowing me to insert the male cable. It was so tight, it seemed dicey, and I almost abandoned ship for fear of breaking something.  It appears that the thickness of the metal housing, and the fact the all of the columns and rows of pins are present and accounted for, but not needed, (compared to the old, cheaper cable, where two columns are left vacant) causes a much tighter fit. The gap tolerance around the female portion of the laptop is very tight.  If you are purchasing this as a cable you'll be removing and reinstalling frequently into a unit with tight tolerances (such as a laptop) I'd look elsewhere.  Otherwise I think you’ll risk possibly damaging the pins, or the computer's DVI jack, every time it's installed. The HDMI side did fit perfectly, and snugly, into the monitor.  I supposed the fact that it all fits so tightly could be construed as a good thing if you're looking for the best possible connection and stability.  Otherwise, really love the cable thickness, overall design/aesthetics, materials, and build quality. Overall, a winning cable with the fitment caveats mentioned.

product_title: Sony PHA-3 Headphone Amp for High-Resolution Audio , Black
review_headline: Superior sound excellence, flexibility, and feature usability. Pairs perfectly with high impedance ER4S IEM and Sennheiser HD800
review_body:
Superior sound excellence, flexibility, and feature usability. Pairs perfectly with high impedance ER-4S IEM and Sennheiser HD-800.

If you are already happy with the apparent volume and sound quality of your current listening experience, a headphone amp (with built-in DAC) such as the PHA-3 is not likely to benefit you. The basic reason for purchasing a headphone amplifier is that most portable devices have trouble driving expensive headphones. There are two effects: the volume is too low, and the sound quality suffers. For most listeners, the soundstage isn't as clear and the music seems "dull." When a headphone amplifier is used, the headphones seem to "wake up" and volume is normal.

However, if you have high quality headphones or in-ear-monitors and value portability (convenient use on travel, or at home around the house), then you should strongly consider the PHA3. There are many fine headphone amplifiers with an integrated DAC, but the PHA-3 is surely one of the best and likely unmatched in flexibility and user features.

I am extremely happy with the PHA-3 and highly recommend it for single ended use with the Etymotic ER-4S In-Ear-Monitor (IEM) and I especially recommend pairing it in the balanced mode with the Sennheiser HD-800 headphones - which sound absolutely fantastic on this amp in this configuration. I still use the ER-4S IEM for exercise, airplane flights, and business travel, but I mostly live with the HD-800's connected in balanced mode with the PHA-3 when I'm relaxing to music or writing.

PHA-3 Critical Feature Summary:
1) Single ended output for regular devices (100mW per channel into 32 Ohms) and balanced (differential) output (320 mW/per channel into 32 Ohms) for specially cabled headphones. I found that for 100 Ohm devices the single ended power sounds wonderful and has plenty of volume.

For the HD-800 (300-600 Ohms), single ended power sounded very good and volume was fine for my tastes, but after listening to the higher power balanced output, I strongly prefer it, even if I do not listen at anywhere near maximum volume which I would find painful.

Balanced output provides a theoretical 4x (6dB) - Sony shows a 3.2x or 5 dB - increase in the power per channel versus single ended and provides more than enough volume and slew rate performance for high impedance (300-600 Ohm) headphones like the HD800. The HD-800 sound absolutely fantastic when driven in this configuration. This critical feature takes quite a bit of explanation. The key point is that you need the right cable to access this feature. More detail on balanced operation is provided at the end of this review.

2) Internal battery - sufficient but you will often operate with the device plugged in and charging while you are listening
-- this is direct experience. At the power levels I use while listening, the unit does in fact charge while I am listening.
-- note: in balanced mode, (which I recommend), the power available is 4x the power from single ended mode, so sizing an internal battery for extended playback is difficult, no matter how "efficient" the amplifier is... Given that limitation, Sony's compromise between battery size and convenience seems perfect to me. (Note: balanced mode doubles the voltage going to the headphones. Doubling voltage, yields a 4x power increase at "high volumes" over single-ended mode, or in this case battery consumption, because power scales with the square of the voltage).

3) small size (about twice as thick as a smart phone and similar in length and width) in a very convenient and attractive form factor. The design of the unit provides audio cord connection protection because the cord jacks are "recessed" behind the volume knob and a projecting metal flange. Supplied silicone bands are perfect for attaching phone devices or mp3 players.

4) accepts digital inputs from all Apple devices, Windows, Android, Linux, etc.
-- Sony licensed from Apple the iOS direct digital interface, so the PHA-3 supports any combination of digital inputs from all Apple iOS devices and the older iPods. I frequently use the PHA-3 with a 160GB iPod Classic when I'm outside.
-- Sony uses a standard micro-USB connector for all Android phones, tablets, Windows, Linux, MacOS, laptops, desktops, and music servers.

5) very high standard of digital data format flexibility and analog sound reproduction ... read detailed reviews online if these items are a critical factor in selecting the PHA-3 over other competitors. The sound quality and dynamic range (no-hiss) is stunningly beautiful on the HD-800 and the PHA-3 easily accepts all the most common music data formats. In my case I use Apple products (MacBook Pro Retina, iPod, iPhone, Apple TV Music Server) to manage my music files and all of the various file formats, encoding bit rates, and sample rates in my collection have worked perfectly for me. If you are a DSD or FLAC music format enthusiast, Sony provides a music player that runs on your laptop for DSD files, and there are many laptop players for FLAC. Also, although it takes extra disk space, you can use a lossless converter to store a FLAC file into an iTunes/Apple format.

6) Sony has a feature called DSEE HX to improve the sound quality of many digital formats... other reviewers have found this helpful but I find it hard to discern the benefit, so this is not a critical feature to me.

7) Cables: The PHA-3 needs at least two micro USB plug to USB Type A cables (one is provided): one for charging while listening, and the other for connecting to your laptop for digital output. I found that a 6 inch 30 pin Apple iPod to USB Type A "synch" cable (not just charging cable) was perfect to connect an iPod Classic. Over time, I purchased another 2 micro USB to USB Type A cables to leave around some fixed charging locations. 4 foot flat cables pack nicely into a carry bag.

Additional Notes:
AN1) headphone impedance:
The higher the impedance of a headphone, the harder it is to drive (it takes more voltage to send the same amount of current). Typical earbuds are about 16 Ohms, high quality in-ear-monitors are often 30 to 100 Ohms, and many high quality headphones are 100 to 600 Ohms. There are interesting engineering reasons for this, but basically it is easier to make a better motor with a higher impedance. There is a very nice discussion of this on http://nwavguy.blogspot.com/2011/02/headphone-impedance-explained.html

AN2) Drive strength and Pairing:
The PHA-3 was designed to pair with the Sony MDR-Z7 headphones. Those headphones are 70 Ohms at 1 KHz (mid range). The PHA-3 pairs extremely well with the Etymotic ER-4S (100 Ohm) and also pairs extremely well with the Sennheiser HD-800 (300-600 Ohms) using a balanced cable. It also pairs acceptably well with the HD-800 (lower maximum volume) using single-ended operation, but most audiophiles will want to purchase or make a balanced cable. It is always hard to know, but to my ears, the balanced cable and differential drive of the PHA-3 make the Sennheiser HD-800 really sing. I purchased my balanced cable from customcans.co.uk. I normally listen to the PHA-3 from a MacBook Pro or an iPod Classic so customcans "default" 1.5 meter size was perfect for me.

AN3) More discussion on balanced outputs and balanced cables for the PHA-3
A balanced cable using the Sennheiser connectors and the 3.5mm TRS jacks the PHA-3 requires is easy to make or purchase. I bought a very high quality one from customcans.co.uk. They will also make a balanced cable for any headphone to your specifications. It takes about 1 week for them to ship your order. Note: although I personally do not use a Pono player, the Pono player also uses two 3.5mm TRS jacks for balanced (or differential) output, so any cable that will connect your headphones to a Pono player will also connect to the PHA-3.

Balanced output is an incredibly nice feature for this price range and yet Sony has also managed to make this conveniently portable. If you are using the Sony MDR-Z7 headphones, Sony provides the appropriate cable with their headphones and there is nothing else to do. If you want to pair the PHA-3 with the Sennheiser HD-800's or another high quality headphone it will take only a little extra effort, but it is well worth it. This feature really influenced me when I made the decision to purchase the PHA-3.

All high quality headphones can be cabled for balanced (or differential) output, however the reason it takes a little extra effort - or an additional cable purchase - is because balanced drive is not a headphone industry standard and companies offer various solutions. For example, Sony (and apparently Pono) chose standard 3.5mm jack cables to keep their product small over the large XLR cables in common use in microphones, audio mixing equipment, and some keyboards (my old Roland RD700 has XLR). A good discussion of balanced cabling and some of the advantages is located at http://www.headphone.com/pages/balanced-headphones-guide. If your headphones use connectors on each driver (like the Sennheiser HD800, HD600, HD650, all Audeze, and HiFiMAN planar-magnetic headphones) it is very simple to make or have made a balanced cable (see the end of this review for basic advice).

AN4) Why is balanced operation important?
To achieve the same sound quality, a differential amplifier system is substantially easier and less costly for a manufacturer to design and package into a tiny, 5 volt or less (4.7V Lithium-ion) USB style battery subsystem, than one single amplifier. The net result is that the PHA-3 has 4 amplifiers ( 2 for each channel), each running on 5 volts or less, instead of 2 "bigger" amplifiers running at 10 volts or less.

In balanced mode, the signals swing differentially, effectively doubling the voltage delivered to the headphone. Hence, from the same USB style battery subsystem, the power available to drive the headphones is nominally 4x (6dB) the power from single ended mode. This results in more than sufficient volume and slew rate for high impedance headphones like the HD-800. In differential mode, two amplifiers are used instead of one to "split the effort" to drive each of the headphone channels (left or right). The positive and negative leads from each (left or right channel) headphone driver coil are independently driven by a separate amplifier. Using two amplifiers per channel doubles the amount of voltage that can be delivered to the headphone driver using the same battery power system. Doubling voltage, yields a 4x power increase because power scales with the square of the voltage.

AN5) Note on modifying your own headphones:
If your headphones are hard wired, you can modify the cable directly and solder it to your own connectors (like 3.5mm sockets) to make it simple to build a replacement cables for single ended or balanced use. In a 3.5mm TRS jack, the Tip is the "+" terminal, the Ring is the "-" terminal, and the Sleeve is connected to the electrical shield (often a "braid") around the two wires inside the cable. Headset coils or transducers are symmetric devices, so labeling one side "+" and the other "-" is only important to keep the phases correct. If you make your own cable or connector, it's easy to use an ohm-meter to find out which wire is "+" and which wire is "-." If the wires are color coded, it's very simple. If not, then as you cut each wire, carefully label each end (4 labels) with a piece of tape. Now use the ohm meter to find which wires are connected to the Sleeve of the TRS jack (probably 1/4 inch) on the cable you just cut. These wires are the "-" leads and need to be ultimately connected to a 3.5mm "Ring" when you are done with your cable. product_title: Mount-It! Premium Aluminum and Glass Speaker Stands for Home Theater Satellite Speakers and for Bookshelf Speakers
review_body:
Hifiplus reported that Andrew Jones used a pair of generic speaker stands at T.H.E. Show Newport ELAC showroom, "For the demonstration, the speakers were shown on generic albeit sand-filled stands priced at $50/pair ...". Elsewhere, digitalaudioreview wrote "The entire system on show had reportedly arrived at the Hotel Irvine in two suitcases, including speaker stands sourced from Amazon.com for US$49." If I'm not mistaken, these stands are the same stands pictured in the photo.

I would have never thought tempered glass was a good medium for speaker vibrations even if the post was filled with sand. Apparently I need to re-examine my preconceptions about speaker stand materials and the value of these stands. To me, certainly any of the neg reviews here now come off as quibbling, nit-picky and thankless if rock star speaker designer Andrew Jones was able to leverage these in conjunction with the forthcoming ELAC Debut B5 to produce sound that left listeners in gob smacking awe...

product_title: BT-1000 On-Ear Bluetooth Headphones Wireless + Wired Technology Headset Stereo Built-in Mic for Hands Free Calling
review_body:
OPENING THE BOX
It looks like I received one of the last pairs of these headphones Amazon had available because they are now listed as out of stock. Other places still list them so I'll submit my review for them anyway.

The first thing I did after opening the box was throw the instruction sheet away. This set of earphones does not do anything the way the users guide says it should, so I figured out how to pair them on my own. Your earphones may still need the instructions sheet, but just in case your set of earphones doesn't react the way the user guide says it should, then the following might work for you too. It's so ridiculously simple!

PAIRING INSTRUCTIONS
No PIN code will be necessary, it pairs immediately without it.

When the battery is charging, the RED LED flashes slowly. Once fully charged, the RED LED remains on continually until the charger cable is disconnected from the earphones.

There is an ON/OFF switch. The switch can probably be in either position while charging but I prefer leaving it in the OFF position when charging.

When you want to pair to a device, push the switch to the ON position and after a few seconds the RED LED will flash once and then turn to BLUE, continuing to flash slowly.

1. If not paired to your device already then start a search for Bluetooth devices and then push the >/II button on the earphones and the LED will start flashing quickly, alternating between RED & BLUE. This will allow the earphones to pair with your device. Once connected, the LED changes to a slow BLUE flash.

2. If already paired to a device turned on and sitting in standby, turning the switch ON will show the RED LED flash once and then turn to BLUE, continuing to flash slowly. There is nothing else to do because the earphones are now connected to the device and the earphones are ready to use.

To disconnect Bluetooth simply push the switch on the earphones from the ON position to the OFF position. The LED lights up RED for a few seconds and goes out and there is a beep.

All done!

SWITCHES
All the switches are on one speaker. They include the >/II and PHONE switches, an ON/OFF switch, and a VOLUME switch that also doubles as a PREVIOUS/NEXT selection switch.

>/II
This button starts a quick alternating RED & BLUE flash when pairing the Bluetooth headset to a phone, tablet, etc.

PHONE (picture)
This answers the phone and turns on the mic for a two way conversation. End the conversation with another press of this button.

VOLUME SWITCH
1. Raises and lowers volume, and loud can be really LOUD when the phones volume is also all the way up. I generally set the phones volume to 50% and keep the headset volume all the way to max.

2. When listening to a play list, the volume switch can also be used to select the previous or the next track on the list. That works also with some streamed stations on the Internet.

BATTERY CHARGER
A charged battery lasts a very long time. Many hours, so I don't have to charge it every day. The charge cable fits into the bottom of the speaker that doesn't have all the switches. Charging goes rather quickly when using the provided charger unit.

MIC
The speaker with all the switches also has a mic hole on the bottom. This mic tested just fine but may not work as well in a noisy area. I'm not one who likes using headphones that don't have a boom mic, and I would rather just switch to speakerphone on the rare occasion when a call comes in rather than try to have a conversation with this type of mic.

OTHER STUFF & FINAL
For the very low price these headphones sold for, they have an exceptionally good quality sound that plays stereo and has lots of bass and lots of clarity. They are out of place for wearing while doing high exertion exercises, but for lounging, walking, or working around the yard, they will have you dancing. The cross band will extend and also fits snugly without being tight. The speakers are comfortable on the ears, and I can wear these for hours and they never become bothersome. They are like wearing your stereo speakers on your head, but without all the bulk and weight. I love 'em.r working around the yard, they will have you dancing. product_title: Belkin Conserve Insight Energy Use Monitor, F7C005Q
review_body:
I have been using a Kill-A-Watt to measure the electricity usage of the devices at my home. It is a simple device to show voltage, watts and the electricity consumption over certain period of time. However, to calculate the actual electricity charge, I had to use a calculator or a spreadsheet to get the money figure. And here comes the Belkin Conserve Insight Energy Use Monitor (F7C005). The best thing for this device was that it had US average electricity cost stored in it, so you get a monthly cost or a yearly cost displayed on the display right away. You also can setup your own cost per KWh for more accurate cost estimation. This device just worked right out of the box and the buttons on the units were very intuitive to use. As I learned from other reviewers, I did not connect this to a device/appliance that consumes a lot of power to prevent any problem (fire) from happening. It also could show power plant carbon dioxide emission based on the electricity usage and this would help some people who care a lot for environment.

The tracking feature helped to have average measure of the electricity consumption over the time and I really liked to see dollar figures directly on the device without needing any calculation. This device served its own purpose very well and I have not had any complaints so far. Another cute and informative accessory from Belkin. Great product.

product_title: Belkin Pivot Surge Protector with 6ft Cord and Telephone Protection
review_headline: Finally can use all six outlets
review_body:
The problem with six-outlet electrical plugs is that you rarely can use all six. Somehow, the electrical engineering wizards who design these things place the outlets way too close to each other, which basically defeats the purpose of using any appliances or electronics devices that have odd shaped adapters.

In the case of the Belkin Pivot Wall Surge Protector, the design is spot on with six outlets; each outlet can be independently swiveled. Other swivel outlets only let you swivel a bank of three at a time, which basically presents the same problem as a standard flat six-plug wall mount--you can't fit all your devices because the plugs are too close together.

This Belkin provided enough space to use every one of the outlets for my electronic gadgets. The most offending shaped one wasn't even an AC adapter, but a very large, round nightlight that hogged up two spaces. But with the Belkin Pivot, I just simply swiveled the outlet 90 degrees, and voila, problem solved.

review_body: I live in Nicaragua and bought this for our earthquake emergency kit. It has been kept in a plastic storage bin with other emergency supplies for a few years now. product_title: KEF Hi-Fi In-Ear Headphones - Aluminum/Black
review_headline: Immersive, large-scale sound -- but only under the right conditions
review_body: What makes these a little bit special is the sheer ease with which they reach down into the deep bass and up into the highest highs--as they should when using two dynamic drivers on each side. Besides the bass being very powerful, it is also well-textured and clear, and the highs have a sense of delicate detail too--you usually don't get both at the same time. But the problem lies in between. The midrange isn't very clean and in fact can be a little harsh. If you check the graphs for these at InnerFidelity.com, you'll see that there's a strong peak at 2 kHz. On my Fiio X7, I EQ the 2 kHz range down about 3-4 decibels, and also EQ the rest of the treble range down just a decibel or two. Because of the excellent extension in both the highs and the lows, these provide grand, large-scale sound, but they're not the best for voices or acoustic instruments since the midrange isn't good enough. Still, for some kinds of electronic or orchestral music they can be impressive. Also they need quite a bit of power to run well. I use the "high" gain setting on my X7, and even sometimes use the AM2 amp module, which has more power.  KEF's unusual system of fitting these into your ears works fine for me, even though it is slightly awkward and a tiny bit uncomfortable over long periods. But from the other reviews here and elsewhere on the Web, it obviously doesn't work for everyone. And over long listening sessions, I become aware that these really aren't the cleanest sounding IEMS, and their sound can become a little fatiguing as a result.

product_title: Ikea 502.432.99 Lack TV Stand, White, 35-3/8 Inches
review_headline: A nice inexpensive stand IF you know what you’re getting
review_body:
If you understand how Ikea products are make and how they’re used, you will “get” this TV stand. The number one reason Ikea products exist is functionality, followed by design. They are rarely what would be called “fine furniture” … they are made to serve a practical purpose and be sold at a reasonable price. Like most Ikea furniture this is made of recycled wood fibers with a hard, semi-gloss painted coating. It is available in white or black.

This product is intended to be used with a small, lightweight LED TV. Unfortunately the product description isn’t as clear as it could be in that regard but from my first-hand experience I would say it is intended for TV’s that are 40” or smaller. It is a lowboy stand that works best for people who prefer their TV to have a low profile, so in other words it is not your best choice for watching TV in bed or laying back in a reclining chair.

Like virtually every Ikea product, this is RTA (ready to assemble) furniture. It ships knocked down and comes with a pictures-only assembly manual. If you have experience assembling Ikea furniture you will probably consider this one of the simplest thing you’re assembled … 10 minutes maximum. Tools required are a Phillips screwdriver and a hammer. There are only 3 major parts … the top, the middle shelf, and four legs. You hand-screw each of the four legs into the top with double-ended screws that are included. Then you attach the shelf using 90° angle brackets. That’s it.

But, as is so often true with Ikea furniture, the pictorial diagrams are very vague, so here are a few helpful hints:

1. The illustrations show you screwing the double-ended studs in with your fingers. DON’T. You will end up with sore, bloody fingers if you do. To attach the top, insert the screw and twist slightly until it just stays in place without falling out. Then match the other end with the predrilled hole in the leg and with BOTH hands screw the two pieces together. When you meet resistance, only continue tightening until the leg is squarely aligned with the top … do NOT force it any further.

2. The middle shelf is very non-Ikea-like in that the holes in the legs are not predrilled. Instead they include a little plastic template that you must use to punch screw holes at the appropriate height. The following is very important: following the pictorial drawings align where the hole should be punched and tap one of the longer screws GENTLY with a hammer, just enough to make a small indentation where the screw should go. Do NOT hit the screw so hard that it completely punctures the leg or you won’t be able to screw it down tightly.

3. While Ikea’s instructions only show the middle shelf being able to be installed at the fixed location that they’ve determined, you can actually attach the shelf slightly higher or lower. If you look at my attached photos you will see that I bought two of these stands … one is used to held DVD’s and the other is used in another room to hold a speaker. The location that Ikea wants you to mount the shelf is not tall enough for anything except the old CD jewel cases. So here’s what you do. Measure where you want the shelf and hold one of the angle brackets under it. Mark where the hole should be with a pencil. Then align the plastic guide with that hole and make another pencil mark on the guide at the bottom of the leg. Then use the guide to punch the holes, aligning the pencil mark you made on it with the bottom of each leg.

4. The instructions are also unclear about how to screw the middle shelf in. They show inverting the table upside-down and mounting the shelf. That is very difficult to do because you have to hold the shelf with one hand, align the brackets with your other hand and screw the screw in with your third hand. So here’s the trick I discovered … after you punch the holes lay the table on its LONG end. When you insert the middle shelf it will be supported by the two legs on the bottom and gravity will assure the shelf is mounted to the leg with no gaps (see photo).

5. The stand is capable of supporting most 40” or smaller TV’s, however the middle shelf is NOT capable of holding much weight. The DVD cases as shown in my photo or a lightweight speaker is about all you should put on that shelf.

Finally, Ikea does not give you an option about screwing the entire stand to the wall behind it. Their lawyers want to make that very clear to you. I suggest you follow their instructions if you will be using this as a TV stand. My photos show that neither of my two stands are being used as a TV stand and I chose not to use the wall bracket for that reason.

Bottom line: This is an attractive stand to look at and is functional. It is not fine furniture and is not very big or substantial. Read the measurements, as the actual stand may be much smaller than you expect. But for what it is, I am 100% satisfied with both of them for the way I am using them. product_title: Onkyo TX-NR809 THX Certified 7.2-Channel Network A/V Receiver (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Fine product...excellent customer service and support.
review_body:
After 4 years of owning and using the TX-NR809 on a daily basis (purchased here on Amazon), I can honestly say I was very pleased with its performance. Then, just a few weeks ago, my Zone 1 speakers quit functioning out of the blue (despite that Zones 2 and 3 were working fine). I called Onkyo technical support to troubleshoot and found out that the problem was a bad circuit board in my receiver. My first thought was "Dude, you're screwed."

Fortunately for me, Onkyo has excellent customer service. They gave me the option of a decent trade-in value on a certified new Onkyo or I could send it back to their factory in Illinois and have it repaired and shipped back--free of charge. I chose the latter option and, while I had to suffer without my Onkyo for about 2.5 weeks, I received my better-than-new TX-NR809 and it's working great!

It's rare to see a company stand behind their electronics after this long of a period of use. I want to take this opportunity to sincerely commend Onkyo on a fine product and EXCELLENT customer service. THANK YOU Onkyo!!!

product_title: Insignia Wireless Over-the-Ear Headphone
review_headline: Great... if you can get them cheap enough!
review_body:
I just bought an Insignia Wireless headset (I am writing using my wife's account since we share it) so I didn't disturb my wife when she goes to bed (I am more of a night owl). We bought an Apple TV for the bedroom and I needed a way to listen to my shows (my stories my wife calls them) without waking her. I read a lot of reviews and some of them had some concerns. Let me tell you my experience after 2-3 days of use.

Difficult to Pair Headphones with Base: I read a lot of reviews saying it was difficult to pair. Yes. It is difficult to pair the first time, but after a few minutes it connected. Since then it connects automatically. I did unplug it, waited 3-5 minutes and plugged the base back in. I also made sure the headphones were fully charged. Since then I have turned the pairing off at the back of the base and turned the headphones off and it still pairs no problem now so just be patient.

*Make sure you have to cables on the base and the back of the TV hooked up correctly this did give me some problems.

2.4ghz Signal Problems: I read where a reviewer or two said they had interference due to the 2.4ghz signal on the headphones and the wi-fi signal. Maybe it is a problem if the base and wi-fi router are close together. Mine are not close together (in a different room), so I don't know if that is a problem, but it is right next to my Apple TV (that is why I bought the headphones in the first place) without a problem.

Hours of Use: I haven't run into an issue yet. I have run it an hour or two longer than a movie with no problem (so at least 4 hours).

Volume Control: This was very big to me. I found out that most HDTVs do not allow you to increase or decrease the volume on Audio Out. You need something (like a toner) to turn it up and down. The the headset has volume controls on the side that work great! I can turn it all the way down next to nothing or up to a pretty high level (not loud enough to hurt), but just below. The headphones do have poor base quality. I haven't watched anything with a ton of base, but enough to notice. This is not a big deal for me... it would be nice, but I knew I would need to spend a lot more money and get Bose Headphones or something like it.

I agree. I wouldn't pay $90 for them so I bought a used pair online for $20 with prime shipping. The came in "Like New" condition... totaly worth $20-$40 dollars!

review_body: Bluetooth connectivity is one of the best and most useful ways to enjoy sound and media in the car, home, and on the go through headphones.  This effective Bluetooth 2 in 1 receiver/transmitter by Avantek helps extend Bluetooth pairing capabilities with items that originally could not be used wirelessly. A regular set of earbuds or headphones can become wireless receivers when plugged into the port on the receiver. This is great for me while doing chores because I would rather tuck this little device in my pocket and pair it with my Samsung Note 2, rather than carry my phone around.  I use it the most in my car, however.  When used in conjunction with my FM Transmitter (also by Avantek,) I can listen to my mp3 player, tablet, or phone via my car stereo.  This is excellent, since my car lacks an auxilliary port.  I plug this into my FM Transmitter to give it Bluetooth connectivity and pair my phone or other device. I like this better than the former way of using my device in a car (through a tape deck "transmitter.)  My device remains free of wires and is easily accessable while I tuck my little Avantek Bluetooth transmitter out of the way.  I love it and highly recommend it. product_title: JBL Charge 2 Portable Bluetooth Speaker
review_body:
This little speaker does the job. I got it after listening to it in the Sprint store, where they sell it for $150. But I opted for the Amazon deal...who doesn't...of $115.

Straight out the box it had a little charge, but I charged it to full capacity before trying it out. Getting a full charge on the thick cable it comes with takes no time at all. Power it up, connect to bluetooth and you're off to listening. It connects up to 3 phones at a time, which is great. 1 person can be playing their music, and if one of the other 2 people want to change it up they can just press play on their phones and it'll take over the beats. Sometimes this can be a bit frustrating if you're listening to your jam...but it's all good...just steal the play back!

The sound is aweome. It has bass that'll make you take a double look to see if it's really coming out of this little speaker. I'm a fiend about clear tones, and the Charge 2 has it. You can hear sounds in songs you never realized were even in the song.

The battery lasts a decent amount of time. We like to listen to music so it's on constantly and it goes all over the house and yard with us. I'd say we get about 6-7 hours on a charge. It says 4 on the box, so maybe I just got a good one, but i lasts much longer than 4 hours.

Compared to other speakers, this is a great deal for the price. We considered the UE Boom, but I liked the crispness of the sound on the JBL Charge 2 better.

Now I will tell you, we tried this out in the boat and were a little disappointed. The sounds just didn't carry in the wind. The loudness in the house and on the carport are amazing. Don't get this if you want a sound stage in the boat. Otherwise it's awesome.

product_title: Bose QuietComfort 20 Headphones
review_body: When it comes to Bose, people either love or hate their products. Bose markets itself as a premium manufacturer of audio equipment that are sold at a premium price. Whether Bose products are truly "premium" is definitely up for debate. Most audiophiles tend to find the sound on Bose products to be artificial, misbalanced with too much focus on the bass and midrange, and have a poor acoustic response. Personally, I've never been the biggest fan of Bose products (speakers, home theater, and car audio), because you can get much better products for much less money. With that aside, when it comes to noise canceling technology, Bose is second to none. The Bose QC20 earphones take the technology from Bose's over the ear headphones and shrinks it down to work as in-ear earphones, and the results are amazing. Just flip the switch to power them on and ambient noise is instantly brought down to a reasonable level.  So do they work as well as the over the ear noise cancelling headphones? The answer is: almost. Over the ear noise cancelling headphones create a seal over the entire ear that helps to isolate ambient noise, and when powered on, active noise cancelation helps to cancel out further ambient noise. Earphones work much differently, as they rely on active electronic noise cancelation to reduce ambient noise and do not benefit from noise isolation because they do not seal and cup the ear. Since the QC20s rely more on electronic noise cancelation, you can hear an audible hissing sound when they are powered on (much like tape hiss) which simulates silence. After about 5 minutes or so, your ears will adjust, and you will likely not notice the hissing, but it is something to be aware of. Also, keep in mind that there is a little box at the end of the headphones near the audio jack. It's about the size of a pack of gum and weighs practically nothing, but it is a necessary evil due to the fact that it contains the lithium ion battery and noise cancelation circuitry. Itis somewhat annoying to have a dangling box from every device that you plug the QC20s into. I do wish that Bose had incorporated Bluetooth into that dangling box to give users the option to dangle or not dangle the box from their devices, but sadly, it was not incorporated this time around.  In reading most of the reviews on Amazon, there are a couple of major concerns that needs to be touched on that I have not read in any of the other reviews:  First of all, Bose recently released a redesign of the QC20 earphones, with an improved case, new design patterns (black with a blue stripe, or white with a blue stripe), and some very minor improvements. This would mean that the old QC20s (black with a grey stripe) will be out of warranty in less than a year. If you purchase Bose products from Amazon or any other retailer that is not a Bose store, BE AWARE that the one year manufacturer's warranty starts from the DATE OF MANUFACTURE and NOT from the date of purchase. This means, if you purchase the QC20s from Amazon, and they have been sitting on Amazon's shelves for 8 months, the manufacturer's warranty is only good for another 4 months after you receive them. Beyond this, the customer then has to pay $150 out of pocket for any replacements or repairs. Secondly, Bose decided to go with a non-replaceable lithium ion battery in the QC20 earphones. The problem with lithium ion batteries is that they will eventually degrade and will hold less of a charge the more that you use them. After several years of continuous use (or about 500 charges) they will eventually not be able to hold much of a charge and will only function when they are plugged in to a power source. It is important to understand that Bose QC20s will eventually need to be replaced when the battery gives out. My first pair of QC20s lasted about 7 months before they went from holding a 16 hour charge to a 6 hour charge. They were out of warranty in the 7 months that I had them (purchased in January, but the warranty expired in March, and Bose wouldn't replace or exchange them because I purchased them from a third party retailer and not from the Bose store; luckily, after much explanation, the manager at the Bose store understood my predicament and was kind enough to eventually replace them [your mileage may vary]).  Overall, the sound quality on the QC20 is above average when they are powered on. In terms of sound, the QC20s have that "Bose" tendency of sounding a bit overly enhanced, with the primary emphasis being placed on the midrange. Some may like this; some may not, but it's a very typical Bose sound. The noise cancelation is astounding when audio is playing through the earphones, as you can focus on what you are listening to, rather than what is going on around you. As someone who has a noise sensitivity, the Bose QC20s are an absolute godsend. They are much less cumbersome than over the ear headphones and do an amazing job at bringing ambient noise down to a reasonable level. So, is it worth the price? I definitely think so. The QC20s may be expensive, but they are currently the best noise canceling earphones on the market today. Aside from a few quirks, I highly recommend them, as I never leave home without them.

product_title: 1byone Window Antenna 35 Miles Super Thin HDTV Antenna with 20ft Coaxial Cable, Extreme Soft Design and Lightweight
review_headline: 1byone Window Antenna 35 Miles Super Thin HDTV Antenna
review_body:
Hooked this up to my HDTV 6 days ago. It picked up all of the local stations upon startup, no problem.

This morning I was watching a local channel and suddenly got the "Weak or No Signal" on screen message. At first I thought the station was having problems since all other stations were coming in just fine. So, I gave it about 30 minutes and went back to the station I was watching. Still the same message. I ran "Auto Program" and the antenna picked up all but this local Fox station. The transmitter is less than 20 miles away and there are no weather conditions that may be causing interference.

My next Troubleshooting effort was to check my other TV, which has a Mohu Leaf 50 antenna. No problems found, the local Fox station was coming in just fine.

Why the antenna just suddenly dropped reception for this station is beyond me. It worked fine for 6 days then all of a sudden the station is beyond reach for this antenna which is baffling considering other stations it is picking up are further away. Since the other TV is picking up the station I'm pretty sure Fox didn't just suddenly pick up their transmitter and move it another 20 miles or Godzilla is on the attack.

I'm off to buy another Mohu Leaf 50.

product_title: QFX R-10 AM/FM/SW 1-7 Radio (Black)
review_headline: It's not junk.  It's not great.  It is what it is.... I'm able to get a few channels.  It works like a $9 shortwave radio
review_body:
This is a hard product to review because a "good" shortwave radio costs 10x more than this one, and an excellent shortwave radio costs much more than that. Frankly I didn't know a sub-ten-dollar shortwave radio was even possible until I found this on Amazon. Because it had no reviews I didn't know what to think so I bought it.

As expected for an under-ten-dollar-radio, it feels cheap and flimsy, but I was prepared to give it a chance. The antenna does not telescope very far so it always remains very short. The sound quality from the speaker is also what you expect in this price range.

When I first tried every shortwave band, I couldn't bring in a single station. There were a few spots while tuning that the static changed but nothing that resembled a real signal. But to be honest I was somewhat expecting that because we have a metal roof. I went outside and tried again, and this time I was able to pull in a station or two on each shortwave band- though the majority of them weren't good enough quality to discern what the station was or even what language it was in.

I plan on tinkering with this more again later during different times of the day and night. If you are looking for a quality shortwave radio, this is not the product for you. If you are only willing to spend 8 or 9 dollars (and free shipping at that) then this product is better than having no shortwave radio at all.

review_body: I was stoked to see that V-Moda finally brought back the 3-button speak easy cable.  I have been using the "red" brand cable because volume control is not something I can go without.  When the cable arrived, I was happy to see that it felt much softer than the 1-button included with my M-100's.  Within a few days of use however, it started to stiffen up.  I have never really been a fan of the Kevlar wrapping.    The play/pause button on the remote is situated lower than the volume buttons.  I can only assume this is to prevent it from getting pressed accidentally, but it makes it difficult to press, especially when you are trying to double or triple tap to skip tracks.  Having large fingers doesn't help either.  This isn't a make or break, and I am starting to get used to it the more I use it.    My biggest gripe is the price.  It costs $30 which twice as much as the single button speak easy cable.  This seems excessive for 2 extra buttons.  If you are like me, and want a matching cable for your premium M-100's, then I think this is a must have.  If not, you can find other brand cable that cost 1/3 the price of this cable.    Overall, the cable is what you'd expect from a company like V-Moda. This cable is built to last, and the one year warranty is a definite plus.

product_title: PonoMusic Pono Portable Music Player
review_body:
Beautiful sound, far better than the price would suggest. Not sure how they do it, but I remember reading in the run up to Pono's release how some felt the sound felt almost liquid in its beauty. Hearing it now, I can well understand what they mean. Everything I throw at it sounds wonderful. It sounded great through regular earpieces. But what really made it bloom was getting balanced cables for my Sennheiser HD600's and listening through that. That gave the impression of a few more db in volume, but more than that. The music had more of a sense of 3 dimensions, if I'm not stretching too much. The soundstage was more defined and the separation of instruments improved. I bought the 24/192 of Every Picture Tells a Story last week from the Pono store and it was the best I've ever heard that, and I've heard a few remastered or otherwise enhanced versions. I could run through album after album and say the same. And of course it doesn't require that tracks be purchased from Pono - ALL my HD tracks up to 2x DSD sound great on it. As others have noted, navigation can be tricky because of the small size and sensitivity of the screen. I wish that were different, but one can't have everything, and it's not so bad that I would subtract a star.

So the device is an easy 5 stars. The store I'd have to put at 4 stars at most, though. The selection of 24 bit tracks is not what I expected. The way it was described before rollout made it seem ALL tracks would be HD. And there are many 24 bit albums. But the majority are 16 bit. Then Neil Young talked about that and made the point that he felt 16 bit WAS HD in comparison to MP3, and that MP3 was the real problem, not CD quality (16 bit). I probably heard what I wanted to hear to an extent, and I have found 24 bit albums in the Pono store that I don't see elsewhere, like Springsteen's The Rising. And 16 bit albums do indeed sound good through the Pono and I have bought a few 16 bit when no 24 bit version was available. And for that matter, MP3 sounds better through Pono.

And the Pono community and customer support are great.

All in all, an easy recommendation for those to whom sound quality matters.

product_title: Bluedio Bluetooth Wireless Headphone (Bluedio U)
review_headline: The R+ Legend vs The UFO: Side by side comparison of features
review_body:
In this review, I will compare the R+ and the UFO as thoroughly as I can. This will help you decide whether you should get the UFO or upgrade to the UFO if you already have a pair of the R+ Legend. Please read till the end and post questions if you have any. Thank you for your patience.

At the outset I would like to say that the UFO is not meant to be the successor of the R+ Legend in the same class. If you were expecting these to have the same set of features with some add-on features, you will be disappointed. The R+ Legend and the UFO are both leaders in their own class. While the R+ is designed to have a heavy bass effect, the UFO is designed to sound more balanced and simulate a virtual 7.1 surround sound experience. If you bought these with the intention of listening to thumping bass like in the R+, you will be disappointed. The UFO enables the listener to experience a full range of sound frequencies and turning on the 3D Effect enhances the bass and treble while suppressing the mids. Both modes sound good but you will not hear thumping bass, unless you play around with the equalizer settings on your music player.

The UFO is designed to look more classy. The color scheme is more conservative, with a matte finish. The R+ is shiny and in-your-face with its color scheme. I personally like and own the black and red UFO, silver R+ Legend and the white R+ (Photos attached). The padding cushions in the UFO are more comfortable than the ones int he R+ and feel like they heat up a lot less after prolonged usage, which make them suitable for watching movies/TV shows. The buttons in the UFO are elite looking and concealed under large panels. The buttons in the R+ are circular and slightly protrude out of the side. This may not look the best but makes it easier to feel around and figure out what button you're pressing. The UFO frame is made of metal alloy. This makes it slightly heavier but also more durable. The R+ is susceptible to damage because of its flimsy plastic build. The UFO promises to be able to withstand a few more accidental drops and step ons. The UFO comes with a fancy looking hard carry-case with a handle, so you can safely store/transport your headset.

The UFO has bluetooth 4.1 technology with is more energy efficient than the R+, which uses bluetooth 4.0 technology. The response of the buttons of the UFO is almost instantaneous while there is a slight delay after the button press in the R+. The R+ has the NFC enabled quick pairing feature, which is absent in the UFO. The R+ also has a microSD card slot to play mp3 tracks stored on a microSD card of upto 32 GB capacity. I particularly like this feature because I can spare my phone when the battery is low. The UFO does not have a microSD card slot. The R+ comes with a built in equalizer that has 3 settings (Pop, Rock and Flat I'm guessing) that can be toggled by pressing the volume up and down buttons at the same time. The UFO has 2 settings: the normal mode and the 3D effect mode. The interface of the UFO is similar to the Bluedio BS-2/3 where you need to press and hold the center button to turn on the device, and hold it even longer for pairing. The R+ only has to be pressed once and it automatically turns on and pairs with the last device or goes into pairing mode. This could be a little annoying because it can accidentally be turned on when something bumps against the button. The LED color scheme for turning ON/OFF and pairing of the UFO and the R+ is different. The brightness and behavior of the lights are also different. I particularly like that the LED lights of the UFO are a lot dimmer and blink with a greater delay than those of the R+, so that it is not too disturbing when in a dark room.

Both the R+ and the UFO last ridiculously long after they have been fully charged. I have paired them both to PC, Mac and android phones and they work beautifully. The 3.5mm wired connection works well but personally I prefer the convenience of the bluetooth especially because the battery is consumed even when the headset is connected via a wire. The UFO performs slightly better when making and answering phone calls, but the difference is negligible.

product_title: CABTE High speed HDMI 1.4 HDMI cable 10ft 1080p with mesh&filters supports 3D&blue ray
review_headline: 4K at 30hz and truly excellent customer service
review_body:
I was initially impressed with this product. The threading around the cables, though plastic - not cloth, is very sturdy, and the cables seemed well built. However, when I ran the cable from my PC to my 4K TV, I could only get 1080p resolution and only at 30hz at that. I went through a lengthy trouble shooting process, ruling out bad ports on my TV, verifying my PC was up to pushing 4K, so on and so on. Ultimately I narrowed down the problem to the cable. I bought another cable from another company and I was able to get the full 4K resolution at 30hz. So I wrote a review detailing my experience and rating the cable poorly.

I was then contacted by Alexandra from SPN Performance customer support. She listened to my story with genuine sympathy and offered to send me a replacement cable and an HDMI booster (because some people do have trouble with cables of this length on certain devices and a booster can help in those rare cases) sent via 2 Day Shipping. She offered all of this free of charge, with no obligations on my part to even modify my review, though she did say she would appreciate it if I felt like doing so.

I received the items in a couple days, and the replacement cable worked just fine. I didn't even need to use the booster to get the full 4K resolution at 30hz. I did try the booster on the original cable, and it still did not work, so that cable was definitely a dud.

In my experience customer service of this quality had all but vanished in today's corporate world, and for the friendliness and willingness to do whatever they could to solve the problem alone I would be tempted to give this item 5 stars. But this isn't a review of customer service, it is a review of the item. And this item, once I got a working model, performs excellently, is sturdy and attractive, and deserves those 5 stars alone. The great customer service just provides the added bonus of rejuvenating a smidgen of my faith in humanity.

review_body:
AS the title says... ZERO stars. It wouldn't even turn on. It has a color screen alright.... a BLACK one.
Do I seem a bit "frosted"? Well, I ordered this for my 4 1/2 yr. old granddaughter who waited excitedly for it to arrive. Imagine the let down when it wouldn't even work!
Moreover, the instructions are a joke and the part which shows the function of the buttons is for a different model!
I noticed last night when I was looking at the reviews again to see if I had missed something on turning it on that, as another reviewer said, ALL the positive reviews were from people who had received this gratis for reviewing it.
I would not impugn the integrity of the the reviewers but I'd bet that each and every one which was sent to them was checked and double checked for proper function before being sent out.
Oh, btw, in case someone is inclined to consider the problem "operator error": I read the instructions twice, I connected the player to both a computer and a AC charger. I tried every combination I could think of for key presses.
When connected to the computer it did function as a USB Flash drive and I could see the sample pictures, video, and songs on it. But I could NEVER get it to show anything on its screen
Perhaps I got the one in a thousand that was bad............. or, more likely one of the 100 out of a thousand that is bad.

product_title: iSound Crescent Rechargeable Portable Bluetooth and Speakerphone for iPod
review_headline: Be forewarned - this product can break VERY easily!
review_body: Please reconsider purchasing this product, as it can fail very quickly. I purchased one recently and noticed that it quit charging within a couple of uses. After trying in vain to research the issue, I opened the case up and noticed the mini-USB charger port had become separated from the small transistor board inside. Apparently, the small leads from this mini-USB port that are soldered to the board are very small and can become broken from normal use, and way the port sits on the board allows for it to wiggle and the contact points are then broken easily. Due to the size and placement of the mini-USB port, you are unable to re-solder the leads and the product becomes completely unusable. I hope the company recognizes this and remedies the fault.

product_title: RCA Air Flat Indoor HDTV Antenna
review_body:
Light weight and flimsy with 6ft cord, I had little hope for this thing out of the box.

This antenna worked much better than expected. I live in a far northwest suburb from Chicago, 45ish miles line of site. I have vynal siding so little interference. I first hooked up this antenna in an East facing outside wall on the second floor and received 42 channels. Yes, many of them garbage programing but even channels from Gary Indiana are coming in with no problems.

I moved it to my attic and hung it on a nail as high as I could and connected it to a 20 ft coax with a female to female, no splitter. I'm now receiving 72 digital channels. Many of the new are coming from Rockford about 60 miles away... With no amplifier.

This antenna is rated for 25 miles per the box and 40 miles per the rca website. If you have aluminum siding or brick you will have much less luck, but that's because of the realities of radio frequencies.

product_title: Inteset 4-in-1, INT422 Universal Backlit IR Learning Remote for use with Apple TV, Xbox One, Roku, Media Center, Nvidia Shield and many other A/V Devices
review_headline: This remote is freakin' awesome...and how to create "Skip Forward" button
review_body: It's simple for basic users, yet advanced enough that you can program macros, or copy buttons (even from a different remote) or rearrange button functionality.  I love how you can lock buttons such as volume or on/off.  For example, if you're using a Roku, normally you'd have to hit the "TV" button to switch your device mode then "On/off."  With this remote, you can program the power button to shut your TV off no matter which device mode you are in.  I bought this remote specifically for the Roku 3, because I didn't want to use two remotes (one for Roku, one for TV).  It's awesome that it's preprogrammed for the Roku, but you can easily program any other device.  You can look up any device it supports online and you can also find the owner's manual here: http://shop.inteset.com/ir_remote_control_device_setup_code_search  Also, their support team is great.  I emailed them from the website above, and they got back to me really quickly.  I didn't know where the "instant replay" (rewind 8 seconds) button was for the Roku.  They emailed me and said the instant replay is programmed to the button labeled "last".  I preferred to set "instant replay" to the smaller rewind arrow button, so I'll I did was use the "copy" function (see manual) and now both buttons have the "instant replay" capability.  I don't have experience with $200 remote controls, but why would anyone want something that expensive?  I feel like this remote can do everything you'll ever need and more!  HOW TO CREATE "SKIP FORWARD BY 10 SECONDS" BUTTON  (opposite of instant replay) for Roku or other DVR devices.   1) Press Roku device ("D" Button).   2) Hold setup for a few seconds until it blinks 3) Enter 995 (to program macros) 4) Press “Skip forward” button (I used the small fast forward button).  This is the button you’re setting the macro to.  The next buttons are the series of commands assigned to your macro. 5) Press the big“fast forward” button. 6) Press “diamond” button once (assuming it’s assigned to nothing.  If you skip this step, it fast forwards only a few seconds.  Adding a “do nothing” button, is like creating a pause in the macro.  The more times you press the diamond button, the longer it will fast forward.  I found you only need to press it once to get roughly a 10 second skip forward).   7) Press “Play” button. 8) Press and hold “setup” until it blinks to save your macro. Now when you press the “Skip forward” button, your show should move ahead 10 seconds, which is a quick way to skip past commercials.

review_headline: Just an All Around Nifty Hybrid
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:c5160d6b7381f52ebfbe4883f243b3d3]]Personally, I see the speaker function being best suited for remote phone answering than music playing although it's not bad in its own right - just a really tiny speaker, even smaller than what one gets on the small cylinder dedicated-Bluetooth speakers - but still has surprising volume. Pair with your phone (Pairing name is an easy to remember \\"MultiTorch\\"), keep by your chair, and reach for it when a call comes in, holding it almost like an actual microphone. The flashlight works at the same time as the Bluetooth function, so as a night time bicycle-mounted combo, that's pretty nifty... and it comes with a bicycle bar mount and a clip mount.

The end cap to get to the charging function does require a bit of pull to get off, yet that also helps towards its IPx4 rating, the typical shower speaker waterproofing. In practical terms, light rain, but anything heavier, you do need to get this under cover. So not quite a true outdoor hybrid combo. I reserve the IPx5 and higher ratings as \\"true weatherproofing\\".

Comes also with a Type A to Type A USB cord for charging the 2600mAh battery, yet you will need to supply your own mini or micro USB to USB for charging whatever mobile device. It is limited to 1A, which is the standard for lower capacity power banks, so hungry, hungry devices like large screen Android tablets or the newer Apple mobile platforms will end up charging very, very slowly. For everything else, though, 1A is sufficient.

What really tickles me is that I have a colleague who's daughter has been yammering after him to get her a portable battery with a flashlight. I know without a doubt this will thrill her to her toes when I hand it off, just being one of those cool hybrid products, and I am sure my colleague will be quite pleased with the peace that comes with it. ;)

-The A900X has a slightly more accurate and flatter sound signature, but the JVC a slight bass emphasis that is fun to listen to without fatiguing my ears. Despite the huge price differential, there aren't day and night "wow this so much better" differences between both. Winner = A900X

-Both have similar wide soundstages for closed back headphones, compared to the very congested M50X/M40X I had tested. Winner = Draw.

-The JVC headband with adjustable sides design is simply more comfortable than the A900X flexible wing system. Winner = JVC

-Performance vs PRICE! Winner = JVC, hands down for being only $35, the A900X cost me 4x as much despite being in an offer, and almost 6x as much if it was at MSRP! I have really felt the buyer's remorse this time with the A900X.

For ~$35 this is a complete steal. While way too big for portable use, this is perfect for a daily beater for home/office that one can rough handle all day without feeling the heartache when seeing the eventual dents and scratches. If you are first timer to the headphone scene I strongly recommend you get this before going any higher up the price pole.

review_headline: Incredible bang for your buck. My favorite electronics purchase in ages.
review_body:
Easily one of the best purchases I've made in several years! I like having music on wherever I go all the time, and yet for some reason I took my sweet time jumping on board the bluetooth speaker train. I did a TON of research; weighing the benefits and drawbacks alongside the cost and my budget... and when the dust settled the SHARKK was my choice.

This item has outperformed every single expectation I've had, and I have used it on a near-daily basis since I got it. I'm not going to pretend to be an audiophile, but I do know how the floor models of other speakers have compared to the SHARKK. This is easily on par sound-wise with the top sellers in the market (your Booms and your Flips and your Jamboxes).

I'm hard of hearing and this speaker gets plenty loud enough. I use it primarily in my apartment's cavernous main room (high ceilings and open floor plan that contains kitchen, dining area, and living room) and it fills the area with sound ably with only the slightest noticeable distortion at the highest volumes.

I listen to all kinds of music (literally all kinds) and the speaker's levels handle them all admirably. The bass is prevalent but not overpowering, and nothing sounds tinny or murky.

And the battery life? It must be far beyond what they claim it to be, because I've yet to have the thing die on me mid-listen... and it feels like I only charge it every few weeks.

This is an absolute gem product. I wasn't familiar with the SHARKK brand before, and that made me weary, but now I am ready and willing and able to see what else they have to offer. Don't waste your money on pricier-and-yet-inferior alternatives... the SHARKK is all the speaker you need.

I charge them on my lunch and they will last me until I leave, about 5 hours.

These headphones are also great when you're very active. When I work out, ride my bike, and do other active activities, these hold em well. The earbuds come with a few different sizes and should be able to find the perfect fit. Another great feature with these headphones is the limitless replacement policy for ear buds. When used a lot, these can lose it's original shape and form, so it's great to be able to get a new set for free!

The top pros-
-lightweight
-durable/flexible
-clear sound
-connect 2 devices bluetooth

The top cons-
-low bass(personal preference)
-short charging cable(about 12 inches)

Overall I would highly recommend these headphones to anyone in the market for wireless, earbud headphones.

product_title: EBL Rechargeable Batteries and Chargers
review_headline: Excellent 6F22 replacement batteries and charger with only a few quirks
review_body:
After using this system for over a month, I am very impressed. The batteries measure at 500maH on a very conservative battery discharge test (to a voltage higher than the cutoff for most small battery tests). By comparison comparable NiMH 300mah batteries test out at about 200mah.

The tester gives you a visual indication of battery state of charge, so as the battery charges, of if put in the charger only needing a boost, the brightness of the blue LEDs for each battery position indicate state of charge. Nice touch in such an inexpensive set of 4 Li Ion "9v" batteries and charger. The only downside is that the voltage of the EBL "9v" drops under 8v when there is still quite a bit of usable charge, much as most NiMH 9v replacement batteries do. Good to make sure this level of voltage is acceptable in your device.

We have used successfully in many different battery powered alarms, the JK Audio line of telephone interfaces, and many old pieces of test equipment which use "9v" alkaline batteries.

Our usual pros and cons report:

Pros:
+ tests out in repeated cycles on GT Power A8 charger to ~500mah, over 3x most NiMH 6F22 replacements
+ very consistent discharge cycles up to 1A
+ included smart charger and state of charge indicator a real +
+ prices are now competitive with NiMH 6F22 replacements at approx 2x capacity

Cons:
- very slightly larger than some alkaline "9v" 6F22 batteries, can be difficult to fit in "9v" clips in some devices
- voltage at under ~40% charge drops below 8v, make sure device will handle this, or recharging at ~40% is ok in this use

review_body:
After seeing numerous dangerous drivers and almost getting into an accident myself due a careless motorist I committed to getting a dash cam.
I spent a week to determine which dash cam to get that would provide the best quality while still being covert and offering both front and rear cameras I ended on the DR650GW-2CH.
Although there was another manufacturer with a better quality camera it was only one channel and would require repeated removal to not be left out.

When I received my camera there was no sound or there was no way to turn on the sound. Contacted blackvue/pittasoft which still received no response after weeks but I also contacted the seller HDVideoDepot I purchased it from who suggested a few things and it still didn't work. HDVD made it easy to return without any extra costs and the new camera has sound immediately. It was probably bad speaker as everything else fully worked but don't expect to get any help from pittasoft.

Overall extremely pleased with this dash cam.

PRO's
Covert cameras - all black and barely noticeable from outside the car.
Excellent picture quality
WIFI connectability to view live feeds, configure settings, playback videos, download stored videos.
Nice playback software with maps and speed to review your path.
Set it up and forget
It may make you drive better as now you can just look back at the footage instead of staring at something and taking eyes off the road.

CON's
LED Light on the rear camera is always on. Need to use black electrical tape to cover because at night it becomes extremely obvious you have something "on" in your rear window.
Slow WIFI transfer - roughly 30 seconds to save a single one minute [FHD] video file over wifi to phone.
Android App - sometimes the app fails to remember Blackvue wifi password so you have to re-enter.

review_body: I have been using Belkin cables (and other products) for literally decades, so when I needed to extend the distance from my muti-CD changer requiring RCA connections to my ancient [[ASIN:B001DLTDQC Bose SoundDock Series II 30-Pin iPod/iPhone Speaker Dock]] I purchased one of these locally. I have not been disappointed.    One of the main reasons why I rated this cable so highly is length. Finding a twelve footer locally is not easy, and even online there are a dearth or them with known quality like Belkin.    Second, the cable construction, including connectors, is nicely done. All of the connectors are a precision fit to the RCA and 3.5mm jacks into which they mate. The outer cable is sturdy with beefy strain reliefs. Equally as important, the signals are noise free. The latter is yet another reason why I rated this cable so highly because the longer the length, the more susceptible audio cables are to noise and interference.    Bottom line: if you need a long cable and want reliability and noiseless operation (in reasonable environments) this one is a good choice.

Feel hot? That's energy being wasted while the device is not in use. Or put your ear up to the brick. Hear a buzzing or humming sound? That's also energy being wasted and wear being placed on the transformer. Have lots of these? Then you're wasting lots of energy. Solution: Get this Tripp Lite Eco Green Switched surge protector.

I currently have the following items on this switched surge protector:
TV, DVD player, Roku
Cell phone charger
All laptop power cables
Ink jet printer
Computer speakers
Computer headphone amplifier
Fluorescent desk lamp
USPS small package scale
That's a bunch of energy being saved, and a reduction of wear on my laptop power cables which constantly hum when plugged in to the wall.

Yes, the outlets are too close together for multiple "wall wart" transformer brick plugs. So, buy more of these surge protectors. It's a small price to pay to stop wasting non-renewable energy.

review_body:
[[VIDEOID:d9ac41d3a16feb890ee5d94ef50b7636]]This speaker includes the instructions, warranty card, a micro USB charging cable (approximately 2 feet, 6 inches long) and a male to male Aux cable (approximately 3 feet 2 inches long).

Antec enters the crowded portable Bluetooth speaker market with the Wav and it other line of portable speakers. I have been familiar with Antec in the computer parts realm for quite a long time and have used some of their power supplies in the past which have always been solid, so I was curious to see if that good reputation translates to their speaker line. This speaker has a stylish upright design, looks durably made and feels solid with some weight to it, but is still portable and easy to carry around. The top of the speaker has the volume buttons, play/pause/answer/hang up buttons, mode button, and next back buttons. The touch buttons are nicely spaced and easy to push and use. They could be marked a bit more clearly but luckily the buttons light up when touched making the symbols easier to see. Bottom of the speaker stand has a power switch, AUX port, microphone port and a micro charging port. Also on the bottom underside is a non-skid surface which keeps the speaker from sliding around. Each of those are hidden away a bit but still easily accessible on the back lower portion of the speaker.

The speaker needs about 4 hours to fully charge and has approximately 5 to 6 hours of play time depending on volume level. Pairing can be done via the standard Bluetooth way or via NFC. Pairing was not a problem with my Android phone. Push the power button and you are greeted with a male voice indicating it is ready to pair. The voice is clear and easy to understand. The speaker's Bluetooth range was about 25 feet before any interruption which is ok for a speaker in this price range.

Musically this speaker sounds very good with clear instrumentation and vocals and ok bass. It doesn't have the best bass I have heard in a portable speaker in this size but the sound was overall very balanced and sounds good. I could not detect any distortion at higher volumes. The speaker's phone call capability was clear and sounded good on both ends of the conversation.

This is a stylish looking speaker that has balanced sound and good call ability with some nice features such as NFC and lighted touch buttons. This has a one year warranty as well.

review_headline: If you want a working pair of wireless headphone without any bells or whistles then these will do just fine.
review_body: I was hoping these would be a bit better but they do the job. At first I had a lot of interference but after moving the antenna around I found a quiet spot. They work fine on the battery power but I wanted to run the antenna part on a adapter to a wall outlet. It does not come with a 4.5 volt adapter so I used my adjustable universal adapter. I got the adapter to produce the juice to run it but the interference from it made the headphones unusable. I am not sure if this will happen with all models but it did with mine. Also, for some reason every once and a while they will just cut-out and I needed to push the reset button on the headphones to get sound again. I am not sure if it was happening because of a precautionary measure for when they get too loud quickly but it seemed like when an explosion or a gunshot sounded it shut it off to protect my ears from the level change. It is annoying but not that bad because just a simple button push on the headphones turned them right back on. I don't have much need for the radio option but it seems to work well enough to listen to local stations. The room monitor option is pretty neat and could be useful if you wanted to secretly listen to something in a different room for some reason. All and all I am happy with them for the price I paid but if you can afford to spend a little more for a better pair I would recommend that. These are perfect for someone without that much cash to throw around.
