product_title: Aune T1 MK2 (Second Generation) 6922 24bit/192kHz Tube Amplifier Mini Hi-fi USB DAC Decoder "Fashion Black"
review_body: I'm a recovering audiophile. Back in the day I enjoyed a strictly two-channel, analog, tube-based system in a dedicated sound room (or what my x-wife referred to as a man-cave untouched by human hands). But life changes and the advent of the Internet and mp3 music files closed the book on that stage of my life..  My first foray into mp3 land was Microsoft's Edsel version of Internet music - the Zune. As buggy and user-unfriendly as Zune was, I found it preferable to continue maintaining a massive vinyl library. But over time music became only a background pass time for me, and desktop speakers were mainly for things like Skype and watching You Tube videos.  A little over two weeks ago all that began to change as I started learning about the T1 MK2. In short, I am now using it with a new pair of Creative T-40 Series 2 desktop speakers. But the audiophile in me was not satisfied with continuing to use the lossy file format of Spotify and Google Play Music. Yet I was spoiled by the virtually unlimited music library of both services. And then I discovered Tidal HiFi. Almost all of the selection and functionality of Spotify and Google, but with CD quality streaming and download capability.  Earlier today my Genalex Gold Lion E88CC Gold Pin Tube arrived and I have now been running it for about 4 hours. And for the first time in years, I'm truly enjoying just listening to music without any other distractions.And the glow of the E88CC (enhanced by the led in the T1 MK2's base) is just enough to satisfy my tube nostalgia.  My main headphone is a Samsung Level Over and I have done some listening hardwired to the T1 headphone front output. But most of my listening has been by running the rear line out (RCA plugs) through Cable Matters® Gold Plated 3.5mm to 2RCA Stereo Audio Cable to the rear input of the T40s. So most of my listening has not been with the T! solid-state headphone amp in the signal path, but rather by using the internal amp of the Creative T-40s, which by theway is no slouch of an amp according to the following You Tube review:https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qmfFMuet_O8 (you have to wait until the final few minutes of the 20 minute review to see what I'm talking about).  I've been having a lot of fun putting this new computer-age, reasonably priced "audiophile" system together and using it to re-discover my love of music. And isn't that what all these media gadgets are supposed to be used for???  UPDATE: 7/26/2015. I forgot to mention how impressed I am with T1's power supply. It is a brick with a serious cord attaching to the main unit. I remember from my audiophile days that attention to the power supply is at least as important as design of the main unit.  I do have one minor quibble. As another reviewer mentioned, it seems silly for the USB/line-in switch to be on top, while the on/off switch is on the back. I am certain most people buy this unit to use with USB-in and don't need ready access to the input switch. Yet, this is a tube unit and probably should be turned off when not using. Seems to me the position of these two switches should have been reversed.  I have been doing more critical listening with my Samsung Level Over phones, comparing the stock 6922 tube (upgraded) that came with the unit with the Gold Lion E88CC. In my system, and given my tastes, I really think I prefer the 6922. Better sound stage and more tube "magic". Vocals sound more natural and instruments more alive and "immediate". Guitar and banjo strings have just the right amount of "bite" with the 6922. And with the Gold Lion I started to notice some "wooliness" and confusion in the lower registers that was leading to a little listener fatigue. While the Level Overs reveal great detail across most of the frequency spectrum, they tend to be slightly "mellow" or relaxed. Perhaps the 6922 compensates to bring the music more to life. Of course, your mileage may vary )))  UPDATE 7/29/2015:  I continue to be blown away by the T1. I am currently trying the Sennheiser HD 598 Over-Ear Headphones. As much as I like my Samsung Level Over phones, I did buy them primarily for travel where noise-cancellation is important.   I won’t say the HD598 is a massive improvement, but I now think I have an ideal combination of the T1 and HD598 for hours and days of pure musical enjoyment. The Creative speakers are great when I don’t want to be wearing headphones.

product_title: Etymotic Research MC5 Noise Isolating In-Ear Earphones
review_body:
Over the years I have had several pairs of Etymotic earplugs, and they're great: The flexible flange seals my ear canal, does a superb job of filtering higher frequency sounds, particularly helpful in environments with loud electronic music. I chose the MC5's on this basis, and because several reviewers on several different sites recommended them for classical music (my tastes are eclectic, but mostly I listen to classical).

I just received them in the mail a short time ago and ... what a disappointment! The flanges are stiff and far too long to fit into my ear canal all the way (is ANYone's ear canal really that long?). Using the same lift-pull method I use to insert the earplugs, the buds barely rest inside the canal, pop out easily, with the least disturbance (jiggling due to walking) of the cord. The sound is excellent if I use a finger for each earbud and press inward and downward, but the sound is flat and thin otherwise. I'm giving them 2 stars because the sound *is* good, it's just that they don't fit.

I tried the other tips; some fit better than others, but none makes a seal that allows the sound to be full.

So I'm returning these. Too bad. Back to the drawing board.

product_title: Monoprice Banana Plugs Closed Screw
review_headline: Beautiful and high quality. Needs strong hands to install.
review_body:
Replacing the bare-wire speaker connections on you receiver/speakers will make your life SOOOOO much easier if you have to move them for any reason. Plus they make a much more solid, reliable connection. You don't have to worry about a few strands that didn't make it into the speaker, specially if you use nice, thick speaker cables like I do.
I use heavily-insulated 14 Gauge speaker cable that is very hard to get into the speaker and receiver, so these are priceless to me.
These closed screw banana plugs are heavy and feel exceptional in quality. They're nicely machined, and beautifully polished, and very clearly colour-coded for positive and negative ports. They are gold plated for superior connection. I can't say that they improve my sound quality, but they definitely do not hurt it.
They're knurled throughout for a good grip, but when I was screwing them back together with my speaker wire sandwiched between the pieces, I did have a hard time. I do wish these were designed with a couple flat sides so that I could have used pliers to get a better grip on them. I didn't want to use pliers on these because I would have damaged the nice finish on them. I have slightly arthritic hands and was in quite a bit of pain by the time I was done installing 8 of these on my hi-fi stereo system. I had to take a break in between pairs. If you have any hand or grip issues like I do, or for older audiophiles with arthritis, these can be a bit difficult.
They are easy to install, but I'd never worked with banana plugs before, so I went to the Monoprice website where they have this great video showing how to install them:
http://www.monoprice.com/Product?c_id=104&cp_id=10401&cs_id=1040115&p_id=2801&seq=1&format=2#video

product_title: Denon 5.2 Channel AV Receiver With 4K Capability and Bluetooth
review_headline: I bought this unit 6-7 months ago and I LOVE it. Right out of the box I was ...
review_body:
I bought this unit 6-7 months ago and I LOVE it. Right out of the box I was blown away at the quality of this low priced unit. It was very easy to setup and the auto-audio adjustment with the included microphone was neat to setup!

I had a much older, slightly less powerful unit pushing my speakers that sounded really really good, but lacked the higher power and better features I was wanting. I was a bit afraid I'd lose the great sound quality from my previous unit with this one, but was VERY pleasantly surprised! It sounds SO much better than the previous unit! The Bluetooth was one of the features I was really looking for and it works flawlessly with all the phones and tablets in our household. The only complaint that I have with the Bluetooth is that it will turn the unit on when my phone is close and starts playing sounds. A cool feature in some instances, slightly annoying when I didn't intend for it to take over my phone's audio. But a silly complaint, so not docking it points on that one.

After about a month of use I experienced the issues that many are listing in the comments about overheating and the unit kicking into protection mode and turning itself off over and over again. I was very frustrated and nearly returned the unit.

However, I decided to do a little research first, and went to Denon's website for troubleshooting. Very quickly I noticed some verbiage about the thermal requirements of this unit and an exact description of my problem. I had the unit in a small (fit the unit perfectly) cubby hole in my entertainment center. I immediately moved the unit out of the cubby to a larger cubby and at first I thought it had done the trick! Unfortunately after a while, it did it again! Finally I moved it again to a very open cubby with plenty of space above the unit. It has been 4 months of continuous use, sometimes REALLY cranking it up (I like my music) and has not since had an issue!

This unit has 5 independent amplifiers in it and is VERY sensitive to heat. If you don't have this unit in a very well ventilated area, you're gonna have a bad time!

Other than the slight headache with heat issues, I'd buy this unit over and over again!

review_headline: it provided the best features for the money
review_body:
My wife has one of these, and it worked well for her, so I got one for myself. I picked this one because, while it wasn't the least expensive, it provided the best features for the money.

If you have music or audio books on your computer in MP3 or WMA format. Just plug the player into a USB port, then open Windows Explorer and drag the files to the player.

If you are using ITunes for your music, then you will have to convert the files first. That is a pretty simple procedure, so set up should still be easy.

Four gigs seems at first glance to be a small memory by today's standards, but that's 500 to 1,000 songs or four to five normal sized audio books. That should be more than adequate for most people.

You can wear it either on the strap for your goggles or a bathing cap. I like the bathing cap because I wear my goggles pretty tight and that lets me remove and drain my goggles when necessary.

The sound is OK, and there is an equalizer function that gives you some variety. You can also shuffle the songs, which is nice, or you can just play in sequence.

There are very few controls that have to take care of a LOT of options, so they aren't as intuitive as one might like, but there is a manual included that walks you through the steps. Once you have set the unit up the way you like the controls are fine, but take the time to work through the manual.

Another thing to make note of in the manual is the care and maintenance part if you are going to wear this in a pool. Chlorine is corrosive, and following the suggestions in the manual can prevent the premature death of the unit.

product_title: Winegard HDTV Antenna
review_headline: fringe area tv wave sniffing beast
review_body:
Love love love it.
It is HUGE. Know that before you decide. But "that" is why I chose this one.
I live waaaay down (3 city blocks) 'straight down' a long extremely steep hill, and the tv stations towers are 15 miles away.
I have crap cell phone signal strength because all the 'waves' go 100's of feet above and over me.
I was using an RCA compact digital tv antenna, and could not receive 1/2 the channels.
To put this together, you will need an open area in a yard of 20 feet by 20 feet.
Very few tools.
Mine is up perfectly with a pair of pliers, a flat blade screwdriver, and a long extension ladder.
I laid it all out in the grass, unfolded the metal rods (called elements), put it together following the 2 page instructions, and this is important...
I 'LEANED' it upright against my house (yep, all 12 feet of it, "almost" straight up in the air), to add the final 3 or 4 largest sections.
I then climbed onto my roof, and pulled it up over the edge of my house, from its upright leaning position, where I had finished constructing it.
I then tired a rope to it (just in case it decided it wanted to slide down my roof), and I tied the other end of the rope to the tv stand (the tripod I used to mount the antenna to when it was finished). I didn't want a smashed antenna if it started sliding back down the roof.
Once it was mounted in its tripod stand, I Googled "television station towers (they'll ask for your address), and they then give you the locations, miles away, and ""degrees"" from your location.
This is so you can "point" your antenna towards the tv towers.
But hers what you want to know.
Did it work when I was done?
It took me 'exactly' 3 hours (not including the tripod stand. I had installed that a couple weeks ago).
It.. works.. unbelievable!
I receive ALL the stations far away; way, way, way down the bottom of my hill.
Crystal clear.
Oh, one lady thing.
My neighbor has a shorter antenna than mine (this one), with less elements.
He had to use a super long pole (his antenna is 15 feet high off the top of his house) to get stations. And he says his come and go from time to time. He also days because his pole is so long (tall), that it moves in the wind and they get a bad signal if it's windy.
But, because this one is so hugh, it picks up just a tiny sniff of any tv signal wafting by it... Mine is on a short 4 foot pole.
Much, much MUCH easier to install. No wind movement. And a perfect signal all the time.
I took pictures of me with my new antenna behind me and Facebooked them.
I was so proud of me.
I did add a tiny 3 inch, 12 volt, signal amplifier to mine (only because I already had it), but it didn't need it.
So... if what you are looking for is a "monster," wave sniffing antenna, to cure a spotty reception area, this is the best on the planet.
Lots and lots of elements (tv wave grabbing rods).
I don't see how to include any pictures, but it looks awesome on my roof.
Don't get in a hurry putting it together.
Don't be intimidated.
Follow the instructions.
They are really short anyway.
PS, one last thing. I actually secured my ladder to my house 1st! Much easier since I didn't have anybody to hold the ladder for me.

review_body:
This solved my problem, but I found it to be frustrating to set up and overpriced.

The wiring terminal is labeled 1 through 12 on top. It's divided into 3 blocks labeled A, Common and B. Below the terminals are labels indicating the wire to attach: L+, L-, etc. But these labels don't align with the terminals -- they are shifted to the left. Also, they are not consistent. They are labeled L+, L-, R-, R+. So don't get in the pattern, as I did, of assuming the + connector is always the left side of the pair.

I found it really difficult to get 14 gauge stranded wire into the terminal slots, as the opening is really tight for this wire size. Three tips that helped me: 1) be very serious about cutting the leads to the recommended 1/4". Any longer and its a bad fit. 2) Once stripped, don't cut the the wire again to get the right length. This fill flatten the end and make it tough to round it again to fit into the terminal slot. 3) Insert both leads at once. It may be tough to align them together, but inserting one and tightening it down then inserting the other is a difficult stretch because the terminals are so close together.

Finally, this is an industrial looking unit. The top of the terminal block is open, so the screws and wires are fully exposed. For the price, they could at least include a simple snap on cover. Speaking of price, the unit seems expensive. Before Radio Shack croaked, I'm thinking you could get a similar switch for less than half the price.

review_body:
[[VIDEOID:744a4e36aff3f4ff814650f8a05c06b9]]Video Notes and Highlights:

IP 4 Water Proofing - the water proofing as expected of a typical shower speaker, dealing with splashes. However, IP 5 is what I reserve as an Outdoor IP standard, being one step up. Practical difference is a light rain - IP 4. Anything heavier, IP 5. Still, IP 4 is my minimum for outdoor use.

Rugged, shock-absorbing construction, while still remaining a light, packable weight. I weighed it at 12.78 ounces.

I find the Audio to actually be somewhat flat. There is bass response, and the mids/highs are clear without overt distortion at max volume, but still the overall spectrum is lacking in deepness I expect from an indoor speaker. Nevertheless, when outdoors, rich fidelity is negligible since such nuances get swallowed up in the open air. What is most important to me is clarity and volume, which both aspects this does have. Plus, I did use a virtual EQ to play around with the balance, so there is that too.

The big aspect is that this plays while concurrently plugged into a USB power source. So even with the good battery life of 5-8 hours, I can have this going off a USB car charger or portable battery as well, like a solar power assist battery. Now that is pretty cool.

So all in all, as an indoor speaker, probably four stars, but as an outdoor speaker with rugged protection, a strong metal loop to prevent undue \\"wandering\\", and the ability to play while being powered/charged, this is a good consideration. Extra, extra credit is given that this is literally 30 bucks cheaper than another brand of the exact same design.

- Discounted price offered for evaluation purposes

product_title: JBL Synchros 400BT Bluetooth Wireless On-Ear Stereo Headphones
review_headline: Great pair of headphones for the money!
review_body:
First off let say I am not an audiophile nor am I a bass head. I don't particularly have a good ear for musical notes, so to put it simply I am your average person who enjoys music.

First off I'll talk about the style. I absolutely love the styling! Very simple looking and not too flashy. The logos are on the stainless steel headband and on both sides of the headphones. So if having logos turn you off this may not be the right pair of cans for you. For the average person however it isn't a big deal.

Secondly I'll talk about the comfort. It is comfortable! Not too much pressure and the handbag is comfortable. I read some reviews about the padding being a bit lacking, but I find it comfortable.

Now let's talk about the sound. The sound is amazing for the amount of money you pay for. In my honest opinion it is just as good if not better than the beats studio. Not trying to bash beats, but it is definitely more bang for your buck. The sound quality is fantastic! Like I said before I'm not an audiophile, but I can tell the difference between bad and good headphones. Now this pair is great! I listen to all kinds of music and this pair does not disappoint! Now for the bass... wow... just wow... I almost got the beats studio wireless due to the bass they produce, but the price was a bit too steep for me. This pair of cans matches the beats in my opinion. Like I said these cans are just great overall!

The touch controls are very easy to get used to. As long as you're semi intelligent you'll get used to it in a few minutes. It is very intuitive.

Now for the negatives. The instruction manual consists of a bunch of visual representations on what to do. I personally prefer some text, but now I'm just nit picking. Took me some time to figure out the charging time, but finally found it takes 2 hours to charge from 0% battery.

I'll update as I keep using the headphones, but so far no complaints!

It just isn't comfortable. After about a half hour, my ears hurt. It pinches too hard. I wear around a 7.5 / 7 5/8 hat. So, if you have a smaller head, it's probably great. For those of us with somewhat bigger heads, going off other reviews, it hurts.

The only time I've been able to wear it for more than 30 minutes with no pain was when I was drinking by the pool. Otherwise, if I wear it for longer, I either have to take a break or just tolerate the pain. It takes away the enjoyment of the headphones.

product_title: Pangea Audio AC 14SE MKII Signature Power Cable
review_body: The improvement in sound from these cables is hard to believe.  I liked the first one I bought so much that I ordered 3 more for my other systems.  I am only giving this item 4 stars because the seller did not disclose the difficulty in using them. These cables are extremely thick and very inflexible. Unless you have a perfectly straight run from your amp to the wall outlet (using a power conditioner defeats the benefits of this cable in my opinion, having tried doing so), you need to order at least twice the length (if not more) than you think you need.  Otherwise, neither of the end plugs will seat squarely. So, obviously, that will cost you more than you thought you were going to pay.  Without the power conditioner in the way, these cables seem to allow your amp to shine and your source material to sound better than ever.  My advice is to save your money for a power conditioner and pay an electrician--less than the cost of a "good conditioner"--to install dedicated and isolated grounded lines to your wall socket. I have also purchased Pangea source component cables, speaker cables and interconnects, all highly recommended.  While I have a limited budget, I have been an audiophile for over 50 years. Before you spend a small fortune on equipment, try these cables first.  You will not be disappointed.

product_title: Fluance AVHTB Surround Sound Home Theater 5.0 Channel Speaker System including Three-way Floorstanding Towers, Center and Rear Speakers
review_headline: This is a great value, especially for those who want to upgrade ...
review_body:
This is a great value, especially for those who want to upgrade from a HTiB setup to something more substantial, but aren't ready to make a huge investment in an audiophile setup. Yes, you almost certainly need a powered subwoofer, but perfectly decent one can be had for a hundred bucks. I have a 13' X 14' theater room and these speakers can easily handle it with a 100 watt Yamaha receiver.

Why not 5 stars? The obvious weakness in this setup is the center speaker, which I found to be mediocre. Considering that it handles most of the dialogue in movies/TV, I soon upgraded the center speaker to a much larger speaker that really improved the setup. The other strange thing is that I found the posts to be very particular about the type of banana plugs they accept. I ended up using spade plugs, because the banana plugs that I had did not fit.

Overall, I think the tower and surround speakers are an excellent value, but be aware that you may benefit greatly by adding a subwoofer and upgrading the center speaker. The speakers look really nice considering their price and they sound fine with music and movies.

It has a remote, which is about the size of a long book of matches. It comes with a power cord, and will not work without it.

product_title: Klipsch R6 Black In-Ear Headphone with Patented Oval Tip (Black)
review_headline: Skip this and get the R6 instead.
review_body: I have a klipsch S4 from 2010 which is still going strong. The cable cracked over time so I put a braided cover on it, the headphone jack died so I soldered the brass metal stereo jack from radio shack and I've been set like this for the past 5 years. The earphones fit well in my ears and the sound quality is just great. They'll probably last another couple of years.  That's probably why Klipsch designers sat in a room and decided that since their products last too long they need to make them less durable while at the same time give the impression of quality. Either that or they hired someone from Beats. Either way this thing feels like an upgrade but a few weeks of use later you realize that this is actually a downgrade.  So instead of the standard cylindrical cable, you now have a clunky flat cable that winds around itself and gets caught in everything else. Sure, it does not tie knots around itself as often and when it does, it's easy to un tie. Since the fit of the S4 was without any complaints, they decided to make the earphone body out of metal so that it'll slide of our your ears every few minutes. Honestly, I can't think of any reason why they made these out of metal. So they can survive being run over by a car?  And don't get me started on the mic, it has an impedance greater than 10 Ohms so you sound really distant and nobody can hear you, the button sometimes clicks sometimes doesn't and the whole thing makes the left earphone fall out, pulling the right one out with it. The clip is next to useless and has too little bite to it to hold on to anything.  Sound Quality: Guess what. Sounds exactly the same as my S4, with a bit more bass added. Midrange is slightly less punchy but barely discernable and there is a very slight drop in volume. Nothing I cannot do with my phone's equalizer. The silicone eartips don't fit my ears well, unlike the S4, which fit perfectly and rarely come off during a run.  Everything said and done, you'll still want this since the S4 is out of production. So buy the R6 instead and save yourself some $40. The mic is practically useless and the remote button with it's added weight add on does not justify the cost.

product_title: iDeaUSA Dual Bluetooth Wireless Speakers - Portable Speaker Combo Pack, 4x Woofers with Buddy Setup, Boombox, Up to 10 hours play time, Built in Mic, NFC Compatible for iPhone, Samsung, Nexus and more
review_headline: Toe Curling Audio Pleasure (but Odd Cut-Outs with the Samsung Galaxy S6)
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:72b619233b45bbc20e96186ce5a96dee]]An idea that has finally come to pass. Two simul-synched Bluetooth speakers. WOOT!

For relaxation and New Age, this is one immersive experience that no single speaker can deliver, not even similarly priced ones, like the Aukey APOLLO with it's 3D sound emulator or the Turcom ACOUSTO SHOCK or even the BlueSYNC SBR Bluetooth Sound Bar. And for crunking, well, big, blasting tower speakers are always going to be the best, but these push the small Bluetooth speaker experience to the next level.

Both speakers have the exact same build, same buttons, same performance. There is a left and right, however, and they aren't marked - yet when you first turn them on (by pressing the power buttons simultaneously), one will say \\"Left\\" and the other will say \\"Right\\". They do play while actively charging, each @ 0.50A The red LED charging light will wink off once charging is completed. Two 3 foot micro USB to USB cords are included along with two gold-plated AUX cords and a couple nice carry bags.

You can use the buttons on either to control the set, as well as the remote phone answering. Both have microphones - talk about aural speakerphone clarity.

Distance wise between the two speakers, I got as far away as 28 feet - a relatively clear line-of-sight, though, is needed. Also, while streaming from my Samsung S6, the right speaker still briefly cut out once in awhile even when near the left speaker; yet when I paired the set to my PC's Bluetooth then later an Android tablet, both speakers played without any interruption about 7 feet apart, one on a chair side table, the other up on a wall shelf, and about 30 feet from my PC. I can't fathom why my S6 causes issues.

Speaking of shelving, there are two included, slightly sticky rubber pads that I assume is for dampening shelf vibration and helping with increased bass response. Initially, the right speaker actually shifted a couple things off my shelf (just plastic supplement bottles), so I put one of the rubber pads down. That did the trick.

I ended up dedicating these two speakers to music paired off a M10X 10.1\\" tablet as a music center. The result is toe curling audio pleasure.

review_headline: Take The Music Outside With No Fear Of Water
review_body:
The weather is warming up, we are finally getting to spend more time outside. Getting outside, playing in the pool or in the water doesn't mean In I can't enjoy my music too. I received a Tekubox Waterproof Wireless Speaker to review and I love it for outside play!
The charge time was relatively quick and it has lasted me quite some time. I have lost track of how many hours I have played it because I turn it off when I am not using it.
, this speaker goes with me out into the yard and I don't have to worry if it gets wet, While my tablet stays safe and dry on the deck. It will pick up up to 33 feet away so I get good coverage out in the yard.
It works for the shower pr bath too, but outdoors is so much more fun! This speaker connected to my tablet within just a few seconds and plays seamlessly.
It plays plenty loud enough for me and the buttons work with a pretty light touch. The speaker allows you full function of your music and phone with multi-use buttons.
At the top you have the power on/off button. The button on the right allows you to skip forward to the next song with a quick tap or increase the volume by holding it down for a few seconds.
The button at the bottom allows you to answer and hang up a phone call. There is a built in microphone that allows you to talk though the speaker.
The button on the left allows you to skip back to the previous song with a quick tap or lower the volume by pressing it for a few seconds. The center button is to pause/resume play.
The speaker is a cheerful bright blue color that stands out. It is compact and lightweight with a strong suction cup to stick it to the shower wall, mirror, or almost any smooth surface.
Summer is only getting started, but with gadgets like the this waterproof bluetooth speaker, it promises to be fun and full of music!

product_title: Diver DB-10 4GB Waterproof MP3 Player with Waterproof Earphones (Blue)
review_headline: Have you heard music underwater before? Because you should probably give it a shot.
review_body:
I'd definitely recommend this waterproof MP3 player to any swimmer. Honestly, the sensation of hearing music while swimming is a blast.

Rating five stars because, in the words of Amazon, I love them. I can't imagine swimming laps without this thing.

The good here:
+Solid build quality.
+Charging was easy.
+Loading songs onto the device was easy - it's recognized as a flash drive, just drag and drop.
+Sound quality was really clear, especially under water.
+The headphones clip very nicely to your goggles, and the whole unit stays put while swimming.
+Battery life is good.
+Seriously, hearing clear music while swimming changes the entire experience, and it definitely helps provide motivation for laps.

The not so good:
+Very little control over music order. This is essentially a shuffle device. You can skip, but that's about it. Not necessarily a negative, but something to be aware of.
+The controls take a little getting used to. To skip a song you press the + button. To raise the volume you hold the same + button. The buttons have been a little rigid up to now, so more often than not, I have been skipping songs when trying to adjust the volume. I expect this to become easier as I break the device in.
+The earplugs need some moisture, and a little force, to help them stay in. It's a bit of a struggle at first, but once they're in, I've had little issue. For the kind of amateur lap swimming I do - freestyle, backstroke, breaststroke - they were fine. You probably won't have any luck if you're doing a butterfly. Then again, there are other waterproof headphones on the market, and they should work with this device. I just haven't found any as compact as these yet.

I would buy these again. In fact, I now have two pair - one for the Mrs and one for me.

product_title: Diver 4GB Waterproof MP3 Player with LCD Display and Earphones (Blue)
review_body:
First off, I really like this product. It has transformed my lap swimming workout. I use it to listen to podcasts and it alleviates the tediousness of my workout. I get to exercise AND learn/be entertained. I've used it for about a dozen swim sessions so far.

Also, the price is superb. I had researched these a couple years ago and they all seemed to be > $200.

Storage size and battery charge seem to be fine so far.

Considerations:
- The device is covered in buttons on all sides. It takes a little getting used to, in the beginning I kept inadvertently hitting buttons. What I discovered is that it's best to leave the player hooked on the googles at all time and to carry it around by the google's straps. Then you can just put it on instead of trying to clip it after it's playing.
- You'll probably need to fuss with the ear phones a bit while you swim to adjust their position. I was expecting this, as I have to do this with regular terrestrial ear buds.
- You can't be too fussy with continuity. If you accidentally forward the podcast in the middle, it's a chore to find the spot again given that it can be hard to read the interface in the pool with the sun shining and it stops your workout. I just keep listening to whatever is next.

Room for improvement:
- I wish it was a touch louder, You don't realize how loud swimming is until you try to listen to something. I've had to calm down my stroke a bit and have had trouble with quieter podcasts.
- I've had a little trouble with "format error" stops, even on files that had worked just fine just minutes before.

It has other features I haven't used, like the radio and the pedometer, so I can't comment on that.

All in all a good product and I recommend it, especially for the price.

review_headline: Love the headphones; Most durable on the market
review_body:
There's a long version and a short version of how I feel about these headphones. I'm not well enough versed to not sound like an idiot to describe the audio quality in full, so I'll focus on the things that I do know about. To be clear, though, I listen to high or lossless music quality, and these cans sound wonderful.

The build quality is exquisite. I have a fear of breaking "nice" headphones because I take them *everywhere* and bike around with them on (dangerous, I know. I live on the edge). Rest assured, there's a pretty low chance of you damaging these accidentally. They can be dropped, bent, and crushed, and as long as you aren't intentionally going at it with a tool, they are solidly built. Perfect for me.

The only problem I have is the fact that I have moderately large ear+head combo, and the stock ear pads started hurting my ears pretty quickly. Many over-ear headphones do, but some don't, so I know it is possible. Apparently, this happens a lot for this V-MODA model, because they offer a set of XL cushions. Normally I would be... irked about these not being included (and costing some $30), and I am, actually. BUT V-MODA recently slashed the price of these down $50 for the express purpose of making the alternate accessories more, um, accessible. So future buyers, good for you.

I use these with an android HTC One M9, a PS4, laptops, and headphone amps with no trouble at all.

The multiple cables and hard shell case are fantastic additions, but again, even storing these things in the case isn't necessary because of their durability (I still do).

product_title: Silverback Flex Pin Connectors, For Spring-Loaded Inputs, 6 Pairs
review_body:
This is he first time I have written a review. I am trying to contribute more to the community since I rely on the reviews of others. I think these are a great solution for connecting your speaker wire to spring-loaded terminals. I just tested it with some 12 AWG. It fits nicely into the hole it goes into. I was a little worried about the screw at first considering the size of speaker wire I am using. However, those concerns quickly faded. The braided tips are very solid and VERY inflexible. For me, these are perfect. It will make it very easy for when I actually install my theater system.

I would like to touch on some of the concerns others have brought up. Yes, I can see that there is a great potential for these to break. Again, the braided tip is very inflexible. Don't think you are going to be able to bend these to the position you want without some repercussion. I don't think you would want to insert these all the way into a spring loaded terminal as you would want to leave some of the tip available to pull on in case they had broken off. I only say this so people are aware. I don't move my speakers around with speaker wire in them and I don't think a lot of other people do either.

I would just have people know to take a little forethought on the proper use of these connectors. I think you would have to be pretty frivolous for these to break, but I can't claim people have been frivolous for those that have had problems. My last words will be that these are great. They will make it easy to wire up your speakers. I am just one of those guys who plans for the worst and hopes for the best. Don't let my words dissuade you from buying these. Treat them with respect and they will serve you well.

product_title: BeoPlay H6
review_body: Comparing headphones around a price point is like comparing flavors of pie. You may have your preference, but can anyone really say that apple is better than coconut creme?  I've been in search of the perfect $200 - $600 headphone for some time, and have found that some models shine on some recordings and less on others. Higher-end cans can be revealing of imperfection and requiring higher-quality files. I've been seeking a natural and accurate sound with detail, and sounds good no matter what I throw at it, from lossless files through a headphone amp to 128kpps files right out of the iPod. With the H6, I've finally found it.  A few years ago I started with the Grado 225, when I just wanted a pair of cans and a local music store gave me a good price -- but the cost was to become a fascination with headphones. The detail of the 225s, which I still have, is stunning for their $200 price. However they reveal imperfections and harshness in some recordings, and can therefore become fatiguing. And their low bass is rather light. I then tried the Grado PS500, at nearly $600, as it promised to smooth out that occasional harshness and deliver more low-end punch. Turns out, while the mids and highs were superlative, the mid-bass could be excessive while the low bass (< 100 Hz) was no more prominent than the 225's. Found that my $100 Bose AE2s reproduced features below 50Hz that were just missing with the PS500s. Couldn't accept not hearing part of the recording for $600 and sold them. I got those Bose AE2s along the way because I needed closed cans at times. I still have them, they're better than their reputation and quite nice for $100, I think, and sound decent playing most anything. Glorious low bass, but they lack the sparkle and detail of the Grados. So I've been looking for headphones with the therapeutic deep bass of the AE2s, and the mids and highs of the Grado PS500s. Elusive. I've been told I can find this combination in a pair of $1000 planars, Audezes and thelike, but I'm not that committed. I've tried a number of others in the lower price points, standouts being B&W P7 (mid-bass way too boomy otherwise very nice) to NAD HP50 (decent, but a narrow frequency band sounded "off" to me). Nothing came through.  The B&O H6 has long been intriguing but the price seemed steep for what might be construed as a more mainstream pair of cans. I shouldn't have held off. Finally purchased these, and they're wonderful to my ears. They sound great with all sources, all genres. Very natural, non-fatiguing, and comfortable. I've read reviews about them being light in the bass department. They're not boomy in the mid-bass ranges like the P7s, or Beats. However, they reproduce the mid-bass range naturally (not at all light) and have a stellar sub-bass signature. The perfect slice of pie for my tastes.

product_title: Bose SoundLink Mini Bluetooth Speaker II (Pearl)
review_headline: Eureaka! The Soundlink Mini 2 does have transport controls! **UPDATED...Day 2...**UPDATED Day 7
review_body:
UPDATED - Day 7

So, I normally place updates at the bottom, but considering this update changes my perspective of the whole Soundlink mini (and drops it down to 3 stars), I figured I would place it up top and leave it to the reviewer if they still wanted to read my initial impulsive impression of the speaker.

After a week of using the Soundlink I've come to realize it sounds like crap. The volume simply isn't there which is primarily drained out by the overwhelming bass heavy EQ they've colored this speaker to sound. And the whole spectrum of volume seems unbalanced in general. If I lower the volume from max about 3 ticks, I can barely hear anything. This left it pretty much impossible to leave the volume at anything less than full volume. But it also has distortion when at full volume, so its a lose lose situation for me. And lets face it, if you are constantly having to blast this bass heavy bad boy at full volume you are definitely not going to get 10 hours out of this thing. The battery level seems to be dropping not insanely fast, but fast enough for me to realize I wasn't going to get 10 hours.

The bass is also a huge issue when using the speaker phone because the bass is so prominent that I can barely hear what the person is saying. It makes their voice somewhat mumbled together. They can hear me very well which is good to know, but useless to me if I cant hear them better on my iPhone's speaker. The connection is also choppy with the speakerphone via the soundlink.

Also, the unit was a little picky when its connected to 2 Bluetooth mediums. A very nice feature, but it kept auto connecting to my iMac no matter what it was set to previously before it was powered off.

I wont make this long and dragged out, as my initial review was long enough, but I ended up returning it. Yes, it is a great speaker when compared to all others in its class in consideration of portability and price. But I am not willing to make the astronomical compromise in overall sound quality as I wasn't planing to carry this speaker around too often. It would have been nice having a portable speaker to carry around when needed, but it doesn't even come close to the sound of a decent pair of headphones which also happen to be portable (including the quiet comforts that I own which sound amazing).

This all being said, I winded up trying out the SoundTouch Portable. I know I was sacrificing the Bluetooth, but I have an iPhone. so airplay isn't a problem for me. The problem was, although it is louder than the Soundlink mini, it still wasn't all that loud and it sounded like crap as well. The bass wasn't there and the whole sound was very flat and also unbalanced across the volume spectrum. Lower the volume slightly and you can barely hear anything.

So I ultimately sucked it up and went for the Bose Soundtouch 20 which 100% is what I am sticking with. I didn't even have to sound compare them side by side when I got home which is unlike me. I packaged both of the other speakers up within 1 minute of hearing how amazing the SoundTouch 20 was in my house. I blows both of these speakers out of the water, is pretty freaking loud, is really not all that much bigger than the Soundtouch Portable (its portable enough for me to carry around the house and uses a standard 8 figure power adapter which I have plenty of lying around the house). I would even not feel hindered carrying it on vacations. I wouldn't be using it on any beaches, but hotel rooms...rock on.

If you REALLY need something portable enough that you are going to be carrying it around everywhere Id say go for the Soundlink 3. I thought it sounded better and louder than the Soundlink mini 2 and the Soundtouch Portable. But if you want something that sounds amazing and able to carry around from room to room (power required), then definitely check out the SoundTouch 20. It has an Aux in jack so it wouldn't be hard to adda bluetooth dongle in the mix if required.

For all you people that are dead set on the Soundlink Mini 2, then some things I mention below in my original review may help...

-----------------------------------------------------

- Original Review-

I kick this review off by mentioning very quickly a couple things no one else did, then describe more in detail below.
1) The Soundlink Mini 2 DOES have transport controls
2) The Soundlink Mini 2 PEARL appretiatedly comes with pearl colored everything. Pearl base, pearl power block, pearl USB wire. Thanks for not dropping the ball and throwing in a black wire Bose.
3) The Soundlink Mini 2’s USB connection is on the REAR of the base. Not on the side like the original mini. THANKS BOSE!!

OK. Review time. I was in the market for a Bluetooth speaker for my kitchen that I could easily take with me when I'm on the go. I already own the Quiet Comfort 15's and was blown away by the quality. I've also own other Bluetooth speakers (before owning any Bose products) and was not overly impressed (UE Boombox, Sony alarm clock speakers, UE Boom, JBL Charge, Jam Classic, amongst some other bluetooth speakers). So I decided to give the Bose a try even though it was quiet expensive to what’s out there.

WOW! I am shocked by how amazing these sound and how much bass they throw. It’s unbelievable.

I honestly didn’t even know about the existence of the Soundlink mini line until the other day, and I got to say, I was bummed about 3 things when researching the original:

1) No speakerphone capability (great for the kitchen when cooking)
2) No transport controls (Play, Pause, Next, Previous buttons on the unit)
3) The ports being on the side of the unit and charging base (I didnt want to see a wire across my counter)
Then to my surprise, I found out the Mini 2 was already out by the time I was in the market for one (just came out this month) and it addressed most of my issues above.

I actually was almost skeptical that it didn’t include transport controls (play, pause, next, back etc.) on the unit because I usually press play on my phone when I'm home and leave it in my office all day. I didn’t see anyone mention it in their reviews (I guess it’s not as important to anyone else), but it does in fact have transport controls!!! All via the MULTI-FUNCTION button.

PLAY - PRESS ONCE
PAUSE - PRESS ONCE WHEN PLAYING MUSIC
NEXT TRACK - PRESS 2 TIMES
PREVIOUS TRACK - PRESS 3 TIMES

The previous model didn’t seem to have any transport controls at all.

The unit itself is solid! It’s a little on the heavy side for portability, but not a deal breaker at all. I feel like I am holding my money’s worth. Charging is now done via micro USB. This means you can pretty much use any wire or connect to USB chargers. It makes this thing much more portable as I don’t have to carry around a specific power cable now. And I already have tons of micro USB cables and USB chargers everywhere in my house, car, work,…Plus the battery life has been extended 3 extra hours of music play (I havent tested yet, but Im assuming this is not accounting for playing music at full volume).

The only thing I’m fond of is they still left the ports on the side of the unit itself (AUX PORT and USB). Most wires are not on a 90 degree angle which means you are going to see these wires sticking straight out to the side. Who wants to see that? Like I said before, they moved the USB port to the back of the unit on the base which I am VERY thankful for. It will mostly be in my kitchen on the base and I primarily use Bluetooth. So I won’t have to see any wires for the most part, hence why it’s not a huge issue for me. But I don’t see why they didn’t just place the ports on the back. Or it would have been even more amazing if they had an Aux port on the base itself.
That’s the only complaint I can find at the moment. I literally just got it a few hours ago, and I’m already blown away. We’ll see how it holds up after some more use/testing.

To wrap it up, I highly recommend! Especially over the previous model if what I mentioned above is as important to you as it is to me. I believe all those extras are worth the extra 20-30 bucks in comparison to the original mini.

***Something I forgot to mention was that I was mostly leaning toward the Soundlink 3 before I discovered the mini. But after seeing it in the store and how massive it was compared to the mini, and considering it didnt have the bells and whistle of the Mini 2, I went with the mini 2 upon glance.

***UPDATE (Day 2)

So...I still stand by my review. This speaker is awesome. But I have to point out something that I would consider to be an important factor.

As with any and all speakers (or anything that produces sound for that matter), the sound arriving at your ears is hindered by a thing us audio/sound engineers like to call 'Room Acoustics'. And while some speakers are affected more than others (mostly due to design), this seems to be more prominent on the Soundlink mini in general.

I tested this bad boy in every room in my house, each room sounding very noticeably worlds different. For the most part it sounded great in every room (especially my larger living room with higher ceilings), but unfortunately, it sounded the worst in the kitchen which is why I bought the speaker. To have in my kitchen.

Don't get me wrong. It still sounds great. But the sound seems slightly drowned in the kitchen.

Now....I know I cant fully blame this on the mini is what most people would say. It's simple room acoustics. You have to blame it on the room. And where I would have agreed and said the same thing in the past, my JBL LSR305's (freaking AMAZING speakers btw!) have a design technology which helps remove pesky room acoustics to deliver a more natural sound of 'what you should be hearing'....and its surprisingly very impressive. Considering Bose is known for their innovation when it comes to audio and being top tier with their noise reduction technology, it would have been nice to see them develop some sort of room acoustics technology for their portable speakers.

And the design itself doesnt help. It is very straight forward. There are no angles to the speaker. Most of those speakers you see angled upwards isnt just for looks. It actually serves a very good purpose which would definitely help the mini's design. Lets face it..most people are going to place this on a desk, counter, night stand....something that is not exactly ear level. This becomes more apparent in a smaller room where you are in closer proximity to the speaker itself if it is not high up enough as opposed to a larger room (like my living room) where I can stand further back and am getting the full sound. It would have been nice to see some kick stands in the base or the unit itself to angle upward or downwards. I am going to have to fancy my own, because the speaker is too low to achieve optimal sound in my kitchen.

This all being said, if you are testing it out in the store, your ultimate best test will be testing it out where you will ultimately be using it. I still love this speaker and think its amazing. review_body:

I had to stop here and let everyone know that it will not last. Sorry Sherwood... once a great brand, now I'm not so sure.

This is an excellent receiver. I've been through several old recycled receivers lately in search of one without a scratchy volume control. I didn't realize they were still available and so inexpensive too. Of course the new ones will never suffer the potentiometer failures due to the electronic volume adjustment so I suspect this will be my last receiver purchase. I was able to connect my turntable, speakers, and an auxiliary cable from a nearby laptop and go back to some peaceful yoga. I have not even played with the BlueTooth connectivity yet so more satisfaction surely awaits. I would buy it again in a heartbeat. The sounds is perfect through my old floor-standing speakers.

product_title: CyberPower PFC Compatible Pure Sine Wave Tower UPS
review_headline: Be careful: may not be pure sine wave output.
review_body:
Be warned: although this is advertized as a "pure sine wave" output UPS, the unit I received was NOT pure sine wave though it was the correct model number. I'm not sure if they are all like this or maybe I just received an "old stock" product, but the box and instruction manual I received clearly stated it uses "adaptive sine wave" technology which is NOT pure sine wave.

I called CyberPower and they said it was just marketing terms, but then I read the original CyberPower press release which clearly stated that adaptive sine wave technology was a cheaper alternative to pure sine wave, and it uses a triangular wave instead of a true pure sine wave.

Now, for most people the adaptive sine wave technology this product uses is fine. It WILL work with active PFC power supplies. That said, if you really need pure since wave output then this is NOT the unit for you.

Also, my unit does not advertize "line interactive" AVR, just AVR, so again I don't know if this is just the way they printed the instruction manual or if I got an older unit with older features because line interactive AVR is able to stabilize voltage without using the battery which is a great feature.

I gave it three stars because it was not Amazon's fault (CyberPower themselves are falsely advertizing the product, not Amazon) and Amazon was very helpful with their customer service (since this is not a returnable item, we had to work something out).

Again, I might have received an older unit and maybe the new ones DO use "pure sine wave" output, however the unit I received uses "adaptive sine wave" output which is similar to, but not the same as the advertized "pure" sine wave output. If you really do need pure sine wave backup power, I suggest testing whatever unit you receive with an oscilloscope before hooking up your equipment. This unit is fine for active PFC power supplies because they don't really need pure sine wave output, adaptive triangular output is good enough, but some equipment DOES need true pure sine wave output.

Let me say again, this is not Amazon's fault and Amazon was very friendly and took care of my problem quickly.

product_title: Portable Waterproof Bluetooth Speakers w/ FM Radio & LCD Display, IPX7 Water Resistant & Shockproof - Ultimate Wireless Handfree Rechargeable Shower Speakerphone
review_headline: Nice Sound From A Durable Speaker
review_body:
There was a time just a few years ago when I did not believe a speaker this small could deliver the sound quality and volume that this one can. Technology has come a long way. The fact that this speaker is waterproof will make it the must-have device when I visit my parents' house for a dip in the pool this summer.

The device is small and compact and to give you an idea of the size it is about the same girth as a soda can and about the height of a can and a half. The exterior is rugged and covered in a hard rubber substance everywhere but the speaker grille. The device is rated IPX7 which means it is pretty much completely water and dust proof. You can find out more by Googling "IP Code" and reading more about the rating system if you are curious.

The device floats, which is nice since it is a great speaker to have by the pool. While it may float with the speaker facing up, which is a genius move, the bass reflex port gets covered up so you'll lose a bit of bass if the speaker is actually floating in the pool.

The sound quality of this device is excellent. For a portable speaker the sound is some of the best that I've heard. It also gets quite loud. I happen to have a decibel meter so I turned the speaker up full blast and started the latest Kid Rock album on it and tested the sound force about a foot from the device and got a reading of 99.6db. To show how loud that really is the level at which sustained exposure may result in hearing loss is 90db to 95db so there is plenty of non-distorted volume here.

The Bluetooth connectivity works well and my phone has no problem connecting immediately to it every time the speaker is powered on. You can keep your iPhone safely out of harms way and still control the volume, skip tracks and even answer a phone call using the built in microphone.

The device charges via USB and there is a port on the back of the speaker that is covered by a rubber protector. There is also a headphone sized jack with the USB port if you want to plug a device directly into this speaker.

I tested this unit out with some Netflix videos on my old Macbook Pro laptop and was delighted to see there was no audio lag with this speaker. You can watch your content without the annoyance of the lip movements not matching the audio.

The unit has a built-in FM radio which is a nice little perk. I live far enough outside of Chicago that I can't really get much on the radio side when inside the house but outside the reception is quite a bit better.

There are two square plastic handles on each side which are a great addition as you can either attach the included lanyard to one to hang it or you can use just about anything that you can string through the holes to hang the speaker where you want it.

The included battery is rated at 2500mAh which is enough for 9 hours of playtime at the loudest volume level. While I did not test that specifically, I know I got over 12 hours listening to it at a lower volume level so it is very likely that number is correct.

Overall this is a speaker that is hard to beat for using outside and / or near water. It would make a great speaker for poolside or for hanging in the shower. The sound quality and volume are excellent as is the durability of the speaker itself no matter where you use it. Highly recommended.

I forgot to mention just weeks before this wildfire/evacuation we took it tent camping in the Jemez Mountains of NM.
We enjoyed great reception (AM/FM) music and news on demand in these same mountains (8000ft above sea level) that catastrophically
burned two weeks later.
Don't hesitate to purchase this little work horse!

Buying another for my car just in case of emergencies.
It's simple, easy to operate and a must for everyone requiring a simple method of receiving Emergency Communications as well as AM/FM
Radio. By the way I am Pleased to report it still works like new after 4 years!

product_title: MEE audio M6 PRO Universal-Fit Noise-Isolating Musician's In-Ear Monitors with Detachable Cables (Smoke)
review_headline: A very well rounded IEM at a fantastic price
review_body:
This is my fifth pair of MEElectronics headphones and I'd been waiting a long time for some legitimate in ear monitors from MEE and these do not disappoint. I received these units over six months ago and have put them through extensive use both for on stage, and for regular air travel. I'd say that these have over 30,000 airline miles on them, including a round trip US to Israel, and US to UK (in addition to a ton of domestic trips). They've held up really, really well. In fact, I'd say they are still pretty much new. Let's take a closer look at them.

First off, let's look at the product itself:

-They come with a multitude of ear tips- silicone of all different sizes, and FINALLY some foam tips for extra isolation. I personally use the foam for everything because of the comfort and isolation. They also hold nice and solid. Don't come out or loosen with sweat or activity.
-The body of the IEMs are a great size, shape, and construction. Some of the IEMs out there tend to be a bit bulky and cause hotspots on the ears after long use, and these are not that way.
-They come with two different sets of memory wire cables. One is the standard cable with an on-line microphone, volume rocker, and button. It works well with phones both for phone calls, and for listening to and controlling music. The second cable is my favorite. It doesn't have the microphone or controls, but the build is much sturdier and a better overall feel. This cable is intended to be used for heavy IEM use (on-stage, and things like that). The connections on the cables seem solid and I've had no issues with them coming loose, disconnecting, fraying, or anything like that.
-They are comfortable to wear in almost any way- cable in front, cable in back, inside clothing, outside clothing. The slider on the cable holds tight so nothing comes loose with extensive sweat or activity.
-The case that comes with these is by far my favorite MEE case to date.It's the right size, relatively hard sized, and not too big.

Let's look at the audio quality:

This was one of my biggest worries with IEMs at this price point. In fact, when I first wanted to give MEE a try I was worried that the audio quality wouldn't be very good. THAT IS NOT THE CASE. These are great full range headphones that give you just the right mix of everything. I'm a bit of a basshead (I play bass, go figure.....), and these pleased me. There's enough bass coming through but not so much that it muddies up everything else. They take really well to EQ mixing so you can give yourself the exact sound that you want.

Overall thoughts:

I dare you to put these IEMs up against others that are 2-3 times the price. You'd be hard pressed to find a better set for anywhere near the price. I have to say, MEE does it again. Do yourself a favor and stop searching. Buy these guys.

product_title: Xtreme Signal
review_headline: Great Antenna - Don't be an Arrow Antenna Lemming
review_body:
So after Xfinity decided to try to sign me to a 2-year contract to keep my cable prices reasonable, and after they had disconnected my cable and internet without warning due to a wiring issue, leaving us without TV for several days, I decided to start the process of "cord cutting" which starts with a good antenna for free DTV.

I live in the Chicago area, so I really don't need to aim for two cities - just aiming at Chicago will get you a ton of channels from Gary Indiana too. However, right in the line of sight to the transmitters are two massive Cottonwood trees, so the normal "Arrow" antenna that everyone else around here has didn't really work as well as I had hoped. Our house needed a broader antenna to help suck the signal out between the tree branches rather than a directional antenna. This did the trick. It was easy to install too - it was largely assembled and with the help of an iPhone app very easy to position for best reception.

My biggest concern was that the extra surface area might cause it to torque or twist on windy days requiring me to reposition it eventually but that hasn't been the case at all. Am very pleased.

review_headline: Antemall Metal Wired In-Ear Headphones - Nice sound - Strong bass - Comfortable earbuds - Work well - Recommended
review_body:
The Antemall Metal Wired In-Ear Headphones are very comfortable and have good sound across the register, with a strong emphasis on the bass range. The upper & mids are good enough too, making the entire experience pleasant when listening to high fidelity with surround-sound tracks, but these are definitely bass oriented. I would recommend this headset to folks that like the bass emphasis, like our teenage son.

Tested music with our Samsung Galaxy S3, we took our time to find the right combination of earbuds as that makes such a difference. Once you get the right ones for your ears, this is a very comfortable headset to wear. My son and I take different sizes and we found that comfort and sound quality depend on the right earbud connection; this headset comes with three different pairs, so test them all out to make sure you get it just right for each ear.

We also tested the in-line microphone for call making, and found it to be good too -- it produced a clear signal and the in-ear speakers did a great job of broadcasting voices to me. Well done; with the headset we received, the clarity and functionality of the inline microphone was great.

As noted - when listening to music or when making calls, we found the sound to be excellent and we did not have any issue with earbud slippage or comfort once finding the right ones for our ears. Most of our listening was done while stationary (and while driving), not while in motion or exercising. review_headline: Best headphones I’ve tested in this price range. Great for a Father’s Day/Graduation gift.
review_body:
This is a review of the SROCKER over-ear stereo Bluetooth headphones. I’ve been testing the headphones for several weeks. Here are my thoughts on the unit.

The design of the headphones is very attractive. The look and feel gives you the impression that this is a premium device. Most people will not guess that these are sub-$100 headphones. Build quality is superb. Both the headband and the ear covers are cushioned. The headband can be quickly adjusted for an exact fit. The unit fits comfortably on my ears and on my head.

These headphones are easy to use. I didn’t have to consult the manual to pair the device or figure out its controls. The unit has a single knob for volume and playback. It works really well. I find that this control knob is much easier to use than the buttons you typically see on headphones. Buttons are often hard to find or hard to distinguish.

Audio is great. If you like a lot of bass, this unit definitely delivers the bass. Some will want to adjust the bass down via a software equalizer, which I do recommend. Teens will love the default bass level, as evidenced by my little brother. He’s been begging me for these headphones.

I used the headphones to listen to music, to listen to the television, and to play video games. It worked great in all instances.

I was able to use the headphones while working out. The headphones stay in place without issue. You may sweat around the ears if you are not in an air conditioned environment, however. For this reason, earbuds are typically a better option for working out.

Battery life seems to be really good. I have yet to run out of power while using them. This unit seems to have better staying power than the other units I’ve tested in the price range.

One thing I would change in the next version of these headphones is to have separate control knobs for the volume and for playback.

Note that I did not test the unit for phone calls. Rarely does a pair of headphones excel in this area. Also note that I received these headphones in exchange for this honest review.

BOTTOM LINE

As I mentioned at the top, these are the best headphones I’ve tested in this price range. It features an attractive design, solid build quality, and comfortable fit. Audio is great. The bass level is excellent, although, some people will want to adjust it down via an equalizer. Best of all, these headphones are priced pretty competitively.

If you are in the market for a great pair of sub-$100 headphones, this is an excellent choice. Definitely recommended.test the unit for phone calls. Rarely does a pair of headphones excel in this area. Also note that I received these headphones in exchange for this honest review.

product_title: Sony SRSX5 Portable NFC Bluetooth Wireless Speaker System
review_body:
I;ve had the SRSX5 but my ears fell in love upon first listen. In my quest for a great soubnding portable speaker I first purchased the JBL Charge 2. I like the physical shape of the Charge 2 but the when listening at low volume I heard terrible distortion. That may have been due to it being an pre-firmware updated version but regardless I couldn't stand it. I wanted a speaker that had great sound at low volume when listening at bedtime or working. But even at "normal" volume when the distortion was less noticeable on the Charge 2, I found the bass artificial and the overall sound unnatural. So I returned it and purchased the SRSX5.

The SRSX5 is a delight. The sound is great to my ears even at low volume, pure and natural with a smooth, well balanced sound with bass that is strong but not overpowering. I also like the shape and size of the SRSX5. Fits nicely in a pretty small space being about 8 inches long. As other reviews mention the top surface where the controls are is a fingerprint magnet. But I don't plan on staring at the top while I'm listening so it doesn't bother me.

Another non-feature on the SRSX5 I like compared to the Charge 2 is that the volume control of the SRSX5 does not sync to my iPhone volume. With the Charge 2 the volume control was coupled to the iPhone volume control. Seemed like an OK idea at first but made it impossible to fine tune the listening level on The Charge 2. I was basically stuck with the relatively course level changes of Charge 2. The SRSX5 does not link the two levels so it's possible to fine tune the level by seperately adjusting the volume on the iPhone and the speaker.

I can't think of anything that would cause me to recommend the Charge 2 over the SRSX5 other than perhaps battery life. The Charge 2 is rated at 12 hours and the SRSX5 at 8. Eight hours is quite sufficient for my use. Overall, there is no contest between the SRSX5 and Charge 2 in my mind. The SRSX5 is the clear winner.

Read a ton of reviews and decided to give these a try, and I'm happy with them. The isolation is pretty impressive, due in part to the pointed tips and angled earbuds, and the sound quality is good. No one is going to recommend these for in-ear monitoring or anything, but for podcasts and music on my morning commute they're great. The cable noise is a bit excessive, but for the price I would highly recommend them.

product_title: Philips BT2200/27 Bluetooth Wireless Portable Speaker with Built-in Microphone and Rechargeable Battery
review_headline: Tiny speaker with good sound and easy setup.
review_body:
My speaker came fully charged and ready to go. Setup was simple - pressing the call button to activate the speaker and then selecting the Philips option in my iPad settings. - It was recognized right away.
The sound is quite good for such a tiny (It fits easily in the palm of my hand, or the pocket of my sports jacket) speaker. Its not super loud, but it is very clear and distortion free. At the highest setting it fills a decent size room with sound, but doesn't overwhelm it. I suspect it would be less impressive in a room filled with people - not for big dance parties! But for casual home listening, its fantastic.
I like to play music as I'm falling asleep. This speaker is the perfect unit for that. I can set it on the bed, loud enough to hear clearly, but sound doesn't penetrate walls to bug others in my home. Its so small that it fits nearly anywhere, including under my pillow.
One caution: despite promotional photos of the unit floating on water, the first warning printed in the instruction sheet is "do not use in water". There are several other cautions in the instruction sheet against using it in a damp environment. And although it looks like it would be fine outside on a rainy day, the cover for the connectors appears to be water resistant only - not waterproof. So I'd be hesitant to float it in the pool with me!
Even so, Philips has produced a fine and durable portable speaker.

product_title: Pioneer SP-SB03 Andrew Jones Speaker Base TV Audio System
review_body:
If you do not need a 5.1 system and your TV is on a stand or console and isn't over 50 lbs., this speaker base by Pioneer is a great choice.
I have a small apartment and my viewing is done mostly through Netflix. For music I listen to Pandora.
Movie soundtracks sound a little better than the music through Pandora. It seems to be tuned more towards the cinematic side than to musical transparency.
But don't get me wrong, the sound is very nice. Don't forget, this system was designed by Andrew Jones, who has designed $70,000 speakers for Pioneer. I was also surprised at the bass response supplied by 2 downfiring bass drivers built in to the bottom of the cabinet which is very solidly constructed. There are also bass ports at each of the rear corners. If you like to listen to electronic music or EDM you should not be disappointed by bass performance. Considering the size of the cabinet which is constructed of a very tasteful and solid black particle board the sound is quite amazing.

Lastly, considering the price, which was for me $200, it was a self-recommending purchase.

product_title: Aftershokz Bluez 2 Open Ear Wireless Stereo Headphones, AS500, Color: Black
review_headline: Great Headphones, BUT only if you need them!
review_body:
I'm a unique case.. I can't wear in-ear headphones/earbuds. I guess I have an irregular shaped ear or something, because up until now every in-ear headphone I have bought has either hurt my ear (cartilage) to the point where it was absolutely unbearable, OR if I found a semi-comfortable set they would simply fall out while jogging.

These are the most comfortable non full-sized headphone I have ever tried. Other then a slight pinch of your temple, it feels like you have nothing on your head. Obviously while they are turned off or paused, you can hear everything, but as soon as you start playing music, you can still hear the outside world somewhat well, but the music kind of drowns it out. Police and ambulance sirens you can hear perfectly well. Holding a conversation while listening to music not so much.

CAVEAT!
If you do not need bone conduction headphones, DO NOT BUY bone conduction headphones!!! Unless your a cyclist, a city jogger or have a an odd shaped ear cavity, then don't buy these. They kind of sound like sh*t to be honest. Compared to a good set of earbuds and even compared to even a crappy pair of full sized cans, these sound terrible, all bone conducting headphones do...

For me though, the benefit of having an extremely well fitting headphone for the duration of my 1 hour workout, greatly outweighs the lousy sound quality I have to endure. All other occasions I'll stick to my MDR-7506 (w/ Beyerdynamic velour earcups) and enjoy unmatched comfort and sound quality.

You need to make the same call. Personally, I'm super happy with my purchase.

product_title: SONOS BRIDGE for Sonos Wireless Network (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Reduces attenuation and creates the surround setup required for Playbar
review_body:
I purchased a Bridge because I had an issue where an iPad streaming Netflix while listening to music would sometimes cause dropped packets. The music would go out and it was very frustrating. Adding the Bridge stopped that issue from occurring due to the dedicated network for the Sonos.

The other reason I bought it is because I was up to a handful of speakers including the full Playbar setup with the rear speakers (Play 1) and sub. In order to do the surround sound with that specific setup, you need the Bridge. I got it and setup was a snap.

One downside, and this may be a criticism of the Sonos system overall, is that it seems difficult to attach the sub to a separate speaker. I have a Play 5 floater and it would be nice to occasionally keep the sub rolling with only the Play 5 (wherever it is). You can't easily detach it without some hassle. Again, the setup itself is easy but it's not something I'd want to do if I were just moving stuff around. Think the equivalent of plugging speaker wires in...not hard but not something you want to repeat. So I guess I don't understand why it is so easy to attach groups of speakers together but the sub seems to fall outside of that.

review_headline: Love the Bluetooth...  Now I just kinda like it.
review_body: Love the Bluetooth, eliminating the wire to my iPhone.  I'm a daily runner (4 miles).  The ear buds are larger than what I'm use to, but still comfortable.  I found myself adjusting my old ear buds more so than the Beats.  Some reviews complain about the wire between the ear buds bothering them while running - I don't even realize they're connected, the wire doesn't bother me.  I give it 4 stars since for the brand & price, I was expecting superiod sound.  Don't get me wrong, the sound is good, but I was expecting to be blown away & I'm not.  Update:  Sadly, after only owning the headphones for less then 2 months they stopped working.  Went for my daily run, pushed the power button & nothing.  Although I knew I still had a charge left on my last run when I put them away, I charged them for most of the day.  Again, upon pushing the power button - nothing.  While charging, the red light was on indicating charging, but still wouldn't power on.    Jumped on line and found the complaints about the unit not powering on, etc.  Pulled Apples page & tried reseting the unit - while connected to power, hit the Power & Down Volume at the same time for 10 secs.  The unit still wouldn't power on.    I called Apple about the product since I was beyound the return period with Amazon, but still under the 1 year warranty with Apple.  The customer service with Apple was amazing - they took all my info, the product serial #, etc.  I received a Fed Ex box within 2 days for me to ship the unit back with my Amazon invoice for repair or replace.  I shipped the unit the same day & was able to tract the progress on line with Apple.  Apple received the unit the following day & sent me out a replacement unit - obviously didn't/couldn't fix my failed unit.  Happy that I have replacements that work, but concerned these too may fail.  Is the customer service at Apple just that good, or are they good from all the consumers that have called with a failed product?
