review_headline: Fancy and versatile battery charger. A review from a battery novice and eager learner.
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:20373ec10cff511ca8ce06386f2f9726]]2/20/16 I till like this charger but the two battery at a time thing is driving me crazy. I still use this to test voltage but rarely actually charge on this device.

I need a universal battery charger and quickly ordered this one without realizing it was so fancy: the LCD screen and plethora of strange numbers fascinated me. At first the only thing that made sense to me was the battery bar: it will take me awhile to really understand the rest of these numbers, but thanks to this charger I'm motivated to learn.

The battery basics [please comment if you can help because I am still pretty confused--I won't be offended, but thankful]
Volts: The volt reading tells you how full your batteries are: they are the GAS GAGE of your battery (apparently there are better measures, but volts is adequate for home use.
Milliampere (mAh): a measure of how much charge the battery can hold when full (SIZE OF GAS TANK in analogy)--the number on your battery is based on one hour but it changes depending on how much charge is required (how fast the car is going).

One of the things I dislike about rechargeable batteries is I never know how charged a battery is [i.e. I think I just charged this, but I can't remember, maybe it was the other one]. This solves charger solves this problem (and effectively charges the batteries.

In summary:
This is more than a universal battery charger. It chargers all the batteries cylinder-shaped rechargeable batteries you can imagine (I didn't even know they made an AAAA), but it can do so at home or in a car! I chose to let the video speak for the LCD screen as I am still learning what all those features mean.

I received this produce at a discount for my unbiased review and am happy I can sincerely recommend it to all of you. Enjoy!

product_title: Brainwavz M5 In Ear Earbuds Noise Isolating Earphones stereo Headphones
review_body: I have used earphones of all styles my entire life, but use in-ear noise blocking earphones to travel, sleep in a noisy unfamiliar environment, relax in bed at night and work in the yard with power equipment.  This is the first purchase of Brainwavz products, and I have to say I am pleasantly surprised.  I won't list all the features and included accessories since many other reviews have already done so.  I will say that I use the default tips (bi-flange) and they are as comfortable as any I have ever worn and they block more extraneous noise than any other similar earphones I have used.  But I will be VERY quick to say that these earphones are the clearest and have the best frequency response than any I have used exclusive of $600 earphones I have used in a recording studio.  At this price, I can't imagine better quality and sound reproduction.  My only modest complaint is the packaging --- specifically the plastic molded display the earphones are mounted on in the box.  The earpieces are imbedded in a depression with bulges that hold them in place.  When you first remove them from the packaging, you have to be REALLY careful to not pull on the wires leading to the earpieces as damage can easily occur.  It's best to gently push them from the bottom to release the "grip" and then grab the thick part of the bottom of each earpiece.  Update March 2017:  I had to buy a new pair of these earbuds.  I still like them, but the left bud stopped working when the wire leading into it developed a bad connection.  I don't know if I caused it, or if it was defective.  With this replacement purchase the seller e-mails me that the earphones have a 2-year warranty -- But the packaging says it has a 1-year warranty as did my original purchase in 2015.  Perhaps I could have gotten the replacement under warranty.  Don't know; too late.

review_body: I feel sorry for anyone who got taken for $43 for a $10 power supply you could have bought anywhere else with just a little bit of knowledge. For around $15 you could buy a universal wall wart that has several tip sizes and can be set for the proper voltage, which is probably 9volts, and that you can choose the polarity which is tip positive. But the fact that it's labeled as a medical healthcare accessory device they feel the need to really squeeze you for every penny they can. Despicable, shady and under-handed. It was probably assembled by a 10 year old Chinese girl at the cost of 25 cents. I would be willing to bet that it doesn't even say Health-O-Meter on it. If it does all that extra money you are paying is for the brand name printed on the label. There is nothing special about this power supply accept the price. I know this because I am a guitar playing musician. All guitar players are gear hounds. The foot switch effect pedals that we use are for the most part powered by 9 volt batteries unless you decide to spend the money on a multi channel isolated dc power supply to save on battery cost. There are a lot of different companies that make the same thing with different features. So take my word for it and get a universal wall wart, I promise it will work just fine. A member of the Geek squad at Best Buy would be able to help you making the correct purchase.

product_title: Sound Intone HD200 Stereo Lightweight Folding Headsets with Microphone,Kids Headphones,Girl Headphones,Boys Headphones,Stretchable Headband,Control Button,,Great Heavy Bass,with Soft Earpad Earphones for Iphone,All Android Smartphones,Pc,Laptop,Mp3/mp4,Tablet Earpieces
review_headline: About as good as sound gets under $20; build is lightweight and not likely to be durable
review_body:
First things first, I received these headphones free for the purpose of review. I'm hoping that my observations and impressions prove helpful to you in your decision making. If you have questions, feel free to post them in the comments section and I'll do my best to answer based on my own experience with the headphones.

What you're getting with this order:
(1) pair HD200 headphones

What these are: A pair of wired headphones compatible with any device with a 3.5mm jack. An inline mic with a couple of remote functions is present. As of the posting of this review, these headphones are being offered at the lower end of the budget price point.

Ok, the most important thing to realize about these is that they're quite cheap and yet they deliver a very impressive sound for the budget price point. So, why are they so inexpensive? It seems to me that they've invested in the speakers, and saved costs on the build. I've tested these pretty thoroughly and have the following observations to share:

Build: The build is lightweight and not likely to be very durable. This is most apparent where the headband meets the cans. They've used a cheap plastic and painted it silver too look like metal and at first glance it really does look nice. Not everything about the build is cheap. The headband has no padding, but does have a silicone coating on the underside that helps a bit. It features a hinge that allows you to fold the headphones flat which I wouldn't expect to see at this price point. The cans have a lightweight plastic housing but they do have a nicely padded faux leather earpiece and speakers are covered with black cloth which does look nice. Overall, they've done a great job making the build look much nicer than it is. If you're someone who takes good care of your equipment, these might look nice for a long time. For those who give their headphones a pretty good workover, expect paint to chip and peel and know that the housing is fragile.

Appearance: I'll just reiterate that they've done a great job of making a very cheap build appear to be of much higher quality. The black, red and silver look very nice together and the black braided cord adds to the appearance.

Sound: This is where the HD200 really surprises. Sound is consistent with headphones that approach the mid-range price point. There is no distortion at max volumes and there is a nice crispness throughout all the ranges. I tested them at audiocheck.net and got the following results:

Frequency response: 20Hz-20kHz
Quality: No parasitic rattle or buzz when drivers are stressed
Wiring: Headset is properly wired.
Polarity: Polarity is preserved.

Anything else of note?: As of the posting of this review, these headphones are eligible for free shipping to members of Amazon Prime; always a bonus to me.

Any negatives?: It's all relative to price point, so it's important to remember we're talking about spending $19 here. The build is underwhelming and though the paint job looks nice now, I have my doubts about durability. At this price, I am always at least worried about wiring, but mine tested out pretty nicely, including the mic. Just know that the attachment of the headphones to the cans and then the cans themselves are of a very lightweight build with a cheap material. I will give them credit for making these 2 parts look much nicer than they are.

I would like to have seen a user's guide. There are no instructions for using the mic controls on the cord (only a pic on the box).

Bottom line: These would get 3 stars from me except that the HD200 provides perhaps the best sound I've run across in headphones priced under $20. They are of a lightweight build and thus of questionable durability, but real effort has gone into at least making the cheap build look attractive, even adding features like a fold flat hinge and braided cord. Ilike them for their surprising sound, and have no problem recommending them to anyone looking to maximize sound quality in the budget price range, as long as the risk of shortcomings in build are understood.dget price range, as long as the risk of shortcomings in build are understood.

review_headline: Orbtronic NCR 18650 Li-Ion Rechargeable Battery - 2 pack - 3100mAh - 3.7V - Recommended
review_body:
These Orbtronic I-NCR 18650 Li-Ion Rechargeable Batteries have been working well in the lights (tactical style LED torches) that we have been using them in. Those lights have low to moderate draw, and are acceptable use for these style batteries, and I would recommend these batteries to others for such use, based on our experience.

The materials note that the core of these are Panasonic NCR18650A cells, with protective drain and overcharge protection circuits from Seiko added. Total quality build. As others have noted, these do seem a bit longer than other 18650 batteries we have, but they do work in the lights that we have tried them in... and they do seem to work very well, both by providing a strong current (producing a bright light) and by holding a very good capacity. Bright lights that stay on longer = good stuff.

We have charged these batteries with two different chargers, Foxnovo's intelligent charger and a similar one made by Nitecore, and have had no charging issues at all. While all batteries warm up a bit while charging, we did not notice any excess heat build-up from these batteries during the charging process or during use.

Neither the Amazon listing or the retail material notes information on a warranty, so if an issue occurs within a reasonable period (say within one year) I would return here to update the review and let you know what the issue was and how resolution was handled. We received these batteries gratis from the seller and put them to use to objectively find out how well they performed. My statements here reflect that testing.

If you are looking for quality 18650 batteries of this style, capacity, price and size, then we would recommend these Orbtronics 18650 batteries based on our experience with them.

Recommended.

Go for it.

review_body:
I purchased this item directly from CCrane, but thought I'd post the review here as well.

Overall, I'm pleased with the product. I had some issues getting batteries to work in it. Thinking I had dead batteries, I bought more... still no luck. Then by accident, I bumped the far right battery and it slide in a bit more. I guess it just wasn't making contact on that side until I jostled it into place a bit. The AC adapter generates quite a bit of noise, so that's a bit disappointing. On FM, dial calibration is way off...a little over 1 MHz, while on AM, it's only off maybe 20 kHz. At the same time, it pulls in EVERY FM station possible from my location... simply outstanding. AM pulls in a lot. At my location today, I was able to hear about 50８f the available stations listenable from my location. This is on par with my SR II... not too shabby.

Overall, with the exception of the AC adapter, the quirky battery compartment, and the FM calibration, I'm pleased. Not having those issues would be great, but the performance more than makes up for those shortcomings.

product_title: Polk Audio Omni S2 Compact Wireless Wi-Fi Music Streaming Speaker with Play-Fi
review_headline: Great idea, but not ready yet...
review_body: PlayFi technology still needs some maturing to do. It works well (when you get it to work) and the sound is great (much better than the best Bluetooth), but it has many hiccups and idiosyncrasies that need to be worked out. It got it to work rather quickly and got off to a good, very excited, start...until it stopped working. It developed a knack for interspersing sound pauses here and there; sometimes one or two--or more--every minute. A couple of times it disappeared from the network until it finally disappeared for good and could not ever be install again. The application would not even "see" it. Bear in mind that the device was working fine a few hours before this and I went through all the usual router and device re-starts, etc., etc. I called customer service a few times and spent a couple of hours with them on the phone trying everything they/me could think of. Finally they told me to send it back for a replacement, which I did, only to have a whole bunch of similar (but slightly different) set of issues. I just do not have the time to spend (perhaps days) to wade through all these issues, so I sent it back for a refund. The unit itself seemed sturdy and well built, and I think the blame is in evolving standards and mismatches between routers, WiFi, and PlayFi protocols, as well as the apps that PA (and other PlayFi vendors) provide (by the way, they all seem to use the same app with custom skins for each manufacturer). I can see (and hope) that in a year or so these issues will be sorted out and that these devices will come into its own as a great solution to good quality networked music.

product_title: Monoprice 4X2 True Matrix HDMI Switch w/ Remote (Rev. 3.0)
review_body:
After about four full months of usage, I feel I have gotten a clear understanding of just how good this product is. After seeing other similar products with significantly higher prices, I gave Monoprice a chance because of the previous history I have with the brand. The product is working perfectly fine and hasn't given me any major problems. I use it with a Sharp 70" and a Sony 42" which I frequently use simultaneously (usually for sports/gaming). After my time with the switch, I have noticed both of these pros and cons...

Pros:
- Easy to use/setup
- Works with Home Theater Systems
- Comes with remote control for convenience when switching input/outputs

Cons:
- Bright LEDs on device light up any room, so you can't leave it on overnight (not good for bedroom usage)
- Remote, while it is convenient, only works when pointed within a very small angle of the device
- Changing the input to one TV sometimes causes the other TV to black out while the change is made (3-5 seconds)
- About 2-3 times I have had to power cycle the switch because one TV will be stuck on a static screen after switching inputs

None of these cons are deal breaking, and are nothing more than just a minor nuisance when they occur. Despite them, I am fully satisfied with this switch as it does what I need. I am not giving it more than three stars because it does not work excellently, as a result of some of the flaws. If the remote worked from wider angles, and the input change were a bit faster then I would probably give it 4 stars. While satisfied, I am definitely not blown away as I have received just what is needed and not much more. If you don't want to spend north of $100, this is a good purchase.

product_title: Sony ICF-C707 Clock Radio with AM/FM Dual Alarm and Large Easy to Read Backlit LCD Display
review_body:
The clock radio that I had since maybe the eighties or nineties finally bit the dust. I needed a new one but I wanted to make sure it had a few specific features. I found this clock at a local electronics store and it seemed to fit the bill, for the most part, at the time. It needed to have the following:

- AM/FM radio... check

- Dedicated buttons for features instead of multifunction buttons... check

- A dual alarm... check

- A gentle sounding alarm (vs. a harsh buzzer sound) or an alternative alarm... check (I think...I've been using the radio alarm so not sure what the buzzer sounds like.)

- A small footprint so it wouldn't take up too much space on my small bedside table... check.

So if the clock seemed to meet my needs as listed above, why the lower rating? Because, as many other reviewers have pointed out... this clock is horribly designed. I don't know what they were thinking when they designed this. Here's my laundry list of whadafuq were you thinking Sony?

- The radio tuner is a small bar-type button located on the back of radio. Seriously? The only more awkward place for it is on the bottom and thank gawd they didn't do that. There is also no fine tuning and a station that I normally had no problem receiving in the past with my old clock radio does not come in well at all on this one.

- The buttons are very small and impossible to locate in the dark as there is no backlighting at all to see which button does what and they are mostly all the same size.

- The clock display (one of my biggest issues with this clock) comes in bright blue with faded black letters, subdued blue with faded black letters, or gray with faded black letters. It does not provide enough contrast. The blue looked pretty in the store but in actual use, it is incredibly hard to read from more than a few feet. Even in bed only a couple feet away it does not stand out well. I've also experienced a very strange phenomena. When I first wake up in the morning and look at the clock, it actually looks blank for one or two seconds before the numbers start to appear. It is so freaking weird! I assume it is a combination of the clock display colors and my eyes adjusting as I wake up but this never ever happened to me with my old clock radio or any other digital clock I've used. It happens consistently and is actually becoming quite annoying.

- Setting the clock feels like a complicated process and I have to refer to the directions every time. Luckily, I haven't had to do it that often.

- The sound is not the best. I didn't expect Bose quality sound but for a Sony product (and the price I paid) I did expect better.

- This unit comes with nature sounds which I tested out briefly, but I was not impressed with them. The quality was not good and some of them sounded too similar. I actually don't use the nature sounds and never intended to when I bought it so it's not that big an issue for me. They just happened to come with this model. Sometimes I hit these buttons by mistake when I'm groping around in the dark trying to find the right button to turn the radio off/on. It is rather annoying.

Some features that I do like:

- The alarm can be set for weekdays only. It will automatically turn off on the weekend and then back on again for Monday thru Friday.

- I use the radio alarm which is something I could never have done before because I go to sleep with the radio on low and it probably wouldn't wake me up, BUT I can set the volume of the radio alarm to be louder than the radio I go to sleep with so I can wake up to music instead of a buzzer. This is why I don't even know what the buzzer sounds like. If I try it someday I'll come back and edit the review to make note of whether it is an annoying one or not. The only downside to the radio alarm volume is that I have to turn it down every morningas it will stay loud instead of going back to the lower volume level.

- There is actually an indoor temperature reading on the radio which is a nice extra. There is a wire with a temperature gauge on the end that comes out the back of the unit.

So though this clock fulfills the basic alarm and music requirements I need, I think the human factor design is poor and it's a bit pricey for what I ended up with. And the magically invisible clock display in the morning is getting on my last nerve. I don't know how much longer I will use this clock. I may look for something else, but now that I have this clock to use for now, I can be more careful shopping for one that has the features I need and the annoyances I don't need. I will also be wary of any blue/black clock displays. Unfortunately, I am also starting to become wary of Sony products in general due to some other disappointing Sony purchases.

product_title: Omicron TURENO HDTV Speaker subwoofer
review_body:
I agree with the others who have posted here. If your budget maxes out at $100 bucks, then this is the sub to get. Yes, Five out of Five stars in its category. Sure, it's not a $1600 digitally-driven Velodyne, but by gosh and by golly this little sub still has the potential to put a big smile on your face.

I have it paired with a set of Andrew Jones bookshelf speakers (another great value) and my old NAD amplifier (via the high-level speaker in/outs) and it sits near the front right corner in my bsmnt workshop. Note: if you're not getting the sound you're expecting out of your subwoofer, then the first thing to do is to adjust its position. After that, fine tune the crossover (in your receiver if you're hooked to the LFE out), and finally the volume.

Oh, if you're hearing a little rattling coming from the sub at high output levels, check the front grille. Mine buzzes when pushed hard, so I just permanently removed it.

I play mostly music through this little setup (as it's in my workshop, and I don't want to cut my thumb off :-) ), but I did hook the sub up (solo) to my 7.2 Home Theater system for a while to test it with movies (two of my favorite scenes are the opening battle engagement in Master & Commander: FSOTW, and also the Limo/Plane escape scene in 2012. Yowza!). I must say that this little 10" did a pretty passable job (best in a corner again), but admittedly in a 600 sq ft room it didn't have the output to match the pair of 12" PSW505's that I normally have hooked to my HT system. I think the PSW10 would do well in a smaller room though.

As far as music is concerned, I've really come to enjoy it for what it is (I certainly had my doubts when ordering though, given the lower specs than what I'm used to). But it seems to handle everything I've thrown at it very nicely, from Gaga's pounding monster beat in "Marry the Night - Zed remix" to her very visceral track "Teeth" Wow!!! Onto Al DiMeola's sizzling guitar in "Splendido Hotel" and the electronic mastery of Jean Michel Jarre's "Concerts in China."

How about Trance - you'll just love Infected Mushroom's "Army of Mushrooms," or Cosmic Gate's "Earth Mover" when played through a sub. Or remember Disco? (yes that kinda dates me, hehe!) Santa Esmeralda "Don't Let Me Be Misunderstood" is IMHO one of the best dance LPs ever produced. Note: keep in mind that your speakers and esp your amp have to be up to the task as well :-)

Rock, Pop, Country, Easy Listening etc aren't generally as demanding of a sub as some of the music I've mentioned, but yes this sub reproduces it all with some pretty good authority (remember, move the sub if it's just not cutting it, and re-check your phase all around!). This sub is the real thing and it should thump pretty darn hard for you.

Yet the PSW10 is still accurate and mellow enough for Yo-Yo Ma's cello, or Rodrigo y Gabriela's wonderful dueling acoustic guitars in "9 Dead Alive." And if you really want a good test, check out Sheffield Lab's "Drum and Track Disk." You will not be disappointed. I played it again today, and I'm STILL smiling. :-) :-) :-)

Good luck, and happy listening! J&H

product_title: Xtreme Signal HDB8X 8-Bay VHF/UHF HDTV Bowtie Antenna
review_body: I bought this unit based on other reviews.  We installed it at my brother's rural home outside Lumberton, NC.  The nearest TV stations are not close, but this antenna brought in stations from as far away as Raleigh, NC and Florence, SC, which are respectively 90 miles and 55 miles away.  We had to play with the configuration.  The antenna has two "wings" which may be configured flat or at an angle to each other.  We tried it in both configurations, and used a compass to point it at the stations we were after.  In flat mode, it pulled in stations from farther away, but it eliminated some stations "to the side."  So we ended up with the antenna in a "V" configuration.  We mounted the antenna on a metal antenna pole, with ground wire.  After a couple of days of messing with it (gradually rotating it with someone outside manipulating the antenna and someone inside testing the channels) we now get 33 channels.  Not every single channel is rock solid (I'm guessing weather conditions impact the reception).  But most of them are reliably watchable and clear.  Since everything is broadcast in digital, there is none of the old "snowy" channels.  They either come in or they don't.  If the signal is weak, some channels will start to pixelate, and you may get a message that says "weak signal."  But in our experience, that's the exception.  We were astounded with how many channels this unit picks up given its reasonable price.  My brother who is retired and doesn't feel he can afford cable or satellite, is in heaven.  He has multiple news sources, PBS, weather,  and all the major networks.  Keep in mind, this is not an indoor unit, although you could probably put it in your attic.  It's fairly large and has to be properly mounted, but once you get it set up, it will do the job.

product_title: Audio Technica AT-LP1240-USB Direct Drive DJ Turntable
review_headline: Very nice, for the most part.
review_body:
I bought this to replace a Pro-Ject Debut Carbon (don't ask).

Overall, for the price, this AT unit is a really nice turntable. The finish is great, the tonearm seems well-crafted and precise, and the onboard pre-amp seems dead quiet.

My biggest gripe about this turntable is the strobe. Platter strobes normally come in 2 configurations for 33-1/3 rpm: 180-dot, for regions with 50Hz power line frequency, like Europe, and 216-dot, for regions with 60Hz power line frequency, like the US. I live in the US, but the platter on my deck has 180 dots.

I'm assuming that Hanpin didn't feel like making a 216-dot platter, but, instead, wanted to universalize the 180-dot one, to save on production costs. To this end, I'm guessing Hanpin finagled the electronics in this turntable so that the 180-dot platter would work, more or less, in the US. 33-1/3 rpm isn't QUITE dead-on by the platter strobe on my turntable (though quartz-lock is dead-on, judging by my KAB Strobedisc).

This isn't what I'd call a huge deal, but it's annoying. It would have been nice if Hanpin and Audio-Technica had managed to produce an honest-to-God 216-dot platter to work in America where, no doubt, a lot of these 1240's are sold. So, if for some reason, you decide to disconnect the quartz lock on your 1240 and you live in the US, you'll probably want to get a separate strobe disc to calibrate the platter speed.

Addendum: After playing with this turntable for a few weeks, I've concluded that the turntable strobe light isn't quartz-locked, unlike the strobe light on a Technics 1200. The AT strobe light is on a much less sophisticated electrical circuit than the one that regulates platter speed. So the dots wander a bit, even in quartz-lock speed mode. The Pioneer PLX-1000 is the same way, because I checked it myself.

It looks like the strobe lights on Super OEM turntables are little more than glorified power lights, given their lack of precision. If you like pretty, illuminated dots, knock yourself out. Just don't use the platter strobe to judge turntable speed, because it's misleading. If you want an accurate strobe system for your AT deck, you'll have to invest in something like a KAB Strobedisc.

I should add that after doing lots and lots of tests, I've concluded that the platter speed regulation in quartz-lock mode is, indeed, dead on. The turntable strobe system is pretty crude, but the rest of the turntable is not. The one caveat is that the turntable locks at exactly 78rpm, so you'll need a separate strobe system to bring it up to broadcast speed. All Super OEM decks probably have the same issue, I'm guessing because of some need to round off the rpm's to accommodate speed regulation.

For instance if I get non MP3 books can I link them to play one after another? Probably, more learning. The reason this only gets 4 stars is the lack of instructions.
Update own it 1 1/2 years, bought it for $ 60 what a buy.
Yes you can set up your own playlist. Create a folder on your device and load it with your songs. Then you can select that folder and it will play all songs in that folder. Id raise this to 5 stars but thats because I love it. But Its hard to get to know how to handle it, if your a senior, and its hard to make random selections. Great for books which is my thing.

product_title: SanDisk  Clip Jam MP3 Player
review_headline: Early problems fixed, but it broke early
review_body: I've been using the Sansa Clip+ for years, mostly while running.  I love the Clip, but for the same price I decided to try the Clip Sport because of the longer battery life, and hoping that the Clip+ problems with the headphone jack connection going bad is fixed.  I read the reviews, and noticed that many of the bad reviews are due to albums not playing in order, and difficulty in making playlists.  Newer reviews reported them fixed, and sure enough the player does read the tags to play albums by track number now, and I had no problems making my own playlists, with the limitation that songs must all be in the same directory, which is also where the .m3u playlist file must be.  I played with this some and looked at the .m3u file in notepad, and found if there is any \subdirectory\ preceding the track file name, any entries after that track do not show up in the playlist on the Clip Sport.  The drawback to this is if you want to put a whole album on the player in it's own directory, but include a track or two in the playlist, you have to make a copy of those tracks and move it to the directory with your playlists.  You'll also want to remove that track from the album directory, otherwise the player will find it twice when you are playing the album.  btw, the playlist does not have to have the same name as the directory as I've seen stated somewhere, and in fact you can have multiple playlists in a directory.  The size is a bit larger and heavier than the Clip+ but not too noticeably.  I love clipping the player to my waistband or fuel belt rather than having to tuck a non-clip player in a pocket where you don't have access to the controls.  The basic buttons (volume, << and >> mainly) seem easy to find and use without looking.  Navigation isn't always intuitive as it can be confusing as to when to hit the raised "arrow back" button and when to hit <<, but this is mostly in the menus as I'm setting it up and playing with it.  I'm prettysure I won't have a problem when sticking to the normal operations for just listening to music.  You can customize the player to remove main menu items you may not want to use, such as Podcasts, Radio, Sports (stopwatch), if all you want to do is listen to music.  Nice way to unclutter the player.  However, they went and cluttered up the music playlist menu with not just 1, but 3 GoLists that always show up on top and apparently can't be removed.  It's an irritation to have to navigate past them.  I'd really like to be able to hit playlist and then select my main playlist without any scrolling.  I don't run with my reading glasses and it's not convenient to try to watch and read whether I've scrolled to the playlist I want.  The single GoList in the Clip+ was annoying, 3 of them is ridiculous.  I'm sure some people use them but they should have a way to remove them for those that don't.  To me this is like having radio presets, but in addition to  your favorites there are 3 that are set to static that you have to pass through to get to your stations.  Speaking of radio presets, like the Clip+ you have to navigate a few screens to see and select them.  No way that I can see to just use the arrow keys to jump between presets.  Annoying, but I don't use the radio much.  The sound seems fine.  I don't have a keen ear for music so I can't judge well.  Swapping between the players, the Clip+ sounds just a bit better to me, but I can't explain why.  It's not enough of a difference to be a factor.  I find the screen easier to read than the clip+ because the letters are larger, but I haven't had it in bright sun yet.  They did add a lock button (holding the back arrow button for 2 seconds) but that doesn't affect the power button.  I really only want a lock button to prevent it from accidentally turning on and draining while I'm not using it.  You do have to hold the power button for a couple seconds to turn it off or on so maybe that'll be good enough.  If the battery lifeis as good as promised and doesn't start to halve over time like some of my clip+'s did, and the headphone jack connection stays good (clip+ had a soldering weakness), I'll be happier with the Clip Sport than the Clip+.  Otherwise it'll be just a touch behind the clip+ because of the larger size and weight, plus my GoLists issue.  I'll update this as I use it more.  Update:  It basically broke a few months ago.  I can't remember if I dropped it or left it in the sun or crushed it or if it broke on its own, but there is a blob in the lower left, and the only buttons that work let me switch between music, radio, and settings, but won't let me into any of those options.  The screen isn't cracked so I don't think I was too rough on it.  It's worthless now.  Lowered from 4* to 2* due to lack of durability, especially something intended for active use. Too bad, as I was pretty happy with it.

review_headline: If you can’t HEAR from this speaker, you’re DEAF
review_body:
The BLUBOON is a very loud shower speaker, but is BLUBOON the real manufacturer? Details inside.

▶ Package Contents
• Speaker
• USB Cable
• Hook
• Instruction Manual

▶ Specifications
• Input: DC 5V/600mA
• Output: 5W THD+N <10% (1kHz/0dB)
• Battery Capacity: 3.7V/500mAh
• Speaker Response: 45mm 4 Ohms/5W
• Weight: 152g
• Frequency Range: 120Hz – 20kHz
• S/N: =>90dB
• Product Size: W87*D45*95mm

▶ Hardware & Testing
The BLUBOON speaker is a 3.4” x 1.8” x 3.7” Bluetooth 3.0 speaker, approximately the same size of the palm of your hand. The speaker is unique because it is IP65 waterproof – the rating given for an item that is dust and splash proof, but not submergible in water.

The first thing you notice when you see the package is how generic the packaging is. All it says is “Bluetooth Speaker”. It’s so generic that you could slap a sticker with your branding – in fact that is what BLUBOON did. They literally put a clear sticker that says BLUBOON.

I really like this waterproof Bluetooth speaker, because it doesn’t actually look like a shower speaker. Instead, it looks like a durable miniature outdoor speaker – something perfect for camping.

The speaker is made of a combination of hard plastic and a rubber trim– a design choice I really like. On top is the speaker grill, with the “Bluetooth” name. On the rubber trim are four buttons: play/answer, volume up/next track, volume down/previous track, and power/Bluetooth pairing. On the back is the clear 3” x 3” suction cup. Overall, the design is simple and isn’t intrusive.

Pairing is very simple. As soon as you turn on the device, it is set to pairing. If you are still attempting to pair, pressing the power button for a few seconds isn’t very difficult. You are then introduced to a monotone female voice that will let you know that you’ve paired.

I’ve used this speaker for about two days now, while I showering and general use. The first thing I have to tell you is this speaker’s LOUDNESS. Very loud. Did I say it was loud? You really don’t expect it from this little thing. The speaker has the typical low bass you’d hear within the music, but not any real bass beyond that. Though, you probably aren’t focusing on acoustics while you are showering. The suction cup was powerful enough to last two whole days on my shower’s window, but I don’t know beyond that. Also, the speaker’s buttons were very responsive. I had absolutely no problems with it.

▶ Final Thoughts
The only thing I have a problem with this speaker is the branding – there is none. A sticker was literally slapped on the front to name is BLUBOON. I mean, what is stopping me for looking for another manufacturer that carries the same product, at a cheaper price? None, none at all. That being said, I like this speaker a lot.

5 stars

Pros:
+ Very loud.
+ Strong suction cup
+ Sleek design.
+ Very responsive buttons.

Cons:
- Completely generic branding
- No real bass

product_title: SOLEMEMO C1 Portable Wireless Bluetooth Speaker with 10 Hour Playtime and 30 Days Standby Time,nfc Compatibility and Full, High-Def Sound (Black)
review_headline: A Solid Brick of Good Musical Value!
review_body:
There are thousands of Bluetooth speakers on the market - I have used a good many of them and found most of them to be 'average,' some a waste of money and just a few to be exceptional in one way or another. I am pleased to report that this new C1 from SOLEMEMO is one of those in the third category!

This is a solid-brick of long-lasting, nice fidelity and portable sound!

It's workings are compact. For its size, it is quite heavy (about 2 pounds) and, I must say, a great deal of really good stuff seems to have been jammed into this brick. Of course, one does not expect concert-hall sound from a portable speaker - but, this C1 delivers a full range of sound (though slightly weaker at the deeper bass end of the sound spectrum.) I noticed this only when listening indoors, with no ambient sounds whatever, to some classical pieces with deep and continuing low bass lines. I doubt that the casual home listener would even notice the fact that the high and mid-range sounds come through with a slightly higher level of 'genuiness.')

The electronics operate exactly as advertised in pairing/Bluetooth 4.0/NFC response and controls and the battery-life of 10 play-hours is, as most will recognize, quite unusual and outstanding for a full day (or long night) of music listening. Many Bluetooth speakers would benefit from having an AC option because the playing life fades after 4-6 hours. Not necessary here. The fact that it reaches a full charge in just over 2-hours via an (included) USB cable is an added bonus for those of us who have become annoyed by how long some other Bluetooth speakers take to charge and does it with a standard (and NOT a ridiculously 'proprietary) USB-mini-USB cable.

At this price point, one reasonably expects adequacy. With this SOLEMEMO C1, you get a good deal more.

product_title: Denon Music Maniac On-Ear Headphones BLACK
review_headline: Small, Portable Denon Music Maniac Headphones Offer Big Sound
review_body: The first thing you notice about the Denon AH-MM200BK Music Maniac On Ear Headphones is the size. These headphones are small and light, and totally designed for portable use.  They fit comfortably on my head and are very light, barely noticeable even for long periods of time. These are on-ear (not over-the-ear) headphones, so they do a decent job of reducing or blocking external noise. I had them on while walking through downtown San Francisco and did not hear any external sounds. I did hear the noise of the trains when entering the BART station but the headphones do a decent job of passively reducing noise.  From a sound perspective the Denon AH-MM200BKs are advertised as being professionally tuned for a flat equalizer response that delivers a neutral listening experience. To my ears the headphones do deliver a relatively flat response with very good detail. Listening to Blood Sweat & Tears second album right now and hearing very clearly the thump of the bass and drums, clear piano, and good natural sound from the horns. I also tested these headphones with music from The Brian Setzer Orchestra, Dave Brubeck, Ella Fitzgerald, and classical music. Burn-in time so far has been about 15 hours.  The headphones have 30mm drivers. Larger drivers tend to produce lower frequencies (bass) better as they push more air. Smaller drivers are better at creating higher frequency sounds as they can move faster. Although the drivers are relatively large (given the small size of the headphone) the highs don't seem to suffer.  Denon provides two 2 detachable oxygen-free copper cables with gold plated connectors. One cable has remote function buttons for iOS devices. They also provide a travel bag (not a hard case) and the earcups fold-in for travel.  Denon also has music player apps available in both iTunes and Google Play. I downloaded the app and it offers a decent listening experience (with an equalizer with presets as well as the ability to tailor your own preset) but it is not needed for these headphones and does not add anything extra, although it is an improvement over the stock equalizer available on iOS devices.  Overall, I like these headphones a lot. They are small yet deliver big sound with good detail. They appear to be well-made and are comfortable, but I am not sure how they will hold up with daily use, especially without a hard travel case. Still, the Denon's provide optimal sound in a relatively small, travel-friendly package. Highly recommended.

I reluctantly ordered these earphones, because to me, they seemed "too good to be "true". But after reading the reviews, which by far seemed more good to me than bad, I took a chance and ordered a set. The first thing I noticed upon opening the package they came in, was that though they do have the much discussed braided cord up to the "Y" part of where the headphone wires part from the main cord, beyond there,again, and up to the ear buds, the wires are not braided. I probably would have passed on ordering them had I known that. But then in the end, that would have been my loss! Because even though the wires of the headphone part are not braided, still they are not nearly so wimpy as "Scullcandy" and some of those other brands are. So after evaluating them a moment, and then being at first somewhat disappointing because of the partly braided cable issue, I tried them out.
And WOW!!! These little babies are by far the best sounding ear buds I have ever owned! And trust me, that probably covers a couple of dozen sets in the past 10 years ! I don't buy super expensive headphone sets, but I figure for 25 bucks, you should be able to get a descent set. Usually they fail after just a short time though. So I probably could have bought a quality 200 dollar set for all of the less expensive ones I have bought over the years! And I am sure I am not alone by any means in this repeating and frustrating cycle. But that is a "catch 22" and it is indeed another story altogether. Therefore we won't go there now.
So back to these ear buds. First of all after plugging them into my phone and into my ears. and then cranking up some music, I noticed how easy the sound was on my ears. The sound is just - well - comfortable! And so is the fit! Usually I am constantly fighting with having to poke the seemingly slippery, crawling out on my ears, ear buds back into my ears, (No matter which size rubber tips I put on them) But not with these! They sit snugly, but not too tightly. And they feel as light as a feather to wear as well!
But the most compelling aspect of them to me is the dynamic response I get when using the equalizer feature on my music player. All of the previous earphones I have had since getting my new smartphone, have had a very sluggish and not a very perceptible response to the EQ settings I constaly am trying. But with this set, Man O Man! When I move any of the 5 sliders on the equalizer just a little, I hear a distinct and a sharp change in the sound! So instead of having to fiddle with the EQ settings for 20 or 15 minutes and still getting no satisfaction, with these little jewels it took me only a moment or two to find my "just right" setting! Also from listening to these earphones, I suspect the elements are of a very high quality. So maybe one of the ear buds of the two won't just suddenly die or fail in a month or two, like has happened to me with the last 2 or three ear bud sets I have had in the past year or so.
If I had four thumbs, I would give these great little ear buds all 4 of my thumbs up! But as it is, I suppose my two thumbs, hoisted to as high up as my 6 feet 1 inch body can get them, will have to suffice.

I'm learning that I am an audiophile, though not the most educated one out there and I love what polk has to offer for performance and price. For those looking for a better deal and hard to find discontinued items polk audio has an eBay store that sells refurbished items at a substantially reduced price. review_body:

product_title: Cheetah Mounts APSAMB 32-65" LCD TV Wall Mount Bracket with Full Motion Swing Out Tilt & Swivel Articulating Arm for Flat Screen Flat Panel LCD LED Plasma TV and Monitor Displays Includes Free 10' Braided High Speed HDMI Cable With Ethernet
review_headline: DO NOT BELIEVE THE WEIGHT RATING...
review_body: DO NOT BELIEVE THE WEIGHT RATING...  I have a 60LB5900 which is 50.7 lbs (ie 114.3 lbs less then this mount is rated for).. This mount bends under the weight to the point that the arms do not keep straight even when it is all the way flush against the wall (the single arm is bending & pushing against the lower arm). This product is extremely under engineered..  Installation was what I was expecting. It was not difficult to assemble or to mount the plate level, though the curving of the plate (intentional per the instructions) puts way more pressure on the wall then it should in the center far away from where the bolts are (studs are 24" on center on this particular wall). There is approximately 1/2" of curve so when attaching this to the wall the center of the wall is pushed back about 1/4" which is ridiculous and not necessary.  Also it would appear that there has been a change in product with the same apparent SKU.. Look at all of the customer images & then look at the image that Amazon shows. The newer revision (amazon's images) have paw prints on the mount where as the customer images show a much beefier 1 piece mount.  I have left a message with Cheetah support & will update this review if they are able to resolve any of my many concerns over this mount.  Cant add captions to the images so I will explain them. 1st: you will notice that the center arm is resting on the lower arm. Have to lift the LCD & push it in to get it all the way flush into this posisition. I have my LCD level at this point.  2nd. Shows the included torpedo level centered at the top of the LCD with the arm pulled out so that the center is not resting on the lower arm.  3rd. Shoes the center arm pushed against the lower arm (before lifting the LCD to push it the rest of the way back).  4th. Shows the same level in the same spot with arm rotated to the right (as you can see these is quite a bit of change from the above).  5th. Notice the lower arm touching the mount. As the stockAmazon images show this was roughly the same spacing as the top before weight was added.  Edit: 5/12/2015  Since I initially wrote the review I was contacted by the seller. The seller sent what appears to be an older version of the APDAM2B mount & refunded 15 bucks on the purchase of this mount. The replacement does hold the weight fine, but it is extremely stiff & essentially does not pull off the wall without much more force then should be required. Also the back of the set where all the connections are is completely covered so changing anything is still a 2 person job.   After I had it installed for a few days the seller contacted me to make sure that everything was good. When I further voiced my concearns the following is what I received back from the seller.   ------------------------------------ Dear Corey,  Thank you for responding to my email and also for sharing that information with us. We apologize for that mount not working for you also. I tried the best I could to help you out and have your issue resolved. You also was fully refunded for your purchase. Since we did reached out to you and tried to assist you the best we could in order for you to be satisfied, would you consider removing the negative review? If not we totally understand. We would certainty appreciate it though. Have a great day.  Thank you, Luis- SPN Performance 877-300-2950 ext 6046 ------------------------------------  At this point it was fairly obvious that they were trying to buy positive reviews so I did not respond. A week has gone by since then & today I receive this  ------------------------------------ Dear Corey,  Hello good day. We apologize for our product not working for you. As a company it is very important for us to read our product reviews and also talk and listen to our customers issues. Doing so is how we are able to make improvements on our products as well growing as a company. Since I did reached out to you and tried my best to help you and also refunded you since our product did not work for you would you consider removing the review? We would really appreciate it. If there's anything else we can do to better assist you or better serve please feel free to let me know. Have a wonderful day.  Thank you, Luis- SPN Performance 877-300-2950 ext 6046 ------------------------------------  A seller specifically requesting a negative review be updated is completely asinine & goes against the whole purpose in having a detailed customer review. This is not a company/seller that I would knowingly do business with again in the future. You can not trust the reviews that are listed for any product when the seller so blatantly goes above just making things right with the customer & specifically requests that the reviews be altered to reflect something other then reality.

product_title: LOFTEK® HDfuryproTwo Input HDMI to RGB Component YPbPr / VGA 2x1 Switch Converter Support 5.1CH Surround Sound.
review_body: I wanted this to work so badly - the video worked perfectly on my Mitsubishi 65511 rear-projection TV with component inputs.  I was able to get the full 1080i HD that the TV is capable of using a new Sony Blu-ray player set to output 1080i.  Unfortunately I could not get 5.1 audio from this box no matter what I did.  I had sound from the optical output, but only when it was switched to the stereo 2.0 setting, and then it was intermittent - I never did get any audio when switched to the 5.1 setting.  The 3.5mm analog stereo output was the only one that produced consistent sound, but that kind of defeats the idea of having a 5.1 surround system.  Then, I thought I would just hook up the coaxial digital output from the Blu-ray player to my older Sony STR-DE915 receiver, but I couldn't get any sound no matter how I set the Blu-ray player, and I tried every setting available!  To be honest, the picture wasn't that much better than my old DVD player, and my old DVD player has component video output and perfect 5.1 optical surround sound output, so I sent the HDFuryPro2 and the Blu-ray player back and went back to my good ol' DVD.  Bottom line:  if you have older gear without HDMI connections, you may get some things to work, but probably not everything.  I hope the electronics and entertainment industries can feed their families on the "analog sunset", because they won't be getting any of my money until my old gear, which works perfectly, craps out, and by then I will probably be dead.  One other note:  I contacted Loftek to see if they had any advice about the converter, and the response I got from an individual whose first language was obviously not English was that he knew nothing about the box and the guy that had designed it left the firm, so if you are looking for customer support, good luck.

product_title: HIFIMAN HM700 32G Portable Player plus RE400 In-Ear Monitors/IEMs
review_body: The HiFiMan HM-700 was my first venture into lossless audio.  I did a fair amount of research before purchasing the player and had high expectations based on favorable reviews at Amazon and other sites.  When I received the unit I was impressed with the packaging and the nice RE-400 IEMs that came with the unit but my favorable impressions began to quickly change when I started listening to the player through my car audio system and the RE-400 IEMs.  When listening to the player through my car audio system I found that the player did not provide significant improvement over my old mp3 player when comparing CD ripped FLAC music files to the same files converted to 320 bps quality mp3s.  I do not have a high end audio system in my car so initially I thought that maybe I needed a better amp and speakers in my car to hear the difference.  However, as I note later, I did hear improved performance when I tried another lossless player through my car system.  I also expected to be impressed with the IEMs since they are matched to the HM-700 but I did not find them to be better than other IEMs that I tried with the player.  The bass response is poor and the overall sound is too tinny for my taste through the IEMs.  A major issue that I have with the HM-700 is the expected battery life.  My experience falls far short of the advertised 16 hour battery life.  I generally only see 5 to 6 hours of operation before needing a recharge.  The user interface is poor as well.  The controls are flush on the face which gives the unit a sleeker appearance, however, in poor lighting conditions or sun glare it is hard to find the buttons to use the player.  After playing the HiFiMan HM-700 for 4 months I finally became so unhappy with it that I purchased a Fiio X3 music player.  The Fiio X3 performance is what I had expected to hear when I made the upgrade to lossless audio.  FLAC files sound noticeably better on the X3 through my car audio system, battery life is at the 16 hour mark, plusit will play 24 bit files whereas the HM-700 will not.  The Fiio X3 player costs a little more than the HM-700 but I think it provides noticeably superior performance.  Overall, I am disappointed with my HiFiMan HM-700 purchase and cannot recommend it.  I wish I had tried the Fiio X3 first.

product_title: Onkyo TX-NR727 3D Ready A/V Receiver - 7.2 Channel
review_headline: Complicated and awkward to operate but sound is very good and it has a lot of features (see update )
review_body: I like the product but I have to say I was pretty disappointed when it comes to operating it.  I suppose your degree of like/dislike will be based on how you use it and how you set it up.  For me, I have a small 5.1 theater setup upstairs and the rest of my home wired for sound with flush ceiling speakers that are powered thru the zone 2 through a monoprice multizone switch.  Operating zone 2 or anything through the remote is do-able but very poor.  The remote is among the worst I have seen.  It works, but the buttons are tiny and the logic could be much improved. The amp sounds good and has plenty of power and has a lot of cool features.  It just needs more polish at the user interface end of things IMO.  What this means....if you didn't hook this up and print out and read the 120 page manual...you can't use this effectively. You probably could not figure out how to turn on zone two at all.  And you can forget about your wife being able to turn on the radio or stream music into the kitchen....it is a pain.  That said, when you get it working, it sounds pretty good.  I have another home theater downstairs in a large room.  It is all sony. All the components and the TV are sony.  They all work together perfectly and it is easy to use. with ONE remote. In my upstairs system with the onkyo 727, I have a mix of components and a Samsung tv.  I have 5 remotes and non of them can do what I want so you need to use several just to watch a netflix film with surround.  When I do this again it will be all sony.  I know some say the sound is not as good but it is not worth the added headaches.  I can not believe it is that hard in this day and age to design an simple 5.1 surround tv theater system with a powered multi zone option.  Bottom line, it sounds good, has lots of features, but it is far from plug and play if you want too USE the features.  The user manual is massive and comes on a cd that you need to print out to figure anything out.    ****UPDATE****  I just was thinking....this would be much better if they had a good app for Ipad...I looked and they do and it was just updated 3/15/15.  Onkyo remote 3.  I loaded it and it resolved some of the user issues I was complaining about.  My wife can now easily stream music from a more intuitive interface.  I have not gone through the app in great detail yet but the basic controls seem to be there and effectively.  Get the App it will help.

One really great feature I didn't mention below (but another reviewer rightly did) is the extremely gradual volume adjustment. It's a smooth, slow, not fast and segmented (or clicking), adjustment, so you can get exactly the volume you want, not a factory-predetermined, stepped level, common in many other receivers (a somewhat condescending design decision that always has annoyed me). This thoughtful, old-school, user-centric feature is, to me, one of the many aspects of this unit that push it into a higher stratum of quality that belies the bargain-basement price. I adore these hangers and have had them all over my house for years. When you walk by the TV, you see NOTHING behind it, it's flat to the wall (you must have a recessed plug mount to hide all the wires).

The biggest trick is making sure that the silver circles are mounted with vigor on your wall. If you do drywall, use the provided toggle bolts, if you do studs, use the lag bolts, etc. Make sure you know what fastener goes with which wall type and you're all set.

When you need to get behind the TV, that little rectangular bar in the lower left of the picture flips forward between the TV and the wall - tilting the TV forward and holding it away from the wall so you can reach underneath. You don't have to take the TV down to do things.

Purely beautiful, absolutely solid -- install them correctly and you'll be very happy with the look.

review_headline: UPDATED and RETURNED, Poor Customer Service.
review_body:
This is my second pair of SOL headphones. My first pair is the Tracks A8 and I love them still. But I wanted something that was wireless as it makes working out at the gym easier. I shopped around and defaulted to SOL Republic Tracks Air. Why? Because these are highhandedly the best sounding headphones, they're durable, and best of all easy to customize. UPDATE: 4/15/2015. So I've owned this pair of Tracks Air for a few weeks now and I love the sound, the range of the Bluetooth, and battery life. But SOL Republic has fell short in one important area; customer service. While using my headphones, I've experienced intermittent sound on the LEFT side. I've tried to troubleshoot the issue by disconnecting the Bluetooth and powering off/on the headphones to no success. My attempts in contacting customer service have been ignored. I e-mailed them on 4/2/2015 and immediately received an automated response telling me that someone will look into the issue. I waited at least 5 days for a response and had nothing. So I replied to the automated response (as I was instructed to if I had questions) and 11 days later and taking to Twitter, still no response from SOL Republic's customer service. I am VERY disappointed at this point, I am forced to return this pair to Amazon in exchange for the Bose Soundlink Bluetooth headphones.

My decision in getting the Bose was simple, one listen and I was blown away with the quality of sound. Let's be honest, Bose has been around for years developing speakers and has been used in so many different applications; how could you go wrong. I will pay a bit more for the Bose, but I know I am getting a product that is tested and proven. The plus side is, their customer service outlet is nearby. product_title: Phorus Speaker with Multi-Room Wireless Audio Streaming
review_body: This review may be a little unfair because I should be just reviewing the hardware, but integral to the experience is the software and that is why I am subtracting a 🌟 star. The sound is decent, and while I know I can get better sound from other speakers, even other Play-fi speakers, I believe that the price/performance ratio is great. The sound is loud without crackling, and the passive bass is decent without being over powering. So why the four star rating? Well, one must use either the Phorus app or the Play-fi app, and while these apps are decent they are not quick nor are they full audio control (unless you buy the PC app for an additional $15, which seems a little ticky-tack as well (you have to purchase an app to use the speaker in Hi-Fi mode?)). But here's what I mean... let's say you want to play a YouTube video through your Phorus speakers, you've got to do that on either a PC (there is a free version, but one speaker at a time), or BlueTooth/AirPlay (limited to one speaker), because the Android or iPhone *apps* don't have a YouTube output. Here's what it does have: Internet Radio (although for some reason, even though I see my local stations in the Internet Radio dialogue, I can't hear it through my speakers... other local stations I do get), Media server, Deezer, KKbox, Pandora (Phorus app only, not Play-fi), QQMusic, SiriusXM, and Songza. Finally when it loses a connection, the app hangs, and I'm stuck, with nothing to \\"click\\" to and no music to play. Now, with all that said, the app does get updates every so often, and maybe then boot time speed won't be such an issue and maybe Phorus Speakers will be integrated into the Android IS (I can wish, can't I)?

review_body: What a difference a week makes. When I first demoed this at a store and I really liked it a lot. But, after using it at home with my new 65 inch Samsung TV for a week, I've grown NOT to like it. The problem I find with this soundbar is that it sounds unnatural, like it has the mids scooped out of it. - A technique used in heavy metal music. It's a very processed sound especially noticeable when listening to human voices. There's plenty of bass (really too much in my opinion, but it can be adjusted) and plenty of treble but the middle part of the sound spectrum is low and can't be adjusted. After fiddling with all the adjustments for a week and comparing this soundbar to a 5.1 surround sound system that is nearly the same price, I've decided that this sound bar is going back. I prefer the warm, smooth, spacious sound of the surround sound system. Don't get me wrong, this would make a great sound bar for some. I really like the low profile of it and it has plenty of input/output connections and it looks nice and sleek. It even came with an optical sound cable which impressed me. But after the testing I've done, I've decided that soundbars are not for me and would only recommend them to people that feel it's too much trouble to set up a surround sound system (too many wires or what not)

review_headline: Sounds great and the battery life is as advertised.
review_body:
This Anker speaker has really good sound and great bass for it's size and price range. One of the biggest reasons I purchased this one was for the battery life. I get so tired of speakers dying, having to find another one in the house which is usually also dead.
After the first couple of uses and recharges, I wasn't so sure about the claims of 15-20 hours of battery life. Since then, I did a test: turning it on and using it for a few hours each day over a three or four day period (making sure to turn it off when not in use). I recorded each playing time until it was out of juice and the total was around 19 hours. I am thrilled with this. Time will tell if the battery will continue to charge as well, but right now it is fantastic.
My only critique is one already mentioned in these reviews. The speaker has beautiful, slick buttons on the front for volume etc, but the slider on/off switch on the side is really cheesy/cheapy. It brings the appearance down a notch.

I love how the sound comes out of all four sides, and it is a nice crisp, clean sound. Although there isn't any adjustments to the sound (bass or treble) other than volume, I find no need for adjustments to it, and I'd rather have the lack of that feature than to have to download an app onto all of my streaming devices to control it, like some speakers make you do.
While reading reviews, I saw several complained about how this speaker isn't loud enough. I didn't find that to be a problem, it's plenty loud enough for my use, I never need it at full volume as that would be too loud, but I'm only using it indoors since there's several inches of snow on the ground outside right now.
There is a larger, more volume unit coming out in April called the FUGOO XL. For anyone wanting more volume, I'm sure you'll be happy with it if it is the same as this one only bigger and bolder.

product_title: Audioengine D1 24-bit Digital-to-Analog Converter
review_headline: Make Sure to use the SUPPLIED USB cable
review_body: I was having an issue with Windows 7 recognizing the device. Every time I booted up, it reinstalled the device and 90% of the time failed. Took many time plugging and unplugging it before it was recognized again. BUT THE PROBLEM WAS ME. The USB cable that comes with the unit is pretty short, not long enough to reach from the back of my pc to my desktop, so I used a longer cord. DO NOT DO THIS!!! Because the D1 pulls its power from the USB port, the added length of the USB cable that I used caused enough added resistance that the unit did not receive enough power, causing Windows to not recognize it. As soon as I changed to the shorter cable supplied, Windows recognized it immediately.  My current setup is that I have a POWERED USB hub, and I plug the supplied USB cable into that, and it seems to work wonderfully. But it is a POWERED, I would not try that with an unpowered hub.   Also, try to plug the cable into the PC directly, not into a hub. I tried plugging it into a powered hub, and experienced a lot of clicks and pops during playback. Plugging directly into the PC eliminated this.

product_title: Logitech Harmony 650 Infrared All in One Remote Control, Universal Remote, Programmable Remote (Silver)
review_headline: Finally - a Universal remote that works and is relatively easy to program!
review_body:
I was desperately in need of a universal remote because my tv remote and my dvd remote both had parts that didn't work any more. I have used universal remotes before, found them nearly impossible to program, and they NEVER powered all my devices This one is different! While it does have some short-comings (which I will outline later), they are not big enough to overcome the cool-factor of this remote. It comes with a mini-USB to USB cord which you connect to your computer. From their website - address given in the Get Started pamphlet - I downloaded the software. I ran it, and typed in my devices manufacturers (like Sony) and the model numbers. The software found each of my devices and even corrected my typing error of substituting a 5 for an S. When I got all of my devices added (a TV, DVD player, Roku, and OLD receiver), I went through the simple Add Activity menu that allowed me to tell the software what steps I go through to do that activity (e.g. To watch Roku: Turn on TV, change input to HDMI1.) Once that was all done, I clicked Sync and waited a few seconds. It finished and I disconnected the remote from the computer. The screen on the remote ran through a few training steps, then I started using it. It didn't work correctly for watching a DVD (the receiver didn't turn on) and the remote asked, "Is everything working ok?" I said no, the receiver popped on, and the remote said, "Did that fix the problem?" It did! I said Yes, and the next time it worked perfectly. I'm happy.

Now for the shortcomings...Some of the instructions are incomplete. I wasn't told to download the program or to go through the training steps before the remote would work. The instructions are so sparse that they are really relying on someone who is, if not tech savvy, at least brave. Also, the buttons to change the channel (the number keys) are at the very bottom of the remote, so it's difficult to hold it in one hand and change the channel. These are minor issues, I feel, and don't warrant down grading the rating to four stars.

One last note: the remote tells you to keep the remote aimed at your devices until everything is ready. You really have to do that, and be a little patient while it turns on the TV, sets the Input, turns on the receiver, sets the input, turns on the DVD, etc. It does work, though, and realizing that it's going through the necessary routine when you only have to push one button (or two) is remarkable!

Update: We just signed up for Fioptics (fiber optic cable) service and got a DVR box. It was simple to re-program this remote to replace the one they provided that had the old-style "guess the device code, hold the button until something blinks the right number of times, test, try again" method with at least 6 5-digit codes for each device we wanted to control. No thank you! I opened the software that sets up the Logitech Harmony 650 remote, added the cable box, changed the TV input setting, and assigned a couple of other buttons from the cable remote to the Harmony Remote. The software walked me through every step and it worked the first time. This is the remote you've been wanting!

product_title: GE 11270 HD Audio Bluetooth Receiver with NFC
review_body: This wallet-sized super lightweight receiver is perfect for connecting a bluetooth device to an existing speaker system.  It comes with a standard micro-USB charger (only 300mA, or 0.3A), so most any compatible charger or battery pack should work fine.  This also means it would be easy to use in other countries.    It has a 3.5mm audio jack as well as optical output, and mine came with a 6' long 3.5mm male to male cable as well as an adapter that goes to 2 RCA jacks.  It can thus be connected to most any existing speaker system, stereo, or pretty much anything with audio input.    The only button on it is the power button on top (hold down for one second to toggle power), and there's a switch on the back to switch between 3.5mm and optical audio out.    I appreciated that there were no annoying beeps or voice prompts when connecting/disconnecting like most of our bluetooth speakers.  This unit currently costs more than other similar devices - even more than many bluetooth speakers, and almost as much as our well performing [[ASIN:B00L3KW0QS JAM Storm]].  If you don't need the optical out, there are much cheaper options on amazon that only have analog audio out, though some others may not have the micro-USB charging port either.    It has NFC but we quickly connected via bluetooth (no password/code needed) and were up and running from an android device.    You can pretty much just plug this in and be ready to play music, or even use it for better sound watching movies on your tablet.

product_title: Symphonized GLXY Premium Genuine Wood In-ear Noise-isolating Headphones with Mic and Nylon Cable
review_headline: EXCELLENT-SOUNDING NATURAL CHERRY WOOD IN-EAR HEADPHONES & MICROPHONE
review_body: Four and a half DISTINCTIVE Stars! These Symphonized GLXY natural wood in-ear wired-headphones are very sleek and stylish. They have silver accents and small cherry red cylindrical wood end pieces which are 12/16th of an inch long and can be seen when the headphones are in use. The speaker part that fits into each ear canal has a soft, flexible black rubber ring cover that locks the headphone plug in place in the ear canal, preventing shifting around.  The strong braided black nylon wires between the 2 headphones and the plug are 8 inches longer than the white Apple wired-headphones. The black color of the wires is not as obvious as the white color of the Apple headphones when in use.  In testing, the plug fit snugly into each smartphone or tablet receptacle. The angled plug is designed to prevent stress on the end of the wires which could cause the wires to fray. The rubber ring did lock the earphones in place in the ear canal and no shifting occurred when walking, standing and sitting down. In listening to music or the human voice, the sound is crisp and clear with no distortion. In placing multiple telephone calls, the microphone 'push on-push off' mechanism worked flawlessly and the sound of the voices was clear on voicemail and while speaking. When listening to music or talking, if either cord is touched a low scratchy sound is heard, maybe from lack of grounding. Using a test music track with low instrument dynamics, the instruments on the track were completely audible with no distortion. In some cases, instruments in the background were heard that never were heard before.  Highly Recommended! Four and a CLEAR Stars!  (1 each pair of Symphonized GLXY in-ear headphones with natural cherry red wood accents. 2 extra small and large rubber ring speaker tips. 1 year limited warranty. This device was provided for testing and an impartial review.)

product_title: Philips X2/27 Fidelio Premium Headphones, Black
review_headline: A Headphone Primer for Normal People + Fidelio X2 vs HD 650 vs HD 800 Discussion
review_body:
Looking for a pair of great sounding headphones? Confused by the mind-bending varieties on offer? Don’t be. It’s easy to narrow things down when you have CIA levels of intelligence on the subject, as I do. I will share this information with you know, free of charge. You lucky fiend.

Okay, let’s start by assuming that your priority is sound quality. For this, you need a pair of ‘open back’ headphones. This means that they go over your head and have acoustic vents in the sides. Basically these are like mini speakers which you slap on your head. People will hear your music but this is only a problem if you listen to duets by Peter Andre and Katie Price. If you do listen to such duets, you have no need for high quality headphones anyway, and this concludes my advice for you, g’bye.

If you’re still here, it means that you want to know if this particular pair of headphones is worth buying. The answer is yes, without hesitation. But that doesn’t tell you very much. This is what you need to know.

Headphone manufacturers have different priorities. Some do style. Some to sound quality. Some try to both, and so on. The acoustics engineers on the Philips Fidelio team are some of the finest. They are especially interested in reproducing excellent sound quality. The products are not cheap, but neither are they the priciest. The build quality is refined and always looks premium. So I like that approach, it makes sense to me.

Now this X2 model is a successor to a model called the X1. Music lovers almost universally had audiogasms with that product because it had a terrific bass response *and* extremely good levels of clarity throughout the middle and upper frequency range. So why bother with this X2?

Well, the Fidelio team has improved the product in a number of ways. The main change is under the hood, with the audio driver (put simply, the dome-like component responsible for the sound). The driver now has a composite design (using a polymer-gel-polymer configuration). The idea is that this enables a smoother delivery of sound throughout the frequency range.

The other big change, pun intended, is that the X2 headband has been extended so that people with even larger heads can get their Bach on. Personally, I don’t have a BFG head so I was fine with the X1. But the X2 will fit more people, so that seems a good design step.

Now, do these changes amount to a substantial sonic improvement over the X1? In my view, and according to my perception, the answer is definitely yes. In fact I think the X2 sounds a great deal cleaner and crisper than the X1. The telling difference is in terms of clarity in the mid and upper frequency range. The bass extension is exactly as deep as the X1, but it is tighter and more controlled. It's not a slight difference. It’s much more satisfying.

So how does the X2 compare to similarly priced open headphones? And what about super high end headphones costing four times as much? Well, I can give you a verdict by pitching them against two Sennheisers. Unlike some reviewers, I actually have experience of listening to the equipment.

Compared to the HD 650, a long time flagship of the Sennheiser’s range, in my view the X2 produces livelier, more engaging sound with a much wider stereo image. Stereo image is that sense of sound coming separately from the left and right channels rather than as some homogenous lump. When you listen to recordings of live music with the X2, you do hear the separation between instruments and vocalists. It’s glorious.

How about the X2 compared to the HD 800, a £1000 super high fidelity headphone? Well, in terms of stereo imaging, I have never heard anything as good as the HD 800. I’ve also never heard anything as clear and accurate. But I can honestly say that the X2 can be discussed in this context of ultra headphones. It’s terrific.

The reason is that the sound of the X2 has a certain drama. It thumps low and it sings high in a manner almost unparalleled amongst the myriad headphones I’ve listened to. So the X2 is easy to recommend. The Philips team has done a remarkable job. They have once again produced that rare combination of style *and* substance.
