product_title: Energy 5.1 Take Classic Home Theater System (Set of Six, Black)
review_headline: This 5.1 system is like a day spa for your ears
review_body:
It has been a long time since I have been inspired enough to actually sit down a write an Amazon review for anything and I feel like I spend half of my life buying stuff on here. Also seems kind of pointless to chime in when there are 800+ essentially glowing reviews. But this system is just that good. I am compelled to write this review by the silky smooth buttery warmth that emanates from these bad boys.

I am not gonna sit here and list some silly amount of gear that I have owned or systems that I have heard. I have been a DJ for 12+ years and am obsessed with audio technology, whether it's speakers or headphones or receivers or DJ gear. I'm not a rich man so I am always on the lookout for the best bang for your buck. I had this Energy 5.1 system sitting in my "Saved for Later" bin for about 5 years, no joke. That's when I first read the review and was intrigued and as I have monitored, they still have not lost CNET's recommendation as the best budget sound system that was first given in 2009 and the positive reviews are still pouring in here at Amazon and elsewhere.

Decided to take the plunge on a Samsung 4K TV with some Best Buy financing and that led me to replace my ancient Onkyo with a Yamaha RX-V675. All of a sudden my Tannoy bookshelf speakers I've had since 1998 lost a bit of their sheen knowing what kind of power I was sitting on with the new Yamaha. So, as one thing tends to lead to another with audio gear purchases, I waited until I saw another of the seemingly regular $299 price drops on the Take Classic (down from $399) and decided to take the plunge. Like a good Amazon fanboy, I went ahead and got the RCA 16 gauge speaker wire and whatever mounting system Amazon says are "frequently bought" with this system.

So, if you've made it this far, $350 Yamaha receiver + $300 Take Classic system = $650 that sounds like $5,000. And this is without a proper subwoofer cable (in the mail, using a janky RCA in the meantime), no YPAO mic calibration (accidentally tossed it with the box) and only a few hours of break in. As soon as I played a song with all of the settings on the receiver punched in correctly, my jaw (and those of three friends who were there who helped me install, more on that later) hit the floor. We were all stunned. I never knew music could sound so good.

A little background on my listening environment: I live in an old 1920s Los Angeles hotel that has been converted into apartments. I have 9 foot ceilings and concrete walls in a living room that is about 12 x 18 feet. My couch is up against the short wall with the TV opposite so no way to put the surround satellites behind. I remembered a friend with a Polk 5.1 system who had mounted them in the upper corners of his living room and it sounded phenomenal so I decided to go the same route, angling the fronts down and toward the couch pretty much at 45 degrees in the corner. The rear satellites I mounted probably more at 70 degrees toward the couch so they have that rear channel position but still are angled enough toward the rest of the room to compliment the fronts when listening to music. The center channel is mounted at the same height...but in the center (duh). I measured 4 inches out from the wall on all them before drilling in the mounts to give the speakers some breathing room as others have suggested.

About the mounting: the VideoSecu Universal Satellite Speaker Mounts / Brackets for Walls and Ceilings are the one thing I would take back in this whole setup. They don't mount completely flush with the speaker (despite some reviewers saying so), they're plastic and they do not come with the alligator wall brackets they claim to in the instructions. I had to hit Home Depot to get some for a dry wall ceiling. I can verify that the 5/16" drill bit they say to use is the correct size, so make sure you get brackets sized for that bit if you go this route. All things considered, they're fine, they seem like they will hold. In hindsight, I maybe would have sprung a little more for something else, but this really isn't the point of the review.

What you absolutely must do is mount your speakers in this fashion if you are able to. There is a reason why clubs do it this way: so that people are IN the sound instead of jockeying to find a sweet spot. The way that this system fills the room with such superbly warm sound is something that anyone who enjoys music or movies needs to hear. It's one of those transcendental "wow I have never heard this song sound like THIS" experiences. I know the Yamaha receivers have a great reputation for surround sound processing so this may be contributing, but we just sat there picking different favorite songs of ours from all genres and listening in awe with big goofy smiles on our faces.

In Pusherman by Curtis Mayfield for example, the percussion was crisp and clear out the back channels while the guitar was sparkling from the fronts. The bassline...THAT bassline sounded so fresh and so clean. Played a few tracks off of Puffy's (criminally under-appreciated) Last Train to Paris album as I know the mastering is top notch on that one and it sounded fantastic. Then went for what is my de facto audition album of late for anything that reproduces audio: DARKSIDE. Listening to the songs "Heart" and "Paper Trails" was sublime. If you haven't heard these guys (they only put out one album) and you're looking for what Pink Floyd would sound like if they were a band now, do yourself a favor. The mastering is impeccable and the Take Classics did not disappoint.

I then threw on the end of the Portland/Golden State game to get a feel for sports and both the surround stage in the arena and the announcers were both pronounced without interfering with each other. Then went for Pacific Rim on Netflix and the opening fight scene really had nice spatial depth to it. People weren'tkidding: this system really does handle movies and music equally well. I have read that this is an impressive feat for a 5.1 satellite system. I've never been disappointed by others that I have heard, but I have never been blown away as I was by the Take Classic.

So there you have it, a review 5 years in the making. It was worth the wait. If you're a normal Joe with a normal sized living room and you like knowing you're getting the best sound that $300 (and probably $1500 or $2000) could buy, don't think about it anymore. I can't recommend these paired with the Yamaha RX-V675 enough, although it sounds like they have been doing any receiver with enough discrete wattage justice for years now. I had my Tannoy/Onkyo combo for a solid 10 years, pretty sure I'll have this one for at least that long.

product_title: Yamaha Digital Home Theater System YHP-S101BL (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
This was my first foray into home theater systems, so I understandably did quite a bit of research prior to purchasing. I wanted to stay under $1000 for a system (including speakers), which didn't seem too unreasonable for a first-time home theater system. Yamaha has an excellent reputation in this area, and this particular system demonstrates why.

The box was admittedly massive, and quite heavy. Upon opening the box, I became almost instantly intimidated. Lots of speakers, wires, cords, etc -- for someone who had never assembled a home theater system, this part will undoubtedly be somewhat intimidating. Assembling the system was no easy task, and ended up taking about two hours to get everything *just right* so that the speakers were adequately balanced and every wire was where it needed to be. This setup process, while tedious, was absolutely worth every minute. It may have taken nearly two hours, but the instructions were very clear and easy to follow, and the entire process was rewarding at the end.

For what is by all accounts a budget, entry-level home theater in a box, this thing packs a ton of features. The bluetooth receiver was a cool added bonus, and has turned out to be what I use it for the most. The pairing process is seamless (once it's on, you will never have to touch the Bluetooth receiver again to initiate a new device pair), and delivers high quality audio (well, as high as could ever be expected from Bluetooth). The next step was hooking up my new turntable, which also sounds quite massive on this system. The subwoofer delivers phenomenal lows, particularly from an analog sound. However, the speakers aren't *perfect*, but are certainly good enough to compensate for their lack of size. They're good enough to make it difficult to justify replacing them. Hooking this system up to my TV and PS4 was also a breeze, and completely changed my experience in using both. Movies just seem so much more real, and video games are far more immersive.

Overall, I would absolutely recommend this as a entry-level home theater system. It would be difficult to find anything cheaper than this (I paid around $400) that can deliver such performance. Yamaha has a reputation for amazing receivers and good speakers, and this system does a good job of demonstrating why.

product_title: Yamaha YAS-203 Sound Bar with Bluetooth and Wireless Subwoofer
review_headline: Good speaker upgrade, but not a home theater substitute
review_body: This is great for what it is, but it's important to understand what it is before you buy it. It will not replace a 5.1 or 7.1 surround sound experience (you need the much more expensive directional Yamaha soundbars for that). It also won't give you the full sound experience that you'd get with a traditional stereo receiver and a nice set of speakers. But it will give you an upgrade to your tv's factory speakers along a few extra bells and whistle like bluetooth streaming. You'll get a nice rich sound that fills the room, handles a variety of music scenes, and works with your existing remotes (you can program the bar to use the same volume, power, and mute remote control frequency as your tv, so your existing remotes will automatically control the sound bar without any reprogramming). When paired with your phone, you can also adjust the bass volume and select different scenes (sports, movie, tv, etc.). The same app also supports the high end Yamaha soundbars, so if you demo it ahead of time, please be aware that the advanced features like room resizing aren't available with this lower end model. So - assuming your just looking for a really good set of speakers with a mid-level subwoofer and don't have the room for normal home audio setup, this will do the trick. If you're hoping to use it to create a realistic home theater surround sound experience, you'll need to ditch this one and go with the $600+ soundbars that can control speaker direction and customize the sound stage...this one won't give you that experience.

product_title: Energy RC-70 Tower Speaker - Black (Each)
review_headline: Simply stunning sound. Can't do better for double the $$$!
review_body: I doubt I will ever buy another set of tower speakers again, these are that good.  If I do, I will scour the Earth for another pair of these.  Audiophile level.  Worth every penny of the $1,000 MSRP, each.  Under $500 apiece and you're getting a massive value.  I took advantage of a big sale price and I am thrilled.  They are ELITE as a two-piece set-up with high quality music and amps.  They spoil you with a wide, gorgeous sound stage.  Everything sounds perfectly reproduced. Ports plugged or not, bi-amped, w/ a sub or without...whatever... they just sound AMAZING.  You simply cannot go wrong.  I have heard a lot of the speakers in this size and range and the RC-70s take a back seat to none.  I like Energy bookshelf speakers a lot, and have owned a couple pairs.  First CB-20 (great), then RC-10 (insanely great), so having been introduced to the Reference Connoisseur series by the bookshelf, had great confidence in this buy. There are pro audio reviews online comparing these to $5,000 pairs of speakers, favorably.  I have envied Def Tech big dogs, and many others.  I have now found my muse.  These are amazing.  At a discount they are INSANE. The tweeters (subtle, highly accurate, clear but not horn-y or overly bright) and mids are dramatically good, the bass is solid, clean, and full.  I do have a subwoofer but the bass of the RC-70s is clean, deep and plenty beefy on the speakers alone.  They do seem to have a break-in period, which I originally doubted even exists, but which many people observe and which Energy mentions in their literature.  They just get better and better.  Best decision I have ever made regarding speakers.  *Edited: with additional time, I am even more in love with these! They never fatigue your ears, they just open up and sound amazing. All music is good. Well-recorded, good sources will shine. All genres too. So glad to join the Cult Of Energy! Consider me a fanboy. Buy with utmost confidence. Google the SoundStage review, and the Sound & Vision review, of these speakers...so, so, good.

review_headline: GREAT FIT, and decent sound quality with moderate comfort
review_body:
As a long time lover of music and high quality audio equipment I wouldn't say these are spectacular in audio quality. That said, this is not why I bought these. I've tried quite a few earbuds and they all have the same problem... I can't keep them in my ears. I have pretty big ears, but tiny ear canals and it's difficult to find ear buds that sound passable while not falling out every 5 seconds while I'm doing things. These fit the bill perfectly. The audio quality is pretty good, however biased towards the low end. The top end sounds thin and a bit low in volume, and the mid range sounds full but quiet. It's nothing that a touch of the EQ (using PowerAmp on my my Galaxy S5) can't fix.

The fit is pretty good. The adjustable "hook" really works well. I wish it was a little less firm (that would make it more comfortable), but it does just what it's supposed to do without any issues. The ear pieces do a good job of blocking out ambient sounds (so buy their MX series if you're a runner and need to hear on coming traffic), but for me to use while working or while doing yard work and needing to block out the weed eater or lawnmower, this is PERFECT.

product_title: Yamaha NS-555 3-Way Bass Reflex Tower Speaker (Each)
review_headline: Pair well with Yamaha RS-700 for stereo music
review_body:
I am very pleasantly surprised by the quality of these speakers. I have had them for one month now, and am enjoying them more all the time. They replaced some vintage JBL LX-44s in my 2.1 music listening system, and I couldn't be happier. I had previously installed (and returned) Def Tech BP8Bs, but didn't like the 'bipolar' sound so I went back to my trusty JBLs.
I was originally driving them with a Yamaha RX-V867 (high end consumer grade AV amp). When I just changed the speaker wires over, I was not impressed (muddy highs..). Then I re-ran the YPAO process to adjust the internal equalizer to them. Much better... And per some previous comments, I did about 40 hours of 'break-in' and they rewarded me nicely.
Placement is important for bass response since they are rear ported. Mine are about 18" out from the wall at the back, which seems to be where the bass sounds the best. In fact, I've turned off my sub-woofer for most listening, and haven't missed it.
Then I hooked them up to a new Yamaha analog stereo amp (RS-700), and they took off. Yes, it's near the same power (95W vs. 100W), but they sound totally different: Much more 'open', much better sound stage, and absolutely clear. Vocals are outstanding, and if I close my eyes, I'm sure there's a piano in front of me sometimes. I have been enjoying listing to Larry Carlton guitar background fills on Steely Dan tracks, and hearing an 'ambiance' that I've never heard before on well recorded CDs (Norah Jones, Diana Krall...).
A clean source is essential with this combo... I use a Marantz CD5004 for CDs, and I'm considering an Oppo for SACD. And I might even get my old Dual turntable tuned up and give it a 'whirl'.

Price seems to have gone up since 2005, but the speakers are still a great deal. Remember that these are 6 ohm speakers, so make sure your amp is compatible.

product_title: MEE audio M6 PRO Universal-Fit Noise-Isolating Musician's In-Ear Monitors with Detachable Cables (Smoke)
review_body:
These IEM's are nearly perfect! For the price, the sound is pretty stellar. They are comfortable, they stay in the ear, come with a myriad of ear tips, and the company appears to be pretty awesome too! The Bass certainly kicks when it needs to, but doesn't muddy up the sound; this is perfect for musicians, because you can hear/ feel the rhythm section distinctly and accurately.

Sadly, however, the top end is a tad harsh. It isn't quickly fatiguing, but sibilance is certainly amplified. I would call it a top end \\"hiss\\" or \\"sizzle\\". If the track or instruments are properly EQ'd, you're most likely fine. But if there's even a little bit of harsh top end, you're sure to hear it quickly. If you believe in \\"burn in,\\" you might try mellowing that top end a bit (heck, some people from head-fi SWEAR that they can hear a difference).

Overall, these IEM's are pretty awesome. MEElectronics is making an amazing leap forward, and for the musician on a budget (or someone looking for quality tweeters), these are certainly competitive. The extra cable with universal controls is a nice touch too!

I can't say for sure if I plan on keeping them; on the one hand, they're nearly perfect. On the other hand, that top end might eventually drive me mad!

product_title: Vanco 280573 HDMI Audio Extractor
review_headline: Great Hi-Res HDMI Audio Extractor for 2 Channel Audio Systems
review_body: I have an Oppo 103D that can play SACD, DVD-Audio, and BluRay Audio.  I wanted to hook the Oppo up to my 2 channel stereo system using the highest resolution possible.  The Oppo's Toslink and Digital Coax inputs limit audio output to a resolution to 48K, but hi-res audio is passed on the HDMI output.  The Vanco goes between the Oppo and the TV and extracts the audio and passes it on a Toslink or Digital Coax output on the Vanco unit.  The Vanco's Digital Coax is connected to my Digital to Analog Converter.  This unit will pass at least 24/192K.  In this configuration I get 24/88.2K on SACD and 24/48K on standard Blu Ray and it can play hi-res music (48K, 96K, and 192K) downloaded from HDtracks and placed on a memory stick.  I have not tried DVD-A or Blu Ray Audio yet - but I'm confident it will work fine.  The unit automatically defaults to 5.1 when powered up.  This is the setting you need on the Vanco to pass hi-res audio.  it you change it to 2CH it will down convert to 48K.  This unit seems very similar to the Kanex Pro HAECOAX.  Works great.

product_title: Klipsch Portable Speaker System
review_headline: It actually sounds a little better than the klipsch kmc and man does it bump
review_body:
When I was choosing a new bluetooth speaker the midrange boombox speakers really caught my eye. The original beatbox, beatbox portable, ihome boombox, and of course the klipsch kmc 3. I have heard all of these speakers personally and have gotten to test out all of them. I will break down the pros and cons of the Klipsch kmc 3 and what the plusses of the other speakers are

Original beatbox portable: I have a friend that owns the original beatbox and all I have to say is wow. It actually sounds a little better than the klipsch kmc and man does it bump! Also the bass seemed more smooth than the kmc 3 becuase of the twin 5.25 woofers. But when I tested out other types of music like post metal, classic rock, ska, blues, and classical it still sounded great! The bass really didn't over power the highs or mids, instead it gave off a warm sounding tone. There were a ton of pros but the cons of this boombox were just to many. First off it had no bluetooth. The only way I could test it was with an aux cord. Yes there is probably a hookup I could buy somewhere, but I really shouldn't have to. A speaker of that price should just have a basic feature like that. Secondly it had no portability. No charging option, nothing. This speaker is just meant to play music in a specific location. In the end I decided the pros outweighed the cons

Ihome: For only $150 (at the time of this review) Ihome offerers a very attractive little boombox. Music from it sounds clean, balanced and distortion free. The design is just amazing too! It looks like an old school boombox with a very modern twist. In the middle it was an area to hold your phone, two 4 inch woofers, and two 1 inch tweeters. The cons were that it runs off 6 d batteries with no recharging option. I don't carry around d batteries at the ready so why not just add a charger? Another downside was dispite having the two 4 inch woofers the bass was relatively weak. It didn't have that chest thumping pounding I wanted. That is personal preference though. I was still very clean and sounded good with whatever I played. Also it got loud just not as loud as I would have liked

Beats portable: I know beats has a bit of a bad name in the audio world but both the beats boomboxes I tested sounded amazing. The portable is the successor to the original beatbox. The strongest part is that it fixed all of the previous cons such as lack of bluetooth, no portability and having no features except just normal audio performance. But to do this it scarfed audio performance. Yes it sounds good, but not amazing like it's older brother. The bass is strong,but not knock you on your butt strong. It was clean but not spotless. Also for it to be portable it needs 8 d batteries. That's hardly portable if you ask me. Still you can hear this thing down the block and it sounds good doing it.

Klipsch KMC 3: The kmc 3 seems to be the jack of all traits. This speaker is bass heavy, but for me that is a good thing. I enjoy a warmer sound. Even with oldies or classical I enjoy a little more punch. I love to hear the bass and the drums clearly in rock songs and of course I like to hear that sounding bass when listening to hip hop. Some people may feel the bass overpowers the mids and highs on other types of music. A simple EQ change is more than enough for me, but again I like warmer sounds. It isn't as balanced as the original beatbox, but it still has clear mids and strong highs. This isn't your typical audiophile sound, but again not everyone wants that. Listening to bluetooth sounds amazing because of the audio compression it uses. So if you're one of those people who uses higher bitrate music in their library this is going to be a welcome feature. As fas a design goes it's not going to catch any eyes. The built quality feels solid but the back is a fingerprint magnet. My only gripe is that there is no rechargeable battery. Instead Klipsch opted to have it take 8 d batteries. The upside is that it's rated at 26 hours of battery life. But everytime you need new batteries and have to unscrew the bottom to put them in. So far that is my only major problem with this speaker.

It doesn't have AM. To me who cares. Not close enough to a city to make it worth worrying about. Besides where I live is becoming dominated by sports talk on FM. It comes with a set of RCA inputs on the rear, 3/8 mini jack input in the front and Bluetooth connectivity. Although the cool factor was using my phone through it. It is paired with a netbook running Win10 consumer preview. I replaced the speakers with Insignia 5 1/4 2 ways because I like my music clean sounding. Have an old passive KLH subwoofer and the sound is really good. I am pleased as a whole with this system. You can't go wrong with it.eally good. I am pleased as a whole with this system. product_title: Simpowel V8 - 9W(4.5W X 2) Portable Bluetooth Speaker with FM-radio, Micro SD MP3 Player, NFC, LED Display and Removable 18650 Li-ion Battery
review_headline: ... my first bluetooth speaker purchase and I am VERY pleased! The praise
review_body:
I'll start by saying this is my first bluetooth speaker purchase and I am VERY pleased!

The praise:

This little gizmo absolutely blew me away with the sound quality. It's important to remember that it's a matter of physics why bass reproduction in open air (not headphones) is very difficult to do with small speakers. Having said that, this little unit produces very nice, round, full bass tones - not loud, but rich. Vocals are clear and natural-sounding. The way it plays acoustic guitar almost sounds like the guitar is in the room with you. Hip-hop and rap are reproduced faithfully, as are rock and blues. Classical is a bit more challenging for it, particularly the delicate higher-register notes such as the triangle and piccolo but considering it's overall performance and taking the price into consideration, I am very pleased.

Other noteworthy positives are the multitude of connection options. Talk about flexibility! It has an FM radio tuner, Bluetooth connectivity, USB connectivity, analog connectivity via a 3.5mm auxiliary jack, and lastly you can play your media files straight from your (up to 32 GB) micro SD card, with bult-in support for MP3, WMA, APE, WAV, and FLAC lossless audio file formats!

The battery life and charging speed is pretty impressive as well. While I didn't track the exact duration of my usage, the battery lasted several hours at about 3/4 volume and still seemed to have plenty of juice left. That brings me to charging, which after that several-hour play time
I plugged in the unit to charge. According to the charge indicator light, it was fully charged in under two hours.

Lastly, I appreciate the use of a standardized, rechargeable Li-Ion 18650 battery. It's extra cool that they don't hold you at their mercy for battery replacement by locking it away inside the unit behind a warranty seal or having some obtuse, proprietary battery design or voltage. This not only allows for easy service if the battery fails, but also allows for a spare to be swapped out in case you run the included battery dead. Also, if you're shopping for a spare battery (I did, as I HATE running out of battery power on my gadgets) you can get one with a higher capacity than the included 2000mAh battery. I bought a spare 3000mAh as a backup.

Ok, now that I've lavished it with praise, here are the negatives:

For as well as it reproduces vocals and bass, I must say that oddly enough, it's the high notes that I'm a touch disappointed with. It just sounds like high-hat, cymbal, triangle, and other high-pitched instruments/effects in the 10+KHz range are just out of reach - a bit muffled, even. My only other complaint is the FM tuning procedure - it requires you to continually press the button over and over to change the station instead of letting you hold the button down and speeding to the desired channel. Time-consuming and annoying, particularly if you're switching to a station a considerable distance from the one you're on.

Now that I've dispensed with the pros and cons, onto the suggestions!

One suggestion I have is to incorporate a small, very basic LCD screen for displaying the folders and file names of media files on the SD card as well as a small joystick or other input device used to select the file(s) you want to play and to have more/faster control of the FM radio tuning.

The other suggestion is to find a way to increase the high-frequency response of the drivers or possibly incorporate tweeters. Maybe even make a slightly higher tier model that incorporates the above suggestions for a slightly higher price. I would have been willing to spend an extra $10 or possibly $15 for the added features.

In summary, if you don't want to drop big bucks for a big, fancy bluetooth speaker you're likely to eventually drop, step on, get wet, drive over, etc., but can't stand crappy sounding speakers, this is the devicefor you! It looks good, it's light, compact, versatile, it's only fifty bucks, and most importantly, IT SOUNDS GREAT!

Ok, the details your all looking for lol, first thing one does with a new set of headphones is try them out, but so you all are aware, BOTH sets of headphones came STONE DEAD, not even so much as a flicker of the LED light, manual says 1.5 - 2 hours to fully charge ... yeah ok, on what clock, a sundial?? try 5 hours almost 6, but thats the norm to charge a set of bluetooth headphones so, please, dont ask me where Bluedio got that estimate from :/.
Once fully charged, I grabbed my cell, turned on Bluetooth, and just about immediately she paired ( maybe 20 seconds, if that ). Perfect, of course I tried em out then an there, but to try an keep conformity here in this review, I want to mention here now that I also successfully paired ( on first try with no problems ) with both my tablet ( Android 4.4 ) and my laptop ( custom laptop running win7 pro in 64 bit, fully updated ... yes that matters lol ) ... anyways ... had no problems with pairing with any of my 3 devices.
CONSTRUCTION: yeah ok, Bluedio made improvements to the headband ( was a weak point in previous versions ) but once you get these in your hands your going to see real quick that theres still a weak spot, at the very function that made these headphones what they are ... the rotation. The pin, where the speaker pivots, while large and substantial and made from an alloy, should prove to hold no problem, its threaded into a plastic housing, an that doesnt have much " realestate " of plastic around it to really offer " sufficient " support, in my opinion anyways. It'll hold if handled with care, but dont get rough with em .. fair warning :). Other then that ONE defect, the headphones are well designed and built. Comfortable to wear, doesnt hurt the ears to wear for hours, doesnt weigh much so the headband doesnt beat down on your head after a few short hours of play. Very comfortable to wear, though I should note, after taking them off ... thats when you realise your ears where pressed a lil bit too much too long, but again, you dont feel this with the headphones on, and the surrounds cushion properly and even provide proper seal for optimum sound ( Yeah I know, Im getting to the sound ok lol ). These drivers are HUGE, by far the largest set of bluetooth headphones Ive owned, BUT while diameter this is true, bluedio kept it fairly shallow so to keep a low profile on the head.

First impression of these headphones ... BASS HEAVY, as everyones saying here in reviews, muddy mids, highs are pretty decent though ... BUT do NOT lose hope by that review or by others ... this is what they make EQ's for :D, and luckily for us, MOST devices now-a-days have some form of an EQ in it, if not theres plenty online in your app store. I spent maybe 10 minutes adjusting my EQ to bring out the most from these headphones ( 10 min btw is because again < audiophile an never really happy anyways lol, but also I have a 10 band EQ for my tablet and cellphone with all KINDS of options so thats why 10 min )

product_title: JAWBONE Big Jambox - Speakers
review_headline: The sound itself from the Jambox is great. It's clear and also has a rich bass
review_body:
I've always wanted a high-end Bluetooth speaker that I could carry around and use for both personal and public settings. After reading reviews, I eventually chose the Big Jambox over the UE Boom and Bose Soundlink Mini. The sound itself from the Jambox is great. It's clear and also has a rich bass. The speaker has a room-filling sound and is convenient to move around.
But one factor that really dampens the overall performance is the STATIC!!! There is an awful static hiss that occurs the moment you either connect to a Bluetooth device (phone or laptop) or through an Aux cable. I've tried a factory reset, but it didn't change anything. Friends have tried connecting their phones to the speaker, and the problem still exists. I've updated the MyTalk software and made sure it was playing on stereo, static still exists. It's a shame because the overall performance is great, it's just the static really detracts from the overall experience.
What's worse, the forums on the official website have a bunch of posts from people having the same problem. One of the mods (who I'm assuming works/is affiliated with Jawbone) actually said that while the static exists, the issue goes away when you raise the volume. Uhhh....what if I don't want to play music on full blast? While it is true the sound drowns out the static at high volumes, sometimes I just want background music, and the static ruins the sound.
It's a shame because it's great with parties, but static ruins the speakers with other uses. I'm planning on returning it; it's worth the cost of postage to get most of my money back.

product_title: Micca COVO-S Compact 2-Way Bookshelf Speakers
review_headline: Good things comes in small packages
review_body:
These are a great set of speakers for the price. i bought them for surround sound as the form factor and size is what i needed for my surround set up. After looking through the reviews i decided to go with these and i am glad i did.

Build quality
excellent. the speakers box looks well made and feels solid in the hand. the terminals accept banana plugs

As main stereo speakers
I wanted to test these out before i put them away as surrounds.So i replaced my Pioneer BS-22 fronts with these speakers and did a test with my sony reciever.I must say i was pleasantly surprised by the sound quality of these. The sound imaging was great and at times even felt like it was better than the huge pioneers to my untrained average user ears. These uses a concentric/coaxial design so you probably need a good amp to drive it. i will test this with my lepai and update this later. this little guy couldnt go as low as the pioneers in the bass dept but that was expected given the the size is less than an quarter(or 1/8th) of the pioneers

As surrounds (my primary use)
These work wonderful as surrounds. produces wonderfull presence sounds and it blends into the overall experience . I tested it out with the Saving Private Ryan beach landing scene and it was awesome

The only problem i can see with this is lack of mounting options which is a handicap when it comes to use as satelite speakers. I happened to have a tiny stand with a small enough top to fit these speakers and i used some blu tac to fix it . To be fair to micca they didnt advertise it as satelite speakers so i wont reduce any points for that . it would be a cool to have some kind of mounting option with these speakers.

if anybody is thinking about buying a Home Theater in a box system/soundbar, please do yourselves a favour and get a decent receiver and buy a Micca MB42x fronts and center with these as surrounds or if you dont have enough money get 3 pairs of these . it will be a much better value and of course you will have better chance of convincing your wife because they are sooo cute :)
You can also pair these up with a powered sub to build a nice 2.1 set up . for the price they are a steal

Update 7/17/2015
I still use them as my surrounds and they work great. i dont like to have bulky speakers for surrounds and this works good enough for me.I will keep the rating as i am completely satisfied for the price. I tried these with my lepai amp for my desktop setup because of the size factor .(Point it slightly up towards your ear for better sound) . The imaging is wonderful but quality is not as good as its big brothers(MB42Xs). For desktop set up you would be better of with those if you can spend 80$. For surrounds get COVO-S no need to spend more

TL;DR :For a desktop setup. You will be much better off with its bigger siblings, the MB-42Xs. For surrounds these are great no need to spend more

review_headline: Finally, Earbuds That Fit in My Ears!
review_body:
For some reason, earbuds have been the bane of my existence for the past decade. Maybe I have oddly shaped ears, but for whatever reason earbuds always seemed to slip out of my ears, even if I am just sitting down and not moving. This lead me to having to wear dorky old fashioned headphones. That is until I received these babies as a gift.

I must admit that I was disappointed upon receiving them. Because of my history with earbuds, I thought that I would have to return them or re-gift them. On a whim, I decided to try them, and what do you know? They fit! They do not slip out, even when I am jogging or exercising at the gym, and they are super comfortable.

The bluetooth works well and is an extra little luxury. It is nice to be able to listen to music or talk on the phone without having to hold the phone or have it in my pocket. Also, it is great not to have to deal with wires or cables when I am using them at the gym.

The sound quality is really good for this price range. Everything sounds crystal clear, and when you listen to music, you can hear each instrument individually.

Battery life is much better than expected. I used them on an 8 hour long bus trip, and they lasted the whole way without needing to be recharged.

These are a great value for the money. They would make an excellent gift, and they are definitely worth trying out if you have had trouble with earbuds in the past.

product_title: BeagleBone Black RS-232 Serial Micro-Cape
review_headline: Works well. Installation of RS232 a bit difficult. Need NULL modem for console.
review_body:
This goes best together with their metal case. It works well for doing console stuff. The RS-232 connector is the standard one you would have from an old AT mother board.

There are some issues. First is that at least the 2+ I have the RS-232 connector takes some filing away of the plastic to get it in their case. It's a bit frustrating. The screw holes also stick out of the case (of course) which makes the case a bit less handsome.

One item of frustration is that to connect this to a PC you'll need a NULL modem cable (eg: it's DTE).

It's also worth noting that they're really nice. I emailed them about how one might put a USB 2 serial in instead and they actually passed my ideas and thoughts to their techies who responded. Thanks!

Unlike their case this isn't for the beaglebone white and is not needed for the white anyway (The serial console is connected to usb via an ftdi chip on the white).

product_title: Outdoor Technology Chips Wireless Bluetooth Helmet Audio
review_body:
It is rare that I give a written review of anything I buy but I feel this product deserves one. I bought this based on other reviews from users on Amazon. I bought these to replace my Motorola S802 Bluetooth speakers. They were great in terms of sound and on the fly functionality but when it was cold they simply didn't work well. You couldn't get through a song without it cutting out 15 times or so a song. Barely doable on cold days.

Today was my first outing with these and not a single hiccup. It was -5 with windchills reaching -60 at the top. So they certainly can handle any cold conditions I throw at them. The functionality is great as well. As long as your helmets ear pieces have the ability to insert the speakers your fine. And since the entire speakers opposite side surface area is a button performing all available controls is very easy. The only caveat for me is that you have to press and hold the left side 6 seconds to advance a track and 3 to back up. I would prefer it the other way around since I rarely go back. But it's not enough of a negative to give it anything less than 5 Stars. I can't imagine anyone not loving these speakers. I see people with regular earbuds all the time. I was once one of them. I can't imaging resorting to that when products like this exist. Being able to have total control of your music on the fly effortlessly is a great thing.

product_title: Sennheiser On-Ear 926MHz Wireless RF Headphones with Charging Cradle
review_body:
I bought these for the sole purpose of watching stuff on my computer so that I didn't have to either watch what my bf is watching on TV, or so I didn't make him put up with what I wanted to watch. I wanted to go wireless because I have a large enough computer screen to not sit 3 feet away from it. This works for what I need.

**Pros**
--Wireless: I haven't tried going too far from the 'receiver' but I was able to go probably about 25 feet away without losing the connection
--Okay sound, but nothing special

**Cons**
--The Hiss or static. It's almost always there, no matter how close you are to the receiver or no matter how much you fine tune it. it's not always horribly noticeable, but there are some times when it can be, depending on your ability to drown out white noise.
--They are huge. I can't lie down, even just to rest my head back on the pillow without these getting in the way.
--The 'receiver' has to be plugged in to an outlet, and the audio source has to be plugged into the receiver. This limits where I can go with my laptop, and it can make it difficult to move elsewhere on a whim (having to unplug and untangle the cords...etc.)

Overall, depending on your need, these work. If you're looking for flexibility or moveability (is this a word?) then these aren't for you.

The mic is a nice touch, I wish it had more controls like a pause/skip button for my ipod, but really not an issue. The sound quality is worth the lack of controls. They are also great for working out, because they stay in my ears so well. product_title: RCA DH24SPF Two Way 3 Ghz Bi-Di Splitter
review_headline: Don't trust positive reviews!!!!! From a Field Tech
review_body:
For the record, I am a cable tech and deal with splitters on a regular basis.

I will say this is perfect for Antenna TV signals.

However, I would strongly advise against this for your internet. A lot of consumers unfortunately are duped by the fact that gold and high number equals better. This is NOT the case.

If you open this splitter up, you will see a very basic analog splitting system. This causes signal to noise ratio on the digital carrier to be lowered. I verified this by opening the splitter up. I also connected by my spectrum scanner to this splitter and picked up -30 decibels of noise. A splitter should NOT have any noise leak in! If it does, it is a result of poor shielding and connectors.

I highly recommend Antronix splitters or equivalent. If you open a back of a high quality splitter, you should see a circuit board.

Also, you want a 5 - 1002 mhz splitter. The max all cable plants in the US currently operate till is 1 Ghz. By getting a 1 Ghz splitter instead, you are focussing on a more distinct frequency span that your equipment actually operates at.

Once again, this is a good splitter for Antenna TV signals. But for digital TV and DOCSIS, it is highly not recommended.

product_title: Aerb® 4G Waterproof MP3 Music Player With Mono OLED Screen Display Support FM Radio / Pedometer for Swimming & other Sports (IPX-8 Standard)-Black
review_headline: DO NOT BUY, THIS IS YOUR WARNING. YOU'VE BEEN WARNED.
review_body:
I had a very disappointed experience with this product, before going on please don't buy unless you want to take the risk of wasting your time/money with this.

First of all, you are receiving what you pay I knew that when I was looking for waterproof MP3 players, so this one it's (or at least I thought) in the sweet spot between price and quality (how mistaken I was).

GOOD/JUST FINE FEATURES
The players has this 'sturdy' (it really isn't THAT reliable) clip in the back, so you can attach it wherever you want, kudos for this. The design it's fine, and the feel it's very good. The pedometer it's kinda wacky in its performance and not very accurate (about a error margin of 10-to-even-20%, I'm an engineer trust me) but it's not a deal breaker and you can be overall be fine with it. You can (manually) input some data like stride/arm/pool length and height/weight. The radio has this auto-search thing that's it's pretty helpful due to the fact that manually selecting a frequency it's a pain in the... finger.

BAD STUFF (pretty much everything else)
Forget about these next things: good FM reception (and 10 year old KID'S TOY has better reception, I should know, Iused that FM integrated walkie-talkie for years), screen rotation (a thing to consider when working out), good sound (I'm talking about the obvious not-good-enough headphones that almost every company uses because they're just cheap, gut ALSO about reproduction fidelity . Again, I'm an engineer, trust me. When you use 320Kbps files the device just becomes a snail and it's response time is around 3-5 seconds after buttons are pressed and there's this barely audible hissing even if you use other headphones), LAP COUNTER (Now this IS THE deal breaker. This product it's the only one in this price range that promises this feature and WHAT A HUGE FIASCO. I'm an avid swimmer, swimming 3-4 Km 6 days a week but the only THREE times I used this product the lap counter was just a MESS.I'd swim 50 meters and it would say I swam 14... U WOT M8. I'd swim 200m and it'd say I swam 54m and 3 laps. At first I thought it'd be something that would just get better but it's not)

In resume, just don't buy this, not worth it. I'm returning mine in hopes that Amazon gives me a refund at this point I'm just very very disappointed.

review_headline: So we bought four of these and they worked great. No issues handling the 220V Aussie current
review_body: We travel from the US to Australia about once a year to visit family. We stay with my in laws in a 100 year old home with few power sockets/ports so we must rely on power strips. product_title: Times Microwave lmr400UF-pl259-uhf-mm Ultra Flex Coaxial Cable Jumper with PL-259 UHF Male Connectors
review_body:
Excellent jumper cables. LMR-400 is an excellent, low-loss, heavy duty coax in the first place, and the connectors used are of high quality. I have several of these from this company in a variety of lengths and they are all very good.

Note: LMR-400 jumpers, even the Ultra Flex, are going to be overkill for most ham radio operators and others. It is a very heavy duty coax designed to be very low loss over a wide range of frequencies and power ranges, and as such, it thick and very stiff. Don't get me wrong, it will work exceptionally well, but caution is needed when using it because even the Ultra Flex is extremely stiff. If you aren't careful, the cable can act as a lever, multiplying the force you apply to bend it, and transferring that force to the connectors on the cable and your equipment and possibly damaging it. When using cable this stiff, position your equipment FIRST. Then position the cable, bending the cable to the proper position BEFORE you hook it to your equipment. Never move your equipment with the cable connected to it. This can generate enough torque to damage the connectors. Disconnect the cable first, move the equipment, re-bend the LMR-400 to the proper shape and position to connect to the device, and only then actually connect it.

Yes, you can make your own more cheaply. But I hate soldering on PL-259 connectors and don't like to do it unless I have to. If you want to do your own, great. I admire you. If you hate doing it, haven't had the practice or experience to feel comfortable making your own, then you can't go wrong with these.

product_title: Mohu Leaf 30 TV Antenna, Indoor, 30 Mile Range, Original Paper-thin, Reversible, Paintable, 4K-Ready HDTV, 10 Foot Detachable Cable, Premium Materials for Performance, USA Made, MH-110583
review_headline: Chicago First Floor Set-up: Works Perfectly!
review_body:
I was skeptical of how well this antenna would work. I live in Chicago. I live in a 3 floor apartment building on the first floor. My neighbor's building blocks the sky in the direction of the towers. Could this antenna possibly bring in a clear signal in this scenario??

Yes! Although it was not easy to find the best placement in my apartment. But I do not deduct any stars for that, as that is just the nature of the technology. My judgement stems totally from the antenna set-up in an optimal position to receive the signal. And it works almost flawlessly.

I saw "almost" flawlessly because I've had occasional moments of pixelation from time to time. But since my location here is far from ideal, I blame it on that, rather than the antenna. I'm sure if I had a clear view of the sky, things would be different. If you check out the picture attached to my review, you'll see my current set-up. My antenna is located on my wall in the corner, high up, next to the window. That wall faces the direction of all the antennas here in Chicago. However, you can see the neighboring house there. It blocks the direct line of sight, but I still get all the signals!

My initial placement took some time to master. Now, I will add that I am not connecting this antenna directly to my TV. I am hooking it up to my Tablo DVR (which is a cool device that allows you to record over the air TV!). The Tablo allows me to move my antenna wherever it needs to go, and it connects to my TV via Wi-Fi. So I had that flexibility. Even with that said, it took me awhile to find the exact location to get all of the channels. Some locations would bring in most, but not all. After a couple hours of experimenting, I found it! Near perfection.

For such a great price, and the amount of savings that this device can bring in the long term if you cut the cable cord, any initial set-up time is worth it. Please keep in mind that I am using this device a few miles from the towers in a major city. I can't speak for the antenna when using it a greater distance away. But for anyone in a major city, I think you'll be happy with this! I am.

product_title: Fiio X3 Mastering Quality Music Player w/ Wolfson DAC WM8740 24Bit 192K
review_headline: Excellent sound, reliable, good battery life
review_body: I bought this mainly for traveling. From Hawaii to San Francisco is about 5 hours and the battery was about half depleted so I assume the 10 hours is about right. The battery will not last from SF to China however like the ipod can. The audio is excellent with high quality headphones. I have Sennheiser at home and Denon noise cancelling for travel. Much better high low and mid range response than anything I have used before. Controls are intuitive and it was a no brainer to setup and use. However, when I first got it I had a little trouble formatting the 64 gig in the unit so had to format in pc with the special format utility they mentioned in the user group and formatted 64 gig no problem and transferred music no problem. So right after I updated to the latest firmware 3.3 I think and the user interface and everything else was 100% improvement with no problems whatsoever in anything I wanted it to do. So I plugged in a 128 gig card and worked no problem. I had to re rip all my CD's of course for the higher resolution FLAC 192 kbps and 24 bit. It takes up more space and 128 gig is not enough for all my cd's at that resolution. It is hard to navigate the controls in a dark setting like airplane and home at night as the buttons don't illuminate and not touch screen like ipod. The X3 has worked perfectly and no problems at all despite being on for 5 hours continuously and fairly heavy use when not flying. There is no video playback like the ipod or Sony devices but for price that's ok. There is no blue tooth or NFC like other players that are more expensive. Overall this is a well built and very reliable player with excellent updated firmware.

product_title: Thump Blu Sweat Resistant Bluetooth Headphones (Black/Pink)
review_headline: Good product, Horrible Customer Service from Manufacturer.
review_body:
While I love my Thump headphones and use them daily, the customer service department is horrible to work with. I actually own 2 pairs of these headphones. Recently my newest pair (rec'd them 1.5 months ago for Christmas) broke. The ear bud cracked off. I took a photo of it, emailed to it Thump's customer service department and was told they would replace my headphones with a different variety. One that is apparently sweat proof and better quality. However, they said I had to pay an upgrade charge. The website clearly spells out that "Thump products are warrantied against defects in materials and workmanship for a period of ONE (1) year from the original date of purchase. If a defect exists, Thump, at its option and to the extent permitted by law, will repair or replace the product at no charge. This warranty excludes damage resulting from abuse, accident, modifications or other causes that are not defects in materials and workmanship. This warranty does not affect your statutory rights." AT NO CHARGE is the key sentense here.

The email I rec'd from them also suggests if I don't want to pay I can pursue a refund with Amazon. However, their website states, "For warranty claims with products manufactured by Thump, do not pursue the claim with the dealer/store from which you purchased the product."

Ultimately, I decided to pay the Upgrade Charge and hope to receive the new ones in the mail shortly.

My last comment-the emailer from Thumps wrote "It is worth noting that the Thump's light weight design does require that one use it with particular care as explained in this snippet from the Thump Quick Start Guide: Thump Limitations: Your Thump is a sophisticated light weight piece of electronic equipment. Please treat it with care as you would an expensive pair of sun glasses. Avoid excessive flexing of the headphones as they may break if spread too far apart, voiding the warranty."

I'm sorry, but I honestly feel like he's calling me stupid. I KNOW these are delicate, but I'm not an idiot. I don't throw them in my gym bag, step on them, sit on them, etc. I paid good money for them and want to continue being able to use them daily. I'm not a dimwit, buddy.

review_body:
Sometimes you come across a product that really just blows you away. Braven's wireless bluetooth speaker system would fill that bill. Everything about it is superb, and puts previous bluetooth speakers I've used to shame!

The setup is easy; the bluetooth pairing was accomplished quickly with no burps. And the sound! I mean, wow, just wow. Rich, deep, but broad with no reverb. It fits neatly in a bookcase and amplifies music with an prodigious power. I was cleaning windows when this arrived. I set it up within minutes and synced it with my music library, and I was dancing while I worked within minutes!

The price of course is higher than you'd get for your average system, but the qualities and features of this set are so much more than average - and indeed, so much better than other systems in substantially higher price ranges - that I can endorse it unequivocally.

My only qualm is that I got this in black. Braven is a cool company that makes this system in amazing colors! I only wish I had gotten one of them. Yeah, I know, silly on my part, but the color choice is so amazing that I hope I can be forgiven for being a little focused on looks. The actual content, an amazing speaker system, is wonderful!

First off is the sizing, I have to wear a headband to get them to seal properly to hear any amount of bass. This is after attempting to squeeze the metal band together for a firmer fit. Which comes to the second problem, there just isn't enough bass in these to really tell how hard it is hitting, I have put a few test tracks into the car to listen to for any improvements I need to make and the first thing is always too much bass in the track. I love these headphones and I don't regret my purchase because it really helped me to appreciate a good set of monitor headphones but now I am looking forward for something from AKG with a little more bass, and around the same level mids, and highs, I am getting from this set. product_title: NO MORE SELLING
review_body:
What do you do if you want to take a shower, love singing while the water falls on your head but don’t dare to take the music device to be exposed to the humidity of your bathroom? You buy a water resistant stereo loud speaker and not only can you listen to your favourite music but in case the music comes through your mobile phone you can also answer your calls without having to wet the phone, how cool is that? I will be honest with you, when I was invited to test this loud speaker I didn’t even know that they existed! On the top you have the buttons that allow you to answer or end calls, to go to the previous or the next piece of music, to pause, control de volume, redial and even refuse a call!

The first thing I did was to charge it (the red light on the top goes off when the device is charged), then, as I don’t have any music in my mobile phone I paired it with the Taotronics transmitter that I have connected to my IPod (as I usually use it with their Donut). It only took a few seconds… I first turned the loud speaker on, a blue light started flashing, I then turned on the transmitter till the light was flashing red and blue and a few seconds later, when I turned on my iPod I could hear the music. It seems that I should have heard a bip as the pairing was finished but I must confess that I didn’t. No worries…. The music was playing and I could take my shower. The sound is very acceptable and the suction cup attached very well to the tiles in my bathroom (always better to wash the tiles so that they are free of grease or dust and for better suction wet the suction cup but those are things you do with any suction cup anyway!). I think that this loud speaker will be very useful as well around the pool, on the beach or even when you take a bath as there are always splashes of water and anyway you wouldn’t want to take the mobile phone or another expensive device into the humidity of a bathroom. The loud speaker is very light and weighs only 110g. Once you have paired it with your device you don’t have to do it again so the next time you use it just turn both devices on. It works within a distance of 10m. Don’t emerge the loud speaker into the water because it is water resistant to splashes of water, not to be placed under the water! When the battery is low you will hear a sound prompting you to recharge it but that I haven’t experienced yet because as I said I have only used it once. It seems that you can use it for 5 hours before having to recharge it, which means many hours of musical pleasure!

The warranty is as usual 12 months and it comes with a charging cable and an instruction manual. Great present to give to somebody….. very original too! I think that I will be listening to music in my bathroom a lot more often!

review_body:
We always seem to be searching for the next best thing in headphones... and now we have found a multi-functional on-ear headphone headset that greatly exceeds expectations, and that does not break the bank.

These Noontec ZORO II HD On-Ear Headphones have outstanding sound across the register, especially in the upper & lower ranges, and are very comfortable to wear. On top of that, the unit's tangle-free flat cable has an inline microphone that works perfectly when using for phone calls in the midst of your jam session. Outstanding. Very highly recommended.

Tested with our HTC Droid DNA and its Beats Audio application, and also with a Kocaso tablet that we have, and the first thing that my son and I noticed was how comfortable the bridge and the earphones are to wear. The ear cushions are firm but velvety soft and the padding across the bridge was quite comfortable. The design made us feel like these were custom-made just for us.

From the first few seconds of music, we both knew that these were not the typical run-of-the-mill headphones... the sound quality is excellent, with a true bass and treble sound really rising above other headphones I have used.

We played all sorts of music from jazz to blue, and rock to country, and.... whatever it is called that 15 year old boys listen to these days. Our music was generated from sources including Amazon's MP3 Cloud, Pandora and our own audio files, and the results were flawless. These Noontec ZORO II HD headphones produce true, powerful bass without compromising the rest of the spectrum, and responded very well to the equalizer applications on our devices. If I didn't have to concentrate to write this review, I would still be listening to their great, high-resolution sound right this moment.

While enjoying the music, we tested the call capabilities and were very impressed; the mechanics worked seamlessly and the clarity of the inline microphone is excellent. The voice heard through the ear speakers makes it sound as if you are standing next to the caller, while the answer button (on the mic) is easy to find by touch. Very simple & effective to use.

While the fit, feel & function of these Noontec headphones are first class, their look is quite nice too... they feel substantially made when in hand, and have that Beats-sleek look to them (without the crazy cost). The material used to make them seems very durable and scratch resistant.

Neither the Amazon listing or the very brief user manual provide any information on a warranty, so if an issue arises I will return here to update the review and let you know what the issue was and how resolution was handled. I did receive these headphones gratis from the seller and, with my son's assistance, put them to work to objectively see how well they performed. My statement here reflect that testing.... and my son has now claimed these as his new favorite headphones.

If you are looking for wired headphones of this style, great HD music playback capability, and price, for use similar to what I have described above, then my son and I would highly recommend giving these Noontec ZORO II HD Headphones a try based on our experience with them.

review_headline: The JungleConcert headphones are perfect if you love that deep rumbling bass ...
review_body:
Find yourself listening to Hardwell, Dmitri Vegas, or the likes of Martin Garrix? JungleConcert lives up to its name and captures that jungle beat, that bass that’s sometimes difficult to find. Unless you’re willing to spend some real money on headphones, you’re not going to find an all-around sound ... the clarity, a perfect soundstage (love this one), an exquisite surround sound experience.

Listening to “Tsunami” was a real experience to say the least. The leather ear cups and padded headband offer up a lot of comfort for hours of listening, and I’ve been listening to a lot of music with the JungleConcert headphones. These headphones lend themselves to genres that grind out that deep rumbling, thumping bass sound. House and Hip Hop are just a couple of them.

The soundstage is really decent and I love it when the sounds move rapidly from ear to ear. I can easily pick out the instruments. One good example would be Diplo & GTA’s “Boy Oh Boy.” The beat is heavy, but I can pick out those voices and each instrument as each is added or moving away. However, when you move into genres that add voices in the mid- to upper-range areas, some of that clarity is lost.

I certainly don’t fancy myself to be an audiophile by any means, but if you do you’ll probably wish to take a pass and move on up the line in price.

There’s no buzzing, static, nor muddling in those lower registers. It’s a tough sound to capture in Bluetooth-enabled headphones, but the JungleConcert has done it. The noise isolation isn’t bad and I didn’t hear much of anything going on around me in the room when I had them on. With 85dB it’s almost a given you won’t hear a lot.

The overall quality of the JungleConcert headphones is very good, but one end of the spectrum is sacrificed for the other. Just make sure you like that deep bass, lower register instrumentation and you’ll love these headphones. Pairing was easy, comfort factor high, and for once there was a thorough, comprehensive manual.

product_title: Bose SoundTrue In-Ear Headphones
review_headline: excellent quality, well worth the price
review_body:
I had my old Bose in-ear headphones for 4 years and the wire finally broke. I was concerned about the quality of these based on some reviews but these are just as clear as my old ones and give a very high quality sound. No added base like with Beats and these reflect the perfect quality of the song which is what I wanted. These are passive so you can hear outside noise and they do go loud enough for me (having lost a lot of my hearing from rock concerts)... but people around you can hear the music if you crank them. I also have a very expensive pair of Shure's that block out external noise which I use for traveling and those are much louder but this is to be expected with passive in-ear phones. These are great for frequent use, they go in and out quickly and the design of the rubber keeps them in place so they don't fall out easily when walking or running.
My only complaint, and I hope Bose reads this, is that the cord is kind of short... they are making the cords about 8 inches shorter than the old models and when I use on my laptop this restricts me from moving around too much.
Other than a slightly shorter cord, I like that they are using a straight slim plug - my Shures didn't fit through my cell phone case with the angled plug and this fits without issue in the smaller case holes.
I've owned Sennheiser, Shures, Beats, Bose and a bunch of other brands, and all-in-all, I think this is one of the best headphones you can buy and its well worth the price.

review_headline: Very happy with my first record player
review_body:
I am writing this as someone who has no memory of ever using a record player before. So if you are a record/record player connoisseur, this may not be helpful for you, because it seems that people who have grown up with records or who have an extensive knowledge of these things are unhappy with this record player.
However, to those of you who maybe want to start listening to records, I think this is a wonderful first record player! I don't find the sound bad at all and it definitely is loud enough for me. I mean, it's not a huge sound system, but I can't imagine why you would be expecting that with records or with something like this. I love it for what it is. It has a great sound with the records that I have, it plays them great, it's easy to use, and it's cute and convenient. I can bring this easily to other areas of my house, or ever to friends houses without any issue. I am very happy with this purchase!

review_headline: Great little speaker.  Read my review about battery charge if you're a runner.
review_body:
I think this is a great little speaker. I run with a friend and I clip this on my water belt and the sound is actually VERY good for a speaker this size. We can both hear it just fine and keep a conversation too.

If you're running for an hour, the speaker is great. My only issue has been the battery charge for our long runs. They advertise 2 hours, however, when we go over 75 minutes, the battery dies. I expect this is because I play it on full volume so we can both hear it. I'm sure if I kept it at a lower volume it would last the full two hours. Perhaps the manufacturer can respond to this.

We are running a half marathon soon. I'm thinking about getting a second one just as a back up during our run. I like the Tadpole and would recommend it.

product_title: HDTV Antenna and Amplifier, Liger® 50 Mile Range Ultra-Thin Indoor Antenna Plus Antenna Amplifier, Antenna Booster - Receive HD Television Signals for Free - Includes Adhesive & Stand
review_headline: Impressive antenna, though you may want to get one without an amplifier
review_body:
Wow, I was sure this wasn't going to work. I tried an unamplified HDTV antenna recently and got 0 channels. When I plugged this one in, it was about 7 feet too short to reach my window, so I just put it on the floor. I don't even receive a cell phone signal indoors. So I start a scan for channels and it finds not 1, not 5, not 10, but 45 of them! Now, most of them aren't usable and will probably improve when I change the position of the antenna, but I can actually see over half of them. About 15-20 are good enough to watch, and of those, maybe 4-6 of them I get clearly with no intermittent break up. Some are even in HD! I do live about 20 miles from a major city though, so if you're in the middle of nowhere this will probably not work unless you have a station within 25 to 40 miles. The range is probably around 50 miles with a decent line of sight. I am probably getting a range of around 25 miles with the antenna indoors. One thing to note though is that I got similar reception with or without the amplifier, so I am not sure if it is actually doing anything despite claiming a boost from 30 to 50 miles in range. I did see one channel that has poor reception go from no picture to no picture + intermittent sound with the amplifier. I compared this amplifier to the Mohu amplifier and found that the Mohu amplifier was slightly better, but still not very good. With the Mohu amplifier, I managed to get intermittent picture as well as sound on that channel.

I compared this antenna to a Mohu Leaf Ultimate (now called Mohu Leaf 50):
The Mohu gets about 20% better reception but it costs about 40% more and is about 30% larger.
So this Liger antenna is much better value for the money, though it would be nice if the antenna was sold separately from the seemingly useless amplifier.

product_title: TEAC TN-300 Analog Turntable
review_headline: Looks great, makes me wish I still had a lot of my old albums
review_body:
This turntable looks great and makes me wish that I still had more of the albums that I used to have, though the turntables I had back in the day did more than enough damage to those albums to make me glad that I've switched primarily to digital versions of the music that I favor.

Don't get me wrong, I like music on vinyl, but there were plenty of reasons to switch to digital and those reasons weren't just because of the scratches that would inevitably befall the music I had on vinyl platters. On the other hand, I would also note that digital lacks something compared to vinyl. There's just something about putting on a record and setting the needle down gently to play the material that is embedded there-in. Yes, even with the pops and hiss that might be there.

I love the looks of this item. It is aesthetically pleasing and fits very nicely into the area where I reserved space for it. It really does seem like a work of art (sculpture style).

Setup of this device was simple, and using this device is also very user friendly. Really there's not much to not like about this turntable. Not quite perfect, but really, really nice. 4 solid stars for me, and a big salute to TEAC for helping to keep vinyl alive.

product_title: Teac Wireless Streaming Music System
review_body:
I don't really have a decent Bluetooth speaker, and I liked the look of this unit, so I tried it.

This unit is very flexible. You can listen to the radio, play a CD (MP3 CDs included), connect via Bluetooth or Near-Field communication. It also functions as an alarm clock. You can access all the features from a very tiny remote that comes with it.

The sound is strong and rich for such a small speaker. I mainly connect using Bluetooth, and it works very well from my Android phone and computer. My wife has used the radio and CD functions, and has enjoyed them. It also looks cool sitting on my shelf.

I haven't used the alarm feature. I don't use speakers in my bedroom and I won't drag this up there at night just for that. The display is also kind of small.

The major drawback for me is the price. The speakers themselves are decently loud and clear, but you can buy much larger Bluetooth speakers for the same price. If you are looking for a cool, retro-looking radio/alarm clock, and CD player, then the price is all right. If you mainly want Bluetooth speakers, then find something else.

Overall, I like this. The sound is good, and it looks really cool.

product_title: V-MODA Crossfade M-100 Over-Ear Noise-Isolating Metal Headphone
review_headline: Great sound, top notch quality backed up by great customer service
review_body: I purchased my shadow m-100's from V-moda directly.    These headphones are absolutely amazing. I've listened to a lot of different headphones in different categories, best being the Sennheiser HD650 which also had a dedicated amp connected to it. After trying out 20+ headphones, I found the V-moda's to be the absolute best to suit my needs. Here's why.  1. Design - these headphones look and feel amazing. The construction is unmatched. I haven't handled another pair of headphones that feel as solid as these. The quality of the material is also amazing. Everything feels premium and I expected to do so when you pay this much for headphones. In comparison, the HD650's which cost almost twice as much as this, were made of plastic, and while they were built well, they just didn't feel premium. These headphones also are somewhat low profile so you don't look like an alien when you're using them in public.  2. Sound - While these might not have a flat response and the bass is elevated just slightly, make no mistake, these headphones are a great studio and general use headphones. They articulate the sound very well and every note in the music comes out crystal clear. The fact that they have slightly higher bass, makes them a lot more fun to listen to. And the bass is just amazing, it's really tight and goes really, really low. The soundstage (openness of the music) is amazing for a closed headphone. And last but not least, these can easily be driven by a portable music player such as a laptop or a smartphone and still sound amazing. The headphone does benefit from having an amp, but it's not necessary.  3. Portability - These are the best portable full-sized headphones. They fold up really small and fit into a provided hard shell case which looks amazing. The case has a little clip on it which you can attach to a bag.  4. product_title: Braven BRV-X Portable Wireless Speaker - Retail Packaging
review_headline: Pretty Good, but treble range sounds harsh, also wish it played louder
review_body: I have been looking at bluetooth speakers for a while now, trying to get something that sounds good, that does not go over the $200 price range.  I read a couple of very favorable reviews of the BRV-X on PC Mag, as well as Digital Trends. While I am not an audiophile by any means, I am particular about the quality of my music, and I do like a good bass presence as well as midrange and treble.    The BRV-X has 2 Audio Modes, or Audio Settings under the cap that unscrews on the back of the device - I tested all my music on the Indoor setting, versus the Outdoor setting. The Indoor setting is more balanced and sounds much better. The BRV-X does have strong bass, it sounds really amazing. And like the reviews stated, the midrange is wonderful on this. But many times where the device does not sound as good as it should is the treble range. The treble response is too harsh, and on a lot of songs, it just was not a pleasant sound. Certain music sounded very clear and amazing on the BRV-X, but it just could not cut it on other music.    A couple of weeks after I purchased the BRV X, another bluetooth speaker that I had been following went on sale at TigerDirect, the Klipsch KMC 1 - so I bought the Klipsch and compared the 2. First off, the Klipsch does get a lot louder than the BRV-X. I know that having a higher Max Volume does not mean better sound, and truth is, the KMC 1 does sound better when it's played at a louder volume, but even at lower volumes the KMC 1 just sounded much clearer, and the treble was not harsh like the BRV-X. The bass response was also stronger on the KMC 1. I like the BRV-X's midrange response better than the KMC 1, but what it boiled down to for me, was again, harsh treble response on the BRV-X just diminished the sound quality of it.    The advantage of the BRV-X is that It's definitely much more portable, and I like that it's water and shock resistant. It's compact enough to bring anywhere, and I would feel much more confident bringing the BRV-Xwith me on the road versus the KMC 1. The downside of the KMC 1 is that it's heavy, and it's just not as portable, it's sort of awkward to carry around, like an oversized brick. I wish Klipsch would have included some sort of handle on it, or an easier way to move it around.  The BRV-X also had great battery life. I didn't calculate the usage, but I could play it for a few hours, and still have battery life left.    The KMC 1 was originally priced at $300, but I picked it up on sale for $130 at TigerDirect, less than half off. And I was able to get the BRV-X for $150 right after Thanksgiving, so being that the sales prices of both of these were so close, I decided to compare them. I am more into classical music and rock and pop from a few decades ago, versus listening to more recent music.    The one other downside of the BRV-X is I wish it played a little louder. It does not play as loud when you have the Audio Mode on the Indoor Setting versus the Outdoor Setting, which is disappointing. If you want it to play louder, switch it over to the Outdoor setting, but the sound quality is not as good.     One other thing to note, is the battery is not replaceable on the BRV-X. I am not sure how long the rechargeable batteries last, or how many charges it will take before this becomes an issue. Being that it's water resistant, I would think that Braven had to seal the battery in the device to accomplish this. Probably not an issue to most people, but when the battery dies, the unit would be useless. Many other units, including the KMC 1 have a replaceable battery.    I have read a lot of reviews on bluetooth speakers for a while, and I have walked into stores and listened to certain devices as well. I know the regular Bose Soundlink is supposed to be the best, but I don't feel like dropping $300 on a bluetooth device. I do like the Bose Soundlink Mini, and even though it's small, the sound quality of the Mini is really amazing. The Mini would have been my next choice. I like the Logitech UE Boom which is also supposed to be water resistant, but I read a lot of reviews that it did not have strong enough bass response, so I didn't consider the UE Boom. Same issue with the JBL Charge - and there are bass distortion issues with the Charge, even at lower volumes.    I will be returning the Braven BRV-X and keeping the Klipsch KMC 1. Despite some drawbacks of the KMC 1, the sound quality makes this the winner for me. If Braven could improve the treble response on this, It would be a keeper.
