review_headline: Decent (for the price) but halves collapses easily.
review_body:
Everything I write here is under the "..for the price" caveat.

Headphones: August EP-650
Paid: 7.99 (Prime)
Rating: more like 3.75

Pros:
Arrived in 24 hrs to So. California. They fit my August EP650 headphones well if not slightly snug. The width fits great. Quality is decent..again for the price. I've only had it for a day, but the zipper is fairly smooth and the case comes with a carabiner.

Cons:
The one biggest gripe is that the two halves don't stay aligned. So when closed and any type of pressure is applied the two halves essentially collapse. This gives very little protection from being crushed if something heavy were to fall on it or if packed very tightly in a suitcase for example. The material, though not very rigid (think heavy/thick cardboard), should give some protection against light to medium thrashing about. But I wouldn't trust it too much.

Again decent 'for the price' and for light to medium everyday protection.

PS. I wouldn't trust the little fabric loop for the carabiner either.

product_title: Sennheiser Digital Wireless Headphones
review_body: I love these headphones.  I have been a fan of Sennheiser for years and have pitied people who shell out as much as $ 400 for Beats.  Germans are obsessive, which is why they are such incredible engineers and they did everything right with these. They are lightweight, I have never run out of battery life (of course, I put them back on the stand when I am done with them) and are probably the most comfortable headphones I have ever owned, but the biggest reason I love them is the SOUND.  What I am looking for in a pair of headphones is faithful reproduction of sound, not artificial booming bass, but balanced sound through the range.  The trebles are crisp and clear, the mids and bass are both precise. When I first received them, I listened to a range of music (including the two "standards" I use to sample speakers and headphones, "Abbey Road" by the Beatles, "Aja" by Steely Dan and "Beethoven's 9th Symphony" conducted by Herbert van Karajan and the Berlin Symphony Orchestra on Deutsche Grammaphon.  All were impeccable.  I have also been using them to listen to Blu-ray discs and they are fantastic for that.  I have a 5.1 surround sound system, which I love, but there are times when I want to watch a movie and not disturb others.  When I was shopping, I seriously considered getting the RS 160s, which have a surround sound mode, but I have no complaints about these.  I can walk around the house with them, I listen to music when I cook. I am very glad that I bought them and would highly recommend them to anyone.

review_headline: Works perfect as an ethernet extender (e.g., home theater PC)
review_body:
I have a home theater PC running Windows Media Center and recently bought an XBox 360 to use as a media center extender. Unfortunately, over 802.11n, video intermittently got choppy and the menus were slow to navigate. The former was the more bothersome of problems, so I did some researching online for alternatives.

Ideally, I would be able to run an ethernet cable from my home theater PC to my XBox 360, but I'm renting, and doing an ethernet run through our finished basement was out of the question.

I looked at MoCA adapters (Multimedia over Cable Alliance) which pipe ethernet signals over coaxial cable; however, they started at ~$80 per adapter (and you would need at least two adapters). I came across these DECA adapters, which were originally designed by DirecTV to give people the ability to use their DVRs (which require an ethernet connection) in homes that don't have ethernet run everywhere. However, these don't work just with DirecTV boxes--they work with any ethernet connection.

The one caveat is that the signal uses the frequencies used by traditional cable, so you will not be able to use this on cables that are carrying cable signals. Here is how I set it up:

The coax sticking out of the adapter connects to the included power adapter. The other end plugs into a cable outlet in your house SEPARATE from the one you are recieving TV on. You then plug into the adapter the ethernet cable and connect the other end to your router. You then have to go to your basement (or wherever all of your cables come together) and use a coupler to connect the free end of the coax cable coming from where the adapter is plugged in to the second room you want to connect to. Then, in the room you are extending to, connect the second DECA adapter the same way (run a cable from the wall to the adapter; plug in the power adapter to the coax tail coming from the device, and connect the ethernet connection to your device).

DECA reportedly gets speeds up to 100 Mbps. I haven't been able to do a formal speed test, but it streams video flawlessly from Windows Media Center and fast forwards and menus have very little latency.

P.S. If you can't figure out in your basement which cable goes to which room, what you can do us unplug all cables from your splitter (i.e., disconnect from antenna or cable provider), then connect the power adapter to the wall plug in the room you are looking for (you will need a spare coax cable and a coupler to do this), then plug the tail of the DECA adapter (again, using a coupler) into each of the coax connections in your basement until the power light goes on--then you have the right one!

review_headline: Compact size with some nice features, but a couple of misses as well
review_body:
Overall, this is a decent bluetooth speaker especially considering the price point. The sound quality (again, considering the price) is pretty good – decent amount of bass, and generally clear upper and mid range. It doesn’t like being pushed hard at high volume, but considering the size, it’s not meant to be something to fill a room with sound. For desktop use it’s fine, and a definite improvement over built-in speakers in a tablet or similar device.

I like the overall size – very compact, and takes up very little desktop space. The size also makes it very easy to toss into a bag and bring along with you.

The build quality seems pretty good. It has a nice, solid feel to it. The case has a rubberized-type coating which makes it pretty non-slip. The grill feels like it is made of metal, and has an attractive “dimple” design.

No problems with pairing, and the range is quite good (had no problems at about 20 feet). My favorite feature is the removable battery. While the capacity is not the best (1020 mAh), the fact that it can be replaced is a big plus, since all Li-on batteries eventually fail to hold a charge.

There are a few misses, however. The control buttons on the top are all the same size and the markings are black on black, making it pretty much impossible to determine which button does what unless you’re in very strong, direct light. After a while you can figure it out, but better markings would be much better.

I don’t like that it does not use a standard 3.5mm cable to direct-connect to a source. It needs a micro USB type cable, which is included. However, that means I have to bring that specific cable with me should I want to direct connect rather than just a standard 3.5mm cord.

The battery compartment door is rather flimsy. It feels cheap compared with the rest of the unit.

It has annoying voice announcements. This seems to be all the rage these days on these inexpensive speakers. What’s wrong with a simple beep sound?

The negatives drop my rating to 3.5 stars. I’ll round up to 4 since, for the price, you get a pretty decent sound in a compact shape with a removable battery. A good, but not great speaker for the price.

product_title: Sennheiser Headphones
review_headline: Got a $100, looking for open headphones?  Look no more
review_body:
These are the best headphones made in their price range.
First, these are the most comfortable headphones I have ever worn. There are many reasons for their comfort in my opinion. One reason is because they are open, which allows air in to keep your ears cool. Secondly, the soft covering on these headphones are non-abrasive when placed against your head. Lastly, since they are made of good quality plastic, they are light, so they are hardly noticeable after many hours of use.
Second, these are certainly audiophile quality headphones when it comes to the sound they produce. They produce solid bass, great mids, and clear highs. The sound is also NOT as though you are in a tunnel like most close headphones, which is exactly what I wanted. Also, if you need to be able to hear what's going on around, while wearing these headphones, you just need to turn the volume down a little. On the other hand, if you want more immersion, you just need to turn up the volume a little and you are good to go. I have listened to the movie Lord of the Rings, which gave a good surround sound experience. I have listened to all kinds of music, which has given good bass for club, nice mids for rock, and clear highs for classical.
Lastly, the build quality and looks bring a smile to my face. Although, some might not like the side grill of these headphones, I love it. These headphones are very well put together and I have no worry about them lasting for many years. I also like the colors of grey, black, and white. They look refined and not childish. You can also remove the plug from these headphones by pressing upward and then twisting, which is great.
If you are looking for a pair of headphones for around $100 then just buy these now. I got them for around $83 at a discount, so if you can get them on discount even better.

product_title: Able Planet Sound Clarity Active Noise-Cancelling Flat-Fold Headphones
review_body:
I'm impressed right out of the box. The case is great (albeit a bit bulky) and will offer excellent protection for these headphones while travelling. These are replacing a pair of pink XNC230's my wife had and she broke the headband portion while travelling (it's hinged plastic).

SOUND: Out of the box I put the batteries (yes, two AAA) into the left headphone, plugged them into my Droid Turbo and went straight to Spotify (Premium subscription so I get 320Kbps MP3). With the noise cancelling switch powered "off", the headphones sounded flat but when you flip the switch to "on", the sound was very impressive. Extremely impressive even for a $40 pair of noise cancelling headphones. I started with The White Stripes and was immediately impressed by the clean bass reproduction on "Icky Thump". Megs bass drum came through loud and clear without muddying up Jacks lyrics or guitar on Catch Hell Blues. I then moved on to Fleetwood Mac "The Dance" in my iTunes music. "The Chain" sounded great ... the initial bass drum got your attention immediately, again, thumping without any distortion. Spatially I didn't feel like I was there, I can tell these are closed back noise cancellation headphones but nevertheless, the sound is good. I wouldn't give these 5 stars if I were paying full MSRP (maybe 4) but at $40, well, lets just say probably the best $40 set of cans I've bought. Comparing these is tough because they're the only NC headphones I own but as for sound quality, I'd put them above the Monsters and maybe even the Beats ...

COMFORT: I've now had these on for a little over two hours and my ears aren't hot in any way and they feel quite comfortable. The pleather and padding used for the ear cups (a little smallish) is quite supple especially since they've never been worn. All in all, very happy so far.

I'll update the review later if necessary ...

Currently own Sony MDR-X10 and X05's, Monster Ntune, V-Moda Crossfade LP2s, Polk Hinge, Beats Mixr & Solo HD and now the AP NC550BC's.

product_title: Powerex MH-C9000 WizardOne Charger-Analyzer for 4 AA or AAA NiMH Batteries
review_headline: It will NOT fully charge your Eneloops
review_body:
I bought the MH-C9000 charger to upgrade from my La Crosse BC-700. I chose it over the BC-900 because the La Crosse chargers leave very little space between the cells for heat dissipation.

The MAHA does seem like a quality item in terms of features and build quality. It has ample space between the cells, though consequently it's rather large. I wanted to give it a higher rating, but it doesn't adequately do what I bought it for and what you would probably be buying it for.

TWO MAIN PROBLEMS:

- It does not fully charge Eneloop and comparable batteries.

- The discharge cycle is too conservative to realistically report battery capacity.

The first problem has been alluded to by NLee, but I believe it may be worse than suspected. Both problems are easily demonstrated. A simple summary of my tests with a 2000 mAh Eneloop AA cell is as follows:

- Charged and discharged with the BC-700, battery capacity tested as 2060 mAh. This illustrates a full charge as well as a realistic discharge test.

- Charged with the BC-700 and discharged with the MH-C9000, battery capacity tested as 1980 mAh. This illustrates a discharge test with the MAHA that will give you a reading below the rated capacity even with a properly charged battery in good condition.

- Charged and discharged with the MH-C9000, battery capacity tested as 1880 mAh. This illustrates less than a full charge in the MAHA combined with a low reading in the discharge test.

THE CHARGING PROBLEM:

The best indication of full charge is negative delta V, the dip in terminal voltage that occurs when the battery is full. The La Crosse BC-700 correctly charges to this point and terminates when the terminal voltage reaches 1.55 v and drops to 1.54 v. Voltage settles to 1.49 v after termination and stabilizes at 1.51 v after some hours on trickle charge. All of this is correct operation.

The fact that the MH-C9000 can theoretically also terminate on negative delta V is irrelevant, because it never gets that far. It terminates when the battery reaches a particular terminal voltage. I didn't catch the exact number, but it is less than 1.50 v, which is definitely too low for a full charge. Contrary to suggestions that leaving the battery in the charger will top it off, the terminal voltage stabilizes at 1.45 v and remains there regardless of how long the battery is in the charger.

THE BOTTOM LINE:

To ensure I didn't have a unit with obsolete firmware, I exchanged several messages with a support engineer who assured me that I had an up-to-date unit that was performing as designed. Thus, I don't like the way it was designed to perform.

With the MH-C9000, you have a charger that doesn't work well for giving your LSD batteries a full charge. It also doesn't work well for testing the capacity of your batteries. Those are the two most important performance factors for me and probably for you.

I still want an alternative to the La Crosse BC-700/900, but I can't recommend the MH-C9000 for this. product_title: Polk Audio Omni S2 Compact Wireless Wi-Fi Music Streaming Speaker with Play-Fi
review_headline: Polk Omni S2 vs Klipsch KMC 1
review_body: I compare this Polk [had it since Xmas] to the Klipsch KMC1,  which is costing about the same price on Amazon, as of today at ~$129, despite their differences in list price.  the Polk Omni S2 speaker is bass heavy due to over boost. I called Polk technical support, and there is no way that the user can adjust EQ to alleviate the bass (at least for the foreseeable future, until they come up with an app) . As a consequence of the heavy bass, you tend to hear the echo or resonant/coloration of low frequency musical passages, which is annoying!  This leads to poor and distorted midrange and high frequency responses.   If you listen to rock or radio talk, it's probably OK, since the annoyance is not perceived noticeably.    However for classical or vocal passages, the effects become obvious.    In terms of connectivity, Polk is among a few first to adopt Play-Fi, that uses your Wi-Fi network for transmission, you can extend to multiple speakers.   While the Klipsch still uses bluetooth for personal listening.  The advantage of Play-Fi, one can argue, is that it has higher bandwidth, but still requires the presence of a Wi-Fi network [e.g. if you're on a remote campsite, the 3.5mm cable comes to the rescue].  but at the end of the day, the sound is what determines the worthiness of the speaker.  Other the note is the Omni S2 by itself is a mono speaker, while the Klipsch is set up as a stereo unit. so for soundstage and musicality the Klipsch is better.  The bass on the Klipsch is not as heavy as on the Polk (cutoff at 65Hz), but it's tight and neutral.  Overall, I enjoy the Klipsch much better for the kind of music we are listening.  Another consideration is one has to double up the cost to achieve the stereo sounding on the Polk.    On the other hand, if you are into the heavy bass, and listen mostly to rock, then the Polk will give you plenty of the hefty bottom.

review_headline: Helps a lot if you are far away from TV towers and sometimes get a "choppy" picture/sound
review_body:
[I don't post reviews until after I've used something for at least 3 months (or longer). Don't you wish everyone on Amazon would do that?]

Our condo is on the 2nd floor in a rural area, but still about 50 miles away from the nearest TV broadcast tower. So, I bought a Mohu Leaf indoor antenna and taped it up high near our window facing the direction that the TV signals are coming from. (In our case, our windows were on the side of our building *opposite* the direction of the TV towers, so I had to aim the antenna to catch the *reflected* TV waves bouncing off the walls of a condo building next to us. Some people aren't aware that TV/radio waves bounce or reflect off buildings like most waves do).

I used the TVfool website's helpful "MAPS" feature in order to see from which direction the TV signal was coming from. (That website works best if you enter your antenna height above ground, then click the box to turn on the green lines to see which direction the *thick* green lines are coming from, then turn on Satellite Map view to zoom in on the map & then drag the red push pin over top your home on the map).

In the end, I was even able to pick up 1 or 2 stations that the website said I wouldn't be able to pick up. But because we are 50 miles away from the TV towers, the TV signal was weak and our TV picture/sound was "choppy" sometimes.

So THEN, I also bought this TV signal amplifier from Winegard. Now we are watching HD quality broadcast TV on six channels out here for FREE. These are CBS, FOX (for watching football games), a Spanish speaking HD channel that I don't understand since I don't speak Spanish, 2 Public Television PBS/MPT channels (one HD channel and one non-HD channel), and also a "classic TV shows" channel that has old shows like "I dream of Jeanie", "The Brady Bunch", etc.

Some indoor HDTV antennas come with a built-in signal amplifier, since a signal amplifier usually works best attached closer to your antenna so it can boost the signal thru the long cable going into the back of your TV. But if the TV signal is strong enough anyway, then I prefer to skip the hassle of finding a separate power plug for the signal amplifier, and instead I like the simplicity of using an amplifier powered by the USB cord (it was included) that I can just plug into the back of my HDTV (see picture down below). That way, by plugging the amplifier's USB power cord into the back of your TV, when you turn off your TV on or off, the signal amplifier also turns on or off at the same time too! (This wouldn't be the case if you had a long co-axial extension cable to your antenna located in a window far away from your TV set, thus forcing you to plug in the signal amplifier into a 2nd power outlet somwplace else since it's too far away to reach your TV's USB power port.)

review_headline: Pretty cool!!! Have really enjoyed it so far!!!

There are a couple of things that I should note that account for the lost star: 1) this multi-hybrid tube amplifier is not shielded, so it does pick up noise from my iPhone and my computer (@  distances less than/equal to 12"), 2) like others, I would highly recommend swapping out the stock tube with an aftermarket one (I have thoroughly enjoyed the JJ tube I mentioned above), 3) the biggest disappointment I have in choosing this model over the V1 is that this model (V2) does not have trim pots to adjust the bias between the two channels (the volume levels of my left and right channels are not at equal with a bias towards the right channel. To date, my soldering/electronic skills have only been developed building custom speakers/repairing damaged wiring, so I am gearing up to get my arms into finer circuit board work with this amp and install trim pots to account for the lack of them on this model in addition to making the additional mods suggested on audio forums (some great info on Rockgrotto like others have mentioned).

product_title: ARCTIC P253 BT - Bluetooth
review_body:
I got these because my other "strap behind the neck" Bluetooth headphone just broke and I wanted an inexpensive replacement. Hence, my expectations for sound quality were not all that high; I just wanted something I can wear when doing household chores or spinning on my bike (not road riding - too dangerous not being able to hear traffic!) and this fit the bill.

It sounds fine, and works okay when a phone call comes in (that is, the other party can hear me well). My only concern about it is that the Bluetooth connection seems to get spotty even though the distance between the phone and the headset is a few feet. Case in point, I was doing yard work this weekend wearing the headphones and had the iPhone in my back pocket - and there were a number of times when the music started to get static-y or there were short gaps in the play, as if the connection were breaking. Just kind of annoying - I didn't have to reset anything.

I guess it could have been the phones' battery was getting low, but there's no way to actually tell. On my other pair, there was a little icon on the iPhone shooing (crudely) now much charge was left in the headphone battery - I don't se that for this one. But that's a minor complaint - certainly for the price these are quite nice.

review_headline: Good price, good performance, no problems 3 days in.  See my added material for a second purchase I made marked with +++++
review_body:
There are a lot of these models of charger for sale and I looked at the reviews of a whole bunch of them. Overall it seemed that most got a 4 star rating and if you looked at the details of the ratings it was common for there to be 20 "bad" ratings for every 60 "good" ratings. One common thread for the bad ratings was that the charger got really hot, sometimes to the point of melting some portion of it. There didn't seem to be much variation in the ratings with price until you paid over $30+ dollars and even those had some portion of bad reviews for one reason or another. So this one had the typical 4 star rating and a low price so I picked it. My observations after a couple of days.... The plug fits nice and snugly into the computer. The cords are quite a bit shorter than is typical of OEM power packs that come with new computers. Longer would have been nicer. It came with a two prong plug which was what was shown in the ad. There has not been a problem with my Dell D820 recognizing this power pack, which was something people sometimes complained about with these inexpensive power packs. It also will both charge the battery AND run the computer at the same time.

So, what about "how hot does it get"? If all it's doing is running the computer cuz the battery is already fully charged it just gets warm, 105 degrees. If the computer is off but the battery is charging it gets pretty warm, nearly hot, I measured it to be around 115 degrees case temperature. If it's both charging the battery and running the computer at the same time it gets hot, around 125 degrees in the hottest spots of the case. It will charge the battery pretty fast, I didn't time it but it seemed like it only took a few hours.

Based on my 3 days of use I would say this is a good buy, just be prepared for it to be hot if you are using the computer at the same time it needs the battery charged. Because it gets so hot I would not leave my computer on with the battery charging if I wasn't home to keep an eye on it. I wouldn't be worried if the battery was already charged up as it doesn't run hot in that case.

product_title: C Crane CC Skywave AM, FM, Shortwave, Weather and Airband Portable Travel Radio with Clock and Alarm
review_body:
I'm surprised that, after all the buzz about this radio on hobbyist websites and blogs, nobody has posted about it here. So I'm giving a quick overview as I await my second Skywave Radio (having ordered the first one directly from CCrane and decided that this one is \\"keeper\\")

This is the official update to the well-regarded CCrane shortwave portable (SWP) which is still for sale; both having been sourced from Redsun in China. It is also a re-work of an intermediate Redsun model not sold in the US, but known in Australia as the Digitech AR-1733 and in Japan as the Elpa ER-C57WR.

The radio covers MW/SW/FM and the aircraft band (omitting LW that previous models covered). It appears to use DSP (digital signal processing) technology like many newer models sourced from Tecsun in China and sold under various brands including Kaito, Grundig, etc. Such radios achieve pretty exceptional performance using a minimum of electrical components because the SiLabs DSP chip does most of the traditional RF stuff right inside. However, all have suffered from various design or performance compromises including uneven sensitivity, unwanted noises, and the implementation of the SiLab chips \\"soft mute function\\" which enraged DXers because, rather than amplifying weak MW/SW signals actually does the opposite; making them \\"fall off the cliff\\" once signal strength goes below a cutoff.

The Ccrane SWP was a more traditional PLL/superhet design that was well conceived except for an occasional annoying design flaw: a digital up/down volume adjustment in lieu of a traditional knob; it powered up too loud, had steps that were too coarse to get the volume right, and you could not lower the volume enough to make for comfortable listening through headphones. The AR-1733 which is the immediate predecessor to this model, has serious performance issues on MW.

The designers of Skywave appear to have taken all of this in; perhaps that is why the release of the radio was delayed so many times. In using it side by side with older models, all the good points stand out. Sensitivity is remarkably good, especially on MW where strong AGC action and excellent useable sensitivity gives great volume even from daytime fringe stations - comparable to larger sets like the PL-660 for instance. Volume control is once again handled using a traditional analog knob. All 5 of the SiLabs \\"virtual filter\\" bandwidth settings are implemented (6 - 4 - 3 - 2 -1 KHz) and work very well. The odd tones and artifacts of previous DSP designs are mostly gone. I cannot detect any evidence of \\"soft-mute\\" being activated. In fact, the overall \\"feel\\" and sound of the Skywave reminds one of all the best points of PLL/superhet sets of a few years back (e.g. Tecsun PL-200/Eton E100, etc). Also for me, where many radios suffer bleed-through of strong MW signals all over the place, the front-end selectivity of this radio is admirably good.

Compared to Tecsun DSP sets some differences stand out. There is no digital signal strength display, only a bar graph. The sound from the speaker is rather tinny (even with the \\"hidden\\" audio tone control set to \\"music\\"). There is no direct control over the dial light. A nice feature that the AR-1733 had (ability to lock the tuning wheel - only) is not carried over. Also many have criticized the lack of SSB capability; not an issue of size really (ages ago, the even smaller Sony ICF-SW100 implemented SSB as well as synchronous AM) but perhaps cost and the capabilities of the available DSP chips.dio was delayed so many times. product_title: SONOS Compact Wireless Speaker for Streaming Music
review_headline: Great speaker, but Spotify experience is not very good.
review_body: Reviewing a system like Sonos is not easy.  It's so versatile, people use it with many different types of set up.  This review is for people that uses Spotify as the primary source of music. Sonos makes fantastic hardware and for a tiny looking speaker like the Play:1 it sure packs a lot of volume.  The sound is rich and very satisfying like most reviews have said here.  However if you use Spotify and use the new features frequently you will only get the barebone experience on Sonos.    Let me tell you a few things about my situation and needs:  -I am new to Sonos and the Play:1 is the first and only Sonos I purchased.  -I recently bought into Spotify Premium and stopped using iTunes.  -My music taste is on the verge of one of those taste changing cycles.  -I really like Spotify's radio function and I hate making playlist.    But to my surprise, Sonos and Spotify does not play well together, none of the new features from Spotify is there, no radios, no \\"My Music\\", no social integration, either you play from a playlist or search for something to play.  This caused a lot of frustration as I've been using Spotify's save to My Music function instead of adding musics to a Playlist.  Now to use Sonos, I have to start using more Playlists, and no Spotify radio support is also a major inconvenience.  As I understand this is not Sonos' fault (Spotify's API for 3rd party is very limited, and a new thing called Spotify Connect making it somewhat of a competitor to Sonos, hence the limited API), so I don't see Spotify opening up their app anytime soon.    Sorry I didn't mean to turn this into a Spotify review, but as the heavyweight of the music streaming services I think people should know the limitations of Spotify on Sonos. Google Play Music on the other hand works well, radio is supported and you can even play to Sonos directly from the Google Play Music app, bypassing the Sonos app entirely.  However Google Music does not have a desktop client and the web interface is notideal. I'm still debating on the best streaming service to use with this system. I wish Sonos could simply make it easier to play whatever you want to hear from your device without being limited by the Sonos app, depends on the usage but sometimes I'm okay with draining the battery on my phone/tablet or leaving my computer on, but please give me the options Sonos!

product_title: AmazonBasics Ultra Thin Indoor HDTV Antenna
review_body:
Decided to up my tailgating game and buy a generator and a TV for this year's Florida-Georgia game in Jacksonville. Was considering adding a portable DirecTV receiver and antenna but read on a couple of blogs that a HDTV antenna would be more than adequate. I decided to risk it and am very happy that I did. The TV signal was crystal clear. We had people stopping by our tailgate all day asking us how we were getting such a great signal. I used 3M Command Adhesive Strips to mount the antenna to a side window on the outside of my SUV and it worked perfectly. Great purchase (I used the 50 Mile Range version) which I highly recommend.

If you Google it, there's a website that gives you expected signal quality for the various over the air stations that are available based on the location you enter so you know what to expect.

product_title: Powebeats 2 wireless
review_headline: Perfect!!! Audio, video sync issues fixed via firmware update!
review_body:
The $200 powerbeats2 are well built, good sounding earphones that feel great when put on...extremely light and comfortable. Unfortunately, as the title suggests, there is a 2 second lag in audio while watching a video. I tried these with an iPhone 6 and iPad air, both updated to iOS 8.1.1. I also tried 2 other brands, Jaybird and Jabra, the latter costing almost half the price, that did NOT exhibit any lag whatsoever. Of course a 2 second lag while listening to music is not a big deal but is extremely annoying when trying to watch a movie or a YouTube video.

In response to my email, beats customer service says they are looking into the lag issue but do not have any specifics if or when a fix will be available. What a shame! I was so excited to finally get my hands on this product, but now I'm just as disappointed! Returned!

UPDATE 12/16/14
The 2 second lag in audio while watching video has been fixed via a firmware update. I have since purchased these again and am very happy with the experience. Way more comfortable than any Bluetooth headset out there and a more balanced sound profile compared to Jaybird and Jabra.

product_title: SHARKK® Bluetooth 4.0 BoomBox Speaker, 18 Hour Playtime, 10 Watt Portable Speaker System, 4400 mAh Li-ion Battery, Ultra Bass Subwoofer Sound Effect / Built In Mic For Calls / NFC Function / For All iPhone / iPhone 6 / iPhone 6 Plus / All iPad / iPad Air 2 / All Phones / Samsung Galaxy Phones and Tablets / Laptops
review_body: If you're the average person who likes listening to music with speakers that are better than your speakerphone (Galaxy Note 4) but don't want to waste money experimenting with portable bluetooth speakers, then this is the review for you. I'm not an audiophile but I hear well enough to tell if a speaker sounds clear and crisp.    Packaging: I really liked the design of the box that contained the speakers. The top and bottom slide off revealing a nicely packaged speaker along with instructions, a usb charging cable with AC adapter, an AUX cable, and (surprise!!) a cloth carrying bag. The instructions were clear and simple to follow. Overall, better then vacuum sealed plastic items and rivals packaging of my Samsung Galaxy Note 4 ($800) item.    Build: I was quite surprised at the weight of the speakers. The speakers are not \\"heavy\\" but have a nice hefty feel that screams quality and does not feel \\"plastiky.\\" It does not feel slippery when held and is quite easy to carry around one-handed. The material used does not feel cheap.    Sound: Loved the startup sound. Reminds me of movies where a planet implodes - AWESOME! It's not loud and annoying but is a good indicator of the bass that is possible with this little thing. The speaker actually rumbled when I turned it on. The bass was nice but not window-shattering or water ripple-making. If you want window-shattering bass then you are obviously looking at the wrong speaker. The sound stays crisp and clear even at highest volume.    Pairing: I've tested the speaker at a 20 ft range and it still worked fine. The NFC option was so useful I didn't have to manually pair my phone through the usual bluetooth scanning, entering passkey, etc. I laid my Galaxy Note 4 (speaker side) onto the top of the speaker's mic area and it paired.    Controls: The controls worked fine with my Galaxy Note 4. I was able to answer calls, pause, play, and skip songs. I would have liked to see the battery meter show up on my phone like what other reviewers claim on Apple products. I feel like Android doesn't get love sometimes. Not a deal breaker but would be a nice feature since it's already available for Apple products.    Overall: 5 stars for awesome sound and build quality. I haven't found any complaints so far. Maybe I'm just more forgiving on little flaws but I haven't found any on this speaker. I get great sound for a decent price and that's all I need. If I do find any flaws, however, I will definitely be updating this review. The last thing I need is another paper weight.

product_title: Powerbeats2 Wireless In-Ear Headphone - Blue (Old Model)
review_headline: These headphones cannot be charged any longer!
review_body:
This product was delivered on Monday, September 29, 2014. The product was packed well and the accompanying user guide was clear and comprehensive.

I use the product three times a week when I run on the treadmill in my gym. On each occasion I use it at least for 30 minutes and for no more than 90 minutes. The quality of sound is excellent as is the fit of the headphones in my ears.

The problem is that headphones have stopped working and cannot be charged. I have used the product for at most 35 times (on 35 days) when it stopped working. It simply does not get charged.

I used to charge the headphones fully once every 4 or 5 days. It worked very well for the first 6 weeks or so. Around the first week of December it started taking 8 or 9 hours to get charged. I made sure that the laptop was on and did not enter sleep mode (I did the same with my iMac). A couple of weeks ago it took 13 hours to charge.

It stopped working altogether the last two weeks. I cannot charge it at all from my MacBook Pro, nor from my iMac or from my Mac at work. There is nothing wrong with any of these Macs as I can charge other products (including my iPhone and an older set of headphones) on these Macs. The headphones are useless now.

I searched the internet and as well as the reviews and found several buyers that had expressed similar problems with this product.

I am appalled that expensive headphones such as these were so poorly made and broke down after very light use.

review_body: Car's Blackout Cloth is a great product. This material is a much cheaper option than other projection material or projection paint. It made the projector image look excellent. The overall dimensions of the frame is 61" x 42" so I had a lot of leftover material. Even though it does come folded (to reduce shipping costs) it's very easy to pull the wrinkes out.  I made a simple wood frame that I stretched the material over (make sure you have a second set of hands 1 to pull the fabric and the other to staple onto the frame). It took about 20 minutes to assemble, stretch the cloth and hang on the wall. I've tried other methods for creating a projection surface that include- photo backdrop paper (worked well be does need to be replaced a couple of times a year, painted wall with a variety of regular paints (the best combination was adding pearlessence to some flat primer but if your wall is not perfectly smooth and flat you will see it every flaw on the surface). product_title: CyberPower PFC Compatible Pure Sine Wave Tower UPS
review_body:
I only received this a couple days ago, and did 1 test. So far I'm very pleased with the function, quietness, and value of this item.

Shipping box and styrofoam was fine, and it showed no signs of rough handling, despite being shipped right before Christmas.

For an initial test, I did the recommended 8+ hour charge with the UPS off. Then I plugged in a 165W load (a headless PC with PFC power supply, idling at a boot prompt), pulled the UPS's cord from the wall, and started my stopwatch. I disabled the alert beep (hold down the button for 2 seconds, until the mute icon appears), and set the UPS display to show expected remaining minutes. Throughout most of the run, the UPS's display and the stopwatch indicated that I'd get 40 to 41 minutes. However, towards the end of the run, I noticed the UPS's display said 1 minute, when I expected it to say 5. Sure enough, the UPS suddenly cut power within 1 minute. Total run time for 165W load was 36.5 minutes.

One big selling point is that this runs silent so far, whether charging, normal run, or running on battery power. I could not hear any noise from it in a quiet room -- no fan noise, no humming, no hissing. This was actually one of the reasons I bought it, after I heard people complaining about the noise of one of the APC models I that I almost bought.

One very minor complaint I have is that the display viewing angle could be better. When you're standing in front of the UPS, and it's near the floor, the very bottom part of the display (part of the numeric display portion) is clipped/distorted visually. Like the bottom centimeter of the display is bent away slightly, or otherwise has poorer viewing angle than most of the rest of the display.

The display function is nice. I've switched it to show output-watts, to tell me at a glance how much power my headless 8-core PC is drawing at any moment.

I also like the new chassis design. The previous CyberPower models looked a little cheezy to me, but this model looks reasonably stylish and discreet. Still, I don't see the purpose of the high-gloss (scratching-friendly) panel in the middle of the top. I'd especially prefer an all-matte or brushed finish except for the display.

I have not tried the software. I run Debian GNU/Linux, and will eventually try some pure open source UPS software.

I'll update my review if CyberPower lets me down, but it's made a good impression so far. After trying it for a while, I expect to buy additional CyberPower units.

product_title: 1byone Amplified HDTV Antenna, with Detachable Amplifier Signal Booster for the Highest Performance and 10 Feet Coaxial Cable-Black
review_headline: This little darling is going to save us $100+ per month!
review_body: **UPDATE**  We have now been antenna only for over a month (I cancelled DirecTV early and paid $65 to get out of the contract), and I can happily verify that it is still working, and the family is happy.  We have a great picture (watched the superbowl last night with a projector on a 120 inch screen, and it looked SPECTACULAR), and no signal dropouts.  The wife said she doesn't miss cable and the kids really couldn't care less.  Once again, that is $100 a month I can do something else with!  I am actually changing my review to 5 stars because of how well it is working.    **ORIGINAL REVIEW**    After tiring of paying $100+ a month to really only watch 5 or 6 channels, I just had to give an old fashioned OTA antenna a shot.  We don't even have any movie channels, but all of the boxes and DVR's were costing us a small fortune every year.    I will admit that I was a bit hesitant to purchase this product.  I did not think it would really work, based on the information I was finding online about my area.  (I purchased the 50 mile version of the flat antenna with the inline 20db signal booster).    Background: My house is 45+ miles north of the broadcast towers in the Dallas/Ft Worth area, and everything I had read said that I would need an outdoor (likely amplified) antenna to get any channels at all.  That was going to involve a lot of work on a steeply pitched roof, and I was not looking forward to it.  I figured I could test this out and send it back if it did not work, plus since it got great reviews ( and I am the eternal optimist), I was hoping for a miracle.    Test #1 - set the antenna in a south facing window on the first floor without the amplifier in place.  Zero channels - not surprising.    Test #2 - added the amplifier.  I could now find 8 channels, but none of them were actually viewable - again, not surprising.    Test #3 - attached the antenna to a TV upstairs - with amplifier - on a NORTH facing window.  Zero channels, because the towers are all on theother side of the house.    Test #4  - move a TV into a room on the SOUTH side of the house on the second floor and put the amplified antenna in the window.  24 channels!!!!  OK, not all of them were usable, but some were and they looked great!    Test #5 - final test.  I bought 50 ft of RG6 coax cable and headed up into the attic.  I stuck the antenna up near the peak of the roof, right behind one of the vents (so that it mainly has to deal with plastic between it and the outside world) and ran the coax down to a TV in my son's room.  The moment of truth.......54 channels!!!    Holy cow - I was in shock.  We got all of the major locals, plus many of their secondary channels (I had no idea they would have -(dash)1, -2, -3 etc channels).  The picture was beautiful, perfectly clear, many broadcasting in Dolby Digital and 1080i.  I also found that here in the DFW area, we have a Chinese channel, a Vietnamese channel and a Punjabi channel.  Lots of Hispanic channels as well (and shopping, and religious), but I already knew about those.    A little aside for those of you thinking about going this route.  The towers also seem to broadcast a channel guide - I was about to bring up (on the TV we have) a list of all programs coming up for the next 12 or so hours.    Is it worth it?  Without a doubt.  The only thing that I was worried about was the ability to record TV, and I found the Tivo OTA Roamio that should do the trick for that little issue (it will cost $150 a year, but for the convenience - and the happy wife - I will happily pay it).  My contract with DirecTV will be up in a couple months, after which they and I are done!  I will have officially 'cut the cord'.

product_title: SHARKK® Bluetooth 4.0 BoomBox Speaker, 18 Hour Playtime, 10 Watt Portable Speaker System, 4400 mAh Li-ion Battery, Ultra Bass Subwoofer Sound Effect / Built In Mic For Calls / NFC Function / For All iPhone / iPhone 6 / iPhone 6 Plus / All iPad / iPad Air 2 / All Phones / Samsung Galaxy Phones and Tablets / Laptops
review_headline: Works as expected and sounds pretty good.
review_body:
Let's first start off with the fact that I was excited to try this out since it's my first BT speaker. I've only had product-specific-docking speakers or used an auxiliary cord. I have no other BT speakers to compare to so this is strictly a first-time, first-hand, non-professional "review."

I was looking at some other BT speakers similar to this one when I came across a review on those speakers that mentioned the Sharkk. I still purchased the other ones for my kids (as they were about half the cost of this one so better priced for teenagers). I'm always a bit leery about buying electronics sight-unseen because I like to see/hear/feel them and then will look for the best price whether it be online or in-store. For the price I found on this one, I figured that I could ebay/craigslist this speaker if I didn't end up liking it--I'm okay with just making my money back.

Anyway, the product was packaged well and shipped/delivered within the expected time.

Pairing the Sharkk to my phone (and later to my iPad) was easy and swift. I turned on the speaker, held down the play/pause button to execute pairing (it also gives you voice notification), turned my phone's BT on and hit scan, Sharkk Boobbox showed in my list of devices, hit Connect and voila! paired (another voice notification confirms as well).

I used Spotify to test how it sounds. Granted it's not always at a consistent level (at least in my experience anyway) but it's what I had to use on my phone at the time as I don't load any MP3s on my phone. That's what I have a 64GB iPod touch for. I turned the volume all the way up on my phone and hit play. The tunes sounded pretty good. It had some decent all-around bass and treble -- not too much of either but enough to be glad the speaker doesn't stink. I listened in my bathroom which is about 5x12 room. I then tried it in my dining/living room (open concept I guess they call it) which is about 20x60 with a 10' ceiling. The sound was still loud but I felt like it could be overpowered by other music or my turned-up-loud 52" television. Then I remember why I bought this size of speaker, it wasn't to fill a huge room or to be a cheap alternative to a sound system I bought it to have something to play my music through without the use of power or auxiliary cords. I bought it to be loud enough to drown out background noise like maybe traffic, leaf blowers, or whatever I may incur outside on a patio or poolside. I bought it to connect my iPad so I can watch movies through whatever movie app when the sound is too low for some reason.

So, did the Sharkk BT speaker do this? Yes it did and it did it well. However, I have ONLY used Spotify for the music and Netflix to watch a few Dexter episodes. I'm sure that if I connected something with higher volume on the device to the speaker that it would probably be much louder as the volume buttons on the speaker DO NOT control the actual volume on my phone. Now, the volume buttons on the speaker DO control the actual volume on my iPad when watching Netflix. I've not tested if it does or does not control the volume through any other means/apps/programs.

I did test the speakerphone option which I really don't anticipate using that much if at all as it's more of a nice option to have than a necessity for me. I could hear the person really well through the speaker and they said they heard me loud and clear as well. I did make the call while in my bathroom and then again in the dining room so my background noise was pretty much nil.

Overall, I'd have to say I'm pleasantly surprised with this little speaker. If I get a little more time to play around with it to experiment with other devices via BT and auxiliary maybe I'll update the review.

product_title: M-DISC 25GB Blu-ray Permanent Data Archival / Backup Blank Disc Media - 15 Pack Cake Box
review_headline: Work great!   Spend a few extra $$ for the inkjet printable ones...
review_body:
These discs work fine, but though there is 25GB capacity, you can't realistically get that unfortunately. I tried (and wasted) several recordings at and around 23-25GB and they all failed... I thought I had a bad drive or bad discs... then I noticed the actual capacity of a new and empty disc in explorer at 23.3GB. So I lowered my data to 21GB and it worked fine. Through several more recordings, I so far have not had a failure if I keep the data under 23GB. I haven't yet researched why this is, because there is only a small file on each new disc that is miniscule, so not sure why I can't get 25GB or closer to it, but that's my experience. I have an LG BE14NU40 burner. Otherwise the discs work great.

The inkjet writeable ones are best if you want to label... evidently writing on a regular disc could eventually leach ink on the reflective surface with time and render your disc corrupt. You can write on the small "inside circle" where no data is if you need to label it with anything, but write small! : ) Otherwise get the inkjet writeable ones that have an extra layer for labeling.

I have lost 2 hard drives within a week before... losing my primary data and backup data... so backups with HDs is not the most dependable method of backup! Flash drives, Hard drives, they all will fail. And so will these... eventually. But it does provide a restoral point and keeping the important data on at least two seperate media at any point in time will allow a restoral if one fails. If interested in a reliable archival system, there are several articles on the net to get an idea of what works for you. Some ideas are too cumbersome to keep up with. I am now using a dual HDD system for immediate backups, and these discs for archiving long term. I store these at a different location, for extra security. This is for stuff I just absolutely don't want to lose, i.e. videos of the kids, pictures, etc... When technology changes, I can always move to it at any time.

For now, this is best for my purpose. They work great.

product_title: Bose Wave SoundTouch Music System
review_headline: Bose quality ~ Bose high price ~ Better alternative exists,
review_body:
Bose is late to the game when it comes to Internet radio. I recently listened to this music system at a Bose store, and while I was very impressed with the sound quality, I don't feel that the high price is justified.

Yes, if price isn't an issue, and you want to be able to play CD's in addition to listening to Internet radio stations, than this may work well for you. As an owner of Bose speakers, I agree that their sound is unsurpassed. The problem here is that you end up paying a very high price for a product that may not satisfy all of your needs.

For me, since I no longer own any CD's, there was no need for this feature. What I was looking for was an Internet radio that was capable of playing a wide variety of Internet stations, such as SiriusXM and Pandora, but without a CD player. After doing an extensive search on Amazon, I ended up purchasing a Grace Mondo Internet radio that was significantly less expensive than the Bose system listed here. Than, after setting up the radio, I purchased the Bose Companion 20 Multimedia Speaker System which I connected to the Mondo radio. Now, at a significantly lower cost than the Bose Wave SoundTouch music system, I have a setup that sounds even better than the SoundTouch. So basically I have an Internet radio that is capable of receiving SiriusXM, Pandora, tens of thousands of Internet stations, and incorporates high quality Bose speakers to boot. I also have the ability to connect my iPad or IPod to the Mondo so that I can listen to music that I've downloaded to iTunes.

The bottom line is that the Bose system listed here is fantastic, but from experience with both this and the Grace Mondo Internet radio with the Bose Companion 20 Multimedia Speaker System, the Grace Mondo/Bose Companion 20 Multimedia Speaker System sounds significantly better. It doesn't have a CD player, but it does have just about everything else. If you don't have the need for a CD player, this is a very viable alternative.ive.

review_body:
I received a set of these Cheetah Bluetooth in-ear headphones for evaluation, and find that they work well, and deliver decent quality sound, with more of an emphasis on treble. Featuring a cord that runs behind your head, it's hard to adequately describe how these earphones actually feel when you are wearing them, but I suspect that comfort could be an issue for some users who have them in their ears for longer periods of time.

I had no issues regarding Bluetooth, as the earphones were easily paired with a Kindle Fire, and a Surface tablet. The phones have a basic set of controls, which once you become familiar with, are mostly easy to use. You can adjust the volume and also skip tracks forward and back, using two buttons. A micro-USB cord is provided for recharging.

The Cheetah earphones probably provide the best sound, when the earpieces seal nicely into the aural canal. There are spare sets of silicone inserts, so you can try and get a better fit. Worn with the connecting cord lying on the back of your head and neck, some may find that comfort is an issue, as depending on the size of your head, there is a certain amount of pressure on your ears. While I don't have any problems wearing the Cheetah phones for short periods, there could be some soreness after a couple of hours.

When properly worn, you should be able to move freely, without worrying that the Cheetah earphones may fall off. It may take a while to get used to how these earphones feel, but if you are feeling adventurous, you may want to give this some consideration.

product_title: Logitech Harmony Home Control for Control of 8 Home Entertainment and Automation Devices
review_headline: The core of your home automation system
review_body:
The Harmony Home Control is a great product. I have it running my in-closet media center and it works flawlessly. I do warn you that this will make you buy more compatible products. I picked up a Lutron Smart Hub + a few Caseta Wireless Dimmers to add some nice lighting automation. Harmony Home Control works flawlessly with Lutron's Caseta Smart Hub + light switches (you need the Lutron Smart Hub to control Caseta Wireless switches).

Harmony App + Simple Remote:
The iOS app needs some improvement. It takes a while to start up and isn't as accessible as a physical remote. The app does stay running in the foreground once launched which makes it somewhat usable but it still doesn't compare to the tactile feedback of a physical remote. The simple remote which this bundle comes with is great for TV + Satellite / Cable box control but starts to show some slight weakness when using it to control devices like a PS3. You can map the standard PS3 controller buttons to the buttons on the remote but there usually are more features available. The iOS app is great for this since it displays the PS3 controller buttons + PS3 Blu-Ray media controller buttons all in the app. For this reason I would suggest going for the Ultimate package which comes with a remote that has a physical buttons + a screen. The Ultimate package comes at a steep premium for the remote so think of your use-case before taking the plunge. This package will be more than sufficient for most users, even techies.

3rd Party "API":
Another great thing Logitech did is open up the product to third-party apps. I was happy to see I was able to write a "recipe" in a popular automation app called If This Then That (IFTTT...available on iOS + Android). My home lights now turn on automatically after sunset when we pull up to our home -- you need Lutron's Smart Hub and Caseta Wireless switches or Philips Hue lights for this to work. The Harmony Hub acts as a proxy between IFTTT& the Smart Hub. You can even configure the Hub to turn on the lights when you unlock your front-door if you have an August Smart Door Lock.

product_title: Universal Remote Control MX-450 Custom Programmable Remote Control with On-Screen Macro Editing.
review_body:
My unit was used, but like-new as described. Delivery was reasonably fast (4 business days).

The MX-450 remote is a tough item to program using the manual programming methods, but it does the job after you spend a lot of time researching and learning how to program it.
The manufacturer provides almost no useful detail on how to program this remote control.

RF control worked with my old $40 RF20, 6-output RF reciever!!

This RF reciever is a lot less expensive than buying the $200 special RF reciever! And you get a extra remote in the bargain (although the RF20 macro capability is a bit limited and its basic programming mode requires wasted time guessing through many possible codes from each munaufacturer, but the RF20 can learn from other remotes if you have a lot of spare time to program each key separately)

One great thing about this MX-450 controller was that the "basic programming mode" worked super. I just pointed at the devices in my cabinet (amplifier, cable box, Blueray with Netflix, CD player, and even a new 65" Samsung Smart TV) and it guessed the correct code for my device on the first try. No trying 10 different codes per device. This is nt learning fomr the remote, but identifying my devices!

This does not get you those valuable Macros, but it does get you a simgle remote that does almost everything 6 other remotes can do. The whole process took me less than 10 minutes for 5 devices.

There is little documentation for programming macors, so you need to spend a lot of time searching for programming assistance.
Universal will not provide the PC programming to end customers, only to their dealers.
Some of the Amazon prior reviews are very helpful.

I suppose the manufacturers dealers want customers to rely on them for programming, so they make DIY macro program as difficult as possible. Fortunately, the device is well designed, so you can still do a good job as a project after some research.

This is sad that this company provide so little support to this MX-450 product, since this could be a great consumer product if it had a freindly software package included.
It could be the best controller on the DIY consumer market with a good software package, even though it is a several year old design.

review_body:
Just spent the last three hours trying to get past the first few steps in the setup process. Some caution:

Got that laptop setup and fired up the hub desktop program again from my desktop aaannnddd hub cannot connect to the wifi. I power cycled my router, disconnected (and powered down) my laptop. Took all protections off the router (making it open), power cycled the hub, and still could not connect - i know it was working as my laptop could connect np through this entire ordeal, save when it was power down for a short time). So whether emulating the android app (i was using Andy android emulator) works or not I cannot say.

In short this product will be returned.

"Harmony" must be the sound people suffering through the setup of these devices, as they're worthless. Stay Away!

product_title: X-Mini MAX v1.1 Portable Capsule Speaker
review_headline: Very good sound, very happy with the purchase
review_body:
I have a variety of small speakers, including the Kinivo and Monster Clarity. I have to say I was quite impressed with the sound from these, easily as good or better than a pair of the Kinivo's. The monster has good bass but both these and the kinivo do better on the high notes. That you get two for the cost of a kinivo and 1/4 the price of the monster is a big plus.

No bluetooth and no microphone like the monster has, but the microphone on most bluetooth small speakers is usually lousy,

These have little magnets in the base that let you stick them together and drop them into their bag. Both have a power switch and both have a 3.5mm plug so you could add two more speakers to it. If you bought two of these kits, you could have quad speakers but you'd have to buy the 3.5mm to 3.5mm male cables.

There is a volume control inline with the dual end 3.5mm sound and usb power cable.

Only downside to these vs the kinivo and monster speakers is that you can't charge and use at the same time. For starters the end that has the 3.5mm/full size usb charging plug has the two plugs just a few inches apart, and the speakers buzzed/hummed and didn't make good sound when I had the usb charging end plugged in.

The supplied charging/sound cable also doesn't have a lot of room to space the two speakers apart...maybe 3-4 inches. But you could use the supplied cable to connect to the first speaker and a separate 3.5mm male to male cable to the daisy chain port. Its not a huge deal, but having them a foot or so apart would improve the spatiality.

Since I got these for about half cost through the amazon warehouse, I'm THRILLED with the purchase. Still a great deal at the regular price.

review_headline: Decent sound from a reasonably priced portable speaker
review_body: I am very picky about my music's sound quality. I cannot stand the tinny sound that comes from most small portable speakers. I listen daily to JBL and Cerwin Vega speakers powered by Yamaha and Pioneer amps (respectively), but I needed a decent portable speaker to play from my cell phone at work. After reading many reviews, I put this unit on my Christmas list and got what I asked for. I am not disappointed. The bass is not floor-shaking, but is definitely present. I can switch the source from my tablet to my daughter's cell phone by simply pushing the Bluetooth button on the speaker and pairing with the new device in the phone's Settings menu. The sound quality is better than the Sony boom-box in the office, which is five times bigger. To earn five stars, this speaker would have to sound like a pair of 100 dollar earphones and cost 50. It will not replace a $1000 stereo at your next garden party, but for 85 bucks, it's a good value.

product_title: Photive BTH3 Over-The-Ear Wireless Bluetooth Headphones with Built-in Mic and 12 Hour Battery. Includes Hard Travel Case.
review_headline: Doesn't sound as sweet as plain ear buds
review_body:
I wanted inexpensive tunes for outside work without cords in the way, and secure fit. I've been using the G-Project, G-Boom wireless boombox (which I can HIGHLY recommend for sub-$100 portable wireless audio! But it impinges on my neighbors at the volume I like) Here are my initial impressions of these headphones (Using both a Galaxy S4 and Kindle FireHD with Amazon music):
DEVICE
- Impressive design. Hardcase is a nice touch. Lightweight. Padded cups and crossbar. Finish is very nice.
- Paired easily and instantly with both devices. Range seems to be 30' - 40' unobstructed.
- Adjusted easily to fit my large head (male 6'2" 250lbs) with extra to spare. Position locked in place and feels secure and comfortable. No pressure around ears which fit inside the cups fully.
- Felt minor perspiration moisture around pad contact after 5 minutes in 62 degree/49% humidity household climate.
I expect they would get pretty damp while mowing a summer lawn.
SOUND
The first song was DJ SNAKE & Lil Jon "Turn Down For Whar": Started Crisp . I was especially interested in the bass response and this heavy bass line was surprisingly resonant! I was very pleased. Unfortunately, it went downhill from there. As I listened to older and older music (digitally remastered 70's and 80's pop/rock) the sound quality steadily deteriorated. In a nutshell it sounds "muffled". The mid and high ranges are stunted. For comparison I replayed the same songs with Samsung earbuds that came with the Galaxy. And It was really apparent the higher end was just blunt. Listen to the opening of Brittany Spears "Toxic". The Photives sound like the opening instrumental ,and the buds like the first line "Baby can't you see".
Neil Young's "Southern Man" sounded horrible. Til Tuesday "Voices Carry" sounded ok. Pearl Jam "Glorified G" (remastered 2011) just didn't sound full or clear.
As for functionality the sound level and track selection buttons on the cups are easy to find and work well. However, a couple times while I was adjusting volume the last phone number I called was redialed on the phone?! But this could be an issue with the phone itself interpretting bluetooth signals.
I am not an audiophile. I just know what sounds good or not to me. I bought these untested based on mostly favorable Amazon reviews (discounting those negative ones where expectations seemed too high). I was expecting something comparable to earbuds. But maybe I expected too much. I think its a quality product for the price. But for me I think I will look to spend more towards better sound all around.

product_title: Pyle PSR14 Splash-Proof Water Resistant Mini Digital AM/FM Radio Alarm Clock with LCD Display and 3.5mm AUX Input, Digital
review_headline: A nice water resistant clock radio
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:c291c67cc53ee2206e736ea2cfe8b6fc]]There aren't too many bells and whistles on the Pyle PSR14, but it's a good basic AM/FM clock radio that's ideal for damp conditions as well as in the shower. For the shower, I hung it over the handheld showerhead support and played the radio while I took my shower. The radio was protected from direct spray, but it got wet from the splashing. The water didn't appear to affect it, and afterwards, I shook the water off the radio and wiped it dry with a towel. The radio has an IPX4 rating, which means it's protected against spraying or splashing water. (International Protection Marking codes, also known as IPX codes, classify and rate the degree of protection provided against the intrusion of dust and water by mechanical casings and electrical enclosures. The codes for water protection range from 0 to 9.)

The radio has analog tuning, no presets, and no weather radio - just AM/FM. But it brought in AM and FM stations pretty well, with more than enough volume to be heard over the shower noise, and decent clarity for voice and music, especially with FM stations. At maximum volume, though, there was a noticeable amount of distortion. In our area, there are dozens of radio stations. The little radio did a fairly nice job of pulling in stations and separating them without too much bleed-over, especially for an analog tuner.

The LCD display with alarm clock is a handy feature, although the display is recessed about a quarter-inch, and without backlighting, it can be difficult to read in dim lighting. Note that when the radio is in use, the display shows the station frequency, not the time. Over a period of several days, the clock kept the time very accurately.

It's not a big radio. At approximately 5½\\"x4¾\\"x3\\" and weighing just over 11 ounces (with batteries), it would be convenient to carry while hiking or camping or any outdoor activity, and rain or humid conditions shouldn't bother it. The ability to play the audio from a phone or tablet through the radio's auxiliary port is a helpful plus.

The bottom line: The Pyle PSR14 splash-proof clock radio is a good choice for outdoor activities, especially if rain is in the forecast. It's also a nice radio for home when you need an inexpensive, basic radio. And of course, there's the shower.

product_title: Beats Solo 2.0 On-Ear Headphones
review_headline: I really want to like my Beats Solo 2 headphones
review_body: I really want to like the Beats Solo 2 headphones.  First of all, I got them here on Amazon for $148.  Apparently it was a special sale.  So when I read reviews from "experts", I note that many simply say something like "good headphones but overpriced."  I bought them mostly to use in the gym.  I workout religiously.  For me, going to the gym is not a social occasion.  When I'm on the treadmill, for instance, I'm totally focused.  That's where having a good set of headphones come in.  I want something that blocks out the conversations around me.  These are the people who are half-heartedly working out but more focused on using the gym as a social occasion.  Truth is, my new Beats Solo 2 can become uncomfortable after about an hour.  When I first put them on I could only go 45 minutes, so I guess I'm breaking them in (either that or just getting used to them).  But they do the job - great sound, not noise canceling but certainly noise reducing, and comfortable for the time I'm actually working out.  If you're looking for a set of cans to use on an airplane for a long flight, look elsewhere.  But if you're goal is similar to mine, I'd recommend the Beats Solo 2 - especially if you can get them on sale!

product_title: Klipsch Stadium (120V)
review_body:
I ordered my Klipsch Stadium from Hi-Fi Heaven. Because I tried everywhere else. Locally and online. None of which could ship to me in Canada. Since the Klipsch company does not sell their products outside of the U.S.
You have to get their products through a retail dealer. But this speaker is more of a novelty item. So it was hard to find a place that could sell it to me outside the U.S.

I did the payment through PayPal which worked out to be $2,200 Canadian. And then when it arrived at my door through UPS it was an additional $200 for shipping and handling. I ordered it on July 21/2014 and it arrived five days later.

Was it worth it for the money? Yes.
At first I was a little disappointed with the sound. Until I tried it using a sound enhancing app that I use regularly on my iPhone. Called SRS MyTunes Pro. There is also a better app also made by SRSlabs called MyTunes Pro HD. But it is only compatible with the iPad. The app basically takes the audio you play and automatically restores the sound digitally in real time. It accomplishes this by adjusting the sound using an advanced algorithm that brings the compressed audio track back to the level it would have been before it was compressed. The difference is like night and day. Especially on a top notch speaker like the Klipsch Stadium. Unfortunately, the SRS apps are no longer available in the iTunes Store. I think it is because DTS (a big audio company that makes the top of the line surround sound audio formats. Commonly used on Bluray movies) bought the small SRSlabs company. Ever since they were bought the SRSlabs website was taken down.
Fortunately I downloaded both of the apps before they were pulled off of iTunes.
Two other SRS products that I own which I highly recommend and are still currently available are SRS HD Audio Lab (for PC) and the SRS iWow 3D (iPod adapter).

I really wanted to hear how good its peak performance sounds like at its loudest volume without upsetting the neighbours. Of course I wouldn't do it at home because this thing gets as loud as a live concert. So I brought it with me when I went to the Galaxy Theater to watch Guardians of the Galaxy with a friend and asked the lady, who we were giving are tickets to, if we could test my new speaker in the Theater after the movie. She agreed. But we had to come back a couple of hours after the movie at around 11:00pm. Because the theatres were all being used right after the movie for the following showtimes. People were going in to the Theater we came out of (after the movie) within just a few minutes.

So we came back and went to the front door. But it was locked. Within a few seconds the lady came and let us in. They were closing at midnight and they seemed to have less staff when we came in. So they must have locked up to prevent unsupervised visitors from coming in.

We went in to one of the theatres that wasn't being used and hooked up the speaker to an outlet near the front of the projector screen. Using an extension cord and a surge protector. Just in case. Because there was a big electrical storm going on outside and the rain was coming down pretty hard.
So I turned it on and connected my iPad to the Klipsch Stadium through bluetooth and cranked up the volume all the way. It was outstanding. My friend was also very impressed. The sound was so loud and clear it sounded like it was coming from the surround speakers in the theatre! The speaker also didn't distort at all even when I played several challenging soundtracks and movie trailers. Including the Hobbit and Avatar. For the music I tried Owl City's "Good Time", Lisa Kelly's "May It Be" and Katy Perry's "Firework" to name a few.

Of course the sound was even louder and richer with the MyTunes Pro App. My friend and I had fun trying different songs and videos until midnight (closing time).

It was even more fun then the movie was!
I really enjoy listening to music the way it was meant to be heard. I have heard many speaker brands. But none of them are as good as Klipsch. To name a few speaker brands I own and tried are: Bose, Altec Lansing, Logitech, JBL, JVC, Pioneer, Philips and Sony to name a few.

Would I recommend this speaker? Yes.

product_title: Monster 100 feet Speaker Cable
review_headline: Audiophile with an Understanding in Electricity/Electronics
review_body:
First off I want to identify myself as an audiophile. I am also an automotive repair technician and one of the things that gets drilled into your head in my field regarding the ever-more-advanced electronics systems in vehicles is wiring: strand, gauge, quality, twisted.

First off for those of you asking why this is better than the Home Depot generic power cord wire consider these three items:
1. This is twisted wire. By definition, it is self cancelling. It is resistant to electrical or electromagnetic interferance (from the other four, six, or eight channels running off of the back of your receiver). This won't pick up electrical noise, and it won't give it out either. Thank a twisted strand for this.
2. This is fine strand wire. Electricity doesn't care how large of diameter the wire is you are using, because the electricity ONLY travels on the outside of the metal. If you have a single wire that is 12 gauge and compare it to a 20-strand wire which is also 12 gauge the fine strand wire will carry more current and a higher quality signal since the overall wire has more surface area. Monster does this. As an added bonus, the wire is more flexible and easily routed because of the fine strands.
3. Nylon line running the length of the cable. When you pull this cable through your walls, ceiling, floor, or wire channeling to hide it from sight you aren't pulling on the wires, you are pulling it along by a nylon strand. This prevents damage to the wiring which you are relying on for your signal. In addition, the twisted pair of wires AND the nylon line are encased in an outer sheath, so it slides through those tightly drilled access holes and panels much easier and with less binding than your Home Depot 2-circuit straight wire. And it is better for the wire.

Now regarding signal quality:
If you blast your MP3's with a cheap HTIB system or a cheap stereo, these wires aren't for you. You are already losing so much audio integrity with cheap equipment and low quality files to notice any difference with this wire - go to Home Depot and pick up lamp power cord and be happy.

For those of you with true cinematic Home Theaters (where you have over $2000 in your receiver and speakers alone - not including your subwoofer) this is where this cable shines. You are the type who watches Blu-Ray movies in 7.1 channel audio on your Full-HD 42+ inch TV or your 4K 3D projector. You already invested many thousands into the highest quality speakers and equipment you can afford, so why cheap out on the wires that carry that signal from your top of the line receiver to your top of the line speakers?

Remember that, even in a fully digital Home Theater, the speakers are by design analog. There is no such thing as a digital speaker, and the analog sound signal is carried through your speaker wire from your receiver to your speakers. You want the best quality speaker wire you can afford to carry that precious signal, especially if you are running your rear surround speakers, or any speakers over 10-feet in wiring. Your Surround-Left and Surround-Right speakers are closer to you (and farther from your receiver) than your Front-Left, -Right, and -Center: don't cheap out on the signal wires to these speakers.

Now my review with my test equipment:
Yamaha RX-A2030 Receiver
Klipsch Quintet 5.0 Channel Speakers
No subwoofer
Blu-Ray movie, audio signal sent through Acoustic Research Pro II Series 6-ft HDMI cable
Playstation 3 as Blu-Ray Player

At nominal max volume (0.0dB) absolutely no distortion.
At true max volume (+16.0dB) absolutely no distortion.
Crystal clear sound, no interferance or distortion and perfect sound reproduction

Tested with standard 14-gauge speaker wire and the same hardware:
At nominal max volume (0.0dB) signal distorted and muddy
Untested at true max volume - I did not want to damage any of my equipment with unnecessary stress

I highly recommend this speaker wire. You wouldn't take your Ferrari for an oil change at PepBoys, so why would you run your speakers on cheap speaker wire?

review_headline: Best iPod speaker in this price range hands down.
review_body:
Wow, what a sound for $59!

I love using my iPod but I don't always want to wear headphones. I recently bought new stereo components for my living room, but wanted something portable for the rest of the house. In the past I tried a few other brands: the JBL was decent, but 2 others I had previously purchased from some big box store (one iHome and some other brand I can't remember) were horrible.

After doing much reading and comparison, I decided on this one. It went from $150 to $59 so I jumped on it. It's AMAZING how much sound you get from this little unit. Now, I ain't gonna lie, this will not replace a full receiver with speakers and subwoofer setup, but for smaller rooms this thing has the best sound I've heard so far in an iPod unit. My friend has a Boise, which sounds great, but it cost him several hundred dollars.

It has a nice profile. It comes with a remote which works with my iPod nano 3g. It fills up my 17 x 17 office with no problems, at a volume level of 32. And at 32 it's loud, because I like it loud. The only thing I am missing is the bottom end, but this is going to be a problem for all smaller units. If you like bottom end, booming bass, powerful drums, you need a true subwoofer. Still though, this unit sounds good in that regard, it's not tinny or all high-end.

Highly recommend!
