On the upside, it's not as clumsy as the previous antenna, and doesn't require any juice, again unlike my previous antenna, but I'm thinking I should have just gone ahead and spent the extra cash on a larger powered version of this thing.

I live in the mid peninsula region of the SF Bay Area, and with the old rabbit ears on the old CRT television I could generally pick up all local stations. I can't really do that with this antenna, although digital signals being what they are, the reception is clearer.

Not a product I would highly recommend, but if you need something quick and dirty, this might do the trick.

product_title: 1byone OUS00-0185 Super Thin Indoor HDTV Antenna with Stand with 25 Miles Range and 10-Feet High Performance Coaxial Cable
review_body:
I live in a major city so I expected an antenna should be able to pick up a lot of stations. I was not disappointed. After scanning for stations, the antenna picked up almost 60 stations. The ones I watch most frequently (CBS, NBC, ABC, PBS, FOX, WGN) came in flawlessly after a little tweaking to find the correct orientation for the antenna.. There were some higher number UHF stations that I do not watch that had some digital artifacts, but I'm sure that would clear up with a slight adjustment of antenna rotation. I purchased the stand mounted antenna and stuck the antenna vertically on a shelf about 3 feet from the TV. The suction cup mounted to the shelf with no problems (be sure to moisten it slightly), and my wife commented on how much better it looks than the traditional rabbit ears.

I would recommend buying the stand mounted versions, as it will give you more flexibility in rotating the antenna to get the best reception. If you mount it on a window and position the bracket into an L shape, I would guess you have around 170 degrees of rotation available. If you mount it vertically on a shelf like I did, you have 360 degrees of control. Note that even a slight change in rotation can be the difference in a good signal and a bad signal.

Since I live in a big city, all of the TV transmitters are probably within 15 miles of me, so I can't attest to how well this will work on farther stations. But in my circumstances this worked great, and I would highly recommend it.

review_headline: Electronics Came to Life with the HDTV Antenna
review_body:
The HDTV Antenna is super. Although I had some trouble finding the right location for maximum signal capture, once I worked out kinks it works fine. Actually the device kind of reminds me of the “rabbit ears” of the 1950’s. The antenna works in both the VHF and UHF, plus the FM, frequencies. Although I was happy with its function on the VHF and UHF modes, I got a big surprise when I plugged it into an old FM hi fi receiver that had been cast aside collecting dust.

For the first time in years I heard FM like never before. To say that the antenna brought this old set back to life is an understatement. Both music and voice came through this receiver like an unexpected dividend. It gave the reception a clarity that I did not expect. Gone were those scratchy globules of noisy interference.

One of the more practical features is its slim lightweight design. It’s certainly easy to move around and plugs right into the standard antenna cable. I say, when a device works the way it’s supposed to you smile and nod your head. When a device delivers beyond your expectations you want to yell, “Buy It!” to your friends. I highly recommend this HDTV Antenna to anyone seeking superior audio and video.

review_headline: A cable worth it's weight in gold!
review_body:
So I'm a little torn on what to say here. I have long been an evangelist of saying that you aren't going to notice a difference between a $1 HDMI cable or one that was clocking in at the $30 mark or above.

Well, I'll still say I feel that most of the changes between a $1 and a standard priced $30 HDMI from a certain .. ahem .. monstrous .. ahem.. company isn't worth the money in my opinion. That being said, Solid Cordz has really raised the bar in what you see coming from their new high end cables.

Or should I say what you see on a high definition 4K TV that has data going over these new cables.

WOW.

Actually, let me rewind for a moment. First I'm going to talk about the quality of the product. The cords for these cables are actually extremely durable compared to your standard HDMI cables. A braided covering on the wire is going to keep these safe through anything short of being cut with a knife and you aren't going to have to worry about damage from stretching or being bent at strange angles.

The covering isn't just for keeping it safe from direct damage but from EMI/RFI signals as well to increase image quality. Speaking of quality the 24K Gold-plated connectors support up to 18 Gbps of data which means full 7.1 Dolby TrueHD and DTS-HD Master AudioTM for sound and anything visual you can throw at it.

While I didn't feel there was much of a difference on my 360 (I'm sure if I had a One or PS4 I would be singing a different tune) there was an extremely noticeable difference using both my Blu-ray player AND my Roku 3. I was pleasantly surprised with the Blu-ray increase but was shocked at how noticable a difference it made on streaming HDX films through Vudu.

[[VIDEOID:7dfe4bad2ae7b7851abf609dc48ace51]] Brainwavz is the one company that no matter what level of headphones I have tried that have been good quality with great sound and extremely comfortable, whether they are in ear or on ear.

I can't tell you how many headphones I have gone through because of that. The case not only holds the headphones but can hold all the earpieces and airplane plug as well.

review_headline: Be meticulous in your setup and it works fine.
review_body: Based on these reviews I was hesitant to buy this unit.  But other remotes had their set of problems, so I went with the Harmony Smart Remote with Hub and used these reviews to set up the unit in a way to maximize the chance of success.  Which I did.  But I'd give the unit 5 stars because it works as it's supposed to, but 3 for setup, hence the 4 overall.    OK, so based on the Amazon reviews I decided that the Harmony app (herein called `app') on my iPhone was not going to be the primary controller because of WiFi connectivity issues other users were having.  I downloaded the app anyway, but I only use it for setup and synch functions so it  is not the primary controller; the RF remote provided with the hub was set up to be the primary controller.    Because all my electronics are rack mounted and visible to the couch where we sit, I set the hub behind the couch near the ceiling so it can `look down, shoot down' and has a good line of sight to all the components.  That way I'm not relying on bounces off any walls.  The mini-blasters are not strong enough at 14 feet away to do this, so I had to rely on physically mounting the hub up high.  It's a pain to get it there, but it works well.    Once the equipment is on hand and the app is downloaded, I downloaded the PC \\"MyHarmony\\" program (herein called \\"MH\\") and did all the programming with the hub connected directly to the PC via the USB cable.    Adding devices in MH was simple as all my devices were in the database.  I defined four activities with the 5 components to be controlled by the hub.    Next, I programmed the buttons on the remote for each activity.  They're mapped into the remote fairly well, but I wanted to customize some button presses to make it easier to do the tasks I wanted.  Because there are 41 programmable buttons on the remote that have 2 functions each (\\"Long\\" press and \\"short\\" press) there are 82 possible functions to check for each activity.  So it takes a while to go through every button forevery activity.  Each button has an option to add a function for either `long' press, `short' press, or both, but oddly when a new function is being added you can only do `both' first before you can select either `long' or `short.'  It's a glitch.  Also, FYI, when you assign a function to a button the list of functions turns `grey' when the function is assigned to a button and remains `black' when unassigned.  So you can tell looking at the list what's been assigned and what isn't. Which buttons they were assigned to, however, is a mystery and you may have to check all 41 to see where it was assigned as they don't tell you.    When all was programmed and at the first attempt to power on, it didn't work. Turns out the power on command for one unit was incorrect.  So I manually programmed that into the hub using the app and the original remote to `teach' the hub what the command was. (The original database had a power `on' and `off' commands but my unit had only a power `toggle.'  So the unit never understood the original command and would not turn on.)    Once that was fixed, things turned on except the DVD player.  Going into the `customize' section of the MH program, I noticed that the box that I had the power problem, above, was sequenced after the DVD player.  Unfortunately the power for the DVD player physically doesn't come on until the first unit is powered on, so I had to change the power-up sequence so the boxes came on in the right order.  Logitech suggests that you can put in time delays here, however, there is no means to allow MH to enter a delay of any kind during the initial power up steps.  My TV doesn't turn the picture on for about 20 seconds, so I was afraid the command to change the input would come too soon and not be accepted by the TV set.  Fortunately in my case the command was accepted even though the TV didn't appear to be `on,' but other users may have this problem where the hub is blasting commands before the intended target can receive it.  There's no way to add the `input' command to the MH customization section and it's not available.  In my case, however, it worked fine.  YMMV.  Oh, and don't add too much delay to the startup sequence or the unit won't seem to respond if you try and do something before the delay time has run it's course.  I tried adding too much delay and the system just wouldn't respond.  This can get frustrating, so I just eliminated the delays as much a practicable.    Once power-on sequencing was done properly, the button presses for each activity was checked. Some buttons had to be reprogrammed and re-learned, but with the original remote this can be done either in the MH program or via the app (you blast the hub with the IR signal from the original remote when cued by the app or MH program)  It learns the new commands well and worked fine once the new commands were assigned.    The `Netflix' and `Vudu' commands for the DVD player, while listed in the available command list, did not work so I set up a macro to initiate these, then assigned them to the movie activity on a dedicated button (the `red' button, of course, for Netflix)    Once all that was done the hub WORKS AS INTENDED:  upon power on all the desired activity boxes turn on and all inputs are selected to the proper ones for the activity.  Change activity and power goes off on the unused boxes and inputs change properly; all at one press of a single button.    So in my case, the hub and RF remote work.  But be careful and map out what you want the buttons to do and if you want to use the app for your control or not.  Upshot: my wife is happy now that 5 remotes are replaced with the one.  And you can't set up the buttons or activities before you get the hub itself from the store as the MH program stops in the setup process until it's connected.  It would have been nice to set a lot of things up before the hub arrived in my possession, but they won't let you do that.    Oh, and you can tweak settings in the MH program and send them to the hub via the app without having to disconnect the hub and move it to the PC, so that's a small help when you get to the point where you're making minor tweaks.    So once I got past the setup I'm happy with it.

product_title: beyerdynamic DT 880 Premium 600 OHM Headphones
review_headline: Excellent Open Back Headphones for Music and Gaming
review_body:
This is my first set of 'audiophile' grade headphones, so I was not sure where my expectations should be to begin with, but I must say there are few headphones I have ever seen which come even close to these. I am using a Mayflower O2 DAC+amp to feed the headphones. I purchased these with the intention of gaming and listening to a wide variety of music.

The build quality is superb. The cable feels thick and durable and the gold plated connector looks great. The ear cups are very sturdy and yet they do not feel like bricks on your head. All of the connection joints are strong and give me no reason to feel they may break, however if they do break it will not be difficult to repair them as they are removable with screws and Beyerdynamic offers replacement parts. The adjustment system seemed a little odd to me at first, but after using them for a couple of months I have never had any mechanical issues with them. They always stay where I adjust them to and the way they function allows the cups to pivot a small amount. The headband is very sturdy with a steel band wrapped with fake leather. While I wish it was real leather it's not a deal breaker, given that the padding is ultra comfortable and has never become uncomfortable even after long gaming sessions. The soft pads on the ear cups are also very comfortable and allow your ears to ventilate naturally.

I really want to stress the comfort of this design. I have never worn a set of headphones capable of the same ergonomics as these. The ear cups are big enough that my ears do not feel squished or any kind of pressure. The clamping force of the band is a little on the weak side which means you cannot head bang with these, however this is likely what makes them so easy to wear for long periods of time. The other factor to consider is the softness of the ear pads, as they are just the right stiffness to maintain shape and yet they are soft enough to prevent any irritation. Excellent comfort overall.

The audio quality is simply astounding, though I must admit I do not have a massive collection headphones to compare these to. I have tried these headphones with a few different amps and systems just to see what kind of differences I can hear. The headphones sound great on any system, but nothing has sounded more clear and precise as when I listen through the O2 DAC. In general I notice these attributes: The high range and mid range sound incredible. Particularly when listening to high quality music the vocalist comes through the mix perfectly clear, not muddy and with too much bass. I could try to describe the sound more accurately but overall it can be summed up as 'extremely clear and precise' which can be extremely useful for positional sound. This is part of why I like them for gaming, but with high quality music you will notice the difference as well. It feels like the musicians are in the room around you.

There is one flaw I suppose that may bother some people. The bass is not very deep and boomy, which for me is perfect as I do not like overly bassy sound, but my roommate and others are on the complete other end of this spectrum where they enjoy as much bass as possible. Don't get me wrong, the bass is there, but it's not 'movie theater' bass that rumbles your chest. For me this is perfect, but for others it may be unacceptable. Something else you should consider is that these are open back headphones, so there will be sound bleed into the room as well as sound bleed from whatever else is in the room. This hasn't been an issue for me, but if you live in a noisy area you may want to consider a more isolated system.

I give the product 5 stars because I can't find anything I don't like about it. I am confident that these headphones will last me many years.

product_title: Pangea Audio - DS300 - Heavy Duty Speaker Stand - Pair - 24 Inches
review_headline: Flimsy, Cheap, Worthless. Avoid. Avoid. Avoid.
review_body:
I am not frequently disappointed by a product, and I have had great luck with Pangea's cables, but these stands are rubbish. Avoid at all costs; these are an embarrassment to the brand.

The manufacturing quality is very low; there are dramatic inconsistencies in the lengths of arms; mine varied by several mm from piece to piece. This is a lot worse than it sounds because the plates are incredibly thin metal, especially the top plate. The unevenness in the arms caused dramatic distortion in my top plate, and I'm not sure there's enough Blu-Tak in the world to heal these sins. I was able to make a true mating to the floor via the different spike lengths (they are adjustable), but there was nothing I could do about the top plate being horribly torqued and warped on both stands due to the legs being uneven.

Independent of the manufacturing tolerances, the real problem here is the plate thickness; Pangea clearly skimped on both the top and bottom plate in this regard. While the bottom plate has a rounded edge to provide some additional rigidity, the top plate is incredibly flimsy. I have a pair of stands that were only slightly more expensive that feature 1/4" thick steel top and bottom plates and they exhibit none of these problems.

product_title: NHT SuperZero 2.1 Mini-Monitor Speaker (Single, Gloss Black)
review_headline: Ive been in love with my NHT Super Zero's ever since I bought ...
review_body:
I am an audiophile on a budget. Ive been in love with my NHT Super Zero's ever since I bought 5 satellites and their 10\\" powered subwoofer, over 20 years ago for my home theater, after reading a fabulous review in \\"Stereophile\\" magazine, written by my favorite Stereo equipment reviewer \\" Corey Greenberg.\\"
I just bought a pair for my large dining room/kitchen area, and I'm once again super impressed, with the sound these physically and sonically, gorgeous mini monitors produce. They are truly high resolution monitors, having said that, their only going to sound as good as the source material is, adding no coloration of their own. But they will reveal any deficiencies in the recordings. They also need to be placed away from any obstructions to appreciate their wide, and deep soundstage imaging their capable of. I have my two main channel home theater pair on speakers stands, my center channel, right below the T.V , isolated and anchored with 3M blue tack,( removes any unwanted vibrations that can muddy up the sound and imaging, and my rear pair, mounted high on brackets, unobstructed, hanging from the ceiling. The new pair, in my dining room, are mount on brackets on a sidewall laterally facing mid point of the area. Im using a no frills 8\\" Acurian powered sub, from Radio Shack. You must use a subwoofer with these babies to enjoy the full spacious sound they produce. It can be a \\"passive\\" subwoofer, ( no internal amplification)of decent quality, if you can find one. (Radioshack used to sell a very reasonably priced 12\\" model under their \\"Optimus\\" label. I intend to replace the Acurian sub, with a NHT 8\\" or 10 inch powered sub in the near future.
And finally, you need good amplification, I personally love the sound \\"Harman Kardon\\" receivers and amps produce. The have a vacuum tube like quality that compliments the Super Zeros beautifully, especially on Acoustic Jazz ensemble recordings. Optimally placed and properly amplified, you will be amazed how wonderful they sound. As I said earlier, Im on a budget and cant afford to spend thousands on my systems. Im also aware of the \\" law of diminishing returns\\". And in todays home audio market, it kicks in at very affordable price points. You can have an awesome sounding system if you pay attention to what you put together. Listen to as many systems as you can, don't listen to sales people, and read reviews to get a working knowledge of how things work. Highly recommended!sound. product_title: The House of Marley Stir It Up On-Ear Headphones - Freedom Collection - Three-Button Apple Mic
review_body:
I bought these headphones in June of 2013 as an upgrade to my failing House of Marley Revolutions. I didn't plan to buy another pair of Marleys', not because my Revolutions were bad, but because I had been looking at Klipsch Image One headphones for a while. On a late night Amazon headphone shopping I ran into these and absolutely fell in love with the design and desided to buy after reading the reviews and having prior fantastic experiences with my previous pair of House of Marley cans. And boy I'm glad I did.

Pros:
1.Sound is fantastic. No where in the volume band 0-100% do I get distortion on either my HTC One or audio interface (I tube based Panasonic combo unit). Dispite being celebrity branded these are NOT bass cannons. The bass is not the deepest and loosest sounding bass, it's very tight and well controlled. The mids are well present throughout the volume spectrum, and trebles sound pure as can be, even too loud for some.

2.Build quality. Germany couldn't even make a car that feels this fell built. No where have a gotton any sqeeking sounds or cracks in intense use. Perfect here.

3.Enviromentally responcible: Recycled aluminum, fabrics, and wood all being present in the design makes me confident in their low enviromental impact if tossed in the bin (NOT HAPPENING)

4.One love. Profits go to the One Love charity. Love it.

Cons:They can't be perfect can they?
1. The cable....... Okay. I'm not the only one who's had bad experience with the cable. It's very fashionable and strong, but in my experience it was a piece of garbage. Failed after less than a week of light use. Luckily these cans work with any 3.5mm AUX cable so replacement was simple.

2.Comfort (Arguable). They were very tight and fatiquing when I first purchased these. Which is a very common complaint on these headphones. The comfort quickly became better and the headphones are alot looser but still form a perfect seal.

Conclusion: The House or Marley Stir It Up's are stellar headphones that offer fantastic sounds, build, and style. Well worth my money 4/5

review_body: These were exactly what I was looking for. Along with being well made and attractive, they are perfectly proportioned for my Ascend Sierra 1's. I did read most of the reviews stating to be sure and mount these to a stud. Not true, in my application. Both of my mounts are installed in drywall with hollow wall anchors and are extremely sturdy. I used Toggler Snaptoggle BA (3/16" x 2-1/2 Heavy Duty Toggle Bolts) in the top and bottom mounting holes and a Toggler TB (#8 x 1-1/2" Medium Duty Drywall Anchor) in the middle mounting hole. This way you can mount your speakers where you want instead of where you have to. I do have my speakers angled down as far as the adjustment will allow and do recommend using the bottom screw hole and the screws provided to secure the bottom of your speaker to the mount. My only negative finding is after using a leveler to mount these perfectly upright, I noticed the brackets holding the speakers weren't perfectly level and had to place a small sliver of cardboard between the bracket and speaker to bring one side slightly higher.

product_title: Xantech DL95M Universal Dinky Link IR Receiver, Manual Adjust
review_body:
I have a 60" plasma TV in the bedroom with my equipment rack in the closet which is on the opposite side of the wall that the plasma TV is mounted on. I use a Xantech extender kit (789-44 block, standard 291 receiver, and 4 emitters). For years I dealt with dodgy IR control. With the lights out in the closet where the equipment rack is, and the TV turned on, I could see the emitters glowing and flickering along with scene changes on the TV screen in the other room. It was the IR receiver in the bedroom picking up a signal from the plasma TV. This would "flood" the IR receivers in each of my equipment items that had an emitter attached. Some tolerated it better than others. The cable box was largely unaffected. The Bluray player had a hard time. Sometimes I would have to turn down the brightness on the TV so that I could control the Bluray player. Finally, I switched from cable to uverse and the uverse receiver box was completely unusable via infrared remote.

So, I bought the DL95M. It was much smaller then the standard 291 so I had to velcro it to the top of the TV. I turned on the TV and turned out the lights in the equipment closet. The emitters were no longer glowing or flickering. I went around to the bedroom and used the uverse IR remote to control the receiver box and each button-press worked flawlessly every time. The "plasma friendly" DL95M was the answer. I should have bought it long ago. (Well, I know why I didn't. They used to be very expensive. This one was half the cost of what they used to be).

Just FYI, I did *not* have to adjust the sensitivity (small screw on the back). It works fine right out of the box but I'm very glad to have that capability if I ever need it.

product_title: Bluetooth Music Receiver, Kissmart® Portable Bluetooth V4.0 Handsfree Car Home Audio Music Streaming Receiver Adapter with Hands Free Calling and 3.5 Mm Stereo Output
review_body:
I received this as a review sample and tested it not in my car, but connected to the 3.5MM Aux port on my [[ASIN:B0035EHLZK Roland KC-110 3-Channel 30-Watt Stereo Mixing Keyboard Amplifier]]. The reasons for five stars are the fact that this worked out of the box, immediately paired and connected when I scanned for it from my phone (after powering this little receiver on), and the high quality of the stream itself.

When I say it worked out of the box I was probably lucky that 170mAh battery had sufficient charge to activate the receiver and put it into broadcast mode for my phone to pick up in a scan. If this does not work for you in a similar manner, charge it using the included cable from any 5 volt power source, like the one that came with your phone or a lighter socket style charger in your vehicle, No charger is included, but they are so ubiquitous these days that you probably have one and it holds the price down on this unit.

The bluetooth connection is crystal clear with no dropouts. I tested mine at twenty feet and had zero problems. If you use this in a vehicle you will definitely not experience any signal drops.

There are a few things I did not completely test. One is how long it takes to fully charge the internal battery and the other is how long it will last after it has been charged. I put my received on a charger for an hour and it was going strong two hours later after I disconnected it.

The final reason why I awarded this five stars is it is bundled with an NFC tag. The tag is not programmed and has nothing to do with the receiver unless you program it to do something like auto connect to it when you are within range. Or you can use it for something else entirely. Frankly I was accustomed to NFC pairing, but had no idea that I could actually program a blank tag until I received this one. If you want to learn more about how to use the NFC tag that is bundled as a bonus do a web search for this phrase: 'The most practical, creative ways to use NFC with your Android device', which will take you to a CNET article and how to video.ost practical, creative ways to use NFC with your Android device', which will take you to a CNET article and how to video.

review_headline: Sound extremely muffled, can't hear lyrics
review_body:
Very Poor quality headphones. My cousin bought them for me as a bday gift, put batteries in, plugged it in, turned on the noise canceling and the sound was so muffled you couldn't even understand what they were singing. Sometimes you'd only heard backup singers. With some songs it worked better, though still muffled, if you pulled the plug out a little from the jack. I tried it with a Dell, Macbook Pro, Asus laptop, Samsung S3, and all had the same results.

I returned it (since you can't get a replacement) and he bought me a second one. Now the second one was a completely different headphone even though it was reordered from the same purchase (matte instead of gloss, carrier bag instead of hard case, only 1 cord instead of 4 accessories) but the second one still had the same issues. I tried everything to trouble shoot it and asked tech-savy guys who own countless headphones (Beats, Bose, Sony, etc.) and they all said it was a dud. Would've given it a higher rating if it even worked.

Pros: looks good, feels pretty durable, pads are soft, tangle-free cord, noise canceling feature (I'm not a pro but it just sounded like the volume was turned up)

Cons: muffled sound quality (at least the 2 I got), lacks hard case, cups slightly too tight just below ear lobes (avg sized head)

review_headline: Just ok... not as bright as expected.
review_body: My TV was working fine.  Since I obtained the TV used, I do not know if the previous owner had ever changed this bulb.  I also had no idea how many hours were on my bulb as the bulb counter was inadvertently reset to zero before making note of the hours.  All I could say for certain is that my old bulb had something between 2,500 and 10,000 hours... 2,500 since the counter was reset and 10,000 hours since the TV was brand new.    My goal in purchasing this bulb was to replace mine with something brand new and use my original bulb as a working spare in the event of a future bulb failure.    I was expecting this new bulb to be brighter than my old bulb, or at the very least \\"as bright\\" as my old bulb.  This new bulb is working and it warms up faster than my old bulb, however, it just doesn't seem as bright. The message also stated that I could \\"reply\\" to the email to provide my feedback.   So I did.  I let the seller know that I thought the bulb was not as bright as it should be. review_headline: works with my samsung s5 with 5 pin to 11pin usb adapter
review_body: I just purchased this item to use with my samsung s5, got a good deal on it. At first, it did not work, but I did not panic, knowing my phone is mhl enabled. I looked at the companies website, and since this product was made way before this phone, it is not listed as compatible, and I didn't have another phone on the list to check the function, nor another adapter. So, I emailed the company, and got a response within a day on what I needed to do. Apparently samsung S5 uses an 11 pin usb plug vs. 5 pin on the mhl adapter, so they offered to send me an adapter (5 pin to 11 pin to slip over the end) at no charge. It arrived, I put it on, and it worked right away, and even works with my powerbank as the power supply. 5 stars on the picture and sound, product does as it is supposed to, and 5 stars to the customer service.

product_title: Sennheiser Momentum In-Ear
review_headline: Amazing sound tuning in a modern "classic" design!
review_body:
I knew Senns was cooking something new to announce during or after IFA 2014, but I had no idea what to expect. The moment I read about Momentum In-Ear announcement and saw a promo video - I already started speculating in my mind how these going to be tuned. With such a bold design look they were obviously trying to appeal to a younger crowd who values bass and want smartphone controls, but calling it "Momentum" tied it up to a family of audiophile quality full size headphones that appeal to a more mature crowd with priorities of sound quality above the looks. I was in for a big surprise when I received my review sample and came to a conclusion that Senns cooked a perfect formula to make everybody happy and managed to deliver that under $100. Here is what I found.

One thing you can always count on with Senns is to deliver a great unboxing experience. Even prior to opening a compact packaging box it arrived in, I had a pretty good idea what to expect by taking a "tour" around the box to find out about its design details, features, controls and accessories. In the past I have reviewed Momentum over-ear headphones, so was surprised how cleverly they scaled down the packaging details for in-ears. You have a similar form fitting foam cutout where they placed a premium quality black case with a zipper and a red stitching details. There was an additional cutout with a small bag containing two pairs of eartips, and also a manual booklet. Unzipping a case revealed what appears to be a wire spool with headphones and in-line remote sitting in the middle and the rest of the flat wire wrapped around. On a back of the spool there was a space for another pair of eartips and headphone plug.

As much as I enjoyed this presentation, I have to admit this spool will not be used again because I found 45deg angles formed during the wire wrapping to cause a memory effect in the wire which I'm still trying to straighten out. Its great for presentation, but not practical for every day use. Luckily, spool comes out without a problem, and you have a high quality headphone case with a space enough to store even a small mp3 player like Clip+. Headphones itself had yet another pair of eartips already on, with all 4 pairs (XS, S, M, L) being silicone and having a signature line across the bore opening (works great as a stopper so you don't push a nozzle all the way through). I would have liked to see some Comply foam tips as well, though actually found included eartips to provide an excellent fitment and decent sound isolation.

When it comes to a design of headphones itself, I found these to have a very unique look to stand out from the crowd. Though I can only see an angled nozzle made out of stainless steel material and metal loop on the back for a strain relief - from a design diagram on the back of the packaging box it looks like inner body is made out of metal as well with a red plastic shell on top of it. Earpieces were very light weight, and I also found a slit port opening at the top which I'm sure contributed to a wide airy soundstage. Right were the wire comes out from the shell, you have R marking on the right side, and 3 bumps on the left side to id L/R even in the dark.

As I mentioned above, strain relief was provided in a form of a small metal loop extended from the back of the shell where you have a stamped and laser etched surface with a signature "S" which looks like a reversed "Z". Wire shielding is flat and narrow and has a slightly oval shape. From earpiece down to y-splitter the shielding is actually bi-colored with a black on outside and a red on inside (a very classy design touch), and all black from y-splitter down to 90deg L-shaped gold plated headphone plug with a very nice strain relief. Y-splitter itself is minimalistic, and right next to it you will find a chin-slider with a small "S" signature sticker. It's very rare to see achin slider in a setup with in-line remote control since you can't slide it beyond that, but it's still effective to bring L/R cables closer with in-line remote/mic. I only sensed a slight hint of microphonics while sitting down and moving my head, but not when I was walking around.

While some companies are trying to take an easy way out by providing either a universal remote with only a single multi-function button and mic or iPhone controls with addition of volume up/down buttons that work only with iOS, Sennheiser actually makes 2 different Momentun in-ear models, one for Android and another one for iPhone. My review sample had in-line remote for Android which Senns call "IEG" meaning In-Ear with "Galaxy" controls. But they are very clear on top of the packaging box specifying that it will work not only with Samsung Galaxy phones but also LG, HTC, Sony and other smartphones and tablets. Unfortunately, some android devices might not support it since I know for sure that Moto implements a different wiring which is not compatible with other common headphone controls. So if you don't have one of those common Android brand phones, please double check with Sennheiser website for a list of compatible devices.

In my case, it worked perfectly fine with Note 2 and S5 where single click was used for Play/Pause/Call, double click to skip next, triple click to skip prev, and long press to start Google NOW. Volume control was flawlessly integrated with my phone, and mic had a great sensitivity where I heard no complains from people on the other side of the call. The location of the remote/mic was at a perfect level to pickup voice without a problem and also to reach controls without pulling on the wire. Plus, buttons on the remote were nicely shaped with id marks and were easy to locate just by touch.

But as you know, without a sound to back it up, all these design details will be worthless. Even so I'm a strong believer in a burn in, especially with dynamic drivers, I still like to get an idea of a sound out of the box. Don't be shocked but right out of the box it had a mid-bass bloat spilling into the rest of the spectrum. For a split second I thought to myself, oh no, hopefully these are not "basshead" beats. Without further hesitation, I put these down for an initial 12hrs burn in, and the next morning woke up to a brand new sound! After an additional 8hrs on top of that, I felt the sound settled down and I was ready to evaluate it.

I found the overall sound signature to be slightly v-shaped with a bright detailed tuning and an enhanced bass emphasis. Starting with low frequencies, these have a deep extended sub-bass texture with a nice rumble and a fast mid-bass punch. Bass is well controlled with just a slight spillage into lower mids. It definitely has an enhanced bass quantity, but it's not over the top and without any perception of mid-bass bloat (which settled down nicely after burn in). Mids are slightly recessed, thus creating v-shaped signature, but it's very tastefully tuned to give bass more power. Upper mids sound very clear and detailed creating a happy medium between brightness and warmth. Especially when it comes to vocals, either male or female, they sound relatively natural with a nice body. Treble is well extended, crispy, but not sibilant. Sound is bright but not too hot or at the level causing ear fatigue. Soundstage has a great width and depth, almost approaching 3D level in some of the songs. Any music genre, from EDM to classical or pop and rock sounded very dynamic and with a great layering and separation of instruments (either if its electronic or acoustic timbers). I really enjoyed retrieval of the details in these IEMs. Also, it was very easy to drive these from any source, either smartphone or DAP, though having a warmer source might be more beneficial to keep brightness under control. For example, I prefer to usethese headphones with my "darker" X1 versus a "brighter" X5. I also found it to be quite forgiving even with lower quality encoded mp3s.

Overall, I was extremely pleased with new Momentum In-Ear headphones! Their sound tuning is full of energy and details to appeal to anybody who enjoys music, doesn't matter what style or tempo you are listening to. It provides extra bass, but does it tastefully without being a basshead monster. It provides clarity and details, without pushing analytical envelope with harsh tuning. It has a fun signature and still keeps upper mids in check to deliver great vocals without being too recessed. Even so I think they are a jack of all trades, I also find them to be a moderate master of all of them at the same time. With a great durable build, a modern design, full integration of smartphone controls (either for android or iphone), and a very impressive sound tuning, for under $100 these definitely deserve a serious consideration!r in a burn in, especially with dynamic drivers, I still like to get an idea of a sound out of the box. product_title: Ape Case 12 CD DVD Blu-Ray and Gaming Case (AC12473)
review_headline: Plastic Doesn't Hold Up in Hot Temperatures
review_body:
I really liked this case a lot more in the first week I owned it. It's about as compact as you can possibly get, just a little bit bigger than the disks it holds. The material felt nice, the strap was useful, and the zipper action was smooth. Unfortunately, over time and a day of sitting in my car, all of my game disks that were in the case stuck to the clear plastic part of each sleeve. When I peeled it off and pulled the games out of the case, they had a residue on them that I had to wash off from the clear plastic part of each sleeve. Unfortunately, what made it worse is that I hadn't tucked all the game disks completely inside the sleeves, so a little bit of the clear plastic on each sleeve touched the bottom of the games, making them unreadable until I went at them with some dish soap to get that sticky residue removed.

I've had this happen to CD cases in the past, but certainly not to all of them. After all, before I got my iPod, I've had CD wallets that have been left in my car for weeks and months at a time without issue. I might use this game case again in the future if I'm visiting a friend's house and don't want to drag all my game cases with me (after all, it really is a great compact design), but I certainly won't trust it in a hot car ever again, and I won't let games sit in it for months at a time.

product_title: JBL J88i Premium Over-Ear Headphones with JBL Drivers, Rotatable Ear-Cups and Microphone - Black
review_body:
As a self proclaimed audiophile these are some decent headphones. I bought these back when they were around $170, now that they're $99 they have become a pretty good deal.

Sound: They are definitely some quality cans, they are slightly emphatic on the bass as they're size and driver measurements would suggest. Very clear, especially when used through a DAC and amp. On a my iPhone 5 I was a little unimpressed with the bass actually, but I was able to help that with the wonderful app Can Opener (any serious mobile listener should give this app a look) The main problem that I had with the sound actually has to do with the fit of the headphones. But very good drivers and supremely clear sound with a good amount of bass. The highs were clear, and the bass was clear and strong without sounding muddled. There is a slight drop off between the mids and lows, so the visual equalizer layout for these would look like a "U" with a slightly lowered left side.

Fit: Of course these will most likely fit your head differently than they do mine, but they fit me very well on level 7 of the 8 available levels. I have a taller and more narrow head, so that fitting makes sense. They are quite comfortable even for several hours of continuous use. The leatherette doesn't get too hot and the pressure isn't much at all. The lack of pressure was actually a problem for me because the sound wouldn't fully tunnel into my ear, it would leak slightly out of the sides, but that is something that I haven't read too much about in the reviews so that is probably unique to my head shape. These are definitely good looking headphones, but also rather large, almost cumbersome to walk around with.

Build Quality: The whole pair is made of matte plastic except for the aluminum shiny bits on the sides and top. I think someone must have gotten to mine when I wasn't looking, as the right connection between the rotational piece and the headband broke, as well as the microfiber parts on the inside of the right ear came apart, revealing the cushioning inside that ear piece. I was sorely disappointed when this happened, but I don't blame JBL for this, as I have younger siblings who like to "take a look at" my things, and I also own several other Harman brand products that have no faults like this. But just be careful with your headphones!

Conclusion: These are a great pair of headphones for the money, I will always recommend these above Beats, especially for the price. Crisp and clear on all the highs, mids, and lows, only slightly emphatic on the lows, and slight drop off in the mids. If you go with the J88i's as opposed to the J88's be aware that they are only iPhone compatible if you wish to use the inline controls that the "i" model comes with.iber parts on the inside of the right ear came apart, revealing the cushioning inside that ear piece. product_title: Marantz CD6005 Hi-Fi Compact Disc Player with USB-A DAC
review_headline: Very nice product in both sound and design
review_body:
This is a review based upon usage of about a week.

I heavily researched my quest for a new CD player. I have been slowly making a return to listening to music more critically and my option until purchasing this Marantz was a Sony Blu-Ray player. It was competent at best, but I didn't believe I was really getting the best from my CD collection.

I had early on established a few criteria for a new CD player: quality DAC, well-built transport mechanism (these have been failing points in the remote past), and both a headphone jack WITH variable output. Early in 2014 I purchased a nice pair of Sennheiser headphones and I like to use them. But without a headphone jack it would mean going through the receiver, which I think would slightly decrease sound quality. But even with a headphone jack one really needs a variable output and Marantz offered both. As Marantz was already in my head as a company from which I felt I could confidently purchase a CD player it seems like it was a perfect match.

So this CD6005 fires on all cylinders for me. Quality components inside. A handsome exterior. Plugged in and running I immediately noticed an improvement to the music coming from my system. Highs were clearer... tighter and bass had more punch and less rumble. I would describe the difference as going from a 128kbps MP3 file to an ALAC one (all other things being equal). The differences are noticeable and obvious.

This is a fairly pricey piece of equipment and Marantz does make two other, lower-level models, but I opted for the CD6005 as I hope it will be the founding product to a revamped 2-channel music system that I hope to put together over the next 12-24 months. But in the interim my current system already is capable of showing me what the CD6005 can do (at least in comparison to a Sony Blu-Ray player) and it is completely awesome to be able to plug in my headphones, adjust the volume and enjoy listening directly from the player.ayer.

review_body: Looked to purchase a Bluetooth speaker to have something to listen to in our hotel and the beach on our recent trip to Florida. A good friend of mine has an EU Boom and was highly impressed. However, I didn't really want to spend $200. So I did some research and read many reviews. I consider myself an audiophile and have a good understanding of wattage, frequency response, db's, etc. I am happy to say that I love the SHARKK. The one spec that caught my eye was the frequency response. All speakers I reviewed went up to 20khz but most only went down to 150hz or so, which limits bass. The SHARKK stated that the response went down to 60hz ( the human ear can can hear 20-20k with perfect hearing. (Age, health, and other variables play into this as well). This unit indeed has wonderful lows. In comparison to the EU Boom, the SHARKK will not go quite as loud , but the QUALITY of the sound is richer and is certainly loud enough for my needs. Bottom line, for the price (or even double the price) I think you'd be hard pressed to find a unit of this nice. It has some ass to it as well. It's not some lightweight cheap plastic thing that is going to bounce or move around at higher volumes. Glad I made the purchase. ADDITION TO REVIEW: I had this thing is the hot Florida sun for 4-6 hrs a day for 4 of our 5 days in Panama City Beach and the battery never let me down.

product_title: Mount-It! LCD, LED, Plasma TV Wall Mount Bracket for Cable Box, DVD Player, Stereo Components Shelf
review_headline: Beware - specs on web page are way off but shelf is OK.  Not great but OK.
review_body:
Beware - specs on web page are way off but shelf is decent if the dimensions work for you.
The web page shows pictures with dimensions of both the one shelf and 2 shelf versions.
It shows the height as 24.5 inches for both. Beware that the 1-shelf version is only 16 inches tall. (30% shorter than shown)
It happens this worked OK for my application but it was much shorter than I expected.
I used it to hang a laptop (used as a media PC) and Wii below a 60 inch LED TV in my gym.
This TV is hanging from the ceiling with a ceiling mount.
I was concerned the width would be close but it was wide enough for a 60 inch TV to align with the VESA holes. I had measured and knew it would be close and it was but indeed it worked.
The hardware is all cheap and not powder coated. For my application since this is just in a gym and not in my house this was OK.
If it was in my house I would replace the cheap screws and bolts etc with powder coated versions that match the rest of the product.
It is not very deep and being curved it is even less deep at the edges. The Toshiba 17" widescreen laptop I have on it just barely fits hanging over the edges a bit. Still this sort of thing is very hard to find (I did a LOT of looking) and this actually worked out decent for me. I would but it again. If I had know it was this short I might have bought the 2-shelf version assuming it is actually taller. The design leaves a bit to be desired in terms of ease of assembly but it is nothing huge. You really need a right angle screwdriver to tighten the brackets down securely that hold the shelf in place. But I happened to have something like that on hand. As it worked out being shorter at 16 in actually made it easier for me because this means it only hits the bottom 2 VESA holes so I did not have to remove my TV from the mount, just remove the bottom 2 screws and slide this between the mount in the TVA and screw it back down. So hanging it was pretty easy. It was a one-person job. It would be nice if the shelf was anything other than glass (well except for plastic of course). I really don't like glass shelves but this is about all you can find. I could always make my own replacement shelf if I had to. The bracket was the important part to me.

I'm not super tech savvy, but I don't think I should have to be to operate a clock radio. review_body: T̶h̶e̶ ̶q̶u̶a̶l̶i̶t̶y̶ ̶o̶f̶ ̶t̶h̶e̶ ̶a̶c̶t̶u̶a̶l̶ ̶c̶a̶b̶l̶e̶ ̶i̶t̶s̶e̶l̶f̶ ̶s̶e̶e̶m̶s̶ ̶s̶t̶o̶u̶t̶ ̶e̶n̶o̶u̶g̶h̶ ̶b̶u̶t̶ ̶t̶h̶e̶r̶e̶ ̶a̶r̶e̶ ̶s̶e̶v̶e̶r̶a̶l̶ ̶m̶a̶j̶o̶r̶ ̶i̶s̶s̶u̶e̶s̶ ̶w̶i̶t̶h̶ ̶t̶h̶i̶s̶ ̶c̶a̶b̶l̶e̶.    --EDIT--: I decided to dissect one of my cables seeing as it was now useless with broken connectors-- who knows, maybe I could solder on some new ends? What I found was almost hilarious. This 'cable' is all rubber. Literally there is a tiny coaxial cable with minimal shielding running through a massive pipe of rubber. Do yourself a favor and purchase some Hosa cables. --END EDIT--    First is the phono (RCA) plugs: they are way too tight. Like, pull the receptacles out of the back of your device tight. Contrary to popular opinion this is not the sign of a quality connection-- the ends should fit and be snug NOT be too small that you have to wrestle them on. If you try and loosen them with a pair of pliers you'll find the cheap gold colored pewter connectors just break apart, not bend like a quality termination. This is enough of a deal breaker on it's own but there is a major design flaw with the connector on the other end as well.  The termination into the 3.5mm phone connection is MASSIVE. This might not be an issue if you are using one of these but I'm using 3 to plug into the back of my soundcard. They don't fit, not even close. This size sheath would look out of place on a 1/4\\" plug let alone an 1/8\\". What's more, I can't imagine having that much leverage on the phone receptacle is a good thing.    I'm giving these one star for very nearly ruining a connector on the back of my expensive receiver and for the chintzy gold colored pewter connectors.

product_title: Cheetah Mounts APTMSB Flat Screen TV Wall Mount Bracket Designed for 32"-55" Plasma LED LCD TV (Actually Fits 20-55" TVs) Includes Free 10' Braided High Speed HDMI Cable With Ethernet
review_headline: Design Flaws + Cheap Price = A Headache Galore
review_body: I bought this mount on Wayfair, because it was on a flash sale for $16 and came with free 2-day shipping.  I have the 51" Samsung PN51F4500BFXZA Plasma, and I thought mounting this would be a breeze.  First of all, the package comes with WAY too many little pieces to put together; in my opinion, assembling a plate/bracket shouldn't be that tedious.  Second, the design of the mount is flawed.  There are two screws at the bottom of each arm, that are supposed to be screwed to the bottom of the mount, for safety.  Let me just say that I couldn't even get the TV to tilt enough so that I could get behind the TV to tighten the safety screws.  I had to take the TV off of the mount 3 times, just to see if there was a way for me to get behind the screen, so I could tighten the little "safety" screws.  Long story short, I was able to get the TV mounted, but there's nothing to secure the bottom portion of the arms, so I'm now super paranoid about my TV falling or something.  I wasn't expecting this mount to be such a headache, but I don't think I'll ever purchase from Cheetah again, as this mount created more worry than security.  Definitely not worth the money.

review_headline: so good. The braided covers are nice
review_body:
So far, so good. The braided covers are nice. Far less worry about accidental damage to the cable itself, especially since these were used for wall mounting, and routing through wall and wall plates. Didn't feel at all bad about giving them a bit of pull to adjust, gently, of course, and not holding by the end. Ordinary cable could be more easily scraped, but these were protected by the mesh. 10' length seems fine for the current setup. Not too long, not too short.

The angle adapters didn't work for my set, but they're still neat, and I'll keep in case they come in handy someday. My TV, however, has the top end facing towards back, making these adapters unable to be used.

Overall, perhaps not as nice as some cables, but they work, I like the mesh protection, and the cost is very competitive. Almost went with monoprice but have these a chance, as I was also getting a wall mount kit that included one, so I got a few more to match.

It's nice to have a "matched set" for the setup. If treated gently, I don't see why they shouldn't last.

product_title: Sennheiser Urbanite XL Over-Ear Headphones
review_headline: Wow. It really is like being there.
review_body:
These headphones are amazing. It feels like I'm right in the studio listenings to the artists sing. The sound comes through crisp and clear.

The build is incredible. These headphones feel solid and the adjustable ear covers help make them a great fit.

Do they produce listening fatigue?

I have a different pair of over the ear headphones, and after a while, they just become uncomfortable to wear because of the pressure that's put on the head around the ears.

These headphones had just a tiny, and I mean tiny, bit of that when using them for hours. The padding is soft enough, and the size makes it so that the weight and pressure from the headphones are more evenly distributed.

The audio cable has a twist to lock feature so that it can't be pulled out of the headphones which is a very nice feature.

The call/audio controls on the cable are easy enough, although the controls could have been smaller.

I noticed a nice touch, that on the inside of the head band, three vertically aligned dots are on the left side. It's braille for the letter "L" for left side.

How do these compare to Bose headphones? It depends on the type you have, but the type we have sit on the ear rather that cover over the ear like the Sennheiser.

I like the base in the Bose better, but I like the fullness that the Sennheiser produces. Also, if the style of the Sennheiser matches your taste better.

The headphones also come with a very nice travel pouch.

product_title: Sony MDRXB950AP/H Extra Bass Smartphone Headset (Silver)
review_headline: Rich deep bass, crisp highs, comfortable, all for a very reasonable price! Simply Duhmazing :)
review_body:
I bought these in store in Sony's store front in San Diego, CA. I have had Bose OTH headphones for over a decade now. 2 pairs in two different versions. They were good but listening to these and several others in the Sony line in store it's apparent that Sony has seriously upped its game.
So here is my review.

Physically the headphones feel sturdy and have good mass. The ear pads are very thick, I tried on every pair of headphones in the store from the $500 Hi Res Audio all the way down and I personally thought these were more comfortable and produced a better sound. The only con as another poster said is they do not include a carry bag, all my Bose have come with carrying cases. Not worth a star reduction but I would like to have had a pouch for them.

Comparing these with my BOSE AE2, these blow my BOSE Over the Ear headphones out of the water. The sound is better, deeper, richer.

The bass response is definitely richer, I felt like with even some of the other Sony models even there was a wall or ceiling with the bass response where if you hit the right frequency it would flatten out. These never did that no matter which album I threw up against them.

For testing I spent an hour and half in the store with my iPod and several albums in FLAC format. I went through various albums, just to name some of the music I sampled on them: Maroon 5 (V), Fireflight (Now), Linkin Park - Living Things, Luke Bryan - My Kind of Party. I had a few playlists I cycled through as I tried on all the headphones in the line. I kept coming back to this pair. I walked out with these and I didnt really need a new pair, but they are just that damn good. If you can go in a Sony store and put a pair through the paces I recommend it, everyone likes different things, but these are an amazing pair for sure. Sony could easily charge $150 for them in my opinion.

Lastly professionally packaged, no clam-shell crap when open them. The box opens to an inner casing, then it folds open like a cigar box and there they sit nice and cozy ready for use. I hate having to cut that stuff off to get electronics out. So to me that was a nice plus.to an inner casing, then it folds open like a cigar box and there they sit nice and cozy ready for use. product_title: Klipsch KF-28 Icon Dual 8" 2-Way Floorstanding Speaker (Each)(Black Ash)
review_body:
This speaker is awesome. I replaced two small bookshelf speakers that I had purchased in a set for 5.1 surround sound system with these. The richness and room filling sound that comes out of these is amazing. Watching movies is like a theater experience and music is rich and deep.

I was satisfied with my previous setup, but adding the Klipsch speakers let me know what I was actually missing. If I ever get the cash I might try replacing the other 3 speakers and the subwoofer with Klipsch products. But for the time being I still have a great sound system that is the envy of most of my guests.

They say these speakers are for small to medium size rooms, but my living room is fairly large and the sound is great. This speaker is also fairly tall and heavy. It looks nice on either side of my 60" flat screen, though. I also prefer the look of the bare front without the protective cover, but there are kids and pets running around so I'm leaving the cover on for now.

Set up was easy since I was just replacing two smaller speakers with these. Although, I was a bit confused by the dual hookups. These speakers have the capability to use bi-wire cables. Meaning there are 4 wires running from the amplifier to the speaker. On the back of the speaker there are two red and two black hookups. One wire is for the high frequency and one is for the low frequency.

This is a newer feature and audiophiles have different opinions about the effectiveness of this setup. I would like to try a bi-wire setup, but the bi-wire cables are very pricey and I would have to order them online. I did try radio shack and the salesman just gave me a blank look and pointed me towards spools of speaker cable.

I already had a spool of 16 gauge wire at home that I used. Even though these speakers have the terminals for a bi-wire setup there are also jumpers between the terminals. Meaning that electrically everything is hooked up and I still got awesomesound without the bi-wire setup.

Like I said, these are nice speakers and they improved the sound of my current system significantly. I could probably improve it more by adding the bi-wire cables and upgrading the other speaker components, but I am happy with what I currently have too.

review_headline: Just what i was looking for
review_body:
Bought this because of all the positive reviews and was looking for a way to get free HDTV with basic programming via full range UHF/VHF. I checked in with Xfinity and they don't even offer HD for basic cable. You are stuck paying for expanded which could run you $75-100/mo after paying taxes, HD technology fee and equipment rental. No way!

I mounted this rig on my roof and had to run coax through my garage and into the living room (the hardest part). I connected this to my old TiVo box and did a channel scan (testing signal strength too). I picked up 99 strong channels (80 of them i will never watch), but the local FOX, CBS, NBC, KQED, ABC came in nicely and with blu ray video quality, much better than the cable company's compressed video signals.

I highly recommend this antenna. The key thing is to install this properly. Go to http://antennapoint.com to see where your local towers are and use your iPhone compass to point the antenna in the right direction!

product_title: Sennheiser Headphones
review_body:
I'm a real fan of these headphones. If you are looking for beautiful sound reproduction and a blissful listening experience at a (relatively) low cost then these are for you. Keep in mind that these are "open" earphones. They don't have a closed back so the music you listen to can be heard (at a lower level) by those around you and you will be able to hear things going on around you as well. This allows the headphone to produce a beautiful sound stage which means you hear the music around you rather than inside your head. If you are thinking about something to wear on a plane, around town or on the subway then these may not be the best choice. If you want a headphone that you can wear at home and that will make you fall in love with music all over again, then these are a great place to start.

If you like songs with great vocals, you will be very pleased with the HD598s. It has an amazing mid-range that really makes the singers pop. You get the sense that the vocals are right in front of you while the instruments are playing around the singer. A lot of people will say that the bass is lacking, but I disagree. I have found the bass to be tight and just what it should be to compliment the music. I have some bass heavy headphones and I never wear them anymore. The sound quality is great on my other phones, but the bass overpowers the music and muddies up the fine details in the music that come through so clearly with these Sennheisers.

Also, remember that your headphones are only as good as your music source. You want something that has a quality DAC (digital to analog converter) and enough power to drive your headphones. These HD598s are relatively easy to drive with an iPod or iPhone and will sound pretty good. If you want to unleash their full potential, look into a player like the Fiio X1, X3 or X5. A good quality DAC/Amp will remove the "noise" that you can get from lesser components and really let these headphones soar.nes soar.

product_title: BoostWaves WA2802 HDTV Digital Outdoor Antenna Remote Controlled Rotation High Band Super Long Range
review_headline: Great product for the price, amazing reception.
review_body: First impressions    I'm not one to write many reviews but I feel obliged to for this product.  Hopefully I can update this later with a full review after I've used it for a while.  This exceeded my expectations for reception!!  I quickly hooked it up, plugged it into the amplifier, stuck it sideways in a first floor hallway closet and it picked up 24 channels (about 9 or 10 stations with 2-3 channels each).  This was pointing it through three walls and through a 8 acre woods that has all of the leaves still on.  I only loosely had it aimed towards the nearest towers (41 miles away) and I was picking up Louisville and a couple of Cincinnati stations (both of which are about 60 to 70 miles away) and they are in the opposite direction.  I know there are more stations at Louisville, cinci, and Indy that are within range.  I didn't have the rotator hooked up yet so I could not test it fully.  The picture was amazing.  Definately worth the $35 I spent.  My only concern is that it didn't pick up CBS, NBC, and ABC from Indy.  They are the only ones around that broadcast in VHF.  I'll have to get it hooked up fully and mounted up higher.  Great product so far.    Update 10/1/14    I finally got it mounted on top my house.  I am getting 35 stations when pointing north.  Several of these are once again, Louisville and Cincinnati stations.  I also now get the indianapolis VHF stations so it works as described.  Some of the out of line channels fade out occasionally but I could correct that by rotating the antenna.  When i did rotate it, I got an additional 10 channels from Cincinnati and about 10 extra from Louisville.  My only complaint is that there seems to be a loose connection where the coax hooks up to the antenna.  If I tighten it all the way I lose power to the antenna.  This might just be a bad cable though.

review_body:
I lucked into a pair of Series I 901s in 1974 and added a pair of Series IV some years later, at times hooked up as a 4 banger. I wore them all out and got the latest series last October. It is driven with a Harmon Kardon MK 3490 stereo receiver that does it all nicely in a 15" X 15" sitting room (no video monitor). I would love to crank these up in a barn! But at the peak volume for the space and placement considerations I have they dazzled me again and the power is more than adequate. Each of the steps taken with the advancement of their design technology has brought audible improvements. The biggest observation is the deeper and more expansive bass than previous models that is very satisfying for all kinds of music. Bose does not recommend using a subwoofer and when I tested that it really muddied up the sound and made the 901s sound even better in 'side-by-side' listening.

I have a pair of Inter Audio foot floor standing speakers that were made by the Bose Corp. as their top of the line speaker before the "direct/reflective" concepts were with us. 10" woofers, 5" mid range and twin (2) oil cooled titanium horn tweeters with 'warning lights' to warn of blow out. There is some tenor sax on John Mayal's "Jazz - Blues Fusion" album that can bring the lights up to bright orange with enough volume. They are in the bunker and great for beer and Qui and lots of loud and fun. Anyway, my point is that the production quality from Bose is remarkable and still fully functional after more than 40 years of regular use. My 'old' 901s are still great for outside and all 9 speakers are hitting it, even if softened with age. You cannot buy much in the electronic world that can hold it's value for more than 12 months. I trust Bose quality of construction as much as the technology.

$1,300 for a pair of speakers is a lot of money for me and I spend it very carefully. I just could not be happier and would do it againtomorrow. I am also pleased that I can get a room full of great music without spending another $1000 on an amplifier. The MK 3490 has a great phono pre-amp that makes my vintage Thorns TD -160 turntable come alive all over again with vinyl, old and new. It puts all the punch and all the clarity out that I can hear and richly fills my space. I have seen these retailed as high as $500 and I found a new one on Amazon for $325. I figured if it was disappointing I would start saving for a big buck unit. One year later and still loving it just about everyday. The Series I Bose would suck up 1000 watts and could take more. Bose will not give much of a recommendation for amplifiers or range of power requirements. The telephone consultant I talked to said, "Whatever sounds good to you." These are vastly more efficient than I expected and sounds great to me. I do wonder what a fancy amp 1000 watts would do!?

I think Bose and Harmon Kardon and Thorns should all send me a check or a sample 1000 watt amp for me to review.

product_title: %Original Superlux HD668B Semi-open Dynamic Stereo Professional Studio Standard Monitoring Headphones For DJ Music Detachable Audio Cable
review_headline: Audio Amazing-ness, but like a vise on my head...
review_body: This is a tough one... From an audio perspective these 'cans' produce a wonderful audio experience. They are efficient for their size, they have a nice long cord (and a short cord is included too). The cords are switchable at the small pigtail connect that hangs off one side of the ear pieces. Not a big fan of that, they would have been wiser to make the connector an "innie" instead of an "outtie". But I'm nit-picking there... This particular headphone is praised by many as a bargain, with terrific sound. I agree with all of that... Here's my issues: they are very uncomfortable (for me). In full disclosure I have a big head, no other way to say it. So my headphones need to be very adjustable. The trouble with these is that distance from the earphones themselves to the apex top center is a solid piece, completely nonadjustable.The adjustment comes from the 2 padded "antenna" looking pieces that rise up inside the outer frame. They move up and down and exert a little bit of down pressure force, very little. What causes the discomfort is the clamping force, the pressure applied to either side of my head. Combine that with the much written about sub par earphone pads and I can only take wear these 'cans' for 30 minutes before they start bothering me. For that reason only I am returning them to Amazon - fortunately I'm a Prime member! If you don't have a big squash these are wonderful headphones for you to consider and produce sound better than models 4x their price. If you do buy them, I recommend ordering a set of velor ear pads - they will transform the comfort of the headphones. In the end the trouble I had with these are my own. God blessed me with an above average-sized melon, for which these headphones don't mix well with. From an audio perspective they deserve 5 Stars.

product_title: Energy Power Bar Elite Soundbar with Wireless Subwoofer (Black Satin) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Not 5.1 -  but a decent sound for our T.V. and music.
review_body: We've had this product in our house for over a week now, and even my wife is impressed with the improved sound quality and clarity.  There are already many helpful reviews on this site, so I won't bother repeating some of the very intelligent comments about the \\"Energy Elite Soundbar c/w Wireless Sub-woofer\\" made by others.    One thing I could not find, were many comments on the optimum placement of the sub-woofer.  Correct sub-woofer placement is absolutely vital to achieving quality sound.  Moving the \\"sub\\" a few feet, or even a few inches one way or the other made a big difference.  The \\"Energy\\" user manual recommends placing this speaker in a corner.  Most experts will tell you that this position will increase the volume of the bass, but because of the nature of low frequency sound waves could reduce the clarity.  There is lots of good advice on this subject available on-line.  Just insert the words \\"sub-woofer placement\\" in your computer's search engine.    In our case, because of the room set up and size, sub-woofer placement was pretty well limited to either left, or right of the television.  After moving this speaker a few times, (left, right, forward, backward), I found the left side of the television, with the speaker pointing at the listening position, to be the best.  However, I also found I was able to marginally increase the sound quality by putting the \\"sub\\" on its end, with the control panel, (where the volume adjustment knob is), facing up.  Of course once you have it in it's optimum position, the next step is to adjust the \\"sub's\\" volume so it blends seamlessly with the higher frequency soundbar to provide a good overall fully integrated sound experience.

product_title: Koss Porta Pro On Ear Headphones with Case
review_headline: Wonderful headphones with the right adjustment
review_body: There is a reason Koss hasn't changed this design since the PortaPros initial release - they're comfortable, lightweight, and they sound great! I'll admit, I was hesitant in purchasing these - I prefer closed-back and semi-open back headphones because they do a better job of drowning out outside noises, but the PortaPros are perfect for the office, provided that it isn't too noisy of an environment. Sound quality is superb considering their size! You will be able to hear all the low bass notes, but you won't "feel" it the way you would with closed-back headphones. Highs are crisp and clear. In my opinion these sound best when the earpads are just lightly touching your ears. Here's how I put them on to get the best sound: Using your pointer fingers and thumbs, move the plastic headband adjustment sliders until there's only about 2 inches left between them at the top. Put them over your head and press on the plastic/foam temple pads until they are nice and snug. Then slide the blue ComfortZone buttons back to your desired tension - I prefer them to be as light as possible on my ears, so 2 clicks is what I use. I've found that when adjusting the headphones this way, I get a much better representation of highs, otherwise they can sound a little washed out. Hope that helps anyone who's found them to not sound as good as they expected! These are great!

product_title: Onkyo HT-S5600 7.1-Channel Home Theater Receiver/Speaker Package
review_headline: I bought a fine quality wood Home Entertainment Center
review_body:
Think hooking up all the Home Theater wiring is too complicated? It’s actually very simple. I list the procedure here. I bought a fine quality wood Home Entertainment Center. There are two bookcase end units and a center section with expanding shelves to adjust for your TV size.

When you watch a broadcast or cable show notice it says at the beginning that it is being sent in 5.1 Stereo Surround Sound? But when you buy a Blu-Ray movie the setup page let’s you watch it in 2.1, 5.1 or 7.1 Stereo Surround. That’s 2, 5 or 7 soundtracks. The movie theaters are 7 tracks.

If you are going to all the trouble to install a home theater, don’t buy the 5.1 version for TV shows, get the 7.1 version for full theater sound. During a movie you will find yourself instinctive turning your head because you hear something from a different direction. In a battle scene you are surrounded by explosion sounds. It makes you feel like you are in the movie. And 3D is even more realistic.

The Home Theater Systems come with wired or wireless (Bluetooth) speakers. The Onkyo systems that are wired have 130 watts per channel where the wireless is only 90 watts per channel. I want to hear my windows rattle when a jet flys by in a movie so I got the wired speakers. I bought an Onkyo THX 7.1 Home Theater Sound System. The “THX” certified means the sound is actually like in the movie theater.

The 7.1 is 7 surround sound speakers and 1 subwoofer. So the Onkyo came with 8 speakers. The cabinet holds 3 speakers, left front, center front and right front. The subwoofer sits on the floor by the right cabinet. I used a sturdy steel tape measure to insert under my carpet to run the other speaker wires along my side wall to the rear of the room. To the left and right sides of my couch are the center surround speakers and behind my couch are the left and right rear surround speakers. What I liked about the Onkyo is that it came with a temporary microphone that you sit in the middle of your room to automatically balance the sound levels in your room.

Here is how to wire each piece of hardware in your Home Entertainment System using my setup as an example. I have nine hardware units:

1. 3 Way Cable Splitter
2. Sony 3D 4K 55" TV
3. Sony Soundbar (Syncs to TV)
4. Sony 3D 4K Blu-Ray DVD (Syncs to TV)
5. TIVO Cable Box DVR
6. Onkyo 7.1 THX Home Theater Receiver
7. Cable Company Internet Modem
8. Cisco Wireless/Cable Router
9. XBox 360

1. 3 Way Cable Splitter
The coaxial cable in at your living room jack is either from your home antenna, cable company or satellite company. It has 4 ports. One In and Three Out.
In – from Cable Company
Out 1 – to 4K TV Cable In
Out 2 – to TIVO Cable In
Out 3 – to Internet Modem

2. Sony 3D 4K 55" TV
Cable In – from 3 Way Cable Splitter
Ethernet In – to Cisco Router port 1
Digital Optical Audio Out – to Onkyo Home Theater Receiver
HDMI 1 – to Sony Soundbar HDMI port
HDMI 2 – to XBox 360 HDMI port
HDMI 3 – to Sony DVD HDMI port #1
HDMI 4 – to TIVO HDMI port

3. Sony Soundbar (Syncs to TV)
HDMI – to Sony 4K TV HDMI 1
The Soundbar Subwoofer is Wireless

4. Sony 3D 4K Blu-Ray DVD (Syncs to TV)
Ethernet In – to Cisco Router port 2
HDMI 1 – to Sony 4K TV HDMI 3

5. TIVO Cable Box DVR
HDMI – to Sony 4K TV HDMI 4

6. Onkyo 7.1 THX Home Theater Receiver
Digital Optical Audio In – to Sony 4K TV Digital Optical Audio Out
None of the Receiver’s HDMI ports are used. The Receiver’s speaker ports are clearly labeled.
Do not use the speaker wire that came with the unit. Get a spool of 16 gauge speaker wire.

7. Cable Company Internet Modem
Coaxial Cable In – to 3 Way Cable Splitter
Ethernet Out – to Cisco Wireless/Cable Router

8. Cisco Wireless/Cable Router
Ethernet In – to Cable Internet Modem
Ethernet 1 – to Sony 4K TV
Ethernet 2 – to Sony DVD
Ethernet 3 – to XBox 360

9. XBox 360
Ethernet In – to Cisco Router port 3
HDMI – to Sony 4K TV HDMI 2

One HDMI cable replaces 5 older cables, 3 component video and 2 stereo sound. It makes hookup much simpler. Don’t forget to get a surge protector power strip for all the units.
