product_title: Brainwavz R1 Noise Isolating Earphones
review_headline: Excellent Sound Quality, Awkward Over-the-Ear Design
review_body:
(Full disclosure: I received a free product from the manufacturer in exchange for an honest review.)

This isn’t my first pair of Brainwavz headphones; along with the R1 model, I also own the Delta IEM earphones, the R3 Dual Dynamic Driver Earphones, and the S1 In Ear Headphones (which just might be my all-time favorite). Brainwavz continues to impress me with its sound quality, construction, and durability, and the R1 earphones are no exception. Whether I’m listening to music, audiobooks, or podcasts, the sound is consistently amazing: clear, rich, and detailed.

The set comes with a hard carrying case with red trim to match the details on the earphones. Inside are six sets of silicone ear tips in small, medium, and large; a set of foam tips; a set of silicone bi-flange tips; an airplane adapter; and a ¼” adapter. The 3.5mm L-Plug is compatible with a variety of devices, including iPhones and iPods.

At about 48” from earphone to L-Plug (32” of that below the Y-cable), the cord is just about the right length: not too short, not too long. The cord is round (the S1 model has a nifty flat, no-tangle cord that I *love*), but a little thicker than some of my cheaper headphones, which minimizes tangling.

The over-the-ear design is a sort of a mashup between a loose cord (such as that seen in the Delta IEM Earphones) and a rigid ear piece, with a “memory wire” that retains its shape after use. Personally I prefer a rigid ear piece; trying to adjust and readjust the wire proved a little awkward and frustrating. It took some practice before I was able to secure the earphones in place. But my husband, who has larger ears that aren’t always accommodated by fixed ear pieces, prefers the flexibility of this design. So, grain of salt.

I’ve only had this pair for a few weeks, so I can’t really speak to durability; but my other Brainwavz headphones have held up well, and they come with a one-year warranty, which is nice.ich is nice.

product_title: SainSonic SS-630 5.8GHz Wireless Audio Video Sender Transmitter + 2 Receivers TV Extender
review_headline: Under-Performs... Not confident it operates at 5.8Ghz as advertised
review_body: I'm not new to AV Wireless. I've had the X-10 2.4Ghz version for over 5 years. And I've had no issues with X-10, other than wanting more range, and less concern for interference. So that's why I was motivated to move to 5.8Ghz; less chance of interference, and more range. In fact, and in short, the SainSonic didn't outperform my X-10 setup I have....... it under-performed. This item should have been a \\"slam-dunk\\" winner, based on the advertising page in Amazon. While easy to set up, it was not an improvement to my signal quality. We use Dish for the Brazilian channel, and I can't mix/share cable signals with our cable provider's run. Splitters can both attenuate the cable signals, and could effect performance of the three services already running on that one cable. And I should mention, I shipped back this unit to Amazon today. You'll only find a couple returns in my account over the many years I've been a Prime Account Member... maybe three returns? This one frustrated me more than the others.    About unpacking the two boxes that came in yesterday.......  Right out of the box I spent a few minutes trying to figure out which of the three identical-looking units were receivers.... and which one was the \\"one and only\\" transmitter!? Seems like a pretty simple task, right? So help me, all three are absolutely identical...... except for a small \\"pad-printing mark\\" on the front cover, in the corner of each unit. Two of them, in a very small font, read \\"Receiver\\", while one read \\"Transmitter.\\" The wild-goose-chase for info didn't stop there.    I was anxious to confirm the 5.8Ghz band operation, which was the very reason I bought this set, plus the fact that I'm passing signal via \\"Component Connections.\\" And that's what this system offers for input/output. While there's mention of the \\"2.4Ghz-5.8Ghz dual band operation\\" in the manual, there was absolutely not one clear instruction or description of how the unit would shift from the lower to higher band... not one! You just need to get ready for \\"Chinese-Factory-Speak\\" in place of a clear instruction set; stupid-literal translations that make no sense.    I'm wondering if this is not a truly dedicated 5.8GHz system. While the Amazon page touts 5.8Ghz only, all of the packaging is imprinted with 2.4Ghz-5.8Ghz. With most consumer electronics I've used, that means \\"auto-switching\\" or \\"user-switchable.\\" I couldn't find anything on the units or in the instructions that specifically addressed how one would either know which frequency band the units would be in, or how to select the operating band. It keeps referring to the 4-switch/dip switch array, constantly mentioning that one must make sure all boxes share the same dip-switch positioning. That's rather obvious, right? But nothing about which positions are 2.4Ghz and which are 5.8Ghz. Again, the English used in the manual is stereotypically \\"funny\\", if part of a Seinfeld episode..... but not so much for a consumer.    While I was able to get the transmitter and receivers set up within a few minutes, (they're basically identical to my X-10 equipment), the performance in the best dip-switch position was about as good as my X-10's if they were intermittent; occasionally inviting spikes of video and audio interference. I couldn't switch my way out of that noisy condition.    To confirm whether it was the Sain...... or is that \\"InSane\\" Sonic units, or maybe a condition that was also effecting my X-10's... I disconnected the \\"InSane\\" units...... and re-connected my X-10's. With everything in the same positions, I actually got better reception from the X-10. And remember, these are 2.4Ghz, not the newer generation 5.8Ghz transceivers.    Bottom line... this appears to be a 1st generation device set, packaged to make one think it's \\"better, more powerful, and more effective\\" than any 2.4Ghz set. Well, at least for me, it wasn't. And again, this will be no more than the 4th item I've ever returned since Amazon introduced Prime. Sorry Amazon, this vendor isn't doing you, or us consumers, any favors. While I don't doubt the high rating is valid for many users, my experience with wireless AV tells me that it's no better than what I bought over 5 years ago. While their product is manufactured in China too, at least X-10 is based in Las Vegas, NV, and their website and published materials are \\"legible\\" and actually \\"useful.\\"

product_title: Eton All-Purpose Weather Alert Radio, FRX4 (Gray)
review_body:
Out of the box mine came with about three quarters internal battery charged. A good thing. The manual however is in very tiny print so best to go to the Eton’s web site -

(http://www.etoncorp.com/sites/default/files/Manual_FRX4_F_loRes.pdf)

and download the manual in PDF. Also, it’s not very intuitive or complete. Example: It tells you how to activate the ‘alarm’ but nothing is said about how to deactivate it. Not sure why anyone would want an alarm on an emergency radio anyway, but……

All of the functions claimed work well. But understand that this is a worst case scenario radio. Total power failure or on foot camping where there is no power. You can plug the radio into any USB power supply, set it outside to charge it via solar or put in some AAA batteries. There is also a crank option for charging as well.

This Eton FRX4 Hand Crank Weather Radio can provide support in the event of an emergency. We have access to AM, FM, and NOAA weather bands, plus a bright LED flashlight and USB charging capabilities.
The down side: Battery charge (internal ) is of very limited duration. After a full charge, mine was dead in 15 minutes using the radio..

If you plan to add it to an emergency kit and store it away remember that the internal battery will probably be dead when pulled out for use months later so I recommend you keep at least 6 AAA batteries with it for right-away use. (Radio takes 3 so you’ll have that times 2.)

product_title: Audio-Technica Closed-Back Dynamic Monitor Headphones with 40mm Driver - Black
review_body:
I bought a pair of these at a local brandsmart because my previous headphones had finally died, and I needed a cheap replacement to use for a few weeks before I spent money on another decent pair. I even bought some trade-in warranty which let me return them after a month, and I would get credit for them. Free headphones for a month, I thought. Here i am almost three years later and using the same pair.

The build on these things is incredible. My desk chair has gotten caught on the cable many times. I have dropped them from various heights more times than I can remember, and they have accompanied me on many road trips over the years. Yet they still feel brand new. The sound felt farther from my ear than I was used to at first.I got used to it though and the sound has been great ever since. The sound was good enough to make me not buy any other headphone. These ended up being the permanent replacements.

The only sign of wear is the padding, which has all but worn down to the fabric underneath the pseudo-leather coating. If I had to dock any points, it would be that this coating flakes away and the pieces can stick to your head sometimes. The padding has also flattened a bit since I first got them, so a good bit of outside noise leaks in now.The headband is still tight though, and the wire is still in tact. Honestly for $20 none of this even matters. These are great headphones for the price and will last years.

product_title: HDMI-High-Speed
review_headline: I always use and like BlueRigger cables but this scenario caused me a bit ...
review_body: I always use and like BlueRigger cables but this scenario caused me a bit of a headache. I am running from a macbook pro, down a mount, through a cable trough under my desk, and into an HDMI patch panel. The cable was having different results with each of my displays. One it would show up and constantly connect and disconnect, one would artifact, and the other wouldn't display at all. Added an amp in line and it didn't seem to help. After pulling the cable out and testing it on another source, it worked fine. Plugged it back into my MBP and it worked fine and thought maybe something was loose. Routed it through the cable trough and it stopped working again. In the end, I ended up routing it isolated from the rest of the peripheral cables and power (sucks when you can't use the intended wire management) and it worked fine. I suspect the issue was the shielding was not holding out the EMI/RFI interference from my extension power cable or MBP power supply. Keep this in mind when running with other cables (especially if you are using a TV on the wall and are running power next to it). I have about 6 other shorter BlueRigger HDMI cables (and a few other brands) in this setup and they aren't causing any issues. Other than that, the outside jacket is very durable and it works as intended.

product_title: Clip Plus 4 GB MP3 Player (Black)
review_body:
I have had my Sensa Clip+ for almost 3 years now and it is nearly indestructable. When I got it I only needed something simple to use, light weight, and small. The Sensa Clip+ meets all those requirements plus it sounds great. All of the other reviews cover how simple to operate it is and how good it sounds so anything I say would merely be repeating all of those great comments.

The one thing I have found is how sturdy it really is. Other than the clip breaking off I have punished this thing pretty good and it still keeps on working flawlessly. I mostly use it for listening to recorded books while walking for exercise and in my car commuting. It gets stuck in my pocket (now that the clip has broken) and gets pretty damp on long summer walks. When I commute it sits in the car all day in blazing heat during the summer and freezing temperatures during the winter and always fires up and plays perfectly when I use it. The batter life is great. I commute about 40 minutes each way and even factoring in an hour or more walking several times a week the battery charge will normally last about 2 weeks.

Just this past weekend I put it thorugh the ultimate test. I removed it from the car after a vacation trip and put it in my pocket while I unpacked the car. Later I emptied my pockets of everything but my Sensa Clip+ and put my shorts in the dirty cloths. My wife handed it to me the following day after it had been through the heavy duty wash cycle. The face plate was fogged with moisture on the inside, the micro SD card was popped out but still in the slot and it wouldn't power up. I put it on my dresser for the remainder of the day and then figured I would see if it would at least charge up. After a couple of hours of charging I hit the power button and it lit off just fine and I could cycle through some of the menu items but I couldn't get the Clip+ to select some of the functions and it would not play. So, I left it on the dresser for another day and late Sunday afternoon I gave it another try. Everything seemed to be working normally. I plugged in the earbuds and presto...I had the sound back as good as ever. Everything is working perfectly. The only thing that didn't repair itself was the clip. It is still broken and missing.

I love this little thing and is so much less expensive than my smartphone and those overpriced Apple products that I don't have to worry about getting sweat on it, dropping it, or getting caught in the rain. What more could I ask for...other than having my clip back?

product_title: Sennheiser Headphones Black
review_headline: Great sound for the money and amazing durability in extreme conditions
review_body: I found the audio quality & comfort for use in quiet spaces to be better than my earbuds costing 2x more for noisy spaces. During the past 2 summers I have worn the 239 on the Appalachian Trail totalling 50 days and averaging 8 hrs/day; about 800 hrs of soggy ear pads & presumably damp internals. I was amazed that the audio quality, cable, plug, headband and even the ear pads continued to sound/operate & look pretty much like new. A few of the tiny screws now show a bit of rust. I compared the sound quality after such \\"abuse\\" with one I just purchased for the home and as a backup. I did not hear any difference. I also compared the 239 with a HD 559 / FiiO e12 combo before buying a 239 for the home. It sounded that good (good enough) for virtually all genres of music. I wish the 239's plug was L-shaped. I used a 6-inch adapter/cable with the L to reduce the risk of breaking the iPod jack or the phone plug when hiking.

product_title: Logitech Harmony Smart Control with Smartphone
review_body: This thing is just about perfect. I only miss the customizable touch screen on the more expensive Logitech remotes every once in a while when I need to change some obscure setting on my receiver or something. Here's the biggest testament to the ease of use of this remote: I programmed it while my wife was sleeping and when she woke up the next morning she managed to figure out how to use the remote without any assistance. product_title: BATTERY APC ES500,ES550,LS500,RBC110,RBC2 12V 8.5AH
review_headline: Works Great Out Of The Box, But May Be Slightly Different Than ES 500 Battery
review_body:
I just put the replacement battery into my UPS, and I'm glad to have battery backup in place, finally! I bought my ES 500 from Goodwill for $15, and I knew there was a good chance I'd have to purchase a replacement battery for it. So now, $35 later, I have battery backup for my computer and my Xbox (when I have it hooked up in here -- I moved it recently and may move it back...)!

As I have not had it very long, I cannot say anything for its durability. As such, I have given it 4 stars. There is also one other reason for dropping a star.

When I pulled the original battery out -- it was a genuine APC battery -- I noticed that the cables for pos and neg were a bit different. The negative cable had a plastic head on it, covering the contact, and the positive cable had no cover on it -- it was just the flat hole for the battery tab with a rubber coating. On the battery, there was a cover over the actual terminal, making up for the cable difference. I'm not sure whether this was a factory setup or not. I find it odd that they would have the difference in covering the respective connections the way it was set. Here is a URL to some pictures I took of the batteries and cables:

https://www.dropbox.com/sh/t7jwvagyfxsj6zr/AAByS6ZP1x3sI2gTKDrkuBbta?dl=0

In these pictures, you can see the difference between the batteries, with the Chrome battery having no cover over the positive terminal. There is also a close-up of the cover on the original, but it's a little bit fuzzy as my camera would not focus that close to it. The third pic is of the cables, so you can see what I mean about the cover on the negative cable and the plain positive cable.

As I said above, I don't know whether the differences were factory standard or whether the previous owner did the modifications himself. As such, I don't feel comfortable giving the new battery a full rating since it may actually be different than the original in that it is missing a cover over the positive terminal. That's the sort of thing that happens when you make a generic battery to fit multiple models, I guess.

I tried out the time that it lasts right away, and the UPS didn't beep continuously for around five minutes **or so...?** with an ASUS VS229H-P, a pair of JBL Platinum Series computer speakers, and my custom Windows 8 desktop (ASUS/Corsair build; prob the most notable components being the mini-ITX mobo, GTX670 GPU, and AX650 PSU). I was watching a video on YouTube and doing some simple web surfing in the meantime.

As for some of the comments others have made on similar batteries concerning the contacts being a different size or otherwise needing modifications to work with their UPS, this particular battery needed no physical work to install aside from the installation itself. It took me about five minutes once I went and got my screwdriver.

I hope this review helps someone make a decision, whether for or against the battery! For my experience thus far, I would recommend it -- though, as I said before, I cannot speak to its lifespan.

This is my first review ever on Amazon. I don't write them because I just don't feel like putting in the time, but this is an exception.

First problem is, you have to actually assemble the bracket itself before mounting it to the wall. Annoying. It's even more annoying when they don't include the right parts. I had 3 top pieces and 1 bottom piece so no matter which way you tried to line them up, the bracket couldn't be assembled. I had an old cheetah mount bracket laying around that I never used, so instead of going through the annoying return process, I just used that one.

Second problem, they only provide 2 types of bolts for mounting the hanging arms to the back of the TV. Both of which were WAY too long even using the inadequate spacers. So, if you have a super slim TV, look elsewhere. I would have needed to stack 3 spacers behind each bolt in order for the bolt to hold the arms on. So, annoyingly, I had to make a run to home depot to pick up the bolts with the correct length. Any you need to make sure the threads are the same as the screw you have to replace.

Eventually, I got the TV mounted, and it looks good. Close to the wall and easily tilt-able. I also love the fact that they give you a 10 foot HDMI cable. But this will probably be the last time I order a mount like this. I have a more expensive mount for another TV in my house, I think from Sanus, that came with so many bolts and screws that it would honestly fit any TV without having to make an unnecessary trip to the hardware store.

I know there's a time and place for cheaper stuff, but this is last time I go this cheap on a TV mount.

review_body:
It's not too hot and not too cold. It's satisfactory (you thought I'd say it's just right, didn't you?). I received my FiiO E6 today and used it with my Android phone when out for a walk. WIth the media volume maxed on my Android phone I first put the FiiO E6 in-line with an inexpensive pair of Panasonic RPHJE120K In-Ear earbuds (not the greatest btw). Having the volume all the way up on the FiiO I would estimate a 15% increase in volume over not having the FiiO. Changing the FiiO EQ presets presented subtle differences in both volume and eq fidelity. Again, it was a pair of earbuds, so I wasn't expecting mountains to move. There was maybe a titch (I cannot define 'titch' but in my world it means very little of this or that) of distortion when turned all the way up -- distortion that is not present when plugging earbuds/headphones directly into my Android.

Then I plugged in a pair of Panasonic RP-HT21 headphones (also inexpensive, but produce a surprisingly good sound). These are what I normally prefer on my Android, but it doesn't have enough giddy up to make the headphones very loud -- which brings us to why I bought this little FiiO in the first place.

Anyhow, the volume increase from the FiiO to the RP-HT21 headphones was, again, about 15%. Adequate for my walking, but not enough if I was biking with wind whipping past me. The big difference with the headphones was the EQ presets on the FiiO. As others have said, there are four settings, and I'd say the Red (led indicator) setting was the 'warmest' with a hefty increase in bass. If you know what a 'Loudness' control on a home stereo amp does, then this Red setting is similar. It produces decent bass and warm fidelity even at low volume. The other EQ presets are either brighter sounding or flat/passive.

It charges its internal li-ion battery via the included USB cable and can be operated while charging. You'll need to charge the battery via a computer USB port, or find/purchase a USB power supply (I have numerous laying around) because one is not included.

The device casing/shell is cheap, no doubt about it. I predict the small slider switches (one for volume, the other for power/EQ) will be the first to fail or break. The whole thing feels like a cheesy toy made in Hong Kong (or China -- doh! It is.) . The transparent belt clip will most certainly snap in two with a few uses. So I would say that the FiiO is worthy, but extremely fragile.

Regarding counterfeiting (which others have cautioned), the colorful plastic display box that contained the FiiO, cables and instructions, had a little FiiO Scratch Query strip on the side of the box. It's similar to the scratch-off stuff you see on a Lottery scratch game ticket. The instructions say to scratch off the coating, reveal the hidden numbers (20 total) underneath and log-on a website (a .CN site in China) to verify the authenticity of the product. I did, and after entering the digits the site confirmed the product as being genuine.

So, 4-STARS because I like it. It is satisfactory - or just right - making my walks with some tunes more enjoyable. review_headline: Nice build quality. Not so great monitor.
review_body: I had been looking for a quality video doorbell/intercom. After much research and sifting through the various product offerings this looked to be one of the better options. What I really liked about this unit, and why I purchased it, was that the monitor intercom unit does not need to be mounted to the wall. I also very much like the built in table-stand and that it can be placed anywhere.    The negatives: The most noticeable issue is the monitor picture quality. It's nothing close to the monitor picture provided by the manufacturer. Definitely some false advertising there. Not super clear or crisp and nothing close to a smart phone picture. Additionally, the video image looks black and white. It actually is color but there is virtually so little color you may as well call it black and white. Built-in chimes are lame. They sound like a cheap toy. Lastly, the doorbell/camera needs to be at face level. At the regular door bell height you only see the person's midsection.    Conclusion: As much as I would have like to have kept this unit I'll be returning it to the retailer.

product_title: Cartridge Combo Kit
review_body:
I inherited my dad's Marantz turntable (and his record collection) when he passed away, and for some odd reason he had a Stanton RS500 cartridge on there. I know for a fact he used to have a Shure on it, but can't remember which model. So I wasn't sure how many hours use the Stanton had and was in the market for an affordable (and decent) cartridge. I came across a garage sale last year and the guy just happened to be selling an Audio-Technica PT300. Of course the guy had no idea how much use it had but to the naked eye the stylus looked like it was in good shape. It was a slight upgrade from the Stanton but wasn't as great as I was hoping for. I had a hard time finding any info on it aside from the user manual but from what I could tell it was a budget cart that had decent sound. So I decided it was time to get a new one online. After doing some research on cartridges under or around $100 I was deciding between the Audio Technica AT120ET, Shure M97xE, and the AT95E. At the time I was a little strapped for cash so I went with the AT95E, but after getting it set up on the turntable and spinning a few records I was really impressed with the sound of this thing. It's well balanced and sounds extremely clear. Although the cart has to be set up exact. I had my VTA (vertical tracking angle) too high which caused the record to skip and repeat the same groove over and over. But after getting it perfect this thing sounds incredible. The only complaint, if you could call it that, is that it's a little quieter than my other carts. I have to turn up the volume a bit more, which makes the background noise of my receiver more noticeable. But that's only when I want to crank it up. Otherwise I'm very happy with this cartridge. I might consider upgrading the stylus to the LP Gear ATN95VL when I reach 1,000 hours of listening.

Best $40 I've spent!

Then, just wrap the cover around the band and zip it up with the zipper placed on top of the band.  It is helpful to use needle nose pliers to close the zipper. product_title: 12 Tenergy 2600mAh AA 1.2V NiMH Rechargeable Batteries
review_headline: Don't throw away your dead batteries
review_body: 9/11/2014 Update.     It turns out that I was able to \\"revive\\" many of the dead batteries that my smart charger would not charge. The issue was that when the voltage of the battery gets below 0.5 volts my smart charger will not charge them. But by connecting a charged battery (+) end to the dead battery (+) end, and doing the same with the (-) ends with paper clips, I was able to \\"jolt\\" the dead battery to a level where it was recognized by the smart charger. This explains the high \\"failure\\" rate that I experienced, though this doesn't explain the rapidly diminishing capacities of the AA batteries.      ******    Original Review.    I have bought a number of Tenergy AA 2600mAh and a number of Tenergy AAA 1000mAh 4 years ago. The batteries have a teal and blue packaging. The Tenergy batteries have fared poorly. Half of my AA have died. I have tested the ones that were left over with my BC-700 Alpha Power Battery Charger, the AA batteries showed capacities of 1900mAh at the high end to 300mAh on the low end, with 1200mAh being the most common. Of the AAA I think half of them have failed as well. According to the charger the capacities of the AAA did wary from 900mAh to 500mAh, but most left over were closer to the higher end than the lower end. Ignoring the failure rate, it seems the AAA have fared better.    As a general observation, at the same size, it seems that batteries with lower advertised capacities tend to last longer. I'm not saying that AAA batteries will last longer than AA though. My energizer 2600mAh AA batteries have not fared well either.

Yamaha R Stereo Receiver
review_headline: R-S700BL Receiver> What a waste of good money.
review_body: Maybe I am missing something but this unit seems to have no power to produce quality sound. I've played with my speaker buttons and the treble and bass dials plus the Pure Direct and CD Direct Amp buttons but all I get is under-powered music. I have to listen to the stereo at an uncomfortably high level just to get any real "surround" sound, so to speak, out of the unit. At a lower volume level I get weak blunt sound quality. At a higher volume it just hurts my head and ears and still I can't hear deep bass, high treble. I just can't hear the subtle quality of my music. This unit doesn't allow me to hear the deeper qualities of my music. I guess it must be a question of the receiver's POWER but I've given the unit about a year now and I still feel the same. I don't think I can hook up an amplifier to this unit either. Also, I the unit does not have one of those plug ins in the back for me to plug my cd player into it or ANYTHING. This unit was like $500 new and I got a used unit for about $300 and still I feel as if I wasted my money. I am simply not satisfied with this unit. I have had a handful of units over my life time, first I had a Technics, then a Pioneer and then I had a Kenwood for about 15 years. I am no stranger to owning a receiver but I did find when I went to buy a new receiver that basically nobody wants to make one these days. Most of the units made these days are made for your flat screen tv, for a home theater. So I had to buy this unit sight unseen. I bought the unit because it was a Yamaha and because I wasn't happy with the basic one or two models that I would find at say Best Buy. So I spent $300 of my hard earned money to end up with something that I've been unhappy with for over a year now. I like to listen to bootleg rock audios while I am at my computer in my room. My old Kenwood receiver left me very satisfied, but it got old and we also had lightening hit the tree outside and it burned a port out in my computer, killed two ceiling fans, a tv, a vcr, and so on but the Kenwood still worked even though it began to have static in the volume knob and later other issues as well. But I could listen to the Kenwood at low volume while at my computer the sound quality was pretty good. I am using the same speakers, two Cerwin Vegas and two smaller Yamaha speakers--- one of which is a little blown. I just wish I knew how to make this unit perform the way I want it to. There is virtually no atmosphere quality to my music these days. I haven't moved my speakers. I haven't lost my hearing to any extent. There's just a lot missing in the atmospheric quality of my music these days and it has to be this Yamaha R-S700BL Natural Sound Receiver. Maybe there is something about "Natural Sound" that I am not understanding. If this is the way the music sounds naturally then I want "unnatural" sound that flows around my room and my head. I pretty much stopped listening to music when I got this unit, so that should tell you a little about how I am enjoying my new stereo receiver. I'm still hoping I can buy an amplifier or something but I don't think the unit is made to work in tandem with such an item. I never needed a stereo amplifier before. Anyway, I'm at a loss and I feel like an idiot as I try to deal with this product. It seems like the answer is to get another stereo receiver but they are very hard to find these days.

product_title: Elite Screens Manual SRM Pro Series, Premium Manual Pull Down Projection Screen
review_body:
So I've had this screen for about a month now and I've had time to notice the pros and cons.

First the pros: 1. The price is very good for what you're getting. 2. The black border helps absorb some of the light from overscanning. 3. Compared to displaying your image on a plain wall, this screen does a better job at representing true colors and images appears brighter. 4. The slow retract option is nice because you can hide the screen when not in use and the retract motion is very smooth. It is a nice alternative for those that want to save money over the electronic version. In my case, I wanted the electronic version but I do not have 120 volts running through my house and I didn't want it hooked up to a power transformer. 6. Casing feels heavy duty.

Next the cons: 1. The black border does a decent job at absorbing overscan but some light will still be noticeable. This is probably true for any screen that uses a black border so this is not a hit on this particular screen or manufacturer. 2. The waviness at the lower part of the screen is very noticeable on mine as it has been for several other customers. It actually doesn't bother me unless I'm sitting near the 160 degree angle where you start seeing shadow effects caused by the waves. From a normal viewing angle, it's only noticeable if there is scrolling text near the bottom. 3. The slow release motion is louder than I expected. If you look at any of the product videos that show this motion, the screen retracts very quietly, in fact, silently. That is not the case in real life application. My 4 year old laughs every time he hears it and he sometimes will retract it himself just to hear the noise. It's like a loud high-pitched fart sound that lasts for about 5 seconds as it retracts. 4. The screen material is made of fiberglass which should make it very durable. Unfortunately, the edges of my screen are already starting to fray in some areas. Hopefully the fraying will not get out of control. 5. Lastly, and most crucial, I can see very obvious vertical lines on my projected image that are more noticeable in lighter scenes. At first I thought it was my projector but the lines were not present when projecting onto a wall. Additionally, placing a plain white sheet of paper in front of the screen made the vertical lines disappear while the uncovered part of the screen was still showing them. This is annoying and I'm hoping that I can get used to it very fast. This is visible from any angle but if you're sitting off-angle it will be more noticeable on the side of the screen that is closest to you.

product_title: Beats By Dr.dre/monster Urbeats In-ear Headphones for HTC (White)
review_body:
The GOOD: sound quality exceptional. comes with a variety of earbuds for comfort fit and ambient noise reduction--everyone's ears are different so choose a buds that give the seal you want. yes, you will get strong base and crisp highs. Using these an average of 3 hours a day for the last 4 months hasn't affected the sound quality. Sun and heat haven't harden or damaged the cords, unlike the cheaper earphones I've used.
The MARGINAL:
1. Tangles in the cord. the cord is NOT flat [the previous pair of monster beats I bought in 2009 cost ~2x as much+ the cord was flat like fettuccine and DID NOT tangle insanely.] The cord here is spaghetti shaped; saying it tangles is understatement. It'll create granny knots on the earbud ends just from setting it down. The rest of the cord creates knot you couldn't tie on purpose. Partial Solution: google lifehacker cord tangle and use the butterfly technique for cord wrapping. Another Solution: cord wrapping container sold on amazon--too bulky for me to carry though.
2. The in-line control [with previous and next ] ONLY works with HTC devices. It's useless and heavy on my mp3 player. it will work on your iphone.

Back To The Tangles: of the hundreds of cables in our house: everything from iphone chargers to knitting yarns- I've never had anything tangle as this does. Perhaps it's the thick cylindrical cord shape+rubbery material storing potential energy as it's unintentionally twisted during use. Simply gathering it into my pocket or setting it on the counter will result in a knotted mess. allowing the mp3 player to dangle freely from the end of the cord after use should release the potential energy that's twisted into the cord~~still I've got tangles later.

product_title: JBL Integrated Home Audio System with Portable Wireless Speaker (Black)
review_headline: Great Bluetooth speaker, but very high price
review_body:
I own several JBL speakers, including 3 of the [[ASIN:B000BQ57BU JBL On Tour Portable Speaker System ( Black )]], which I bought in 2007 (when they were $50 each - the current price is outrageous), and the [[ASIN:B000O7N4IE JBL CS480 5.1 Channel Home Theater Speaker System (Black)]], which has been going strong since 2008, and a [[ASIN:B0096T7U04 JBL Micro II Ultra-Portable Multimedia Speaker (White)]], which I've had since 2013. They're all great speakers, and have never given me any problems, so I have an affinity for JBL audio products, and this new Voyager Bluetooth speaker lives up to my expectations.

When both pieces are together, with the center/portable speaker attached magnetically (I think), the full sound is extraordinary. With the center \\"puck\\" released, it doesn't have nearly the same 'oomph', but that's expected, since you're disengaging the larger speaker/subwoofer. However, it does sound quite good in comparison to other portable Bluetooth speakers of similar size & specs.

The battery life of the puck is pretty good, yielding about 4 hours of play time, and when the puck is reattached, there's a nice set of small lights indicating the charge level.

It looks great, it sounds great, and I'm now using it as my main Bluetooth speaker in my kitchen, replacing another great speaker, the [[ASIN:B00EWEHIE6 Boston Acoustics MC100 Wireless Bluetooth Speaker System]]. However, the price is quite a bit higher than I'd be comfortable spending on it. To me, a reasonable price would be 175 or so. But good luck finding it at any price other than 249 - I did a quick search, and every seller had it available at the exact same price; maybe the price is fixed by JBL..?

I was looking for a cheap mount to mount my gf's new TV. Usually you can't find cheap and durable in the same mount but this one seems to be the best of both worlds. The thing is ridiculously easy to install. Follow the instructions and you wont have any issues. Find a stud, get the thing somewhat level, drill pilot holes for your lag bolts, put your lag bolts in and done.

I like that I don't have to get the mount perfectly level. From past experiences I will level the wall mount base but then the arms have too much compliance and allow some twisting or offsetting resulting in a crooked TV. With this one you could mount it 3-4° off center but the mount allows TV to spin 5°+ to compensate for mistakes or manufacturing tolerances.

The sheer number of mounting combinations it provides is awesome. My TV ended up being a weird 200 x 150 mount but it still had all the holes in the right places to mount it. I did have to use the washers to keep the screws from going through the holes but it is mounted very solid.

The TV mounting part is removable so you can pull your TV off without have to completely remove the mount. Two Phillips head screws and the mount comes off. It is designed so the top fits in a slot so the TV can't just fall off the mount after undoing the screws, you have to lift it up then out to get it off.

I noticed some people complained about it being hard to move around, you can either lubricate it or just loosen the bolts/nuts like 1/6 turn or so. All the tools to do this are provided in the box. I did have to fiddle with the bolts a little to get them to the right friction point.

The mount extends long enough that you should be able to go up to 40" and swivel 90° left or right. The tilt adjustment knobs might get in the way if they bottom out and the handle is sticking straight back but even then there should be enough space because of how far it sits off the wall, if it does then just tighten it more or readjust the tilt a little.

This mount has such a small foot print it really is a compact mount. It only needs one stud to mount to so you don't have some giant 16" plate attached to the wall like usual. Overall great mount and I will probably end up buying a few more.t more or readjust the tilt a little.

product_title: Tenergy ARC5200 External Battery Pack Portable Phone Charger 5200mAh Power Bank Battery Back-Up - Built-In Lightning Cable and Micro USB Cable #51064
review_headline: Takes over 7 hours to recharge fully from empty
review_body:
I can't give it a more accurate rating until I know what price it is selling for. As it is right now, I'd say "It's OK".

It works flawlessly, if a little inconvenient. Most power banks I own start supplying power when it is plugged in. For this one to start charging, you need to first press the power button. It does turn off automatically after about 10 seconds or so. If you quickly disconnect one device and connect another one, it will continue charging.

It has one Lightning connector and one micro USB cable. Unfortunately, you cannot connect your own cable to it, so if you have two iPhone or two devices that uses micro USB, you're out of luck. iPhone owners might be able to use a micro USB to Lightning adapter to charge two iPhones at the same time. And obviously, only devices with the Lightning connector (iPhone 5 and later) can use this.

The shape makes it easy to hold, though it is fairly large for its capacity. I did not open it up, but it looks like about the correct size for 2 18650 batteries, 2600 mAH each. It's slightly curved to make holding it easy. A bit too big for pants pocket, unless you wear fairly baggy pants.

It managed to recharge my phone (Galaxy Nexus, 1750 mAH battery) almost 2 times from empty, which is about what I'd expect for a power bank of this capacity. It takes a mind boggling 7+ hours to recharge from empty. There are 3 LEDs that indicate the state of charge - 1/3, 2/3 and full respectively. If it is empty, it will show one blinking LED. When charging, the top most LED will be blinking. I let it charge until the top LED stopped blinking. I was using a 2.1 amp charger as well, so it wasn't for lack of current. From calculations, that means it recharge at around 0.3C, which is nice for the battery's longevity - unless you're in a hurry. The power bank is rated for 500 cycles (again, about what is expected for 18650 batteries).

In summary : It works well, slightly inconvenient, built in cables, and takes a long time to recharge. Get this if the price is right, and if you need to charge a device with a Lightning connector and a micro USB connector at the same time - and if the price is good. Otherwise, you may want to find another charger.

product_title: Emotiva UPA-500 Five-Channel Power Amplifier
review_headline: Emotiva rocks - A perfect upgrade for Home Theater
review_body:
The upgrade bug hit me and I am glad I took the hit. I own a Sony Elite DA2400 ES receiver which has been a great performer so far. I have been waiting to get into the world of separates for a while and thought I will start with the amp first. I own a simple set up for HT with Bose 301s taking Front L/R and the center anchored by the venerable Def Tech Procenter 1000. The rears are in ceiling speakers. Polk RC60i and subwoofer a Polk PSW505. So far the sound has been great, but once I installed the Emotiva UPA 500 and powered all speakers through it the upgrade was immense. Everything sounds much more clear even at lower volume levels.

Set up guide
I researched a lot of forums on how to set up an external amp with your AV receiver and did not find information anywhere to let me know how to go about it. As a bit of an experienced audio nut I decided to take the plunge and figure it out myself. The following things are needed when connecting a power amplifier to an AV receiver instead of a Home theater pre like Marantz AV7701.

A lot of forums told me that i would need to gain match amps to receiver pre outs. That is partially true. A lot of AV receivers do not put out rated 2Vrms on their pre-out when their volume is raised all the way up. This is needed for some of the expensive amplifiers such as Bryston, Classe etc. The advantage with this particular amplifier model is it hits the maximum output level for getting the 80 watts not at 2V but at 850mV which most receivers under 1.5$ will hit. Instead of spending on a very expensive pre and amp set up, if your HT resides in a rooms which are around 3000-5000 cuft of space... go for this amp. I can guarantee you that you will hit the THX rated levels of 105db easily in your listening area provided you have efficient speakers and a decent enough subwoofer. I actually measured peak levels around 100dB/8feet playing the Lord of the Rings battle Scene. If you look up noise levels you will see thatat 100dB you will lose your hearing pretty quickly if its sustained. I needed ear plugs as it was insanely loud.

1. Make sure that your existing AV receiver has pre outs for all channels that you would like to amplify. these can be unbalanced (RCA connectors) or balanced (XLR). I am guessing if it any AV receiver within 1500$ its gonna have unbalanced connectors.
2. Use RCA connectors to hook up AV receiver pre outs to amplifier inputs for the specific channels.
3. Remove connections from the speaker outputs on receiver and plug them into the outputs of the amplifier.
4. If your AV receiver comes with an auto calibration software, hook up your mike and do the auto cal like you would normally. Once the levels have been set up tweak them for finer adjustments on your receiver.
5. You will control the volume level directly through the AV receiver.

Listening tests

Diana Krall, Norah jones and other Jazz artists - the performance sounded deliciously sweet, my Bose 301 speakers sound like they just got opened up a notch. if you really want to get the full performance from these speakers or any other mid range priced speaker i suggest you upgrade your amplifier first.The volume levels are also pretty apparently higher. Example, if previously I needed to listen to background music, I needed around -20dB on the AVR, i need to be only at -25 to -30dB with this amp to get clean and clear sound.

If this little amplifier can sound so good and loud at the same time, most folks are mad for setting up 200W/channel amplifiers in their home. 5-stars to Emotiva for this gem. A definite buy if you are looking to step your home theater/listening experience.

review_body: Great receiver with all the features you would expect from a 2014 receiver (8X HDMI 2.0 inputs/1X out, wireless connectivity, iOS/Android app, 4K upconvert, etc)!  Small foot print and light weight make it a perfect fit for my living room theatre system.  Was a bit nervous about the 50W per channel but haven't once noticed it as being a problem.    Couple issues are keeping it from 5 stars:  1) Receiver has frozen 3 times in the 1 month I've owned it.  Had to unplug it to get to reset.  2/3 times it reset all my settings and I had to reconfigure.  Will be calling Marantz in the near future to resolve the issue.  Will update with Marantz's response.  2) Won't stay connected to my wireless network.  I have to reconnect almost every time use the iOS app or stream music from my phone/computer (works perfect when connected).    Wireless connectivity issue is a minor issue but the freezing issue is quote annoying especially when it erases my settings.  If freezing issue can be resolved (through firmware update or otherwise) I will change my rating to 5 stars and strongly recommend to friends and family they follow suit in the purchase of this receiver.    8Sep14 Update:  Unit continues to freeze.  Hard reset as directed by Marantz had not impact on the issue.  Will be calling Marantz back.  Downgrading my rating to 2 stars until freezing issue is resolved.    27Oct13 Update: After contacting Marantz a second time, they have offered repair at a service center or replacement with a b-stock unit.  Not sure which option I will choose, if any.  Since installing the latest firmware update (~2 weeks ago), I've not had either the freezing nor the network connectivity issue as originally reported <knocks on wood>.  Upgrading rating based on positive customer service and success with recent firmware update.

product_title: ARCTIC P31X Variation US
review_body:
Much like it's close brother the [[ASIN:B008EOXXFI ARCTIC P311 Bluetooth Stereo Headphones]], the [[ASIN:B0064LCL74 ARCTIC P31X Pack Bluetooth Stereo Headphones and UD2 Bluetooth Adapter Set]] offer multi-use function for on the go and in the home with the included USB Bluetooth adapter.

One important consideration to consider before buying these headphones is that they are Bluetooth wireless only. They can pair with the included adapter, or with most other Bluetooth devices (Tablets, MP3 Players, Etc.). Why this is important to point out is that sometimes, wireless headphones have the option to `alternatively' connect to non-Bluetooth devices with a removable 3.5mm cable. However, that option is not available on this particular pair of headphones. With that said though, they actually perform very well over Bluetooth and that is what they are designed solely to do.

In the box you will find: the ARCTIC P311 Bluetooth Stereo Headphones, A USB Bluetooth dongle, a hard shell carrying/storage case, a Mini USB recharging cable, and an instruction sheet with a drivers mini-CD for the USB adapter. The headphones, designed to be out of the way but ultimately functional, look very nice, and are designed as one size fits most. The soft cushion comfort pads on the headphones give them a great fit and make them quite comfortable for extended wear. While wearing them on a walk around the park this afternoon and for the last week, I almost forgot they were even on my head. All the controls you need to interact with your music are located on one single side, great for keeping on demand control over your playback/calls.

I want to note, I have found that these headphones are capable of adding considerable volume over that of the original devices' `top volume', so this is a really cool feature for those who like their music louder. The sound quality from these headphones is nice and certainly above par. Bass is actually quite respectable, could be a bit deeper, however the overall quality is very reasonable in consideration of the selling price.

Overall, the [[ASIN:B0064LCL74 ARCTIC P31X Pack Bluetooth Stereo Headphones and UD2 Bluetooth Adapter Set]] perform very well for music playback and phone calls. Bluetooth pairing was easy on my Android phone and on my Nexus 7 tablet. Driver install for the USB adapter wasn't too bad and connection seems to going well so far. What I like so much about the headset is they are really lightweight and perform better than expected.

It works as advertised, learning codes, programming, etc. It doesn't have a USB connection or any other way to program in codes so if you've lost a remote and this URC doesn't happen to have the code that you need, you're out of luck. From what I read, a One For All remote can be plugged into a computer so you can download codes even if they aren't built-in and you don't have the remote. I considered the One For All but I didn't like how secretive they seemed about the codes. Logitech harmony with USB programmings seems like it would have been the best, but it also costs far more.

The shape isn't wonderful: I would have preferred a peanut shape. Also, the buttons don't have a nice click to them, they just feel soft and springy, so I often think that I pressed one in when really it didn't register.

I thought that the light would be more useful but it only turns on when you press the light button, not automatic like a One For All remote, so it's less useful.

This remote works but could have been better. They need to take some design cues from One For All.

product_title: Ultra-High Performance 5 Ports HDMI Amplifier Switcher Support 3D 3 4
review_headline: Does the job, but autoswitch nonfunctional and random blank picture is maddening!
review_body:
This is the only HDMI switcher I have ever owned, so I have nothing to compare it to.
- Metal housing is built to last! No vent holes though, and it gets pretty warm...I put 1/2" spacer blocks under mine.
- Compact & lightweight. Small footprint nice, but cables will pull it around...may need Velcro/tape to hold it where you want it.
- Blue "channel" LEDs irritatingly bright. Labels unreadable at ~2ft/dark. Illuminated number panel "cutouts" would solve.
- "Intelligent" automatic switching has never worked...manual only. Remote works pretty well, but not lighted.
- Picture quality seems fine. My receiver is not HDMI, so can't speak for audio quality.
- Significant lag (blank screen) when switching. Some claim this is common to HDMI technology, not particular to this switch.
- No mfg info in "Chinese-English" manual. Product not identified. Online search revealed Portta model PET0501.
- Picture randomly blanks out (black screen). Frequency & duration increase the longer unit is on. Occurs on both my sources, but frequently on Blu-ray and rarely on Cable box. Heat? Source Device? HDMI format? I don't know --- my BIGGEST complaint.

product_title: SkipDr DVD and CD Manual Disc Repair System
review_body: I literally just got this a few minutes ago and opened the box, and figured I'd try it out to quiet my kid down- I had two Wii games that were scratched a bit.  They wouldn't play; kept giving error message that the disc was unreadable.  At first I was annoyed, I couldn't find the piece of blue cloth and white felt in any of the packaging.  Then as I was repacking it into the box, I found them shoved into the handle piece.  So look around if you don't find it.  The directions are easy to read and understand fortunately (I'm one of those that usually doesn't mess with directions) with pictures too thankfully because I could not figure out how to put the disc into the thing until I looked at the picture....anyway, sprayed the alcohol/water mix on it, popped it in.  Cranked it around the two times it recommended.  Dried it off with the blue cloth, and then buffed it a bit with the white felt thingy.  Had my kid try it out, and voila....both worked and were playable.  The thing doesn't look like much, it's plastic.  But, it did work.  I wonder if those with the poor reviews maybe didn't follow the directions?  It states clearly the disc must be kept wet with the alcohol mix.  Or, if the scratches are that bad/deep, it may not be repairable.  The first review posted is very detailed in how the whole thing works and is very informative.  Once you understand the concept of what it's doing it makes sense.  The only complaint I have with this, and why it's not 5 stars, the handle to crank the thing is detachable, which is fine-I assume for storage and shipping.  It's easy to snap on, but it snaps off too easily while trying to crank it, at least mine is.  I just have to stop every few cranks and make sure it's still secured, and have it on the edge of my desk while I'm cranking it.  Otherwise, $16. investment to save not having to buy new games/movies.  Very happy with it so far.

review_headline: Great sounding headphones with some nice features
review_body:
I've had these headphones for a little over a week now, and am very happy with them overall. The reason I am giving them 4 stars rather than 5 is twofold:

1.) I have yet to be able to access the advanced menu options. The menu says I should press the power and multi-function button to get to this menu, but that doesn't appear to do anything. Maybe this is simply user error. I am pressing the two buttons simultaneously and holding them, waiting for an audio queue. If someone can explain what I'm doing incorrectly, I'll be happy to revisit this review. But perhaps the instructions should be more clear.

2.) Occasionally, the bluetooth connection just drops inexplicably, leaving my tablet blaring through its internal speakers. I've had this happen at work a couple of times and it's embarrassing to say the least.

Other than these couple of things, they are terrific headphones. The pairing process couldn't be easier, and the controls are easy to use while wearing them. One nitpicky thing: pressing the multifunction button twice to skip to the next song and three times to go back isn't exactly intuitive, but it works well enough in practice. The bottom line for me is that the Tracks Air headphones sound great. The dynamic range is good, and you can even get the bass thumping if that's what you like.

UPDATE 7/25/2014: As a commenter pointed out, in order to get to the advanced menu, the headphones must first be off. Then press the power and multi-function buttons simultaneously. The headphones will power up and provide voice prompts for advanced menu options. I still maintain it should spell this out more clearly in the instruction manual.

product_title: TEAC CD-P1260 CD Player with LCD and MP3 Playback
review_body:
For people in a hurry: I've had this TEAC CD-P1260 CD player for about 7 months, listening to it almost every day (or several hours a week), it sounds great and has worked flawlessly. The built-in headphone jack/amplifier works well. I am very pleased with the quality.

This TEAC P1260 is a basic CD player, meant to be installed as part of a stereo system for listening to music over speakers, though it's possible to use it all by itself by plugging headphones into the jack on the front. This player plays only commercial audio CDs, CD-R/RW copies of commercial CDs, and CD-R/RW discs with mp3 files. It will NOT play .wav files or anything else, and the manual says it may not play variable bit-rate mp3 files. I don't listen to mp3s because they sound crappy, so I can't confirm that. But a friend gave me a disc with .wav music files, and this TEAC CD player would not play it. Every other CD player in the house would, including an inexpensive boom box, so be aware that this P1260 is limited mainly to commercial audio CDs and copies of such CDs. I think that's what most people would use a CD player for anyway.

This is a quality item. It feels heavier to me than the 20-year-old CD players I own. The opening and closing of the drawer is quiet and dignified. The finish of the metal case is a matte black that doesn't look cheap. The display consists of white alphanumeric characters on a very soothing medium blue background. The buttons used for basic operation are arranged logically from left to right: open (close), play (pause), stop, skip back, skip forward. The labeling of the buttons is somewhat hard to see in dim light, a common problem with modern stereo equipment. There is another horizontal row of smaller buttons below the above for shuffle, repeat, program, and intro check (plays the first 10 seconds of each track) functions. I never used any of these functions. I also never used the remote, but I did note that the buttons are well spaced and also logically arranged. On the back are the tin-plated left and right RCA jacks for connecting the P1260 to an amplifier or stereo receiver; the necessary cable is included (about 1 meter long).

An outstanding feature of this low-priced CD player is the built-in headphone jack and amplifier with volume control. The jack is the large, 1/4 inch type, which means most headphones will require an adapter (decent headphones come with an adapter). Many audiophiles claim that a separate headphone amp is necessary for good listening, but I thought this built-in amp sounded just fine. It has enough power for even the most inefficient headphones in my collection. If the P1260 is connected to an amplifier, plugging headphones into the front jack will disconnect the RCA output jacks on the back.

The specifications given in the manual claim 8X oversampling, if you're interested, and the frequency response is 20-20kHz, within 2 dB. The frequency response could be a little tighter, but then it would cost a lot more.

Some credible reviews of this TEAC CD player have indicated reliability problems. As I said at the beginning, I have had mine for 7 months now, using it as much as most people would, maybe more, and I haven't had any problems (knock on wood!). In my experience, TEAC has always made quality audio equipment, so I really didn't expect to have problems. Maybe I have just been lucky so far. All I can report is my personal experience, which has been totally satisfactory. It sounds great, works great, looks great, and has the feel of a quality piece of audio equipment. I think it is a great buy for anyone looking for a no-frills, basic CD player.

product_title: Asgard 2 Headphone Amplifier
review_headline: This Schiit Is Transcendent...Even Sourced From An iPod
review_body:
Like all the other reviews posted, I'm BLOWN AWAY by how great the Asgard 2 makes my music sound. Like others have said, I feel like I have to go back and re-listen to my entire music collection.

But I don't like to post reviews if they merely repeat what others have said, so I wanted to write this from a complete newbie's perspective. Also, no one had discussed using an iPod as their music source yet, and since I'm doing that, I thought I'd comment.

So my \\"system\\" is basically a pair of wonderful Sennheiser 650HDs and an iPod. For YEARS I've ignored all the reviewers and audiophiles out there saying that the Senns have to be powered by a headphone amplifier because, frankly, they already sounded WONDERFUL. About two years ago, I broke down and bought a Headroom Total Airhead portable amp which did basically NOTHING to improve the sound quality of the very hungry Sennheisers.

So I took the plunge and picked up the Asgard 2. Schiit is a great company and they make great products. To their credit and my frustration, they won't answer questions about \\"if it's worth it\\" or speculate about \\"what I'll hear.\\" In fact, their policies regarding these questions are listed on their website. I asked the sales representative via email if sourcing the music from an iPod will negate the quality of the amp. In ONE MINUTE he wrote me back but said that he couldn't comment, as per their policies, on questions regarding \\"whether it's worth it.\\" I had other audiophile friends tell me that I needed to get a DAC in addition to the amp. A DAC is a system which transfers digital music to analog form, which tends to sound much richer and more textured. I decided to hold off on the DAC, especially since you use many of them with a laptop rather than an iPod. Plus, I was told that IPods do come equipped with a primitive but pretty functional DAC already built in. Not sure either way. But here's what I do know.

I ran my iPod through a RCA stereo to dual cable into the Asgard 2 and then connected the Sennheisers to the front. The sound was TRANSCENDENT. I've been listening all this time to my Sennheiser 650s without REALLY listening to them. In talking to my wife, I compared it to owning a Ferrari and driving it only to the grocery store on main roads. It's still very nice, it's still very fast, but that's not what a Ferrari was MEANT to do and the Asgard 2 has freed my Sennheisers to really take off. It's not just an issue of volume either. Though I'm familiar with some audiophile-ese, I'm not even sure what some of it means and I really never find too helpful. So I'll just say this: music, of all kinds (death metal through classical, jazz through indie rock) sounds INCREDIBLY rich, DEEP, and full. Yes, I hear things in songs I've never heard before, but more than that, the entire soundstage just seems immense. There is music, tone, texture, and detail coming from everywhere, and best of all, it's not overwhelming or exhausting.

I absolutely recommend the Asgard 2 to anyone considering taking the plunge into more serious audio equipment.

product_title: Polaroid Premium VIP Passive 3D Glasses
review_headline: Probably the best 3D glasses I've worn yet.
review_body:
First off, the all-plastic construction is about as good as you can expect from a similarly priced pair of sunglasses. The lenses are probably the best I've seen on 3D glasses; very little distortion at all is visible. These come in a hardshell case with a microfiber cleaning cloth. Due to the curvature of the lenses, these will not fit over eyeglasses. if you wear eyeglasses, I recommend you either opt for contacts, or get a pair of 3D clip-ons, of which there is a good selection on Amazon.

I've had the opportunity to use these a couple times now. The first thing you'll notice is the extremely wide field of view you have with these. The frame is not an issue, and doesn't get in the way of the movie, even if you sit in the first row at the theater. The fit is comfortable and the frames, and lenses, wrap around the sides of your face, staying out of the way. The lens frames are tall as well, with the top resting above your eyebrows while the bottom is lower, about level with the bottom of your nose. You can freely rest your head back without the frames ever getting in the way.

Unlike the cheap glasses you get at a theater, these do not hurt your nose, as the nose pad area actually does the job. No more soreness on the bridge of your nose.

Since these are more curved than regular glasses, they will not fold up and fit in a pocket very well. In fact, it's actually easy to damage the lenses by folding the arms too close. The lenses, like pretty much all other RealD compatible glasses, are thin polarized film, and thus, are flexible and need to be handled with care, hence the hard case for these.

review_body:
I've been dealing with this situation since 2008. My first harmony remote was the Xbox 360 branded version up until some of the buttons failed years later. Innovative but unreliable hardware up until now. My friend's 890 had failed buttons, my harmony 1000 had sticky buttons (not physically, software keeps repeating codes). I was worried this was gonna be like the failed Logitech iPad link but was truly mistaken. For the value, it does WAYY better than those expensive home automation remotes.

My needs were no line of sight, reliable, & easy to use, ALL of which were met. To this day I still can't understand how my family can't operate a basic remote by pointing so it needed RF. The great thing is that you can just leave it sitting out and it is POWERFUL enough to shoot the strongest IR signal anywhere & connect to wifi. Fun & easy setup with any (modern) smartphone or computer. For more advanced users, it even lets you hook up IR emitters on the back, horray. Now you can HIDE those UGLY boxes & wires while still having awesome sound & keeping it EASY to use.

Performance & Reliability:
The most important, this thing has a VERY good distance. I had trouble with my TV turning on but that's the TV problem. I easily attached an IR emitter to solve the problem. INSTANT on & off, much faster than the older harmony remotes. The smartphone app does a lot & I mean A LOT. I'll admit the smartphone app is a little slow & buggy but I think that's because I'm far from the wifi. What's important is that my grandma can use the remote now. Did I forget the remote? BEST remote ever & geniuses for using the hub instead of the remote. No more battery or range issues. The remote is small, easy to use, nice feedback. This isn't just the best harmony remote. This is the BEST & greatest value universal remote PERIOD!!

product_title: Pioneer SP-FS52-LR Andrew Jones Designed Floor standing Loudspeaker (each)
review_headline: Alright I'll say it at this price point there is NOTHING better.
review_body:
Alright I'll say it at this price point there is NOTHING better. I've been looking for budget speakers to get into the home theatre world for a while. I'm a college student, though I appreciate the amazing sound quality you can get from one of the Klipsch Reference speakers, I can't afford them. I first picked up a pair of Energy CB-10 bookshelf's (less than these on amazon for a pair) and I was appalled. I hated them and I tried various different setups with different receivers and subs and never found a good balance.

Eventually I picked up these and right out of the box they blew me away, like I said earlier they are great for their price point. These wont blow away speakers that cost 2-3 times as much but they will not leave you thinking about buying anything else at this price point.

They give you very clear mids and lows. Only thing I could complain about is the highs aren't as crisp as what you would find from Klipsch. But that is personal preference. Always take speakers home and try them out to see if you like them. I will also note that even though these sound great out of the box give them a week or two of solid listening and they will sound better. This is the so called break in period and I believe they apply to these speakers as well. If you have the budget to spend twice as much I would highly recommend the Klipsch RF-42 II they sell for 239 each at fry's, if not look no further!

Also keep in mind these go on sale often! usually for 100 each on amazon. And apart from the subwoofer that comes from pioneer the other components that supplement these are also amazing value.

product_title: Symphonized NRG Premium Genuine Wood In-ear Noise-isolating Headphones|Earbuds|Earphones with Microphone
review_headline: These are an amazing pair of headphones
review_body:
***UPDATE 2/19/2015***
After about five months of regular use, the left earbud blew out. I e-mailed the company about the issue and they sent me a new unit in less than a week. I've noticed that this new pair of headphones makes less noise when brushed and the headphone jack is sturdier and built better. The audio quality is still amazing. Overall, I'm very satisfied with Symphonized's customer service.

***ORIGINAL REVIEW***
I don't typically write reviews (in fact, this is the first Amazon review I've ever written), but after using the Symphonized NRG headphones I felt compelled to type this up. Before I go in depth, I'd like to point out that I'm no audiophile, but I like to think that I've owned enough pairs of headphones in the past to provide an accurate review of the Symphonized NRG for the casual music listener.

First of all, I just want to say that I am absolutely satisfied with these headphones. The sound quality is spectacular, especially for the price; these headphones can easily hold up against top tier competitors that are quadruple its price. Whether the wooden build provides any real advantage or not, the audio is very clear and crisp and the bass is boomy, yet not too powerful. I listen to all sorts of genres, from rock to pop to rap to country, and these headphones made me feel like I was rediscovering each of my favorite songs. The noise-isolating feature works fairly well - definitely way better than the typical low-price headphones marketed as \\"noise isolating.\\" If you're wondering how the microphone fares, I can't comment on that because I haven't used it yet.

There are still a few drawbacks to the Symphonized NRG. The nylon cable was a bit thinner than I expected, but it still feels reliable and durable. However, the cable does make some noise when it is brushed up against a surface, which I found to be slightly annoying. I also wish the button had volume control on it.

Overall, the Symphonized NRG gives you quality, top-tier sound for a very low price. I would recommend these earphones to anyone who listens to music daily.

PROS:
+ Amazing sound quality
+ Great price
+ Noise-isolation works well
+ Sturdy nylon cable
+ Cool aesthetics
+ Lightweight
+ Fits comfortably in the ear

CONS:
- Cable makes some noise when brushed
- Microphone button lacks volume control

product_title: Mediasonic Homeworx HW110AN Super Thin Indoor HDTV Antenna - 25 Miles Range
review_headline: Make sure your TV setup is correct!
review_body:
After an hour of fooling around, I thought it didn't work. Turns out, I didn't know what I was doing. On my TV (a 2008 Panasonic Plasma, yes it has a built in tuner, as most/all TVs after 2007 do) and probably yours, you may not be able to just plug it in and go. Here are two things I had to be sure to do (you should be able to do these things somewhere under your TV's menu and setup function):

1) Make sure your TV is set to "Antenna." It may be set to "Cable" by default. On my TV, this is under SETUP and PROGRAM CHANNEL. Yours may be different.

2) This may seem stupid, but be sure you're actually clicking on some sort of SURF or SURF MODE under setup. I looked up the number of my local channels and surfed them manually, and nothing came up. When I hit SURF MODE, the TV surfed through on it's own and found 19 channels.

This thing just sits right behind my TV, and the picture is perfect.

product_title: Sony BDVN790W Blu-ray Home Theater System (2013 Model)
review_headline: great quality home theater system, but poor usability in the interface
review_body:
This is a difficult review to write because there are two aspects to this home theater system system - equipment quality (engineering) and usability (user experience). In a nutshell: this product is very well engineered for the price, but has poor usability. More details below.

Engineering review (5 stars) - These are well made wired/wireless speakers with nice range, surprisingly good volume levels, and a decent sub-woofer. Setup is a joy with color coded wires and self tuning levels to adapt to your space. It looks great and the wireless rear speakers remove the clutter of wires from your entertainment space without compromising sound quality. The side loading Blu-Ray can be a little tricky on a tight shelf and the LCD is hard to read unless you are near (and slightly above) the device, but these are minor issues in an otherwise solid system. Nice job, Sony!

User Experience review (2 stars) - The user interface was clearly designed by engineers. For example, you are not allowed to relabel inputs into usable terms like \\"Xbox\\" or \\"TV\\", but instead are forced to select from non-descriptive names like \\"HDMI 1\\" or HDMI 2\\". Even good ideas, like the dedicated Netflix button on the remote, are badly implemented. When you hit the button, the device will report a 3-step process where it is going to connect to something called \\"The Internet\\" and attempt to access something called \\"Content\\". Once these 3 steps are done, the device waits for you click an acknowledgement that it has completed this process instead of just launching Netflix without additional intervention required. Whose idea was that? Lots of other examples abound. If you have a somewhat non-technical person who will be using this system and you need to switch between devices with any frequency, they might struggle. Bad job, Sony!

Overall, this is a good system for the price and perhaps Sony might fix the user experience shortcomings with a software fix?

product_title: Bose QuietComfort 15 Acoustic Noise Cancelling Headphones (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: So good they made me jump on a flight, and ignore my boss calling me.
review_body:
I have owned my pair of QC15's for about 2 and a half years now. I use them daily in the office, and on flights between Australia and the UK.

Construction:
Initially I was surprised by the plastic materials of a $300 pair of headphones. After lots of use, I am very comfortable with them. They are not light weight, but are astonishingly comfortable.

Comfort:
Holy sleeping airline passengers Batman! I have worn those nasty on-ear headphones you get on flights before, and used in-ear headphones to sleep on flights. These are not just in a different league, I suspect they are playing a different sport. (Obviously they are - NC vs no cancelling!). My ears did not hurt from being pressed back against my head, as with on-ear headphones and the inner ears do not hurt as with in-ear headphones. I wear them at least 4 hours a day, sometimes up to 10 hours a day at work. The only issue is that when the company "saves" money by not having the aircon going, I tend to sweat in them (this is not a sexy look).

Sound:
I am not an audiophile. I have tried various over and on-ear headphones in stores, and cannot tell anything between them. They all sound good. The GC15 is no different.

Noise cancelling:
I think the key term here is "noise". They do not cancel voices, they soften the background noise. Jet engines, keyboards, aircon, general hustle and bustle in the office away from where you are. Occasionally ring tones of my phone (I wasn't ignoring you, honest boss!).
Also, I took a Qantas Dash-8 on an internal flight recently and was in for a shock. I basically sat down and put my headphones on - got rid of the cable to show that they were no plugged in. Took off, all good. Love those propeller planes. Half way through the flight I turned my headphones off to the hostess. Actually jumped at how noisy the inside of the plane was in comparison to what the Bose was reducing the ambient volume to!

Battery life:
I use Duracell AAA batteries. I get weeks at a time with them, with the use specified above. The pouch has a Velcro holder for the airline plug and for additional batteries. I have read reviews which state they get less from their QC15's. Only thing I can think of is that they use cheaper batteries/rechargeable. And whilst they probably have better economy as a $/minute use, I think you cannot complain about battery life if you do that.

Changes:
A few things I would like changed. Bose, goodness sake stop pandering only to Apple customers with your leads and sound systems. Android has a huge fan base and we would love to have controls on the phone line.

I would love to see an add on for the headphones: a Bluetooth attachment. I have seen DIY versions, but nothing which I would be happy to have dangling out of my ear. Yes, it would probably need its own battery, but please just make one. These headphones would be brilliant to walk around with then. (ps: I know I have just asked for a lead, and then a thing to take the lead away, but in answer to that inconsistency: Shhhh.)

Get rid of the tacky "Bose greeting cards" stored in the pouch. You have a marketing department. They should know better than this.

Summary:
If you travel on planes (ignoring those freaky quiet A380s - seriously they are amazing), or work in a noisy workplace, or just like getting away from the background noise, then get these.
