product_title: Nuforce Polycarbonate Body In-Ear Headphones - Sky
review_headline: Colorful and fun, but ultimately lacking
review_body:
Sufficient for the price but nothing spectacular. For under $20, they make a relatively decent pair of in ear headphones. They fit well, at least for me, and come with a nice cloth pouch for storage. However, the are somewhat lacking in the sound department.

Sound wise the NE-770Xs lean somewhat heavily towards the bass end which is common with headphones in this price range. Unfortunately, the bass the NE-770Xs have is a bit more bloated and really blurs the mids. This issue is exacerbated by the small sound stage that the NE-770Xs have.

Pros:
+Red/White rings on earbuds for Right and Left is useful
+Nice shade of blue
+Easy to put in and comfortable

Cons:
-Small sound stage even for this price range
-Overly bassy without sufficiently high quality bass
-Mids suffer because of the high amount of bass

Ultimately, I can say that these make a decent pair of headphones. I personally find them quite stylish even. However in terms of sound they don't perform well enough. If you're not looking at the fashion aspect of these headphones and want a bit better sound for a comparable price, try out the Sennheiser CX200 headphones. They are a bit more of a pain to put in and not quite as comfortable for me but I think the sound is worth it (they have better highs and mids than these). And don't worry, the CX200s aren't hurting for bass either. As an aside, if you wait for it, the CX200s sometimes come down below the $18 list price for these headphones.

product_title: Asus WL-ANT-157 Antenna
review_headline: They only made my performance worse with RT-AC68U.  Your experience may be different.
review_body:
I tried these with the Asus RT-AC68U and did not get any improvement at all. In fact I only seemed to have gotten worse performance at the targeted locations. I bought 3 just to try. I tried using 1 as a replacement for the center antenna with the two included omnidirectional antennas on the sides. I also tried different combinations of two on the sides, and even all 3.

It's possible that your performance will be different than mine and could be better, but I found that aiming the included antennas in different directions and moving the router around a little had better improvements. My experience could be very much specific to my structure and the metallic objects/furniture in my house causing the problem. My point being that if you have few wood walls or are trying to direct over open air, it's possible these work better for your situation. It didn't for me.

I then got the three [[ASIN:B00DMJI9TA Super Power Supply® 3 x 9dBi 2.4GHz 5GHz Dual Band WiFi RP-SMA Antenna for Routers ASUS RT-N16 RT-N66U RT-AC66U RT-AC1750 D-Link DIR-655 DIR-665 Buffalo WZR-HP-G450H TP-Link TL-WR1043ND TL-WR2543ND TL-WDR4300 Omni Directional Network Extension Mini PCIe...]]. These had a profound improvement at my trouble area and improved performance around the entire house. They are a good price ($20 for all 3) and actually had a good improvement. I was even able to get a connection an low (3-5Mbps) transfer rate in my driveway. Before changing the antennas I couldn't lock on to the wifi signal and if I did, it couldn't actually transfer data.

I can't say I exhausted all options of placement combined with these directional antennas and as I said before with your structure and situation you could have a different experience.

If you're desperate, it's worth trying if you think it'll work for your particular application. But in my house, it didn't work.

product_title: Monster Cable MP EXP AVU Outlet Surge Protector with USB Charging with AV Protection
review_body:
First, this is not at all what is pictured in the photo (as of 8/2/14). The photo looks like a power strip, which this is not. This is an outlet box, which is what I actually wanted (as opposed to a power strip, of which I don't need any more).

The main downside:
-It is fairly big and bulky. But it's designed to replace the current wall outlet, so I expected that.
-Takes up both of the original outlets. That is, it plugs into the top of a 2-outlet receptacle and blocks the bottom one. You're getting 6 new outlets but still wish they would (somehow) create one that only used one of the original two outlets so I could still have one direct-to-wall outlets available.

The upsides:
-Gives you 6 outlets instead of the typical 2
-Includes 2 USB outlets to power devices (one for lower power USB devices like phone and mp3 player, the other for higher powered USB devices like tablets). An added upside: the USB outlets are on the bottom of the device. I have another similar outlet-replacement device and it has USB ports on the top of the device. In theory, I expected the USB ports on top to be better, because more than likely most of my devices would be higher than the outlet. product_title: Beyerdynamic Headphone Ear Pads Black
review_body:
I bought these for my Audio Technica m50's...like so many others have done before me.

The legendary m50's have one issue and that is their cheap pleather ear pads.

I didn't have the uncomfortability after 1 hr issue or sweatiness as heavily as other m50 users, but these issues are there to varying degrees for different people.

Honestly, I could live with the stock m50 pads as many people don't have issues, but if you wear the m50s a lot, this luxury purchase makes sense, especially after the eventual cracking of the plasticy stock ear pads.

These oft-recommended EDT ear pads are a good replacement for making the m50's more comfortable, no sweatiness issue and higher longevity (the won't crack).

The EDT pads take a while to install. Start at the top and use a rounded end plastic spoon or fork underneath to slide and push the envelope over the ridge.

As relates to the sound. Hmmmm. This is VERY subjective! I would align myself with some who say that these pads make the bass more reverbish and wider in soundstage in consequence.

The separate middle rounded fabric mesh that comes separately on the EDT can be put on or off. With the mesh off, the sound is slightly more sibilant. You can use the EQ to adjust that. I got used to the slight top end bump and currently leave the mesh off. I'm still experimenting with this at the moment. The middle mesh is slightly thicker than the stock mesh and using common sense, you can figure that it'll alter the sound a smidge. You have to be really anal about this issue to really care though. Alternatively you can cut the old mesh off your old m50s and place it here instead. If you want to make a hobby out of this issue it's up to you. Most won't care or have the time to play with it as they just want more comfort and use the mesh so the driver stays clean against the smudge from the backpack or skin flakes/hair.

In the end, I'd suggestto buy these once your stock pads crack or are having big comfort/sweat issues. Otherwise I'd postpone this purchase as these are OVERLY expensive at $24.

product_title: Denon AVR-S700W 7.2-Channel Network AV Receiver with Bluetooth and Wi-Fi (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Noticed it here first... amazing receiver for the price.
review_body:
For a 7.2ch receiver at a relatively affordable price, this is an excellent receiver with very few faults, if any. In this price range, you'd be hard pressed to find one better with as many features as it has in addition to excellent audio performance. Support for tons of codecs, all the bells and whistles you could want including Bluetooth, Wifi control (the smartphone app works really well though the UI could use a slight bit of work), Zone 2 support, several streaming services, 4k/60 support, HDMI 2.0 etc.

The back supports banana plugs, as it should... you don't want to be messing around with bare wires twisted around the posts.

I've tested it with an Xbox One, Xbox 360, a PC (detects DTS-MA, Dolby TrueHD etc. just fine with all of them, except the Xbox One which throws each channel out separately as LPCM 5.1 which is comparable though it doesn't light up the receiver's DTS MA and give you the warm feeling only an audiophile can understand), a Chromecast, my cable box etc. The Audyssey room calibration system is way better than DCAC on Sony's receivers and Yamaha's YPAO - setting up your speakers in all your oddly shaped rooms is made very easy.

I did not check the Airplay feature and Spotify Connect, but I know for sure that everything else works great! Just make sure you turn HDMI passthrough on so that you don't end up with no output to the TV when you switch the receiver off.

I went this after weeks of research and feel extremely happy with my decision having used this for a couple weeks now. My other choice was going to be a Sony STR-DH750, but a simple comparison of the power supply specs in the manual for the Sony and Denon will show you which one can actually drive as much as it claims to drive.

Pros:
Very good audio performance, comfortably drives my Monoprice 5.1 set (the premium 10565, amazing set for the price since it's an upgraded Energy Take Classic clone) with no distortion.
You can combine audio sources playing with different video sources going to the TV (eg. Bluetooth audio playing + Xbox game video to TV).
Bluetooth connects automatically to a paired phone (once you get it set up right) when the phone's in the room and you turn BT on on the phone. This may become annoying to some folks.
Audyssey (even Bronze) room EQ makes setup a breeze with an included calibration microphone!

Cons:
Only 2 of the HDMI ports on the back of the receiver are 4K capable. Not a big deal personally.
COMPLETE THE FIRMWARE UPDATE FIRST, you don't wait till you set everything up because the firmware update resets every single thing on your receiver. I did wait, and this pissed me off plenty.
Bluetooth was a lot of trouble to set up and the receiver would stop connecting to bluetooth phones and devices after a while and never reconnect until I removed the power cable and booted the receiver back up again. This somehow solved itself after a couple factory resets and I've had no trouble since.

While I was trying to set things right with the Bluetooth, I did chat with Denon's customer service. They were really nice, quite good with audio equipment as against the typical random-call-center person type.

review_body: December 14, 2014 Update  It's been about six months since I purchased these headphones & I STILL love'em!! It's now becoming winter in Buffalo so I've encountered one drawback. That's that the overall size of these are too big for any of my hats to fit over when I wear them \\"normally\\". I've found though that I can invert the 'phones with the crossbar under my chin & that works better. Obviously, they don't feel as stable this way but it beats the pee-dog-pooey out of earbuds.    Otherwise, I haven't noticed any degradation in sound quality at all. I've been slowly converting my vinyl collection over to digital and, in listening to stuff I haven't heard in decades, I'm hearing parts I've never heard before. Even songs I thought I knew like the back of my hand. It's just amazing.    Battery life seems to be eternal. I'm not walking for as long a time as usual, of course. The recent ice & snow make walking more than just a little dangerous, especially for someone who has already broken his leg twice in four different places.  But, my point is, I can't remember the last time I placed these on the charger. I use them quite often to watch movies or listen to music on my PC with the 3.5 mm cord, which doesn't drain the batteries, but they don't seem to bleed off the charge either. That's amazing to me.    There are no signs of anything coming loose or disconnected as I saw a few others mention. Again, I probably don't use mine as much as others might--Maybe 1-2 hours daily. They still feel as solid as when I first took them out of the box. I still have a little difficulty with the controls, though. Sometimes they work flawlessly. Other times I just resort to using my phone for the controller.    All in all, the positives far outweigh the minor negatives. Still a great value for great performance. These would be the perfect gift for anyone who really enjoys their A/V collection! Happy Holidays to all!!!    -----    August 24, 2014 Update  I've had these for over two months. I think I promised an update in my initial review so here it is:    Every single day that goes by I'm still so happy I bought these headphones! I'm currently on vacation in the Rio Grande Valley of South Texas visiting my brother who is battling colon cancer. My headphones made the long trip down far beyond simply bearable. I'm still astonished at the sound quality.    I listen to an eclectic mix of music. Godsmack to Mannheim Steamroller to John Prine to Metallica to Dan Fogelberg to Herb Alpert to Spyro Gyra to Macklemore & Ryan Lewis.    My normal \\"reference\\" system is my PC which is equipped with an M-Audio Audiophile 2496 card and my Klipsch ProMedia 4.1 400 watt multimedia speaker system. After over 15 years the surrounds on the sub speakers bit the dust and I have not had the time to repair them. The August headphones have very nicely bridged the void.    On \\"So Far Away\\" from Alan Parsons' \\"On Air\\" album I can hear perfectly all 4 voices of Christopher Cross' harmonies just as if I were listening to the ProMedia.  Ditto Chip Davis' delicate high hat in the more intense passages of \\"Toccata\\" on \\"Fresh Aire III\\" and the \\"ch\\" sound of Lars Ulrich's electronic kick drum at the beginning of Metallica's \\"One\\" It's like every time I listen to any song I haven't heard in a while I hear stuff I haven't heard in years.    We did a straight up comparison with my August phones and my brother's Bose corded headphones his wife got last year for half price for $99. It wasn't just me. He agreed that my headphones sounded far better than his. Midrange was more defined, bass was tighter & fuller, highs more clear & crisp.(I'm writing this on my S4 so I'll enter the Bose model # later)    A charge seems to last forever....or far longer than my phone at the very least. My only complaints remain about the track and volume controls on the headset. Even after 2+ months I still struggle with them. Granted I've been Type I diabetic for 37 years & my fingertips have lost a lot of sensation but you'd think over time I could adjust but so far I'm still having problems.    Minor issues though when compared to the positives. Don't know what else I can say to encourage you to try this product.  I absolutely love it!  No regrets whatsoever. I'd buy'em again in a heartbeat.    ____________________    First off, one of the main selling points for me is the EP650's option of either wired or wireless operation. Since I do not have BT on my desktop PC, it's so nice to be able to just plug in a 3.5 mm cable.    Product was very well packaged. Headphones come in a real box-not the impenetrable plastic bubble that is the bane of my existence. Product has a real manual, as well.    The EP650 have a nice, solid feel to them. Yes, they're made of plastic but they feel solidly built. When I unfolded them they clicked resolutely into position. An honest to goodness *click*. I was worried when I saw the size & shape of the speakers because I have pretty big ears. I was pleased when they completely covered my ears, and did so comfortably.    They are very nicely padded and they almost feel weightless. I had tried (& returned) a pair of Creative WP350 BT. They just never felt \\"right\\". One, they're \\"on-ear\\" where the EP650 covers the ear. I also had to hold my head in a particular position otherwise the signal cut out. The August model feels really comfortable. They felt great from the get-go.    The August headphones do get a little warm on the ears on hot days but it's a minor annoyance for me. I usually wear them for one to two hours every day and only on the hottest days have they been uncomfortable.    I had no issues connecting up to the EP650 with my Galaxy S4. I have my player set to continue on Bluetooth connection so it's just power up & go. Very convenient. I've used the 3.5 mm cable on my Sony Bravia TV, too. There's no volume adjustment but it serves its purpose.    The controls are a little disappointing although they work very well once you press them The main Power/Play/Pause/Source button has an indentation but neither the volume nor the track buttons have any distinguishing marks on them to aid your fingers. I have to fumble around a bit to achieve the desired result.    I don't remember \\"noise cancelling\\" being listed as a feature but the August model definitely has that benefit. I noticed a good -10 dB drop in ambient sound when I put them on with no output. I was really surprised. Medium volume is plenty even while mowing the lawn.    The sound quality is amazing. I listen to many different genres of music and have some favorites I use to test my equipment. With the EQ set flat, the EP650 is pretty balanced though a little heavy on the low end. I personally prefer that while some \\"purists\\" may not. In my normal setting I am able to hear all the key voices & instruments in all my test songs along with one or two I actually hadn't heard in a very long time.    Battery life has been stellar after a couple weeks of owning the EP650. The initial charge took about 3 hours. I have often charged the headphones with an AC-USB adapter from another device with no issues.    The built-in mic is a godsend, too. Every call I have made or received has been clear and the person on the other end could hear me perfectly. I don't game online so I cannot comment on that performance. So far, the EP650 has handled easily every single thing I have thrown at it music-wise & physically. I have dropped it a couple of times but it seems to be no worse for the wear.    I'm very happy with the EP650 & recommend it to anyone who wants a good quality product that over-delivers for the price.

product_title: Bluetooth Speaker, DKnight Magicbox Ultra-Portable Wireless Bluetooth Speaker Powerful Sound with build in Microphone, Works for Cellphone
review_body:
The Magic Box is a great buy at its cheap $30 price point. It fares very well against many of the more expensive, brand-name alternatives on the market with similar specifications. I do wish it was just a little louder, and don't jump in expecting Bose-quality sound, but you'd be hard-pressed to find a better deal at this price. And with its small size and great battery life, the speaker is perfect for the beach and long trips.

Battery life clocks in at around 8 to 10 hours--although you can expect a drop-off at higher volumes, and if you choose to use Bluetooth instead of an Aux cord. There's rubber padding on the top and the bottom, which does a good job at protecting the speaker and keeping it from shaking/falling on a moving surface (like the dashboard of your car).

Unfortunately, my first unit was defective, and Bluetooth didn't work. DKnight customer service was very helpful, and I've since ordered a new one to replace it. Alongside the fact I have a couple of friends who own the same speaker and haven't had issues, I wouldn't have any reservations about ordering from DKnight in the future.

product_title: Bowers & Wilkins Zeppelin Air Wireless AirPlay Speaker Dock
review_body:
I've recently purchased the Zeppelin Air to play my iPhone music and allow others to use the AirPlay on their devices. Coming from a Hi-Fi background I was sceptical about how good it would sound playing my iTunes library. I shouldn't have been concerned. For a £500 device, it sounds fantastic. The bass has punch but not at the expense of the mid and top. It's clear and about as refined as you will get at this price mark. It fills my medium sized living room no problem at all.

It looks great although it's not very protable. As others have mentioned, it has no handle so once it's in place, it stays there.

The AirPlay was easy to set up. I've read a few reviews from people who have had issues. I didn't bother with the instruction manual (being a man). I donwloaded the handy iPhone app and followed the instructions. About 5 minutes later, my phone, iPad and partners phone were all pumping out music over the air. I've not had any drop out issues although I haven't used AirPlay too much as yet. I didn't even notice any sound degredation switching from AirPlay to docking which was a nice suprise.

Overall I think it's a beautifully designed, convenient piece of kit for someone who just wants to dock their phone and listen to good quality sound. For the price, it does what it says on the tin and more.

product_title: Avantree Bluetooth Transmitter and Receiver Low Latency
review_body:
This new version of the Avantree bluetooth transmitter is finally perfect for listening TV audio on bluetooth headphones. You can attach it to an USB port of your TV and to TV audio line out (rather than the TV headphone jack), thus you won't need anymore to reach to the back of your TV every time you use it to power it on or off, to recharge it or to connect/disconnect audio. It will automatically power on and stay on whenever you turn the TV on, and you can put the TV on mute and still receive the audio via bluetooth.
The transmitter keeps all the good features of the Saturn Pro: small, light, easy pairing, option to operate on battery or usb power, good usb power filtering to avoid audio noise, apt/x low latency.
Also, one very useful new feature is that the Priva II now supports dual link to pair two bluetooth headsets/receivers at the same time. So both I and my wife can both listen to TV on bluetooth headsets without disturbing the children.
The only thing that it loses with respect to the Saturn Pro is that the Priva is a transmitter only, while the Saturn could be configured either as transmitter or receiver, so I now use the Priva to transmit TV audio and the Saturns to receive it.

[The following one is my old review for the Saturn Pro.
I've received two of these units as a replacement of the previous "saturn" model from Avantree. They are physically identical to the previous ones, retain all the good points (pair easily, small, light, etc) and also SOLVE the two main issues which made the previous ones quite inconvenient to be used for listening TV. More specifically, audio is no longer cut out when the volume is somewhat low and I can use them powered by the USB port of my TV without causing any additional noise. Also I didn't experience any inappropriate auto power-off with this new model. My compliments also for the excellent customer service.
My only remaining wish is for an auto-power-on feature when connected to an USB port.]

I installed these in a kitchen/dining area with a sliding door to an outdoor deck. They're easy to control from my phone, which is where I'm streaming the music from, with the app - so the speaker volume and light brightness can be easily changed. In the summer we often eat on the deck, and with the door open the speakers are powerful enough to be heard outside.

Previous to this I would just have my phone volume cranked up and then bring it from the kitchen where I was cooking out to the deck to eat, but the quality was never great and I had to carry it with me. Works great so far except for just one thing. This appears to be a sturdily built cable but it is a little too stiff which may or may not be an issue depending on how you need to use it. If the cable must make a sharp bend such as when the connection exits to the rear and it is placed close to a wall there might be more stress on the connector that you would like.

In my case my big screen plasma TV has its connections pointing out the side but are only a few inches away from the edge. If I want to keep the cable from sticking out the side, I have to make a sharp bend. I sure would hate to break the connector on my TV. That I am sure would be big bucks to fix!

I have several other HDMI cables, some came with the equipment. Some are stiff and some are fairly flexible, however, I don't remember ever seeing this pointed out in their descriptions.

product_title: Pioneer Headphones
review_body:
I wanted to love these headphones. I like them a lot. There are a couple of issues, which I address below. There was a third, but that turned out to be user error. My apologies to Pioneer.

The enclosed literature is mammoth. I pulled the packet out of the bottom of the box, and a multitude of separate leaflets fluttered into my lap. Weeding through them to find the looked for information is pretty tedious, though not a deal breaker. There are pamphlets for residents of Australia, California, and several in various pictographs--none of them useful. The English instructions were pretty sketchy, mostly warnings about the dangers of high volume and ingestion (!).

They come in a great little zippered pouch, just right for dropping into a tote or purse. The cord is very long, and the first problem with these is that despite the length of the cord, the controls are too close to the earpiece. This means volume must be controlled by touch alone. This, coupled with the very small size of the control box, makes it necessary to remove the earpiece to adjust the volume. It seems like it would have been just as easy to put the control box further down the cord so removing the earpiece wouldn't be necessary. I have small hands and fingers, and I still found it impossible to adjust the volume by touch alone.

Middle sized earpieces come installed, with a smaller and larger set included. When I tested the headphones, the earpieces kept falling out of my ears, so I set out to install the smaller earpieces. The instructions say just to push firmly. Nope. The flange that's supposed to fit over the plastic earpiece is the exact circumference of the earpiece.

Here's the solution: There's a lip around the earpiece. Snag one side of the flange over the lip and twist while pushing. It'll go right on, but not if you follow the printed instructions.

Having the right size earpiece makes a big difference in my happiness with these headphones. They still aren't the best fit in the world for me--I have weird ears, and have to be careful the weight of the very long cord doesn't pull them out, but the sound is lovely. I don't listen to all that much bass heavy music, but right now I'm listening to a favorite collection of John Williams soundtracks. That music covers pretty much all the musical bases (no pun intended) and I'm hearing nuances that I've not heard before. All the lushness of Jurassic Park comes through, but the instrument sections are distinguishable as well.

It's the first time I've heard the glass windchimes in Seven Years in Tibet. Wow!

Itzhak Perlman's violin in Schindler's List is simply gorgeous. It'll kill you.

product_title: Monster Cable MP EXP AVU Outlet Surge Protector with USB Charging with AV Protection
review_headline: Worked great for two weeks, then stopped.
review_body: --UPDATE--    I took this from 4 stars to 1 after using it for 2 weeks. All the below was valid while it worked, then it just stopped working. The outlets no longer work and neither do the USB ports. It wasn't under a heavy load (although we did use the USB function regularly), but there was only one device plugged in. The only solace is the little red light still comes on.    I'm GREATLY disappointed in this poor workmanship.  I have no idea why it would just fail after two weeks, when I have other power strips that have lasted for 15 years. Just disappointed overall with this experience.       Original Review:    The first thing that I noticed about this power strip is its slim-line footprint. It's lighter than other power strips that we've used, yet its claims of effectiveness are just as prominent as any other strip.  The biggest issue for us that with only 6 outlets, it's not really suited for our entertainment center (which this was clearly designed for).    I did manage to plug it in using some of our system components, and honestly, I didn't see any difference. The documentation proclaims that the MONSTER power filtration can provide \\"better picture and sound\\" but I did not find that to be the case. Admittedly, I've invested more than a couple of bucks into my system, but I can't imagine exactly what they're referring to.    When I plugged in the coaxial connection, I did not see any noticeable difference in quality, in ether HD or SD. I might be expecting a lot though. I will say that for some reason I have burned out one TV and one Cable box on the erratic power here where I live, so the coaxial part might actually help with saving my current set-top box. Really no way of the average user being able to tell this though.    The single biggest advantage of buying this power strip over a competitor are the USB plugs. These are very handy and charged anything we plugged into it (mostly iDevices and a Kindle). I can see this being the single-most-used feature of this device. The only disappointing thing is that if you're using this exclusively for your TV/Entertainment center (And why wouldn't you? It's designed for a cable input!) then you're probably going to have it BEHIND the entertainment center (hiding the wires) and not out in front. Even if you did have it where you could easily reach the plugs, the cables stick right out.    So aesthetically speaking, it's a design flaw. The USB ports should be somewhere different. If however, you are using this with the same USB cables all the time, then it's much less of a deal -but we tend to swap cables a LOT in my house with six people running around, so I just can't see what the designers were thinking when they placed the USB plugs where they did. It;s just awkward.    But to their credit - I wish the USB feature was embedded in every device like this now. It worked exactly as it was supposed to, and while we didn't note that the product charged any faster or any better, we did notice that it just worked. And it's a fixed location so less chargers walking off.    Ultimately, because of the design, we had to give it four stars. I think it's a great product, but I don't see the practically of using both the coaxial plugs and the USB plugs together without the knowledge that you won't remove the USB plugs often. I hope I never have to test the \\"fireproof\\" feature, or every have to take advantage of the MONSTER Warranty of $150k for connected devices. All and all it's great, but I can't position it in my living room without the USB cables being hard to plug in, or the coaxial cables sticking out...

product_title: Audio Technica ATH-ANC23 QuietPoint Active Noise-Cancelling In-Ear Headphones
review_body:
These headphones are great. I take the bus daily and occasionally go on a long-haul flight or two, and these definitely help get the engine rumble out of the way.

Noise canceling: is more impressive than what I had expected for something at this price. Without music, I can hear some engine noise left in; but once music is on I actually missed a bus or two because I didn't hear it coming. The noise canceling is not that effective on a jetliner, though, probably because jet engine noise has a higher frequency than buses so more of it seeps through. But again it's definitely much, much better than having nothing at all. What I love about these is that they don't make much hissing sound when noise canceling is turned on, unlike some others I've tried. This would definitely be very helpful if you're trying to sleep on a plane.

Sound Quality: I'm not that picky and these sound great to me. There's ample bass and treble in the mix, so I'm pretty sure if it doesn't sound right you can fix it by tweaking your phone/music player. More importantly, these will work without having ANC turned on. The volume will be a tiny bit lower (but probably because you can hear the noise), but it's definitely better than being unable to listen to music at all once the battery dies. The volume knob is helpful if you just don't want to take your phone out every other song to adjust it.

The Control Box: I didn't find it that annoying as many others pointed out, but that's probably because I always have a jacket or belt to clip it to. It is a little heavier than ideal, though, and the one time it fell off my shirt, it almost ripped one of the earbuds out of my ear. I imagine having it dangling wouldn't be a good idea, but you can always clip it to your pants' pocket which is way safer than on the shirt. There's enough cable on both ends of the box for you to position it pretty much anywhere reasonable.

Battery Life: very promising. I've used it for twoweeks now, around 2 hours daily, and still has not needed to change the battery.

There's no monitor button, which would be very handy. And the noise canceling actually do work somewhat on human voice too, so if you need to talk you'll have to take them off to hear the other person clearly. I couldn't make out what the other person is saying with ANC turned on but no music. But this doesn't happen a lot for me so I'm perfectly happy without it.

product_title: Sol Republic Tracks Ultra Headphones
review_headline: A beautiful set of balanced headphones for the generally casual music lover. That just means no audiophiles or whatever.
review_body:
The SOL Ultras set bass aside a bit and focus on delivering better clarity, especially in the high frequencies. Despite a slightly over-the-top brightness in that range, these headphones are very good sounding. Bass is still there, though not as punchy as previous SOL iterations of its headphone line. Its solid, but if you like your bass, go with the Tracks or the Tracks HD.

Mids shine as well, as SOL has managed to fix that issue with their Ultras and Tracks HD. Vocals and guitars do not sound muddy anymore, thankfully. The sound balance in both of the aforementioned products is wonderful, but for some songs, I'd actually go as far as saying BASS is drowned out by other aspects, especially in metal and harder alternative rock. In chunky rock, bass guitar already struggles to make itself present, as bass is used as an accompaniment rather than an attention getter like dance and rap use it. Sometimes, guitar riffs or raw vocals completely run the bass over.

The Ultras look stunning though. The deep blue color is gorgeous and the SOL logo is etched into the circular metallic finish of the ear cups, giving off a very elegant and luxurious vibe. They are harder to clean, and dirt likes to get caught in the metal grooves, though, as an advanced warning.

product_title: Brainwavz M2 In-Ear Headphones
review_headline: Amazing sound and comfort at this price!
review_body:
Brainwavz seems to have headphones at every price point, from the super economical up to studio quality high-end models. I have several different Brainwavz headphones, at various price points. All are at the top of their respective classes. By that I mean they have the best sounding $30 headphones when compared against other $30 headphones (or even more expensive) and so on. The first thing that stands out with these headphones is that they are NOT plastic. Next is the cable. It resembles a coated braided cable more than a typical headphone cable. It's tangle free - to the extent that it tries to "untangle" when spiraled up - but it's still flexible. The cables also loop over the ears and stay there.

Also included are a variety of tips, including a set of memory-foam Comply Foam Tips, and a compact carrying case.

As for the sound - these sound great at all volume levels with everything from classical and opera, to rock and metal, techno and industrial (I like almost all music styles.) The highs are not tinny, and the bass is decently deep - probably the best I've heard in ear-buds without separate bass drivers.

They are also light weight and comfortable. I wore them at the gym and mowing the yard - both involved a lot of movement and sweat. They stayed put. Remember - correct fit depends on the correct tip size. Try different ones till you find the one that works best!

product_title: Philips O'Neill THE SPECKED In-Ear Headset
review_body:
Bought this on Amazon for $19.99 and have had it for about 5 months now, so this review is based on my usage through that period.

Good points
- durable cord. Despite its appearance, does not fee like cloth, more like nylon. I use it for calls nightly, and usually fall asleep with my headphones on, and its held up despite significant pulling/crushing (this is exactly why I got this set for)
- solid jack (3.5mm) with stress point, so it doesn't suffer through wear and tear.
- driver units are made of tough plastic and hard rubber, so they are able to withstand stress and won't crack at the cord/driver connection point

"Okay" points
- average mic. Have had some difficulty having ppl hear me on occasion, but this is rectified placing the mic closer when I speak
- average sound quality. Better than the standard Iphone headphones, but the sound for these Phillips lacks in comparison with another pair of in-ear headphones I have (House of Marley Conqueror's). I'm comparing them as I got em for the same price, but the Marley's have better depth of sound, volume and bass. The Phillips' have a solid enough sound, but less warm and full.
- the cord - less prone to tangles than regular rubber/plastic cords, but still some difficulty.

"Meh" points
- the colour - this is actually okay in my book, but most ppl would find the lime green/red/black/white/grey colour combination a lil too much. These definitely have more 'character' in this aspect.
- the cord - I notice some discolouration from the time I first got these till now, the green cord isn't as bright as it used to be. A minor quibble and not something you'd notice unless you owned em.

Overall, these are worth at least the money I spent on em, though typically where I live, a similar set would go for probably $40, closer to the MSRP (listed as $39.99 when I bought these on here). If you are looking for a durable pair and not exactly acoustic perfection, these are a solid pick.

product_title: Okki Nokki Record Cleaning Machine with dust-cover
review_headline: Does what it's supposed to do
review_body:
This is my 1st RCM -- I've collected records for 30 years and used isopropyl and cotton in the early days and in later years used solutions derived from the internet along with MFSL felt pad brushes. I can manually clean a record as good as a RCM but it's a lot more work and takes more time. I'm also a big 45 rpm collector and sometimes these garage sale finds are grimy and filthy and I strongly recommend cleaning by hand before using any RCM because you'll gunk up the platter and pads on the cleaning wand.

The person who gave this RCM one star and complained, is in my opinion a \\"one in every crowd\\" type, i.e., don't pay attention. Having said that, I thought any RCM would work magic when in fact they don't. They'll clean a not very dirty record and make it clean and shiny. You could probably transform a VG+ record into a M- record depending on the type of dirt -- if it's finger prints or smoke film it will clean very well.

Anyway, I'm glad I purchased the Okki Nokki, the build quality is fine, it's reasonably quiet, the smaller-than-VPI-size is nice -- and it looks cool -- but it's not a magic machine as I thought it wound be, I still need to clean gunky records by hand before I used the machine but in the long run I'll clean records a lot faster with any RCM than by hand.

If you're the type of person who is willing to steam clean, wash and rinse and maybe repeat to get as clean a record as humanly possible, a RCM is indispensable simply because of its ability to vacuum the cleaning solution and rinse water quickly without getting the labels wet. Finally, In my opinion if you plan on cleaning 25 or less records a year you don't need a RCM. Buy more vinyl instead.

product_title: Beats By Dr. Dre Studio 1.0 Over-ear Wired Headphone Red Noise Cancelling NEW
review_headline: Bad Company, Horrible price point for what you get
review_body:
While these headphones sound pretty good for certain genres of music (rap & hip hop), they are lacking in so many categories. Primarily, the price for what you get is terrible. They are constructed of cheap plastic that is known to break over time, wires/cables that are garbage, and sound quality that is mediocre when compared to the likes of other brands for the same or considerably less money. They wont even advertise specifications on their website because they know they are under-engineered; this is particularly embarrassing... The ONLY info you can actually find anywhere on the internet is their frequency response which is not impressive at all.
Beats Studio($300) : 20hz - 20,000hz
V-moda LP2($200) : 5hz - 30,000hz
...wow. That explains why they don't advertise their specs.
Another category where Beats falls short is construction. Made almost entirely of cheap plastic, they are known to break over relatively short periods of time. I, as well as a few friends can attest to this. The Studios I purchased did not break on the outside, but were snap, crackling, and popping within a month. Annoying white noise is present as a result of their build-in amplifier and pointless noise-cancelling features that should NEVER be included in "Studio grade" headphones. While they have a decent warranty policy, companies such as bose and V-moda have far superior ones.
All in all, these headphones sound OK, but not anywhere close to where they should be for the price. This high price point is probably a consequence of the over-marketing/advertising they do. If your looking for style and don't care much about sound quality or durabilty, these headphones are for you..
I think thats the main demographic for Beats anyway - people with lots of money to spend on a fashion statement.

product_title: Waterfi Waterproof Headphones with Short Cord for Swimming, Surfing, and Running
review_headline: Working great, once I learned to wear them right
review_body:
I've been trying to get waterproof earbuds to work for me for many months, and at about the time I purchased this pair, I feel like I've got it down. I try to do an uninterrupted "swimmer's mile" of 1650 yds. every time I swim, about 3-4 times a week, and flip turns at each end. Anybody trying to get with their earbuds knows that doing flip turns increases the likelihood of water getting in your ears. And while I've gotten accustomed to losing one channel or the other over the course of my swim, I no longer need to anymore. Here's how I do it.

Your typical waterproof mp3 player affixes to your head somehow. IMO, that's really the best way for lap swimmers. But here's the deal. You route the wires *from above,* under the straps for your goggles, and down to your ears. I think all the pics always show them coming in from below, like you're jogging or whatever. I always get water in my ears when I do it this way. But routing them from above, with the straps helping to hold them in place, I'm now able to swim for an hour or longer, doing any number of laps, flip turns, or swimming underwater, and never losing my stereo sound or getting water in my ear canals. And while you can, with cheaper earbuds, just tuck all the excess wire under the straps also, it's not necessary with this set. I use these with my Pyle mp3 player, swim at least an hour per session, and they are working great for me.

I got this gadget as a Mother's Day gift for my Dear Old Mom. She's 91 and, aside from failing hearing, is bright and lively. She consumes the daily newspaper and likes to watch the news and opinion shows on TV. But even with hearing aids tuned by the audiology department at Northwestern Hospital, she was missing chunks of TV audio. She had particular difficulty with women's voices and accents, as in the shows PBS imports from England. On the other hand, I know that the best way to converse with her is by telephone. She uses an amplified phone without her hearing aids. So, I reasoned, what if we could put the TV audio into her ears as directly as telephone audio?
These radio frequency headphones are fabulous! We took some time to work out the which combination of frequency filters and enhancers worked best for her. And now she can hear clearly, even "Downton Abbey" and "The Father Brown Mysteries". She can walk into the kitchen to get a snack, into the bedroom to get a sweater, or go to the bathroom without having to hurry. Did I mention that, in addition to her failing hearing, she's not quite as fleet afoot as she once was?

product_title: BlueAnt Pump - Wireless HD Sportbuds - Black
review_body:
The BlueAnt Pump - Wireless HD Sportbuds Black are a premium set of Bluetooth headphones that are designed to be used while exercising or any type of physical exertion. I've used several sets of headphones that have been designed for such use, but this is the first Bluetooth pair that I've tried out. First of all, this is a great feature and makes going for a run or working out in the gym much easier. The lack of cords to get tangled means that I could place the phone in my pocket or use a holder to keep it on my person without worrying about it become unplugged. The range was pretty good - up to about 25 feet before the sound started to cut out. Battery life was consistent with what the packaging claimed. Included is a USB charging cable but no wall adapter. Also had a phone conversation while wearing these, so they work well syncing with the phone for more than just music.

As for the sound - it's pretty standard for a set of sport headphones. Not great but it will get the job done. When spending so much for headphones you'd like a little better sound, but unless you go over-the-ear the sound quality is limited in any set of headphones. And such noise reduction may not be great for running on roads! Another feature is the water resistance, and I have run in the rain with these. They held up well.

Also included are different sizes of buds to place in your ears and stabilizers. I found the largest size to fit me best (I'm an average size man). The stabilizers need to be placed just right otherwise they can cause physical discomfort. This is one drawback while experimenting while trying to find the right fit and sound quality.

Overall I am pleased with these headphones. I'm still tinkering with finding the right fit for my ears but I have a feeling that I am never going to get that depth of sound that I'd like. Keep that in mind while considering if these are right for you. For active people these are a good fit; for a set of headphones for general use you can do better for the price.s for general use you can do better for the price.

product_title: Mount-It! Universal TV Wall Mounting Bracket – For LCD, Plasma, or LED TVs – 42-70”
review_body:
While this wall mount seems very solid and easily accommodates my 48" LED TV, I had several issues with set-up.

Two vertical brackets attach to the back of the TV and these brackets hang on the arm of the wall mount. The kit comes with many options of bolts to attach the brackets to the TV, however the ones that fit the threads of my Samsung LED TV were either too short or too long. I used some included spacers (meant for curved-back TVs) to make the long bolts fit. The "ultra-low profile" nature of the mount means that any cables that plug into the back of the TV may not fit between the TV and the arm once mounted. I worked around this problem by using the spacers between the TV and the brackets to allow for more room for cables to pass. (Be sure to thread the cables between the arm and the TV so that they will not get caught in the mount when it is pushed against the wall.)

The vertical brackets are adjustable to tilt the TV, however, they will not remain perfectly vertical due to the weight of the TV and the extra distance given with the spacers. It is also nearly impossible to adjust the tightness of the bolts that control the tilting once mounted.

The brackets are designed to hang on the top edge of the arm then swing into place at the bottom. A small screw on each bracket can be tightened to keep the bottom of the bracket from swinging away from the arm. These screws are attached to the one weak point of the bracket, so they bend that small piece of bracket and therefore don't provide enough support to keep the brackets from sliding back and forth on the arm when adjusting the position of the TV. I overcame this problem by using multiple layers of duct tape on either side of where the brackets hang on the arm to keep the brackets from sliding.

Despite these issues, the mount is clearly secure on the wall and has little to no "play" vertically even when fully extended. Extending the mount takes alittle effort as all the joints are rather tight, and I suspect they may free up with time.

product_title: Comfort Duett with Neckloop
review_headline: For Mild To Profound Hearing Loss
review_body:
That's what I have.. a mild to profound hearing loss. I wear the new BTE or so called RITC digital aid. I don't bother with the programming and just switch to T mode. I'm in my younger 30's and I find the Comfort Duett very discreet can be worn under your shirt and makes the conversations clearer. I couldn't be more happier with this product. I've tried several other listening devices and this Comfort Duett is by far one of the better ones. Some of you may not find it suitable due to several factors: Degree or Hearing loss, the lack of tone control, or it's lack of output gain(volume). If you want more power and tone control you need to be looking for the Williams Sound Pocket Talker Pro or Ultra. I own the Pro because it has a durable belt clip which I can use to attach to my clothing. The belt clip on the Pro is much more reliable than the Ultra. But the features are the same except the Ultra has external Tone Control. The Pro version Tone Control is located inside the battery and I wear it as my daily driver (without need to adjust the Tone). I wear the Comfort Duett when I'm physically active with my life and need something lightweight and temporary. Sometimes I use it when on dates and special events were I need to be a little more more discreet. The comfort Duett is worn on my neck comfortably like a pendant with T mode switch ON at the hearing aid. If you have profound hearing loss like me you might find yourself with the Comfort Duett volume setting maxed out and your hearing aids volume settings maxed out to reach a desired gain. Just to give you a general idea; the Pocket Talker is so powerful I don't need to have the volume more than 5 to reach desired comfort level. Hope this helps.

Theres only one small con is the reason for the 4 star.. since it's not a bluetooth device theres no need for the annoying green led to be flashing every 3-4 seconds when it's on. If you want to be more discreet you have to wear something dark over it or blinking bright light will draw attention from whoever is facing you. Someone mentioned that using black electric tape will help.. I haven't tried that yet. But that's all for this review.right light will draw attention from whoever is facing you. review_headline: I've owned many earphones. This one tops them all
review_body: It goes without saying there simply aren't any earphones that can reproduce the sounds as well as these can. product_title: Sangean America Inc AM/FM-RDS/Bluetooth/USB Table-Top Digital Tuning Receiver
review_body:
I'm using this on a nightstand next to my bed as a clock radio alarm. The radio reception is quite good and the sound quality is not bad for what it is. The feature set is perfect and I find it intuitive and easy to use. What I really like is the knob that is used to change settings, I can quickly change the alarm time by rotating the knob either way for instance. One of my personal pet peaves are alarm clocks that have you hit a button 45 times to set the time 15 minutes earlier. It's quick and easy with this device.

There are two things that I really don't like though (I was debating subtracting 1 or 2 stars). First is the brightness control. The dimmest setting is perfect for a dark room but as the room gets brighter in the morning the display doesn't get bright enough in unison. It doesn't take much room light to make it unreadable. The next higher brightest setting is way too bright in a dark room. Too bad, so close, and it's just a software problem, easily fixed by adding a few intermediate settings. The second problem is that there is no reasonable battery backup or nonvolatile storage for the settings. When the power goes out at my place, I lose everything, time, station presets, alarms, all of it. That's a big pain where I live, enough so that I bought a small UPS specifically for this radio. But, come on, this is a $150 device, it should tolerate power outages without having to spend an extra $35.

Overall though I really like it. If there was only more control over the brightness settings I'd call it absolute perfection, even with the extra I had to spend on a UPS. It has the perfect set of features and usability otherwise.

Update 7/13/15:
I'm dinging it some more stars. Every few months the thing crashes and reboots. Yes, just like a software crash. I was actually looking right at it when it happened one time, no power outage or anything, it just randomly died and restarted. When this happens it resets all of your settings so, again, you have to go through the rather tedious setup to get everything configured. Hopefully you remember it all. Absolutely nothing is saved, you lose everything. What a pain. It's also not confidence inspiring if you use need an alarm for critical appointments.

Don't count on saving all the money diff by buying this older item, as you'll soon be forking up 25% of that diff to get the adapter replaced. I will vouch for the sound quality of this item, which reproduces lossless and hi-res audio perfectly (even without the subwoofer optional add on).

product_title: Cheetah Mounts APDAM3B Dual Articulating Arm TV Wall Mount Bracket for 20-65” TVs up to VESA 400 and 115lbs, Mounts to Two 16" studs and includes a Twisted Veins 10’ HDMI Cable and a 6” 3-Axis Magnetic Bubble Level
review_headline: Instructions are terrible, product is okay
review_body:
I got this product to wall mount a 46" Samsung TV. I wanted the dual articulating mount mostly so I could pull the TV off the wall and mount cables. I went with a cheaper option, and I slightly regret it.

First things first, the instructions are absolutely terrible. For something like this, it is not very difficult, but something as simple as providing a hole pattern for the wall would have went a LONG way. There was nothing like that, so I was on my own to figure out the holes and to mount them in the studs. Then, there was a lack of labeling for the products, what goes where, who knows? Once I got the piece mounted on the wall I went to put the pieces on the back of the tv. (Also, no mention on making sure that you have it level, which MIGHT be important). What the product came with, and what the pictures show are two entirely different things. Its not that hard to figure out, but just be sure you pay attention. The hooks obviously go on the top of the mount, but if I followed the hole pattern on the arms I would have put it on upside down.

Now the BIGGEST problem that I had was for the safety screws. I had to forcefully bend the bracket to mount the safety screw in the bottom. There weren't any instructions saying what to do here, where to put it, anything like that. So that took me longer to get that in there correctly than anything.

Several reviewers also noted that the tilt on the mount makes it unusable. I would agree with this assessment, BUT there are two silver pins included that you can lock the tilt in place. It still tilts a little bit, but very slightly. From where I'm looking (straight on) it looks great, but its noticeable from the side.

All that said, I probably should have got a different mount. I wouldn't recommend this for folks.

Pros:
Holds the TV well
Articulating arms
Price

Cons:
Instructions are terrible
Safety screw mounting bracket not lined up
Tilting issues/>Tilting issues

product_title: Diver 4GB Waterproof MP3 Player with LCD Display and Earphones (Blue)
review_body:
I purchased this item because I work outside and I wanted something that could handle sweat and rain. The headphones are nice. Sound quality isn't awesome but it's good enough and it blocks outside noise pretty well. The coiled cord is also a nice feature because I work with equipment and it doesn't get caught on things.

The MP3 player has a built in radio which is nice because I like to listen to talk radio in the morning. The audio quality is lackluster so I guess the OK headphones are a good fit for the product. There is no option for shuffle. Biggest downside to this product. I think I can get over poor sound quality after a while but no option to shuffle?

This isn't really a true mp3 player either. It's basically a USB drive with a headphone jack. It doesn't display song title, artist, album stuff. It displays the file name. So if you want to organize your songs, you need to put them in folders and name all your files.

This is a very basic MP3 player and it's best feature is that it is waterproof. In my opinion this item is way over priced. You can get an ipod shuffle, waterproof headphones, and waterproof case for the shuffle for the same price, maybe a few dollars more.

This product wasn't for me. Maybe it's perfect for somebody else.

product_title: Klipsch Image S4i-II
review_headline: Best Bang for your Buck Earphones by far
review_body:
The audio quality is fantastic and very noticeable compared to the cheap earphones most people use or get for free with devices. The controls and microphone are great and work at least as good as any other similar earphones. What I mean by that is that the controls work fantastic but the microphone picks up noise a little too well sometimes causing people on the other end of calls to get annoyed by any background noises. If you're in a quiet room the microphone is great.

The oval shapes of the silicone ear pieces fit great in the ear and do an excellent job of blocking out noise. If you're exercising or riding a bike I really do suggest leaving one side out because the noise isolation is so good, I believe it is hazardous to be so unaware of your surroundings.

Some people may never need more than the stock earphones you'll get with their devices but some people also don't know how much they're missing by not spending a little more on quality headphones. If you enjoy listening to music, you owe it to yourself to try some quality earphones and you really don't have to spend that much to get them. You can buy some big name brands for 3x as much money but you won't get 3x more quality if any at all. Klipsch is a well known company for quality audio and I've purchased many of their products and in my dealings with their customer service, it has always been a great experience.

One thing you should be aware of, you're going to want to make sure whoever you are buying it from on Amazon is an approved vendor for Klipsch products as I know some people ran into warranty issues when buying from non approved vendors.

product_title: DSLRKIT D-BH109 AA BATTERY HOLDER FOR PENTAX K-R KR K-30 CAMERA bh109
review_headline: It Does the Job for a Little Bit at a Great Price
review_body:
I was hours from home when I realized I hadn't packed the charger for my K-r. I have been wanting the AA adapter for a long time, and went for this instead of Pentax's when I saw the reviews and amazing price.

The product description claims this will "double the shooting time." It won't, but I did get about 1/3 of what my original battery can do for each set of four AA's. That's fine by me since I will be using this only as an "emergency" backup. The fit is a bit tight for the AA's themselves, and took a tiny bit of effort to insert and remove them. Also, the second set of batteries I put in read as depleted within a couple of minutes, but showed a full charge again after I removed this holder and popped the batteries in and out again to make sure they were positioned correctly.

I'd love to give this five stars based on price and that it does work. I'm giving three stars because it's finicky and, while I knew AA's probably wouldn't last as long as a full charge on my K-r's original battery, I expected a little more life out of them based on this product's description.

product_title: TDK Life On Record Trek Bluetooth Wireless Speaker
review_headline: Love the portability, sound is good for size
review_body:
I have more BT speakers than I care to mention, but let's just say a LOT. I don't try to collect them, but in my search for The One, I have gone through (and still use) many.

This one ranks up there with the better ones if you consider the size. You're not going to want this as your main BT speaker, since as I mentioned, there are so many out there, and if you don't need the portability, then you will easily get better sound in other options (for not much more $$).

But this is the smallest one I have used, and if you wanted something for travel, or even something to carry on your bike, for instance, this would be the one I would use.

I doubt I would ever get a second for the stereo effect, just due to cost, and again, if I am going to pay that, and get that extra bulk...there are much better sounding options out there.

Love the weather-resistance, build quality is VERY tight, very impressive, and most important, the sound is quite impressive considering the small size.

Very highly recommended if you specifically need an ultra-small BT speaker.

product_title: Sony STR-DN1050 7.2 Channel Hi-Res 4K AV Receiver (Built-in Wi-fi & Bluetooth)
review_body:
So far, this seems to be working extremely well. I personally like the fact that the physical remote control is simplified, but I think that's a topic where there'll be some people who would much rather have the more feature-rich remote of the previous generation of devices.

There's a sort of inevitable "Yikes" moment when you open up anything like this that needs to have so many different connections available. Once you take a few minutes to get yourself oriented, though, it really isn't too hard to set up. Everything is pretty clearly labeled and it really only took a few minutes to reach the point where I had devices sending audio and video through the receiver.

There's really a ton that this thing can do, from handling very high end video signals to passing signals along to a second zone. I'm basically getting a feel for it a little at a time, hooking up additional devices and playing around with things like the microphone they include to help configure the speakers and apps like Pandora. On one hand it's really nice that it can do so much. On the other hand, it's hard not to wonder how many of the people who end up choosing this are really going to learn and use the full range of features, rather than falling into the habit of just hooking it up and using the basics (swapping between devices and that kind of thing).

It's a very good receiver, though I think they haven't quite worked out the interface to the point where everything is so easy to find and use that it's absolutely amazing. I really like being able to do things like stream audio to it wirelessly. I'm also very happy that it has component connections for the older game consoles that we still have in the house.

As they continue to do software updates, I might come back a few months down the line to update this and say it's amazing. For now I'll say that it's working very well and doing what they promised. The only tricky part is that you have to be honest with yourself about which features you're really likely to use, because I think it's very possible that some people looking at this would be served just as well by a slightly cheaper model that doesn't do quite as much.

I sincerely caution other buyers to beware of buying Philips electronic devices. I'm sure most of them are fine, but when you do have a problem don't expect to get any support. review_body:
**This only works with iPhone 5 and above, and the latest iPod versions***

I was excited to try this clock radio. As stated above, it only works with iPhones and iPods that have the smaller connectors--it doesn't work with anything below the iPhone 5, or older iPods. I have an iPhone 4s, but fortunately I was able to test it with my daughter's iPhone 5.

Connection was fine, even with a case on the phone. Charged it really quickly and the sound was pretty much ok. (No, not the same as a pricey stereo system, but still adequate). Alarm feature worked well.

The only problem I had was with the time display. You can change the level of brightness, but even at the highest level, I couldn't read it at night. I'm nearsighted, and black numbers on a white background do nothing for me. To be fair, the device is located on the opposite side of the bed from where I sleep, but my previous clock radio had fluorescent green numbers which I could see quite easily with just a little squinting. I realize not everyone is nearsighted, but I thought I'd include this observation in my review.

The look of the clock is nothing special. You can see it's fairly cheap and not high-end.

Overall, it's not a bad buy, but I wouldn't say, \\"Wow! You must get this right away!\\"

product_title: UWaterG5 100% Waterproof Action MP3/FM Player
review_headline: Your Own Underwater Soundtrack is Here!
review_body:
Picture yourself in the middle of a brisk morning ocean swim, somewhere picturesque under the soft dawn sun where you are at one with the water. Then you think, “This could get better only if ‘Champagne Supernova’ by Oasis were playing right now.” Till now, the prospect of certain electrocution made that pretty much impossible, but no longer.

The UWater G5 MP3 Player/FM Tuner is a tiny, completely waterproof device that can stand depths up to 10 feet. The earbuds are specially crafted to keep water out and sound in. The device holds 4GB worth of music and pumps it out in either MP3 or WMA formats. Plus, you can switch to the FM radio and find out what’s in the Top 40 while whitewater rafting.

During my testing I was amazed at how much such a little device can change your whole experience of being in the water. Swimming back and forth in my pool with my own traveling soundtrack made the workout a ton more enjoyable and the earbuds stayed in place remarkably well. If they do come dislodged, the UWater G5 comes with a few pairs of different earbuds, one of which is specifically made for lap swimming, so you can give those a try.

The whole device is deceptively light at only 21 grams (plus the earbuds). My one big recommendation is it works best when you are wearing either goggles or a wetsuit of some kind to attach it to. There is a painfully secure clip on the back, so it will not come off accidentally. The cord is rather short, so you will need to attach it close to your head, which is why goggles, a swim cap or the strap of a helmet for those more extreme sports will do nicely.

The UWater G5 be set for normal play, shuffle play and FM tuner mode, which allows you to create a workout playlist or something more specific, like a sailing soundtrack. One piece of musical advice: Do not go eight to nine feet underwater and listen to “Don’t Fear the Reaper” by Blue Oyster Cult. Sets the completely wrong mood.

The UWater G5 is a simple, straightforward and powerful little device. It’ll change the way you look at getting in the water.>

The UPS doesn't power much for me, just the cable modem, router, and a few other things. I waited about an hour or so into the power outage before starting the generator to power the house and I had internet access the whole time which was expected. In summary I have two objectives. review_body: Paired the Teac AH01 with a set of Fluance SX6 and an old 8" Cambridge Audio sub and the sound is first rate, about 80% the performance of my living room system for 1/50 the price.  I'm using the optical out from my computer and the coax-digital from my Blu-Ray player to the AH01 and the sound that this combination puts out is really good, a great bargain. My idea of what sounds good is based on my living room system for serious listening sessions: it is composed of 3 different sets of speakers (KEF 103.3 Reference w/ cube, Rauna TYR, Magnepan 1.7), SAE X10-A amp or Harmon Kardon Citation XX amp, Schiit Modi DAC (optical), using only WAV or FLAC files from custom build Intel Xeon workstation, so this "cheap" system on my lanai with the Teac AH01 / Fluance SX6 / 8" sub is an outstanding value. Unpacked the little box, plugged the usb into the side of the TCL, one end into the cable box HDMI, and the other, larger, end of the U-vision cable into the TCL... \\"no signal\\". Check everything four times, different sources, different USB ports for power. \\"No signal\\" everywhere. I am hoping it is just a defective cable as when I tried my Macbook Pro's USB port, the computer said that it was shutting down my other USB ports because one (the one the U-vision was plugged into) was drawing too much power.

Amazon of course made the return simple and I am hoping to have a replacement cable this week. fingers crossed!

UPDATE 6/26:
Got the new cable today thanks to Amazon. Plugged it in, instantly worked, and my TCL 50\\" 4K TV flashed 1080P 60 when it was plugged into my Comcast cable box. Exactly what I was hoping for and everything looks better!

I will also try the cable with my Sony S6200 Blu-Ray player to see if the Marseille chip can enhance the already excellent Blu-Ray upsampling.

This is an easy purchase to recommend!

UPDATE 6/29:
Watched Avatar through the Sony S6200 with 4k upsampling turned on and a standard HDMI cable -- looked great! Then I switched the 4k upsampling off in the BD player and set the output to 1080p and used the U-Vision cable... a whole 'nutha level! I was actually getting distracted by the detail I was seeing as I watched the movie.That tells me that the Marseille chip does a better job of 4k upsampling then Sony's flagship BD player... Wow!

Great cable!

At a discharge rate of 380 mA, it took 137 minutes to reach 3.2 volts - a capacity of about 867 mAh. For comparison, they ran 16 minutes longer than the Trustfire 900 mAh, and 92 minutes longer than one of the generic '1200 mAh' cells.

Note that these are flat-top batteries, with no buttons and no solder tabs. Most of the negative reviews here seem to misunderstand what these batteries are and what they are for. They are NOT replacements for non-rechargeable alkaline or lithium batteries. They're not even what you would ordinarily consider a consumer item. For industrial and commercial applications, these are exactly what they claim to be, and they're the first I've tested to actually exceed their marked capacity. They might work in your consumer devices, but do your research first.

review_headline: Small speaker that is comfortable outdoors... it's weatherproof and can take some bumps
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:mo3M4MUJJBORYOT]]I've tested dozens of bluetooth speakers. This one is somewhat unique in that it is weatherproof and has a more ruggedized design that makes it suitable for camping, hiking maybe even kayaking and certainly it is comfortable around water. The speaker has a nifty plastic carabiner style clip at the top. This clip makes it easy to attach this to a backpack loop, belt loop or even a deck lashing cord on a Kayak.

The case of the speaker has a tire-like appearance and it is these rubber \\"treads\\" that help protect the speaker when it is being subjected to rough and tumble conditions.

The backside of the speaker is flat and smooth. Included with the speaker is a small double sided suction cup that you can stick to the back side of the speaker. This lets you use it in the shower, or to stick it to a window, or smooth surface.

Also included:
- USB to Micro USB charging cable
- 3.5mm male to male Aux cable

This speaker has a waterproof rating of IPX5. That rating indicates this is capable of withstanding blasts of water from all directions. What that means practically is that you can drop this in the water or get rained on and not worry... assuming the rubber flap that covers the USB port and Aux in is securely closed.

I've been able to play this speaker for nearly 12 hours as long as I don't have it going full blast. Charging takes less than 2 hours and is done by using the provided USB to Micro USB cable. You can have the speaker connected to USB power at the same time you are playing the speaker.

The controls are all arranged in a row along the right side of the speaker. The buttons all have emossed icons on them but it is quite difficult to see them. There is no text next to the buttons to indicate their function nor do the buttons themselves have any color on them to help you see their function. There are spearate volume and track buttons that I prefer over the dual function buttons that a lot of bluetooth speakers employ.

When you turn the speaker on there is a confirming beep but no such beep when you turn it off. I'm constantly wondering whether it is truly off or not. The only real proof that it is off is that the LED light (near the base of the carabiner clip) goes off, but that light is very small and I did not even see it until I looked very carefully. It's difficult to see in bright daylight.

The sound quality is quite nice. It lacks a bit in the lower end but otherwise is clear and balanced. It doesn't play that loud but certainly loud enough for personal use and for small area sound coverage. Perfect for hanging in a tent or on your patio.

Its small size makes it easy to throw in your suitcase or backpack or just clip to your belt loop.

One thing I find somewhat irritating is that I cannot simply stand this up and have it stay put. The round design does not have a flat spot for doing so. Therefore it tends to roll to one side or another until the carabiner hits the surface, then it stops rolling. Or you can lay it flat but then the sound is going straight up instead of out.

With a long play time, robust design and pleasing sound quality, this will please the outdoor enthusiast. I like it because I don't feel I have to baby it.

product_title: Sony MDR10RBT Bluetooth Wireless Headphones
review_body:
I second all the reviews that tout the sound quality, build quality, and comfort of these headphones. For someone who flies fairly often for work, these headphones have been the best \\"upgrade\\" to air travel that can be bought for under $200. Indeed, they are worth much more than their price for the following reasons.

1. They block out a substantial amount of engine noise and loud conversation.

2. They send a clear but not unfriendly message to neighbors that I'm not looking for conversation.

3. Therefore, they allow me to hear--and hence enjoy--the music, movie, or book that I'm listening to, or to nap in relative peace and quiet if I want to.

These headphones are heads and shoulders better than my comparably priced earbuds, which (1) did not block noise nearly as well; (2) were not as obvious to neighbors seeking conversation; and (3) did not produce sound as clear or beautiful as these (after a few hours of break-in).

Finally, while I'm sure that active noise-canceling headphones would do an even better job of canceling ambient noise, don't underestimate the convenience--especially in the cramped quarters of economy class--of not having wires that tangle, clutter, and get yanked out when you're shifting around in your seat. Trading wired active noise cancellation for wireless bluetooth is worth it, IMO.

P.S. The batteries have easily lasted a full day and a few hops around the country. Though I have not yet tried, I am optimistic that these headphones will last through a long international flight.

The sound quality is perfect. product_title: Wave® Multi-CD Changer - Platinum White
review_headline: No mode to play a single disc and then stop
review_body:
I was super excited to buy this changer. I had wanted it for years for my bedroom Bose Wave system.

But I was extremely disappointed to find out there's no way to play a single CD and then stop playing--except in shuffle mode. If you have more than one CD in the changer + main unit, it will play them forever. Not even all CDs and stop, but all CDs, forever.

So back in the box and back to Bose it goes. Buyer has to pay return shipping, which in my case was $16 for FedEx ground from Boston to South Carolina, where the unit ships from. Other reviews had mentioned this, but I didn't notice them.

This issue aside, it works ok. The changer has two AUX inputs, so you get more abilities to hook up external stuff, which is cool. The only other main negative is that changing CDs is very loud--gears grinding and things clicking. It sounds painful and it's stressful to hear--is this thing scratch up my CDs? Will my partner wake up while I try to decide between disc 2 and 3?

But if you want to listen to music forever, and don't want to listen to a single CD and then stop, it might be an OK buy.

They are a bit more comfortable than the 80's because of the bowls and they sound great on anything I use with a small portable dac. .

Many companies like Beats tend to focus on bass and highs but neglect the mids, but the SR225e delivers on all levels with a perfect balance of the three. Practically no noise reduction on any model, but that is intentional because it is part of the open air design that makes these headphones stand out from others. You just can't get the full open sound in NR headphones like you can with these.

Buy these headphones, you will absolutely not be disappointed. This version also has the 1/8 plug for modern portable devices as standard, and a more dense polycarbonate for better resonance.
