product_title: Audio-Technica Solid Bass In-Ear Headphones
review_body:
I will be comparing these IEM's to the Sony XB300 and the ATH M50's. Right now i own the XB300's but i have borrowed some m50's from a friend in the past.

My initial reaction towards these IEM's was a bit disappointed, but after some comparison i'm pretty happy with them.

Isolation - Better than the XB300 for sure. Maybe on par compared to the m50's.
Microphonics - Not that big of a problem for me.
Soundstage - I'd these have a better soundstage than the Xb300's but less than the M50's. But i was surprised of how good it was for the price i payed.
And personally I dont think they are uncomfortable.

Now for the good part, the sound

Highs - not bad. i really like the highs on here. Crisp and clear, but not over emphasized and no treble spikes. The highs are also better than the XB300, I'd say not as good as the M50's, but not that far away.

Mids - these are the reason why i like these so much. not the best mids in an IEM, thats for sure, but compared the XB's, these are amazing. Compared to the M50's these are not as good, but for the price, i actually like these alot and you'll see why in a bit.

Bass - Here is the part where i was both disappointed but amazed after some comparison. these IEM's have more mid bass than both the XB's and the m50's. But both the XB and the M50's have more sub bass. but here is the good part, the bass on the CKS55's is much cleaner and tighter than the XB300's and id say they are ABOUT on par with the m50's in the clarity department.
and ever after a bit of EQing these IEMs the can have more bass than the XB300's and still have more clarity, and the mids are not affected. Thats why i really like these headphones, they maintain clarity and even after EQing alot of bass (as a test) the mids are much easier to hear than the XB300.

Well these headphones are pretty sweet. Will probably be even better after burning them in.
They are now my newpreferred listening earphones. I love Audio-Technica.

**Update**
Just did a bit of editing and after about a week the earphones are still going strong. These IEM's are a great value for the money!

product_title: Fiio E07K Andes USB DAC and Portable Headphone Amplifier Black
review_headline: Not for loud audio or the bass junkie
review_body:
This review was written using a set of Audio Technica ATH-M50s.

This is a very nice amp overall, but I had an e11 before and I have to say the difference is noticeable, both in a good and bad way.
For me personally this product wasn't what I was looking for but I can see it's merits.
Pros:
-Noticeably crisp, refined audio
The E11 also enhanced audio but not as refined in my opinion. It's noticeable, but not by an overwhelming amount.
-LED screen with glass
-Dual output for headphones so two people can listen at once
-USB connection that acts as a conduit and allows you refine your COMPUTER'S audio as well as any portable device

Cons:
-Not as much audio control as the E11.
With the E11 you could make the slightest adjustment by turning your knob only a tiny bit. This product works in units of 2 and goes from -10 to +10, but unless you really like your audio to sound muddied down for some reason, you're really only gonna adjust in the positives.
-Not as loud
This is really going to be a subjective thing, but with the E-11 I maxed it out and controlled the volume with my ipod, which sat at about 75% volume with fantastic bass and loudness. With this I can turn it up to Max on both the E07K and the ipod, it doesn't reach the same volume or bass as the 75% mark when using the E-11.
-L3 not included/line in cable short
I wouldn't complain about this if the device had the same layout as the E-11 with the input and output ports being at the top. HOWEVER the output port is on the bottom and the included cable is way too short, so either the amp or your ipod will be upside down if you don't want to buy another accessory.
This is less of an issue of money (if you're dropping $80+ for a portable amp, you can't be that broke) and moreso one of inconvenience.
-Glass screen
While I don't necessarily think this is fragile, it seems a bit excessive to have this type of display thathas a chance to break when you can just have very functional knobs like the E11 with a rugged body.

So, all in all, if you want highly refined audio and don't want it too loud, with bass not being a terribly relevant matter, this is the product for you.
If you want something to pump out bass with pretty good audio refinement and great volume, the E11's are the way to go.

product_title: AmazonBasics Ultra Thin Indoor HDTV Antenna
review_body:
This works beautifully. Just plug in to your TV's cable connection and use the \\"scan channel\\" function on your TV to get the available channels in your area. As long as you're in a decent reception area this includes all broadcast channels such as ABC, CBS, NBC, Fox and PBS. They are also many other non-cable channels that are more off the beaten path, but, hey, they're free.

Make sure to try many, many different locations for channel scans. Just by moving over my antenna one foot I went from receiving 30 channels to over 60+ channels. The manual is right when it says the antenna's reception is very sensitive. Great product.

product_title: BDI Vista 9950, Flat Panel TV Stand
review_body: The problem with permanent wall mounts for flat-screen TVs are that they are permanent. Husbands, has your wife EVER NOT wanted to re-arrange a room?  The quickest way to trigger a desire to move things around is to sink four huge bolts through the drywall and into the studs.  This stand is so beautifully made it is a piece of furniture in its own right.  It is so well made I bought two.  It is remarkably easy to put together, and comes with many sizes bolts for different TVs, although because it has to be heavier than the TV attached to it, you'll want two people to move the box and set things up.  The oval base is very heavy, and the main part of the stand could support a small bridge.  My only objection is regarding the photograph used to sell the stand: the grey panels on either side of the TV are NOT part of the stand (speakers I would guess). There is no adjustment for facing the TV up or down, but I find the height perfect and don't miss that feature. When everything is put together it is VERY stable, attractive, and modern looking.  And when the wife says, "You know..." just have her grab one side and you the other and move it to the inevitable new location.

product_title: MTX Audio IX1 StreetAudio On Ear Acoustic Monitors
review_body:
This headphone are awesome! I do not usually post review up because either the products I buy are average and do not really meet my expectation. These headphone only get 4 stars because they are a little tight and may not fit well on a larger head. Audio quality gets 5 stars from me!

First is the sound quality of these headphone are one of the best I had heard. I owned the monsters inspiration noise cancellation headphones, vmoda m100, sony mdrx10, custom one pro and the value of these tops. I'm a bass head and usually like headphone with bass so that is my man priority, but not over boated bass. I hated the custom one pros, I had high expectation for these since review was so good but with an ipod to run these; they are just horrible, the worst headphone I bought out of the one I listed. The monster's bass is not very good when you have the volume very high as the sony mdrx10. The vmoda m100 have very good bass but the mxt have better bass. The bass on these headphone are punchy, tight, and the best part, it does not distort even at max volume. The mids are very good on these headphone but not as clear has the vmoda, but much better than the monsters and sony. Now since these headphone are made by mtx which is a car audio specialist, the highs on these have very good but not clear like the vmoda. The mxt have this great tweeter sound like if you were to add tweeter in your car audio. In high volume you can really distinct the sound, also it doesnt distort at high volume so you get great sound quality. If you are into car audio and looking to get almost the same audio quality in headphones these are for you.

The build quality are these are really good. The cushion are really soft and the design seems to be sturdy. The downside to these headphones are that they are a bit on the smaller side. I have a medium side head and I have to extend them all the way to fit my head. So if you have a big head these may not fit too well. The clamp force on these are a little tight and they are made that way to block out noise and provide best audio quality. After wearing them for an hour, I have to take these of because they are kind of tight. What i did was use the box it came in and stretched it for 24hrs and now the feel is much better and now I can wear them for a much longer period of time.

These headphone are great for people looking for a headphone dub steps, hip pop, pop, rock , rap. The tweeters and bass makes this headphone shine. I preferred these over the vmoda m100 because they provide better bass the monster, vmoda, sony, and better tweeters response the the rest. Trust me these headphone are have some crazy audio quality that you will like especially if you are a car audio enthusiast. Also these headphone are $200 which is a much better price than the vmoda that provide the same quality in some aspect. The vmoda are some good headphones but they are a bit pricey and these mxt are just as good at a lower cost. I have been looking for a good headphone for a while and the mxt provide the best audio quality on a $200 budget.

These headphone are really good!! Trust me!! Best headphone for bass around $200!!

product_title: Mohu Jolt
review_headline: Have not found the best amp yet, but this one is very good!
review_body:
I have tries several store purchased amps such as the RCA and Phillips amps, TWC amp, the Terk amp and now the Mohu Jolt Amp. Out of all of them, the Jolt is very nice for the money. None of the others could use a USB slot for power. On the TWC amp I had to use coax for a power cable. Different. Anyhow, I hooked up my Mohu Leaf antenna and got a lot of stations but a few were very pixelated. I plugged in the Jolt in to the USB slot on my TV and I got almost all the stations that I couldn't get before. I liked it. At that point I got an idea. I like to play with stuff to see if I can get things better so I tried the TWC TV amp that was already in line from my cable TV hook up while at the same time I had the Jolt amp attached to the back of my TV. Wow! I got all the stations in my area with the exception of Qubo and ION TV witch are the farthest from my house. I know of know one in my area that can get those two TV station. I know of three other cord cutters within a 5 block area of my apartment. I think I am doing very good now with the two amps in series. Just though someone my want to know just in case anyone else may want to try. Worked for me but I can't guarantee it for you though.
***One other note. Others have stated in the reviews that they wish that the Jolt had a LED on them to see if they were on or off. I can say that on my Jolt, when I plug it in and you look down around the edges of the USB slot on the Jolt, I could see a blue LED inside. Good enough for me. Hope this review helps someone.

product_title: Klipsch S4-II
review_headline: Failed after 4 months of very careful use..
review_body:
Wow, what a shame to see a product with such potential go down the toilet. I've been using the S4's for a few years now because they sound so great and stay put in my ears when I'm jogging. These are the newer version 2's which from what I can tell the only difference to the old ones is they use a flat linguine type of cord instead of the old fashioned rounded ones. Huge mistake. The older S4's would last me 6-8 months on average with daily use (I live in NYC and have them in pretty much any time I'm out and about). I was so attached to them that I'd suck it up and buy another pair once the old ones failed - it was always the same spot/issue: the area of the cord goes into the plug would die out after being bent too much.

The last time I re-bought I was unaware of the redesign with the new cord until I took them out of the package. I was skeptical of the flat cord crapping out even quicker because it's flat which makes it even weaker at the aforementioned point of entry into the plug at the end. I bought them in August and sure enough after not even 4 months of use I had to strategically bend the cord at the jack to make the broken wires inside connect to one another. So incredibly annoying.

Bad move on your part, Klipsch. These buds are so awesome otherwise. I really want to keep using them but it's time to move on. Stay away from these unless you keep the input plug straight at all times and baby it, and/or want to keep on shelling out $ for a new pair more often than you really should. If you put your device in your pocket like I do it's only a matter of time before the wear and tear where the cord/plug meet gives in. Consider yourselves warned!

product_title: Logitech Harmony Smart Control with Smartphone
review_headline: Overall a great solution to replace multiple remotes
review_body:
I purchased this remote to consolidate tv/dvr, Apple TV, and ps3 remotes:

Pros:
Setup was fairly easy. If you have a dual band router, the harmony hub might have trouble initially finding the wireless network. I recommend connecting the router to a desktop/laptop for initial setup and using the tablet/smartphone app after initial setup.

The remote is highly customizable and while I don't use the app all that much, it does allow you the option of using your tablet or phone as the primary remote or as a replacement remote for individual devices.

Cons:

At the end of the initial setup with a desktop/laptop, the Logitech website attempts to install a software which most antivirus programs will block as spyware/malware. I cannot access the my harmony website to customize the remote without installing, which I won't. Do your own research before downloading the software as some blogs have identified the software as a type of keystroke logger. Logitech says it is safe, but since I don't have to use it I chose to block the software and make modifications using my tablet or phone.

Sometimes the remote and devices can get out of sync. For example the tv turns on but the cable receiver doesn't cycle on. If you hit the off button to turn everything off, it will turn the tv off, but then turn the cable box on. This is rare, but all devices need to be off before starting an activity and you need to remember to push an activity button only once and let all devices cycle on before trying to push the button again, otherwise you might turn your tv off before the cable box comes on, or vice versa.

Overall, a great remote. I dinged it a star for the spyware/ malware.

The Bose QC15 are much better. They sound much better and the white noise made by them is almost non-existent. For the same price and made by the same company, I would recommend trying out the QC15's before these.

product_title: RCA RTS735E Home Theater Sound Bar
review_body:
I own an old '95 Sharp TV that has always had poor sound quality. The Best Buy salesperson warned me it wouldn't sound good with out a surround sound system that I couldn't afford at the time. I have partial hearing loss in one ear that has increasingly made it difficult to understand dialogue even when the sound is obviously loud to me. I don't watch TV often enough to justify upgrading to a flat screen or HDMI until this TV dies. So, I set out to find one simple speaker that would work to keep the sound at a bearable range and still understand the dialogue. I read all of the reviews and product info on this and it didn't explain enough, so I decided to buy and if it didn't work, I'd return it. I received it today and am so very pleased I took the chance. It works absolutely beautiful! I can understand every word and the sound isn't blaring the roof off the house.

What you need to know if you questioned what I did ... yes, it will work with an older model TV as long as you have an audio out jack. Yes, it includes the audio cables that connect from the unit to the TV. Yes, this is all you need, you do not have to buy an additional speaker. Yes, the adapter is in the box, but somewhat hidden, encased inside one of the foam packing inserts. And yes, all you need to do is plug it in, turn it on and adjust the volume on the unit or by using the included remote that yes, comes with batteries. I have no idea how to fine tune it with the remote as others have noted, but I "hear" no reason to. I'm happy!

Profound improvement of the bass. Gives the Apple EarPods the low end they are otherwise missing. A little too heavy for me but I'm in a distinct minority regarding my preference for modest bass. I think most people will find the result perfect. The rest of the EarPod's spectral response is already pretty good and these preserve that. I found that breaking the ear canal seal just a bit moderates that bass into a range more comfortable for me.

They are a bit difficult to get on the buds but you won't be taking them off again and the tight fit makes for a good seal and security. They won't be coming off by themselves.

The ear canal fit is plenty comfortable and will make the EarPods very suitable for exercise and running.

These transform the EarPods from passable to quite good. They might even move the EarPod knockoff clones from awful to passable.

product_title: Crosley CR3010A-BK iDuet Radio (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: What Good is a Clock Radio that Doesn't Have a Lighted Clock?
review_body:
As someone looking for a compact retro clock radio with an ipod dock, this item from Crosley seemed to be the real deal - It's got a wooden case (when's the last time you've seen a new clock radio with a wooden case?), it sounds great with a rich deep sound, the retro clock and AM/FM look great - what's not to like?

Well turns out that this unit has a fatal flaw that makes it almost useless as a clock radio - there is no light on the clock, so you can't see it at night! I couldn't believe in this day and age that a company would sell an alarm clock without a lighted dial, so I shined a bright light on the dial for a few hours and discovered that the hour and minute hands DO have a tiny glow-in-the-dark area towards the end of the hands, but even with the glow-in-the-dark area, you couldn't see the clock hands at night. I tried shining lights on it for hours, I left the unit sitting in the sun for hours, but no matter what I did, the clock dial is dark at night.

There is so much to like about this radio that I am very disappointed that you can't see the clock, rendering the unit useless as an alarm clock.

Pros:
Beautiful and solid real wood case
Great retro design
AM/FM dial radio
Deep and beautiful sound
Fits a wide range of 30-pin apple devices
Small footprint

Cons:
The clock cannot be seen in the dark
It only has a 12-hour alarm, so you set the alarm for 6 o'clock, it will go off at 6am AND 6pm
The antenna is one of the old telescoping metal units that means you have a two foot antenna sticking up on your bedside table

product_title: Audio-Technica Audiophile Closed-Back Dynamic Headphones
review_body:
The wings that hold these headphones in place are not strong enough. Within a few seconds, the headphones slide down under their own weight, and they continue to slide when I move my head. The ear pads, and the weight of the phones end up resting on the tops of my ears. I don't feel like there's a good seal between my head and the ear pads, and the sound suffers. I had hoped to use these at my desk during work, but I think they'd drive me crazy.

In terms of hats,... I have a big head. In Little League, there was only one helmet that fit me. If I wear an adjustable cap, I have to go to the largest setting.

I searched for tips to reduce the slide of these headphones. I found comments from people who say they have big heads and that these headphones stay in place just fine. So, maybe those people have *really* big heads, and I've misjudged my own circumference. Or maybe it's just my pair of ATH-A900X headphones.

In any case, I have to return these. I'm not usually a fickle shopper, nor am I a review writer. For the price I paid for these headphones, I should feel better about the fit, and I think I should warn other shoppers. If you're trying to decide between A900X and another model, maybe try the other one.

On a positive note, when I hold the headphones in place, they sound excellent. Also, they look cool in a classic sense. They're not over-stylized like so many headphones on the market.

product_title: BlueRigger High Speed HDMI Cable with Ethernet, Supports 3D and Audio Return (3 Feet)
review_headline: Preimum cable for a value price: (UPDATED)
review_body:
I love the BlueRigger HDMI cables I've gotten. They work great. The construction and even the packaging make them feel high end. The cable connectors are well made and I expect they will last through many plug-unplug cycles. The cable has a heavy protective cover and nice blue accents on the connectors. It's very attractive for a cable!

It supports Ethernet and Audio Return plus 3D which I don't use. I like this because of the \\"future proofing\\" it provides when I add or update my gear.

This is not my first BlueRigger cable and the others have been excellent. Thus here I am again and this HDMI cable does not disappoint.

The only very minor issue I had with one of these cables was connecting a HDMI output on a video card to a TV. The heavy plastic around the connector was a tight fit where the plug was on the computer. To be fair the plate the plug was in was slightly recessed which seems the root of the issue.

For making a product that is of premium quality at a bargain price I give the BlueRigger HDMI cable 5 stars.

Update: February 26, 2014
I had one of my cables get bent. Not the cable, the metal part of the connector. About 30 degrees off straight and the cable stopped working. This was damage that was related to an accident with a component taking a fall so while I hoped the cable might survive such an incident I can't say the problem was a cable defect.

After this happened I took a deep breath and sent an email off to BlueRigger explaining what happened with my nearly 1 year old cable. They responded promptly saying no problems and letting me know I should have a replacement in 3 to 5 days. I was very pleased with their outstanding service!

When you have a product that operates perfectly you learn the product is well made. When something goes wrong you learn about the integrity of the company. BlueRigger made me a very loyal customer with this simple replacement of an inexpensive item. Well Done BlueRigger!item. Well Done BlueRigger!

product_title: Call Recorder/Software, plugs into MIC
review_headline: Just what I've been looking for
review_body:
I've been looking for a way to record phone calls -- for interviews and for other projects. I had an old Radio Shack adapter, but it had a horrible hum that drowned out the audio. Solutions for under $20 are not worth the price -- you get what you pay for.

I narrowed down my choice to the JK Audio QT Quicktap and this Digital Loggers adapter. I decided to go with the Digital Loggers because it can plug in-line or into the headset; Quicktap only says it works via the headset. Digital Loggers also has a USB version of this device, but they said they only support Windows. The Mic version is platform independent. (I'm using it with a Linux system. It also works well with Mac.)

In the box is the adapter, some cables, and a 3" mini-CD with software. I haven't tried the software since none of my computers support mini 3" disks.

I have the tap between the wall and the phone. The Mic jack is a nice, long cable and goes right into my computer's Mic-In. Recording is painless.

There is an 8kHz hum. It is extremely narrow band. However, recorded voice over the telephone is at 6kHz max, so a low-pass filter at 7kHz completely removes the hum. The other option (which I am currently using) is to record at a lower sampling rate. 16,000 samples per second omits all of the hum and has a crisp, clear recording. (At a 16kHz sample rate, the spectrograph shows a very narrow-band 4.1kHz hum, but my ear doesn't hear it.)

It is very easy to hear both sides of the conversation. The volume slider it good for boosting the mic input audio signal. The one thing to watch out for: I sometimes get "quiet callers" -- you know, those people who sound like they are whispering and even if you crank up the volume on your headset all the way, they are still very quiet... If they are quiet on the phone, then they will be quiet on the microphone jack. There are other phone taps that permit per-side volume adjustments, but this device doesn't do that.

product_title: APC BG500 APC Back-UPS Pro 500
review_body:
After sad experience, I have learned that a battery backup is a must for computers. Basically, this will provide you with a short amount of time, after the power goes out, to safely shut down the computer. Nicer models, like this one, include a way to communicate with your computer that the power has gone out. When the computer gets that signal, it will shut down safely. This can save you so many headaches.

Even if you have a standby generator, which would mean you power is only down for 90 seconds, this is a vital piece in the equation. It allows your computer to stay on until the generator starts up.

The only downside to this is it isn't meant to power everything indefinitely. You should only plan to power your most critical components. You would be surprised how quickly the power can drain out of the battery if you plug everything into it.

That said, I have been using this and have been completely impressed. Irronically, two weeks after getting it, the power went out. I had set up my computer to shut down after 3 minutes. It safely shut everything down with no data loss.

This is completely unnecessary for laptops.

Yes $200 may not be feasible for everyone, or necessary for every computer. But if your computer has critical data, then the money spent on this is better then the potential of time and data loss.

If they are installed in a closed-back environment, you will get much better response on the low end. However, you shouldn't expect to get resonating lows out of these speakers no matter how you install them. If you need a quality sound distribution, be sure to augment these speakers with a small sub or pair of larger speakers elsewhere.

Our speakers are installed in a dining room ceiling. We use them almost exclusively during mealtimes and only then to play light background music for eating. (Because, seriously, who wants to hear the sounds of people chomping) For this application, having the speakers biased towards the highs is not a problem since the volume and types of music being played don't benefit much from low-end power.

I have been an Etymotic fan for quite some time, and having their top of the line (at the time) ear phones showed me a level of sound quality that I didn't even know I was missing! When I saw these, I had to try them....but let me give you a little more background before I start my review.

Two years ago I completed my treatment for stage 4 oropharyngeal cancer which included some pretty intense chemo and radiation. Unfortunately, my left ear was directly within the field of radiation. I have quite a bit of hearing loss from my left ear, and the chemo apparently did some extra to both. I cannot hear anything but muttering in a crowded, loud restaurant, and even at home with the television on and the kids talking, it is hard for me to make out individual sounds. I have not gone for a hearing aid as they are quite expensive, and I am getting good at reading lips.

With that said, I will tell you that the BEAN works. It does amplify sound, and to a point it might be clarifying it as well. However, I there are a few things that I do not like. First, there is no volume control and only two levels. The softer level is a little too soft and the louder level is way too loud. I found myself switching back and forth often. Switching is easy if you have finger nails, but if not it is quite a challenge. There is also no on/off switch. The only way to shut it off is by opening the battery compartment (and then the battery falls out....and these things are tiny and easy to lose). Etymotic should have put a switch to shut it off. Battery life is rated for two days if you do not \\"turn it off,\\" and two weeks if you do (doesn't seem that great).

There is quite a lot of feedback until you get the right in-ear piece. For me, there wasn't any that fit just right except for the ball shaped piece, and even then, they kind of stuck out (which looked a little obvious and a little silly). I often had to adjust it to try to get a better sound or stop the feedback. You really have to push these in, and when you do, the feedback pretty much goes away unless you move it or it gets loose. I did not expect to \\"hear\\" myself walking the way I did. I do not know how to describe it, but whenever I walked, I could hear it, and you would think a giant was walking...it is almost like I could feel it. I don't know how comfortable I would be taking these to party our out of the house. My ears started to hurt after an hour, and I remember the same problem with my other Etymotics....but that was for music, and I rarely had them on for that long.

While the sound was amplified, it was also a little hollow sounding. There was no echo, but it just seemed like I was in a tunnel.... Hollow is the best way I can describe it. With them in place, I am now able to tell where sound is coming from more accurately. I have gotten very good at reading lips in the last couple of years and I didn't realize how much I counted on it, until I put these in. I am going to continue trying them out, at least at home, and in short bursts and see if my ear will acclimate and become comfortable. There are several different sized ear inserts, but nothing was just right for me. The problem, I think is that along with different sizes are different types. I think I would have liked to see more size options versus different types.

One thing to be careful of is when you remove them....DO NOT pull them out. There is quite a bit of suction created and it will hurt and might even damage your eardrum if you pull it out very quickly. Gently twist and while twisting SLOWLY remove it. It does come with spare filters and a packet of batteries (batteries are difficult to put in and take out, but there is a tool to help pop them out), as well as a nice storage case.

If you are losing (or lost some of) your hearing, and cannot afford to spend thousands on hearing aids, etc., this might be enough to get you by, but won't win any fashion show thoughyou will certainly hear more. I should also note the discomfort I felt was in both ears, not just the side that was radiated. My situation might also be more unique. I would give it 3.5 stars, because of the negatives I mentioned.you will certainly hear more. I should also note the discomfort I felt was in both ears, not just the side that was radiated. My situation might also be more unique. I would give it 3.5 stars, because of the negatives I mentioned.

product_title: XBOOM XBOOM-IB Mini Portable Capsule Speaker with Rechargeable Battery, Enhanced Bass and Resonator (Black)
review_body:
My laptop has a horrible set of speakers. Which is a shame because it's where I watch all my DVDs. So a little portable speaker was just what I was looking for. And I'm very pleased that it worked well.

Compact, it comes in the box as a small red ball. But with a simple twist it pops up into an accordian shaped speaker and can be re-twisted back to its original shape for storage. There is a small permanent (don't worry, it has a handy little area it clips into at the bottom of the unit for storage) 3.5mm input/output cable that plugs into most electronics (laptop, phone, Ipod, etc.) and a detachable charger that has a USB and 3.5mm input/output plug. There's an on and off switch on the bottom and an audio port so you can hook it up to multiple speakers using what they call the "Buddy Plug" function. And of course there's the volume dial, also on the bottom of the speaker. It also comes with a little cloth pouch to store the speaker in when not in use.

Personally I just keep it attached to my laptop though. It stays charged this way (there is a LCD light that shows Blue for fully charged and Red for not charged). I turn it up and while it isn't as loud as cranking a TV up to full blast it gets loud enough that I can hear my shows clearly from across the room. The audio is clear, none of that fuzziness when you get to the loudest setting. Although it does have to be open for it to get the best sound clarity, but that's the way it is designed and I can't think of why you'd try to use it closed anyway. It doesn't shake the walls with how loud it gets, but it's definitely loud enough to enjoy. Like I said before, this has been permanently attached to my laptop since I got it and I use it instead of the laptop's speakers now. It's very handy.

I also love the deep shiny red color. The unit can actually come in a multitude of colors so you can mix and match or color code according to your gadgets. While not pertinent to sound quality, it does mean you can match your decor if you are so inclined.

This is a nice little speaker. Perfect for any device you have that just needs that added sound boost. I would definitely consider purchasing this speaker if I needed another one.

product_title: V-MODA Crossfade M-100 Over-Ear Noise-Isolating Metal Headphone
review_body:
There are few things that differentiate a very good product from a great product. I purchased this V-Moda Crossfade M-100 for my brother's birthday, who lives in India, from V-Moda's website. This headphone turned out to be out of the world and far far better than any other large scale consumer headphones available in market today. This product is truly a great product but with a twist. A great product is not great until the user has a chance to experience it. Just by making the best sounding headphone it does not become a great product....it has to reach the end user as well. And that's exactly the challenge now for V-Moda as a company for its shipping process...internationally specially when shipping to India or similar sub-continental countries. V-moda's website offers 3 types of shipping.

1. regular shipping w/o tracking by USPS :$20
2. USPS shipping with tracking $40 (10 business days delivery) and
3. UPS shipping :$100 (5-6 business days )

Naturally we went for option 2 but this journey will take us to an uncharted territory. After 10 days were over we still haven't got the product in India. On top of that tracking showed customs had charged a huge duty since they evaluated this as a high value goods and then send to local Postal office for delivery. Local PO upon seeing this never delivered this product and marked as "absent during delivery" meaning the receiver not present at home and now they can auction it within their staff and whoever wants to pay the customs duty can now buy the product while the actual customer is waiting for delivery. This kind of internal gangs are going on within the Indian postal department without the knowledge of V-Moda or the customer. My brother then started searching the product from PO to PO going door to door to every postal office within 10 miles of home looking for the product. After searching for whole day and using secret reporters he finally landed onto the PO who were stealing international high value goods. But the PO employees would deny that any such product with the tracking number is there in their office. After arguing back and forth for more than 2 hours and physically searching the place he finally was able to find it. this is how we came to know that it was marked "absent" which was clearly not the case. this kind of activity is going on....

you must be thinking why I am writing these things under review when this is beyond the scope of v-moda in a foreign country. well the thing is like I said before a great product is not great just by making it but it has to reach the customer. V-moda must insure products when shipping to india or similar places or only ship by UPS courier or FedEx/DHL and never by USPS which finally gets handed over to local foreign PO. India is a big consumer in today's world and V-moda should make efforts towards reducing shipping charges towards sending by express courier. Instead of charging $100 for that they can negotiate a better rate from those providers and only ship by that means. I have also researched that found that stealing of high value goods are not uncommon in India Post and other similar countries and I want to make sure any user who wants to buy this product in India to be aware of this and the fact that he/she may never get the product if mailed by regular mail even with tracking. And also for V-moda is that to remain a customer for life the product is unquestionably the best in class and best in market but if it does not reach the customer what good does it do.

product_title: uxcell Series 3.7V Flat Tip Battery Holder Case for 3 x 18650 Batteries
review_body: I bought these to facilitate a more rapid battery change for a project I'm on.  The current system has a 3 Lithium Ion 18650 Battery system that when discharged must be recharged before use again.  The battery system cost $450.  I decided to modify the system by creating a external battery source.  That's where these battery holders come into play.  I verified that the holder is a series holder and I'm getting 12 volts.  I will permanently mount two of these inside a small case and wire the two in parallel.  When the lid is closed it will hold the batteries in place.  This will more than double the current capacity.  When the batteries get low on charge I can just open the lid and change out the batteries on the spot.  The lack of 5 stars was because a piece of plastic had broken off during packaging or shipping.  Also the wires seem too small for a three battery system.  If I required a higher current delivery then they would surely be inadequate.  The wires are probably AWG 28 and maybe even lower at AWG 32.  There is enough room to replace them to a larger gauge which I will do.

I’ve had this radio for several years now and it operates no less than 3 hours every single day. I still love it, but the volume control has been a little flaky on it for some time. I decided to replace this rotary encoder myself and was going to source an equivalent part from Digikey or Mouser. But for the heck of it, I sent an email off to Grace Digital Customer Support, hopefully to get a part number to make my job easier. Within a day, a woman named Sarah got back to me and had the factory original part shipped out to me. THIS IS NOT A TRIVIAL REPAIR, but I have an electronics manufacturing facility at my disposal and the experience to do the job myself. The takeaway from this update is that Grace Digital has exceptional customer support, even after the product is out of warranty. I can’t say enough for the company or the product I have.

Original Review:
What an awesome product. Nice warm sound that I didn't really expect from a single speaker. The battery pack is a little pricey, but totally worth it. I take this all over the property, whether it's the bathroom, garage, workshop, kitchen, bedroom, etc. The features this radio has is very impressive. I used to keep old boom boxes spread around the property. However, due to a radio station on this side of town, I had trouble tuning in the stations I wanted. No longer an issue with this product. Pandora is awesome as well if I'm just looking for music. I've got 5 boom boxes to take to Goodwill now and the house looks better without them scattered around. I really recommend the battery pack. Turning off the display when not active will provide you a portable player that will last all day. I rarely treat myself to toys, but this was well worth the money. I've read people having connectivity problems, but I put a little extra into my network and kind of splurged on a really nice Asus router last year and have no problems. I can carry this off my property and still connect.ct.

review_headline: This is a magical compact digital TV antenna. I have three of them installed in my attic, one for each of my TVs.
review_body:

Two of them go directly to flat-screen HDTVs and one goes to a Zenith Digital Receiver connected to an old (but very good) Sony projection TV via one of it's component video inputs. All three provide more stations than I ever expected.
All TVs get the same channel set, 50 channels of perfect HDTV, including all the major networks. I live in zip code 33433, and point the antennae toward Miami.
The mounts are excellent. They are very sturdy and mount nicely to any vertical brace in an attic. I have two mounts on the same vertical. One on each side, placing the antennae side-by-side at the peak of the attic. One is upside-down, but it makes no difference.
There is little to put together and the antenna is compact, making it easy to manage in an attic.
My cable contract has been terminated, which more than pays for 3 RCA ANT751s in two months. I would give this product six stars if I could.

review_body:

To narrow down the problem (laptop vs adaptor), I connected the laptop to my other Sumsung monitor. The image was different, but not any better. The screen displayed thick pink horizontal lines, flickering and also low res. So, it's definitely the adaptor's fault. To double-check, I connected laptop using my other microHDMI to HDMI cable (from Mediabridge) to Samsung TV. The image was perfect.

I never used Accell products before and will never buy them again, since they can't make even a simple piece of hardware work reliably. I will try next MediaBridge adapter.

product_title: Philips HTS3306/F7 Home Theater (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Great audio quality hampered by clunky menus, limited feature support, poor design choices, and laggy audio
review_body:
I have owned this home theatre system for several years. It was easy enough to setup and install, with color coded plugs for each speaker and plenty of length. The audio quality is great and volume is excellent -- I've never had to turn it up above 25 (and it goes much higher). The 1000w amp is a workhorse and the speakers and sub channel output lots of sound with no distortion, even at high levels. This IS a wall-shaking, window-rattling system. The available audio equalizer presets and surround modes are also useful and work well. Unfortunately, there is no support for optical audio input (coax digital only -- weird), so I had to buy a separate digital coax to optical converter to output audio from my TV (and now my Xbox One) to my HTS. One final comment on the speakers -- the color coded plugs for the speakers aren't standard 1/8" jacks nor are they bare two-wire speaker cable to wire up to the receiver. They use what seems to be a proprietary square plug which is convenient for setting up this system but if one were to attempt to upgrade to a new receiver, they might find themselves having to do a little bit of wiring work cutting off these special plugs and/or replacing them, or otherwise also have to replace the speakers -- certainly a pain if you've installed wire-guides around your living room but not out of the realm of reason if one were to opt for another home theater-in-a-box.

Despite the awesome sound quality for such a low priced system, there are a number of other problems I have had since I purchased it that prevent me from giving it a higher rating. The menus are unresponsive and clunky. When I press the arrow on the remote, it takes a moment for the menu selection to change on the screen. This lack of responsiveness is also present in many of the "Smart" features of the device, leading to slow performance in the Netflix, Pandora, and VUDU apps (I haven't used any others but I'm sure they suffer from the same issues). If you've got other "Smart" devices or set-top boxes, you may want to stick with those for your streaming services.

Setup and configuration menus for many of the system's settings take place in a dedicated menu which must be accessed through the HTS/BD player video. Unfortunately, this means you need an HDMI connection just to change settings other than audio input source, surround mode, and audio EQ presets, even if you never intend on watching a Blu Ray -- a constant problem for me, as I use this system only as a dedicated home theater audio system. There is also no HDMI passthrough with screen overlay (shouldn't this feature be standard by now?), which means it occupies an HDMI slot on your TV just for Blu Ray playback and settings changes. Random thing: the system takes several seconds (up to 30) to power cycle from on, to off, back to on. I don't know why. In the menu, there is an option to turn on "Quick Start" which makes turning the receiver on or off instant. Why this isn't the default setting, and why they didn't choose to just have the one option, is a mystery to me. Of course, this wouldn't really be a problem except for the single largest flaw in the system: the audio delay.

Yes, the dreaded audio delay -- the home theater junkie's worst nightmare. Watching anything with audio going through the digital coax connection,results in a horrible delay in audio, causing every person on screen to have a terrible lip-sync effect. I mentioned my converter earlier in my review but I assure you it is not the issue, as even when using a straight digital coax to digital coax connection (through my old TV) the delay is present. When you first turn on the device it's not apparent, but it seems the DSP's are laggy and introduce an unnoticeable-to-the-ear slowdown to the audio stream, because as time goes on the delay gets worse and worse until the receiver is power cycled. Philips' "solution" is to go intothe settings of the HTS to adjust speaker distance. This corrects strange audio delays due to poorly positioned speakers but does nothing for the "lost time" audio delay experienced just by using the system for regular intervals. The only real fix is to power cycle the system, which as I mentioned above is time consuming (up to 30 seconds) unless you first went in and enabled the "Quick Start" option.

Bottom line: if you can afford a few more bucks for an equivalent 1000w home theatre in a box setup, go for it, especially if you've got BluRay and streaming choices elsewhere.

product_title: Logitech Harmony Smart Control with Smartphone
review_headline: Thought it broke after 1.5 months. Awesome product, good replacement for my Logitech 890 remote which had RF.

----------------------
BACKGROUND: I owned the Logitech 890 RF remote for 5.5 years but everybody throws it around on the ground so now the channel button sometimes goes up or down 2 even though I only pressed it once. So, I bought the Logitech Smart Control as the new replacement.
My equipments are SONY tv, SONY DVD/VHS player, Denon 1912 receiver, SONY PS3, XBOX 360.

PROS:
- android app is fast and I can pause the DVR box while the kids are watching tv to get them to listen to me. (I have a Samsung Stratosphere II smartphone, ASUS RT-N66U router that is 70 feet away upstairs)
- RF to go around corners/through walls

CONS:
- only 1 IR blaster included instead of 2.
- took several tries to find the hub, it finally synched.
- doesn't have COX Cable LIST command in the database so I had to teach it (took 3 tries). Also, there's no physical button for the LIST command so I had to program the blue button to be the LIST command... Geez, the LIST command should be its own button...
- uses small CR2032 battery (looks like a nickel coin) and the battery that came with it was dead, I would have preferred a rechargeable battery and docking base like my old Logitech 890.
- only has 3 activity buttons, could use 2 more
- Smartphone app is not as easy to select the buttons as the remote because the buttons are spread across several screens and I have to scroll to them.
- I can't set the volume button long press to tell my Denon receiver to continuously lower the volume. So, I have to press volume several times to lower the volume to what I want.
- There's no screen so when the remote is out of sync with a device, it cannot ask you questions about a device.

product_title: Onkyo TX-8020 Stereo Receiver
review_headline: Does what it's supposed to do
review_body:
If you're in the market for a no-frills, straight up, 2-channel receiver that can drive some relatively efficient speakers, the TX-8020 might be just the thing.

The good:
- most everything is straightforward and easy to decipher; connections are a snap
- 50 watts per channel is enough juice to drive speakers that will fill a small to mid-size room with reasonable volume levels
- enough inputs for the unit's target market
- sound quality is excellent
- receiver reception appears to be very good
- easy-to-use remote
- relatively inexpensive

The "nits":
- The descriptions for the wee little buttons for speaker selection, tone control bypass, etc. are hard to read
- heck, those wee little buttons themselves can be hard to see
- Odd base on the binding posts makes bare-wire speaker connections tricky (banana plugs are a snap)
- movement of volume control not proportional to increase in sound volume; it works fine... it's just... weird.... kind of
like how a CVT car transmission seems weird after driving a geared transmission for 40+ years

Though it's difficult to describe, the TX-8020 produces a subtly different sound than the Technics unit it replaced: the sound is "rounder" - high frequencies are not quite so "brassy"; inner voices (musical) are more distinct; radio reception has a much "punchier" bass - a bit more than I care for, but that's just me. There is no noticeable (to my ears, at the volume levels at which I listen) distortion. Overall, it's a very nice, easy-to-live-with sound.

One of the other reviewers commented about the amount of turning of the volume control that is needed to increase the sound level. I's true. But while it does feel a little odd to make full rotations of the volume control to gain minor increases in sound level, the TX-8020 gets just as loud as the similarly powered Technics it replaced. There are no digital inputs or outputs on this unit. It's "old school"; folks who are looking for HDMI, optical, or other connections will want a different unit. An a/v receiver this is not.

review_headline: Above average multiband radio and a great value
review_body:
All of what has been said in Amazon reviews by experienced users and third party sites is correct about the PL-380. There are three main points to consider before purchasing this radio, one of which is an improvement I haven’t seen mentioned here yet or I overlooked. Otherwise, we’re all aware of what you’re getting in this feature packed radio. Just read the description
.
1 - The Tecsun PL-380 is virtually deaf on LW
2 - AM sensitivity is mediocre but improves from 900 kHz on up. Using a passive loop remedies this.
3 - The Silicon Labs si4734 DSP chip “soft mute” phenomenon is unnoticeable or non-existent on the PL-380 as it is annoyingly so in the PL-360 and other Tecsun DSP based radios.

Soft mute is a behavior of the si4734 DSP chip and how Silicon Labs thinks consumers would enjoy listening to radio, especially on AM and SW. While it does reduce interference and static once locked onto a station, it also changes the way we’re used to DXing the bands. The si4734 chip is intended to “mute” or reduce all the nastiness in between stations once signal levels reach a determined threshold. That’s a great theory in a perfect world and if propagation of signals was reliably constant, but it’s not realistic. The reason most people buy a radio like this is to tune around and hopefully discover and identify a faint signal. Other implementations of the si4734 DSP chip (like the one in the PL-360) make tuning around the MW & SW bands irritating. If a signal doesn’t meet the predetermined threshold, the audio will be reduced or “muted” as noise. This becomes more troublesome with fading signals as are most found on SW. The best way to describe this would be, imagine listening to a strong signal and you decide to tune off frequency to see what else is around. If another signal 5 kHz off is lower or equal to the noise threshold, volume drops from what you were originally listening to. My PL-360 behaves like this in a dramatic way, to the point where volume drops nearly 50 percent of original. When signals fade in and out, the volume will jump up and down.

Thankfully, Tecsun seems to have addressed this issue in the PL-380. Soft mute on mine is barely audible even when listening with ear buds and volume is uniform when dialing around. Ability to select several bandwidths makes this a real gem. My only gripe is the digital volume control, it’s not linear enough and steps are too coarse. I was mistaken into thinking it was analog since it’s controlled by a thumbwheel dial. I have no hesitation recommending the PL-380 over the PL-360 since I own and have used both. You get a whole lot more radio and performance with the PL-380 at a negligible higher price point.

product_title: Cable Matters Micro USB to HDMI Adapter for Samsung Galaxy S3/S4 and Note 2 in White
review_body:
This is a perfectly functional MHL cable. No issues with functionality whatsoever. One thing to note: the Micro-USB end has a very fat casing. This means it likely won't fit into your cell phone case, if you use one. You'll thus probably have to take your phone out of its case to use this thing. This can be solved by taking a razor blade to the rubbery plastic to slim it down a bit. I did this with no problems (I've been using it this way for months now). The video quality is good (nothing evidently terrible unless I'm streaming low-quality source material).

As for MHL: it's OK. Through no fault of the cable, my battery still drains when using this to stream video while the power is plugged into it. This is because (evidently) MHL caps the charging current at 500mA. For reference, my Samsung Galaxy S4 (with which I use this cable) came with a 2000mA charger. Since streaming video and sending it through the MHL cable to the TV evidently drains more than 500mA of current, the phone has a net decrease in battery charge while streaming video. This is a bummer, but not the end of the world. Just thought you should know what to expect. Also, my TV has a slightly non-standard aspect ratio (I think it's 1366x760 or something arbitrary/stupid like that) instead of a standard 16:9 (1366x768), so the output from this cable cuts off a few pixels at the bottom and top of the screen on my TV (this doesn't happen on 720p or 1080p sets).

product_title: Polk Audio OWM3 On-Wall Speaker (Black)
review_headline: Upgrades my mixture of moderately price equipment to a pleasant 7+2 surround-sound system nicely
review_body:
Since I use these speakers only as L/R Surround speakers in a 7+2 surround-sound setup, I can only say how it sounds as part of the whole setup, not for what they do by themselves! I use a speaker setup wizard in my receiver to adjust the volumes of individual speakers for 3 to 6 listening areas where we sit to watch TV.

From the Amazon customer reviews, I knew these speakers were decent as Surround-sound speakers, but weak in the base. I picked them up this October to replace two KLH main speakers with 9" woofer and 4.5" mid-range which I was using as Left/Right Surround-sound speakers. There was nothing wrong with the KLH speakers, but it's base overwhelmed the main speakers and was so large my wife complained it made our entertainment room look like a used-speaker warehouse. As mediocre as some reviewers feel these OWM3 are, they do this job better than misused L/R main speakers!

Our 7+2 setup sounded nice but not noticeably better than 5+1 when we played "Pearl Harbor" and "Avatar" from DVD & Blue-ray disks with only 5+1 Surround-sound audio tracks. Over Thanksgiving, we rented the Sci-fie movie "Pacific Rim" that actually contains a 7+1 Surround-sound track and I was never so captivated by an Sci-fi action movie. My son who has a Onkyo 5+1 Surround Sound system really like how the audio came out of my audio system. He also liked the way this Polk Audio speakers come across as L/R Surround Speakers, and the way they look. My 7+2 stereo system consist of a mix of well-received equipment built from a low-to-midprice equipment. It consists of:
Receiver: Onkyo TX-NR626 7.2-Channel A/V Receiver
Main Speakers: a pair of really old ADC L/R floor-standing speakers with 10" woofers and 3 3/4" tweeters. They are encased in walnut and are heavy.
Center Speaker: KLH with Dual 4.5" mid-range speakers (from a 5+1 Surround-sound speaker set). Only press-board case painted black.
L/R Surround:Polk Audio OWM3
L/R Rear Surround: KLH L/R Surround speakers from same old 5+1 Surround-sound system
Right Subwoofer: Sony SA WM-250 with a 4.75 star customer review on Amazon
Left Subwoofer: The Subwoofer from a Logitech Z-4 2.1 Speaker System with a 4.5 star customer review on Amazon. (This has a deeper base but does not sound as dynamic as the Sony subwoofer.)

While our equipment is not audiophile stuff, it works quite well with the Polk Audio OWM3. I have the Polk Audio speakers mounted on the wall about level with the top of a French door. With action movies, we can hear the special effect sounds from them. I can say it works well with my setup, but I can't say it stands out. I set up my receiver to play music in "Surround-sound compatible mode" which sends sound to all 7+2 speakers. I usually turn of my Left Subwoofer when I play music or I'd get too much base. My setup wraps me in sound, and the Polk speakers pulls it weight in delivery thoroughly enjoyable music that includes pop, jazz, country, new age and musical, mostly from Pandora, Spotify and Slacker Radio.

product_title: MP3 USB SD Player Module with Remote Control
review_headline: Excellent no frills MP3 Player without display.
review_body:
MP3 Player module arrived with the Remote non-functional. Parts Express promptly replaced the player with a new player with a functioning remote and I did not have to return the non-functional player.

The MP3 FM player module has no display, and is supplied with a remote. The player module has a SD slot and a USB input. The player has an LED which blinks when the player is working. The player is supplied without a case, without a 5 Vdc power supply, without power switch, and without input and output connectors requiring that you supply these items and assemble the module into a usable MP3 player. The unit is supplied with a battery for the remote. The MP3 player remembers the track being played, and the volume setting. A connection diagram is supplied.

If you are not handy in building electronics equipment, I would give this unit a pass. If you realize this module will require some assembly and installation, and are handy in building electronics equipment you will be rewarded with excellent MP3 player performance.

I installed MP3 Module in Radio Shack plastic Box (2 X 2.5 X 5.0). I used screw on panel as the base. I Added rubber feet (Waxman Super Sliders Bumpers ½ inch 0 74523 02153 8) to the box. I added 12V input connector (Sunkee DC Power Jack, Screw Nut DIY 180 Degree X00017GVIL) and color coded (white/red) RCA input jacks (Radio Shack Gold plated, mount with nut). I used a Radio Shack Universal power adapter (1.5-12V dc) (273-1662) that I happened to have on hand, set to 4 Volts output. I used the type M output tip set so that the center conductor was positive.

The MP3 player has 5 equalization settings plus no equalization. With no equalization the player response is flat within 1.6 dB from 17 Hz to 20 kHz into a 23kOhm load (excellent). There is no signal clipping or digital saturation with the no-equalization setting even at maximum volume (excellent). There is no digitizing frequency on the output waveform (excellent). The digital volume control has 15 levels. The maximum output is approximately 1.8 Volts peak to peak into a 23kOhm load (0.64 V rms). Random noise is about 50 mV peak to peak (17.7 mV rms). No power supply noise was evident with a radio shack 4 Vdc power supply (excellent).

I consider the equalization setting s of this player as being incorrectly implemented and not of any particular usefulness. With a recording level of 0dB the equalization settings cause digital saturation. With a recording level of -6dB only one of the equalization settings causes digital saturation. Equalization setting 1 has no digital saturation at a recording level of -6dB with some attenuation of treble. Equalization setting 2 has no digital saturation at a recording level of -6dB with some boost of the treble. Equalization setting 3 has no digital saturation at a recording level of -6dB with some boost of the treble. Equalization setting 4 causes a midrange boost with digital saturation in the region of 1 KHz at a recording level of -6dB. Equalization setting 5 has no digital saturation at a recording level of -6dB with some boost of the midrange and treble. Therefore, I consider these settings basically not of any use since they do not accomplish a loudness setting or a normal room response setting. I recommend that the manufacturer revise the player to eliminate digital saturation at 0dB recording level at all settings, and incorporate a low volume loudness setting and a typical room response of a gradual increasing attenuation with increasing frequency. Another useful equalization setting is a midrange boost.

Since there is no display, you will need an oscilloscope to tell which equalization setting is in use.

The Remote on off button is non-functional. The remote mode button is non-functional. The mute, pause, next track, previous track, EQ, Volume up and Volume down keys are all functional. The remote has a fast forwardfunction. The number pad can be used to select the track to be played.

Within the limitations above, the no frills MP3 player Module has excellent performance with no equalization and will require the addition of an amplifier to drive speakers and adjust the tone.

product_title: Sangean H205 AM/FM Weather Alert Waterproof Shower Radio
review_body:
So far, I am pleased with this Bluetooth-enabled shower AM/FM radio.

The radio comes with a bracket that allows easy installation to a tiled shower surface and it seems adequately strong for securely holding the radio in place. The handle smartly rolls into a recess in the back of the radio so it is completely hidden when not needed (as in my case since I installed the mounting bracket with the included ultra-strong 3M adhesive strips). Likewise, you can remove (or not install) the included carrying strap.

The sound quality is decent for a shower radio. No stereo (only one speaker) and no booming bass, but the frequency range seems good for a small radio. Better than my last shower radio and doesn't distort very much, even when played loudly. When using Bluetooth, the volume is dependent on both the volume setting on the remote Bluetooth device (e.g. iPhone) and the volume setting on this device.

I like that all the controls are push-button; no knobs or analog controls, so it is easy to control while showering. The FM radio is much more sensitive than my old shower radio. I can easily pick up all local stations and even some distant ones. The included wire antennae is adequate, thin, and relatively short (compared to my old radio's very long, bell-wire type antenna). The radio is fairly intuitive to use, but do yourself a favor and read through the short instruction booklet (written in multiple languages) before using to understand all the nuances of the controls (e.g. how to pair a Bluetooth device, how to set the clock, etc). I like that I can preset my favorite radio stations into five memory buttons (five for FM and five for AM). Having a built-in LED light (the owner's manual calls it a "torch") on the right-had edge is nice to have in the event of a power outage while you are in the shower. There is also a button long that same edge that will sound an internal alarm. I can't imagine why anyone would want to do that, as it isn't very loud. So you are better off yelling for help if needed than pressing that alarm button.

I'm not sure what others are complaining about regarding the short time-off timer, nap timer, and auto-off settings. To me, it is just easy enough to simply press the Power button when you are finished listening to the device and everything shuts down (except the clock display). I will probably never use the timer functions, as I only plan on using this as a shower radio/speaker, and not as an alarm clock or portable radio.

I'm knocking one star off for a few things. First it is a bit too pricey ($85.00) for what it does. Second, the rubber cover that protects the connector port for the optional power supply (located on the left-hand edge) doesn't stay closed very well. It wants to pop halfway open. I will probably seal it with a small dab of silicone sealer just to be sure no moisture gets in through that port, especially since I don't plan on buying the power adapter. And I can always easily open it back up in the future should I change my mind. And third, for the price it should have included two-way Bluetooth so I can at least control the playback functions on my paired iPhone with this device. It would be nice to have a better display that shows info about what is playing via Bluetooth and maybe even album art. As it is, the display only shows you the current time of day and some simple device status information (such as radio band, Bluetooth pairing, battery life, etc). The contrast of the monochrome LCD display could be sharper, too. Maybe the next version of this radio will have two-way Bluetooth. For me, this wasn't a deal breaker, though.

In summary, I would recommend this device for anyone looking for a good quality radio/Bluetooth speaker to use in their shower at this price point.do that, as it isn't very loud. So you are better off yelling for help if needed than pressing that alarm button.

product_title: Klipsch Image X7i - In-Ear Headphones
review_body:
This is my fourth pair of Klipsch in-ear headphones (Custom-1, Custom-2, Reference S4i, Image X7i). I "upgraded" from Reference S4i thinking it would be a nice improvement, especially considering it's currently $200, which is $80 more than the Reference S4i debuted for. However I can't fathom why anyone would want this over the Reference S4i's. For one thing, the bass of the S4i's is far and away better than these. I listen mainly to EDM, and if you're someone who really values bass, the X7i's are simply a bad choice. The difference is really night and day between the S4i and X7i in this area.

Now it may be that the X7i's have better highs, but I find that once the volume gets to a certain level, it actually gets to be unpleasant. I can't quite explain it but I don't experience the same thing with the S4i's. It just makes you either want to turn them down or take them off, and we're probably talking about 50% volume on the iPhone here.

The other big advantage of the S4i over the X7i to me is the physical design. For one thing the cord on the X7i is unnecessarily long. I don't know why anyone would need a cord that stretches practically down to their feet. The X7i's also have a much greater tendency to slip out of my ear than the Reference S4i. I use the largest earbud size provided by Klipsch, and have no problem whatsoever with the S4i's. I also had no problem with the Custom-1 and Custom-2s, and I believe the reason is that the plastic piece that the earbud directly connects to is at a right angle from the ear with the Custom-1, Custom-2, and Reference S4i. With the Image X7i, though, that plastic piece curves into your ear, which seems to result in more downward pull by the wire, especially if the wire or plastic piece gets bumped in any way. The S4i's stay snug in your ear at all times, though. And the wire is shorter, and to be honest seems more durable to me, as it's made of a different material.

product_title: NVX® Perfect10 Studio Over-Ear [42mm Driver] Headphones with ComfortMax® Earpad Cushions and 1/4-inch adapter [XPT100]
review_body:
A well-made and great-sounding set of cans!

Out of the box: very nice presentation with a durable case, extra cables, extra very nice angled pads, adapter, instruction booklet.

The XPT100 is well made, seems durable, and has a handsome understated look. Out of the box, the sound was superb. This is a fairly neutral headphone with a slight mid-bass hump and just a slight flabbiness that doesn't spill over into the warm, detailed mids. The highs have some sparkle, are well behaved and not at all sibilant.

After about ten hours of burn-in (which I do to all new headphones) using white noise, pink noise, radio noise, and frequency sweeps, the bass, to my ears, lost that slight flabby characteristic and became tighter and even deeper. The mids came a little more forward and opened up more and female vocalists like Norah Jones, Nina Simone, Sara K all were presented with clarity and detail. The highs seemingly had a little more sparkle and cymbals took on a more realistic sound.

Overall, I am very pleased with the XPT100. Apparently this has the same driver as the Brainwavz HM5 which is more expensive and, to me, not as comfortable. Clamping force is only moderate and the cushioned ear pads will surround your ears in superb comfort. Sound quality is right up there with much more expensive headphones and this deserves a definite best buy for build, comfort, and sound quality.

Purchased from Amazon's 3rd party vendor, Sonic and was delighted with their service, shipping, and pricing.

review_body: Currently, I am using two sets (2x 4-pack) of Rocketfish Banana Plugs to connect the speaker wire between my Yamaha RX-V573 receiver and the two Yamaha A1738 speakers. Concerning the installation, make sure that you've stripped about a half inch of the plastic coating off of the speaker wire and twist the copper wire into a nice spiral. After lining up the black and red plugs on both ends of the wire, you can go ahead and unscrew each banana plug. After pulling the wire through the bottom piece of the banana plug, make sure to fasten the appropriately sized plastic collar. Then, screw on the top of the banana plug while putting pressure on the bottom of the banana plug to ensure that the wire is firm/tight (no moving/wriggling around) within the banana plug. review_headline: Poor quality control, PITA RMA service...
review_body:
I have a couple of pairs of the old H2O Audio wraparound headphones with an old H2O housing for an iPod Nano. They were uncomfortable and always slipped out, but they worked, didn't leak, and kept me sane on solo multi-day kayaking expeditions. I wish I could say the same for whatever the company has become under the X-1 label.

I picked up an X-1 Surge on a whim. Expecting improvements over the earlier headphone models. I was wrong. The good news is that essentially only the name has changed, so the X-1 headphones fit into older H2O housing head phone ports. The bad news, is that once you plug them in, you aren't supposed to take them out. I'm sure X-1 will disagree, but having the plug on my headphones split apart where the two colors of plastic on the jack failed to bond occurred even before I left the house! I will try to upload a pic. Looking at other negative reviews on this page citing product failures, this seems to be part of a trend.

I went to make a return and was directed to X-1's site where my RMA process failed. You need an original receipt from an authorized reseller, as if these headphones were so popular that there were a slew of Chinese knock-offs out there. These are the cr@ppy Chinese knock-offs! So be careful if you get them online from Amazon, and not one of the Amazon resellers, as they may not be authorized.

Generally I would keep my paperwork if I was buying a vintage Ferrari, but not for a pair of $40 earbuds that are destined to get beat-up. So I have been going back and forth on the road to nowhere by email with one of their CSRs. If there was another product that fit the H2O housing that I already have invested in, I would toss these and start again. I have never suffered such a corporate belligerence over such a cheap product. It is what sparked me to write my first Amazon review.

I found a glowing evaluation of the earlier and identical H2O-labeled Surge Contact headphones on iLounge while researching their failures online, I but cannot understand why. Allegedly they sound amazing, even compared to non-underwater headphones. Waterproof headphones are tinny and flat, That is it. When they seal off the little ear speaker, they cut off most of the dynamic range of sound. To hear anyone gush about resonance and acoustics is to listen to lies. Airplane headphones stuffed in a pillow sound better than these.

product_title: Yamaha RX-V673 7.2-Channel Network AV Receiver
review_body:
Cons
-No owners manual included (a receiver is one of few items where I really want a printed manual, especially if quick guide lacks key information)
-Quick Guide LACKS large image of back of receiver (really?!?!?)
-Print on remote is way too small
-Registration REQUIRED to download owners manual that should have been in box. 17 and under cannot legally obtain owners manual because you must be 18 to register.
-Firmware download broken on Yamaha site

Pros
-HDMI input switching is fast
-Configuration of input & audio pairings is the most intuitive I have seen. Easy to rename, easy to select if you are not using a universal remote.
-The remote controls my raspberry pi XBMC (raspbmc) flawlessly (via HDMI CEC)
-I like the on screen pop up menus and input/volume feedback

My use is a 5.1 setup with a zone 2 area. I have not setup or used the zone 2 yet, so will have to update later if I have any issues.

Our media sources are Dish Hopper, PS3 (netflix/amazon/bluray/bluray3D), a Raspberry Pi with XBMC (RaspBMC - it totally rocks to play video, pic slideshows, ripped music we own), a hardwired minijack for audio, a bluetooth-enabled optical input (comes tomorrow), and an occasional laptop or phone hooked up via a long HDMI cable behind the couch.

When I look for a receiver, I look for sound, ease of initial setup, ease of use, ease of programming with my universal remote. This is the best receiver that I have on a lot of fronts and once Yamaha fixes the cons that I have listed above, they will have a very good receiver.

The MOST IMPORTANT item in the printed materials is a clear image of the back of the receiver, but this receiver lacks it. I, like most people, do not have a clear view of the back because it is in a cabinet. I can tell where things are by view and feel, but cannot read the print.

After running the setup and adjusting things as per the instruction manual, direct mode still had the best sound, with all other modes mudding up the sound. Finally, airplay was spotty and wouldn't work all the time with random drops, and sometimes just blank audio. I also noticed a few times it was silent in direct mode and had to completely pull the power to get it to work again.

Bottom line, for a 2 top end 2 speaker w/sub setup, sounds great in direct mode, when it will hold the settings. Too many other little inconstant issues to make this worth using. I will be trying the Marantz SR5008 and will post a review on it.

product_title: SONOS Compact Wireless Speaker for Streaming Music
review_headline: Nice sound, directions and apps need some work.
review_body:
Recently I decided to upgrade my home sound system and decided to start with a SONOS Play:1 and a Bridge; the price looked about right and the thoughts of not having to have wires all over the places while having my place with music as I wanted it was appealing so I decided to start small and see what it was like. Opening the boxes (I picked up a bridge at the same time, this review is about my total experience) I have to say that SONOS did a quality job packing thing. Configuration seemed simple, plug in, download, and begin configuring; this is where the train starts coming off the track somewhat. The unpacking and plug in was simple enough (bridge to router, Play:1 and bridge into an outlet), the trouble started when I started configuring things. I went through SONOS’s directions (select the component, push the button when the application tells you, continue on) and thought everything was working great; and it did for a little while. Actually the first round of music went smoothly and when I went to listen to some more my music cut out or skipped a little (or a lot). It seems that sometimes my Play:1 would cut out of the connection for no reason (the bridge was always there). Researching online I learned that the frequency used for out of the box by SONOS is near that of some wireless home phones and what needed to occur was to change the channel used, but to do that you needed to have the Play:1 and the bridge up at the same time… good thing they provided the means for a direct connection. After doing the direct connection and changing the channel I was able to get wireless sound in my place (it was a near run to me returning the system).

Rating wise the sound is a solid 5, giving great sound where I've placed the speaker; but I have to rate the system a 4 because SONOS failed to make it an easy set-up. By providing a simple sheet with common setup or connection problems I’d have given this a 5 star rating but don’t feel I can because of the pain, need to learn, and almost reaching the point of returning the product. (Note: on the SONOS website under FAQs they mention that SONOS uses 2.4 Ghz, the same as some phones).of the pain, need to learn, and almost reaching the point of returning the product.
