review_headline: Works with Google TV / Logitec Revue !!
review_body:
I purchased this without knowing for sure if it would work with my revue / google TV but I was absolutely thrilled to learn that it works beautifully. Even better, it only took 5 minutes to do the initial setup since the revue immediately recognized the make and model of this device after searching for it. (it didnt automatically recognize it but i went into settings, selected TV source and I put in the make and model and bingo)

A little background: I cut the cord on cable long ago and with a good antenna on my roof I have received crystal clear over the air HD broadcasts since day #1. (The antenna itself is probably 50 years old and works beautifully. Many people don't realize you do NOT need a special "HD" antenna or expensive cable provider because of all the confusion/noise cable companies propagate in their quest to get people to pay for things that already are/should be free). But I digress.. I purchased the Logitech Revue to combine my web experience (browser, netflix, youtube) with the over the air (OTA) TV channels I receive but like many I was not able to have the fully integrated experience of google TV (watching TV while browsing / picture in picture, single remote to do everything, etc) until now..

Once the revue recognized the Homeworx DVR MOST of the keys on the original logitech remote just worked out of the box without me having to program anything (switching channels, menu, info, channel guide, even the record button!!).

However, I did notice that a few of the keys were incorrectly programmed (eg". while REC worked great, for some reason the STOP button was sending an incorrect IR command even though it was linked to the Homeworx STOP command on the revuea) I am not sure if this is the fault of Homeworx/Mediasoniq in that they published incorrect IR codes or logitech's fault but in either case the revue let's you solve this problem by overwriting the default IR codes by learining directly from the remote. I was also able to map some of the function keys on the revue to some of the Homeworx's functions that weren't automatically imported (eg. EPG, USB)

I also noticed that Google TV's "movies on TV" function suggests movies channels that I dont have and I suspect that is because google TV does not pull this information from the Homeworz channel guide but rather from a local cable service (you must choose one in your google TV setup and "över the air" is not an option)

All in all I am very pleased with the Homeworx HW-150PVR and its compatibility with the Revue and Google TV but I have only had it for about a week now. I will update the review if anything changes in the future.

product_title: Datacomm 50-3323-WH-KIT Flat Panel TV Cable Organizer Kit with Power Solution - White
review_headline: Just installed 2 of these over the weekend.
review_body:
In one of our rooms, I already had a single gang pass-through into a closet for cables/power but was running my TV's power cable right through the same hole in the wall, which apparently isn't up to code. When I found this kit, I figured it would let me keep the clean look but make things a bit more safe.

I was very happy with the kit and the install. Everything you should need is included in the kit, including the in-wall power cable and an extension to plug it in on the outlet side. One of the things to be aware of though is that if your TV (or whatever you're plugging in) has a 90 deg plug, you may want to test fit the plug in the outlet before you get everything connected. You may need a short extension to connect it into the receptacle, as the outlet is recessed a bit (something like this: [[ASIN:B000233WJ6 C2G Cables 03137 Outlet Extension]]

The only thing I'd personally prefer is a different opening for the low-voltage cables. I'd rather have just a flat, rectangle opening or something that isn't as restricted. It's not really a problem to feed cables through or anything - actually I pulled all of my cables before I even installed the electical boxes. It was easier to pull the cables through the rough openings in the wall and then slide the faceplate over them. But I'd just like a bit more space in feeding the cables through.

Both of my installs were completed without issue and the plates fit securely and cleanly (not that you see them anyway). Definitely would recommend if you want a clean and SAFE in-wall install for your TV/home theater.

He has an active lifestyle that includes splitting wood, driving horses, and running tractors. The likelihood of his breaking a portable speaker is high. The Cuve's sound is great, far, far beyond my expectations for thirty dollars. The other day he stopped at our neighborhood bar and grille for a morning cup of coffee. Now, everybody in the bar knew each other, so what I'd personally resent in another restaurant was perfectly fine here. The manager hadn't turned on the sound system yet, so he set the Curve and his phone on the bar and played some country music. The other customers were amazed at the sound. So when the manager turned on the sound system, they told her to turn it off--they liked his soundtrack and speaker better.

Maybe this will put the sound in perspective through written word. I bought a Jambox a few of years ago from Best Buy when the only color options were black or white. There were two levels, one around hundred and fifty dollars and the other close to three hundred. The difference in sound quality was so clear I had to buy the more expensive model even though that was not what I'd budgeted for. Had it been available then, I'd have bought the Oontz Curve instead because of its price and its sound.

Btw, the manager at the restaurant has ordered a Curve for her personal use.

I spent a considerable amount more on these as I wanted to see if the different type of cable would change the sound of the earbuds at all. I believe I bought a type of silver wire. They looked great, but when I plugged them into my ipod, right away I started hearing all kinds of sounds that I didn't want to hear. Everything the wire touched made a sound. Imagine rubbing a microphone on the ground. This is what I would hear when the wire would rub against my shirt or whatever. This was very annoying and what was even more infuriating was that the base of the wire broke within 2 months. I'm assuming it broke because the wire seemed a bit stiffer than the factory wire and I would wrap the cable around my ipod when I wasn't listening to it.

Then I found this cable online and read favorable reviews. It looked like it was a little more flexible than the previous cable and a good alternative to the overseas cable or the factory cable. When I received it, I was slightly disappointed. It wasn't as bad as the other replacement cable I had purchased, but still not as good as I had hoped for. The wire was a bit more flexible, but it still had a stiffness that I didn't like. Also it does magnify the sound when it comes in contact with anything. Not as severely as the previous cable, but still at an unacceptable level. I'm assuming that anyone buying these earbuds cares about sound quality, so stay away from this replacement cable. Then like my previous purchase, the wires at the base of the cable broke within 2 months again. First it was my left ear that went out, then the right ear would flicker as the wires would connect and disconnect as I moved. What an annoyance.

Pros: Cheaper than the factory cable, Beautiful Silver wire, Nice connector, Sound quality is good when it's idol

Cons: Expensive considering it doesn't last very long, Magnifies unwanted sound, Wire is very fragile, Wire is a bit stiff

product_title: Wisedeal 100pcs Solderless Flexible Breadboard Jumper Wires M/M With A Wisedeal Keychain Gift
review_body:
I ordered two of this item expecting to receive 200 pieces. To my pleasant surprise I received 245 pieces! However, the advertised Wise Deal keychain/thermometer was not included. No big deal. But now I won't know what the temperature is in my pocket! ;-)

I received my order in eleven days which I was happy with considering the item shipped from China to the US over the Christmas holiday and shipping was free!

I sacrificed one of the jumpers to \\"reverse engineer\\" it to see what's in it and how it's made. The very flexible wire consists of seven very fine copper wires twisted together. I'm guessing the gauge is 26 AWG. This wire is very solidly crimped to a tinned stiff solid steel wire, that appears to be 24 AWG, with a brass crimp connector.

The crimp connection is covered with a PVC grip 10mm / 3/8\\" long leaving 9mm / 5/16\\" of the steel wire exposed. The PVC grip is slightly problematic. Most DIP ICs have 0.10 inch pin spacing. The diameter of the lower portion of the PVC grip is just a hair larger at 0.11 inch so you may have to stagger the jumpers on your solderless breadboard. Also, the upper portion of the PVC group is even larger at 0.12 to 0.13 inch. It would have been better if the entire group was 0.10 inch or less in diameter.

The wires I received came in seven colors: black, red, orange, yellow, green, blue and white.

As advertised, the wires come in four lengths. The quantities and lengths (measured tip-to-tip) of jumpers I received were: 187 pieces of 117mm - 4 9/16\\", 35 pieces of 160mm - 6 5/16\\", 11 pieces of 200mm - 7 7/8\\", 12 pieces of 240mm - 9 1/2\\".

76% of the jumpers I received were the shortest length, but that's fine for me and I think would be for most folks. The quantities of colors of wires by length was uneven. For the 117mm - 4 9/16\\" wires I received quantities varying from a low of 19 white wires to a high of 37 black wires with the other five colors in therange of 24 to 29 wires. Not a big deal. Just don't expect to receive equal quantities of each color.

Overall I'm happy with the product and the price. My only beef, and it's a minor one, is that the PVC grips should not exceed 0.10 inch in diameter and this is why I gave it four stars instead of five.

product_title: HomeSpot NFC-Enabled Bluetooth Audio Receiver for Sound System
review_headline: Perfect modular design; dubious bluetooth connectivity
review_body:
This receiver is very nice in a number of ways, but has connectivity drawbacks.
First of all, the design and components are all modular and can be used with any devices, making all parts of this except for the actual receiver multipurpose.
The power cord is a usb-120volt adapter that can be used with any usb cable, and the provided usb cable can likewise be used with any compatible device.
The audio cables (2.5mm-2.5mm and 2.5mm-RCA) can be used directly with any sound equipment and work well both with and without the receiver base unit. The audio cables aren't high quality (that is to say, if I were to buy a 2.5mm-RCA cable to directly connect my audio device to a set of speakers, it would be of a higher fidelity and quality than what is included here), but are sufficient to support the quality of audio that can be transmitted over bluetooth.
I use this in a single small room, so I can't comment about the bluetooth connectivity at a distance, but I can comment on close-quarters usage.
I've used this device with my Mac laptop and my iPhone 4s. Leaving the device alone, I've had great results with the music transmitting wirelessly in high quality with no static or interruption.
However, when using another blue tooth device on my laptop - such as a mouse - the connectivity usually encounters lots of problems. The music transmitting will cut in and out rapidly sometimes, and a handful of times I've completely lost the connection. Sometimes the connectivity will remain intact, but at least 50% of the time I have considerable to serious issues.
Playing music through my iPhone is equally "perfect" when the iPhone is at rest, but I find that if I handle the phone for more than a few seconds, my hands will interrupt or block the bluetooth connection, and the sound will cut in and out. That means I can change albums pretty easily, but if I need to send a text while listening to audio, that audio stream will likely be interrupted.

Overall, this is a very nice modular package that works extremely well with good audio when transmitting from devices at rest, but it generally experience problems when you interact with the device that is streaming audio, or when you are using any other device that is also transmitting a signal.

product_title: MEElectronics Sport Fi S6 In-Ear Sport Headphone System with Armband
review_headline: Universal Isn't One Size Fits All
review_body:
One day last week the mailman brought me a set of these [[ASIN:B007IL4ROE MEElectronics S6 Sport-Fi Noise Isolating Memory Wire In-Ear Headphones]] from Meelectronics. There are some things that I really like about these. They come with a great zippered carrying case that you can slide onto your belt and a wide variety of earbuds that will let almost everyone find just the right fit. The sound was quite good, the in-line control works well and I really like the \\"extension cable\\" so that you don't have to have excess earphone wires hanging everywhere. Both wires have clips to keep them in place, an added plus.

I did have a couple of issues. Fitting the earbuds to my ears was distinctly counter-intuitive, even with directions. Took me three tries. Actually, it was kind of like learning to use a mouse for the very first time long ago - pushing when you're supposed to pull, going everywhere except where you want to go.

The armband would be great but it is far from universal. I'm short, so for me it was a choice of having the armband restrict my shoulder movement or making it difficult to bend my elbow. Taller people would find this less problematic. I also found it hard to adjust the band one-handed and while the cell phone compartment fits most phones, we could not get my son-in-law's larger smartphone into the pocket.

Grandma's $0.02 - Nice headphones for many active people, great storage but the armband doesn't fit shorter people well.

product_title: Klipsch S4-II
review_headline: Better than the stock Apple earbuds, but not much
review_body:
I respectfully disagree with other reviewers who think these sound great. (And, yes, I've inserted them correctly.) I'm not saying other people are wrong. My intention is merely to warn prospective buyers that not everyone agrees that these are the most amazing earphones ever.

I think they sound a little better than the Apple earbuds that come with iPhones and iPods. They are also bass-heavy, which some people like but I don't.

The noise isolation is better than Apple earbuds but not as good as Shure earbuds, several models of which I've owned. This is a good thing for people who don't want to block out as much outside noise as possible, but not a good thing for people who do.

Build quality seems very good, the cords seem less prone to tangling than many earbuds in this price range, including Apple's. I had a previous set of these. After 1.5 years, one of the silicone earsleeves fell off somewhere and I never found it. These come with extras, which I appreciate very much.

I bought these on some kind of Amazon dealbox special for just $30. If I'd have paid more, I'd probably have regretted the purchase. But for $30, I'm perfectly satisfied with them and will be happy to use them at the gym or while shoveling my driveway, applications where sound quality isn't critical.

I see many other Amazon customers love these earphones. You should give their reviews as much weight as mine. I'm just one voice. But I think it's important to get multiple viewpoints before spending your hard-earned money, and I wanted to share mine in case it's helpful.

product_title: TECSUN PL-380 DSP FM stereo. MW. SW. LW. World Band PLL Radio Receiver, LCD Display, ETM Function Added
review_body:
Perhaps I got the bum one in the batch, but this poor little unit is just not up to the task of shortwave listening.

On FM and AM bands (for local stations) receiver is fine and the unit sounds good. The ETM feature is very handy.
But for shortwave bands it lacked sensitivity and was incredibly susceptible to noise.

I compared performance against a communications receiver and another shortwave receiver, using the same (and different antennas). For example, the US national time time signal (WWWV et al) on 2.5, 5, 10, and 15 MHz would be crystal clear on my other receivers, but was buried down in the noise on this little guy.

Interestingly, couldn't pickup any LF signals which were very strong on my other receivers.

Even using the various settings, such as changing the bandwidth on the receiver didn't do much, other than muffle the audio.

Oh well.

product_title: Creative ZEN X-Fi 3 8 GB MP3 and Video Player withTouchscreen
review_headline: Much potential, horrid exectution, GRAND DISAPPOINTMENT
review_body:
Compared to older Zen products that I have purchased, this was, quite simply, a disappointment. I bought the X-Fi 3 after losing my Zen Mosaic, thinking after months that I had lost my Mosaic for good this time. A week after this came in the mail, I found my old one and have not so much as turned this product back on. That should tell you something.

The battery life is my biggest gripe. It's nearly dead after only 4-6 hours of use. My last MP3 player could easily reach 16-24 hours before needing a charge. I've never seen one with a battery life so short, and all I am doing is listening to music.

One perk is that the menus recognize the SD slot and the internal storage together and there is no differentiation between the two. It makes for nearly 40gb of storage (With a 32Gb SDHC), but the lag that ensues EACH AND EVERY TIME YOU TURN IT ON is a deal breaker, easily ruining this perk. I'd rather have some kind of option to load it instead of waiting minutes every time I wish to use my device.

I've had the touch-style buttons go unresponsive on me a couple of times, but so far resetting it with the reset button on the side has helped to fix this. Of course it means another round of loading screens in order to simply get to the player's basic function, but It's nice that It wasn't permanent.

It plays most audio files, including FLAC which was a huge selling point for me since I collect game and movie soundtracks in said format.

The headphones that came with this are great no matter what you plug them into, but as for the player itself throwing great sound, It's crap. I plugged in my old pair of headphones I used with my Mosaic and this player sounded tinny at best... but when plugged back into my Mosaic or even my husbands Ipod touch, they sounded great once more.

In closing, I feel like there are far more bad things than redeemable ones about this product and I would urge anyone with any kind of expectations of this product quality wise to either lower them or choose something different.
I'm glad I found Old Faithful or I'd be beating my head against a wall every time I want to listen to my music library.

review_body:
So glad I finally got my hands on a pair of these monitor headphones, they are extremely comfortable. I am coming from hd515's (been good to me, and are really comfortable also.) the leather on these is really soft and breathable, the foam is soft too and never seems to get hot. If I wear these for 3-4 hours listening to music It might get a little moist on the part that comes in contact with my cheek, but if I remove the headphones for a couple seconds it feels fine again.

These are a part of a big familly of clones that all have minor variations, the brainwavz HM5 being another pair available for purchase here on amazon. From what I understand they all use the same housing/drivers and differ only in pads and headbands.
These sound really nice, warm and clean and the volume can be turned up pretty loud without being uncomfortable.

The headband that some complain about being 'flimsy' feels pretty good to me, I think it's so bendable because the inside of the band is mostly made out of metal and it has alot of flex. This makes changing the pads really easy, and it's great for my big head.
These headphones are Big, the pads are big, the housing is big they are just big and I think thats part of what makes them sound so nice. they are closed but at the same time there is lots of room inside the housing.

I'm going to buy another pair, because at this price point I could see myself using them on the road or in public. The sound on these is phenomenal for the price range they are in. I almost bought the ATH M50's but I'm glad I noticed these, I've been eyeing these since I saw another variation on jaycar..

Pros
- Comfortable!!!!
- Really comfortable!
- Great sound quality
- Nice aesthetics
- detachable cable
- comes with cables of 2 different lengths
- earpad material is breathable and compfortable

Cons
- they feel light for how big they are, I know this is probably a good thing really, but they just look like they would be heavy. Theres not many negative things I can think of when it comes to these headphones especially at this price point.

product_title: Mohu Leaf 50 Indoor HDTV Antenna (Certified Refurbished)
review_body:
I'd been using the Leaf Plus for about a year. My house is in a terrible location for cell phone and TV reception. The houses in my neighborhood are very close together, and we're down in a valley out in the country. The Leaf Plus was able to get most channels in my area, but I would still have to move it and mess with it every time I used it. The same location wouldn't work with every channel. It was a bit of a pain, so I decided to try to Ultimate instead.

First, a few notes about the Ultimate vs. the Plus. The antenna itself looks just about the same, but rather than being laminated, it's got a stiffer, flat finish that definitely looks better. It also has two small holes at the top for using push pins or something to attach it to a wall.

It's still white on one side and black on the other, just like the Plus, but now it has a Coax connection at the base of the antenna, instead of a set-length cord that kind of limits how far you can place it from the TV. Now you can use any coax cable, or just use the provided white cable which is somewhere around 10-12 ft in length (much longer than with the Plus). It's a flexible cable that is easy to pin to corners. The other end plugs into the provided signal amplifier (powered by USB or AC), which then goes into the TV. This Amp is black and slightly larger than the white amp from the Plus. I definitely prefer the black, since it fits better with all of my components and doesn't stand out as much against my darker walls. I just had to switch my coax cable for an all-black look (something that's not possibly with the Plus). It's also nice being able to plug the power into the TV via USB rather than running another power cable into an outlet (this also helps with vampire power, since it's not drawing any when the TV is off).

No on to performance. I don't have to move it around the room nearly as much as before. I'm able to pick up nearly 20 channels. Every now and then a channel will cut out alittle and I'll have to tweak it, but nothing like before. I'm not sure if this is actually due to a better amplifier, or just due to the fact that I can now use a longer coax cable and get the antenna closer to a window.

My only complaints aren't really even an issue with the unit itself. I'm not able to really hide the antenna since reception in my area is so bad. Any attempts to cover it or place it somewhere inconspicuous cause the signal to drop out.

I currently just use this and Netflix for all my TV viewing. I still miss out on not having ESPN, AMC, or HBO, but not having to pay a cable subscription makes it worthwhile.

product_title: Kinivo 501BN Premium 5 port High speed HDMI switch with IR wireless remote and AC Power adapter - supports 3D, 1080p
review_headline: Good inexpensive solution for a TV that doesn't have enough HDMI connections
review_body:
I ordered this to use with an older Samsung DLP TV with only a single HDMI port. The switch works great, changing inputs is smooth and I have not had any problems with the switch itself. There are also no audio or visual issues introduced by the switch. I do have a couple of minor issues with the device, well, 1 issue and 1 item on my \\"wish it had\\" list.

1. Having the output and 5th input on the sides is awkward because using them gives the box a significantly wider footprint. This would be less of an issue if both input 5 and the output were on the same side. Because they're on opposite sides it is impossible to position the switch vertically if you use input 5.

2. I really wish the box had an IR extender or at least the option of ordering one. If I could velcro the box to the back of my TV and just mount a remote IR extender somewhere around front it would alleviate issue 1 for me. Being able to stash the box out of site would also let me hide the bright blue and red display elements on the front of the switch.

Bottom line, as long as you can position this horizontally (assuming you need all 5 inputs) and don't want to stick the switch in a cabinet somewhere out of sight this is a great solution for under $40.

The Bose SoundDock 10 is much, much BIGGER and HEAVIER than the Bose SoundDock Series III and has a much larger, fuller sound than it's smaller sibling. The bass is deeper and richer but I still haven't found an ipod docking station that can truly generate a truly three dimensional \\"Hi-Fi\\" soundstage and I don't think I ever will. The sound is pleasant but don't expect it to compete with a multi-thousand dollar sound system. This dock's good for small parties and feels at home in a small living room or large office. It's not made to travel. It weighs nearly 20 lbs., so find a place for it either at home or at work and leave it be.

Don't pay attention to past reviews knocking the Bose SoundDock 10 for not having a Bluetooth adaptor because it now comes with one along with a 30 pin connector. I am told the range of the Bluetooth is around 35 feet. At work where mine sits, this sounds about right. Having a 30 pin connector is a bonus for me because for $20 more, I can now purchase an adaptor to convert it to the newer fitting so I can hook my 5th generation ipod with the thick case because there's no back supporting bracket to get in the way.

I haven't had this thing for but a week but I've owned Bose equipment in the past and they've never disappointed. The Bose SoundDock 10 will never replace my B&W 802D speakers but for causal listening, it produces a pleasant, clean sound.

product_title: PCT 1-Port Variable Gain Signal Amplifier With Active Return
review_headline: Fixed my internet problems with Comcast
review_body:
I've been having problems with Comcast for years ... Multiple truck rolls, tried many different amps (both from comcast's stock, and my own), this is the first one to solve the problem.

Basically, without splitters, going straight into my cablemodem, the downstream signal was 'just right' at +5db, but the return signal was very marginal at 48dbmv. After using a typical 4-channel active return amp, the signal would generally look like +3/50dbmv. Comcast will swear up and down that 55 dbmv is the limit, and therefore 48-50dbmv should be fine. Unfortunately, I was getting frequent T3 Timeouts where the cablemodem would disconnect/reconnect. The downloads were generally very fast, but my uploads would be somewhat inconsistent in performance. Also, if you looked at the CM status page, you could see the counter for Correcteds/Uncorrecteds would be incrementing (slowly) throughout the day with the amp.

T3 timeouts generally indicate that the headend is having a problem hearing your signal, and at 48dbmv, this is a very marginal signal.

Eventually, I decided to cancel cable TV (partially because of this issue), keep just the modem, and remove all amplifiers. The signal levels improved to +5/48dbmv, and dropouts decreased to once every other day instead of multiple times per day.

Not wanting to leave this alone, and trying to improve further, I found this item, and installed it. It required some tuning to get the signal levels 'just right'. My downstream was already fine, and any amplification risked making things worse, but the upstream required some significant boost.

Unfortunately, there was very little information in the package, but I found that at the minimum settings, the amp actually acted as an attenuator, meaning I could set it to pass through the signal at the same strength as received for the downstream, while amplifying the upstream only.

After some research, I determined the target for 'best'performance was to have the modem report +5db on the downstream and 40dbmv on the upstream. After reaching these settings, and doing numerous transfer tests, I have had zero correcteds/uncorrecteds, I have been consistently getting 120Mbps download and 20Mbps upload (the performance I am paying for), and, while it has only been a few hours, no T3 timeouts!

It's a shame that the product has been discontinued, but thankfully it seems to be plentiful in stock, with fast delivery from Amazon Prime.

Fully recommend this for anyone who is having problems with their cablemodem signal and understands how to read a signal level. Adjustment requires turning a screw, resetting the cablemodem, and checking the updated levels.

product_title: Arctic Cooling Bluetooth Stereo Headset with Microphone
review_headline: Good sound; reasonable comfort; controls could be improved
review_body:
Overall, these are a decent pair of bluetooth earphones. The build quality is good for the price, with sturdy arms that fold so the headphones can be stowed easily in a carry case (or pocket). The ear padding is on the thin side, but there's enough to maintain comfort for a reasonable amount of wear time.

The sound quality is more than decent for the price. They won't stun you with huge bass and crisp mid and upper ranges, but for general all-purpose listening (e.g., music, movies, etc.) they get the job done well.

It paired easily with a Fire and a Nexus. The operating range is quite good - I had no problems maintaining a connection from the opposite side of a large room (about 20 or so feet).

Misses center on two issues: controls and the case. The controls are small and unobtrusive, which is nice from an aesthetic standpoint - the headset casing looks sleek. However, in actual usage, it can be hard to find the proper button by touch alone. Some type of tactile cue would have been nice to ensure you get to the right button each and every time.

I also think the case could have been better. While it's stylish (sort of a triangular shape) with a crease in the cover that adds visual interest, there's no mesh or straps on the inside to hold the headphones and/or cables. The end result is that while the case looks nicer than others I've used, it's not as practical or functional. I find that to be a significant issue since I use these type of headphones away from home (e.g., at the gym, while exercising, etc.) and the carry case gets used a lot.

Given that these are priced the same or a bit higher than other similar bluetooth headsets, these misses warrant dropping the rating by one star. However, they remain a good choice if you're looking for a generally inexpensive set of headphones - they sound pretty good, seems to be well-made, and have a good operating range.

product_title: TDK Life on Record IE800 Dual Dynamic Drivers Headphones, Black (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Dual Dynamic Driver Delivers Delicious Delight
review_body:
I've become jaded lately with higher end IEM's. I've spent thousands on finding that perfect pair of earphones that I can take with me anywhere, are lightweight, comfortable, and sound like heaven, with just the right amount of bass. Now the issue at hand is that most higher end earphones and custom IEM's are driven by armature drivers. These require little to no air movement to create sound. The problem with this is that even though you get life like details and instrument reproduction with armatures, very few armature drivers are able to reach sub bass regions, and most have trouble reaching lower bass regions without crackling or distortion. Dynamic drivers usually have very little problems reaching sub bass regions and specialize in providing deep bass response. This is because dynamic drivers work on the principle of moving air through the drivers via vents in the earphone housings. The drawback of this is that dynamic drivers usually have issues with delivering clear details and more natural timbres in the upper and mid regions. With the TDK IE800, you have an earphone that works on DUAL drivers. So you have one driver that focuses on bass and sub bass clarity and frequency response, and another dedicated driver working on mid and high frequencies. The first thing I did notice about these IEM's is that they provide gobs of details. Even the quietest cymbal click or chime ring comes through clearly and competently. The other thing I noticed is that the bass is tuned to mid to upper bass frequencies. What does this mean? It means that these are NOT bass heavy earphones, despite having a dedicated bass woofer. I'm not sure why TDK chose to do this, but the IE800 still delivers just the right amount of bass, either of rock tracks or hip hop tracks. Just don't expect teeth rattling bass. These don't go there. Steady competent and realistic bass? Yes. You get that. Next this is noticed is that these are more mid forward IEMS. This means that the vocals are slightlyforward, and that guitars/string instruments are most definitely forward and up front. The highs are delivered with clarity and competence, and decay is good. Cymbal crashes go about what they should, and are the right timbre. Are the TDK IE800's jaw dropping, or do they provide a WOW factor? No. I simply don't think so. I think I get more wow factor out of my Ultimate Ears 700 or my JVC HAFXT90's. The JVC's have a slight edge. Ever so slight. Though the TDK's and JVC's both share many different traits, the separator to me is the JVC's ability to deliver more controlled and undistorted sub bass. The JVC's make hip hop, R & B, and pop tracks just come alive. The TDK's work better at delivering clear and crunchy rock and heavy metal music, with speed and resolution. Rock and heavy metal tracks really pop with the TDK's. Guitars and vocals so lush and forward in the mix.
housing
If i have any real complaint about these earphones is that because they are dual dynamic drivers, the housing is a tad on the large size. Now they are surprisingly light. These things are as light as some of my armature driver earphones, but they are long, with a long nozzle, so they tend to be uncomfortable over long usage. The hard plastic housing made the outside of my ears sore and ache after awhile. Using Comply foam tips did not help this. They just aren't all that comfortable to wear for long periods of time. Microphonics is also very mild by using the built in cable/chin cinch, coupled with the flat cable.

Overall though, I won't take stars away for both the fit and lack of sub bass. The reason for this is because for another person, the fit might not be that bad to them, and for others, they don't listen to or require music that reaches really deep for bass. When you look at the price, the high quality of the drivers, and the wonderfully clear and detailed delivery of the music, you just can't help but fall in love with these earphones and the mid forward sound signature. fans of classical music, opera, and rock and metal will be very pleased by the TDK IE 800. For those people, these do deliver deliciously delightful sounds. Can't go wrong with that? Right?

product_title: RCA 900MHZ Wireless Stereo Headphones
review_headline: Good solid inexpensive wireless listening that is expandable
review_body:
We have a unique scenario where we have two televisions in our living room. One is watched by a disabled child, so we needed a way to watch the second TV without having the noise and confusion from two televisions blaring loudly. These fit the bill perfectly.

The headphones are made from a high-quality plastic and are a one-size-fits-all model. The padded auto-adjustment band make for a comfortable fit for almost anyone. Setup is easy. Just plug the power adapter into the wall, plug the 3.5mm cord into the headphone our audio out jack on your TV, select the transmitting channel on the base (1,2,3) and the headphones and listen. An optional adapter can be used to plug the 3.5mm cord into a 1/4\\" headphone jack on audio receivers, or to convert 3.5mm into RCA-type outputs. Charging is accomplished by taking the small charging wire connected to the base and plugging it into the charge jack on the headphones. Volume levels are very good, and we've experienced battery life of 6-8 hours of listening depending on volume levels. Usually audio quality is good with practically no interference. Near microwaves, you'll get some static and pops. Because these transmit on the 900MHZ band, you don't have to worry about interference or impact on your wireless home network, and transmission range is quite far. Typical ranges are 50-100 ft. between walls and floors.

Durability: These things are tough. Ours have survived 5ft drops, falls off furniture, and the rigors of teenagers.

We use one primary base as the transmitter and 5 additional sets of headphones with base as chargers. Our family can finally watch movies or television while our youngest watches her cartoons on a different TV.

Average prices online start at around $30 new and are a bit higher in brick-and-mortar stores, so they are value priced.

product_title: OontZ Angle Bluetooth Speaker [ORIGIINAL] Ultra Portable Wireless with Built in Mic up to 10 Hour Playtime works with iPhone iPad tablet Samsung and smart phones - Black Grille
review_body: I paid $39 for this speaker on Amazon.  For $39, it sounds great.  We use it around the fire pit in the yard, while camping and picnicking on the lake islands. I also like to use it while relaxing in the tub. It is loud enough for a small group in close proximity or in a quiet setting. In a big group setting, the volume will not cut it.  The biggest drawback is the fact that you have to unpair the first device from that device's settings (not from the speaker) before you can pair it with any other device.  That is a pain if the first device paired is on and in range.  For example, I have an iPhone and an IPad and my wife has an iPhone.  If I use the Oontz with my iPad, I have to go into the iPad settings and tell it to forget the Oonzt, before the Oontz will pair with any other device, as long as my iPad is within range of the Oontz.  Other than that, I doubt you can find a better speaker for $39.  Also, I have used it as a speaker phone and it worked very well.  Battery seems to last for a good long time.  I have used it for 4 hours without a charge.  I cannot give it a 5 because of the pairing issue, which is just a slight inconvenience.  It's small, lightweight  and convenient.  Packs easily into the bottom of my backpack  If you are like us and don't require ear busting volume and will be satisfied with "good" sound versus the high fidelity of much more expensive speakers, you should buy the Oontz Angle!

I also expect sound bars to have ample inputs to address the myriad of gear we now have. This get's darn close.

First off, the unit is a bit bigger and heavier than I expected, as it comes with a bigger and more powerful sub than most. Setup was a breeze, and the fact that this can learn from remotes is another plus, especially given the mediocre included remote.

The sound is rather good, albeit overemphasizing the highs. You can adjust the sub a bit, even via the remote, which does help, but honestly, it's not a big deal. You don't get an overwhelming surround sensation, but you do get an overall surround vibe. I always wish for more, but I can't say I was disappointed in that regard. The convenience of this unit coupled by the three HDMI inputs and great sound, place this sound bar in my recommended list.

Wireless connectivity is great and so is the content.  You can access the help features and watch your program or movie without interrupting your viewing. And the receiver remote is truly universal.  Moreover the set-up is truly easy.  I would have to say, the only thing the 1040 has over the 727 is watts.  I would recommend this AV Receiver over either the Sony or Denon.  On second thought, I really do not think the Sony and Denon are in the same category as the this Onkyo.  You be the judge.

product_title: VideoSecu Ultra Slim Thin Flat LED HDTV Fashion TV Wall Mount Bracket for 32" 37" 39" 40" 42" 46" 47" 50" 52" 55" 58" 60" 65" LED TV VESA 200x200 400x400 up to 800x800 - Adjustable Cable Length 1Y2
review_body:
I'll never use one of those over-engineered metal mounts again. This thing works. I know it looks kinda questionable but, trust me, the hardware is first class and you can hang a 100lb TV with this thing no problem.

Okay, now for some caveats. First, you need to carefully examine the spacing of the holes on your TV and consider where you plan to put those all important wall hangars. As depicted, the hangars go inside the cable holders that connect to your TV. That's fine, and a good design unless, as in my case, your TV holes are 16" apart. That makes it impossible to hit two studs spaced 16" apart. It simply won't work. You don't have enough slack in the cable to hang the TV. It's hard to describe here in words but for most people it won't make any difference. But, you will NOT be able to hit two studs with most TVs. No big deal though. If you want to use both of the hangars, hit one stud and use a good quality (not the ones included with the kit) drywall anchor. My TV is a 55" LCD weighing in at 55lbs. I elected just to use one hangar, mainly because I wanted to center the TV in a particular location on the wall (see below). I'm very happy with the integrity of the mount. I pulled on the cable with all my 170 lbs before hanging the TV. It didn't budge.

That brings me to another installation issue. If you want to hit a stud (which I highly recommend) you will limit your ability to precisely select the location of the TV. It's just the nature of the design. So, either commit to two wall board mounts are just one one mount and hang your TV like a regular picture. This thing ain't going nowhere and you'll be fine with most LCD panels up to 60" or so with just one hangar. If you have more flexibility, use two hangars. Personally, I was more comfortable with one hangar in the stud (centered just where I wanted it) than using two wall board mounted hangers.

The hardware pack is awesome. If you can't find a machine screw that fits your TV I'd be surprised. And, if you can't, I'm sure Home Depot has what you need.

The Kickstand is a great design too. Just make sure you follow the directions and have it pointing UP.

Also, make sure you use BOTH of the cable clamps. The cable comes with soldered terminators but those things might not hold up under the weight of the TV. So, use the two clamps provided even if you are pulling the cable all the way to the mount at one end. It provides an extra measure of security. I suspect that some of the failures people experience with these types of mounts is because the relied on the soldered terminators and didn't install the clamps on both ends of the wire as the DIRECTIONS SPECIFY.

This is a hands down no-brainer. Unless you need your mount to articulate in some way, this is by far the best and least expensive solution. A rare combination!ind a machine screw that fits your TV I'd be surprised. And, if you can't, I'm sure Home Depot has what you need.

review_headline: Here's what I know about using these...
review_body: I bought two of these to bring with me on a trip across europe. They're so great. I think you could go to any country and be able to use these -- BUT keep in mind these do NOT convert electricity -- DON'T PLUG ANYTHING IN THAT DOESN'T HAVE IT'S OWN LITTLE TRANSFORMER ON IT (they're usually either built into the plug itself -- it makes them bulky, or they're in parts, which will connect to each other, for example, a laptop cord with the box in the middle.) You should be able to tell by the info printed on the plug that has the input amount like 100-240V... be sure to look up what the electricity output of the country you're visiting is. Most modern chargers (phone and laptop) can handle all the different levels in different countries, but simple electronics (like a desk fan) will either get too much electricity and overheat/catch on fire, or they won't get enough to function correctly.

product_title: Skullcandy S6AVFM-289 Aviator Mic3
review_headline: Honest in depth review  to help you choose the right headphones
review_body:
First of, I wanted a headphone that is stylish, and have good sound quality. I didn't want to get Beats by Dr. Dre because: one everybody has them, two you are paying for the bass, and three it's 300 dollars. I am not an audiophile, but an audio-enthusiast, and I hope my review helps those who are looking for decent headphones.

Price 4/5
Price is fair for the design, branding, and solid construction, are there better headphones at this price range? Yes, like my Sony MDR-7506 Professional Headphones, but you won't be seeing me wearing my Sony's in public. But as a "lifestyle" headphones, these are priced right.

Style 5/5
These are very stylish, it has some class too it. The inspiration behind he design are the classical aviator sunglasses. These headphone has that retro look with a modern edge to it. You will definitely stand out in a crowd of Beats. The styling is sophisticated, but not so much to take the fun out of it. All in all, great design.

Construction 4/5
For me, it seems a little flimsy, especially the headband. My above mentioned Sony's are rugged, these aviators, not so much. With that said, it is well built; construction quality is there, but I wish they used more solid materials. But I don't plan on working out with them, or go on hikes with them, so unless you're the type of person that bangs their headphones around, this will more than suffice.

Sound Quality 4/5
First off, if you are looking for a subwoofer type of headphones that will rattle on your head, like Beats, don't get these. But if you want a well balanced headphones, with great sound quality get these. The bass in these headphones are good, and balanced. It will not drown out your music. It does seem a little "dull" compared to my Sony, but it's not a bad thing; its hard to explain. The highs are clear, the mids are profound, and the bass is perfectly balanced. Now, if you want to listen to EDMs, hip hop, or twerk music, where the bass is the most prominent feature of the song, get beats. With this said, I have no problem enjoying my EDMs, hip hop, and other music then twerk music with these headphones.

Overall 4/5
A sophisticated, stylish headphones with great sound quality. If you are looking for a balanced headphone, with decent bass and great sound quality, at this price point, this will make you happy. If you want a subwoofer on your head, these aren't for you.

We recently added surround speakers to our home theater. After way more research and consideration than necessary, I purchased Definitive Technology ProMonitor 1000's. I looked at these Definitive Technology speaker stands but decided they were pretty pricey. Instead, I ordered Sanus EF-28B 28\\" stands. They looked similar and were about half the price. Maybe the Sanus stands would work for some people, but the design of the base wasn't stable enough for me and I couldn't see a satisfactory way to secure the ProMonitor speaker to the stand. I could use two-sided tape, or drill new holes in the support pad, but either approach still left the issue of the unstable base.

So the Sanus were returned (forty dollars for return shipping was a lesson learned) and the ProStands were ordered. Happily, they arrived four days later. I should have ordered them in the first place! They are well-built, stable, and our ProMonitor speakers attach with a single screw. They are more attractive than they appear in the Amazon listing. You can feed the speaker wire through the stand via openings at the top and bottom of the cylinder. I would have liked to have the option to route the wire through the bottom of the stand and underneath the base, rather than out of the hole at the bottom of the cylinder. As it is, you can see the wire trailing across the back of the base of the stand. It's not a big deal, but it would look nicer to have the wire hidden.

Overall, an excellent match for our ProMonitor speakers. Highly recommend.

product_title: SpeakerCraft CS3 Center Stage 80-Watt Bluetooth Ready Television Speaker (Black)
review_headline: Yeah, the remote's a joke, so?
review_body:
After trying - and failing - to fall in love with the Zvox 420, I decided to take a chance on this little beauty, despite the remote control disaster inflicted upon it by someone who should probably be fired. The remote control is indeed a silly little thing, but ... the SOUND of this thing is really just so terrific that it's worth it, especially at $399.

Also, the remote control isn't THAT bad. It's just disappointing, unintuitive and chintzy. But it does work, and did I mention the SOUND?

The CNET review that many have been influenced by indicated that the Zvox 580, which really is the competition for this guy, didn't sound much better than the 550. Well, the 550 has exactly the same speaker configuration as the 420 - it just has an extra thingy that converts dolby and lets you use an optical cable to transmit sound from a non-box cable connection to the TV.

So.. I am assuming that my 420 sounds very similar to the 550, which (according to CNET) sounds ALMOST as good as the 580. In other words, the 420 is not appreciably different from the 580. So, I did NOT try the Zvox 580 when the 420 failed to impress me. I tried this. The sound really is the kicker. Both my kids, who have been listening to the 420 for 2 years, noticed it instantly.

It's just bigger, boomier, and .. hard to explain .. more effortless. This thing just exudes sound in an open, resonant way that is way beyond the 420 (which is clear and tight). Also, the bass is just on a whole 'nother level.

I have no interest in shaking the walls and disturbing the neighbors. This doesn't do that, but it's bass is way beyond Zvox bass. It resonates and impacts at a deeper level. Also, the highs are tinklier and airier. The remote control lost this unit one star, but it's a very good, simple TV sound system, very well worth the (new) price.

product_title: ZVOX 4002201 Audio Z-Base 220 Low-Profile Single Cabinet Sound System
review_body: I bought this to use with a newer LG TV that has only optical digital audio out.  This audio base looks like a good solution but has one glaring flaw, while it has digital-optical inputs, it cannot decode Dolby digital sound.  If you have a Dolby digital source, it is silent.  The sound is OK, but not as good as the Audio Engine 5 speakers I have attached to a different TV (tried the Z-Vox in this setup because the TV has analog sound out and I wanted to see if it was DOA).  While I could fix the lack of Dolby digital by adding a DAC that decodes Dolby digital (Amazon has one by Gefen that works well) I ended up sending it back because once one fixes the Dolby digital issues with an external DAC, the value proposition of the ZVOX is not very good.  If you are severely space constrained and your TV has analog audio out, this might be a solution, but if you have optical out only or room for a  sound bar or speakers on stands, there are better solutions out there.

product_title: Pioneer VSX-1121-K 7.1 Home Theater Receiver, Glossy Black (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
We loved our Pioneer VSX-921-K, so when it came time to get a receiver with HDMI capabilities, we got the VSX-1121-K. As other reviewers have stated, it's a great device... when it works. I'll let you read other reviews to find out the positive side of this unit, but I'm here to vent...

This unit died at 19 months of age. If you noticed, that's 7 months after the measly 1-year warranty expires. Now, I don't know about you, but when I spend as much money as I did for this thing valued at $750, I expect it to last a lot longer than 19 months. Pioneer, of course, suggested a system reset, which does nothing useful, before telling me that the unit needed to be repaired. Well, isn't that nice?

How it began:

The first thing I noticed was that one of the HDMI ports would black out intermittently. We don't use all the HDMI inputs, so we swapped it to another one and the problem was gone.

Then, one day I turned on my system to watch my cable service, right after the receiver switched on, I hear two loud thumping click sounds in a row and then there is no further sound output, regardless of the volume setting. However, I can still see the picture on my TV.

At first, this happened about 10 percent of the time when I switched on the unit, and I could fix it by turning the receiver off, then on again. Soon, however, it started happening about 80 percent of the time that the unit was switched on and I had a lot of trouble trying to get the sound to come back again. I tried powering off/on and I tried switching inputs until it finally worked again.

I temporarily fixed this problem by programming my remote control to mute the receiver for 5 seconds when starting a DVR session.

Eventually this happened: When I switched the system on to watch or listen to anything, the receiver powered up and the display lighted up. However, there was no sound output, neither passing through from other devices or generated from within the unit (such as the internal radio tuner). There was no video output except for the unit's built-in menu screen which displayed with incorrect colors, and even this only showed up occasionally.

After a frustrating experience with a local repair shop (that's a different rant), I picked up the receiver, brought it home, plugged it in, powered it on. Within 5 seconds, it powered itself off. After a few more attempts with the same result it would not even power on anymore. The \\"Advanced MCACC\\" light blinks on the display panel, and that is the only thing I get out of the receiver. Back to the repair shop it goes.

I am really disappointed in the early demise of this product. These problems all started after the 1-year warranty expired. We really can't afford repair costs or a new unit right now, which is one reason we bought what we thought was a reliable product. Apparently not. We'll be looking at other alternatives to Pioneer the next time we can afford to.

review_body:
And sometimes it doesn't. I recently routed a run of subwoofer cable out the back of my house, and to the other side of the house via a 40 foot run of buried PVC electrical tubing. I did this because I could not run it through the attic, and did not want any cable visible. I have two powerful subwoofers behind the viewing position for my home theater.

In the middle of the night, with the amp and TV off, the subwoofer would start to hum. The volume would increase. The house, indeed the neighborhood, would rumble. It turned out the subwoofer cable was picking up electromagnetic waves from other sources, like an large array antenna, and amplifying them. The reason was because the cable was not shielded. Or not sufficiently shielded. I removed the plausible causes, such as ground loop, or feedback from cable TV. Nothing worked. I asked for help from folks who fix these problems for a living.

An expert in the field told me scrap all my old cable, and recommended Mediabridge Ultra cable. I tried it; replaced all buried cable and so far, no problem.

In order to avoid any possibility of malfunction of a subwoofer, it pays to use high quality cable, especially if the run is over four feet...

review_headline: A surprising work-around for twitchy sync from a device like this.
review_body:
This product is twitchy if your idea is to use it with your old VCR. The video picture quality probably won't be stable enough for this device to maintain sync long enough to actually watch a whole movie. But here's something you probably didn't know. If instead of using this device, you simply connect your old VCR via the RF output (type F connector), even to flat screen TV like Phillips that do not advertise the ability, what you will find is that the old analog channel 3 still works just fine on those newer digital tuners, and so you can still watch movies from your old VHS (or even Beta) VCRs that way.

Some flat screen TVs (like Sanyo and Samsung) sport S-video, composite video and audio inputs which work fine too, but transitional digital tuners for most new TVs also support the old analog channel 3 or 4 output from your VCR. Much less twitchy than this thing.

My room is a typical living room with a wall mounted TV and the in-ceiling holes are forward in the room. I wanted something to help angle the audio to the rear third of the room where the couch is and these are perfect. I researched these against the other popular brands and even though there is VERY little information about them out there, they sound great.

I use three of these for the LCR fronts and the ICE-850's for the rear. The Acousitc Range is good and I'm not currently using a sub with them. I've played a few Blu-Ray's through them and have been very glad. It was less the $500 for a 5 speaker setup and I would definitely recommend them if you're on a budget or just looking for something on a tilt. When I first had them in I play the Dark Knight and it reproduced the sound extremely cleanly in my opinion. I have them connected to a Denon AVR-1612 amp and a a Sony S390 Blu-Ray player.

Wrap-up:
For my use, which is some general TV (sports, Homeland, occasional Blu-Ray) these are great. I use the DTS mix so I'm getting a lot of center channel only mixes and even then, the single speaker (with the others used for ambience, etc) it sounds great. I have run them in multichannel stereo and it sounds just a good.

All in all, I would definitely recommend them.

review_headline: Good intentions and not much more
review_body:
I've not heard competing products and that does not matter since I am not comparing this to them. I am comparing this to what is promised, deep rich bass and amazing sound. The music comes out flat with lackluster bass, if at all. True, it does not distort at the highest volumes but then it's harsh enough at those volumes that it doesn't need distortion to make it unpleasant. I kept this anyway because it's lighter and the batteries last longer than my Soundworks Playdock from a decade ago, remember that? The Playdock's sound is far superior but it's heavy, contains a sealed lead-acid battery, and no bluetooth.

Well, I've only used the XL about a half dozen times over two months and one of the active drivers is no longer working. Now it is a single active driver mono with four passive radiators. How sad and pathetic. And it's well passed the 30 day replacement only warranty. Good thing I paid less than a hundred for it but still, it confirms my feeling of ever decreasing quality of Cambridge Soundworks products ever since their second generation Soundworks Radio, of which I have three and only one of them still have a working CD player. Another one I had to get replaced within a week. But I digress... It is hard for me to put any trust into their products that contain any sort of electronics anymore. I have had many amplified CSW computer speaker sets from last decade and they are all still going strong with numerous new owners. But now, it seems like their quality has gone down and without the convenience of a storefront, it's harder for me to justify ordering something from them sight unseen and unheard.

The XL is great in concept and is very sleek looking. The buttons are hard to read in lower light. Build quality seems very high. Too bad working quality is not. I have not had bluetooth dropout issues that others may have experienced. It works with my Nokia N9 phone up to about 30 feet away direct line of sight. People may associate me with audiophiles but I do want to be associated with that group. I enjoy good musical reproduction. The XL falls far short of that. It is acceptable for its given size, when it worked.

Update 21Dec2013: I took the grill off my unit and removed the front+side from the C shaped back and found the problem. One of the wires to the right speaker was tinned but there was no solder on the speaker terminal. This means the wire detached from the terminal and that explains why it stopped working. Nobody soldered the wire onto the speaker. An incomplete manufacturing job and a simple quality inspection would have caught that. I've uploaded pictures of my unit. After soldering the wire onto the speaker terminal, it is now working again. Good thing I am handy. I've added another star to the rating even though it is poor assembly and quality control and the sound is still something to be desired. However, I feel it sounds better with the grill off. Too much sound reflecting off the grill and back into the unit. But that's subjective.audiophiles but I do want to be associated with that group. I enjoy good musical reproduction. review_headline: If it seems too good to be true...

Well, if it seems to be too good to be true, probably is. I tested the antenna itself and it appear to receive an adequate signal. The problem is with the remote control for the rotor. There is a small red light on the remote marked "Instruction light". No idea what it does and no help from the instructions. In other reviews, I see that others have had a similar problem with the temperamental nature of the rotor remote. As a side note, the remote requires two AAA batteries which are NOT INCLUDED.

I wanted to contact the manufacturer for assistance with the remote but, alas, there was no contact info for the maker, UPLINK Technologies, on the packaging or instructions and no warranty card. Tried web search, not there either, just a computer consulting firm of the same name. This might be a problem should a warranty issue arise.

On a brighter note, AS ALWAYS, Amazon stood behind what it sells, issued a UPS return sticker and credited my account.
YEAH AMAZON, YOU ARE THE BEST!!!!!

product_title: Belkin Pivot Surge Protector with 6ft Cord and Telephone Protection
review_body:
I've had this for several years and never had a problem with it; I've run a gaming PC (and peripherals, including a printer) on it before, and various other electronics. It was probably my favorite surge-protector/power-strip due to the pivot plugs. I'm really leery of using the generic white power strips that inevitably (almost mysteriously) turn up in the household cord box, and I've always used Belkin for anything remotely heavy duty or pricey (PC's, TV etc.). Last night, however, it melted. I had a plasma TV, blu-ray player, small electric fireplace and mini-fridge plugged into it at the time(the mini-fridge and fireplace are built into the entertainment center, and quite small). Too much? Maybe, but I've had those same four items plugged into it for over a year now, and the power requirements for the above items are less than what I've used it for in the past. And I would hope that the surge \\"protector\\" would cut out before it started to melt, but it didn't stop until I found it and unplugged it.

The lettering on the face of the fireplace plug is actually melted into the surface of the socket, and the hard gray plastic that makes up the body of the surge protector had started to melt and warp as well. I'm glad I was awake when it happened, although I wish I knew exactly what happened. Do I need to chuck the fireplace? Obviously I won't be using a single protector for all four items anymore, but I'm a little alarmed that the protector didn't cut power when it started drawing enough juice to melt itself.

product_title: Musical Fidelity V-DAC MKII
review_body:
I bought The Musical Fidelity V-DAC II with the recommended Pyramid PS3KX Regulated Power Supply, and I noticed a big improvement with the Pyramid power Supply. Bigger soundstage and great rhythm but nothing prepared me for the HUGE improvement when I used the V-DAC II with an Anker Pro 14400 portable charger! Once you hear your music with the Anker V-DAC combo you will realize that the wall wart that comes with the V-DAC II is junk.
The difference is stunning. With the Anker Pro there was no longer that very subtle abrasiveness and grain that kept me from fully getting into the music with the Pyramid. I could clearly hear natural decay to notes, the sound stage was even bigger, and black black background. But best of all was the over all organic relaxed nature to the sound. You can play everything from classical, folk, rock, and techno and it will all came through authentic. I could play music louder and still stay relaxed. You have not come close to the real potential of this amazing little DAC without a good battery power supply like the Anker. I still recommend the Pyramid for playing music between charges or back ground listening because its really good, but the Anker Pro is the ultimate for serious listening sessions. At the heart of my 2nd system is a heavily modified Fischer 500C Tube Receiver with premium caps throughout, and its the best digital I have heard through it. You would probably have to spend a lot more before you hear a noticeable difference with the battery pack combo. A no brainier triple combo for peanuts!

product_title: SONOS Compact Wireless Speaker for Streaming Music
review_headline: Great compact speaker - perfect as surrounds for PLAYBAR!
review_body:
This is the SONOS component I have been waiting for since getting my PLAYBAR! Until now, I have been using two PLAY:3 speakers positioned in portrait mode. The PLAY:3s sound amazing but are a little bulky for my setup (my wife has been complaining since setting them up that they take up too much space and are unsightly). She was pleased when I replaced the PLAY:3s with PLAY:1s. I gotta admit that I was pleasantly surprised as well. I had my doubts that these small speakers would fill the room the way the 3s did. They have no problem accomplishing that. I highly recommend these to use as surrounds with the PLAYBAR and SUB. This creates and instant (almost) wire-free surround system that will continue to please and impress.

Prior to dedicating these speakers to my living room as surrounds, I tested them individually as well as stereo paired with each other. Wow! These little speakers have an incredible sound stage - individually as well as paired. I was expecting the sound to be very directional but it is the opposite and fills the room with rich sounding audio. If you are familiar with SONOS speakers and the sound they make, expect nothing less from these. They will truly blow you away. Obviously not as loud and don't create as much bass when compared to the PLAY:3 or 5 but I don't image anyone would expect that from this compact design. I also like the portability aspect of this speaker. I have been utilizing one of my PLAY:3s when out on my patio - now I will use a PLAY:1 as it is more portable and will take up less space on my patio table.

One last thing to note - the mute button that you may be used to being on the top of the speaker has been replaced with a pause button. The new software supports pausing instead of mute. This is a very subtle improvement but I actually really, really like it. I plan to get a few more to place in the remaining rooms of my house - something I didn't expect to do before there was a sub $200 SONOS speaker.

product_title: JBL Synchros Powered Over-Ear Stereo Headphones
review_headline: Great comfort, Awesome Sound, Cool Look!
review_body:
I picked these headphones up for my music loving son for Christmas. I wanted to put in a timely review for those who might have a similar idea. Unfortunately I can not get my son's feedback, so I asked my hubby to give me some input after using the headphones a few weeks. He is not the audiophile my son is but he uses headphones a lot for work and pleasure.

His thoughts:

*Packaging is very nice.
*Very well made, premium leather ear cushions and lightweight steel band. Comes with a very nice travel/carry case.
*These are very comfortable over ear headphones. The adjustments actually have numbered markers so you can always set it exactly the same every time.
*It comes with two cables that have microphone and basic controls (answering phone call, start/stop music, volume, advance or backup to next song), one for Apple products the other universal for other music devices and phones. I like the fact that you plug in the cable jack into the left headphone. Many times headphones go bad at the permanent connection of the cable to the headphone itself.
*The right headphone is where the two AAA batteries are inserted for turning on JBL LiveStage Digital Signal Pocessing . You have to twist off the outer cap of the headphone. There are two little dimples to help with grip when turning the cap. It's not the easiest thing to remove and replace.
*OK now for the sound. Noise insulation of the premium leather over the ear cushions is excellent. Sound is phenomenal achieving professional audio sound with JBL PureBass performance. The bass comes through deep, rich and full. Now the interesting twist to the headphones, by switching on (small switch on left headpone) JBL's LiveStage DSP, the audio is enhanced to recreate the experience of listening to a live performance. Sound is crisper and more present, you truly have the sensation of being at a performance, as if you are really there. The difference playing with DSP on isclear and obvious. Overall the sound and the experience using the S500 is the best I've experienced. The S500 really brought out details and nuances in songs I've listened to over and over again, over the years.
*One interesting note: On my iPhone 4 and iPod, when I turned on LiveStage DSP, the music was crisp but somewhat muted, not at all like when playing directly from CD or iTunes on the computer. It was actually better to have DSP off when listening to music on my iPhone 4 or iPod. It must go through some conversion from the iTunes library or something else is affecting it.
*One thing these do not come with is noise cancellation technology.

I tried the headphones out too and compared them to the ones my husband uses on a daily basis: [[ASIN:B009NE5YC8 iLuv ReF, Deep Bass On-Ear Headphones with Canvas Fabric Exterior for Smartphones - Black]]. These headphones are a 1000 times better in sound quality and comfort but, then again, they are twice the price so they better be!

Neither my husband or I pretend to be audiophiles but, if these headphones last, and you will hear back from me if they don't, they are worth the investment for those who are.

Highly Recommended.

review_headline: For Toshiba Satellite P775-S7320 - Lasted Less Than A Year
review_body:
I purchased this as a replacement charger for the Toshiba Satellite P775-S7320 in November of 2013. This cable DOES power and charge said computer about as well as the original and is obviously very affordable. However, it is NOT an exact match for the P775-S7320 and will pop out of the laptop with little provocation. This may be a good thing, though, given the circumstances; if you're like me, you had to replace the original charger because you were in some way horrible to it, either letting it get bent up or pulling on until it finally lost its will to live.
The only major downside to this cable is length. Whoever sat down and decided that four feet was an appropriate length for a laptop cable needs a good kick in the pants. The thing BARELY makes it around my recliner to plug into the outlet in the wall directly behind said chair. Need to plug in across the room? Forget about it. I would not recommend this charger for students or professors, those who use their computer to give presentations, or anyone else who might need a little reach for their rig due to sparse or unpredictable outlet placement.

UPDATE

As of September of 2014 (less than a year of use), this charger cable has developed a problem with sporadically failing to communicate with my laptop (computer reverting to battery mode in spite of being plugged in). The issue seems to be with the connection between the wall cable and the power brick. There is no problem with the connection to the wall (trying an outlet on a different circuit made no difference) and the connection to the laptop is solid. Breaking and reestablishing the connection between the wall and the power brick appears to have no effect and neither does bending or pinching the cables at either end of the brick (cables exhibit no signs of damage) or rotating/elevating the brick. Connection may be lost whether the brick is running hot or cold and giving it a good shake will sometimes reestablish the connection, but it will eventually fail again, even if the brick is completely undisturbed.y fail again, even if the brick is completely undisturbed.

These settings will get you in the ballpark for great sound. Of course, you can adjust based on your desires, but this is a great starting point. product_title: Sirio Sy27-4 4 Elements Tunable 26.5-30mhz Yagi Antenna
review_body:
Just finished assembly. Went together with no problem Had to use metric converter but that was just a minor annoyance.
I planned to use this antenna on 10 meters for Amateur work so I had to convert the antenna element lengths to a shorter measurement.
This is very simple to do by multiplying .95 times the current CB length. My measurements put me on 28.5 mhz and the antenna is usable down to
28.2 and up to 28.8 and still operate under 2:1 vswr.
Hardware is good and uses allen set screws with supplied wrench. Joints are protected by plastic sleeves. Unit uses a gamma match to feed
power to the antenna and it is easily adjusted for proper matching.
I am turning the antenna with a CDE AR-22 R which is a light weight non locking rotor. I'm guessing a light weight TV rotor would suffice.
The antenna is very light and can be held over head with one hand. Not much more wind loading than a large TV antenna.

product_title: Comply Foam Premium Earphone Tips - Isolation T-100 (Black, 3 Pairs, Large)
review_headline: Beware of counterfeits sold as Comply tips!
review_body:
I ordered a set of T-400 tips from third-party seller \\"wholesale and selling,\\" fulfilled by Amazon, which arrived in a small foil packet rather than the usual retail packaging. I was suspicious, so I called Comply and they confirmed that these are unauthorized knockoffs. Beware of third party sellers offering especially good deals on these tips, and make sure whatever you buy comes in the original retail packaging.

I did end up getting a set of real Comply tips (medium size). I put them on a pair of Hifiman RE-0 and a pair of Monoprice 108320 IEMs. On the Hifimans, isolation seemed to be just slightly better than the original silicone biflange tips. On the Monoprice IEMs, isolation was fairly poor (though definitely better than the cheapo rubber tips that they come with). I think the shape and large size of the housings on the Monoprice IEMs prevented me from getting them in as deep as they should have been. I didn't do any A/B comparisons of sound quality with/without Comply tips, but my vague impression is that there was a bit more low/midrange fullness with the Comply. I recall the isolation being better on my old pair of Shure E2c's with their original compression foam than it is with the Comply for either of my current IEMs. The Comply tips don't feel very tight in my ears (though they are definitely not loose), so it's possible that I would have been better off with the large size.

review_headline: Not as sturdy as I would have liked
review_body: I ordered 2 of these media shelves and found them to be just ok.  The first one we put together and had some trouble getting the shelves to be level all the way around. If the pieces are not in exactly the same place the shelf will be uneven AND, if you push to hard the whole plastic piece will slide with the shelf, rendering it uneven.  After some practice on the first one we set out to put up the second one.  This one had a backward lean despite everything we did to fix it.  We ended up taking it apart,trading top and bottom poles until we found a combination that yielded a sturdier outcome.  In addition, you need to tether these to the wall (kit included) for them to remain stable.  Overall, they look decent, but it was a lot of work to put it together, deconstruct and build again in an attempt to create even and level shelving.  I would only buy this product again if I needed one to match the two I currently have.

-Bluetooth-

-Sound-
Impressive bass, amazing midrange, and perfect acoustics. The sound for this size of speaker is simply astounding

-Value-
Don't question the $200 price; Bose could be charging a lot more for this speaker. The only gripe I have is the cost of the protective cover and the travel case (~$70 for both). The player does have an autostop when the record is done playing. But the arm does NOT move automatically back to the rest. But I believe that was also included in the description.
