product_title: Terk VR1 Automatic TV Volume Controller
review_body:
The Terk VR1 works as expected. The product fits in the palm of your hand. That switch on the front activates or bypasses the leveler so you can bypass it during movies or other media when you want to hear the original volume dynamics. The leveler comes in handy at night when you want to watch a movie without disturbing others. This device eliminates the need to adjust the volume level when switching channels or video devices. I can't hear any distortion, hiss, or other anomalies in the audio as it works. It can handle 4.6 volts peak on the input. You can only use it on audio from a device to a device. Here are some examples of how it can be connected:

(cable/satellite/DVD) -> VR1 -> (Television Set)
(TV set/cable/satellite/DVD) -> VR1 -> (Stereo Amplifier)
(Tape Monitor Out) -> VR1 -> (Tape Monitor In)
(Tape Out) -> VR1 -> (Tape Deck/Computer)

It cannot be used with the speaker output of an amplifier as the levels could destroy the leveler.

UPDATE -- The audio can \\"pop\\" depending on how steady the original volume is. The \\"pop\\" is caused by quick clamping of the volume during loud jumps in the volume level. The \\"pops\\" will increase the more varied and sudden the volume changes. This is simply just the leveler at work. The audio might be improved on, but it will most likely increase the price of the product.

review_body:

I had two main reasons for the replacement.

1.- My Onkyo do not handle HDMI 1.4a and I wanted to get rid of few cables.

2.- Air play.

My results

1.- As for the HDMI 3D management it was AWESOME.

But... The PS3 issue, where video signals seem to cause a problem in the PS3 unit and makes it freeze... There is plenty of info for this issue in some forums, but I did not see any related info until it happened to me and had to research for a solution (hint: there is none)... 2.- Air play audio quality... SUCKS... really, as it also sucks when I connect the iPod via the USB connection in the frontal panel. Why? Audio via optical from the iPure to the unit sounds MUCH better than any alternative... Go figure!, but that is a lot of cables I could not get rid off...

Also, no being able to manage the iPad through its own screen when connected via USB is a big downside (you have to do it via Marantz RC and gets quite laggy).

Final comments... I do not regret my purchase and I am quite happy with the warmth of the audio from this unit. However, the PS3 issue and the unexpected lower quality audio I got from Air Play and the front USB audio/control issues. I paid $999 for this unit, but due to those minor flaws I do not feel It was a bargain at all. 4 stars until maybe they address these flaws via software updates.

product_title: Bose AE2 Around-Ear Audio Headphones
review_headline: Love clarity? These are the cans for you
review_body:
I have had both the AE2 and the OE2 headphones and have tested them the past few weeks.

Basically the AE2 are a very comfortable pair of headphones. They have some great clarity and are very lightweight. The only problem I have is that their is a very little bass response to these cans. That is the main difference between the OE2 and the AE2. The AE2 have very crisp and clear sound. The clarity is unmatched compared to the OE2. The OE2 have a great bass response but the vocals and clarity of them feel that there is a veil over them and sound a little muffled. So in reality, its a give and a take for either pair that you decide to buy. I will also point out that the AE2 do feel more comfortable then the OE2. I felt the OE2 ear pads were slightly small and somewhat tight on my ears, but they are not uncomfortable by any means.

In the end, if you are not the type to sit and listen to music for hours, trying to hear the little details of the songs, and love BASS, go with the OE2 and use an EQ. If you want the pure listening experience, with pure clarity to your sound, and care more about that then just the bass, I would go with the AE2. Dont get me wrong, there IS some bass to the AE2, but they will never thump your ears.

Lastly just want to say, in my opinion, if Bose would a set that had the clarity of the AE2 and the bass of the OE2, then you would have a very amazing set of cans. I believe the QC15 have all that, but I do not wanna pay over 300 for headphones.

Also, Bose has the best customer service in the business. If you break your headphones after the warrenty period, they will exchange your set for more then half off. I paid 60 for my OE2 after sending in my broken OE.

Since I prefer clarity and hearing every little detail in a song, I prefer the AE2 over the OE2.

Its all about preference. I would just try them both out from a store, and return the pair you like less.

product_title: Ear Earbud Heaphones with Flexible Ear Hinge
review_headline: Don't jump into conclusions so early. just give it some burn-in time.
review_body:
Few months ago I was looking for a good open headphone under $50 . I spent endless time reading expert reviews on head-fi.org and suddenly stumble upon these headphones.
These HTF600-S headphones might not work for everyone, specially frequent travelers who are looking for good sound isolation. And these headphones are open headphones so they ll leak some sound in full volume. So you might not want to use these in full volume, if you are in a office, public environment, or if you care about your privacy, but they won't leak sound like Sony XB-500 . And the sound leak is quite acceptable for a open design headphone. So these are perfect for home use.
I've seen some reviews that people jump in to conclusions so early without burn-in time. When I first listened with these Panasonics, the sound was so dull and there was a harsh treble sibling so I had to play with EQ to get rid of it. And I also used these with my Walkman player too, but there wasn't much bass in the early days without burn-in time. But after 30+ hours of burning time now these sounds like a complete different headphones with mind-blowing sound quality with awesome soundstage . After the burn in time the harsh treble sibling disappeared and now these Panasonics generate some incredible bass with my Walkman with Megabass on. But I don't think these high impedance headphones are designed to work with portable players, but still they are quite capable with my Walkman. Unfortunately currently I don't have any good sound card with headphone amp to get full advantage of these Panasonics, I'm currently using my terrible Realtek ALC 898 on-board chipset, but still these Panasonics gives me some fantastic results with on-board sound card too without an amp. Soon I ll test these with either Asus Xonar STX or Sound blaster z and update my review later.

product_title: Denon DHT-1312BA A/V Home Theater Receiver with Boston Acoustics MCS 160 5.1 Surround Speaker System (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Fair Price But Only Fair Performance, Expect Failure
review_body:
I use this receiver and speaker system for TV, movies, music, and video games. It is a vast improvement over the HD TV audio output. However, it has two issues in its performance. When attempting to play PS3 on this system, the TV screen will \\"skip,\\" show a split second black screen, or even drop input altogether to the TV for a few seconds. I can tell that the PS3 is still working properly as it works without this issue when I played directly to the TV. I call customer service and they gave me the solution of turning everything off for 30 minutes and then turning everything back on again in a certain order. I never had that issue with other equipment. The other problem is that it didn't work to clear up the skipping completely. Also, I conserve energy by turning things off when not in use, as it saves my electric bill and the environment. I can't keep performing a 1/2 hour process everytime I turn things on.
After playing games for an hour or more, the skipping usually goes away, but for that time, I am getting my butt kicked on call of duty.
The other issue is that the subwoofer stopped working. I found the fuse was blown, one day, when I thought the music should play better with more bass. Bought new fuses and replaced them several times, but never got the subwoofer working again, as the fuses continue to blow even with the subwoofer settings changed (polarity).
I called customer service again concerning this issue. I am awaiting their response and will post when they reply. I hope they cover the subwoofer's issues, as I just barely made the 1 year warranty point, and I can prove it.
My family has owned receivers and surround sound systems in the past. We never had any issue for years with either speakers failing or black screews occuring.
I wouldn't recommend this product to anyone just yet. I will have to await their response to my subwoofer issue.
The sytem does play Fios TV and all the included HD channels withoutissue or the black screen interruptions.
The sound is pretty good, but without the subwoofer, is certainly not optimal.

Update:
Customer service stated that Bestbuy was able to repair this equipment. Traveled to Bestbuy, and they said that it would cost me $80 to have it sent out to a diagnosing center, even before it would be diagnosed and repaired. Is this subwoofer even worth that much? Certainly not. Even if they offered to replace the sub, which they weren't nice enough to do even while it was under warranty, I have no doubt it would fail again. Went and purchased a Polk subwoofer that is smaller, but still has improved sound and greater sound amplitude than the sub that comes with this Denon Home theatre. I will never buy any equipment from this company again. Also, they began to give me unsolicited emailings about their products after I submitted a customer service request. Thanks a bunch Boston Acoustics. Don't bother fixing my problem, but feel free to offer me more of your inferior products.

product_title: Apple iPod nano 16GB (7th Generation)
review_headline: Ups and downs but largely the same as the last generation
review_body:

OS has been trouble free.

Cons - the removal of the back clip is a huge loss and a terrible mistake by apple. That was the most handy feature of the last generation, and most likely a ploy to get people buying clip on cases and the like. That play/volume toggle on the side is an architectural disaster - it overrides the lock so if you wrap your headphones around it and leave it in your pocket/bag it will more than likely start playing until the battery dies. Furthermore, the new usb input plug means that if you lose the cord there aren't too many people you can borrow/steal one off like the old cord.

At the end of the day most of these changes are aesthetic - the functionality of the device is almost exactly the same as the previous generation. If you can get your hands on the older ipod nano in new condition i'd recommend that to save money.

Beware if you need an AC adapter, as a portion of the voltage could leak into the TV via HDMI port & over time mess your HDTV up. Hasn't happened on this item, but it did on a similar item I bought that needed an AC adapter to work properly. Buyer beware on these things. review_headline: Wish I had discovered it sooner
review_body:

This one is great. I use it with three different mp3 players to listen to audio books but I don't own an Ipod so I can't comment on how it works with that item. It works so well with the players I do use I can hear just fine with the volume level set at about 1/3 of the possible settings.

It's smaller than a pack of cigarettes and much thinner. Very light weight and the rechargeable battery lasts for hours. It's also very helpful that another battery and a charger are provided.

Input and output are standard mini phone jacks. One control turns it on and off and adjusts the volume. That knob turns with a certain amount of effort and has a partial cover that makes it unlikely the volume will change accidentally. There is a small blue LED light to indicate when it's on. Both it and my player fit into the pocket of an armband type pouch I wear that makes it out of the way and easy to reach if adjustments are needed.

I've read the quality of the earphones used will make a big difference in the sound output. I'm using Klipsch IMAGE 4 earphones and even though they are not extremely expensive, both the spoken word and music are quite clear even with external background noise like traffic.

product_title: Logitech Harmony 650 Infrared All in One Remote Control, Universal Remote, Programmable Remote (Silver)
review_headline: Great remote ... minus one star for price.
review_body:
Love this remote. It's replacing a Harmony 550, which is very similar. Very nice being able to control everything from a single remote. We've only got a TV, TiVo, DVD, and stereo, so not a really complicated set up, but I usually use both the TV and stereo for volume as the stereo has a graphic EQ that I can tune to bring out the voices better, so I need volume for both. The color screen is nice but BW would have been fine too.

One issue is that when you pick up the remote, the screen lights up. This is nice when you pick the remote up, but I find that when I'm watching something, I usually have the remote in my hand to fast foward through commercials. So every time I move my hand, the screen lights up. Logitech used to have a way to disable this, but they've removed if from their latest remote software. I hope that add it back. The 550, to its credit, had a button dedicated to turning on the screen's backlight, but it was a BW screen and in good light, you didn't need the back light.

This version has a plastic back rather than the faux rubber back that was on the 550 which is a huge plus. My 550 still works fine, but that rubbery back has gotten all sticky and now has a ton of dirt stuck to it. Your hands stick to it too so no one wants to even touch it. I've tried to clean it but it's impossible (Logitech would not offer a replacement, repair or refund, but to be fair, it was over 4 years old). The 650's plastic back is a welcome change!

The buttons also feel better than the 550 and don't make the 550's loud "click". My wife hated the clicking on the 550 and so never used it ... she didn't even like me using it but was nice enough to put up with it. I'm still trying to convince her this one's worth trying, but no luck yet.

My only two complaints are (1) price, and (2) uses traditional batteries. Amazon dropped the price to $50 for a day around Christmas and I caught that sale, but usually it's $60or more. At that price point, it ought to have a rechargeable lithium ion battery and a charging station.

I'm very happy with my purchase in spite of these two issues and would buy another one if this one broke. I'd really like to see Logitech to make these rechargeable or lower the price, but it's still a great product.

product_title: Mustang Screens
review_body:
I looked at the Elites but would have had to order a larger size than what I could practically fit into my living room or else pay a lot more money. Mustang offered this motorized screen in the exact 92 inch size I needed for a great price. (Be warned that the housing is a bit wider than the actual screen width.) I ordered it on Saturday and it arrived on Monday. Amazon Prime continues to amaze!

I installed the screen (these screens are heavy so use 2 people and install very securely!), pressed the button and it smoothly unfurled itself so far it frightened me at first. I thought it might actually unroll too far and damage the unit. I hit the "stop" button and the motor stopped instantly and smoothly with no jerk or hesitation. The remote is nothing short of amazing. It actually controls the screen from inside a bathroom around a corner from my living room where the screen is installed. The only thing I wish it had but doesn't is a switch to integrate with my projector to automate the use of the screen. However, at this price point, that is not much of a consideration and the remote is a snap; hit the button and walk away.

I've now been using the screen for over a month. I spent the time to "micro-adjust" its stopping point in both directions and it is precise to say the least. Everything about this screen exceeds my expectation, especially with regard to the price. Friends and neighbors are also very impressed with it.

As far as picture quality goes, I notice a definite improvement in it over projecting on a wall. It has a few variances in the white screen but these in no way detract from the viewing experience and aren't noticeable when in use. I'm sure a "videophile" might long for more but I am a practical user who finds it isn't necessary to throw away excessive money on most toys.

This screen is a great value, arrives in perfect condition due to effective packaging, and should serve me well. I will update if any functional or mechanical problems develop but, so far, I couldn't be happier or more impressed than I am now. Highly recommend.

review_headline: Stop shopping and buy this mount
review_body:
PROs:
-Rock solid, sturdy steel.
-mounting holes fit 3/8" hardware.
-build in level IS accurate- but be a man and use your own anyways.
-Cheap

CONs:
-includes drywall anchors, which will give the novice the idea that its ok to hang a TV from them.

I bought two of these mounts after the $79.99 mount from Walmart didn't work out. Basically, the backing plate was too short and would not cross two studs while still giving me the ability to center the TV on the wall (only 25").

The mount arrived well packed and includes all the mounting hardware, washers, and toothed lock washers, as well as a 6ft HDMI cable. The major plus of this mount is the backing plate, which is 36 1/4" overall length. This allows you to easily center on two studs, or in my case, grab three (see pics). The backing plate and hanging brackets are made from very sturdy steel, which is wonderful given another brand on amazon which which advertises that they save steel and help the environment by using thinner uprights. Are they serious? You are going to hang several thousand dollars of TV off the wall and your main concern is the extra 3oz of steel? Incredible.

Anyways, in the usual fashion, throw out the small lag screws and drywall anchors that come in the box- You should not be hanging any TV from drywall anchors. A nice plus about this mount is that the backing plate holes are large enough to fit 3/8" lag screws. I used 6 of the zinc plated 3/8"x3 1/2" lag screws for a total of two per stud. This cost about another $5 from Home Depot. With this arrangement, I can literally hang my whole 280lbs off the mount.

This mount is absolutely rock solid, well engineered, and most importantly- CHEAP. I don't understand how the box stores and other online retailers are getting away with $120 for a mount when this is simply perfect. Just make sure your TV is as wide or wider than the backing plate or you'll see it from behind. Also, as with any mount, make sure your holes are centered on the studs so you don't skive out the side- especially with 3/8" hardware.

product_title: Onkyo TX-NR616 7.2- Channel Network A/V Receiver (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Problems at first - but still a good value
review_body:
After seeing all the negative reviews on Amazon & internet forums I was hesitant to purchase this receiver. The value finally won me over - at the time it was $50 less than comparable Denon / Yamaha 5.1 models and had LOTS more features. When I got it I plugged it into my LAN & tried to update the firmware. It would not update, so I assumed it had the latest. Shortly after first power up, I started noticing static / white flickering on the screen. It was definitely related to the receiver, because it did it with the OSD on, and I noticed it only when upconverting sources to 1080p.

After some research, I realized the latest firmware update must be done via USB - I did the update and the flickering / static seemed to get better but did not go away. I called Onkyo tech support and was told to try changing the HDMI cable to my TV. I thought the tech support person was crazy, but decided I would humor them. After switching to my other HDMI cable, I have not had any flicker/static issues. Still not sure why the cable change made a difference - both cables are from Monoprice and were purchased at the same time - I have been using the "faulty" one for a year with another source without issue. Oh well, it works now.

After the firware update & cable switch, I still notice one glitch. Sometimes when I turn the receiver on, it seems to take awhile for signal to get to the TV. It's almost like it takes 30 sec - 1 min for the HDMI to initialize. Annoying, but I can deal with it. Other than that minor glitch, I'm very happy with the receiver. The network features are great, as well as the Android app. I love that I can stream songs/playlists wireless from my phone and control all the receiver functions from my phone / Kindle.

Although I think this receiver still has its bugs, it seems the major problems plaguing early buyers have been resolved (or I got lucky). I have been using the receiver for just over one month now. Itoffers a lot of value for the price point, and would recommend it to others. product_title: AUDIO TECHNICA Noise-Canceling Headphones
review_body:
In this review, I will give you my first impressions of these decent noise canceling headphones and suggest a $30 mod that will improve the overall experience of these using these cans.

Summary:
I received my ATH-ANC27 headphones today from Amazon, so keep in mind these are my initial impressions and nitpicks. I researched this model considerably online before purchasing. The overwhelming consensus online is that these are a good bargain for a good pair of noise canceling headphones. I find the user reviews here on Amazon, rather than the \\"expert\\" bloggers, to be more accurate and representative. They offer decent sound quality, acceptable comfort, and quite good noise canceling. There is a reason Bose QC15's are the gold standard in noise canceling headphones. At this price point, they are worth keeping but they are not competitive with the Bose QC15.

Unboxing

First, the packaging was very easy to open and get started. It seems ridiculous to mention this, but today most electronic components are sealed in impenetrable plastic sarcophagi which have undoubtedly resulted in countless ER-trip-worthy lacerations (I refuse to open them without the presence a sober adult, capable of driving me to the hospital just in case). Included in the package were some nice touches: a nice carrying case, a velcro sleeve for holding the several included audio adapters, a 2.5mm to 3.5mm jack-to-jack cable, and an alkaline AAA battery (so many devices forgo the battery or may as well have by including an utterly worthless \\"heavy duty\\" zinc carbon battery). The unboxing was expedient except for the battery installation which required a quick glance at the manual. A quick setup guide on the right ear piece battery cover would eliminate this.

Build

The build quality is above what I expected for a sub sixty dollar set of noise canceling cans. The padding is fair quality. The \\"leather\\" is a little plasticky. The plasticparts on the headband don't feel fragile but I don't expect them to last years (hey, neither did my Bose AE's). The ON/OFF switch is a little stiff and junky feeling. They look decent in the case but the profile is large making them look a little goofy on the cranium. The cable and adapters appear to be gold plated. The cable is a little thin and has a nearly useless \\"locking\\" mechanism (a protruding rubber key on the jack) to keep them in the left ear but the perfect length to stick an iPhone in your pocket (I'm 6'2\\") and I'm all for a single stereo cable. All-in-all, they are built very well for the price.

Noise Canceling

The first thing you'll do after installing the battery is turn on noise canceling without music. The first thing you'll notice is not the silence, but the soft white noise (\\"hissing\\") in the background. It's not obnoxious to me, but it is noticeable. The seal on the headphones is not good. My Bose AE2's passively cancel out much more noise with a better seal than the ANC27's will in passive mode (i.e., OFF). In a quiet environment the noise canceling is negligible. I went into the laundry room, turned on the fan and the washer and the dryer and flipped on and off the switch...on...off...on...off. The low frequency noise cancelation is very impressive. For air travel, these would be superb. The high frequency noise cancelation was adequate but not great. Bose QC15's also do a much better job at low frequency cancelation (which is what you really want for most noises). I went out to the garage and used some power tools (e.g. a belt sander to mod a Bose cable, see below). Again, great noise cancelation. For $60, I am very impressed. Are they Bose QC15 quality? Nope. Are they close? Hard to say. I'll do a side by side comparison tomorrow. But I suspect the answer is: for 20% of the cost you get 80-90% of the value. There is a reason Bose QC15s are the industry's gold standard. The noise cancelation isthe selling point for these headphones and their strongest suit...if you don't mind the white noise background which vanishes when listening to music.

Audio Quality

The sound quality is not the strongest suit of these headphones. With noise canceling OFF these cans sound terrible. WIthout active noise canceling, the sound is muddled, distorted, sloppy. They sound like a cheap pair of noise canceling headphones. That is with noise canceling OFF. With noise canceling ON, the sound is more crisp, clean, and clear. Unmistakably better audio quality with the use of a AAA battery. I will not use these headphones without noise canceling. I'll go so far as to carry a few spare AAA's in the case to avoid the temptation. That said, the noise quality is not great even with the noise canceling ON. The mids range from okay to very weak depending on the song. I have been listening to over an hour of my favorite songs and I find myself often distracted by the lack of distinct mid-frequency voices, especially when they are the dominant melody (e.g., guitar or vocal solos). The bass ranges from clear and clean to boomy and excessive. If you like bass, these have enough. The highs are clear...clear enough to distinguish 128kbps vs 192+kbps mp3 encoding. Compared to Bose AEs, AE2s, and QC15s which, like all Bose products I've owned, offer excellent, clean, crisp, clear, flat performance across all bands, the ANC27s sound will leave you wanting. They are far from the worst and best headphones I've used. Again, (variations on a theme) the performance is good for $57 noise canceling headphones.

Comfort

The ANC27s are not comfortable. I have a large head (7 5/8 - 7 3/4) but small ears. They fit, but barely. My ears touch the foam inserts inside the cavity, which at first is not noticeable but leads to mild fatigue in as little as 30 mins. They are also hot. They do not breath well, they are tight, and the plasticky leatheris not nearly as comfortable as Bose AE style cans. I suspect I can wear these for a 2-3 hour flight but I suspect that I'll be glad to take them off at the end. I can wear my Bose AE2s and QC15s for hours, all day even without discomfort (they may be a little warm but its not worth taking off). Comfort is, in my mind, the worst part of these headphones but the sound quality is a close second.

Suggested Improvement

The obvious improvement for these headphones almost goes without saying: they need a cable with an inline mic with remote. The good news is you can make one with a Bose AE2i replacement cable [[ASIN:B0059F3EXG AE2 inline remote and microphone cable]]. The bad news it costs $30. The worst news, you need to grind off the rubber fitting. I tried this tonight by using my benchtop belt sander. I was careful and took my time and the entire experiment lasted 2 minutes. It worked with my iPhone 4 and ANC27's. Attempt at your own risk and use appropriate PPE and don't say I didn't warn you. But it's worth $30 to me to be able to remotely control my volume, music, and have a phone conversation with the ANC27s on.

Bottom Line

The less than stellar (Incubus is on right now) sound quality and discomfort of the ANC27 headphones earned them an honest 3 stars. These headphones may be a 5 star for value but I wanted to present a sincere and honest review of the ANC27's performance. Bose QC15's would be a 5 star. I nearly gave them 4 stars but I figured I can upgrade them later if I feel like it. I'm sure I'd want to downgrade the 4 star to a 3 star in the future as the excitement of a new toy further decays.

Worth the $$$? You decide.

Do you want the gold standard QC15 quality, quiet, and comfort (get it?)? Spend $300.

Want a cheap alternative that performs at about 50-75% the level of QC15s at 20% of the price? ANC27s will do that.

product_title: Smith Skullcandy Single-Shot Helmet Audio Kit
review_body: If you like to ski to music, but can't stand earbuds, take a quick read about these things.    I have two equal, but different, sets of the Single Shots. I bought a pair of skullcandy drop-in's at Mt Snow a little while back (not Amazon) and have skied with them for about 10 hours total.  The sound was, actually, quite good; better than I expected.  However, the clicker thing (the button you press to pause, skip, etc) broke after three presses.  Three.  Within 1 minute there was no longer a way to pause or skip songs.  The volume selector is on a wheel, but a bit sensitive (should be on a \\"click,\\" not a smooth \\"roll\\").  If you bumped it, the volume went either through the roof or dead silent.  I expected more for $50, but given the selections available, I figured these would have to do, and so far they've been ok, soundwise.    However, I was looking to trade up and decided to purchase the set here on Amazon only AFTER I contacted Smith Helmets DIRECTLY and asked them if they had an alternative to Skullcandy, because the reviews were soooo bad.  They told me Skullcandy had changed their manufacturer last year and that the quality was much better for the 2012-2013 season.  With that in mind, I gave them a go.  These must be an older model: the clicker broke after FOUR presses, and the sound is like something out of an AM transistor radio from 1983.  I fiddled with the connections, phone settings, etc and got the same terrible sound over and over again.  Unbelievable.  I've gone back to the old set, and will have to deal with the inability to change/pause songs, unless I want to take off my glove when it's 10 degrees outside, dig into my pocket and manually press the buttons.    And while these are both Skullcandy Single Shots, the ones I have (that work) are white, while the other crappy ones (bought on Amazon) are black, and came in a box that specifically said \\"Smith Helmets\\" across the top (I have a Smith Vantage ski helmet).  The ones in the pic here on Amazon are not the same that were delivered, either.    I'm beyond surprised these things are so awful.  I've had a Skullcandy pipe dock for years and the sound is great.  It was like $25.  These headsets aren't worth a tenth of that, with the piss poor sound and quality of the controls.  I can't believe I've spent this much time on a review, but I don't get skiing often, so when I do I want s  *** that works, especially for $50.  I should've known better after reading the lame product description too, about \\"silky beats\\" and \\"shredder heaven.\\"  Give me a break.  Smith needs to switch providers, and I can't believe there isn't a bigger market for this.  Helmets are EVERYWHERE on the slopes on both coasts, and I know earbuds aren't for everyone.  This is as simple as it gets, and man what a disappointment.  It's 2013 for Pete's sake.    Bottom line; the white pair are good if you don't mind a broken clicker, and avoid the ones made for Smith with the black casing.  I just sent an email to the vendor for a return.

After breaking mine in using the JLAB's dedicated "break-in" webpage, and after normal use as well, they sound much better than when I tried them right out of the box.

With that said, the sound quality is exceptional on these headphones. I can hear low frequencies that I couldn't notice before from my skullcandy's. I also notice more depth in the music I listen to, as if I am listening to a sound system with three speaker types.

The only one con about these headphones is that they don't straighten out easily. They curl up and twist a lot and I've been having a difficult time getting them to straighten out. This issue though is negligible and can be overseen.

Overall these headphones deliver exceptional sound quality and have a very stylish look to them. I do recommend these headphones to anyone who wants to enjoy full range, deep bass, and stunning clarity. I also strongly recommend that whoever buys these headphones must break them in before using them to get the full experience.

review_body:

Couple of self inflicted issues:

Firstly, I did not really realize how big these speakers are. The front 2-speakers are almost a foot and a half tall, not exactly a big deal but it does make the room look a little cluttered.

Secondly, the center speaker is over 8 inches in width. If you have your TV on it's factory stand, you will have a difficult time finding room for your center speaker. I ended up putting mine behind the TV, partially on the stand and slightly hanging off the back of the entertainment center. Again not a big deal but just makes the setup appear less organized. Third, Like the prior points the rear speakers are pretty large as well. I bought 4 stands for the rear speakers but the speakers do not sit well on the stand. Their weight made the stand lean in one or another direction, not a big deal but it was a pain in the ass to get the speaker to sit correctly on the stand. The speakers do not have a mount to \\"bolt on\\" to the stand but do have a hook to hang onto a wall screw.

Like others have posted, the cables that are provided with this system were very weak. Ended up purchasing my own wiring, but again not a big deal....

UPDATE 6/27/2013:
I've had this unit now for 4 months so it is due for an updated review:

Firstly, I've had HDMI issues like others have noted. A couple of solutions that have completely eliminated the problem. I did a full reset of the receiver by press and holding the \\"VCR/DVR\\" button while doing that press the \\"STANDBY/ON\\" button. You will see the word \\"Clear\\" in the display screen and the receiver will go into standby mode. I had some custom settings but I did not reconfigure them as I felt this may be creating additional complications (I may retry this againand update this review later)

I unplugged the power to the receiver, let it sit for a minute, and then plugged it back restarted it. Mind you, I lost all of my setting but the problem went way for now. IT DID HAPPEN AGAIN though and I discovered this is primary a handshake issue between the cable box, receiver and the TV. You MUST turn on the receiver first, then the video source and then the TV LAST. At least this works for me and I have not had a HDMI signal issue going on two months now.

Second issue, the back right speaker makes crackling noises during some action movies. I haven't fixed it and it doesn't always happen but it may be a production issue or something. Not a big deal but it is annoying

product_title: V-MODA Crossfade M-80 Vocal On-Ear Noise-Isolating Metal Headphone
review_headline: Not as awesome as you would think
review_body:
***Edit - Headphones broke two weeks after opening. The plug within the one headphone just \\"popped\\" and that side won't play music anymore. My guess is they just rely on a solder joint to support the plug alone. If the hardware isn't soldered right or it's off kilter, after a few listens and few times setting the headphones down the solder joint fails. Apparently it's not a major problem for everyone else, but considering the uncomfortable pads and the lack of bass along with them breaking I'm passing on trying another set of these. Moving on to something else.

Overall they are a good set of headphones. They sound decent, are built like a tank, and fit decently. I honestly thought about returning them, but they are built like a tank. That was one of the big things I was looking for. I've broke or wore out too many cheaper pairs that it just seemed worth it to buy something better. If it weren't for the lack of bass and some of the life in the music I would probably be completely content with them. They seemed to have gotten better with some burn in time, but maybe that's just me getting used to them.

Sound: The sound was really not what I was expecting. I understand that they are supposed to have a relatively flat response. They seem to have that across the board except for bass. Wow was I underwhelmed! They sound like they are slightly muted in that range. The bass is there, but there is no \\"punch\\". None. They also seem to lack something in the highs. Not sure how to describe it, but nothing really just \\"pops\\". Otherwise everything is very clear and distinct compared to anything else I've ever heard. Little details from songs like the details of a bass drum or little details from a singers voice just seem to have appeared in songs.

Build quality: First thing picking them up out of the box that I thought was heavy. They feel solid and I don't think breaking will be a problem. Not too much to say here really except they feel like they will last for a while.

Fit/comfort: They aren't as comfortable as you would think. They hurt my ears after a while to the point I have to pull them off and rest for a while before putting them back on. Also they slide off my head easy. I've tried adjusting the fit by extending the sides of the headphones as well as bending them and it still seems to be a small issue.

Other notes: When it gets cold the little connectors that hold the actual speakers and housings (\\"cans\\") seems to creek and rattle sort of. I need to find a small allen wrench and snug them up to see if it helps, but it's rather annoying when walking. It seems to click every step. The cord that comes with the headphones does weird things with my Android phone. When I push the button on it random things turn on. Not really their fault and not necessarily an awful thing since I had no need to use them as a microphone. The way the cord comes out of the headphones is also annoying when wearing a jacket. It's a very solid connection, but the plug is straight which seems to catch on the collar of my jacket every time I wear them. I feel like an angled plug would have been better. That way there was some give and didn't just pull that side of the headphones off when it caught or got nudged when moving my head.

product_title: Logitech Pure-Fi Express Plus Omnidirectional Speaker Dock for iPod and iPhone
review_headline: One of The BEST iPod Players for The Price
review_body: I have this Logitech product and I am so happy with it. I own the Bose SoundDock and the sound coming from this device is decent. Although the sound cannot compare with the Bose SoundDock's it is costs a whole lot less. Just for the record, the Bose SoundDock has a deeper bass and a much clearer sound. Still, I do like the sound that comes out of this player. It has a a very pleasant sound that is neither too bassy or too trebly. It just sits in the middle and is pleasant to listen to. It is even better than the other Logitech Pure-Fi iPod players because the sound just delivers all around the room. I cannot say enough for this product. I can't believe that the price for it is so low compared to its competitors when in fact it sounds better than all of them. I also have the other Pure-Fi iPod players and the only thing they have over this model is that they can be charged and then taken anywhere. This model cannot be recharged but will take batteries. I like the convenience of being able to take the other Pure-Fi anywhere without having to fumble for batteries. Other than that I love the sound that comes out of these babies. My Bose SoundDock will now be second string to this one. What I also love about this model is that it actually has a visually appealing clock. The black lacquer appearance of the iPod player stands in contrast to the clocks bright digits which I think is stylish. I love the combination knob and button. You simply press the knob to turn off the unit. This same button is used as a knob to control the volume. The Bose SoundDock does not have a power button at all and must be turned off with the remote. That was a very poor design decision on Bose's part. Further, the Bose SoundDock's volume control is rather a pain to use. I like the feel of the volume control on the Logitech. The remote for the Logitech is well designed and has a better appearance than the other Pure-Fi models and definitely better than Bose's. Overall, I highly recommend this iPod player for the value.

product_title: AmazonBasics High Speed HDMI Cable

One thing to note about this particular cable is that it's rather thick. This did cause issues for a bit as my PlayStation 3 sat close to the wall. Because of the cable's thickness it resisted the bending required, but after a slight change to my setup I experienced no further issues. I've been purchasing AmazonBasics USB and HDMI cables, and still have no reason to look elsewhere.

Highly recommended for both price and quality. 5 of 5 stars.

product_title: Kinivo 501BN Premium 5 port High speed HDMI switch with IR wireless remote and AC Power adapter - supports 3D, 1080p
review_headline: Works great--but does not auto-switch off of PS3 input
review_body:
I have had this for a couple weeks now, and I wanted to hold off the review until I had gotten to use it for a while. My setup includes my computer which is used for both gaming as well as watching TV, a PS3 and an XBox 360.

This works exactly as described. There is no quality loss (which is expected since it is powered). The nicest feature is the auto-switching. As soon as you power on a different device, it automatically switches to that device. Then, when you turn it off, it goes back to the last device using it that is still on. For example, I will be watching TV on my computer, then turn on my Xbox, and it switches automatically. When I turn my Xbox off, it switches back to my computer as long as it's still on.

That being said, the second part does not work with my PS3. When I turn the PS3 on, it switches like normal. However, when I turn the PS3 off, it does not switch back to the previous device. I think this has to do with the fact that the PS3 is always drawing power, so the switch cannot tell it is off. In any case, it's a minor annoyance that I don't mind.

The only real downside is the placement of the HDMI output. They opted to put the output on the side, which makes wire management a little difficult. I would rather have 3 inputs on the back, along with the output (like in the 3-port model), then the other 2 inputs on either side. This is the real reason I gave it 4 stars instead of 5.

product_title: FiiO E10 USB DAC Headphone Amplifier
review_body: Want to add some life to your crappy mp3s?  Then you want a DAC!  And this little bad boy is a fantastic bang for your buck.  I decided to check it out after blogger audiophiliac from CNET gave it a positive review:  [...]    My music really does get a great boost in quality.  With my [[ASIN:B000065BPB Sennheiser HD-280 PRO Headphones]] and it sounds just wonderful.  The coax output is also handy to connect to my home theater.  Here's the little trick they don't tell you in the manual; the default settings are 16-bit/44.1khz.  Change it to 24-bit/48khz or 96khz, opening up the extra 8 bits allows for noticeably more detail.  It's very small, perfect for a soldier on the go like moi.    I've read a bunch of reviews, and there does seem to be quality issues, but after 2 months mine is holding up well.  DACs do benefit from burn-in, and I can say that after some use, the bass seems fuller than when I first got it.  While on the subject of bass, maybe its just me, but my experience with the bass boost is that it's pretty meh. . .maybe if you use ipod headphones or small desktop speakers; But I'm use decent audio equipment, it just adds a muddled overbearing boominess.    Can you get a better DAC for more money?  Hell yes.  But if you're looking for quality, affordability, and portability, this might be just what you're looking for.

product_title: RCA RCRPS06GR 6 Device Universal Remote
review_body: This lovely device makes me think, \\"Why, oh, why didn't I get one of these five years ago.\\" It's hard to overstate how satisfying it is to lose the remote-control smorgasborg. The price is less than one good pizza, so if you feel the need, I advise to just get it. This particular unit, the RCA RCRPS06GR, has a number of features I like. A minor one is the backlight so I don't have to turn on the lights to see which button I need. Much more crucial is the \\"learning mode\\". You see, I happen to have a very old Dolby pro-logic decoder by MidiLand and it is *never* on any supported devices list. Thanks to this RCA's \\"learning mode\\", the new remote can now control my old MidiLand decoder. It also controls my Panasonic TV, Panasonic DVD player and Aveo Set-Top-Box for Cable/DVR. Four separate devices with one remote. The other devices were all setup from RCA's pre-supported device list. And the few features that weren't given a button were simply recorded in \\"learning mode\\", which lets you program any key. There are macro capabilities I didn't bother with, and a multiple device power on/off feature I found didn't work too well. One think to keep in mind is, you absolutely must RTFM (read the freakin' manual) to use this, and you will need two hands. Without the manual you will never know the various device codes or special button combinations to use for programming. Getting it all setup for my system took about an hour, but being a nerdy kind of guy, I actually had fun. I hate to be one of these \\"five star\\" reviewers, and I'm sure plenty of other multi-device remote controls would do the job, but this is the one I got, and it does exactly what it is supposed to do, and I love it. Five stars it is.

product_title: SuperMediaStore Glossy CD Jewel Case Inserts For Laser or Inkjet Printers 50 Sheets
review_headline: Horrible software; perforations are a joke
review_body:
I tried the recommended software for this and it was lame. For the life of me, I couldn't figure out how to print both the inserts at the same time. Doing them separately means extra work, as well as destroying the previously printed insert that gets scraped up on the second pass. I ended up just doing them both in photoshop and printing from there. Once I got my printer settings right (Canon Pixma MG6220 http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B005GOPXRA/ref=cm_cr_ryp_prd_ttl_hst_1), I was really impressed with the print quality.

EDIT: I hadn't tried to take the inserts out of paper yet. It's not very well perforated, so they're REALLY difficult to take out. I just did some Avery business cards that were super easy to pop apart, but this is a joke. I have to be really careful to not bend my artwork and screw it up when I'm trying to bend the paper to get the perforated part to break open. review_headline: For those thinking its sound is too "muddy/mushy"
review_body:
First of all, I already have a Triplefi 10. So, I had high hopes for this one too.
I got the mic-less version here during Gold Box deal for $84.99 during the Cyber Monday week.
My first impressions were not so good about this. Although, I loved the packaging and all the goodies it comes with.
It shows that Klipsch really put thought into the 'presentation' aspect of their products.

The earphones came with a medium silicone tips installed.
I then switched to the large double flanges, still not getting a good fit (but I didn't realize it then).
The sound was HORRIBLE! They're mushy and muddy. The highs were so unpleasant. I was so disappointed that I
went to google and eventually headfi.org to read if there's a burn-in period for these bad boys and if other people
had the same impressions and gotten better as they were more burned-in.

THEN, I switched the tips to the large ones - the biggest in the set. And VOILA!
No more mushy or muddiness! I figured that at the end of the day, it was all about getting the a DECENT seal/fit.

So, if anyone is not really happy at first with their X10, I'd recommend them to try a larger tip before
posting them for sale on ebay.

All in all, I give this one a 4 star. I would not get them at the full price, considering I already have a Triplefi 10
and very happy with it. BUT for $84.99, it was a no-brainer.

Since it only does passive switching and does not hold all ports active, it cannot prevent my xbox 360 from rebooting when changing inputs (Xbox will reset if there is an audio dongle present, and the HDMI signal is disconnected and reconnected).

Additionally while the main device construction is solid, the remote is exactly the same as my cheap noname 3x1 switch's remote. That means the internals are probably produced at the same place as well (this is also consistent with the xbox reboot issue, which I have with the cheaper one).

While my previous experience with Belkin was much better, this switch was disappointing. Since it does not always work, and does not have any advanced features, I cannot really recommend the purchase. review_body: As the other reviewers have said, this is a waste of money.  The construction is cheap, flimsy, brittle plastic of the sort you'd find in bad carnival prizes.  You know, the blister-packed Walkman knockoffs in bright colors and horrible fake chrome from twenty-five years ago (and hey, whaddaya know, these are made in China, too!) that your little sibling or niece or nephew that was hopped up on cotton candy hounded you for and after spending fifteen bucks and half an hour at the rigged game you finally won for them and it broke by the next afternoon.  And then you found one just like it at the dollar store the next week.  Basically, it's one of those, but with a USB interface and cable and a nicer package.  The motor is incapable of turning a 90 minute Chrome Oxide cassette at the required speed, so even if the batteries held up through a complete play, you'd have a slow, warbly copy of your tapes.  Perhaps with shorter tapes and luck of the draw on the build you might get a unit that could play at proper, consistent speed, or you might have better luck using an AC adapter, but this doesn't come with one.  Personally, I'm writing this one off as a learning experience.  The little USB cable and the Audacity software are nice to have, though, so it's not a total loss.  Then again, I'm one of those who sees the little plastic cup as being half full rather than half empty, even though what's in it is a urine sample.

product_title: Peerless HDSWHDI100 Wireless HD Multimedia System
review_body:
When I initially ordered this thing, I was not sure what it was. What it is is a multimedia transmitter/receiver that transmits the audio/video of 2 devices to a receiver located (up to) 100 ft away. It is very easy to set up, just plug your 2 components into the transmitter, plug the transmitter into your primary TV, and then you plug the receiver into your secondary TV.

My goal was to get my DVR and my PS3 (located in my basement) to transmit upstairs to my family room. Right now, my family room TV is only hooked to a DVD player because I'm too cheap to get a 2nd DVR. This solution seemed perfect, as it would allow me to both watch all my stuff upstairs in HD with this device.

In the end, I can tell you that it works very well, but not as I had liked.
Below are some pros and cons.
Pros:
- The audio/video quality is flawless. There is no latency despite the fact it is transmitting through walls. The transmitter are separated by about 2 walls and 1 floor (a linear distance of about 25 ft) and a walking distance of approximately 55 ft.
- The setup is extremely easy. It took me no time at all - I just had to put this box in between the media and the TV, that's it!

Cons:
- My setup did not go as I had planned. The transmitter has 2 HDMI in ports, but only 1 HDMI out port. This means that it doubles as a SWITCHING ADAPTER. I didn't need this - my devices are all plugged into an A/V receiver, I don't need another switching device.
- You can only watch 1 device on both TVs at a time. You don't have the option to pass-through the DVR on TV1 and transmit the PS3 on TV2. This thing was designed to have the transmitter in the same room (or adjacent room) as the receiver - if they are so close to each other, why would I want to watch the same source on both TVs?
- This was designed to be used within line of sight between transmitter and receiver. As I have utilized it in a different way, I can't use my IR remote to change the DVR channel (in my basement) from my family room.

In the end, I did not get the setup I wanted. The complexity with connecting both the DVR and the PS3 into the transmitter, and then connecting the transmitter to my Home Theater receiver created the need for me to use another remote control for the Peerless Wireless HD switching device. Furthermore, it would mess up my audio setup. Like many more of you who know your audio, each device requires different settings. I have programmed my receiver to customize the audio settings for it's HDMI1 (DVR) and HDMI2 (PS3) ports. If both of these devices are plugged into this product, I would be forced to have only 1 audio setting for the two.

I have a universal remote, so I could have made it work by adding this product's IR codes into it. However I don't want to be forced to switch between one device or the other on BOTH of my TVs - I want to be able to mix and match my devices with my TVs. The goal was to be able to still play my games upstairs while my family hijacked the home theater for a kids movie or show on the DVR. Or vice versa, if they want to hijack the PS3 to watch Tinkerbell on Blu-Ray, I could watch Burn Notice on the DVR. In the end, I decided use this product with only my PS3, and it works great - I can use my PS3 both upstairs and downstairs. I can now get my Netflix, Amazon Video, and can play my games upstairs, which is a lot more than I could do before, and all without any extra work or setup. All I have to do differently is keep one of my PS3 controllers upstairs!

IMO, this product should include 2 transmitters, each with 1 HDMI-in and 1 HDMI-out port. This way they would simply be a simple in-line box between the multimedia device and the TV. Then the receiver can receive both transmissions, and then you could switch FROM THE RECEIVER BOX which transmitter you wanted to watch from.

review_headline: I believe these are the best value available
review_body:
I purchased these in-ear headphones after considerable research. My previous earphones were Beats. They lasted nearly two years, but were completely done after this period of time. I believe in-ear headphones should last longer than two years if they cost $120. I use these Klipsch S4 the same way I used my Beats: for walking 1-3 miles each day, periodically at the gym if my wireless gym headset runs out of battery, and on planes when I pack light and choose not to take a headphone with me.

About me - I care a great deal about my music quality and consider myself somewhat of an audiophile. But I also care about price for an in-ear headphone. I have my expensive Sennheisers for when I really want to hear the intracacies of music. I also consider myself a purveyor of music in that I have a basic comprehension of music production and quality beyond the average listened. For example, I interned for MTV in 2000-2001 (Making the Band), I also own Sennheiser headphones for my office (HD 650, these are my "nice" ones), noise-cancelling Sony headphones for the plane, Motorola blueooth for jogging and the gym, and Ludacris' on-ear Souls for when I need my ears to breathe. Anyway, after all my online research I decided to purchse the Klipsch S4s for $78.

The sound quality is 8/10. The music is head how it is intended, but it can't quite compete with the Sennheisers. The noise-canceling is excellent for in-ear headphones. When I wear these with no music the fit is tight and I can barely hear the outside noise. When music plays your surroundings wash away. You hear basically nothing but the music. The bass and treble where it should be (unlike Beats, where the bass and treble are so strong it sounds like crap).

The wires get tangled easily. This is a drawback and my biggest complaint having owned Beats previously. Monster definitely has the wiring down. The wires on the S4 don't just get tangled. They hold their tangled shape. This means you can't even make the wire straight without tugging on it. The wires are not long. I give the wires a 3/10. It is my sole complaint.

Finally, I purchased these and they worked well for nearly 4 months. Then the copper input seemed to lose its connectivity. I was not happy. I did not pay $80 for 4 months of use. I called Klipsch. They were in touch with me quickly, even over the Xmas holidays, and offered a replacement immediately. Furthermore, I felt as though the individual I was working with (Greg Niehaus) was honestly worried about my issue. review_body:
Many listeners were initially (and understandably) reluctant to spend either money or time on the tiny in-ear (IEM) headphones that began to dominate the market 6-7 years into the present millennium. It simply made no sense that these miniature devices could produce the spacious, private sonic universes of full-sized headphones or their somewhat smaller, lightweight cousins. Manufacturers routinely included with their CD players, cassette machines, FM radios, etc., \\"disposable\\" reproductions of headphones that were half the size and weight of the phones prized by audiophiles. But though judged inferior in sound quality, these smaller phones motivated listeners to seek similar-sized phones but with the audio quality associated with the full-sized, studio-style models. In this category, the two that emerged as the best values--the most compact headphones offering the biggest sound at the smallest price--were the [[ASIN:B000089GN3 Sennheiser PX 100 Lightweight Collapsible Headphones]] and the \\"dark-horse\\" [[ASIN:B00001P4ZH Koss PortaPro Headphones with Case]]. The Sennheiser phones were the \\"winners\\" in terms of comfort, endurance, and the \\"smoothness\\" of the full-textured tones, with accurate as well as balanced representation of all registers of the musical scale. The Koss phones, considered somewhat \\"odd\\" in appearance, nevertheless remained the preference of a vocal minority, who found them equally full-frequencied but producing a somewhat \\"punchier,\\" more incisive, reproduction of the low ends of the spectrum without sacrificing natural, mid-range presence.

The point of the foregoing is to explain MEElectronics' addition of \\"travel lightweight headphones with swivel cups\\" to its line-up (the manufacturer entered the market several years ago strictly as a maker of budget-priced, high-quality \\"ear-buds\\" and \\"in-ear\\" phones) and to identify the precise niche of the MT-21 headphones. In terms of build-quality and sound, the MEElectronics headphones deserve comparison with the aforementioned phones by Sennheiser and Koss. On a recent trip to California, I took a pair with me along with the Koss Porta-Pros. Compared to the Koss phones, the MEElectronics had more bang and pop. Bass sounds were thunderous while the treble end of the piano resonated with unaccustomed vibrancy. Nevertheless, I suspect that listeners accustomed to the head-banging sounds of the multi-channel Dolby systems of most present-day theater systems will prefer the MEElectronics to either the Porta-Pro or Sennheiser phones.

But not all listeners are thrill-seekers. Listeners who favor full-frequencied but more evenly balanced audio with accurate representation of the discrete sounds of an ensemble will still most likely be drawn to the Sennheisers, with the Koss Porta-Pros somewhere in-between, perhaps the best bet for the listener who alternates between classical chamber music and big band jazz. review_headline: Solid wireless Bluetooth clock! Wouldn't sync with our iPad 2.
review_body:
Right out of the box I thought I could get away with not reading the instructions, but I couldn't. Sadly, the instructions are not all that clear. The instructions state that it has an AUTOSET CLOCK: \\"... meaning the clock will automatically set itself when first plugged in...to Eastern Standard time and will need to be adjusted for other time zones...\\" I live in Eastern Standard time, and I can tell you the time was not correct, nor was the date; I had to manually set it. I was a bit disappointed with this, the [[ASIN:B005KQ2O2G Logitech s400i 30-Pin iPod/iPhone Alarm Clock Speaker Dock]] that we own automatically sync time and calendar when you dock your phone. That would have been a nice touch on the HX-B440 Cube. However, interesting to note that the Cube does not have a docking station, which is actually a good thing considering that most people have cases on their phones that prevent docking! With the Cube you get a USB port you can use to charge your phone; works great, but it's a bit slow to charge over a wall charger.

Trying to set up Bluetooth with my iPhone 4 I had a bit of a problem with the instructions, which state \\"Use the Source button on the Cube to select Bluetooth.\\" It doesn't work. You have to select POWER first, and then press SOURCE to toggle to Bluetooth. Once I did that I paired my iPhone quickly. My husband didn't have any problem either. However, our iPad 2 would NOT sync. product_title: Klipsch IMAGE S4 -Ear Enhanced Bass Noise-Isolating Headphones
review_headline: Great value when on sale, cord can be annoying
review_body:
I wear isolating plugs daily for about 4 hours a day during my commute.

My previous plugs, that I still have (have owned these for at least 8 years) are Shure E2C's and I picked these Klipsch plugs up due to the really great sale price.

The sound quality is really nice, they have a warmer and bassier presentation than the Shures do, lending a bit more towards my personal preference and needing less EQ on the player. They have about the same efficiency as far as output goes and give plenty of playback volume from the Android phone I use to drive them.

The sound isolation seems to be in par with the Shures as well. It's critical with these types of plugs to get a full seal on them for both isolation and proper fidelity and response. A note, if you don't like the feel of foam hearing protection plugs properly sealed in your ears, don't bother with this type of plug as you won't get the seal needed for the performance any other way. It's a cheap test before shelling out for canal phones, just get a pair of disposable foam crush hearing protection from a hardware store and see if you tolerate them fully and properly expanded in your ears.

The cord is quite a lot thinner than the E2C cord, which is plainly a monster design and very heavy duty. However I feel the quality of material on the cord may hold up o.k. over time. It's very thin but made solidly.

The one nitpick that I have is fairly annoying though. I prefer the 'sports' style fit where the ear buds are rotated so the cord winds up pointing to the front and slightly upwards. This gives the best seal for me and the cord is intended to wrap up and lie over the top of the ear ear from the front. They seal better at this angle and this also seems to reduce the 'microphonics'/thumping from the cord when you move around.

The issue is the cord material doesn't seem to relax over time very much so the cord doesn't lay in a relaxed way over the topof the ear and tends to 'spring' free if you move around. It's fairly annoying.

A good buy otherwise, particularly in the $40 range they are going for if you time it right.

product_title: Pyle Hi-Fi Wireless FM Headphones
review_body:
According to my experience, if you want to enjoy the stereo sound from any source such as CD and DVD players, TVs, movies, you should not buy a Wireless RF headset with an FM feature. When turning the headset on, the FM stations will prevail, and it's very difficult for you to tune your stereo from your TV, Computer, CD changer, and whatsoever...into your headphones. I have bought 2 Wireless headsets with FM radio features and encountered the same problem, and I have to returned them to the stores where I have bought them. Previously, I have bought a Sennheiser set HDR-120 without FM stations with the price of $69.99 at Fry's Electronics in San Jose, CA, and I am very happy to have it. The bass is not very strong but enough for you to enjoy the movies or the music without damaging your hearing capability. The treble is very clear that pleases your taste. The headset is easy to tune in the source of music you have chosen. The instruction also says that the headset will automatically turned off if you set the volume too low. That's normal, and I find it not a big problem. The instruction also says that the listening range is 100 meters, but I never go that far. I walk around the house, the garage, the back yard,the kitchen, the bathroom, and I still hear the music from the transmitter.
In brief, if you want to enjoy the quality of the headset, don't buy a cheap one and the ones with FM stations. \\"Cheap thing is not good, and good thing is not cheap.\\" That's the Motto I have applied in my life.

product_title: Cheetah APTMM2B TV Wall Mount for 20-75" TVs up to VESA 600 and 165lbs, and fits 16” And 24” Wall Studs, and includes a Tilt TV Bracket, a 10' Twisted Veins HDMI Cable and a 6" 3-Axis Magnetic Bubble Level
review_headline: Flawed, but great for the money
review_body: The unit arrived quickly and in great shape, upon opening the packaging, it became clear that this was of less-quality than some other more-expensive mounts. It was missing a few nuts and bolts that connect the two-side pieces together. The two vertical supports were not formed correctly either, this made the unit off-kilter and not square. I was able to mount the mount in place easily enough and use my level to square it on the wall before securing it down all the way. Once secure it easily hung my 46' LED TV. For the money, this product will work, but do not be disappointed if the product is missing pieces or is not entirely square. It includes some bonuses like a free level and HDMI cable, but do not use the included level, it is of poor quality and will not be able to accurately measure if the mount is perfectly level.

product_title: Sennheiser Headphones
review_body:
I got tired of replacing my cheap, easily broken headphones every month, so I did some research for a high-quality, reasonably priced product and found a wealth of good reviews about the Sennheiser HD518. If you use cheap $20 headphones, you will be blown away by the quality of Sennheiser! You can easily tell the difference in your music with these. Sounds have much richer bass and crisper treble, yet the two balance perfectly. The range allows you to hear elements of your music that you may have missed before. Indeed, this product gives you a whole new listening experience.

These cushion-y phones are also comfortable on the head and ears, and the over-the-ear design allows for better immersion. However, if you wear glasses, you'll need to take them off to wear these. After several minutes it becomes uncomfortable. Fortunately I haven't found this to be a problem. My glasses can bend outward and rest on the outside of the phones in the grooves and they stay in place.

Using these phones has given me new appreciation for music. I've since upgraded my audio card to get the most from these phones -- what a difference! Even better, after a year plus of use I haven't noticed the slightest defect. I am very impressed with this product and will ONLY buy Sennheisers in the future!

product_title: Monoprice Noise Isolating Earphones
review_body:
Like everyone else, I agree that for the price you get some damn good sound out these earbuds. especially notable it that it has respectable bass which is damn near impossible to find in cheap earbuds. These are the only ones I've found to be inexpensive while giving a hardy bass and a generally clean unmuddled sound. Hands down these are the best in the price range and even give competition to more expensive sound equiptment.

The wire tangles all the freaking time and is a bitch to untangle. It is so annoying I deducted a star from the rating. It's inexpensive and thus forgivable, but higher-end buds have tangle resistant wires that these just ain't sporting.

They offer big enough sound that they are great for noisy commutes in public transit. You won't block out the sound of a trolley blasting by in a closed tunnel, but engine noise and chitter-chatter from folks around you pretty much melts away to a minimum and lets you listen to your music without interference. I often use my commute to catch up on podcasts which are mostly just people talking. Even those spoken word podcasts are easy to listen to while on a bus train or trolley.

Something else to note is that some people might dislike the tips it comes with. I bought the Sony EPEX10A Hybrid tips and use those with these which may have effected the sound quality I'm experience. I believe the Sony tips offer a better seal which I presume would greatly contribute to the quality of the Noise Isolation feature these Monoprice earbuds have (which would explain how awesome they are for public transit)

product_title: Bose SIE2 Sport Headphones - Green
review_body:
I love Bose's products and have always had good luck with their speakers and radios. The sound on these items is crystal clear and their performance rarely disappoints.

I've been content to use the headphones that come with my iPhone or iTouch on my runs. These white ear buds work fine for a while, but I've found that they tend to wear out in a matter of months. They do the job, but they're not the best for active/aerobic use. After a month or so... well, just take a close look at the speaker that fits into your ear after a good month's worth of active use; it can get kind of gross.

I am an avid runner and like listening to music or audio books while on the road, so my headphones get a lot of use. Bose's headphones come with three \\"StayHere\\" tips: small, medium, and large. The StayHere tips look a bit odd at first, but they fit snuggly and as the name implies, they stay in place during a run.

The headphones: There is a noticeable difference in sound. Tones come through full and rich, not as tinny as a standard pair of headphones. There is also an extension cable that provides an extra foot if you need it. I'm 6'1, and like to run holding my iPhone, so this works out perfect for me. I even like the lime green color. In a house with teenagers, I can instantly pick out my headphones from theirs.

The Armband: I wasn't all that crazy about the band; however, I typically don't run with one. It will be a nice extra for some, but wasn't a great fit for me. I did try it, but it felt like I was wearing a blood pressure cuff.

I wore these headphones during a 1/2 marathon in early October and they held up great. They helped me tune out and focus on running and the music without having to worry about them falling out halfway through. Truely powerful little speakers!

Sound: 5 out of 5
Durability: 4 out of 5

product_title: AUDIO TECHNICA Noise-Canceling Headphones
review_body:
Overall the sound reproduction is quite good, with deep bass and clear sound. Pretty comfortable too. The noise cancelling feature works pretty well for situations such as airplane noise and such. Doesn't block out speech or other more randomized noises though.

Unfortunately, and I'm not sure if these are common problems with these headphones, sounds hard panned to the left channel are dropped out of the signal completely and those hard panned to the right are centered. It's ok for movies but if you want to listen to music it sucks when a particular instrument is just missing from your favorite song. Perhaps this is a result of the fact that the 1/8th inch TRS cable is removable and often comes loose during normal wear causing either a complete drop in signal or weakening of it. The cable is supposed to lock into place with a quarter turn, but it doesn't always stay in place.

If you're planning on just using this on long jet flights then go for it, otherwise I would not recommend this product unless all your music is mixed monophonic.

product_title: Sony Bluetooth Speaker
review_body:
At $100 this has a lot of competition. Sony offered it directly for half that on Black Weekend, so I decided to bite. Physically, it's a very solid speaker, heavy enough to hurt someone if you brained them with it, and about twice the size of the Logitech mini boom box. Hard to find anything to compare its size to--I guess it's slightly larger than a 20 oz water bottle. Pairing was easy, it has a dedicated button that switches between BT and the 18\\" minijack, and it works with my iPhone and Mac.

Sonically, it's decent so far--not outstanding, and doesn't get very loud, but rarely distorts at top volume. I've used it for only a few hours... I think at this point I have to repeat myself: at $50 there's not much competition that sounds this good, but at $100 there probably is. So, three stars, an average product. I'm certainly not unhappy to have it, but I'm still looking for something better.

After a few days of use, I think it lacks the brightness in the high end that I like. The bass is decent and not overpowering or overly thumpy. I only listen to classical music, so if you're familiar with that, it sounds decent until you get to the complexity of an early classical symphony, and at that point the sound starts to become unclear. So it's fine for listening to chamber music, less so for operas and larger symphonies.

product_title: Koss Pro4AAT Titanium Pro Headphones
review_body:
The sound is amazing. The lows are as low as I need them to go (I am not a Bass-head). The highs are good, but not great. I am listening to Goldfish, Dr. John and Native American Flute Lullabies, the highs are present, but not overly so, the bass is there, but not booming and the mids are fantastic. The sound stage is getting better as I listen, although I am not sure if that is them breaking in or me getting used to it. If any noise is made, these pick it up, it is just not 'in your face'.

This is a high quality product that will last a while. There is nothing fragile or flimsy about the frame or construction. Upon first putting it on my head, I could feel the squeeze. I am used to the pressure now, but it does take a while. I have a big head, and at full stretch, these barely fit on my head; that said, I can feel the weight of the headband on the top of my head. These are not light, but I feel that the heavier weight is a give/take with the quality parts and construction.

The feel: Other than the weight, the ear cups also seem to be a bit of a burden. It will get hot after just a short time of use. The sound cancellation is not as good as I thought it would be. Others cannot hear what I am listening to, but I can hear them and what they are saying when I have them on not listening to anything. The inside of the cups has a nylon mesh, and because the cups are not deep at all, it is rubbing up against my ears. So there is that to deal with.

For the price, you are getting a set of headphones that will last a while. I can tell why Radio professionals would use these. I would purchase them again for the same price (Koss.com offers these for $20 more).

product_title: Marantz SR7005 Audio Video Receiver (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
My first high end receiver was a Yamaha RX-V1. It gave me many years of trouble free enjoyment. My next receiver was an Onkyo TX-NR805. It lasted 18 months when the display went blank. This was a defect on many of the 805 models. After being fixed under warranty it wouldn't power up a month after the warranty ended. I then bought an Onkyo TX-NR807. My mistake. The HDMI board went bad resulting in no audio. This is a defect on many of the 807 and other models for that year. After this I decided to dump Onkyo forever. One reason in deciding to buy the SR7005 is the 3 year warranty (2years for Onkyo). The SR7005 I purchased is made in Japan. No more Chinese Onkyo for me.

For my ears the sound quality is a toss up compared to the Onkyo. Gotta keep it honest.
The GUI looks nice and is easy too use. Some people don't like the small round display. I like it. It has a larger display behind the drop down door.
I've had zero problems with it. Everyting has worked smoothly with the airplay using my Asus Infinity tablet and my iPod touch. Fast response.
Playing mp3's with a thumb drive works very well. No hiccups.
No problems with Pandora via airplay. Spotify via airplay works great also.
The HD radio works well.
Like most receivers the remote has itty bitty buttons. I'm not going to deduct a star for that. Disagree all you want. My choice.
Not a deciding factor in my purchase but it has drop dead gorgeous looks.
For music my speakers are 4 ohm (KEF 104/2) and the receiver does not run hot even when pushed. For watching bly-rays my speakers are Polk Monitor 70's
with the CS2 center and monitor 40's for surrounds. A pair of Klipsch RW-12D are used for subwoofers. Maybe I missed something but I don't see any major difference
between this model and the new model.
Save yourself some bucks and buy this one instead of the newer model.
