product_title: Sony STRDN1030 7.2-Channel Network A/V Receiver (Built-in Wi-fi & Bluetooth)
review_headline: Best receiver I've owned so far - it is packed with features
review_body:
This is the best A/V receiver that I've owned so far. I've owned an [[ASIN:B0015S8PGW Onkyo TX-SR606]] and a [[ASIN:B004NHCGJO Sony STRDH520]] in the past. This receiver pumps out better sound and has ten times the number of features.

I'll skip going in to too much detail about things like the 5 HDMI inputs, the wattage, and the other bullet points that are clearly listed in the extensive product description here on Amazon. Instead, I'll focus on some of the other questions that I'd be left with as a potential buyer.

== BLUETOOTH ==
This A/V receiver allows for audio streaming over Bluetooth, so you can play music directly from your phone for example. I tested this feature using my Samsung Galaxy Nexus running Android 4.1 (Jelly Bean). This replaces my previous method of streaming audio from my phone, the [[ASIN:B004VM1T5S Logitech Wireless Speaker Adapter for Bluetooth Audio Devices]] that I had connected to my older Sony STR-DH520. This receiver can remember pairing information for 9 Bluetooth devices.

== WI-FI / NETWORK ==
There is an antenna on the back of the receiver for connecting via Wi-Fi. The range was fine in my living room. There is also an Ethernet port for a wired connection (my preference).

Before you customize the receiver's settings too much, be sure to download the latest update using the settings menu. The download was fast on my internet connection, but the update itself took about 30 minutes to be installed. After restarting, some of my speaker settings were lost and needed to be reset.

Using the network connection, you are able to play music on network DLNA servers, which I was able to do using mp3 files stored on my Windows 7 computer in another part of the house. (The receiver cannot play DRM-protected files.) There are also a number of services available using the \\"SONY Entertainment Network (SEN)\\". Many of the services, like Pandora and Slacker music streaming, are free and require minimal setup. For example, I linked to my Pandora account after logging in to SONY's special website (listed on the screen) and entering the receiver's code, so all of my Pandora stations and presets show up. I was also able to connect to Slacker's example stations without having to connect to any account. There are some other services available, including vTuner and a pay service called \\"Music Unlimited\\".

Another available feature is \\"Party Streaming\\", which requires Party Streaming-compliant devices. 20 of these devices can be saved to the list at a time. You may also play music from your compatible iOS devices using AirPlay.

There is an iOS/Android app called \\"SONY Media Remote\\" that allows you to control many aspects of this receiver from your smartphone via Wi-Fi. I installed on on my Galaxy Nexus running Android 4.1 and it works surprisingly well. Response time is just as fast as the regular remote. Personally, I probably won't use it all that much only because I prefer tactile buttons instead of a touchscreen when using a remote, but it will still be a cool thing to show off to visitors. :)

== AUDIO AND VIDEO ==
Yes, the audio and video is great, especially after using the included auto-calibration microphone. I am using this receiver with a Dish Network receiver, a PS3, a Logitech Revue with Google TV, a three year old 46-inch Samsung LCD TV, and an [[ASIN:B001202C44 Energy 5.1 Take Classic Home Theater Speaker]] set. HDMI handshaking (the amount of time it takes for audio/video to connect when changing inputs) does not take too long, a few seconds at most. The speaker connections on the back allow for twisting the speaker wires and clamping them in, or you can use banana-plugs as I do.

== GUI MODE ==
Most of the advanced features of this receiver are best used in GUI mode, which is a crude-looking, text only screen representation of the menus and information like the currently playing Pandora song. This feature is slightly obnoxious and could have been so much better because all of the text displays only a few characters at a time and then scrolls the rest at a very slow pace, even though there is plenty of room on the screen to display more characters at a time. It would be great if they would fix this in a future downloadable update.

== ONE MONTH LATER ==
I am a huge fan of sci-fi/action movies that have incredible special effects and sound... sometimes at the expense of storylines. Movies like \\"2012\\" and \\"Transformers: Dark of the Moon\\" come to mind. Well, I just watched \\"Battleship\\" on BluRay with this receiver and my Energy speakers. I turned the volume up louder than I have ever done with my other receivers. My ears are almost bleeding. I can't even critique the movie all that much because the visuals and the audio were so amazing with this setup.

== SUMMARY ==
This is a great receiver, and I am very happy with it. There are many features that I haven't delved into because I do not have compatible devices (an iOS device, Party Streaming devices, etc). But the features I have used above are great and are ones that I have never had on a receiver before.

review_headline: I SPENT WAY TOO MUCH FOR THIS...
review_body:
I didn't actually get this off of amazon, but I use amazon a lot and feel like making a short review or rather, share my opinion of these cans. First of all, I got these for ONE HUNDRED DOLLARS...!! Double the amazon price, and I can say straight off, for a hundred dollars, it is NOT worth it. -There are many better sounding headphones at this price, no doubt. Buut, as it is on Amazon - $50 - I say Not a bad price. The Build quality (while it lasted) is good - as they describe and advertise it, and it will hold up to every day use. The cable is also quite nice, it doesn't have any cable rubbing noise, is almost tangle-free and of course is durable + you can use it an extender for other headphones or earphones. Unfortunately, stretching the headband constantly to 180 degrees will slowly benefit to the process of its destruction. I did this to show off to people all the time (as a joke...if that makes sense) and just now when doing the same thing, the left side of the band has cracked and is close to completely snapping off. This is of course my own fault, but just a warning: DO NOT KEEP BENDING THEM TO SHOW OFF...haha

To me, the sound was okay and really not so bad considering the price point. The bass is quite a bit more muffled than desired and does not reach too low, but there is quantity (like others say, comparable to beats, but of course not nearly as much - good thing.) The mids are perhaps recessed, but not too much and still plays vocals decently. The highs aren't so bad but are probably not something that stands out much, still decent though. Soundstage - kind of poor, sounds bloated and the instruments and singers are further away. It may seem like I'm bashing on the phones (literally..) but this is sheerly my opinion of them.

They play most genres decently. I found myself liking electronica, dubstep, rap and (maybe) pop more, but not so much classical and more mid-centric genres. Well, that's just what I think~

All in all,as I've stated, not a bad headphone and nice for travelling. Although it does not excel, it gets the job done for a reasonable price. It plays music fairly well, is comfortable, it's light and it's durable. If you really like it then go ahead, otherwise do some research and find a better sounding phone for the same price, or even better save up for a real keeper :)

product_title: Barnes & Noble NOOK Simple Touch with GlowLight, Wi-Fi, 2GB, Includes Power Adapter
review_body:
I bought one of the first Nook Touches in 2011, and have been very happy with it (aside from occasional image ghosting issues). When my wife kept taking mine to read, I decided to get her one, and the Nook w/ Glowlight had just came out.

The internal light works great, and we happy with the device for a few weeks. Then one night it accidentally slid off her nightstand about 18 inches onto carpeting. The next night she turned it on and two very obvious cracks were in the screen (only visible when Glowlight is on). The cracks weren't subtle either, but are much brighter than the normally visible glow. When the Glowlight was off, you couldn't tell there was any problem.

I looked it up on the internet, and found a page where someone had a picture of the exact same problem. So I took the Nook back to B&N, and they wouldn't let me exchange it or get a refund. I didn't give up, however, and decided to demonstrate how fragile the screen is. I held my keys over the Nook (about 6 inches above it) and dropped them. 3 more cracks instantly appeared. The manager then let me return the device, and I got a normal (non-glowing) Nook instead. (FYI: The newer Nooks do not have the occasional ghosting issue, and non-glowing Nooks are quite sturdy in my experience).

If they had not let me return it, I would have taken it home and recorded that same thing happening over and over again, then uploaded the video to YouTube. When the device worked, it was awesome, but having such an obviously flawed design that can't withstand minor impacts would seem to invite a class-action lawsuit once more people experience the same issue.

product_title: Sanyo NEW 1500 eneloop AA Ni-MH Pre-Charged Rechargeable Batteries

Now we just need to get everyone else in our communities to stop wasting money on alkalines and switch to rechargeables. Well, when I think about it the frequent sales of alkalines must mean that the demand is less than before. Alright, carry on!

product_title: Monster MCC AVL300-S Home Theater and Lighting Controller with Omnilink (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
I ordered this remote because I wanted to put my components behind a cabinet door. It works great and was easy to program, except for one detail they left out. You must pair the remote with the Omnilink, otherwise nothing happens. I had to Google it to get the answer, so save yourself the hassle and pair it to start with. Do this even if you are not using the remote to control your rooms lights.

Pairing Monster Light Modules/Omnilink with the MCC AVL300 Remote

1- Login to your account
2- Select \\"Modify Settings\\"
3- Select \\"Modify\\" Lights
4- Select \\"Pair Z-Wave Devices\\"
5- Ensure Remote is connected to the USB Cable
6- Select \\"Next\\"
7- After the remote updates you will get a screen with instructions to pair control net lights. Disconnect the Remote from the USB Cable.
8- Take Remote to Omnilink, Ensure that the Omnilink has power.
9- Select \\"Next\\" on Monster Remote
10- If you have lights then follow steps 11-15
11- Select individual light.
12- Walk to light Module select \\"Add\\"
13- Press and hold button on module
14- You should get the message at \\"added\\" on the Remote screen
15- Please follow steps 11-13 to pair all the light modules
16- Press \\"Done\\" once all the light modules have been paired
17- You will get a message as \\"You need to Add RF-Extender to the network\\"
18- Walk up to the Omnilink then select \\"Add\\"
19- Press and hold \\"Connect\\" on Omnilink for 3-4 seconds
20- You should get RF Extender Added
21- Connect remote to USB and select \\"Next\\"
22- After the remote Data is transferred you should have Green Check mark on all light modules and Omnilink as paired.
23- From the Home page run a final update on the Omnilink and the Remote

Feel free to contact Customer Technical Support on 1 877 800 8989 if you need further assistance.

product_title: AKG Acoustics K550 Closed-Back Reference Headphones
review_headline: Phenomenal for a $300 Pair of Headphones
review_body:
For those who don't know, AKG has been a manufacturer of mid-fi consumer headphones since 1959. They're currently a part of Harman International Industries, who you've heard of in the form of JBL Pro, harmon/kardon, Lexicon, Mark Levinson, etc. Just know that the manufacturer has a quality pedigree in mid-fi audio and, anyone who knows a modicum about audio, will give you a thumbs up when they see them on your head.

So, let's get down to it: these headphones are far from perfect, but they're one of the best values at the $300 price point. I would easily recommend these to someone over the Beats lineup (including the Pro series) or the Sennheiser 600s or 598s. They're clean, accurate, and demonstrate a wonderful amount of detail.

On the flip side, there is something wrong with the mid-highs. It's a nuance 90% of people would never notice, but it's there. The resonance in this frequency can be distracting, but not even remotely as distracting as the flaws I've found with other headphones around this price range (say like the artificial bass in Beats). If you have a good two channel system or are used to listening to higher quality audio gear, you'll hear it. If you live in the mid-fi range of audio equipment, you'll never notice it. It's not obvious in everything.

Also, a word of warning: low quality recordings need not apply. These headphones are accurate enough to make lower quality MP3 rips sound atrocious, as they'll pull out all of the imperfections and hollowness of the transfer. This isn't a flaw of the headphones, it's a flaw of the formats. Rip good music or listen to CDs and you won't be disappointed.

product_title: 16 Post 8 speaker Wall Plate
review_body:
I used these terminals and wall plate for a multi-room audio install. I needed something with 16 posts that wasn't pre-labeled for surround sound and couldn't find anything at my local home improvement store that would work.

The termains are solidly built and the pate is cleanly finished and fits over the terminals perfectly. You get everything you need for install if you're willing to screw it directly to the wall or have an electrical box already installed. I used a two gang low voltage wall bracket for mine to hold the plate more securely and leave myself plenty of room in the wall cavity for the wires.

The terminals are the same on the back as on the front and simply screw out to reveal holes to insert the speaker wire and then you screw them back down onto the wire (see user picture). You can also use banana plugs (which I did for the front). The terminals are pretty close together so getting all the wires inserted and tightened down can take a bit of dexterity. The holes for the wires are also located on the top and bottom of each post, rather than on the sides which makes inserting the wires tricky as well. Holes on the sides would have made more sense to me.

Overall though this was the perfect way to clean up the install and it's working great. I would purchase this plate again in a heartbeat.

I got this idea in my head that I wanted the kind of cables guitar players use, with the cloth outer jacket, thinking that it would be more durable and maybe stand up to my apparently abusive use. Since I'm not a guitar player, I have no idea what that kind of cable is called. The \\"braided nylon jacket\\" line on this item is what caught my eye. In the picture the cable looks hefty and the connectors look sleek and not too bulky. I ordered two.

product_title: Headphones Mp3 Player with Sd Plug Card White
review_headline: Great wireless set for the gym
review_body:
This review applies to the [[ASIN:B00810WIQU Headphones Mp3 Player with Sd Plug Card White]], however I found many different versions of the headphones, so much of this review may be helpful when considering similar models, even if there are some different features on the other sets.

I was seeking a wireless headphone set for the gym, preferring to avoid having dangling wires getting in the way of the equipment. This set is a closed design, meaning you will hear nothing but music while wearing them. You will not hear someone talking to you while standing right in front of you. This can be a benefit or a hindrance depending on how you look at it.

The set looks a bit bulky for the gym, but it's way better than those earbuds with the cable hooked to a device attached to an upper arm strap. I can never get earbuds to stay in my ears anyway, let alone having them yanked out because the cable got caught up on something.

When unpacking the set, take extreme care in removing the protective plastic on the LCD display. I had difficulty even though I used an X-acto blade to grasp a corner to peel it away. I suppose one could use a sewing needle if done carefully.

This unit charges through the USB connection to your computer in about 4 hours after a complete discharge. The red LED turns off when fully charged.

I was impressed by the sound quality. As I wanted a set only because it was wireless, I wasn't expecting much, but this set can rival other wired headsets for audio equipment. This particular model also came with a cable with stereo connectors on both ends to convert it to a standard wired headset if needed, plus a twin-wire cable set with a small, inline microphone for two-way communication through your laptop's headphone and microphone connections.

The instructions were translated on the cheap, and were not very comprehensive, so I offer these observations to complement the instructions and to assist in your buying decisions.

MP3 Section:

This model had an EQ switch which supposedly changes the equalizing of the sound to match the genre of the music. There are five settings, and the display shows your choice. I found that setting #2 gave the most aggressive sound for my purposes at the gym. The EQ, by the way, only works for MP3 - not the FM section. Powering on defaults to the beginning of the last MP3 song played. To switch to FM, wait till the MP3 song begins, then press M/FM. Press Play/Pause to play or pause a song. A short press of the FF moves to the next song, while a long press forwards through the song. There is no way to fast forward through the MP3 songs, unfortunately. You'd have to repeatedly press FF to get to a selected song. This could get quite tedious if you have a lot of songs on the SD card. The unit plays the songs in the order that they were copied onto the card, and there are no provisions for playlists.

FM Section:

The FM search function is a one-time-only affair. Just press and hold the Play button while in FM mode and the device will search for all stations it finds with a signal. And I mean ALL stations. Mine stored 30 stations, some with signals so weak I could hardly hear anything above the static. And there's no way to remove a station from the list. As an experiment, after quickly pressing Play, I put the unit inside a large kettle and put it in the microwave as further shielding. The thing still found 21 stations, many of which were still very weak. You MAY be able to manually seek your favorite stations and touch Play to store only those. I haven't tried that yet, but I plan to test my theory soon.

When you switch to FM, it defaults to the last station selected. If you switch to MP3, it will resume wherever the previous song left off. A short press of Play will advance to the next stored station. A short press of FF will advance the FM receiver oneincrement for tuning to a precise station. A long press of FF will seek the next available station. If the device seems stuck in FM mode, reseat the MP3 card or tape the card in place.

All in all, the set meets my needs - a great sounding, dual function wireless headphone that's easy to use and inexpensive as well. Though it lacks other desirable features, for the price you cannot ask for more.

product_title: Bose SoundLink Bluetooth Wireless Speaker
review_body:
It's no surprise; this is the best Bluetooth speaker out there right now - and I know; I've tried them all. Literally. But here's the problem: It's too heavy, and just a bit too big. Of course, to get the kind of sound you get here, you need the size and weight - if not more! It does what it does well, in a small package, but in my side-by-side testing with the Monster ClarityHD Micro, (the new one, not the old one), the ClarityHD has sound ALMOST as good and is MUCH smaller and lighter. Half the size and a third the weight. I can put the ClarityHD in my pants pocket. The Bose would be hard to fit in a jacket pocket, and would weigh it down so much as to be really not an option.

The ClarityHD also gives you features the Bose doesn't offer: You can use it as a speakerphone - and an excellent one, at that - and it takes voice commands, (turn up volume, next song, etc). It has a wrist strap - because its light enough. And it gives plenty of volume without distortion. Granted, the Bose hits much higher volume, but think of the use-case... hotel room, picnic, outdoor on the patio... These places don't call for mega-volume - and the ClarityHD is much louder and less boomy than the popular Jambox.

So, its sort of like the digital camera paradigm: \\"What is the best digital camera? The one you have with you.\\". For most people, that is the camera in their phone, or the small camera in their pocket, purse, etc. When I travel, is it more convenient to throw my excellent Canon SX230 P&S in my bag, or my big DSLR with lenses? Same here. I was about to sell my ClarityHD and I started thinking about my use-case... When was I really going to use a BT speaker? At a hotel. At a restaurant, (maybe). Picnic? Beach? Around the house...? Maybe, but I have speakers and what not everywhere. Is the sound \\"good enough\\" from the Monster for these occasions? I'd have to say Yes. Is it even quite good? Yes. Is it as good as the Bose? No. But its the best I've heard for the weight and the size and the price. The next step up is the Bose, but I fear it will never make it into my overnight bag, fanny pack, or pocket. Also, I don't have to remember to carry the A/C adapter and chord... the Monster ClarityHD uses standard microUSB charging. Think about it.the best I've heard for the weight and the size and the price. The next step up is the Bose, but I fear it will never make it into my overnight bag, fanny pack, or pocket. Also, I don't have to remember to carry the A/C adapter and chord... the Monster ClarityHD uses standard microUSB charging. Think about it.

The knob on the earbuds themselves is relatively heavy, and this causes the headphones to rest at an angle in your ears.  Because of the points from which the sound emanates, this can give the impression of unbalanced sound or of underwhelming bass/volume.  When the earphones are properly resting in your ears, the sound is solid and balanced.  However, essentially any movement (including walking) is enough to knock them slightly out of place, leading to the unbalanced sound issue.  Also, durability is poor.  The seam between the knob and the part the rests in your ear is weak, and mine broke here after only a couple months of regular use (compare to iPod earbuds that lasted me years of almost daily use).  If you can sit still while using these headphones, they might be passable.  Otherwise, I suggest another option.

product_title: Logitech Harmony 300 Remote Control 915-000143 (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
I purchased my first Logitech Harmony 300 Remote from Best Buy (sorry Amazon) in June 2010 to control a [[ASIN:B0036WT4KG Samsung UN55C8000 55-Inch 1080p 240 Hz 3D LED HDTV]], a [[ASIN:B003CP0KGY Yamaha HTR-5063BL 630-Watt 7.1 Channel AV Receiver (Each, Black)]], a Cablevision DVR and a Playstation 3 via a Logitech adaptor (I eventually replaced this with the Panasonic DMP-BDT210). The number of brands supported by this remote is impressive and you always have the option to manually program the remote.

With the My Harmony website, this remote was extremely easy to set up and replace devices and assign custom keys. The site and set up are truly intuitive. Once you have everything setup, you can modify any setting by returning the site and connecting your remote via USB.

I cannot understate the convenience of this feature.

I cannot give the Harmony 300 remote 5 stars because after a year and a half, the volume up button began to work only intermittently. I recently replaced it with the same model because, in spite of the durability issue, the ease of set up is hugely convenient. (and it was relatively inexpensive) I simply plugged in the replacement remote, logged into the My Harmony site and hit the Sync button. 5 minutes later, I was up and running with my newly programmed remote.

Pros:
1. myharmony.com - This site makes set up a breeze.
2. Controls up to 4 components. (Some people may find this to be a minus)
3. Plenty of available buttons to cover almost every function
4. Affordable, especially considering how easy it is to set up.
5. You can assign the volume buttons to control only your receiver volume, no matter which device you have selected. Great for a home theater.

Cons:
1. Build quality. My first Hamrony 300 had a malfunctioning button in a little over a year and a half.
2. It only has a single multi-function button (ie, watch movies, watch TV) vs. the higher end Harmony remotes, which have several.

If you are looking for an inexpensive universal remote that is easy to set up, I would recommend the Harmony 300.ony remotes, which have several.

If you are looking for an inexpensive universal remote that is easy to set up, I would recommend the Harmony 300.

If you have a problem, you will likely get an email like this one: \\"This product is covered by a warranty from FiiO. If you would like to obtain manufacturer's warranty service directly from FiiO, please email FiiO at [e-mail address removed].

As an alternative, we can exchange this for you under our extended exchange program. Be sure to enclose a detailed description of the issue you are experiencing and a money order (USPS, MoneyGram, etc) for $13.5 to cover the exchange fee and return shipping and handling of the replacement back to you.\\"

Yes, it actually said [e-mail address removed], so they did not even give me an email address.

Going on the Fiio website, I found that I am free to mail the amp, in the original packaging, to: Address: 2/F, F Building, Hougang Industrial Zone, Shigang Village, Huangshi West Road, Baiyun District,Guangzhou City, China.Postcode: 510430

I am not going to find out what it would cost to mail this dog across the world and will instead chalk it up as a learning experience to not buy cheap, unsupported Chinese junk.

The E6 worked relatively well when it worked, but it is just another disposable piece of plastic garbage and I would have been better off buying a better amp, even if it cost more money.

Before you purchase this amp, ask yourself a question...do I feel lucky?

I purchased this primarily for the bedroom, as the cable output was right where our bed goes, and was putting a lot of pressure on the cord. It's a good thing I bought this when I did, as it actually put so much force on the cord it ripped off the crimped connector on an RCA gold-connector 25ft cord. So, first I had to fix that, which I accomplished with a cheap twist-on RG6 F-type adapter from Radioshack (first time I've done it, I couldn't believe how simple it was to install a twist-on connector, I got a 10 pack and have been using them all over the house). Then, I twisted on this Right Angle F-Adapter Coax Adapter, and plugged into the wall. Now its super-secure, and no signal degradation (we have a digital adapter box from Comcast, haven't lost signal or lost picture once).

These things feel solid, no idea how they would fall apart either. We ordered from bargain cable (side-note: sometimes sellers actually have different products under the same listing, so its good to note the seller when its 3rd-party), shipping was quick and the product works as advertised, plus they were cheap! So, an easy 5-star product.

product_title: JLAB Go Wireless Bluetooth Headphones
review_headline: I tried over a half dozen headsets and found this one the best
review_body:
I really like this headset.

While I occasionally want a Bluetooth headset to use with my phone my main reason for seeking a good Bluetooth Stereo headset was to use with my iPad. I don't hear as well as I used to and I find the speakers on the iPad, even at full volume, to be too soft (it points the sound to the rear of the unit while I am usually in front of it). The sound from those tiny speakers belies the real fidelity that the device provides.

I have tried over a half dozen various models seeking one that works well for me. While I have tested it on my phone and find that it works as well as any of the other units I tried for phone calls, I find it really delivers on the issue of stereo sound from any Bluetooth source.

Regarding the ear pads; a very important feature to me is the ability to hear exterior sound while listening to stereo source. Whether it is indoors or outdoors, I want to hear the phone ring, people talking to me, sirens or traffic approaching me, and so on. These rest in the outer ear area allowing other sounds to penetrate the music or soundtrack. This does cause a minor lack in fidelity which is evident when pushing the earphones hard into your ears (you hear much richer bass and greater overall depth) but this is compensated for by turning up the volume and does not pose a threat by sealing out the external world of sound.

The lack of adjust-ability is made moot by the design whereby the angle of the back section hangs as low as necessary behind your head to take up the slack. This results in a \\"one size fits most\\" design in that, in the event you have a very, very large head, these might not be for you.

The other consideration that should be addressed is the fantastic price. $40.00 and free shipping makes it the best price/performance ratio I have found. Cheap enough that I plan to purchase a backup to keep charged and ready when needed.

product_title: Panasonic Lightweight Headphones with XBS Port
review_headline: Good, tight, intonated bass--not boomy mud.
review_body:
I play bass and I listen to jazz bass. I never listen to rock, hip-hop, rap, or the sounds of train wrecks. Bass to me means tight, deep, sonorous, well-intonated double bass (i.e., contrabass, upright acoustic bass), not the moo-moo-burp-moo boomy, muddy bass that generally comes out of rock bass guitars. These cheap little headphones deliver the kind of bass I want to hear. The mid and treble instruments sound great, too. And they're comfortable; I could wear them for hours at a time. I personally prefer a one-sided cord, but that's not likely to be found in a cheap headphone. In any case, I would gladly give that up for phones of this quality at this price.

I've been using Sennheiser PX 100 phones with iTunes on my computer for years, and these Panasonic RP-HT21 headphones compare very favorably at a fraction of the price. You need to adjust the volume up somewhat compared to the PX 100s, which is easy enough to do, and after I do that I'm not sure I could tell them apart. The RP-HT21s don't fold up, but I use them at several locations around my home so that doesn't matter.

These headphones are a steal at the price. Get 'em before they disappear. I and others will be ordering backups.

PS: I'm not hard on my headphones. If these don't hold up over time, I'll adjust my rating downward, but how much time do to want for this tiny price?

For how long I sit at my computer working every day, why not go for a top-notch audio system? And with iTunes Match, all of my music files are now at least 256kbps, so the audio files won't be a noticeably weak link in the sound chain.

After reading a very helpful MacWorld review of the NuForce Dia and three other similar products, I decided the Dia's superior DAC (compared to its Icon-2 sister product) and remote control outweighed the loss of a USB audio input. After connecting my Mac Mini to the Dia using an optical audio cable ([[ASIN:B0002JFN10 C2G / Cables to Go 27015 Velocity Toslink-to-Optical Mini Plug Digital Cable (1 Meter)]]) and using some quality Monster speaker plugs (had to buy these: [[ASIN:B000WXBY7I QuickLock MKII Gold Flex Pin Connectors For Easy Self Crimping Terminations - 2 pr. pack Quick Lock Flex Pin]] because only had banana plug connections, which unfortunately the Dia doesn't accept), I'm all set.

And I can echo what Marco Arment and R. Matthew Ward from MacWorld have said: the sound quality is fantastic. The DefTech speakers are really good, and in my listening so far the NuForce is equal to them. I'm coming from a $250 set of Bose 2+1 computer speakers and am blown away by how much better this setup sounds.

Highly recommended.

review_body:

The little top strap on the top makes sure that the earphones grip your head and won't cause slippage. If you push back one side of the headphone so one ear is left uncovered, it is still comfortable! The bendy plastic is flexible but supportive.

The fabric covered cord won't tangle, and the \\"tearaway\\" feature is nice in case you leave yourself accidentally plugged in and walk away.

The best thing: I can't hear my coworkers when they are deep in conversation or when they're using speakerphone on their conference calls.

The thing that can be most improved: It's not exactly foldable--so how about providing a drawstring bag that you can stash your headphones in so they don't get dirty? Because I'm an on-the-go mom who needs to be able to throw this in all kinds of bags while on the go.

product_title: Pioneer Crew Steez Portable Music System
review_body:
Hello, I purchased this stereo (boombox) simply for its clarity, sound, and for it's portability. I'm going to make this short so it is easier to make a decision for yourself if you want to buy the Pioneer Steez.

Pro's
portable, has remote, very clear sound, many different plug-ins for optional plug in devices, clean, cool look, has a handle, large LCD screen.

Con's
heavy, requires batteries if not plugged in, not very loud if crowd starts cheering, handle is not at all ergonomic, power cord/supply very small gauge wire limiting potential power usage, does not come with very secure way of supporting Ipod anything, no place to store power cord for \\"portable stereo\\", no low, mid, or high adjustments... this is only controled through device that is plugged in, too expensive for the performance of this stereo.

Ok, So I did buy this from Amazon.com. They are always able to beat anyone elses prices. However; this stereo does not meet the quality for price. I'm very scetchy about taking it out for the thought of it getting scratched, dented, or stolen(due to it's price). I immediatly started having problems with having to adjust both my Ipod classic and my Ipod touch just to get the stereo to play. I found it easier to just plug in the \\"aux\\" port and let the Ipod's play on random. I also found this stereo to be cumbersome to carry around. Although it is big and cool looking, I look like an idiot carrying it. If there was a carrying bag/strap and internal-rechargable Lion batteries inside, I would have given this stereo an 8 out of 10. The other reason I'm not 100% happy is for how \\"not\\" loud it is. In a small apartment it sounds great. Outside, not so great. Oh and I did have to make a spacer for my Ipods to be placed inside the cradle so if there was any movement the Ipods would not cut out. And the last but not least, this is the year 2012, was is 4gb of music going to do for me or anyone. I have over 30 gb of music. another 20 in movies.

Hope this helps
Tony

product_title: Philips CitiScape Uptown Headphones
review_headline: Low volume...but then I read more about BURN IN..NOW they are FABULOUS
review_body:
I've read about `burning in' headphones before because I had gotten an expensive set that seemed too quiet. When I got these, I had the exact same issue. I grew up in the 80s, we crank it :) So I read up on burning them in and tried it. WHAT AN IMPROVEMENT! I almost can't believe that there are not directions in the box on how to do this! So, I'll tell you what I did after all of my reading. First I got an app (a free one) that only played `pink' and `white' noise. So, basically it was white noise like when you are in-between radio stations on the dial. Just static at two different tones. I played them all night at the highest level the app called for. (Personally I thought that was too low to do anything...) Then I played music on them for a day. Just the songs on my iPod which has a lot of Breaking Benjamin, Pavarotti, 80's tunes, Downhere, Keane and some instrumental by Mozart. I did play it at a lower volume at first, then for a few hours on full-volume. I just put the headphones on a table and let it go while the music played. Like magic, the volume is much, much better and the sound is incredibly improved! To me, this is what expensive headphones should sound like. Lots of full-sounding music that envelops you. LOVE THEM!

I also love the look with the cool brown and steel grey. Very cool and unique as I've never seen headphones in this style. They are super-comfortable and once they were `burned in' they really did block out all other sounds. I have not put them through the `lawnmower' test yet, which is where I usually wear headphones, to block the sound of the mower! I love the flat linguini-style cord. My other expensive set has the same style cord and wow, it's amazing. I never get it tangled. As to the volume control that is loaded onto the cord itself, I have never understood why they place it so high. I guess it's so that you can find it easily if you are...driving? Mowing??! :D Just my personal preference would be to have it lower down on the cord, no biggie.

I give these my highest rating and praise...they would make and excellent gift! Honestly, for any age. The sound is awesome enough for teens or adults, the cool styling and colors are too.

Sheri Gill - Writer, Mom, Mage!n the cord, no biggie.

product_title: Dish Network VQ2500 Tailgater Portable Satellite Antenna
review_headline: Performs as promised but that is deceptively limited.
review_body: Set up and use was easy - the reason I bought this system to replace the tripod and dish arrangement I have been using when traveling.  However, this system only works with one tuner at a time.  As delivered, you are able to watch - in real time - one program. It automatically 'finds' one satellite and then switches to another when you change channels allowing it to focus on only one thing at a time on the 'solo' receiver (sold separately for 150.00) it is built to work with. Note that the solo receiver does NOT have a DVR; if you want to record or even pause/resume you have to purchase an external hard drive and pay DISH $40 to unlock the capability.  In the past I just threw one of the 722 receivers from one of the bedrooms into the camper with the tripod/dish and was able to record two programs and watch another simultaneously.  The downside was that it sometimes took frustrating hours to point the dish and local channels weren't available.  But then I didn't have to get DISH involved in that system.  With the tailgater, I will have to call DISH and pay a $7.00 (for now) service fee for it to work and in that process they unlock the locals for wherever you're parked. If I knew everything I know now, I would wait until DISH releases a promised receiver with more than one tuner and a built-in DVR for the 'gater before purchasing the system.

review_headline: This Radio Is Worth Using For Tough DXing

The radio when plugged into the headphone jack works wonders, it's better than any other portable on the market, and some people call this a communications receiver under $300. The reception was kinda poor because of the summer lightning storms, but when winter comes around I will give this an new update. Anyways, the FM reception works great, and to make it even better it has a switchable attenuator and wide and narrow filters for FM which made my FM DXing a breeze, and the FM dipole made it even better. What also like about it is that the radio has separate FM and SW jacks and a AM/LW jack on the ferrite rod that switches off the internal ferrite rod antenna when plugged in with a loop antenna. For AM DXer's this radio works good for AM DXing with the rotable ferrite rod antenna, the selectivity is good with the wide and narrow filters, it's better than the regular portables.

The short wave radio reception works great and the SSB reception is very active, which I could hear the hams better than I could with my other portable radio receivers. The Air band is ok, but mediocre, needs improvement with a better outdoor ground plane scanner antenna for better results. The radio does go down to 76 MHz to 90 MHz for Japanese use, but it does not go down to 64 to 76 MHz for East European use. The long wave band goes down to LORAN-C 100 kHz to NAVTEX on 519 kHz, and the AM band covers from 520 kHz to 1710 kHz, and the Short wave covers from 1.711 MHz to 30 MHz. And FM is 76 to 108 MHz which means for Japan it would be 76 to 90 MHz then channels 1 to 3 for TV audio.

product_title: Onkyo UP-HT1 HD Radio Tuner (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Onkyo UP-HT1 HD Radio Tuner Review
review_body: It works great.  I'm now able to listen to the HD2 channels not available on a standard analogue tuner.  (The only thing better would have been for the tuner to have been a built-in tuner, rather than an add-on device.)  If you buy the Onkyo TX-8050, you MUST buy this HD tuner.  Simply click on PORT and you have HD radio.  Needless to say, sounds great!  Also, the iPod adaptor daisy-chains into the HD tuner and it too works great.  2/10/17 Update: The tuner still works great.  I don't know why it was discontinued?  The only way it could have been better is if it had been installed inside the TX-8050 receiver.  The way it plugs into the TX-8050, it essentially is an external "internal tuner," referred to as "port," rather than tuner.  Also, if you want to switch to the iPod adapter, you simply depress port a second time; you don't need to walk over to the UP-HT1 tuner to manually switch back and forth.  Once you get used to the idea that the UP-HT1 is "port," it's just like using the regular tuner, only better of course.  My guess that it was offered as an option, was to keep down the base price of the TX-8050?  I'm certainly thankful that I bought it when it was available.  PS: I also bid on and bought another HD tuner that is no longer available.  My guess is the HD tuners were too good at prices considered to be too low, so they were discontinued.  If you have a chance to buy this tuner, buy it!

review_body:

They arrive in a very good quality soft \\"leather\\" drawstring carry bag and all the necessary cables. What makes these small powerhouse speakers so nice is that almost all of the cords and cables are housed inside each unit. They easily pull out and then retract when done. So you don't have wires hanging all over the place while in use. Another neat little feature - each speaker is flat on the bottom and rounded on top. They have magnets on the bottom so they can be joined together when traveling. They end up looking like a capsule.
These have MUCH better sound quality than I even hoped for. I have a new Dell laptop and it has wonderful speaker volume IF you are watching a you tube clip or a DVD. But, when watching a streaming movie through Netflix, the movie volume can vary greatly. The mini speakers bring everything up to a level that allows you to enjoy the movie without straining to hear it, especially when traveling in the car.
Another nice feature - I put the computer volume on HIGH and the movie volume on HIGH - then you can control the volume on the speaker unit. I was having to constantly go into the computer while watching a movie and adjust the volume. Now, I simply adjust the volume using the speaker.

I am very surprised by the quality of this item. They are very sturdy and well made.
You won't regret purchasing these little speakers. They're well worth the cost and I was surprised to learn that they have a 45 DAY RETURN POLICY AND A ONE YEAR MFG. WARRANTY.
My favorite feature is the hidden cords. It's so nice to not have to deal with cords when you are ready to put the speakers away.

review_body:
These are pretty good headphones. The sound quality is good, if bass-heavy, and I didn't hear any distortion even when I cranked the volume up to the loudest I could stand (which is not terribly loud, I'll admit). I don't think the sound quality is anything special, though, and for this price, I would have expected something pretty awesome.

They don't drown out outside noises. On that scale, I'd say they do better than basic earbuds, but not as well as the kind of earbuds that actually stick into your ear canal.

One thing I love about these headphones is that the cord is not permanently attached. You can unplug it from the headphones. That's great, because I go through headphones pretty fast, and usually it's because the cord gets damaged. This way, I can just buy a $5 cord from Radio Shack rather than have to buy new headphones when the cord shorts out. The cord has a pause button, which is nice, although it's way up near my ear.

These headphones could be more comfortable. My ears got sweaty from wearing them, and they eventually felt kind of uncomfortable because of their shape on my ears (I prefer ear-shaped headphones to perfectly round ones like these).

Overall, I would not recommend these headphones at this price. I think you can get better value for your money.

review_body:
Overall, it works OK. The only complaint I have is that it does not output in 16:9 resolutions which is what alot of monitors use these days. It accepts a 16:9 input, but the output resolutions are only available in 4:3 and 16:10. What does this mean? If you have a 16:9 monitor (1280x720, 1600x900, 1920x1080) the quality will be degraded quite a bit. It's still usable/watchable but I don't think I would consider it \\"1080p HD\\" as the title describes. The best way to make it look decent with a 1920x1080p monitor is to set the OUTPUT resolution to 1920x1200 (a 16:10 resolution). Some graphics are (obviously) distorted however, due to the stretching, etc.

Also, It goes into standby pretty quickly, which does not really matter for me - but if you're considering just having this behind your desk and toggle input on your monitor, it will not work since you will need to press the menu button to turn it on.

When I first got it, I almost returned it due to not having 16:9 support but I don't think the difference in quality is really enough to go through the hassle. You can tell it's not the native resolution, but it's fine overall.

Since the item stated it had \\"1080p\\" which is 1920x1080, it gets dropped down to 3/5. None of the resolutions offered are REAL HD resolutions (1280x720, 1920x1080 = real HD resolutions).

product_title: J-Tech Digital Premium Quality Most Advanced HDMI 4x2 Matrix Ver 1.3 Certified for Full HD 1080P Support 3D with SPDIF Digital Surround Sound or Hi-Fi Stereo Audio Output
review_headline: It works well but super weak in analog audio output
review_body:
THE SHORT:

* Works well and as described.
* Analog audio is super weak, you'll need to crank your TV volume way way way up.

THE LONG:

I got this HDMI switcher so that I can extend the use of my 10-year old Sony LCD TV (which, by the way, is one of the last and best Sony TV that was fully developed in-house.) The TV does not have HDMI input but fortunately it has DVI. As you may already know, the DVI and HDMI have the same video signals just different connectors. An adapter takes care of that. Though, DVI does not carry audio signals and therefore audio need to run on separate cables.

My setup includes the TV, a PS3, a Mac Mini, and a digital set-top-box. All with HDMI outputs.

Prior to this purchase, I used a HDMI switcher to take care of the video and a manual audio select switch (the kind with mechanical push-buttons) for audio. This setup was very inconvenient. Every time, I want to switch input I'd have to get up and walked to the TV and manually switch the audio to match the video.

With my Mac Mini that's sitting at the desk across the room, it was able to send the video via a long HDMI cable but running an audio with that distance is a challenge. So I end up watching the video on the TV while hearing the sound coming from the speakers at the desk. This is really an awkward experience.

Now with this HDMI switcher, I'm finally able to simplify the setup. Video and Audio can now be transmitted from all sources via HDMI cables. The TV now gets the audio signal from the HDMI switcher. I can now switch video and audio with one click using the provided remote. (I'll soon program my universal remote to operate the switcher). During the set up, I was amazed by how much of that cable clutters were removed from around my TV!

At first, I was totally happy with this new setup. But as soon as I start enjoying the shows, I noticed that the switcher put quite a damper on the analog audio signal. I now have to turn the TV volume way up from normally 10 to 50 (out of 100). It seems all fine at level 50 except that when I switch the TV to other (non-HDMI) sources, the TV sound would be super super loud!

I ended up having to buy (actually assemble one from a kit) a small audio amplifier to boost the audio. This really degraded the sound quality as well as introduced hiss noises! Now I'm searching for a professional equalizer/pre-amp in as small package as possible. Thanks to Amazon's vast selections and easy search, I found some DJ equipment that seems like would work. (note: I don't have the room for a full-size amplifier/tuner.)

So, yeah, the thing works well except for the flaw of super weak audio.

product_title: Onkyo TX-NR1009 THX Certified 9.2-Channel Network A/V Receiver (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
I purchased the Onkyo TX-NR1009 to upgrade from an old Yamaha receiver and the sound is fabulous. I have Polk LSI speakers (15's, Center, FX and LSI 9's) and this receiver drives them extremely well. I bi-amped the main speakers and this is easy to do through the menu's. My unit did not come with a printed manual but other than that I'm very pleased with it.

The sound is very clean and some of the music surround modes such as Neo:x are really excellent. I literally hear things in songs I've never heard before. I wired it with an Ethernet connection to my home network. I understand there is a wireless device you can use to hook it up but it works great wired. It does Pandora great. I also have my music library on an inexpensive home NAS Drive and it plays those songs just fine over Ethernet. I also use a turntable for vinyl and this receiver has a phono pre-amp that works great. I'm still learning what all it can do.

After my initial listen, I ran Audyssey setup. It did a great job of adjusting for speaker distances and setting the low end cutoff to 40 hz for my smaller speakers (surrounds, center etc). However, the Audyssey sound curve set to music really made the whole thing sound worse - a lot worse. I turned that off for each source. I suggest that you turn this off or try it both ways and see what you like if you are going to primarily listen to music.

On the minus side, the remote is kind of lame and not fully back lit so I keep a small flashlight handy to illuminate it. However, the iPhone remote app works OK. It makes you select the device each time but other than that works fine and it is very cool to fire up Pandora from another room. If you are not going to either do 9.1 or bi-amp your mains and run 7.1 (or set up other zones) then the TX-NR809 would be the better choice for the money. Since I bi-amped the main speakers I did have a use for all nine amplifiers so that is why I chose this unit.

review_headline: Best in price range even better than others with higher prices.

I also have Polk's PSW505 subwoofer. I just checked online its frequency range, power, impedance and connection to make sure it'll fit my basic needs.
When i unpacked it, the first thing i have noticed is the very nice looking in addition of a quality feel, is its elegant piano black top plate. the sides are MDF and also made with quality in mind. Then i plugged them into my Onkyo receiver and played some music at first with relatively low volumes. I noticed a slightly better performance and sound, then i played a BD movie (Avatar), it was also slightly better than the performance of my old B&Ws M-1. I then made the MultEx Eq calibration, and i noticed a damn good test sound, crisp and loud. I played an \\"Arman Van Buren\\" audio CD which i use mainly for testing sound quality. I pumped up the volume to 60 (THX level is 82). The highs were very crisp, the mids were warm and very clear and the base is relatively strong for a front bookshelf speaker. I didn't increase the volume any further 'cause my ears started to hurt (kidding), but i felt that this is like 50% of the speakers power and it performs much better in high volumes than in low (although still very good at low volumes). I just recommend to have a good subwoofer to have a smashing strong overall base.

In short, i never expected such performance from that price range. You'll be more than satisfied by the presentation, performance and quality of the sound from these another great Polk's set of speakers.
Just have in mind that it is not video magnetic shielded...but who cares :)

product_title: ViewHD HDMI Switch
review_headline: Searched forever for an HDMI router, this is it!!!
review_body: After many, many hours of searching and sifting, I finally found this repeater, and it does exactly what I needed it to do!  Now, my usage might be a bit different than what most people are looking for, so I'll explain the setup, and why this was perfect for me.  Like many others, I have several HDMI devices (X-Box, Blu-Ray, Cable Box, Laptop, Etc...) that need to be funneled into a single output.  And of course, this task has been handily solved by the plethora of HDMI Switchers out there that have (x)number of inputs, which you can then cycle through and send to a single output.  No, sweat there.    However, I needed a way to route the output to EITHER the Receiver (when I want multi-channel audio with my video), OR straight to the TV, when I didn't need the Receiver turned on just to watch something with a simple stereo signal (or rather when I didn't want to eat 785 Watts just to hear a non-audiophile quality youtube video).  In other words, there are times when I want the HDMI signal sent to the Receiver, and there are times when it's neither practical or necessary to have the receiver on, and I'd rather just bypass it and send the signal straight to the TV.  I suppose I could have split the audio out from each device via S/PDIF or Optical, and just sent the audio to the receiver, while piping the HDMI signal to the TV, and then when I wanted the receiver on, I could just switch between the audio sources at the receiver level.  This has several drawbacks however.  Namely, audio quality.  S/PDIF and Optical audio paths do not have anywhere near the same bandwidth as HDMI (ie, no uncompressed, lossless, multi-channel audio formats).  Configuration problems arise as well, as you'd have to route a separate audio path for each and every device (read, at least twice as many cable$, and TOSLink ain't cheap), which is kinda absurd as the audio signal (and a superior one at that) is already included in the HDMI stream.  So for ages, I've had to get up and physically plug the output from a traditional switcher into either the Receiver or the TV.  A pain in the rear for sure.  Man, I thought, if there was only a switcher that worked the opposite way.  Instead of multiple devices into a single output, I need a device that can take a single output and route it to multiple outputs.  I needed a repeater, not a switcher.  And this is what this does.  Note:  This is not a Splitter.  Splitters take a single input and simultaneously output to two or more outputs (like viewing a Blu-Ray movie on two or more TV's at the same time).  Those things usually need their own power supply, and are way more expensive (if you want one that actually works) than a typical switcher.  This is a Repeater.  Actually, it's Bi-Directional.  So, you can use it as a traditional switcher as well.  Typical usage:  1. Take an HDMI source and send it to a TV in one room, OR send it to a TV in another room.  2. Take an HDMI source and send it to a TV, OR send it to an HDMI equipped receiver (my scenario).  3. Reverse it (it's bi-directional) and use it like a typical switcher.  So for me, the setup is:    Each HDMI device is sent to a typical HDMI Switcher.   This switcher has a single output.    This output is sent to the ViewHD repeater via HDMI cable.   Then TWO HDMI cables (one to TV, one to Receiver) are attached to the ViewHD.    Press a button and the HDMI signal is sent to either the TV or the Receiver.    Simple and extremely effective.  I have no idea if it supports 3D stereoscopic information (doubt it at this price point).  Maybe someone else can test it and post a review.  Hope this helps someone else in a similar situation.

review_headline: Will be ordering another one - Great Mount!
review_body:
I bought this mount in 2009 when I was building a new home (from another supplier - not Amazon - yeah I now, it was before I \\"found\\" Amazon and now it's my #1 place to shop!). We decided we'd wall mount our 40 inch Sony LCD flatpanel over the fireplace. I was pleasantly surprised by the mount's structure. I was even more surprised when, after it was mounted, the pressure adjustments allow for you to use just finger or two to move the left or right, and (although you need two hands when pulling the TV out from the wall, or turning it down on a slight angle is also smooth and easy) even with the heavy weight of the TV on it. Couldn't be more happy with this mount! Didn't find any missing bolts are parts. In fact, it came with a (seemingly) a hundred or so different size bolts/screws all laminated in a sheet of plastic for various mounting scenarios for different TV model mounting. I was almost disappointed to have so many extra screws they shipped that I didn't need.
Then two years after in our new home, I decided I wanted to have the ability to mount our smaller 32 inch Samsung LCD flatpanel outside, mounted on our house, so we could sit on our deck and watch TV on special occasions. The idea is to have the mount on the house, and part of the mount on the TV, and when we wanted to move the TV outdoors for a few hours to watch something, to be able to \\"put the two parts together\\" quickly - like a quick release/quick attach mount. At the time (last year) I couldn't find this same model mount where I had bought it, so started searching for similar construction mounts. I couldn't find ANY that had a quick release. Now after all that searching, I took another look at this mount I already had in our living room, and realized! - although it never said anything about being a \\"quick release\\" it is really: The bracket that mounts to the wall is flat with a half in lip that sticks out. After you mount the bulk of the mounting hardware to the back of the TV set, you raise the TV to the wall and let it hook onto the wall mount. Then you use 2 set screws at the bottom to keep it from accidently being bumped off, or sliding sideways off the wall bracket. But taking a second look at that, I'm a strong guy, and our 32 inch flatpanel that doesn't weight very much would pair perfectly with this mount so I could mount it outdoors, leaving only the wall mount bracket only on the house, and bring the TV outdoors when we wanted to entertain or watch on the deck. When we pull the TV down it'll be indoors on its table mount, with the wall bracket still attached. So I just purchased a second one to use outdoors (the silver model S not the black figuring the silver one might deter rusting better) and will have my outdoor TV mount bracket after a LOT of searching and not finding a single hit for \\"outdoor quick-release TV mount bracket\\" and various iterations for months! Until I took a second look at what I already had in our living room and decided this can work outdoors too!

review_headline: An Ideal Gift For The Music-Starved Person
review_body:

For years I have suffered--either good radio stations don't come in clearly or local ones come in clear as a bell, but are just noise to my ears. Then came Pandora--too bad our computer is located in the basement. Unless I want to sit down there, music options still remain limited.

My kids are astute--they know two things--mom loves music, but is also technologically impaired. I received this Grace Solo Wi-Fi radio receiver (paired up with a Cisco Valet wireless router) as a Christmas present from them. It is absolutely wonderful. Set-up (by the kids of course) took minutes. The adapter is easy to use, music or news comes in clearly and selections are limitless. I couldn't be happier. If you have a parent who sounds like me, consider this as a gift. It is one of the best presents I have ever received.

Update: The Grace Digital Radio adapter is placed where I spend the most time--the kitchen. At first it worked well, but after purchasing a new microwave, little problems arose (music mysteriously turns on by itself, music turns off when microwave is in use...takes awhile for music to restart).

I have since read up on the subject: home wireless networks based on the 802.11b or 802.11g standards transmit their signal in a narrow radio frequency range of 2.4 GHz. Various other electronic devices in a home, such as cordless phones, garage door openers, baby monitors, and microwave ovens, may use this same frequency range. Any such device can interfere with a Wi-Fi home network, slowing down its performance and potentially breaking network connections.

My solution? I try to use the microwave as little as possible while the adapter is on. Another option when the microwave MUST be used--decreasing the power level on the microwave causes NO interference with the adapter. The microwaving process takes a bit more time, but there are no music disconnections. So far this is the only problem I've encountered. The pleasure of listening to enjoyable music far outweighs this minor inconvenience.. So far this is the only problem I've encountered. product_title: Sennheiser Portable On-Ear Headphone with Powerful Bass
review_headline: Average sound quality with a good build
review_body: first off, i have a pair of grado SR60 for day to day use, so that is my comparing standard. i also own several other low to medium range headphones such as panasonic htx-7, sennheiser earbuds 400/500/360/470/471, grado sr80.  i purchased sennheriser PX90 from amazon as a factory refurbished product. the packaging was really good with sennheiser brand.  these headphones are really light with moderate clamping force (the headband is black-coated stainless steel and adjustable with soft rubber cover on top). the overall build quality is really good and robust. it should last for years of use as long as the drives stay good.  as of the sound quality, it is only marginal better than the usual ten-buck headphones. the sound stage is very flat. the sound signature is warm and recessed with little separation among instruments. voice does not present very close (not in a good way though). the drivers are not as efficient as they should be (meaning you have to pump up the volume to hear good). in short, these cans don't make your music addictive like grado cans do.  i had a sennheiser PX100 before. if my memory serves right, PX90 sounds very similar to it (PX100, although priced much higher, is no match to my tried-and-true SR60).  so to round off, these little cans are okay for twenty bucks that i paid for. they are open and leaks sound so they are not suitable for noisy environment. if you are looking for better sounding options, these are not up to expectations (be prepared to spend at least sixty dollars to get any decent musical headphones).

review_headline: Superb Comfort, Like hearing music again for the first time.
review_body: I was skeptical, even at black friday prices, I've had my favorite pair of headphones for years, just a $20 pair of koss headphones that always did the trick. I got these because I've been doing video and audio editing quite extensively lately and I thought I should see what sort of quality can be obtained with a better product. I am on a student's budget, and so cost is the Only reason these headphones get 4 stars. At what I paid on black friday, these are easily 5 star headphones. At the usual cost, I'd still call it a bargain if you're an audio enthusiast. Not only do these really help with editing because I'm now able to pick up on the smallest subtleties, but listening to my music collection is like listening to it all again. The subtle chiming, ringing, humming, buzzing of every instrument is incredibly crisp and immersive. On top of all that, even compared to my turtle beach headphones I use for gaming, that put comfort before audio quality, these are significantly more comfortable and of course, significantly better audio. I can't speak to other headphones in this arena, but from what I read, in other reviews these headphones seem to excel against similar headphones as well. To people that find the audio quality disappointing or not significantly changed, or with low level noise.... I suspect that lies in what you're connecting to, or you've got your music in a lossy compression format. Connecting through my speaker system, I can't find a mite of noise feedback. In fact, I often wear them without music at my computer to dampen out the sounds of my home rather than my noise cancelling phones that give off the subtle hissing. Under Eighty Dollars, these are 5 Star phones, IMHO.

product_title: V-MODA Crossfade M-80 Vocal On-Ear Noise-Isolating Metal Headphone
review_headline: Excellent choice for a lightweight on the ear set.
review_body: This is my second set V-Moda headphones, my first set is the V-MODA Crossfade LP and they have been fantastic.  Once again, the build quality, comfort, durability, case, cables, and of course the sound are all 5 star!  The V-MODA Crossfade LP where a bit heavy on the head, these are lightweight, both pairs feel great on your head and ear comfort will allow for hours of wear.  A major difference in these headphones compared to the Crossfade LP is that ear cups are rather small. Instead of the padding resting on your head and surrounding the earlobe with ovver the ear cups, these rest directly on the lobes with on the ear cups. Unlike many on the ear headphones the driver is still recessed and you have excellent ambient noise isolation. Full size over the ear cups generally provide a greater degree of isolation, but these still do an excellent job while maintaining air circulation around your ear.  Once again, V-MODA has produced a set of headphones that are made with strong components such as a steel frame and plates. No worries of cracking, or breaking, even with drops and flexing.  A nice case protects your investment and includes a place to keep the detachable cables which have a mic and 1 or 3 button remotes.  The cables are Kevlar Reinforced all feel very durable remaining flexible without holding the shape from storage.  The cables also provide good isolation and do not transmit vibration or sounds from the cable moving around.  The sound quality of the M-80 seems much flatter than the Crossfade LPs. With the GoGear Connect 3 Mp3 player there is finally a good alternative to the ipod touch (and I love my ipod!). The navigation isn't completely self-explanatory and I had to consult the included Quick Start guide a few times to figure out how to work this thing. *Compact and light weight

*8GB memory capacity

*Large touch screen with a resolution of 480 x 320 pixels. Navigation is through the familiar right & left swipe on the screen but it also has a home and back button.

*Good visibility even in bright light

*Powerful, loud speakers so you don't even need any earplugs to listen to your music, and you can easily watch a movie together with a friend

*Excellent video streaming, without any annoying pauses or interruptions in the middle of a movie. There is a preloaded sample video of a car race on the player and just watching that made the superior video capabilities obvious. I almost felt as if I was live on the race track. Pretty cool!

*Pretty good battery life, although I didn't quite get the 25hrs out of my battery that the manufacturer promised

*Android operating system, which allows you to download tons of apps and games

*Preloaded apps let you get started right away. I didn't find all of them useful or necessary and many of them will try and get you to buy a paid subscription to enjoy their services. But one app that I love is the Audible app which lets me access and listen to all my audiobooks on the go.

*Fast web browsing though a WiFi connection, and you can save all your settings simply by logging into your gmail account

CONs:

*The biggest drawback of this device is that it doesn't have a camera, which is really disappointing any android device should have at least basic picture taking capabilities

*The small on-screen keyboard is a pain. It takes forever to type in your password without hitting the wrong letters. And using a stylus isn't an option since the keyboard only responds to touch.

*No physical buttons to Play, Pause and Skip your music tracks, this makes it difficult to listen to music while you are driving and when you can't really look at the screen to see if you are tapping it in the right place

*While testing the skype function I found that during a phone call I could hear the other person well but they said that they could barely make out my words even when I tried to speak directly into the microphone on the mp3 player.

Overall, I like this mp3 player and I would recommend it.ll on-screen keyboard is a pain. It takes forever to type in your password without hitting the wrong letters. product_title: TDK High Fidelity In Ear Headphones
review_headline: All the better to hear you with, Zooey Deschanel
review_body:
It's probably unfair of me to review these headphones while listening to Zooey Deschanel singing on [[ASIN:B005V4FJC4 A Very She & Him Christmas]] because, frankly, everything is better when Zooey is singing to me. Nevertheless, I will try to be objective...

When Zooey sings to me through these headphones, the sound is better than when she sings to me on any other headphones I own. I've never considered myself much of an audiophile, and have gone through life thinking that a $10 set of headphones is good enough for me. But, Zooey deserves better...I'm sitting here, switching back and forth between these TDK headphones and a less expensive set of J2 Jbuds, and here's what I notice...on the TDKs, the lows feel better, with a greater body than from the J2. I get this comfortable feeling from the lows of the drums and the string bass on \\"Rockin' Around the Christmas Tree\\". And the vocals? The detail in Zooey's voice comes through beautifully, as if she is here in my living room, singing just to me. By comparison, the J2...hang on, Zooey's singing \\"Blue Christmas\\" to me right now...

...OK, I'm back...where was I? Oh, yes, on my non-TDK headphones, the vocals sound more scratchy and hollow, and it gets worse as it gets louder. But on the TDK EB900, the vocals sound great, even as I turn up the volume.

I think part of what makes the sound so great is the form-fitting foam ear tips that are included...roll them slightly in your fingertips and put them in your ears, and they nicely conform to each ear to help keep outside sounds on the outside, and Zooey on the inside. Several rubber-like tips are included if that's what you prefer, but I really like the comfort and feel of the foam.

One slightly odd thing (and I want to make it perfectly clear that this is definitely NOT Zooey Deschanel's fault): Because of the cloth-like outer material used for the tangle-free cord, when there is no music playing the friction of the cord against my clothing is rather loud in my ears. I thought that this might have been because of the foam tips, but it happens with the other tips as well. When music is playing, however, the problem is practically unnoticeable...and of course, when Zooey is singing, all of life's problems become trivial anyway.

For me personally, the TDK EB900 headphones have raised the bar for quality sound. I now know it is worth the extra money for better headphones. I can't see myself wandering down the $300-headphones road anytime soon, because these TDK headphones are great for my inexperienced ears. But if I ever DO head down that more expensive road, I hope Zooey will be at my side.n my ears. product_title: Genuine V-Moda Octave Earbud Hi-Def Earbuds/Headphones
review_body:
I decided to try these V-Moda earbuds because, quite frankly, the cost of most of the Bass Freq models is absurdly high these days. The V-Moda \\"Octave\\" Hi-Def earbuds sound pretty fantastic with a balance between clear, higher ranges (treble) and thumping lower ranges (bass). The rubber earbud protectors are comfortable (I prefer earbuds so if you have trouble with this headphone style you should continue to stay away) even after hours of use. They feel and look pretty durable, even when compared to the Bass Freqs so I thought I'd picked a complete winner. Unfortunately, I kept getting a nagging feeling that I was missing something. For my test music, I played a hip-hop song I knew to be full of bass and listened to it with both the Bass Freqs and the Octaves. The 'thumping' base I thought was quite acceptable on the Octaves turned out to be no so much when compared to the Bass Freqs. I don't listen to a lot of hip-hop/rap, but I do love to hear bass in whatever I'm playing and so I am a little disappointed that the Octaves aren't quite as powerful as the Bass Freqs.

On the other hand, for about $30 you do get a very good-sounding pair of earbuds with their own carrying bag, a set of earhooks to attach to the earbuds, a splitter so another listener can enjoy the beats with you (assuming you want to sit that close;) and extra silicone fitters for the buds (which, by the way, appear sturdier than the Bass Freqs, which seem to go a little soft after a couple months of use so the noise-canceling seal isn't as great). I've decided to stick with the Bass Freqs for iPod listening, and I've been using these Octaves for my part-time transcription job; they cancel noise better than any other headset I've tried and because the higher tones come through darn-near crystal clear, recorded speech is amazingly easy to pick up.

Verdict: I love the headset, just not for what I originally purchased them for. If the bass was as rich and deep as the Bass Freqs while still maintaining clear higher tones, the Octaves would be 5-star for sure.e still maintaining clear higher tones, the Octaves would be 5-star for sure.

product_title: Bose SoundLink Bluetooth Wireless Speaker
review_headline: Great Little Boom Box, esp. if you Like Bass
review_body:
I received my Soundlink about two months ago, and I must say, it's has a nice sound for such a compact box. Of course, Bose is known for reproducing sound in such compact speakers. My college roommate had the Bose Bookshelf speakers and I had the full sized JBL 3-ways, with the Titanium Tweeter. I must say before writing anything further that I'm really a JBL guy because the Highs and Mid-ranges are reproduced much crisper/cleaner in JBL's, for my listening tastes anyway. If you're a Bass-y type guy, then you would probably lean toward Bose products.

Now with that said, I need to tell you that I've been driving an Infiniti car for many, many years and it has a Bose system (didn't have a choice here). I absolutely love the sound in my car from my Bose system! I listen to a variety of music, from Rock, Classic Rock, some Pop/Alternative hits, Classical, Jazz, Pandora, and easy listening tunes.

Getting back to the SoundLink, I've listened to it off and on, inside and outside (patio and beach). It sounds best when the back of the speaker is facing a solid surface, like a wall, so that the rear speaker can really shine. Outside, the sounds does not carry a great distance, esp. with nothing behind the rear speaker. Plus, if you have a lot of outside ambient noise, you'll want to be pretty close to the speaker, or just switch to a headset (if you don't have anyone else listening of course, which kind of defeats the purpose of a speaker). With my particular sound tastes, the Bose is a bit bass-y, but I was able to compensate for this with an Equalizer App on my Samung Galaxy S2 (NICE phone btw). I like the WinAmp Pro app, which is only 5 bucks and comes with an Equalizer, but I'm sure there are some free apps out there also.

Conclusion: 4 Stars for a pretty nice sounding portable bluetooth speaker! I would have given it 5 stars if it came with a Remote (yes, NO Remote!). PLUS if I was able to compensate for the soft Highs and Mid-Ranges with built-in controls instead of having to use an Equalizer, it would be music to my ears. I couldn't find a decent portable with Bluetooth made by JBL, but more and more manufacturers are finally making quality Bluetooth devices. Btw, If you like to compare it to something with Bluetooth for about half the price (and maybe more highs, according to the reviewer) I liked the review on the Altec Lansing iMW725, which can be seen here: http://www.amazon.com/review/R2XZT1YKZDF47Q/ref=cm_cr_pr_viewpnt#R2XZT1YKZDF47Q

product_title: Peerless HDS100 HD Wireless Multimedia Center - Black (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
Pros: Product is easy to set up and operate. Just plug HDMI cable into transmitter unit and cable/satellite box and another HDMI cable into receiver and second TV. Great picture and clear sound. Five stars for ease of use and picture/sound transmission. I use it to receive a signal on my kitchen TV (impossible to get cable installed in that room without almost remodeling kitchen and a bedroom). Very happy with that aspect of the product. Cons: The IR device that is supposed to let you use your cable/satellite remote to change channels, etc., just doesn't work that well. But the biggest drawback, and the most annoying, is that the transmitter unit overheats like crazy. After a few hours of use, it just stops transmitting until I power it down and let it cool off. review_body:
