They're white and clearly designed for women/girls (the packaging is for ROXY, a female surf fashion line, and it mentions girls in the slogan), which is nice, but really sort of unnecessary, because most people would think of headphones as unisex (or so I would imagine). Anyway, I gave these to my wife who was pretty psyched about them, but a few days later turned 'em back in to me, and I'll sum up her review here:

PROS:
Compact, low profile earbuds fit nicely in smaller ears
Microphone, remote, and volume controls on the ear cable
\\"excellent\\" sound (probably not audiophile level or anything, but they didn't leave much to be desired)
included soft zippered case and a variety of alternate inserts

CONS:
White cable (ok, so this may be a pro for some)
Microphone/remote too high on the cable - closer to your ear than your mouth
bulkier-than-average remote
short cable (possibly this was a design feature for \\"girls\\", but it seemed annoyingly short)
**the cable is made out of a pretty hard plastic, and after more than a week of use it never un-kinked properly.

The biggest complaint, and the subsequent deal-breaker, was that cable. Too short, and that problem was compounded by the fact that it kept rolling back up on itself in the shape it shipped in. Maybe a smaller person (shorter that 5' 6\\") would not be bothered, and maybe the mic would be close to the mouth a person with a small head. If that's you, then enjoy!

review_headline: Looks great, lots of clearance, easy to build, some lateral motion
review_body:
Ordered this Bell'O stand last week over a few other ones in the in the $150-$200, mostly because this one was taller and had more clearance in the middle shelf. I had to make sure that whatever stand I got could accommodate this center channel speaker: [[ASIN:B004MF4S0M Pioneer SP-C21 130 Watt RMS 2-Way Speaker]], which is huge at nearly 8 inches tall. Even with this stand I had to finagle it in by putting it in sideways and then slowly turning it and dragging it to the center, sliding in the little rubber rests the speaker came with when I was done. Ultimately, it fit perfectly! That
The whole thing looks very sharp. For some reason, probably because of overhang fears/to push you to buy the larger model, this stand is rated only from 27\\" to 46\\". Know that this stand is 44\\" wide, and overhang with my 50\\" Tv is maybe an inch on each side, if not less.

The other thing that bothers me is just how little space there is between the bottom shelf and the floor - only about an inch, maybe less. I knew this getting it, but this may be a concern in case of serious flooding - it's worth bearing that in mind.
Otherwise: this is very nice-looking piece of work that didn't break the bank, fulfilled my clearance needs, and was easy to put together. Go for it!

product_title: beyerdynamic DT 880 Premium 600 OHM Headphones
review_headline: DT880 Premium compared to AKG Q701
review_body:
In my quest for a reasonably expensive headphone to beat my actual favorite, the AKG Q701, I often did read about the Beyerdynamic headphones and I decided to try the DT880. Considering that I am very often using my Iphone 4 with or without a headphone amp, I decided to go for the 32 Ohms model. I made sure to give it a fair burn-in time so for a week, I did let it run almost constantly with some variation of music and pink and white noises. Today, I can estimate the burn-in to have passed the bar of 100 hours.

In order to compare effectively the two models, I will use my Iphone alone in the first place and then add a FiiO E-11 and reuse the same tracks. I expect the AKG to under perform with no amp as this phone is very power hungry. The tracks I will use are those that I always use when trying to compare headphones, because I love them first but also because I know how they should sound and more importantly because they provide a good sample of music genres and tonalities. The tracks will be compressed at 320Kbps and are as follow:
- Ultrasone Sound test Siley Put short (Jazz, Binaural recording perfect for localization of sounds).
- Ultrasone sound test Wellen track 7 (sound of water waves perfect for the head stage definition).
- Frank Sinatra: How insensitive (Jazz, good also for localization of sounds).
- Robin Thicke: Lost Without you and Angel (Perfect for the voice testing and for bass impact).
- Pink Floyd: Astronomy Domine from A piper at the gates of dawn (Rock and excellent also for the localization of sounds).
- DJ Magic Mike: Feel the Bass (Infra-Bass, enough said...) will be played from my computer because it is missing on the Iphone.

But first, let's start with the non musical parts:

Comfort: The Beyerdynamic DT880 Premium 32 Ohms are extremely comfortable. Their pads are the softest I have ever experienced and rest comfortably around your ears. On the top of your head, I think it is some faux leather. The pressure level is absolutely fine. They are slightly heavier than the AKG but I would still give them 5 stars. The AKG are also extremely comfortable. Their cushions aren't as soft but they also fit like a dream around my ears and the pressure is lesser. I can keep them on for hours.
Conclusion: DT880 : 1. AKG: 1.

Price: I paid $255 for the AKG (MSRP $479)and $309 for the DT880 (MSRP $359).
It could be deducted from the pricing that the DT880 keep a better value than the AKG. Personally, I do not know what to make of this. One may deduct that the MSRP was overblown for the AKG or that the DT880 are overpriced now. While looking at the final price, the AKG appears as the better deal.
Conclusion: DT880 : 0. AKG: 1.

Packaging:
The AKG come with two cables but no carrying case. Both cables are green and of high quality. Both are too long for a portable use. The cables are easy to connect or disconnect and it is a plus because most times, the cable is failing before the rest. Since these headphones are not meant for a portable use, a carrying case was not really necessary.
The DT880 come with only one cable and it is not removable. It is also a bit long for a portable use. It also comes with a huge carrying case. I like it because it is sure to protect it but it is way too bulky for thinking about using it when I travel.
Conclusion: DT880 : 0. AKG: 1.

Sound Isolation:
The AKG Q701 are an open design.
The DT880 are a semi open design.
Both are leaking quite a lot and are not meant for use in public areas. Although the DT880 are slightly more portable, I would still not make them my choice for outdoor use. Both should be kept for home use, listening to music or playing video games (both are excellent at it).
Conclusion: DT880 : 0. AKG: 0.

Now, let's come to the real important part of this test: the sound. I will start by saying that the sound for both was really good out of the box but improved quite a lot with the burn-in time. My first impression before going any further is that they are quite similar, with maybe the AKG sounding a bit more natural and with a larger head stage (open design versus the semi open design of the DT880) and the DT 880 with the mids a bit more forward and overall more powerful. I may sometimes find the DT880 a bit more tiring. Note that the 68 Ohms of the AKG are very deceptive since they sound as hard to drive as maybe a 300 Ohms headphone set.
I will finish this introduction by saying that I am partial to a large head stage and as natural a sound as possible. I like analytical headphones and so far the AKG proved perfect in that field.

Ok, let's start:
- Ultrasone Sound test Siley Put short (Jazz, Binaural recording perfect for localization of sounds).
Both headphones delivered very well on this track. The DT880 were a bit more powerful than the AKG. The AKG sounded a bit more precise but this is by a hair...

- Ultrasone sound test Wellen track 7 (sound of water waves perfect for the head stage definition).
Once again, it is a wash between the two. Both are delivering well on every detail and head stage. You really feel the waves coming from afar, getting past you and going the other direction. Some birds are heard in the distance to the right and one come your direction and it is well rendered by both sets.

- Frank Sinatra: How insensitive (Jazz, good also for localization of sounds).
The DT880 are definitely more powerful. The voices are more recessed but still present on the AKG. Both deliver nicely and I cannot fault any. Though they sound different, nothing is missing for either. Amped or not , both sound magnificent.

- Robin Thicke: Lost Without you and Angel (Perfect for the voice testing and bass punch).
These songs are nicely performed with both headphones. Their signature is different again, with the mids a bit more present for the DT880 and also more power. Once the FiiO amp is connected, the bass improvement is slightly better on the DT880.

- Pink Floyd: Astronomy Domine (Rock and excellent also for the localization of sounds).
I like the AKG better on this song but it is not because the DT880 are at fault. Once again, the mids are not as forward on the AKG and it gives me an impression of neutrality more visible than with the DT880. But once again, the DT880 offer a superb delivery.
Used with the FiiO E11, the AKG start shining and takes a slight edge in my listening pleasure.

- DJ Magic Mike: Feel the Bass (Infra-Bass, enough said...) will be played from my computer because it is missing on the Iphone.
The infra-bass is maybe the most difficult sound for any headphone to reproduce. I failed completely a Sennheiser 598 for it's lack in reproducing it. In this case, both do work well, with once again the DT880 more powerful without an amp. Without a proper amp, the AKG won't be the best because of the power limitation.
With the amplification provided by the FiiO E11 turned to the max, the DT880 start distorting slightly and leave me with a tingling in the ears due to the vibration of the diaphragms. This does not happen with the AKG. When I try to use a similar comfort level for my ears, the AKG appear slightly better.

Conclusion:
I have failed to find better than the AKG Q701 but I found it's equal in the DT880 Premium. I would suggest going for the DT880 if most of the use is done without an amp or if one prefers the mids a bit more forward. I would suggest to go with the AKG if the price is an important factor (you will save about $60) and if you like a more neutral sound. product_title: V-MODA Crossfade M-80 Vocal On-Ear Noise-Isolating Metal Headphone
review_headline: Amazing sound quality - Great build quality
review_body: I will admit up front that I'm not an audiophile, but I aspire to be one. Either way, I really love great sounding music. I agree with most of the reviews listed, so I won't go into all the details, but here are my thoughts on the V-Moda M-80's.  Originally I was going to get the Senn HD 25 II cans. Everyone raves about the sound quality and I was sold. The only thing I didn't like about the Senn's was the looks. They are not exactly great looking cans. While browsing headfi, I noticed the M-80's were getting a lot of attention and people were comparing them to the HD 25's. With the fact that they actually look great, I decided to pick up a pair.  The build quality on these things are amazing. The flex steel makes it so the headband can flex out to any size and not affect the shape. The cables are awesome. A lot of people have complained about the cloth covered Kevlar cables, but I've not had any problem with them. The biggest complaint was with using the mic on the cable. As the cloth rubs on your clothes people could hear the reverberation. V-Moda now includes a shirt clip to help alleviate this problem. I've yet to use the clip and haven't really had any problems. I don't move around much when using these on the phone though.  The sound quality is simply amazing. As everyone else has said, the bass is tight and right on. I had a couple pairs of Klipsch In-Ear phones (X10 & S4i) and some Sony MDR-V700's that didn't sound this good. The mids and highs sound really nice to me as well, but as I mentioned before, I'm no audiophile.  Comfort wise, these cans are great. With my Sony's, your ears would get hot after about an hour and start hurting after 2 hours. I've listened to these M-80's for 8+ hours straight and never had any discomfort. The memory foam on the headphones conforms to your ears. The longer you listen the better it conforms. I'd say I have an average sized head. If you have a large head you might feel some discomfort, but a quick bend of the headband would likely fix that problem.  The sound isolation is another thing I was concerned about. With the Klipsh in-ear and the Sony circumaural headphones sound isolation was really great. You couldn't hear anything around you. With these headphones being supra-aural I was afraid they would let sound leak in. I was pleasantly surprised how well these isolate sound. I've yet to try them in a very loud environment, they work very well at blocking out noise in normal environments.  The warranty is the last thing that sold me on this set. Not many people have pointed out the amazing warranty that comes with these cans. To start, you get a 2 year warranty against any defects. That's much longer than most company's offer. Due to the fact that these are built like a tank, V-Moda probably feels safe giving that warranty. In addition to the amazing 2 year warranty, it comes with \\"Immortal Life Program\\" which provides you with a 50% off coupon should **ANYTHING** happen to them after the 2 year warranty is up.  Overall, I'm incredibly happy with the V-Moda M-80's. I'd highly recommend them to anyone who enjoys high quality sound, likes good looking cans and amazing build quality.

product_title: Creative ZEN X-Fi 3 8 GB MP3 and Video Player withTouchscreen
review_headline: A really fine MP3 Player with extra features that may occasionally come in handy
review_body: After test-driving this Creative ZEN X-Fi 3, I can say that I will use it primarily as an MP3 player. It delivers high quality audio, and the ear phones work really well and look nice.  The primary documentation for this gadget comes in the form of a CHM file stored in the gadget's file system.  When you plug the USB into your computer, you'll find that CHM file in a folder named \\"Documentation\\". Other folders such as Music, Pictures, and Videos contain pre-populated sample files that you can use initially when test driving the gadget.  I played a little bit with the Mic and Recording features to determine whether I could use the Zen as a dictation machine and concluded that the resulting time-stamped wav file's low-quality playback isn't going to cut it for me. The user interface supporting those features need work also (not quite user-friendly, can't delete the wav files thru Zen's menu items [I had to do it when the Zen is plugged in to my computer and I can go directly to the Recordings folder to delete that folder's contents]).  Although the ability to store and share photos and videos can come in handy sometimes, the supported formats (see manufacturer-provided product info above) for viewing such media with the Zen are currently quite restrictive. If the files you want to view are supported, the Zen can be used for such purposes in a pinch (say, for example, you're in a restaurant and you just want to share something casually and you don't own or want to bring along a more capable device).  The extra features that I will have a use for are: the Time and Alarm setter and the FM Radio. You have to use the ear phones as antennae for receiving the FM radio casts, which do come in quite clear.  The alarm beeps for about 5 seconds only and the beeps are not loud, so it's good only for the occasional appointment reminders and such, and only when you have the Zen in your shirt pocket or somewhere real close by where you can easily hear the beeps.  The Zen is quite small in size -- not much bigger than a match box -- and the touch buttons can be finicky sometimes;  when you're not getting a response, you know you have to increase the pressure on a button just a tad bit more. Nested menus are sometimes difficult to interact with, but other than the two problems I've mentioned above, they work just fine once you're past the initial learning curve (I should mention that the file deletion problem I encountered was limited to wav file deletions [recordings] only; I was able to delete video files easily from within Zen, for example).  Overall, I think the Zen delivers really good audio, and some of its extra features can come in handy occasionally. Sounds like a good value to me!

review_body:
I have a really great AV receiver from a a few years ago with NO HDMI inputs. Imagine that!! I tried switches from Monoprice but they demanded super thick cables and never worked right. I finally bought a manual switch that seemed to work consistently without a loss of signal but what a hassle actually having to get up to do the switching. This little switch is wonderful.

I love the fact that it automatically switches to the powered on device so there's really no need to use the remote (or in my case, teach the commands to my learning remote). It has pretty blue lights but I'm thinking of hiding it since it switches automatically. There is no signal degradation and my picture has actually improved. I love it, I love it, I love it.

My setup (if you care): DISH box plugged into a Logitech Revue Google TV, Sony Blu-ray player and a Roku all plugged into the switcher with Class 2 High Speed cables. The switcher is plugged into my ONE HDMI input on my TV. I get sound from the optical (Toslink) outputs into my receiver.

For me, I was looking for a small system with a bit more kick and I think this sys did the trick. It can be pretty powerful so I don't use the volume control aggressively. I like to listen to jazzy music that needs some bass and I think this system handles is pretty good. Although, I did get spoiled by dedicated subwoofer, so it took me some time to realize that I cannot expect that from a much simple smaller system.  There are some unintuitive placements on the remote (eg. tuner button is nowhere near iphone/cd/usb selection, although all these are selected by same button on the unit so I would expect them to be in the same place on the remote), but I think these are pretty minor. Wow, what a difference! The sound was amazing in Neo 6 and DTS. I have been missing out on so much. I use my receiver for listening to music, watching blu-ray(ps3) and online videos(pc). This unit plays loud and clear. My Jvc would distort my Athena AS-F2's, I would constantly have to adjust my sound fields. Even my Kenwood 12 inch 200 watt sub needed constant adjustment. This Onkyo unit plays them loud and clear, all sounds out my towers are crisp and detailed. There is a setting for double bass for your sub, which has allowed me to turn my volume lower. While watching movies or listening to music you can adjust quick settings for center sub and
sound fields. Now I am going to be looking to upgrade my center and surrounds to Bic or Athena depending on reviews. The internet radio is icing on the cake, it does take a few seconds to start but the global selection is worth it. I have not really got to watch t.v. to judge the upscaling but will soon.

I am extremely pleased with this unit and haven't found any weak points yet, but will keep you posted if there are any problems or noteworthy discoveries.

ok it is now March 30, 2012 and I am still learning that you can adjust this more for each device like ps3, pc, tuner, etc etc etc. I have been running my unit for3 hours at 30db+ (you can set how volume is displayed)and the unit is 90+ degrees but if you have a high power unit your case should be open air. If you do put it in a entertainment center you should have a fan installed and even my 1080p digital cable box gets as hot as my stereo and it is just display...this unit is all about customization and user preferences but you can just plug and play but you will be missing out on its full potential. product_title: Koss Headphones
review_headline: Favors mid-range and high-end clarity over powerful bass
review_body:
I use earbuds a lot, and tend to buy some of them to test drive. My preferred buds for the past few years have been Koss \\"The Plug\\". So I wondered: would these be a new or improved version from Koss?

THE TEST

Listened to my usual mix of music (pop, rock, electronic, world, podcast) for a couple of hours, then switched back to the standard. I figured that I needed a couple of hours to get used to them, and then the differences would be obvious when I switched.

SUBJECTIVE IMPRESSIONS

Before the comparison, I noted that the sound was lighter, with perhaps better articulation of the mid-range and high end. The bass is there, but not at all boomy, or even really that strong. I found myself wanting a touch more balance on the low-end. However, for voice use (podcasts, book on tape) they were better. I don't need a strong bass, which tends to tire my ears, when listening to voice.

Comfort-wise, the mid-sized bud cushions fit my ears fine, maybe just a touch small. They did ok at sealing out the noise of a quiet long-distance bus. My ears are normal-to-large, and I am a man. The package does include smaller and larger cushions if you need them. Mirage has a smaller profile and is slightly lighter. However, The Plug has always been comfortable for extended wear.

THE COMPARISON

Eventually I switched back to my usual buds. The first thing was I had to turn the volume down: \\"The Plug\\" appears to be considerably louder at the same volume setting than Mirage. Next, I found that for music, I thought \\"The Plug\\" was smoother and, of course, has more bass. When I first got \\"The Plug\\" I thought they had too much bass, but over time I have come to prefer their balance, even if it is not flat.

CONCLUSION

I'll stick with \\"The Plug\\", as long as the ones I have hold together or I can get more. I might use Mirage for listening to voice for better clarity, but \\"The Plug\\" does reasonably well at both.

Naturally, choice of earbuds is a matter of taste, and I could easily imagine that for some tastes and purposes these will sound better.ly imagine that for some tastes and purposes these will sound better.

product_title: Logitech 915-000144 Harmony Link - Black (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: This really is the future... Although a little bit off
review_body: I almost never write reviews.... Although I do find them pretty helpful when looking into products.  Which is why I needed to create this one because all of the reviews I was reading seemed either to be outdated or just plain incorrect.  The link is my third harmony product... 550 then moved to the harmony one then the link.  On installation, it should be noted that the harmony one and the 550 used software installed on your computer... The link uses a web app... And yes, like one reviewer noted earlier... It is a bit hard to find on their website.  I was initially stuck at first since I kept trying to use my computer based software to find the link and it would not find it then realized I had to use the Internet app... Then installation was a breeze.  I also installed the link app on my iPad and my iPhone.  The great thing about them \\"linking\\" with the link is that they know what the current setup is.  Let me explain... If I got home and turned on the watch tv function with my phone... Then sat down later to watch tv and use the iPad app to browse listings and control everything.... The iPad app knows the tv function is currently on and lets me go from there.  If however... You have another remote (especially another harmony remote) and change the activity to say... Watch DVD... The link will still think you are watching tv and you'll get issues.  So if you go with the link.... Stay with the link.  With regards to functions.... People kept complaining that it is very limited... This might have once been true but not now.  Like any other harmony product... It has activities... And like any other harmony remote... You program your activities to do whatever you want.  Watch tv and change channels on the dvr while changing the volume on the receiver... No problem.  Turns everything on and off and sets up all the right inputs just like any other harmony remote.  And it has all the buttons of a regular remote.... Both the iPad and iPhone apps.  The iPad app is the easiest to use since it displays tv listings and has the bigger display... But to the right are the basic functions...then pull it out a bit and you have expanded functions like numerical buttons and help and exit then pull it out even further and you have access to all of the buttons on all of your remotes.  Same thing goes for the iPhone app... You just have to look for it a little harder since it doesn't have the real estate for the pull out function.  And as for the listings... Once you set up your favorites... It will show those listings first so there is really no need to scrowl thru 500 channels like one guy said.... Set up your favorites and you'll get those right away.  The reason it is four stars instead of five is that it can be a bit annoying to have to unlock your iPhone or iPad then go find the app before you can control things.  Having the regular harmony is kind of nice in the you would just pick it up and push the buttons without having to work to get to the buttons... But it's minor.  The fact that I can turn on and off the tv without being in the same room simply because it is connected via wifi is great.

product_title: Bell'O BWS101 Two-Shelf Component Wall System with Multiple Color Panels (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Extrememly well made, strong and beautiful , but......
review_body:
I'm really impressed with the quality of this shelf system. Every piece is extremely sturdy and machined perfectly. When I refer to machining I'm speaking of the quality of the screws and the taps. Everything fits together perfectly. The supplied hex wrenches and regular wrench work very well with the supplied hardware(screws, nuts and lag screws). You will need a ratchet or strong drill motor to drive the lag screws into the studs.
The glass shelves are thick, strong and nicely tinted a dark grey. I have no doubt they would support 50 lbs, I suspect they could hold a heavier load as long as it was sitting close to the mounting bracket.
Something that I didn't see mentioned here was that these selves do not have to be set up in a stacked configuration. They can also be set up individually or side by side. Installation is easy if you have a good knowledge of stud finding (make sure you put these into wood studs, cinder block or cement). Another point to make is that the mounting brackets are heavy (which is a good thing). You may need help holding them in place while mounting. In all it took about a half hour to install the brackets once I had the holes for the lag screws layed out. I highly recommend these shelves.
As for the \\"but\\" in the title of my review. Three complaints, all small. The first one is that the instructions are in several languages and following them is a little tedious. I missed a detail about mounting a support bracket when I installed the first shelf. Not a big deal, it took me about 5 minutes to fix it, but it was still frustrating reading the directions. Second complaint is the packaging. Everything is very well protected, but the Styrofoam that is used in the packaging is REALLY messy. I don't know where they found this stuff but it breaks up into tiny little pieces when you touch it. I'd strongly recommend unpacking it outside. Which brings me to my last complaint. It would be really easy to lose some pieces while unpacking if you aren't really careful. They used ever square millimeter of space available. Completely open the box and make sure none of the components are stuck to the box (that's what happened to me) There's a parts list included, double check that you have everything before you throw anything away. I hope my complaints don't discourage anyone from purchasing the Bell'O shelf system. I will go out of my way to purchase more of their products.really careful. They used ever square millimeter of space available. Completely open the box and make sure none of the components are stuck to the box (that's what happened to me) There's a parts list included, double check that you have everything before you throw anything away. product_title: Elenco - Regulated Variable Power Supply - 0-15 volts (Assembly Required)
review_body: The power supply runs off of the LM317T variable voltage regulator, so it has a fairly low part count and is relatively easy to assemble. In my kit, the 220uF and 470uF electrolytic capacitors had been also replaced with one 1000uF cap, but it worked fine when assembled, so no issues there.(perhaps the design was revised without updating the instructions). Testing the supply with a multimeter, I noticed that the voltage output actually ran up to about 16.5V at its maximum, and the voltage seemed to remain stable under a load.  On the downside, however, the circuit board that it comes with is fairly low quality, meaning that the thin copper traces can lift off the board and become damaged if one is not careful when putting it together, or if the power supply is dropped after it has been assembled. I was also troubled by the lack of an on/off switch, as now the only way to shut it off is to unplug it. Lastly, with a current rating of only 0.2A at 15V, I am not entirely sure how practical this is at its upper voltage limits.   All things considered, everything worked as advertised, and I was able to solder the entire thing together in a couple of hours. Now that it is finished, it is quite useful for my other projects, and will probably save me quite a bit on batteries.

review_body: I live in Phoenix AZ so outdoor living is a big plus (well maybe not July and August) I built an outdoor movie area at the back end of our property. I had built a Tori gate to bridge the opening the tree bases make and noticed it would be a good place to hang a movie screen. I did and it has been a blast. I started with a digital projector and an odd assortment of speakers and an old all in on surround amplifier. It was good but I needed more sound so I bought a Sony 7.1 amplifier and a set of ss-f6000 towers for the fronts, a  SS-CN5000 center speaker and 2 pairs of SS B1000 for the surrounds and backs. After the break-in period they have been wonderful. I buried the wiring in conduit to keep the wires out of the way. The main seating area is surrounded and engulfed by sound. It's just like being at the theater but it only costs a dollar to rent the movie and you can have a beer, or five, while you watch. For the price, these are great speakers and if they work this well outside, I can only imagine what it would be like in a living room or den.

The Auto-On feature works well so that I only need to power my preamp when I want to run some tunes.  But the real test came at a birthday party, 60 or so guests, and a dance floor.  A request was made to use my setup for the dancing. There would need to be loud music for the night, techno dance type.  I was excited to give my vintage JBL's powered by the Daytons a go.  Suffice to say that the APA 150s were driven hard and never balked, never gave up, and never even got beyond a slightly warm.   They sound great with tons of punch and lots of damping with whatever was thrown at them.  The JBLs sang and put to shame any DJ system I've heard. review_body:
Bought this so that I would have some shelf placement adjustability to center below a 37\\" LCD on a wall in a master bedroom, with a dresser below. Most other shelves seem to need to be centered on a wall stud. This one attaches to two consecutive studs and offers a lot of freedom in placement.

I have the legs fully retracted, with a blue ray DVD player and cable box stacked on it, and there's still a good 5\\" of space behind to the wall for cord management. This might stick out a bit too much for some people's taste in a similar situation, but I like the look, and so does my wife.

With a little cord management, this thing looks clean. It has a nice black cover over the wall bracket that offers a good background to hide cords, etc. Using simple velcro cord ties and a little work, I was able to conceal all cords from most angles of view. I also installed the Wiremold Flatscreen Cover Kit [[ASIN:B0015EA3NO Wiremold CMK30 Flat Screen Television Cord Cover Kit, White]] to cover all the power cords and coax on the wall from the shelf to the floor, painted it the same color as the wall, and presto- professional looking installation at a fraction of the cost.

product_title: Marantz NR1402 AV Receiver (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
I love everything about this AV receiver: Its relatively small size, easy setup, great sound and a reasonable price.

I replaced an HK AVR146, a huge, heavy, confusing, poorly thought-out AV receiver with its opposite. I had wanted to add rear speakers to my system, but the initial setup with the HK was so difficult and the unit so cumbersome to deal with that I kept putting it off. My complaint of the HK was that stereos used to be easy to set up while computers were difficult, but now that computers are much easier to use, it seems that stereos (or AV receivers) have now become difficult. Why? The Marantz NR1402 AV Receiver was super easy to set up. They provided a microphone and a clear on screen wizard that allowed me to set up a 5.1 system in minutes, with barely a glance at the on-line manual.

My speakers are Wharfedale Diamond 8.2 front speakers, 8.1 rear and a 9.CC center. The sound is fantastic. I love this system. I can't say enough good things about the Marantz NR1402. This is exactly how a relatively complex piece of consumer equipment should be designed: quality materials, great visual design, perfect size to weight ratio, and easy setup.

My only complaint is the printed manual. Not only is it badly designed, much of the instruction was just wrong. It basically told you to run the setup without plugging in the unit first. Huh? Did anyone proof this before it went to press? The supplied user's guide on DVD made up for it. Lots of details and links. I wish Nikon would follow this online user's guide design.

One other comment, even though I haven't yet set up the remote, it is a universal remote that can control all your devices. More after I set this up.

product_title: Philips Fidelio Primo Docking Speaker
review_headline: Excellent Sound and Elegant Good Looks
review_body:
I've been and audiophile for over 3 decades, and I would not have thought of Philips as a name I would associate with high quality, but that seems to have changed. They still sell plenty of low end products, but this is a very impressive speaker dock. I would hold the quality of this unit up to Bose, Bowers & Wilkins, or Boston Acoustics. I was intrigued by the unique design, and I finally had a chance to hear it play at Fry's using my own music on my IPhone. I was very impressed with it's clear sound and tight bass, but was reluctant to pay $500 for it.

I saw this on Amazon listed as a refurbished unit for nearly half it's list price, so even though I was not in need of another speaker dock I could not resist. The remote is small and looks good, but not as responsive as I'd like. You have to be at just the right angle to get it to work. Also, I have not figured out what the advantage is to their app they have you download onto your mobile device. It seems to work just fine w/o it. The only issue I have is when I left my IPhone docked over night while on vacation and my alarm went off at full volume! It is the fault of my cell that has it pump out that loud to force the tiny internal speaker to be able to wake me up, but far too loud when docked. Something the designers had not anticipated.

This is not a small portable speaker dock at nearly 2' wide and rather heavy, but I still wanted to wrap it in my robes, stuff it in a duffel bag and take it on the plane with us as a carry-on for our trip to Disneyland and other vacations we've taken, much to my Wife chagrin. I love the design style and good clear sound that I can turn up outdoors and not feel so limited, like I would with most any other small speaker systems I've tried. At full volume it does not seem to clip like most powered speakers with their limited wattage. Even at low volume the bass is remarkably rich, where other definitely fall short. I've no had it well over a decade with frequent use it has shown to be well built and durable, even taking it to my construction job sites with me. This remains one of my best purchases to date.nt use it has shown to be well built and durable, even taking it to my construction job sites with me. This remains one of my best purchases to date.

review_headline: Don't waste your time or money
review_body: Onkyo used to make excellent products. Sadly that is no longer true.  I originally purchased this receiver because it had the best features for the cheapest price. Let me just say, it's cheaper for a reason.  Within the first few minutes of installing this, I noticed that anything connected via HDMI would artifact (white lines would appear randomly and frequently). This made me disappointed, but it sounded good so I though I'd live with it. Within a few hours, the entire screen was flashing and displaying green colors. I tried a blu ray player, a ps3, a laptop, a cable set-top box; everything resulted with the same issues. I even tried three different HDMI cables. The unit was unusable after about three hours.  The remote is hands down, the worst remote I've ever seen. I've been using various electronics for 20 years, and even I had to mess around with the buttons before I got the hang of it.  I'm going to be returning this product ASAP. All around, one of the worst electronic purchases I've ever made. Onkyo will never have my business again. A quick call to my local trusted home theater installer, and it turns out that he's been running into the same problems for years. He used to exclusively sell Onkyo receivers, but the quality has gone down so much recently that he had to stop selling them.  It would be one thing if the product lasted a year, but it was basically DOA. Hopefully I'll have better luck with my next receiver (as usual I will be purchasing through amazon).

review_body: This is a great alternative to those bulky expensive metal articulating monstrosities. Don't make the same mistake so many other's do with their expensive high-end HDTV's.  You wouldn't hang a nice piece of art up close to the ceiling then tilt it down for viewing would you?  Hell no!  Place your TV at eye level and for maximum aesthetic satisfaction, the tighter to the wall the better. This mount does the trick.  Some Samsung 40\\" HDTVs use the VESA 200X200 standard.  Here are somethings to be aware of:  Samsung ultra-slim TVs (at least the D series) have Recessed VESA holes as opposed to flush VESA holes.  This mount may require you to go to the hardware store and buy washers, new screws, or take a hacksaw to the included screws.  If you are handy and have a hacksaw, you will be fine.  This mount is best suited for the HDTV which is hung on the wall then not touched there after.  If you constantly have to plug things in and out of your HDTV (for example swapping game systems with DVD players or USB devices) then this isn't the mount for you. The reason is because there is only one screw holding your very expensive HDTV to the wall.  Even the lightest TVs can weigh 20 pounds. Too much moving of the HDTV will eventually loosen the screws and possibly bend the TV frame at the VESA holes.  The kickstand doesn't work unless you modify it by shortening it.  There just isn't enough slack in the wire to tilt the TV out 4 inches.  (This is the same kickstand sold with the VESA 400 X 400 ultra-slim mounts, which works very effectively)  This is not a big deal because if you are buying this mount, then your HDTV is small and light enough to take off the wall, make your cable swaps, then place back on the wall.  Overall I'm satisfied with this mounting solution for my Samsung UN40D6400, but it helps to be handy and not have a need to swap cables in and out of my HDTV

product_title: iBeats Headphones with ControlTalk From Monster - In-Ear Noise Isolation - Black
review_headline: iBeats Review plus Beats by Dre Tour Earbud Face-Off
review_body:
Looking to jump into the celebrity endorsed headphone bandwagon? You might want to take a look at the iBeats. They are Monster Beats' entry level earbuds and they are aimed to replace your stock Apple white earbuds if you ever wish to upgrade. At 99$, they're still a bit overpriced, but trust me, they sound awesome.
I was actually surprised by their performance. I prefer their sound and feel now over my other Beats earbuds, the Beats Tour!

Yeah... the iBeats are surprisingly amazing. Probably because of their metal cavity and smaller size (compared to the Tour's bigger cavity), the iBeats have a tighter and more intense bass response. The mids get sacrificed a bit because of this but in my opinion, they sound more exciting than the Tours. They put me more in that musical in-the-zone trance than the Tours because of those more prominent sub-bass levels you could feel in your head

I was kinda baffled about this. We all know that an earbud's sound is critically determined by the size of the eartip that you use (that's why earbuds usually come with various size eartips. Beats gives you seven sets.) The eartip needs to fit perfectly to create that ear cavity seal which will optimize the sound. Keeping this in mind, my perfect iBeats sound was achieved with the 2nd to the smallest eartips. I was using those same size eartips on the Tours all along but since I've heard the Beats sound better with those, I decided to go the next size up with the Tours. With that, the Tours' bass response improved but even then, the iBeats are still tighter and bassier. The Tours have more prominent mids but the iBeats have that more modern EQ curve with goosed up lows and highs plus a scooped middle.

The iBeats also feel better in the ear because they're solidly metal. When you slide them in your ears, you could feel that smooth, cold touch of chrome. And since they're smaller, they feel secure and lighter. The Tours have this big logo on the earbud andsometimes they're uncomfortably heavy. But I admit, the Tours look a lot better than the iBeats.

Both Tours and the iBeats have Control Talk for iDevices, meaning they have mics and buttons for answering phone calls (for iPhones), recording (for GarageBand) and buttons to play, pause, skip, tracks and control volume.

My nitpick about the iBeats is the wiring. They're thinner than what I'm used to with the Beats Tours. The Beats Tour has this flat and thick Fettucine style cable that's said to be tangle free. The iBeats have this thin wires that look that they may snap with one accidental yank. They still feel like well made Monster cables though. I think the reason why they made the wires thin is to keep them as light as possible.

The albums I've been testing these earbuds with were Metallica's \\"...And Justice For All\\" and Animals As Leaders' \\"Weightless\\". I know, these are not marketed for heavy metal but they actually sound great with Beats because of the pulsing deep bass lines, thumping kick drums and thick mids and highs. I also tested them with Radiohead's first track of their \\"Amnesiac\\" album. That track has an awesome sub-bass track. I also played some Dr. Dre (what else, yo) from Spotify. Everything sounded awesome and pimped up!

So, yeah, if you want to upgrade from your regular earphones and listen to music more intimately, I recommend you get the iBeats first. The Tours look cooler and more sturdier, but the iBeats are more comfortable and have a surprisingly heftier bass response, plus they're $50 cheaper. Although there are other good or even better headphones out there at these prices, they don't look as good as these Monsters.

It does charge! Just seems kind of slow. The BIG flaw we encountered was the charger isn't adjustable to allow docking with phones and iPods with thick cases. This means you'll have to remove the case each time you use the clock; which rendered the clock radio useless for my husband. Would have been nice if Logitech allowed for more versatility.

Other than that, I love this clock, my husband not so much. I only rated it 3 stars because I felt the buttons could be better, and the ability to charge/dock any phone with ease isn't possible. Still, I'd recommend it, or at least give it 3 1/2 stars if Amazon allowed.

product_title: J.Fi Acoustic Natural Ebony Wood and Metal  (Ebony / Titanium)
review_body:
As a forewarning, I used these earphones to replace a set of professional Shure earphones that I loved(I stepped on them accidentally). In comparison, these headphones look much cooler, I like the wood shell. They do produce a nice sound with decent highs and lows, but the bass is no where near my old pair. They also seem less powerful than the Shure phones in general. That being said, these were $150 less than my previous pair so all in all I feel they are a good value. I tried them intermittently with my IPod earphones, and the J.Fi's produced a much richer sound.

They are not great at blocking outside noise, which I attribute to the ear tips. I tried all of the tips that came with the earphones and didn't love any of them. I like the look of the foam tips, but they didn't sit in my ear well and gave inconsistent sound, which differed with movement even just turning my head. I currently am using the largest pair of rubber tips which take away from the overall look of the phones and are OK at best in blocking outside noise. They do however, stay in my ears even when running or working in the yard. I may try a tip from another company to see if there is improvement with the noise blocking. The Shure tips really filled my ear canal opening and blocked out noise even when I wasn't listening to music.

Bang for the buck, I think these are a good entry point to higher performance earphones. I do not regret buying them at all. I am not sure if I would buy these again or try a Klipsch or Bose next time, not because I don't like them, I just haven't experienced those products and would like to compare performance levels.

product_title: Sennheiser CX 500 In-Ear Headphone
review_body:
A while back I purchased an inexpensive set of GoGroove \\"in-ear\\" headphones. The main purpose of these were for working out at the gym, and so I felt it wasn't a worthy investment to spend a high amount. I consider over $50 to be over budget considering its intended use. And for $15 the GoGrooves did the job (sort of). Just not adequately so. The tonal quality kept changing, and I found myself constantly fidgeting with the ear pieces to reposition them. And well... let's face it... the fidelity was never quite there. And in all honesty what should people expect for a $15 set of cans? For serious listening at home, I own a pair of Sennheiser HD580's for that. But for on the go or working out at the gym I was ready for something better - but still didn't want to overspend on something that could easily get lost, misplaced, or damaged.

So I did some research and stumbled upon the Sennheiser CX500's. Now there are many similar styles and comparable models, but I was still in the mindframe of sticking with a sensible budget (again, for their intended use). At a $20-$25 price point, I couldn't resist taking a chance on these but kept scratching my head about the price. These are normally $120 marked down to $20-$25... and Sennheiser no less! Always the skeptic, I felt there must be a reason for this. Generally speaking, if it sounds too good to be true it usually is. After doing some research, I discovered this model of headphones had the unfortunate problem of being \\"cloned\\" by fake knock-offs. There are a few excellent videos on YouTube that showcase the differences between the fake Sennheisers and the real ones. That being said, let me summarize my immediate impression with the Sennheiser CX-500's:

1) These are definitely the REAL ones! If you decide to purchase these, please do yourself a favor and buy direct from Amazon. If you purchase from eBay, there's a good chance you may get the inferior knock-offs. There are some vendors on Amazon that sold the fake ones, while others sold the real ones. If you opt to purchase from another vendor, definitely do your research before you buy. For me, the $1.00-$2.00 difference in price wasn't worth the hassle or risk. Amazon's customer service and backing of their product is second to none, and made me feel at ease placing this order. But I still admit my fingers remained crossed until the package arrived.

2) The packaging is one of those ultra-hard clamshell type pain in the a*sses to cut & pry open. Immediately I felt this was a very good sign, but at the frustration of taking nearly 10 minutes to get the darn things out!

3) The headphones come with a cloth case that has a nice tight \\"snap\\" to it - which is one of the indications this product is genuine. As you examine the case, spare pads, the presentation, and the earphones themselves you can sense and feel QUALITY to them.

4) The resolution of all the fonts - from the case, to the clip, to the plug, to the wire (and associated parts) - is very sharp and crisp. No cheap \\"ink-jet\\" style markings in sight (another good indicator).

5) The volume slider switch indeed works PROPERLY! Meaning... when turned all the way down the sound is NOT silent, but instead muted down to about 5%. The knock-offs cut the sound out completely. This is not Sennheiser's design, so beware of this.

6) The headphones will still pick up noise from any vibration done to the upper half of the wire above the slider switch. Any vibration done below this switch is pretty much inaudible. Some people have commented the headphones aren't Sennheisers if you hear noise when the upper wire is touched. This isn't entirely true. Even my HD580's will make a noise, but I imagine the fake ones being a LOT worse.

7) And now what most people likely want to know... how do they sound? I will say right out of the box they sounded MUCH better than the \\"GoGroove\\" models I purchased several months back. Immediately I experienced rich bass and good clarity. The high frequencies felt a little strained, but this is perfectly normal as the speakers haven't been broken in yet. In fact, I started noticing IMMEDIATE improvements after listening for 15 minutes, and yet even more improvements after a couple hours. These headphones keep sounding better and better! I fully expect these to reach near full capacity after 20 or 40 hours of \\"break-in\\". By the time I wrote this review, I could already experience very impressive audio. Wow, I am loving these!!! And I'm writing this review from the standpoint of an audiophile, but with reasonable expectations. I may be picky, but am not a snob about it.

Now to be honest... do these sound like $120 headphones? NO!!! Absolutely not. But they do sound significantly better than the $15 GoGrooves and the similar priced Skull Candy brand. But obviously, this is an unfair comparison because Sennheiser is well renowned for their audio quality and comfort. I would say these sound like a $60+ pair of headphones. If I paid $60 for them I would probably rate this product at 4 (* * * *) stars. But at $25... or even $35 I am rating this a 5 (* * * * *) star purchase. These are genuine Sennheisers, and while the CX-500's don't have the electronic noise isolation they still do a decent job passively blocking most of the ambient noise out. These headphones fit more comfortable and \\"snug\\" compared to the other brands mentioned. The position of the speaker always seems to find the \\"sweet spot\\" on its own, and continues to keep the best distance away from the inner ear. I could never get the other brands to maintain a consistent fit this way (even with the interchanging pads). As a result, I can wear these headphones longer while listening to music at softer volumes. And better yet, I haven't experienced the need to mess around and fidget with these too much. They pretty much go in the ears perfectly right from the start. If these were available at this price back when I ordered the GoGrooves, I would have likely bought 3: One for myself. One as a gift. And another as a spare! I truly believe these are priced so low because of the unfortunate knock-offs that are prevalent. If you do your homework, I think you will find these are an excellent purchase at an even better value! Thank you for the sweet music, Sennheiser, and keep up the good work!

UPDATE (12/15/11): I HAD THESE HEADPHONES FOR ALMOST A MONTH NOW. THEY *STILL* SOUND TERRIFIC! IN FACT, THEY SOUND SLIGHTLY BETTER AND I BELIEVE THEY ARE AT THEIR PRIME NOW. I WOULD ACTUALLY SAY THESE SOUND LIKE $75+ HEADPHONES. THEIR COMFORT IS EQUALLY AMAZING. THEY DON'T MOVE OR DISLODGE THEMSELVES (THE CLIP HELPS WITH ACTIVE MOVEMENT). THERE IS ALMOST ZERO EAR FATIGUE. I CAN EASILY SAY THEY'RE ALMOST AS COMFORTABLE AS THE OPEN-EAR DESIGNS THAT FIT OVER THE EAR. I'M THRILLED WITH THIS PRODUCT, AND AM CONFIDENT OTHERS THAT ARE ABLE TO GET THE GENUINE SENNHEISER BRAND WILL SURELY BE TOO!

They started to actually leave my jaw dropped. I compared them to Beats Pro and well, I found the Beats inferior in style, sound quality, AND comfort. But I must say that the Crossfades are a bass biased headphone. What that means is if you like bass, this is the headphone for you. Also, these do have a nice extent of passive noise cancellation. I think it cancels up to 10 or 12 db. Like I said before, these headphones are a bass biased pair headphones. With that being said, that means these headphones are bad for certain genres such as: Rock, Metal, Jazz, etc. The bass just overpowers the song. But, that does mean that these headphones work good with other genres such as: Rap, Pop, Dubstep, etc. If you're into that type of music then go ahead, be my guest and buy these headphones.  *EDIT*  It's been about 3 weeks since I got these and they are still going strong. The only problem is a little chip in the black plastic surrounding the metal faceplates. It was no big deal though, I just painted over it. Also, the speakers sound even better than better. They have better highs, mids, and bass now, even considering the conditions I've put it through. Dropped probably 15+ times. Once off a 20 ft drop; harsh weather: snow, hail, massive rain. I bought two of these power line network adapters, and a refurbished Cisco router to see how it would work out.  I had them all set up in less than 5 minutes and am pulling down a 20mbps downloads and 5mbps uploads through the new wireless router, that is pulling its signal from our primary router downstairs.  When I plug directly into the new router with a wired connection, it increases my download speed to 25mbps and the upload speed stays the same.    This obviously is a far cry from a 100/1000mbs direct CAT5 connection, but is is a much cheaper alternative to having CAT5 run throughout the house, and is plenty fast enough for streaming videos/music etc.  I also plugged my DVD player in my room directly to the new router I set up and am able to stream Pandora and Netflix through it without any issues. product_title: Apc Smart-ups Rt 8000VA 208V (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
If you are using the device to run something like a refrigerator or a film projector, I guess it is OK. But if you are running a mission-critical computer system, it just isn't up to par. First of all, it arrived DOA. The APC support people were very good about replacing it, but a batteries failed a few months later. Again, they were very good about replacing them, but I would greatly preferred if the hadn't failed in the first place. Even if you ignore these problems, the thing has all kind of shortcomings - shortcomings that you would not expect from something that was supposed to be an industrial-strength solution:
1. The power connections are skinny little screws that seem more suitable for connecting devices using hundreds of watts rather than thousands.
2. Repair manuals might exist, but I looked online and couldn't find any. So the only way to fix it is to ship the whole thing - all 285 pounds of it - back to the factory.
3. There is no way to replace just the power module, like you can with HP UPS devices.
4. The device has 4 big, heavy batteries, and when one of them fails, there is no way to tell which one. A complete set of replacement batteries costs $900, and to add insult to injury, the manufacturer doesn't have them in stock.
5. It has a web-based menu system, but some of the menu items are flaky. For example, if you test email notification and it fails, the screen just freezes.
6. The menu is confusing. It seems like there might be a way to send text messages when there are serious problems, and email messages for routine notifications. But if there is, I can't figure it out. And in any case there are no screens summarizing what you have programmed.
7. If you lose your connection to the web-based manager and try to re-connect, you get this message: \\"Notice: Someone is currently logged into the APC Management Web Server. Please try again later.\\" All you can do is wait until the previous connection times out, which is several minutes.
8. Because it is a line-interactive UPS (rather than double conversion), there is no way to be sure that you really are protected. It might give no sign of problems, but still fail to protect your computer. It can also get \\"confused\\", and give bogus error indications which can only be cleared by Momentarily turning off power to your mission-critical computer.

Better choices for quality UPS equipment are Powerware, Liebert, and Marathon.

product_title: NuForce NE-600X Red High-efficiency In-ear Headphones
review_body: As a long time Grado Labs fan, I was almost heartbroken when I finally broke my trusty SR-80s one time too many and couldn't fix them.  After finding myself thrust back into the headphone market I was shocked by the variety out there.  I'll cut to the chase:  Do these sound as good as my Grados?  Probably not.  Do they sound better than any in-ear headphones I've ever tried?  Yes (but I haven't tried that many).  Are they a good value for less than $30?  Absolutely!  When I first put them in, I nearly shipped them back, I was underwhelmed.  Then I took the time to play with the fit and was very impressed with the sound quality and isolation.  I'll have to see how well they hold up, but so far I'm glad I got them.

product_title: Logitech Ultimate Ears 600 Noise-Isolating - Dark Silver
review_body:
I'm not going to write about how great these sound since there are plenty of reviews that do that (even though they sound almost as good as the TripleFi 10's I have). I'm going to write about Ultimate Ears customer service.

I received a set of UE 600vi earphones as a gift. After a couple of months, I noticed the wire starting to pull our from the jack end of the cable. Even though at this point, the headphones were still working, it was only a matter of time before the cable pulled out or broke internally. Late on a Friday night, I emailed support through the UE website, explaining the problem and received an automated \\"we'll get back to you within 48 hours\\" reply.

The next day (Saturday), I received an email apologizing for the problem and asking me for some information (name, address, model number, etc.) and since I received the unit as a gift, some pictures (one with a handwritten note indicating the provided reference number) for \\"evaluation\\" of the problem. I provided the information and pictures (box, UPC number, close up of the cable pulling out, and entire unit with the handwritten note). Withing minutes, I received another email saying they would replace them with a brand new unit and provided a UPS return shipping label. They also thanked me for being an Ultimate Ears customer. They are on the way back as I write this.

I had a similar warranty issues with another headphone company (received as a gift where the left earpiece stopped working, which was an issue well documented) and they wouldn't honor the warranty without a receipt (even though they were a new model and had not even been on the market long enough for the warranty to expire). The did finally agree to sell me a new set at a discounted price but sent only the headphones, no accessories, no ear tips, nothing. UE is sending a new box with all accessories.

The 600vi is not my first Ultimate Ears product and certainly won't be my last.

LL

product_title: Sony MDR-ZX100/BLK Studio Monitor Headphones-Blk
review_body: The Sony MDR-ZX100s update the infamously shoddy headband design of Sony's popular V150 headphones, while maintaining the excellent sound quality that made the V150s such a desirable product. The ZX100's swiveling cans seem adequately durable, and allow the headphones to fold up flat for transportation and storage. So they've got that going for them... which is nice.   In my opinion, the only other widely-available pair of headphones that give the ZX100s a run for their money, at this price point, are the Koss PortaPros. If you're at all finicky about your consumer electronics, I suggest checking out the PortaPros before you commit to buying the MDR-ZX100s. I ended up preferring the ZX100s for purely aesthetic reasons; the throwback styling of the PortaPros just didn't scratch me where I itched.   For me, the headband is still the weakest point of this product. In a perfect world, the cans would fold up further into the curved headband for added portability. After all, many competing models offer this feature. Overall, however, because of their superior sound quality, I consider the ZX100s a good enough value to earn a 5 star review.

product_title: Nyrius SW100 Digital Audio Optical Toslink 3 Input Selector Switch Compatible with Fiber Optic Cables, HDTV, Blu-ray DVD player, PCM, Dolby Digital, DTS, XBOX360, PS3
review_headline: Does the job but it's not elegant
review_body: It's a $20 product and I didn't expect much. I did expect it to be smaller, and have more accurate tolerances with regard to the ports. (More on that later) I don't pretend to understand the design challenges encountered with constructing the device, but it seems reasonable they could have crammed its innards into a paper coaster sized case. I viewed the reference photos but I still wasn't prepared for the chunkiness of the device. It also looks and feels very chintzy.  The modulation of the selector switch is clunky and tends to hesitate before snapping  back into its detent. The ports are overly snug. I have three different manufacturer's cables and I had to force each into the ports with about the same amount of resistance. They snap in firmly, but I was hesitant at first to snap the first cable in place. I've never had a digital optical device with a port tolerance that far off and I've never had a problem with loose cable connections. That said your cables won't fall out or even wiggle. :) Something else I noticed about the ports is they have circular symmetry, unlike cable terminations which are symmetrical on two sides (think square vs. trapezoid). I realize this adds some flexibility when it comes to placement of the device with relation to tension on the cables running to it. The manufacturer should highlight this in the product sheet as a \\"feature\\" and explain the benefit. This actually added to my hesitation when I seated the first cable because when I pulled it out after it failed to snap in place with a reasonable amount of applied force, I noticed the port symmetry and had to make sure I wasn't doing something wrong.  It's clunky, chunky, and built with poor tolerances, but it works... for now. And I've hidden it inside a cabinet so I don't have to look at it. I wish I'd gotten a black one.  I estimate I'll use the switch about once a week. I'll report back if there are any issues with durability.

product_title: Coby 8 GB 1.8-Inch Video MP3 Player with FM Radio
review_body:
I wanted it for my kids to listen to audiobooks - Forget it - It is nearly impossible to get this done.

WHY: This player arranges all titles of a folder in alphabetical order! All titles with \\"A\\" are placed before all titles starting with \\"B\\" so for example the chapter \\"End\\" plays before \\"Intro\\". I imported the CDs with iTunes (you need MP3 or WMA format, so sometimes you cannot copy the disk directly). This is fine, if you just have \\"Title01\\" \\"Title02\\" ... But if iTunes recognize the Cd and automatically names the chapters, it will be a mess, no way to play them accurately. Funny thing is: It sorted \\"Titel 01\\" to \\"Titel 13\\" right, but after \\"Chapter 1\\" comes \\"Chapter 10\\" (goes on with 11, 12 ... 19, 2, 20, ...)! So don't forget the \\"0\\".

If you have more than 1 CD for one audiobook: The Player is fine with several Folders for example \\"hocu a/hocu b/hoku c\\" (make sure you have the same indication in album/interpret/... otherwise it could be tricky to find the 3 Cds in an connected way on the player). Make short names otherwise you will have to wait a long time to read which folder you are looking at while the player is moving thru the title. Don't name the CDs \\"CD1/CD2/CD3\\" it will not recognize this and you will just see one Folder \\"CD\\".

I spend hours and hours to try everything, I installed the Coby Media Manager from the player and hoped this one will do it - nope! So I will have to change the titles manually, I have to find new short names (not to spacy, so that the kids still recognize what they are listening to!). I really do not understand, how this impossible is possible. A lot of fancy things Videos and Photos (on a quite tiny screen) but no understanding of how to play audiobooks properly. I can't spend a lot of money to get 3 kids an iPod or another highprice player. And all players in this price class have some difficulties in one or another way! Sorry to say this, but this is a \\"pain in my a\\"

product_title: Harman Kardon HK990 2x150 Watt 2.2-Channel Stereo Integrated Amplifier (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: A tale of two units,it's not good
review_body: I have a 2.1 stereo system so when I read the reviews for this amp I thought it would add several features missing from my system. I was looking forward to the built-in dac and room correction most but the added power also interested me. I ordered directly from Amazon and the amp arrived in perfect condition. The amp is big and heavy and imho a beautiful piece of work when off. When the amp is on the power light and light all the way around the volume knob are a very bright white that cannot be dimmed,this is very annoying in a dark room. Even though the manual is sparse on specifics I found the set-up to be quite easy and intuitive. With the amp in direct mode the sound was quite good but less dynamic than other amps I have used (Accuphase,Ayre,McIntosh,PS Audio,and now Yamaha). When I used the EZ set eq set-up the processing pushed 90% of the sound over to the right speaker no matter where the microphone was placed in the room. HK advised me to return it for another unit and said that they had not heard of this happening.  I received the second unit from Amazon and noticed immediately that the amp in direct mode sounded bass heavy and muffled. This time when I ran the auto calibration it worked perfectly and sounded great,not muffled at all. That evening I listened through the headphone output and there was quite a bit of noise on it. The next morning I turned on the amp and two of the characters on the display were not working. I contacted HK again and again they said that they had never heard of this happening. I returned the second unit to Amazon the next day and that afternoon received an email from HK offering to exchange it for a unit directly from their warehouse but it was too late at that point. I decided not to risk buying a third unit.  I don't know if HK had a bad batch that didn't get inspected and checked before leaving the production line or what but both of the amps I received from Amazon had the same 07/10 build date on them. I would also like tosay, since when is an amp produced 18 months ago still being sold as a new product,these are usually called nos (new old stock). However,Amazon was great throughout this whole process and HK customer service was quite good also but I just couldn't seem to get an HK990 that worked properly. I buy a lot from Amazon but I don't think I will buy high priced electronics from them again and I certainly won't buy any high priced electronics made by Harman Kardon,that's for sure.

product_title: Dayton Audio APA150 150-Watts Power Amplifier (Black)
review_body:
I needed a no-frills amplifier for my gym room. I didn't need any pre-amplifier features but wanted to have a volume control knob, and did not need an immense amount of power due to the small size of the room. The Dayton unit fit the description perfectly and I am very happy with my purchase.

I have the amp hooked up to a pair of Sony SS-B3000 speakers. I have two signal sources, a Sony LCD TV that in turn gets its signal from a Roku box and a DVD player via HDMI, and a Squeezebox Touch player. The amp has only one input so I use a cheap external RCA signal switcher to toggle between them. The unit has line out connections in case you want to chain it with another amplifier, e.g., to drive a subwoofer.

The unit is extremely solidly built and simple to set up and operate. It is compact, exactly the width of the Roku and Squeezebox Touch units which I keep on top of the amp. Voice quality is very good to my non-expert ears, and the unit delivers so much power I rarely have the dial turned to more than 20%. The design is simple, with just the volume dial and an on/off button on the front panel.

You can toggle on the signal detection feature using a switch on the back panel. With that feature activated, the unit sniffs the incoming signal level and goes to sleep if the audio source has been idle for a while. I am extremely pleased with this functionality. It wakes up really quickly, and does not take a high signal level to wake up (My comparison point is my Onkyo 2x100W power amplifier which I have downstairs and I can't use its signal detection feature because the input volume needs to be turned up relatively high for the amp to detect it, and the amp goes to sleep when there are quiet passages in the music, like for Chopin). The LED embedded in the power button changes color from red to blue to indicate whether the unit is sleeping or active.

product_title: MEElectronics M9P Flat Cable In-Ear Headphone with Headset Functionality and Universal Volume Control
review_body:
I've been using the headphones about an hour now on a variety of music that I own. So far they are doing very well on all types of music. The bass is great for $15.00 ear buds. The packaging seems a little flimsy but a great buy none the less.
Sound Quality - Most genres I've listened to are projected pretty well. Ear buds needs broken in to get full sound and so far these are doing pretty well. Tweaking with the soundboard gives a pretty good response on the ear buds. I've used an iPhone as well and the same goes for mobile devices. What little you can arrange for a mixer and equalizer, the ear buds respond well.
Feel - The ear buds aren't as comfortable as I would have liked them. I cannot complain because I've only used 1 of 4 included sets of replaceable buds. There is a pretty snug fit on the ones I am using now. I haven't worked out/ran with these yet but I can't see any problems with staying in my ears for that.
Packaging - the packaging is a little flimsy but they are $15. You get the ear buds, a clam case with a stout zipper, and 4 sets of extra rubber buds. The case is not 100% smash-proof but will hold up nicely I assume. The zipper is pretty heavy duty and doesn't look like it will jam or break easily.
Warranty - 1 year from manufacturer.
Cord - The cord is actually the cable inside of a plastic tubing. Straight from the packaging, the tubing is kinked and annoying but I see it straightening out soon.
Control - the control works actually pretty well. I am usually skeptical about non-Apple products working with my Apple products and this seems to be pretty legit. The control works for voice commands, phone calls, answering/hanging up calls, skipping songs, pausing and replaying songs.

After mounting the TV I recommend you use caution whenever you must move it, especially with the arm extended. product_title: Onkyo HT-S5400 7.1-Channel Home Theater System
review_body: I looked at many other home theater systems but chose the Onkyo S5400 because it had more options to attach external video sources. The home theater systems that included a DVD player seemed to be too much of a compromise.  I paired this with an LG Blu-ray player and I get the benefit of a home theater system with my chosen DVD player and the option to attach many other sources.  In all this is a great system, especially for the price.  Just over $300 for a full featured AV receiver and 7 good speakers. The sound is great!  Set up was easy...the color-coded speaker wires helped in attaching speakers and the auto-speaker set up was a quick and easy way to optimize the surround speakers.  I have an xbox360, AppleTV and LG Blu-ray player all attached via HDMI with great results.  I have also attached my iPhone at times and it is great to be able to control the iPhone using the Onkyo remote.  Very good picture passed through the AV receiver and as mentioned before a full and robust sound.  Using the system is pretty easy...the manual is complete and easy to read and the remote is pretty easy to use.  I am giving the system only 4 stars, however, because of three shortcomings that are probably the result of  trade offs to keep the price low.  The system does not have internet access so no Internet Radio nor an iPhone app to control the receiver. I also have a Pioneer Elite receiver with Internet access and the iPhone app is a very nice feature. The other drawback is something that took me awhile to figure out as the necessary information was buried at the back of the manual. There is no converting of input signals..no up converting nor down converting of video input to the video output. This means that if your input is HDMI then the output must be HDMI.  If your input is Component then the output must be Component.  This means the best way to use the system is to have all video inputs the same. In my case I use all HDMI inputs but if I ever connect something that is notHDMI I need to add another output (e.g. component or composite) that matches my input. Lastly, the on-screen display works only when the video output from the Onko to the TV or projector is HDMI. If you are using component or composite video outputs then you cannot use the OSD.  In summary this system has a few shortcomings but the benefits and low cost certainly outweigh these few limitations. Using all HDMI inputs eliminated all of the display and conversion issues.

review_headline: Good Quality and Easy to Set Up

After reading up a bit on the various mounts, I chose these because a) they got good reviews and b) they were rated for 20lbs, which gives me more leeway on what kind of speakers I can use them with. I'm not like alot of reviewers on here, in that I would rather use mounts that are rated for at least 1.5 to 2 times the weight of my speakers.

For mounting about 8 ft high I used the dry-wall anchors and 1 1/2\\" wood screws that came in the package. I don't know why a lot of reviewers warned against the supplied anchors, if you are careful and know a little bit about dry wall anchors and how finicky they can be you will be able to mount these just fine without worrying about finding a stud (provided, of course, your satellites are not too heavy).

The mounts look good, the setup looks clean, I am definitely satisfied with my purchase.

UPDATE 9-17-2012: I have the much larger BIC Venturi DV52si speakers mounted now with these brackets and they handle the extra size and weight just fine. Using drywall anchors on one side and stud-mounted on the other and I have no issues. These mounts work very well.

product_title: Grace Digital GDI-IRDT200 Hi-Fi Internet Radio Tuner
review_headline: Not bad, kinda- could be so much better.
review_body:
This unit does do what it says it will, but other reviewer's complaints about usability and appearance are on the mark and I won't repeat them here. Additional notes I would add-

* The webpage interface gives you very little control over the devices' settings. Pretty much the ability to create and edit \\"My Stations\\", \\"My Streams\\" and \\"My Podcasts\\". There are MANY other settings which are only accessible through the irritating knob interface.

ON EDIT: I have had this unit for several months now and the issue of how it is controlled is really its biggest problem. There are FOUR different ways to control the Grace: the front panel, the remote control, the \\"reciva\\" webpage and the smartphone app. Every of these controls a different, arbitrary subset of what you need. You would not believe how little control you are given with the interfaces that have the most potential: the web-based control and the smartphone app are very, very limited. The remote control is the only way to store presets (you store presets 1-9 one way and all the others in another way, of course). The front panel interface is so complicated and obscure that those presets become very important. So why can't I store a preset through anything but the remote control? I'd tucked mine away in a drawer, since I have an iPhone. Now the manual and the remote control are kept at hand for easy access.

The net effect of all this awful user design is just exhaustion. I am the 'master' of this box in my household (I still refer to the manual): everyone else has thrown their hands up and walked away. [END EDIT.]

* PC users can apparently play music stored on their computers somehow: this is not an option (AFAIK) for Mac users' iTunes systems, although it is promoted here as available.

* I have been unable to find, anywhere, a way to mute (or pause) playback with this thing short of turning it completely off.

* It has an FM antenna input, using what I am told is the European PAL connector. USA users with a coax antenna are on their own for finding an adaptor. Vendor refuses to send such adaptor.

* If you TRY to use the FM antenna input and your chosen station is also streaming to the internet, that signal overrides the FM input no matter what: you can't listen to the FM broadcast. (well: you could disconnect your internet feed...)

* Push the power switch to turn the unit off and the pilot light LIGHTS UP. Turn it on: light OFF.

So, in all, this is an inept box, but the only one of its kind at this form factor and price point.
