product_title: Soundcast SurroundCast - Wireless Receiver / Transmitter Audio System
review_body:
I purchased the Soundcast wireless system to avoid running rear speaker wire under carpet and heavy furniture. I had reservations that it would work in part because the units were small and concern other wireless devices would interfere with the signal. Nevertheless with the confidence of Amazon's return policy I ordered it. The install was fairly easy after reading the directions. Do that. Don't just assume you \\"can figure it out.\\" there is an order of making the connections that is necessary. As other reviewers have indicated the term \\"wireless\\" applies to getting the audio signal from the transmitter ( near TV or A/V amplifier) to a pair of remote speakers. In my case about 15 feet away. Customers have to realize that there is a speaker wire connection from the Soundcast receiver to your speakers. If you desire a total wireless speaker system where the remote speakers have built in receivers look elsewhere and be prepared to spend many hundreds of dollars more. But it is unfair to comment that \\"this system isn't totally wireless.\\" if you expected that I have a bridge in the Desert I'd like to sell.

In conclusion so far very good performance in the one month since installation. No interference from other wireless devices. You should understand that not ALL programming is broadcast with 5.1 surround sound. So don't think there is something wrong with the product because you do not always hear sound from the rear channels. I would recommend the product as it does what was described.

January 2013 Update:

Over the past few months I had what I thought were either transmissions or receiving issues with the Soundcast units. It did not seem that they were working properly (blue lights were our). Called Soundcast tech support and they were VERY helpful even months after purchase! Had our Satellite tech come over and he helped determine problem was actually with my A/V Receiver. Replaced the A/V with new Denon and Soundcast is working fineagain.

If you buy just realize that not all programing on cable or satellite is broadcast in 5.1 Surrounf Sound so can not broadcast something it is not receiving.

The design incorporates the tilting tightening screw directly into the mounting bracket. His is fine and all and not a reason to stay away. but \\"IF\\" tilt is a must have for you then maaaayyybbe i would think about it. Currently, I'm not ready to spend a large amount of money for headphones, but I still appreciate good sound (I've tried expensive headphones before and whatnot) and listen to a lot of music.. so I was looking for a balance of reasonably clear sound but at a low price.  My old budget pair of Panasonic HJE 300 earphones were starting to break down, so I was looking to try something new, and was willing to spend about $10-40.    I've owned the M9's for almost a month, so they've had a chance to burn in.  The sound is very clear for the most part, and I feel they're effective for everyday use.  You've probably read in other reviews that the bass is pretty heavy.. it's true, and it can be a bit overpowering at times.  I can understand if that might bother some people, and if that's you, you might want to look elsewhere. For myself, I like it and consider it a strength.  I think it does a good job of being strong yet not too muddy, with almost any genre.  Although a genre like hip hop or pop may benefit more from these than classical music, I thought classical music sounded good on them as well.    I used to own a pair of the old Sony Fontopia earphones.. it's hard to remember exactly, but I think they're both comparable sound-wise.  The M9 bass is probably heavier though, for better or worse.  The M9's have a clearer sound than my Panasonic budget phones, although I liked the Panasonic fit in my ear and cord build quality ALOT.  The M9s are pretty decent fit and good build quality, although I wish the cord didn't hold its shape so much (when I uncoil them, they're still a bit bent).  It isn't bad by any means, though.  To sum up, I think the M9's are pretty good, if not very good within its price range.  If you want a good value, I would recommend them.  But I do think they are still \\"budget\\" or \\"mid-price range\\" headphones, and I think it's unfair to expect them to perform like Bose headphones or whatever.  If Ihad more money (or maybe, if I was willing to spend more), I would probably look into more expensive options for best sound quality.  I don't know if I would buy the M9's again when it comes time to replace them (there's just so many options out there, I'd like to try something new), but they are still solid performers.

I use it with a 2008 Macbook > Fiio E10 > [[ASIN:B000OABTPQ Audioengine A5]] speaker setup and listen through [[ASIN:B000GKTQPY Sony MDRV6]]/[[ASIN:B0006GCCN6 Grado SR225]] headphones.

I was satisfied with the built in Realtek soundcard on the laptop but after reading some reviews and seeing the price I decided to give the E10 a try and see for myself if I could improve the sound quality at all.

The E10 comes in a nice little aluminum tin with included instructions, 2 sets of rubber stick on feet (8 total), and a 1M mini USB cable. The unit itself is very small and looks/feels well made. The volume pot has a good amount of resistance and does not feel cheap at all. One of the complaints I read about them was some units introduced a crackly noise into the sound if the headphone cable or the unit was moved around as sound was being put through it. This seems to be a manufacturing issue on the first batch of units shipped from China. I seemed to get an E10 from the second batch as I haven't noticed the issue yet. If you have run into the issue, I suggest contacting Amazon for a replacement.

The E10 installs automatically upon plugging it into Lion 10.7.2 and Windows 7 64bit. You just go into your sound options in each OS and switch your output to the E10. Nice.

After a week and after doing some back/forth switching between the E10 and headphone out on the laptop there are some subtle, but pleasing differences. The main thing I noticed is the highs (treble) in any vocal music being 'smoothed' out. The overall sound is a bit better but, in my opinion and on my system, the difference is not a night/day change. But then again I didn't expect an $80 DAC to give me that WOW! factor. Its definitely helped the sound quality improve but not to a level of a much more expensive DAC. Everyone will be using a different laptop/PC, speaker, headphone and our ears are all different so remember that I can only give my opinion on what I hear. Others might hear more/less in their particular usage.

But the changes I did hear made me happy enough to give the E10 a 5 star rating and recommend it to others.

product_title: APC Back-UPS XS BX1000G 1000VA Tower UPS (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Not bad for the price, but stepped sine-wave units are becoming a limitation
review_body: For $100, this is a decent 1000VA unit with a few nice bells-and-whistles.  With that said, I'm finding more and more equipment that can't handle a non-true sine wave as this produces.  Some modern PCs won't handle it (and it's not always obvious which ones), and other manufacturers such as CyberPower have created an entire line of \\"PFC-certified\\" units to address that.  Also, plenty of non-PC equipment such as small appliances that I (ignorantly) thought would function fine on nearly any UPS also can't handle any type of simulated sine-wave.  I used to always buy APC-brand UPS units, but the prices of any true-sine wave APC unit (seems the Smart-UPS line are the only option currently) are just too damn high compared to other brands.  Not specificaly in relation to this unit, but it also seems that the quality and reliability of APC products has been going down-hill.  We have many of them at my workplace, and it's become common at all levels for them to fail or at least have the batteries die within a much shorter period of time.  So, if this serves your need, the price is right and the runtime is good.  If it doesn't for any of the reasons listed above, I say check out CyberPower or some other brand instead.

product_title: Ematic EMS004PL eSport Clip MP3 Video Player with Video Recorder
review_headline: esport mp3 player for normal people
review_body:
The easiest mp3 player I have used. It is really nice to be able to drag and drop files from my music folder to my mp3 player folder.

If you are buying a 4gb mp3 player with a camera and tuner for $22, you better bring your sense of humor with you. I bought my eSport for $30. Since I had my sense of humor handy, I decided to get the pink model. I like the color. I think it sets my dark running shorts off nicely.

When I plugged the player into my computer, it worked! It actually started to charge. To make things better, my Linux Mint operating system recognized it. I was so shocked my mouse hand went numb! I opened up a random music folder and dropped the whole thing into the mp3 folder and the player took it. When I looked at the folder, it contained both mp3 and ogg files. Ogg is the open source music format. Since it took the music so easily, I got cocky and drug an avi file over to see what would happen. To my surprise, all of the music played. As an added bonus, the Japanese music showed up on the display in Kanji. The video did not work because I did not resize it.

The music player worked. The buttons are extremely clunky but navigation is possible. The player comes with a cheap little speaker that works. It is kind of neat to clip it onto the back of my bike jersey and listen to poor quality music. When I am going up the side of a mountain, it is nice to have a tempo to help set a pace. I don't really listen to the music but the tempo is there. I listened to the player through some Bose headphones with satisfactory results. It was not like listening to the music from a PC with a $200 sound card but the sound was okay.

The video camera works. With 4gb of available memory, you can record for a while. The camera works. It has a flash but I am not sure it does anything. Half the time when I take a picture, I am not sure if I took the picture or not. ¾ of the time when I take a picture, I am not sure if I am in the camera mode. The pictures and video transfer to my computer by drag and drop.

I am currently using it as my car mp3 player. It has about 6 hours of battery use and still going strong. When I turn it off and back on, it remembers the track it was playing. Every time I throw it back into its hole for the trip, it changes the song from the touchy controls that are only sensitive when you don't want them to do anything.

Pros:

It is cheap
It works!
Very easy file transfer
Plays variable formats, mp3, wav and ogg. I did not feel like looking for Apple files to drag over.
Lots of memory storage
Expandable memory
Nice colors
Comes with a cool video about a rabbit

Cons:

It is cheap
It is slow
Navigation is frustrating
I can't figure out where the buttons are located
It is big

Final grade - Pass

It is a $30 mp3 player. It does what I want and some extra stuff. It is easy enough to figure out. I did not read the instructions and managed just fine. The buttons do not work very well but they get the job done. I will not cry when it breaks. I bought a cheap mp3 player so I could sweat all over it and not cry when I get caught out in the rain. Remember your sense of humor when use something like this.

product_title: JVC Noise Cancelling Headphones - Black
review_headline: I'll never get why people spend so much for Bose.
review_body:
These headphones are great. Ive had them for almost a year now and have used them on airplanes, while mowing the lawn and while vacuuming. Mind you, on the latter 2 activities you can still hear the muffled sounds of those things running. They do a great job of blocking sound when you turn them on. When turned off, they still sound great. The pads a very soft and super comfortable. They fit on my head comfortably and do not start to hurt or get annoying after extended listening.

I'm impressed at how bose has duped people into spending $300 on headphones that are realistically no better than these $100 headphones. I have used both and while the bose may look flashier, they are not worth and additional $200. The JVC headphones are one of the rare purchases Ive made where I'm completely happy and satisfied.

product_title: C Crane Company SoftSpeaker Pillow Speaker
review_body: I purchased the product for my father who has Parkinsons.  He loves to listen to the radio to get to sleep and when he wakes during the night.  When his old pillow speaker bit the dust, I had difficulty finding a replacement in stores so purchased this one from Amazon.  I was afraid that he would have to go for quite sometime without his music but the speaker was delivered within a couple of days.  Dad loves it, especially the cushioned design.  An uncushioned speaker can be uncomfortable and for someone with trouble moving as adjusting the positioning can be difficult.  Even if this speaker ends up right under his head during the night it is still comfortable.  It has a good quality sound, is much more comfortable than his last pillow speaker and was inexpensive.  All in all a great little speaker.

product_title: Polk Atrium 6 Parent (not_buyable_sku)
review_headline: Amazing sound better than my BOSE
review_body: I purchased these for my outdoor cabana pool bar and attached them up under roof just a couple inches away from direct rain and hooked them up to my dual zone Yamaha audio receiver with 18 gauge wire (could have used 16 gauge but wanted to be able to conceal the wire the connection in the back of the speaker is the screw binding posts with the hole that allows for wide variety of gauges). These are bit wider than my Bose 151 and look nice, but not as sleek looking as the Bose, but I prefer amazing sound over looks. (they loo Before I bought these I spent hours researching technical detail on several speakers including the previous Bose 151 that I just bought without research and solely because they were BOSE, never again. I actually first bought the Yamaha AS-390 and I blew one of the speakers with Santana. I returned and decided to use my computer engineering background and actually do research like I do for virtually every thing.   Some Tech Specs:  The reason I chose the Atrium 6 instead of the Atrium 4, or 5 is because the 6-8 are not sealed but ported, Polk cause this there PowerPort Bass Venting. Some how they designed it to be weather proof even with the port.   The mid/woofer: 1 - 5 1/4\\" Diameter (13.34cm)Dynamic Balance Aerated Polypropylene Cone with rubber surround.  Tweeter: 1 - 1\\" Diameter (2.54cm)Anodized Aluminum Dome Tweeter with Neodymium motor structure  The Frequency response: is 50Hz-27kHz, 8 ohms, they recommend 10-100 watts a channel of Amplifier power. They weigh 5.4 pounds and measure 11 11/16\\" H x 7 11/16\\" W x 8 3/4\\" D  (amazon dimensions were wrong.) They swivel 180 degrees and can be mounted at downward angle.   Test:  Technical specs only go so far, you have to hear/see them to really know how a product works. I  tested these bad boys with Lynard Skynard and Santana. 1st zone is my bose(under the deck a good 100 feet)and 2nd zone is my Polk. Don't get me wrong the Bose are great, but they have have a major flaw. NO BASS. Highs and Mids are great. I put up the first song slowly increasing the volume afraid I was going to blow the POLK's like the previous Yamaha speakers to Santana. I reached to Max volume with no distortion and great Bass, I was just in awe that such small spears were producing such amazing bass while still keeping the Mids good. Then I turned the Bose zone on and stand in the middle of both of them and the Polk were so much better I was sold to Polk instantly (Bose could handle max volume too no problem). I don't ever need to go that high as I had my neighbor come outside and ask me why I was blasting speakers at 10:30 pm at night on a Tuesday. (our closest neighbors are close 600-800 feet away)   Real life usage:  Christmas eve party came and these bad boys took some punishment, loud music, Football games (hooked up to TV) and especially  Karaoke. We had a spontaneous Karaoke war with a neighbor 3 houses down on the Christmas eve party. They could hear use perfectly and we could barely hear them. The next day he came over to wish me a Merry Christmas, but his real motive was to ask me about what speakers I was using. I jokingly told him I couldn't tell him because then I would have to hear his karaoke and I barely heard his Boo's yesterday. Then I brought him inside and showed them to him. He said he was going to buy them since he was impressed at the quality of how clear our horrible voices sounded. Anyway for around the same price as the BOSE you get more bang for your buck with these. I'm assuming the whole line of atrium must be amazing. I chose the black ones cause my Bose speakers are white but have turned to an off white over the years.  So far so good, will update the review if any issues issues arise. I highly recommend these speakers.

product_title: Pigpony Brand 4GB MP3 Player MP4 Player 2.4-Inch Screen Built-in 5MP Digital Video Camera Webcam FM Radio Voice Recorder and E Book Reader (Silver)
review_headline: Great little unit for the money
review_body: Having read the other reviews, I thought this would be great for my kids.  I wanted something good, but not too expensive, and this sounded perfect.  So I bought two: one black and one silver.  The units arrived quickly.  They came without printed user manuals, which is a great \\"green\\" move and saves both paper and money.  However, I've never used one of these things before, so it was good my older daughter had one before and knew the basics of how to use it.  The vendor's customer service folks told me that there is an electronic user's manual inside the MP3.  It would be a good thing if they would include a small piece of paper in the box giving start-up instructions and where to find the users' e-manual.  Regarding our experience, we unpacked both units and had problems charging them up.  The problems resolved for the black one and it charges just fine now and plays great.  My daughter has had absolutely no problems with it and LOVES, LOVES, LOVES it.  I think it's an absolutely fantastic purchase for the price.  I can't answer for folks who are audiophiles or techno-experts, but for a tween-ager, this is an amazing device.  The only less than stellar thing I can say is that, when listening to classical music, the earbuds make flutes sound like a harpsichord.  I thought it was a really, really interesting interpretation of the piece until we played it on my car stereo, LOL.  So upgrade to better earphones or speakers if you want a better sound, but the player itself is fantastic.  Our problems charging the silver unit did not resolve, however.  I emailed the vendor's customer service department and they responded quickly with instructions on how to charge it.  Tried that, didn't work.  Exchanged email some more and tried everything they suggested, and finally arranged to ship the unit back for an exchange.  Had to ask for a return shipping label, which they graciously emailed.  But when I took it to the post office, it was for the wrong weight and I had to go home and ask for yet another label for the correct weight and repackage it for shipping with the new label.  Got it mailed (finally!).  They received it 4 days ago and I'm currently waiting for the replacement unit to arrive.  So, bummer that the unit didn't work out of the box.  Even more of a bummer that it has taken about a month to get the unit back to them (part of which is my fault for not getting it to the PO quicker, and part of which is due to the wrong weight on the label).  But it has been very, very easy to correspond with the vendor's customer service rep. and she has been uniformly really pleasant to deal with and very apologetic that I'm having to deal with this.  So 4 stars for customer service.  I'd give them 5 stars if this had been resolved sooner and without all the delays on the return shipping label, but overall, they've been apologetic, cooperative, and helpful, big things in customer service as far as I'm concerned.  I'll update my review after we've received the replacement unit and see how that one works.

product_title: Sony MDR-EX57LP Headphones
review_headline: You get what you pay for...3.5 Stars
review_body: You always get what you pay for and this product is no exception.  It delivers decent performance for the price.  I bought these to use at the Gym.  Here are some details:  As I write this,I am listening to some older Smooth Jazz (high bit rates) on my Lenovo laptop.  The performance with my Iphone wasn't as solid.  BASS:  Both good and bad.  The good is that these phones provide respectable punch on most songs.  On some drum riffs, the bass can be a bit muddy and uninspired. It can't handle synthesized bass well for the most part.  Overall, mediocre...but my Brookstone headphones blow these away...again, those cost quite a bit more.  TREBLE:  The treble is somewhat unremarkable.  Not good, not bad.  It is just okay.  Suitable for casual listening, yet will not wow you with most songs.  Audiophiles steer clear.  MIDRANGE:  I was most pleased with the Midrange reproduction.  On newer Jazz, George Duke(high production value+high bit rate), these headphones sound better than average on the mids.  The sounds are gently punchy, and the effect is enjoyable.  I was especially impressed how the percussion sounded on headphones this inexpensive.  The soundstage presence is about a 6 out of 10.  If you read reviews from professionals or audiophiles, they always say the same thing...put in good stuff to your player and get good results.  Use these only with high-quality audio files.  \\"Normal' files will sound less than stellar.  Summary:  Significantly better than the stock Ipod headphones that come with your product.  Great mids  You get decent performance at this price point.  Overall, 3.5 stars: better than just \\"ok\\", but just shy of 4 Stars value.

product_title: Audio-Technica-USB Direct-Drive Professional Turntable in Silver
review_body:
I've been around quite a few record players at my parent's house and in school and decided to finally make the plunge and buy one. The ATLP120 is fairly easy to set up and right off the bat produces great sound quality. I had the entire system set up and hooked up to some iPod speakers and playing within an hour. My only complaints are that the counter weight takes awhile to find the right calibration for balance, I found either the tonearm was being too heavily weighted or not weighted enough and flying around. after about 20 minutes of fiddling I was able to find the right setting, but I am afraid to touch it and loose the current balance. The stylus needle is also very close to the cartridge head and I had to use a pair of tweezers to slightly bend it closer to the platter.
Overall, for someone who isn't a huge audiophile or looking for an entry level turntable, this is definitely a good model.

product_title: Etymotic Research MC5 Noise Isolating In-Ear Earphones
review_body: I work in noisy office environments where multiple people play their music out loud on bad computer speakers. I happen to be especially sensitive to noise. I have been on a long, expensive journey to find the best headphones for blocking out outside noise and these are them! Without a doubt! I have tried Bose noise cancellation in ear and over ear, Sennheiser, Skull Candy, Beats and many more. These are the only headphones that keep out almost all outside noise. The sound is what you would expect from headphones in this price range. Good, but not excellent (which is why I held back from a 5 star rating). They are still the best headphones I have ever owned. I love them. I ride the subway to work in NYC and I no longer hear people playing video games on their smart phones with the volume up, or crazy people loudly preaching the good word of the lord, or people listening to loud music on really cheap headphones, or people with tourettes (seriously). All the annoying noise of a busy city... gone! I get to work happy now. Seriously, these headphones have changed my life. I am sure that the sound quality goes up with the higher priced Etymotic headphones, but for me, these are perfect. Best to know that I bought mine at J&R in NYC in person. I told them my situation and they handed me these. They said without a doubt that these were the best for what I wanted. I was prepared to spend $250, but the honest professional at J&R sold me these. She was absolutely right.

product_title: Monster MCC AVL300-S Home Theater and Lighting Controller with Omnilink (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: find something else, unless you have loads of patience and lots of time
review_body: This remote is a good value, but the glacial speed of the programming software is unbelievable.  To make a minor adjustment, is an easy 10-20 minute waste of time.  My story:  I bought one of these about a year ago. It took several hours to get setup for a fairly simple system. TV, receiver, DVD, cable box and three zWave lights.  However I was pleased with the performance, if not the dismal display that was harder than expected to read. But it was useable, and filled the need. Then about 3 months ago, the remote started to fall apart. The buttons near the #3 wouldn't work most of the time, and the toggle in the middle fell off, and after numerous attempts to reattach, it finally got lost somewhere in a reclining chair.  The Monster support team was challenging to get through to, but eventually said they would cover it under warranty, though I should expect to get a \\"refurbished\\" one back, since they no longer make these. The quote was \\"send it to us, and we will try to dig something up in the warehouse.\\"  I did this, and after a couple of weeks, a replacement in a zip lock sandwich bag was returned to me.   This has been a royal pain, since it doesn't seem to want to communicate with the RF repeater.  Add to this that the software is unbelievably slow to work with, and you end up with an entirely frustrating experience. Honestly the software had to be designed by someone that never had to use it as a user. It probably works well in their development environment, but try to use it over the internet, like they require, and it is just not worth it.  I say, find something else,  because this is just not fun. And since it is no longer something that Monster seems to be pushing, I don't see anything improving any time soon.

product_title: Peerless – AV SmartMount Projector Mount for Ceiling Applications – for 50lb/23kg Projectors – Universal System
review_headline: Peerless PRG Universal Mount, Buy it...
review_body:
I have owned three different projector mounts and this Peerless is the best by far. I understand Chief mounts are good too but from what I understand they do not have the ease of adjustment. I am using this mount on my JVC RS40. This is a monster home theater projector and weighs 33lbs. Out of the box this mount works fine. What is interesting is that Peerless customer service said this universal mount will not work. I don't know why they would say that. The mount is rated for a 50lbs projector and the specs indicate the arms with reach all four mounting holes on the JVC - and it does. So what is up with Peerless customer service? I found out this mount works by reading reviews on the AVS web site and confirming the specs. I highly recommend this mount. It is expensive, but the quality and ease of adjustment are worth it/critical IMHO. You need to square the projector with the screen and the adjustment design of this mount make it a breeze. The problem I had with other mounts is that once set, they wouldn't hold, the projector wandered, just slightly... but enough to mess with the picture. The other mounts were a pain attach the projector on, not the Peerless - lifting a $3K, 33 lb projector on a ladder is not fun.

Is this the only part you'll need? Probably not... It was for me as I used parts of my prior ceiling mount and drop down. You can use this mount to attach directly to the ceiling, in that case it is all you need. The drop down tube (pipe) is a standard thread 1 1/2 inch. You can use PVC pipe and it attaches fine, I tried it. No, not as strong as steal but I think it would be fine for 35 to 100lbs? So basically there are three parts to buy in a drop down style, the mount, the drop down tube, and the ceiling bracket that attaches to the drop down tube. I hope this review helps, I highly recommend this mount even though the cost seems high it works great!

product_title: GTMax High Resolution DVI-DVI Male to Male Gold Plated 15 feet Cable 4.5m for HDTV, Plasma, LCD
review_headline: Still getting the job done after 7 months.
review_body:
It's unfortunate that someone here has given a careless 1-star review, blaming this cable for causing his graphics card to overheat. That's like blaming your inkjet printer for your divorce. It boggles my mind, really.

What's only slightly less mind-boggling are reviewers who have only good things to say about this cable, yet only give it 4 stars.

I bought 3 of these cables 7 months ago and they are still performing great, every one of them. They were, and still are, very affordable and they're digital, so they either work or they don't. From my experience and every review here, it looks like they work great!

Remember, DVI cables do not carry audio data, like HDMI does. Also, note that there are a few types of DVI cables (you can tell by the \\"teeth\\"). For best results get the right cable for your graphics card and/or monitor (i.e. if your monitor has built in speakers and your graphics card provides the option of HDMI, etc). A lack of research on your part does not justify a bad review for a product that does exactly what it was designed to do.

I will be buying more of this exact cable as my monitoring needs grow.

This means that unless your box is full when you try to move it, it is somewhat unstable with the snaps coming undone.  It also won't stack at a uniform height unless it is nearly full.    If the box is full, it holds the snaps closed better, it will stack at uniform height, and the lid becomes stable.  I bought a bunch of these thinking I would have an adaptable/expandable CD storage situation.  I expected to NOT have full boxes.  But I didn't know how unstable these boxes are for the use intended.  Thus my 3 star rating.

product_title: plug
review_body:
I needed the ability to plug multiple kitchen electrics into an outlet that was hard to reach. This solves that problem and more. I just couldn't be plugging and unplugging each thing as I needed it to an outlet back in a corner and behind things. I'd need longer arms at the very least. Being able to use the food processor, the stick blender, the spice grinder, the blender or the food saver when needed without a major effort to plug the thing in each time matters a lot to me and that deep corner on the counter is where they all live. The one outlet with two plugs just didn't cut it, nor was there room for a standard corded strip to plug things in. This thing is great because I could remove the switch plate and plug it into the outlet and screw it tight. The wall mount keeps things as tidy as possible and allows me to keep 5 things plugged in all the time with an extra slot for the occasionally used item. I'm only using one gadget at a time so I'm not overloading the circuit, just making things easier on myself.

The surge protection is an added benefit because my food processor and blender are not things I'd want to replace if a power surge damaged them. I've used this receptacle for multiple years and have never had any electric sustain damage. In fact I liked it so well, I added two more where I needed to plug in more things that the standard two up outlet would allow.

product_title: Nyrius SW201 HD Component Video YPbPr & Digital Audio Optical Toslink 3 Input Selector Switch with Remote Compatible with HDTV, Blu-ray DVD player, Satellite, Cable, PCM, Dolby Digital, DTS, XBOX360, PS3, Wii, iPod
review_headline: Not great for a Vizio Razer LED-LCD HDTV
review_body: I just bought a Vizio Razer LED LCD-HDTV and needed a component switch to hook up my non-HD devices such as a cable box, Wii and PS2. While the TV can support up to 4 HDMI ports, it only has one component port and I need to hook all three of those devices at once to the component port. I bought this component switch based on a majority of the glowing reviews here and should have done better research.  Now while this component switch does work well for the conversion rates(480, 720, 1080), the contrast and saturation are not converted well. Whites and blues on this TV are extremely bright and washed out with this switch. Some colors become more dull than others such as purples, greens and reds. I had to do a lot of tweaking to my TV settings in order to get the picture to adjust to the original signal quality. Maybe it's the TV type as I do not have access to an older LCD or Plasma to test this out however I should not have to tweak my TV for this switch. Also the remote is really small and you can easily lose it.  So while this component switch does what it is intended to do, if you have the same HDTV that I have, try and find another switch instead.

product_title: FiiO E11 Portable Headphone Amplifier With Micca Accessory Pack (Wall Charger and Extra Battery Pack)
review_body: I thought I would write this in case anyone might be considering using this amp the way I am, without headphones?  I know it is intended as a headphone amp but I have been using it for another purpose; to boost and enhance the sound from my mp3 player(Zune HD and Sansa Fuze+). Whenever I listen to music from one of my players thru my Sony receiver the sound is always a little flat and thin, since I use the headphone jack as a line out into a line in input on my receiver you loose something  in the sound because of the headphone out so I have my FiiO help to boost the sound so when it comes out my receiver it has a fuller more robust sound. For this purpose the amp works pretty good, I'm sure as good as it can for the way I am using it. The point I wanted to make is that a charge does not last that long as I listen to music much of the day. After about 8hrs the amp needs charged again so that is the reason I bought from this particular vendor, I have a spare battery so I always have a fresh one ready to go. As soon as one battery goes dead I out in the fresh one from the charger and charge the one I just took out. It works for me what can I say! The amp does add some needed power to this setup and the music really does sound much better then without any amp at all. The only drawback, if you decide to listen to music thru an mp3 player this way is that the two EQ settings tend to overpower the bass so I keep the EQ set to off on the amp.  I have used the FiiO with various headphones and the sound is clearly much better but I wanted to write this review in case anyone was thinking of using the amp like I am. I had an e5 and e6 but they just didn't sound as good as the E11 does for the way that I use it. My conclusion is that the amp is made very well, definetly worth the money and you get that much appreciated 2nd battery and charger that enables you to keep the music going non stop. Hope this might be of some use to anyone who is thinking of boosting the sound from their mp3 player, it really does make a clear and positive difference.

Original review from 12/2011

These are very comfortable to sleep in

Not overly sensitive volume (other headphones are either too quiet or too loud to sleep with [not just a ipod volume function])

The revised design from V1 has an angled headphone jack and additional felt pad to keep ear pieces in position

Man these things keep breaking! The wire gets pulled away from the end of the jack causing one side to go out and eventually both headphones will quit.

With only a 6 month warranty I am on set #3 and having sleepphones for a year and a half has cost me over $120. My latest set has just broken and i will not be purchasing another set. product_title: Audioengine S8 White 8-inch Powered Subwoofer
review_headline: The sub you won't know is there
review_body:
I use this sub with AudioEngine A5+ in my living room, and can't say enough good things about it. I listen to a lot of jazz and eighties rock. Acoustic bass solos can sound horrible with a subwoofer because they can jump in and out of the subwoofer's frequency range. This results in a noticeable boominess in the music which comes and goes. I can tell you that if you properly setup this sub, you will not experience that. My jazz recordings sound stellar, and the acoustic bass sounds clean and smooth no matter what kind of notes the bassist chooses to play. Secondly, subs tend to smear the sound when listening to eighties rock drummers who use a lot of double bass drum alongside vigorous strokes on the low toms. The S8 subwoofer sounds tight and punchy when playing this kind of material. Just check out any Dave Weckl solo for an example. And lastly, the S8 sub can be used to improve movie soundtracks. I run my television's audio into the sub and it does a good job (but don't expect it to knock you out of your chair).

I would recommend taking experimenting with room positioning options. Put the sub in the spot you'll be listening from, and go to different places where you think you'll place it. Squat down on the floor and listen to see which spot sounds better to you. Also, you'll want to make sure you set the crossover frequency properly (a good starting point is setting the dial at 12 o'clock) as well as the phase (probably ok to leave it at 0 unless you hear a difference). You should play a test song that goes all over the bass so that you can make sure nothing nearby is picking up on certain frequencies, which causes rattling (at worse) or increased bass volume at times when the music did not call for it (at best).

Overall an extremely musical and enjoyable subwoofer.

product_title: Artisan Black Diamond 240 Disc DVD Album with 120 Liner Notes/Title Cover Page Capacity Using Metal Ring Binder
review_body: As others stated, the rings are nice and tight and the quality of construction seems good.  There are four sets of rings with fifteen pages in each (60 pages total, front and back on each for 120 covers, and two disks on each page for 240 disks total).  If you like to alphabetize your collection, then opening the rings to new pages can be a little bit of a pain, depending on how far you are from the middle of a ring.  If you want to insert at the beginning or ending page in a ring, then pushing all the pages to the other side as you open the rings can be difficult as they are slippery, it's harder to push the binding side down on the rings once the pages are filled with disks and covers, and it can be tricky to hold them in place with one hand while adding the page the the other.  Bigger rings might help some with this.  In terms of space savings, a full binder takes up something like fifty to seventy-five percent of the volume of the stack of empty DVD cases that filled it (DVD's - not blu-rays which usually have smaller cases).  For a small collection the space savings will not be great, but the convenience of being able to easily move a whole stack of DVD's, and being able to easily flip through the pages still makes it worthwhile.  For a larger collection, you will start to realize appreciable space savings once you fill a couple of these binders.  Overall I am very pleased with the purchase of these binders, and I plan on ordering a few more, as well as a set of refill pages.  If you are searching for a way to better organize a large DVD collection, you will be happy with this product.

review_body: Avoid this product as it produces a large amount of electrical noise on whatever electrical system it's plugged into. I got this last October as a spare but began using it occasionally at home and found today I could not listen to AM radio at all anywhere in the house on any of 4 radios!  I unplugged electrical things but the noise continued until I unplugged this adapter. When I plugged in the normal Dell adapter the radios were quiet and I could tune in stations. I plugged in the cheap Chinese adapter and the noise returned, a loud buzzing on the radio.  The replacement is/was a spare for traveling but ended up using it full time not thinking there was a difference, boy was I wrong! Now I wonder how much this thing affected everything else plugged into the house wiring such as satellite DVR, stereo system, computers, etc. It's headed for the trash now, I can't take a chance with expensive electronic equipment. I just hope it hasn't messed up my laptop or it's battery. Avoid this junk item.  As an added note a few days later, I went through the rest of my power adapters and found 2 others that generated the same AC noise on my house wiring. These were adapters that have no ferrite chokes on the output line. Thats where the offending signal comes from. I'm investigating some cheap snap on ferrite chokes to help solve the problem with those.

product_title: Nvidia 3D Vision 2 Wireless Glasses Extra Pair
review_body: Compared to 3DVision 1 glasses, these are definitely better.  The larger lenses are better and seem to not be as dark as the old ones, even when its not being used with a specific 3dvision2 monitor.  The nosepieces stay in place better than they did on the first model too (they came off so easily on that one that i ended up removing them altogether even tho it wasnt quite as comfortable).  The \\"arms\\" of the frames are also much nicer.  instead of being made out of thick, stiff hard plastic they are made out of a flat, more bendable material.  If you have supra or circum aural headphones, these glasses will be much more comfortable to wear with them, and the cups will make a better seal around your ears.  There are two main flaws that I've found with the glasses though.  The main on is that, while the majority of the frames are a matte black finish, the areas immediately around the edge of the lenses were (for some reason i can NOT comprehend) given a glossy coat.  The lenses are recessed a few mm into the frames, supposedly to reduce glare from nearby lightsources, but the glossy shine of the frame around the lenses reflects the picture on your display and creates an outline of shiny distracting light around the edges of your vision.  While this would be annoying with any pair of glasses, its seems to be an even bigger nuisance to have on 3D glasses because it can mess with the sense of depth and overall experience.  Very distracting to me, but some others say it doesnt bother them so much.  Some ppl have recommended putting non-glossy tape, like electrical tape, around the edges of the frames around the lenses to get rid of the shine, or to use fine-grit sandpaper to dull the shine, but these are stupid things for someone to have to do to a product to make them acceptable.  The second issue might only apply to me and other ppl with larger-sized melons, but while the arms of the frames ARE a lot more comfortable than the previous gen glasses, they are not quite longenough and the ends kinda rest directly above my ears instead of above and behind like most glasses.  It's not that big of a deal tho i suppose, theyre still pretty comfortable in spite of this, but i really wish nvidia would make glasses that are bigger or adjustable in more ways than just replaceable nosepieces.  But, in the end, its a solid purchase, a good upgrade if you currently have 3dvision glasses.  And yes, they work with older 3d vision emitters just fine.  3DVision itself is awesome and i have a hard time enjoying games without it anymore these days!

product_title: JVC HAFX34B Marshmallow Headphones
review_headline: Better than even more expensive options
review_body: I originally purchased these headphones for a replacement to the cheap factory headphones that came with an MP3 player I purchased sometime ago.  At the time, I didn't think much about them as I just assumed any headphones would be better than the factory provided headphones.  Because I used these quit often and in very hard environments (gym, running, biking), the wire at the base eventually came lose and gave out.  I then purchased a more expensive pair from a different brand.  It was at this point that I realized just how good these JVC headphones really were.  I immediately ordered another pair of these, threw the other ones out, and never looked back.    Here are a few of the highlights of these headphones that really stood out to me as compared to the other ones:    Comfort - These so-called marshmallow headphones are by far the most comfortable in-ear headphones.  You really forget they are in your ear, while other headphones make their presence very obvious. They just fit.  Period.    Functionality - Using the provided larger marshmallow adapters, they do not fall out of my ear, even when running or riding a bike.    Sound - These have really good bass reproduction, but at the slight expense of being a tad more \\"muddier\\" than some other brands.  But since my MP3 has an equalizer, I can adjust it to sound almost perfect.  The other headphones in this price range are severely lacking in the bass department.    A few of the cons are:    Build Quality - Overall pretty good, but because there does not seem to be very much adhesive where the wire goes in at the jack, it is allowed to move freely around and over time, this can cause the wire to pull out, as it did the first time I purchased these.  This time around, I wrapped some electrical tape around it to make a more solid connection between the wire and the jack.  Not a big deal.    Wire Creak - What I mean by this is when jogging or running, you tend to hear the wires in each headphone creak as you move up and down.  They have provided somewhat of a fix for this by providing a little rubber piece that slides up and down the two wires to hold them close to your neck so they don't move around as much.  A minor inconvenience that you quickly get used to.  Other headphones don't even provide this rubber piece.    Overall, I would say probably one of the best in-ear headphones for the money.  You will not regret purchasing these.

However, it IS probably worth the $60 Best Buy charges for it, and it is A STEAL at the $35 Amazon charges for it.  I use it to listen to my iPod classic in my cubicle at work, where I'd like decent sound, but also want it quiet enough that I'm not disturbing my co-workers.  With my prior (much cheaper) player, you either had to turn the volume up way too high to actually hear your music (and then the sound wasn't full at all), or you could only hear parts of the song.  This is much better...even at lower volumes that won't disturb your co-workers, you can pretty much hear the fullness of the song.  The only problem is you'll be tempted to turn it up higher because then you get a rich full sound...and even a little desk rattling bass thanks to the tiny subwoofer.  It will not fill a room, obviously, but if you're looking for something to listen to with quality sound in a small space, this is the product for you.    Other than the sound, it is nice and compact (although a little heavier than you might like), and so easy to take wherever you want to go with it. product_title: Mohu Leaf 30 TV Antenna, Indoor, 30 Mile Range, Original Paper-thin, Reversible, Paintable, 4K-Ready HDTV, 10 Foot Detachable Cable, Premium Materials for Performance, USA Made, MH-110583
review_body:
I bought this indoor MOHU Slim Antenna to replace an old Radio Shack amplified rabbit ears type antenna. The old antenna would pick up all the available stations but required a power wall wart and a lot of constant fiddling to get all the stations. The MOHU Slim Antenna gives the same reception without a power supply and once I had it adjusted, worked as well or better than my old antenna.

Set up: True you can mount it anywhere indoors, but then don't expect 100% reception. Another reviewer suggested to mount it to a larger sheet of cardboard and by trial and error find the best location and angle. Make sure to rescan channels with each new location/angle.

What I did: As a musician I had an old wire type music stand. I taped the antenna to it and placed it near a top floor window of my house. I did a few scans and eventually got the channels I expected. ([...] will tell you what to expect in your location) Some angle adjustment is needed to get the best reception. I kept rotating the antenna and finally found the perfect position and all the expected stations are clear and no further adjustment is necessary. Of course your reception will depend on your location, tv tuner sensitivity, trees etc.
In Northern NJ I receive 40+ channels that are a mix of network, PBS, music only, NOAA, foreign and Spanish.

product_title: Sennheiser On-Ear 926MHz Wireless RF Headphones with Charging Cradle
review_body:
I'm one of the many people who saw the many 5 star reviews and immediately rushed to buy these headphones. I quickly became one of the many people who realized that it's impossible to use this product!

It is absolutely impossible for you to keep these on your head, defeating the purpose of wireless headphones. The problem lies in the design of the ear part of the headphones: they're not indented at all! This means there is no way for them to hug your ear and stay on your head like a normal set of headphones.

The ear area is completely flat and isn't made of a material that would at least attempt to stick to your skin like leather might. As soon as you put them on your head you immediately notice how unlikely they are to stay put. As soon as you nod your head forward (like some people might do when they listen to music!) they'll slide right off. If you want to listen to music from your computer while doing things around the house, forget it!

What's the point of cordless headphones if simply moving your head around causes them to fall off?

I only used them for about 2 minutes before realizing they sucked and I couldn't keep them on my head. I did notice the hissing that people are always talking about, but it goes away when the music comes on. I walked into the next room in my house (about 25-30 ft away) and the quality didn't change at all.

So if you plan on listening to music nonstop, the sound quality isn't bad. But if you're like me and sometimes you want to pause a song so you can read/do something, you have to listen to the annoying hiss.

Cliffs:

product_title: Pangea Audio HD-24PC HDMI Cable 4% Silver Plated (0.6 Meter)
review_headline: Not All HDMIs Are Created Equal.
review_body: Background:    High Definition Multimedia Interface (HDMI) is the best audio / video (a/v) digital interface ever made. It achieves superb a/v performance at a reasonable cost compared with other digital cables such as Toslink (Toshiba Link) & S/PDIF (Sony / Philips Digital InterFace). The HDMI standard / version is also improving with time & this digital interface is here to stay for a very long time to come.    I'm tired of reading about 1's & 0's digital theory that's been beaten to death by consumers & critics alike. There are many things that may be theoretically correct but practically it proves out to be otherwise. In my experience, the quality of materials used / implemented does have an impact on performance with all digital cables & components. It comes down to one's budget, expectations & understanding of electronics.    Over the years, I have tried / used many branded & non-branded HDMI cables. The following are a few branded HDMI cables that I currently use in my a/v system:    1) Monster MC 1000HD, priced @ USD59/2m [[ASIN:B000UF3FT8 Monster MC 1000HD-2M Ultra-High Speed HDTV HDMI Cable (2 meters)]],  2) Pangea Audio HD-24PC, priced @ USD70/2m [[ASIN:B0031Y5I68 Pangea Audio HD-24PC HDMI Cable 4% Silver Plated (2 Meter)]],  3) AudioQuest X Cable, priced @ USD30/6.5ft [[ASIN:B00092HOCQ AudioQuest HDMI X cable - HDMI plugs 2m (6.56') braided cable]] &  4) Mediabridge Ultra Series, priced @ USD10/6ft [[ASIN:B0019EHU8G Mediabridge Ultra Series - High Speed HDMI Cable with Ethernet - Category 2 Certified - Supports 3D & Audio Return Channel [Latest HDMI Version Available] - (6 Feet)]].    I've used the above V1.4 HDMI cables, of different lengths, with LaCie LaCinema Media Player, Pioneer DVD Player, Oppo Bluray Player, HD Cable Box along with a 17in Dell LCD TV, 32in Panasonic LCD TV, 42in Panasonic Plasma & a 50in Panasonic Plasma TV.    Performance & rating:    Here's my take on the HDMI cables listed above:    1) Pangea Audio HD-24PC priced @ USD70/2m:Rating: 5 Stars.    The good: Build quality is second to none. The cable will surely outlive the components it's being used with. Impeccable black level performance & I'm truly floored using this HDMI on a 50in Panasonic Plasma TV. It truly stands out with it's price to performance ratio. It's a real bargain because of the good discount & free shipping in Amazon.    The not so good: Thick & a lil' stiff just like their power cables, so not very ideal for flush wall mounted displays. Needs ample space behind the TV for cable management.    2) AudioQuest X Cable priced @ USD30/6.5ft:    Rating: 5 Stars.    The good: Very good build quality. A lil' thinner & so easier to handle than the Pangea Audio HDMI. Great performance for large screen displays. Just a tad less impressive with black level performance than the Pangea Audio HDMI. It's a very good purchase especially at the heavily discounted price & free shipping in Amazon. It w'd be hard to find a HDMI cable at this price that can beat the X Cable for build quality & performance.    The not so good: Nothing at all. Really, it's that impressive for the current listed price.    3) Mediabridge Ultra Series priced @ USD10/6ft:    Rating: 4 Stars.    The good: For the price, one of the best budget HDMIs out there. Very good for small screen displays & surely an upgrade to really cheap freebies that we get with most Bluray players, DVD players, Cable box etc.    The not so good: Cheap build quality when compared to the other HDMI cables that I have. Not recommended with displays larger than 40in as picture quality is a tad less crisp when compared to the other HDMI cables that I have in my system.    4) Monster MC 1000HD, priced @ USD59/2m:    Rating: 3 Stars.    The good: Good build quality, better than the Mediabridge HDMI but falls short in aesthetics & build quality when compared with Pangea Audio & AudioQuest HDMI. Performance is just as good as the AudioQuest HDMI cable.    The not so good: At half the cost the AudioQuest HDMI, with the heavy discount & better build quality, is a better buy / bargain. It's time for Monster to offer better discount on all their cables.    Conclusion:    For display screen sizes below 40in, sources less than 1080p & cable lengths below 2m, a $10/m HDMI is just as good / effective as a $100/m & above HDMI cable. If U are unhappy with a $10/m HDMI only then sh'd U try something a lil' more expensive than that.    For display screen sizes above 40in, the more robustly made Pangea & AudioQuest HDMI cables did make a difference in my system. The blacks were a lil' more well defined. The overall picture quality was a tad smoother, deeper & clearer.    There are some brands of HDMI that are priced @ $100/m & above. At that level, one gets to buy exotic HDMI jewelry. It surely will have great build, finish, EMI / RFI shielding etc but it does not necessarily improve performance under the above conditions of screen size, source strength & cable length. It's surely not for everyone.    The savings made on a `value for money' HDMI cable can be used to buy something else in the a/v system that can actually make a visible & audible difference, such as power cords, power conditioners, interconnects etc, just to name a few components that truly matter to me.     In my experience, Silver is surely the best conductor for a/v, closely followed by Copper. I also prefer to use solid core cables over stranded cables & Silver plating over Gold plating wherever circumstance & budget permit. Gold & Platinum plating is used only because they are noble metals & do not easily corrode (oxidize) like Copper & Silver. Brass is cheap & is 360 percent less conductive than Copper. I'm surprised to see Gold plated Brass connectors still being used in most pro a/v systems & cables including HDMI. I'm sure the use of Brass is the most effective way to keep cable costs low.    The Pangea Audio HDMI uses the best materials amongst all the HDMIs I've used & listed above. It uses 24AWG (American Wire Gauge) Silver plated solid Copper conductors. Unfortunately, it's terminated with Gold plated Brass connectors. I'm yet to get hold of a HDMI that meets all my expectations & yet be priced sensibly. In a/v U get what U pay for, even then, there is a level after which U reach a point of diminishing returns. That's were good homework / research really helps. Knowing were to draw that line is the key point in this hobby.    If the HDMI requirement is for a screen size above 40in, the source is full HD (1080p) & the cable length requirement is above 2m, then I'd recommend that one tries both - the cheap Mediabridge HDMI & a better grade HDMI from Pangea or Audioquest. Amazon has a very good return policy, so one c'd return the less impressive cable within 30 days of purchase. What more can one ask for?    Just my $0.02.    Brgds.

Feel like an idiot after recommending it to all my friends. Excellent quality sound when it worked, much better than iPhone's originals but unfortunately not that durable.    Doc      Edit: Managed to contact Jlab. After a couple of emails with customer service my replacement J3s are on the way. I was really surprised by how cooperative they were. Thumbs up Jlab!!!

product_title: ONKYO TX-SR606 7.1 Channel Home Theater Receiver
review_body: This receiver has serious problems and Onkyo isn't willing to fix them. After about a year and a half the on screen display failed, followed a few months later with HDMI syncing problems. This is a known issue, just Google TX SR606 and HDMI. The  HDMI daughter card fails and needs to be repaired or replaced. I blamed my other components (PS3, Bluray player) not thinking a less than 2 year old receiver would fail so quickly. Finally I could not get either to sync and show any picture on my HDTV. Bypassing the receiver and connecting either component to the HDTV and problems disappear except now that means no Dolby TrueHD and DTS-HD Master Audio. Will never buy another Onkyo product.

product_title: Rocketfish Bluetooth High-Definition Stereo Headphones for Most Bluetooth-Enabled Devices Black RF-MAB2
review_body:
Honestly if I could give these headphones a zero for durabolity I would. I bought my first set from best buy and the button jammed after two weeks of use, the second pair I had for two days and the side part with the buttons fell off, luckily I had purchased the best buy service plan for the second pair. I then had a third set in which the same button jammed, I took that one back and for a fourth and final pair and once again the panel fell off after one days usage. I would use them in the gym while I was lifting weights but not for cardio due to me fearing that they would fall apart, but they fell apart with just everyday usage.
The sound quality on these are outstanding, and I had liked the fact that i could walk around my house and stay in range with my phone. They where also comfortable, and affordable but they will fall apart. review_body: These are one of the worst headphones I've ever purchased in my life.  Don't even waste your time with them; they are of such low quality that you might as well invest the $20 in the lottery, as you'd have more satisfaction with knowing you might acquire something more worthwhile.    With that being said, the headphones look cool, if you are seeking extra pizzazz to compliment your [unique] outfit.  However, the sound quality is absolutely horrible.  I don't agree with some other reviews that stated that the headphones sounded \\"great\\".   Go walk into a dollar store and purchase a set of headphones--That's what you're getting.  The plastic is very cheap as well and I don't see it lasting very long at all.      I returned this product though because it was somewhat defective.  The wires are also very low quality, and right out of the box, it required me to fumble around with it to hear anything.  The sound crackled, wherever I plugged the headphones in (to ensure it wasn't my device that wasn't working).      In conclusion, don't buy this. I don't normally give products 1 star, but this was the golden [or not] exception. Usually you pay for what you get, but in this case, I felt cheated.

review_body: You don't want this charger, you want a \\"smart\\" charger.  This is based on a steady charge rate and a timer.  Maybe it's OK for AAs and AAAs (but even those take eight hours), but if you want to charge 10,000mAh D-cells, you get to unplug and restart this charger FOUR times over the course of THIRTY-TWO HOURS!  100% my fault for not paying more attention to the product I was buying, don't make my mistake though.

product_title: Polk Audio RC80i 2-Way In-Ceiling Speakers (Pair, White)
review_headline: Good for the price for home theatre, but don't expect great music
review_body: I ordered these speakers based on the low price (120/pair) and polk's name for a new home theatre system.  After different testing I find that while they do work well for the price and sound good, they do not have a good frequency response for regular music. They sound muddy at higher volumes and have a definite accentuation of the vocal ranges while neglecting the low, low-mid and high ranges. With a good eq this might be addressed but id rather opt for a better quality speaker and try the Boston Acoustics hsi 470s instead.  I'd recommend this only to someone who does not plan on playing alot of music, just movies, or who wants them as a small room background music speaker.

product_title: Sennheiser Light Weight Supra-Aural Headset with 3 Button Control for i-Pod
review_body: I use these for work. They are comfortable, portable, and sound great! Buy these! The bass response is clean and pronounced, with excellent clarity in the mid range and high frequency.

product_title: iHOME iPod/iPhone Portable Speaker Case
review_body: I have an iPhone 4 and this iHome works perfect.  I wanted a small, portable, convenient device that I could take with me to the beach, a picnic, work, etc.  I was given a cheap little speaker from a company give-away and thought it was great, until the sound gave out after about an hour of use. product_title: Sennheiser Bluetooth Headset with Noiseguaurd 2.0 SRS WOW HD
review_body:
[Original Review - June 4th, 2011]
Design:
The 360 comes with a metal reinforced extendible headband and looks quite sturdy. The soft, leather padded ear cups are foldable to a full 90 degrees and fit snugly inside the carrying case. The PXC 360 BT weighs about 180 grams and is a little heavier than it looks. However, they are comfortable to wear, even for long durations. The battery is located on the left ear cup and is removable/replaceable. The right ear cup holds all the controls as well as the the audio jack. The buttons for toggling Active Noise Cancelling (ANC) and Bluetooth are located at the bottom of the right ear cup while that for SRS-WOW HD is located under the \\"reduce volume\\" button. The controls are intuitive but take a while to get used to. The button at the center controls Play/Pause as well as the master control to turn the headphones on and off. The ANC button controls TalkThrough and ANC. There's also a Braille symbol for `L' embossed on top of the left ear cup.

Sound:
Quite frankly, to fully appreciate the sound quality of the PXC 360 BT, you'll need an external sound card or a headphone amplifier as the integrated sound card on your PC or notebook is probably not good enough to exploit the 360. The 360 reproduces music really well. All my previous headphones used to sound like they passed all the audio through a static equalizer before passing it to the ear cups, so I'm glad I can finally hear music the way it is. Although it does a really good job at reproducing the mids and highs, what really caught my attention was the quality of bass. It'll knock your socks off. I mostly listen to hard rock and heavy metal where good bass is a necessity and the 360 doesn't fail to deliver. For a regular user, I would say that the maximum volume is adequate. I wish I could turn it up a little higher but to be fair, being a \\"metalhead\\" I'm not satisfied unless there are two amplifiers blowing music into my ear. As the ear cups coverthe ears, it reduces a significant amount of background noise (passive noise cancelling) so everything is audible even on low volume.

I couldn't make out any difference in audio quality when played via Bluetooth or the wired cable. I even tried comparing FLAC files (bit rates ranging from approx. 760 Kbps to 1100 Kbps) but I couldn't notice any difference. The 360 even supports apt-X, but I don't have any apt-X enabled device so I couldn't test it. I've heard it sounds much better over apt-X.

Bluetooth:
I own two phones (Samsung Captivate and Nokia N82) and the 360 paired with both of them in the first attempt. Unlike my previous headphones which would occasionally lose the audio signal in short bursts, in the two weeks that I've used the 360, it hasn't lost the signal even once. The PXC 360 BT supports Bluetooth 2.1 + EDR along with A2DP and AVRCP profiles which permit fast-forward and rewind playback options as well. Bluetooth range isn't an issue as I was able to receive an uninterrupted feed even when my phone was approx. 30 feet (with no obstructions) and 20 feet (with a wall in between) away. I didn't face any interference issues from Wi-Fi signals nearby.

Active-Noise Cancellation:
The manual claims that the 360 can reduce background sound by up to 90%. Although I couldn't \\"feel\\" the 90% decrease, it does a remarkable job at reducing low-frequency sounds. I use these headphones while biking and it manages to completely cancel out the sound of wind as it gushes past me as well as partially cancel out the sound of cars as they pass by. I haven't had the opportunity to test it in-flight but since it cancels out all the engine sounds and humming noise from traffic and the exhaust fan at home, it should work in-flight as well. Unfortunately, using ANC comes at the cost of a lower bass output so use it wisely.

SRS-WOW HD:
SRS-WOW HD is the most useless feature ever as it makes music sound hollow. Only a few songs sound decent with SRS-WOW enabled but you're probably better off without it. I don't use this feature at all.

Talk-Through:
I like this feature a lot. It basically lets you hear what's going on outside without having to take off your headphones. There are microphones at the rear end of each ear cup that capture the sound from outside and feed it to the ear cups when Talk-Through is enabled. There is a slight delay but it's barely noticeable so it's not an issue.

Operating Time:
I was able to achieve operating times close to what's mentioned in the manual, which are listed as follows:
Wired + ANC Enabled : 20 hours
Bluetooth Enabled : 10 hours
Bluetooth + ANC Enabled : 8 hours

Pros:
Sturdy Design, Comfortable to wear
Wired + Bluetooth option
Great Sound Reproduction (esp. Bass)
Active Noise Cancellation works great
Talk-Through
Replaceable Battery
2 years warranty

Cons:
Outrageously Expensive
Max. Volume could have been louder

Conclusion:
Overall, I'm very happy with these headphones. I like having the option to choose between wired and Bluetooth and active noise cancellation only makes it better. I'm also glad that I can use the PXC 360 BT as wired headphones even without the battery. I'd recommend it to anyone who's always on the move. Even at $329.99, it's still ridiculously over-priced in my opinion.

I would give it 3.5 stars out of 5. ( 5 for excellent features - 1.5 for price )

[Update- July 14th, 2012]
Nothing has broken in spite of me dropping the headphones a couple hundred times. The sound quality is still excellent and the battery has yet to show signs of wear. Pairs perfectly well with my Galaxy S3 and still performs like it did a year ago. Considering how often I use it (every day), how long I've used it (over a year) and what I've put it through (used it in Oregonian rains + previously mentioned drops), the cost is justifiable and I've changed my rating to 5 stars.

product_title: Belkin Speaker and Headphone Splitter
review_headline: Head phones work fine but microphone doesn't work
review_body: The splitter works fine for the head-phones but couldn't get the microphone to work. It seems to be some contact issue with the splitter and the socket on my laptop. If I pull it out a tiny bit and hold it, I can get it to work faintly. Otherwise, there's no microphone function. I wish I had a solution for this. This one turned out to be useless.

product_title: Sony ICFCS10iP Speaker Dock with Alarm Clock and Radio for iPod/iPhone
review_body: I've been waiting a long time to get a speaker dock/clock radio am am very satisfied with my purchase.    Pros: Great style, grip handle on back of speakers for ease of moving/carrying was a nice touch.  Very good sound quality with a noticeable difference when the extra base settings are used. Volume can go very loud without distortion.  AM/FM presets are easy to use.  Having FM was really important to me).  Would be great to take with you on a weekend away by car (to use in a hotel room), but would be too bulky to try to pack in a suitcase for a flight. I have and Itouch and my husband has an Andriod phone... I can dock my Itouch easily and he can plug in his android so we can listen our own music. LOVE that this doesn't require batteries to run.  Like the remote control too. Dimmer options for the clock are a nice addition too.  Cons: Even though the sound is really good, it would be great to have detachable speakers to allow for more of a stereo experience.  Also, we used to have our old radio on top of the fridge in the kitchen and I was hoping to put this one up there to replace it.  Unfortunately, all of the preset dials are on top, so I can't see them when its on top of the fridge, so we moved it to the counter.  I'm sure I could use the remote, but I prefer using the actual buttons.   In the end, I'm VERY happy with this speaker dock...might even get one for the office too.

product_title: SanDisk Sansa Clip+ 2 GB MP3 Player - Black
review_headline: Does Exactly What It Needs To
review_body: After owning an iPod video for a couple of years, I realized that I didn't want games, videos, 16 GB of space or anything else like that on my music player. I got the 2 GB version, which cost $250 less than what I paid for on my iPod. After I filled up all the storage space on it, I bought a microsd card, and tripled the storage space. The size is perfect for running with. The screen is also easy to read in bright sunlight.    So if you want a music player that doesn't require bloated, proprietary software to use and just plays your music, this is the thing to get.

product_title: Creative D80 Wireless Bluetooth Speaker (Black)
review_body: This is one of those awesome products that applies existing technology to real life. Easy to set up, and easy to connect to from multiple devices (only one at a time), it makes an ipod a stereo.      We had no problem connecting Ipods, Ipads & Macs, though the newer products had the best range (no problem from the next room).     The only shortcoming was the sound quality, but I've been spoiled by Bose speakers elsewhere; it's definitely not Bose level, but it's plenty adequate.     Keep in mind that although it's wireless, it still requires plugging in. This should be obvious, but for some reason I was surprised (thought we could use it in the car).

review_body: I have tried many types of ear buds and these are the best. Very comfortable, great sound and excellent noise reduction considering they do not cover the ears like expensive headphones.

review_body: I use this to connect my 2010 macbook pro to my tv. It's better than other methods because you only need one piece (not the cord and adapter) and it transmits the audio as well. I definitely recommend this.

product_title: Onkyo UP-A1 Dock for the iPod (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: I bought this Ipod Dock for use with the two Iphones (4) in my home. I must say I was a little worried particularly about video playback and was amazed at the Video Quality output and the sound output using this dock.    Connecting the dock to my Onkyo TX-NR 709 and connectiong Iphones to the dock was no issue at all.     Simple plug and play. Iphones immediately recognized the dock and started charging on connection.    The tricky part was operating the iphone using the remote.    Step 1: Make sure that you have the IPOD app open on the iphone - otherwise Onkyo will not be able to pull up the playlists or videos    Step 2: Getting the Onkyo into the right mode. The Onkyo manual or the Dock manual was not very clear on this issue. My topmost priority was to get the videos and podcats off my iphone to play on my HT and TV. So after some searching this is what i found out.    By default, the Onkyo is in standard audio mode when you connect the iphone via the dock. In this mode you have to select the playlists via the iphone (i.e. through the IPOD app) and then once you click play the Onkyo HT will continue to play your selected playlist in the order that you have selected.   Note: In this mode there is NO on screen display and effectively Onkyo remote is useless - apart from using to switch to the Port Mode.    Surprisingly, the MODE - THX button is used to switch the Onkyo HT to Extended Audio or Video Modes.   But before you click on it make sure you have pressed the PORT button on the Onkyo remote, as otherwise it will change the audio mode to THX without switching the Iphone to Extended Mode.    The Order of switching loops around like this once you press the THX button on the onkyo remote repeatedly  - Iphone Standard Mode (No On Screen Display)  - Iphone Extended Mode - Audio; All playlists and music files are displayed on the TV screen and you can use the remote to play any audio file / playlist that you select. Beware there is a slight delay in the response ofthe Iphone - i guess because the instructions are being relayed back and forth between iphone and the Onkyo HT.  - Iphone Extended Mode - Video; For me this was just what I wanted. As I was able to browse my podcasts, select individual videos and so on. Very simple to use, exactly same interface as Audio Extended mode so you have to look at the TV screen to know which mode you are in.    Lastly, the good part is that once you are done playing and have removed the iphone, Onkyo remembers its last setting and in future whenever you connect the iphone, Onkyo will automatically go its last mode. Since i figured out this minor thingy, i've now never had to switch the Onkyo mode since its been done.    Another good surprise was that the iphones fit into the dock while they are in the protective casing. After having borken the screen of my old Iphone 3, I always have my iphone in an extra protective casing. So the dock is wide enough and deep enough to support the iphone even if it has an extra casing on it.    One additional piece of information, I have a Logitech Harmony One Remote, and apparently it fails to operate the Iphone. Apart from the play button, no matter what manual programming or other instructions I try to pass on to the Onkyo I have never been able to make it work to control the iphone once it's connected. Hopefully someone will be able to shed some light on this.    In summary Great add-on and definitely worth every penny.

product_title: BIC America F12 12-Inch 475-Watt Front Firing Powered Subwoofer
review_body: It's a decent sub for the price but has its limitations. It could be heavier (enclosure walls could be thicker). Finish quality is not perfect (traces of veneer delaminating at edges). Power rating - not sure how they came up withe the numbers but trust me, the whole PCB (with heatsink being the flat back plate only) weighs no more than pound (seems almost tiny/flimsy) - laws of physics defy this thing from reaching 100W. Also - and this is the biggest fault I found at the price level - the amplifier never truly shuts off (not even with the switch in off position). The device would consume 7W no matter if it's in off, standby or on (obviously power usage would go higher once the sound volume rises, never seen it over 20W in limited tests conducted, did not want to aggravate neighbors too much). Going to positives - the price was right, the sound/bass is definitely an improvement over my old smaller sub, it looks good with front grill off and the long power cord lets you place it where desirable.  It does what it supposed to do but because of the standby power issue it sort off limits your choice of receiver (you may want to get one with switched power outlet to compensate for deficiency of this sub - unless you don't mind extra few $ on your utility bill (month after month)).

product_title: 10 Small Sharp Phillips Panasonic Griffin EarJams TuneBuds Replacement Silicone Ear Buds Tips Sleeves

product_title: Logitech Harmony 300 Remote Control 915-000143 (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: I have never been a fan of Harmony remotes but gave this one a chance because of the cheap price, compared to other Harmony remote. product_title: D-2 Rubber Duct Cord Cover
