product_title: VideoSecu Tilt TV Wall Mount Bracket for most 37 to 70-Inch LCD LED Plasma Screen Display up to VESA 400X400 684X300 700X400mm with HDMI cable, Bubble Level MP502B 3KR
review_body: With so many mounts to choose from, it was not easy picking one. I picked this mount based on the reviews that it had received, and I'm glad I did. The quality is superb, the installation and instructions were clear, and the mount came with various different types of fasteners depending on what type of wall you were installing it on. I would highly recommend this mount to anyone looking for a good quality mount that won't break the bank. I used it for a 42\\" LG LCD.

product_title: Apple iPod shuffle 2 GB 4th Generation
review_headline: WARNING: iPod Shuffle 4th gen + sweat = dead unit
review_body: Tonight while at the gym doing cardio, my 2nd iPod Shuffle 4th gen died on me. I got the first one in December and it was dead by March. The second one lasted about as long. Unless you do not perspire at all when you exercise, or can find a way to completely shield the device, DO NOT BUY the Shuffle to use while doing any exercises that cause you to sweat heavily. I had the unit clipped to the collar of my shirt with the earphone jack parallel to my shoulders - not even in a position where sweat would drip directly onto the unit - and it just suddenly went dead after about an hour. It seems that the unit is very sensitive to / not shielded well from moisture. Maybe sweat traveled down the earphone cables and got into the jack, causing the unit to short out. Regardless of the reason, this a huge design flaw (I never had this problem with the 1st or 2nd gen Shufle or 2nd gen Nano). Even though the 4th gen's redesign was a big improvement from the 3rd gen Shuffle (minus the voice over feature / button which I think is a waste of real estate), I have to give this product only one star for it's lack of protection against moisture. The product designers at Apple should know that many consumers choose this device to use while exercising b/c of its convenient size and clip-on design. People sweat when they do strenuous exercise. Apple should have included a warning or disclaimer that these units were very susceptible to mositure. I find it irresponsible of them to not have addressed this in their marketing or in the owner's manual. They should continue to replace any and all units that fail in this manner. I know I will be taking mine back to the local Apple store for a replacement. This product should be marketed: For couch potatoes only.  Update 1/12/12: Since writing this review I've returned 2 other units, the last one today. They told me I could get a replacement or buy a new one, both at the same retail cost of $50. I politely gave the unit, box, and headphones back to the rep stating that it was time for me to find something a little more moisture-resistant. And no, thanks, I didn't want to keep their (crappy) headphones. My review and rating still stand: 1 star. Perhaps for those who would use it differently, it'd be a great product, but not for me. Hopefully they'll make the 5th gen shuffles a little more water-tight.

product_title: Powermonkey PowerTraveller Portable Charger (Grey) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: If it hold 2200 mAh and my battery is 2140 or 2170, how does it only charge the battery about 40%? Just looking at the numbers it should be able to FULLY charge it from empty! I plugged it in at 45% and it only took it just above 80% before it ran out!

product_title: Klipsch IMAGE S4 -Ear Enhanced Bass Noise-Isolating Headphones
review_headline: Very good sound quality and ear-fit
review_body: The best attribute of the Klipsch IMAGE S4 Headphones is the very good sound quality they reproduce. The earpiece tips allow for much noise reduction, but don't expect them to approach the noise-cancelling qualities of that kind of over-the-ear headphone. I have only two minor complaints about these headphones. Firstly, the spring in the clothes clip is not anchored very well--held in place only by a millimeter-sized ridge on one part of the clip. product_title: AThumb Blue and Red 3D Eyeglasses Cyan Anaglyph Simple style 3D Glasses Extra Upgrade Style To Fit Over Prescription Glasses for Movies Games
review_body:
For anyone with glasses who has tried to use those 3D glasses packed in with movies, you know they're a total pain to wear. You usually end up trying to stick it over your glasses and stretch it around, and it never fits right, never stays in place and just feels horrible.

These glasses fix that problem.

These are more like traditional sunglasses (and anaglyph 3D sunglasses-style glasses are nothing new.. but these actually stick out a bit further, so your regular glasses fit inside them. The lenses are also very large, so you don't get the \\"light leaking\\" from the lenses themselves.

The quality itself isn't the greatest. I feel as if I try to open it too wide, or drop it, the pair is done with. The positive of this is that it's pretty lightweight, so you don't get that \\"poking\\" feeling.

What I considered a downside are the 2 clear plastic holes (one on each side) - I'm guessing these are to make it easier to see if someone is coming up on you, but I found it to just allow light in and cause distractions (everything you see if red/blue, except for on the very sides of your head). This can be \\"fixed\\" with duct/gaffers/electric tape if you need to.

A lot of people are commenting about the actual shades of red/blue (cyan). Mine were very accurate and nearly identical to my \\"paper\\" glasses.

Mine also had a NVIDIA 3D VISION logo on the side, but I highly doubt these are nvidia -- the logo appears to have been put on very poorly with paint (a stamp?) as it's smearing as if they were stamping these quickly and moving them before they had time to dry.

Overall, works great.. quality could definitely be better though.

One other thing to note - if you're using this for movies, check which type of 3D glasses yours needs. A lot of newer movies are using the green/magenta colored glasses, and these won't work.

product_title: Coby High-Performance Isolation Stereo Earphones
review_headline: Best comfort I have found! Not actually asymmetric.
review_body:
I bought these and the [[ASIN:B001GS8FZM JBuds J2 Premium Hi-Fi Noise-Isolating Earbuds (Black/Electric Blue)]] at the same time. The only reason I bought two at a time was I needed a long, regular y cord for mt biking and walking the dogs, while having an asymmetric for working out. THESE ARE NOT ASYMMETRIC!! Yes, you can adjust the cord to fake asymmetric but it looks stupid and is a hassle. I wanted an asymmetric pair, nearly returned these and could not be happier I kept them.

After several variations of Philips earbuds, Sony MDR-AS40EX Active Style Headphones, multiple pairs of V-MODA Bass Freqs (above average sound and comfort, poor quality), and a month with the JBuds, I have concluded these are well above average for the price. The noise cancellation and sound are excellent for $15. The comfort is the best I have ever experienced even though my initial glance made me think they would be uncomfortable. They look a little goofy. The cord construction and overall quality seem average. Hopefully they last a long time.

They are the first headphones I have comfortably worn for 2+ hours and they stay in quite well. The picture doesn't show it, but the driver are angled towards your ear canal. This makes them fit and sound better while using a lower volume. Most headphones rely on the volume of the silicon tip for comfort. These are a little different.

3 stars for working well and not looking terribly stupid. +1 for great sound for the money. +1 for being the most comfortable in-ear headphones I have ever used. These are the first I have ever comfortably worn for 2+ hours and they don't fall out easily. They will remain a 5 star headphone as long as they prove durable.

How are these not shooting to the top of the bestselling list?

**EDIT** Why are they not at the top of the best selling list? The Y split is poorly built. -1 star.

product_title: Grado Prestige Series SR225i Headphones (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: I wanted to simplify my review and get right down to sound quality.  These headphones sound like no other. The drivers are super fast; they keep up with sharp tones and rapid changes in dub step and trance better than any other set of drivers I've heard. They also sound absolutely natural and evil when you drive an electric guitar through them. Dude, they'll blow your mind. They're exceptional for every musical genre.   Vocals? You'll die and go to heaven. Incredibly well-rounded mid range, good extended low end and the best vocals I've ever heard come out of a set of headphones in my life. My favorite set of cans used to be a pair of Sennheiser HD590, which many people will agree were great for vocals. Sorry -- the SR225i is my new favorite by a thousand miles.   Build quality? Light weight, comfortable for most (if your head is big, bend the headband outwards a little so the cups don't murder your ears). I wear them for many hours at a time. The cable is very thick and high quality. These headphones use separated ground channels all the way to the jack which probably explains some of the thickness. After a few months of owning them I had accidentally ran part of the cable over with a Dyson AirMuscle vacuum. There wasn't even a scuff.. the cable is quite simply a tank.  These headphones sound like seeing through a camera lens that has been perfectly cleaned. Best headphones for the money, end of story people.. if you enjoy music, you'll enjoy these headphones

It has a repeat option, and even a repeat folder option.
And equalizer so you can change the sound quality to best match the style of music you're listening to.
It organizes the music by folders; and if you have multiple things from the same artist it puts it all in one main folder with sub-folders.
I can add music using the Windows Media Player.

My only things I've found wrong with it, are minor, and some even fixable with a little hunting.
Here lately I've noticed that I had problems turning it off. It would just play, pause, play, pause, repeat, repeat, and repeat. And after doing this for about a minute or so I felt like throwing it against the wall.
But I just went in and manually changed it to turn off after a period of inactivity. So now I just pause it and set it down, I never have to actually hold the button to turn it off anymore. Easy Fix.
Also, I noticed that it sorts my music by latest added, and I can't get it sort files alphabetically. I've tried everything, but I think it's something you do as you add the music, not after the fact.
The scroll is a bit slow, so trying to figure out what song you're listening to is requires you to stare at the screen for a while.
Song change is bit slow as well, but I've found that if you pause it first it goes a little faster.

product_title: Skullcandy Titan In Ear Bud
review_headline: Great for the price, but make sure to burn them in.
review_body: Here it is short and sweet: These are durable (I have them self-coiled in my back pocket all the time and a few months later they're still no problems), they have punchy and just slightly loud bass without EQ once you burn them in (meaning give them time to even themselves out, maybe 100-150 hours of play at slightly higher than listening volume), the treble is a little less defined but isn't too bad (again, get's better with burn in), and again, they are very durable. You can EQ these things into bass oblivion or crisp vocal heaven without a problem. Very versatile for the price as long as you have some rudimentary EQ control.    The bass is overpowering and muddy at first but will get much better. These things can get super loud if you want them too, but you might overdrive the speaker with too much bass if you're being stupid. If you're an audiophile you're going to want to do a little EQing like adding some crisper highs or subtracting a little of the mids, but not too much AFTER BURN IN.    For the price these are great. They're almost good enough to be entry level in-ear monitors, but not quite.    I can't shove the whole burn in thing down your throat enough. Let these babies grow up and you'll have a great set of elementary headphones.

product_title: TAPE2USB Cassette To PC Recorder (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: I've been using this Tape2USB for about one dozen tapes so far and thought I'd post a review while I'm busy converting an old Screaming Trees tape.  It seems to do the job, but has several issues. First is that I don't like the hassle of the Audacity software, so I am using the EZ Vinyl Tape Converter software I got from a record player purchase. It's more user friendly and lets me just type in the album and track info. I still need to edit out the one track where I was flipping over the tape and finding the beginning of the next track. But I find that's easier than having to edit and than rename each track one at a time. It puts everything in iTunes.    I use Wikipedia to see the duration for each track and it helps remind me of how long each song is. I haven't heard a lot of these songs in over 20 years and those silent parts within the songs might make me start a new track accidentally!  From those times I can see that the player runs a little fast. Most songs are not nearly as long as the times on Wiki (or on the actual liner notes of the few tapes that include that info)and are usually about 8-10 seconds shorter. If a song is listed as being 4:20 long I will have to click on New Track at about 4:10 or 4:12.  I find it best to start a new song as soon as the current one has ended and not wait to see how long the silence between the songs will be.  Some albums have a shorter time between songs, which is when the Audacity software probably becomes more valuable.    I am recording with the \\"Play Cro2\\" button in the ON position, as without it on the tape seems too muddled.    This has been a much cheaper and easier way to convert all my tapes. My home rack-mount Sony tape unit had frozen up and a replacement would be difficult (few places sell tape players of good quality anymore). So I seem to be getting my money's worth out of this unit.  FWIW, I've seen tapes for sale at the big record stores for just $1 while used CDs are at least $7-9. I will try recording a tape version of a CD that I also own and see if I can tell the difference!

All in all, a noticeable improvement, but I was a little disappointed.  Then I tried the ipod headphone output into the preamp's mp3 input and the improvement is great.  The receiver volume is at a normal level for the amount of sound being produced.  I know I'm running through both the ipod's amp and the preamp before the stereo's amp, but none of the 3 are maxed out anymore.  Basically, the line out levels from the ipod are too low for this preamp to bring them up to the level I wanted, but it works great with the headphone outputs.  The anemic ipod bass is gone too. product_title: Philips ActionFit Sports Neckband Headset
review_headline: Great headphones for running with the iShuffle 3rd Gen
review_body: Just picked up these bad boys here to replace my stock ear buds from Apple.  I wanted something with a short cord that held firmly in place when in my ears.  The fact that these are antimicrobial and washable is just a huge bonus.  Your headphones never get that sticky dirty feeling after a couple times out.  Just run them under some water and they clean right up.  Bass is really good, fairly good highs and mids.  The control works well with both my iPhone and the 3rd generation iShuffle when running.  Easily allows you to clip your iShuffle on the back collar of your shirt and controls work better than the stock headphones.  Playlist function, volume, track advance, track back, fast forward and reverse all work well.  Hence, the 3rd gen iShuffle and these headphones make for the best combo for the long distance runner.  Extremely lightweight and it comes with a nice little bag for storage along with your mp3 player.  For under $40 how can you go wrong.  Con- After washing I have noticed that if you don't leave them out to dry with the earphone side down it won't drain properly. If water gets in the speaker it can cause the volume and clarity to reduce significantly.  It does come back, but not until it dries out completely.  So wash them at the end of the day and let them dry out overnight and they should be fine 24 hours later.  You may want to try and only allow the running water to hit the section that comes in contact with your ear canal.    Other than that, great product.  Highly recommended.

product_title: Da-Lite Mounting Brackets Model No.23 - wall mount bracket - 2 PACK ( 40933 )
review_body:
The image for these Da-Lite mounting brackets actually shows three different models (small, medium, and the largest, #23). This photo matches the image from the instructions, so I can see the source of confusion: the manufacturer includes all 3 images on their promotional material for each individual size, which can be confusing.

At least with respect to the largest such mount, the brackets are quite sturdy and well-constructed. Yes, they're simply plastic, but they're HUGE in cross-section, and clearly able to sustain heavy load. From the markings, EACH bracket is rated for 75 pounds, so together they can easily withstand a combined 150lbs of force.

I mounted mine to a cinder-block classroom wall using a few cheap Tapcon cement screws, and it locked solidly into place. Note that with the larger unit, the screen will hang a minimum 8\\" or so away from the wall (maximum perhaps 18\\" using the included steel extension rod), which will reduce your picture size somewhat if you can't move the projector back.

product_title: Bose SoundDock 10 30-Pin iPod/iPhone Speaker Dock
review_body: Bose products appear overpriced for what you get--this is almost always the argument against shelling out the $$ to get a Bose system. And therein lies the issue--when you get a Bose, you are buying it for the sound. When you get the SoundDock 10, you are getting it for the sound + the relatively small, stylish package.    Sound and listening to music is a very subjective experience. People often describe the sound they hear usually in terms of power, or bass, or clarity, etc., and while there may be objective means of measuring these values, the conclusions we get to is simply based on our subjective experience; \\"Does it sound good to me?\\"    In that vein, I offer my review. To me, these SoundDocks offer amazing, AMAZING sound. I own two SoundDocks -- the Series II and now, the SoundDock 10) and in its class, each offers the best overall all-around sound. The SoundDock 10 will blow you away--you will find it hard to believe that that much power and audio quality comes out of what could merely be just a large boombox. I played back the Transformers movie score as my first sound test, and I could hear clearly the full range of the music--from the deep thump-thump-thump of the drums to the highs of the wind instruments--clearly. No distortion, no compromise. I turned up the volume and I am not sure what mark I hit, but it wasn't full volume--and the sound was deafening, and yet, clear, clean, distortion-free.    So, it's clear--I like it. A LOT. The price tag is hefty, 'tis true, but the return on your investment comes back to you sonically and in the SoundDock 10's simplicity. If you want to get fairly close to a home theater implementation coupled with a way for you to listen to your iPod or iPhone--all in one singular piece of audio equipment that can fit on an end-table in your living room, this is it.    Oh, and another thing. Many have compared the SoundDock 10 to the B&W Zeppelin--I cannot compare the two in terms of sound, but aesthetically, the SoundDock 10 just looks more \\"grown-up\\" and discreet; the Zeppelin is like the hip yuppie on his way to adulthood. I'm for the former. But that's just me.

product_title: Acoustic Research Xsight Universal Remote Control
review_headline: Confusing out of the box features, need to setup online account!
review_body:
Set up was a bit painful, but was ok. Please be aware that the owner has to first setup an online account and only then will be able to set this up through computer. If you are comfortable setting the devices without computers, I guess there wont be a need for setting up an online account.

During setup, the steps are confusing enough for a beginner. The setup process asks us to disconnect the remote at some point and do some action on the TV. Just follow the dumb steps blindly. There is no logical thinking involved here. Good part is, it could acquire signals for my Apple TV.

Now comes the tough part.
1) Everytime I need to change the volume, I need to switch to TV option and change the volume. I run the DVD player as well as my Apple TV. With Youtube, not all the videos have same volume. I need to keep toggling between devices for the volume option. This beats the purpose of having \\"Master Device\\" for some specific actions.
2) When ever I change the device, by default, the RC menu lands in next option for that device. Example, if I switch to TV, it takes me to \\"Digit Enter\\" and \\"Format\\" options. This causes confusion as to what to do next. It should just stay back on the menu, with TV device highlighted. Now, when I need to swap between devices, I need to go back to the devices option or back button and change the devices again.
3) They have setup quick actions like \\"Good Night\\" and \\"Hello\\" options. \\"Good Night\\" is supposed to switch off all the devices. But if I have one of the devices turned off already, using this option will switch off the devices that are turned On and the ones that are already switched off will get turned on. I know there may not be any option to check if a system is on or off, since this is just IR signal, but like I mentioned before, the name of the quick features just add to the mounting confusion.

Overall, I feel its not worth the price. I got this on daily deal for $20 and hence not cursing this RC as much as I would have, if I were to buy it at regular price. I rarely use this device now and rely on device specific remotes if they are handy and reachable.
Out of 5, One star less for having to create an online account for setting it up and two less for usability problems.

product_title: Skullcandy Titan In Ear Bud
review_body: These ear buds are the best I have ever owned. I bought them to replace my apple in-ears, that I have had for several years now. I have to say, the Titans are so much better in sound quality and fit, I can´t believe I missed out on that all this time! Of course I knew, the apple headphones were not the best on the market, but I always thought that I would have to pay much more for a decent pair of comfortable headphones, with good insulation und sound quality. Totally wrong! These do the job perfectly and they fit great - even better than my old ones! No matter what I do, they stay in place and they don´t hurt my ears.   My husband has one of these noise cancelling headphones from Bose. He used to really love them and I always was a bit jealous, but didn´t really want to spend that much money on headphones. Now that I have these and my husband tried them, he even thinks about buying some for himselfe. He says, they might be the better choice than the noise cancelling ones because they do an equally good job in blocking out the noise but don´t need batteries. Also, they are much smaller and have a really impressing sound quality. I wouldn´t consider myself being an expert in that field - as I said, the apple in-ears worked fine for me - but with these, I just hear so much more and clear and they fit so much better. I am glad I bought them!  I read some of the reviews before buying these and I remember one saying that you should try all of the silicon buds before deciding which one you are going to use. I totally agree, it really does make a difference and I would have chosen the wrong size if I hadn´t tryed them all.  Somebody elese wrote that he/she got tiny little electric shocks from one of the earbuds. That actually happened to me once! If I wouldn´t have read about it before, I probably would not have realized what it was, since it wasn´t really strong. Still, it was a little \\"sting\\". I then noticed that I had the bud in my ear in a way that the part, where the cable goes out, directly touched my ear. I just turned it a bit and it didn´t happen again(I used these headphones every day for the past two weeks). I guess, it was just a stupid coincidence, that it was sitting in the one position where this could happen. Still, it´s reason enough to deduct one star...  As for the durability I can´t really say much, since I have had them only for about two weeks so far. But I registered them for the lifetime warranty, so I am optimistic that I get a replacement, should they decide to fail any time soon.  I also bought the 50/50 headphones with microphone. They are really good too, but if you need to decide between them and the Titans, and the mic. isn´t as important to you, go with the Titans! The sound quality is a bit better, although I felt the 50/50 were a tiny bit more comfortable. I think, there is also a version of the Titans with microphone available, don´t know if the quality is the same though.

product_title: VideoSecu ML531BE TV Wall Mount for most 22"-55" LED LCD Plasma Flat Screen Monitor up to 88 lb VESA 400x400 with Full Motion Swivel Articulating 20 in Extension Arm, HDMI Cable & Bubble Level WP5
review_body: Shipping was on-time all the way to Alaska. Packaging was good to go. I mounted easily into a single stud (I'm not a dummy but I wouldn't say I'm handy either). Once mounted it's very sturdy and is exactly what I was looking for. I mounted a Dell 23\\" Ultrasharp that is VESA 100x100. I now have a lot more room to fit my work laptop on my desk and whatever I feel like. I have a secondary screen on the desk too, a 19.5\\" Dell Ultrasharp, and I'm going to order this same mount for it after knowing I like it and for a great price $27.99, free shipping, free level & HDMI cord.       I would follow Brianstech's review for install because his directions made things easy. One thing I did different was drill the middle lag bolt first, ratchet it down so there was still enough room to hang the mount on the middle lag bolt, set the mount on the middle lag bolt and marked the top and bottom holes with a pencil and using the free level and then drilled them after I put down the mount (it was actually a little tough to hold the mount, hold the level and then mark the top and bottom hole so I had a box that was luckily about the right height with a sweater added on top so I was able to let the extended part of the mount rest on it). Once you are ready to mount and screw down the final two lag bolts his idea for putting the monitor face down on a bed, screwing the mount to it, hanging it on the middle lag bolt and then screwing in the top and bottom lag bolts worked great. I did have my friend hold it, though, because I was leaning over a desk I didn't feel like moving. I think it can be done alone but if you have someone for just 1 or 2 parts of the install it makes it easy. Being close to the wall would help.      Only negatives: The bolts weren't labeled but it was really easy to figure out and it's nothing to worry about. It can be a little stiff at first but you can loosen the joints and/or grease them a little. Makes me feel safer actually.      This is my first purchase on Amazon and I'm very pleased. I hope this review helps.

product_title: Monster Monster Turbine Mobile High Performance In-Ear Speakers
review_headline: Earphones great, mic not so much.
review_body:
I had listened to my iPhone through Monster in-ear speakers and was very impressed. Enough so that I returned them and purchased this product with the mic instead.

Bad idea. I use my phone outdoors quite a bit and I found that even barely a breathe of air movement made my end of the conversation virtually unhearable. The mic picked up every last whisper of air and amplified it over the sound of my voice. So much so that I stopped using them altogether and ended up returning them.

On a side note, the cord length of this product was noticeably shorter than the earphone-only version. This would not have been a showstopper for me but was an annoyance in my particular application of using them on my bike. With the earphone only version the cord was long enough to run under my jacket and then in to my helmet. With this version the cord was a bit shorter and was not long enough to route this way, leaving it outside and exposed to the wind and other elements.

product_title: JBL SB 300 Soundbar and 150-Watt Subwoofer
review_headline: Great Performance - Does What It's Supposed To
review_body: This system comes in a huge, huge box. I don't know if that's a necessary component of a review, but it's pretty impressive when you get it. But, it's not really as big as it seems. The Soundbar is packed vertically with the subwoofer below it, and there's plenty of open space in the box. Anyway, on to the review.  The soundbar sounds fantastic. I have watched Jurassic Park and The Lost World on this system, and it booms. The subwoofer is particularly impressive. Now, this thing is meant to replace a 5.1 or 7.1 system, but it simply can't. That said, it gets as close to doing that with a single speaker plus subwoofer as I can imagine. If you want to sacrifice a little sound to have almost no clutter in your living room, or wherever you put this thing, I think it's worth it. You only need to plug this in and send an optical cable to your TV, and that's it for the cables. While watching the Jurassic Par Blu-Rays, the T-Rex roared was particularly impressive. The floor shook. Everything was good. I've also played some Playstation 3 games on this and the sound is very crisp and very clear. I'm very happy with this system.  The only minor complaint I have is that the remote that comes with it is pretty awful. Now, odds are that you'll have a universal remote and will program it to take care of this system as well. If you don't have one, though, the remote that comes with this thing will convince you to get one.  If you're looking for a soundbar/subwoofer system, you'd do well to look at this JBL system.

The white LED flash light isn't that bright, because it has only one LED, but it is usable if you need to find a keyhole in the dark. When in the USB mode, a red LED will light up to indicate that it is turned on.

It takes two AA size batteries. Certainly you can use Alkaline batteries like Duracell and Energizer, but rechargeable batteries are more economical and earth friendly.

\\"Normal\\" rechargeable battery are of the Ni-MH type, which is 1.2V in voltage.

Now there is a new kind that is Ni-Zn, which produces a voltage of 1.6v - much closer to the voltage of Alkaline battery.

The brand I use is called Powergenix; each AA battery is rated at 2500 mAh in capacity. A fast 1-hour charger plus 4 battery cost only $18.

[[ASIN:B0029NZVZ0 PowerGenix ZR-PGX1HRAA-4B 1 Hour Quick Charger with 4 AA 1.6v NiZn Rechargeable Batteries]]

IMO, this is the best type of battery to power this USB emergency charger, because the higher voltage makes it last much longer, and you can charge it over and over to save money.

review_headline: Horrible batteries, barely had a charge to them
review_body:
Back in the 1990's I was tasked with testing a series of different batteries to see what ones where the best. Back then we found that Kodak batteries where pretty good for the price. So when I saw these on Amazon for a low price, I thought, \\"great, a decent battery for a low price\\".

product_title: Emerson Radio Jumbo Triple Display Dual Alarm AM/FM Clock Radio with SmartSet Technology (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Fantastic for those who want to sleep in pitch black dark
review_body: When I sleep I like the room to be as dark as possible. I dislike all the display lights on my stereo, my DVD player, my TV, and my alarm clock. When you add up all the light they put out I find it annoying when I want to sleep. Enter this alarm clock:     It has a feature to turn the display completely off....and when you want to know what time it is, you simply wave your hand in front of the clock and the display will turn on for a few seconds and then turn back off. This feature also works for the snooze function as well. This feature can be turned on and off with the flip of a switch on the side of the unit.    Another feature not found on most alarm clocks is that the time the alarm is set to go off is constantly displayed right below the current time. This alarm clock also has what I would call a \\"constant alarm\\" feature. Meaning that you do not turn the alarm completely off when you get up in the morning. You just press the button to silence the alarm, and unless you tell it not to, the alarm will go off again the next morning.     There are also 3 different day group selections you can choose for the alarm to go off. They are 1. 7 days a week. 2. mon-fri only. 3. sat & sun only. Since there are two alarms you can have it set up to have one alarm go off during the week and the second alarm go off at a different time on weekends. You can also have both alarms go off on the same day at different times.    In my humble opinion, if you are in the market for an alarm clock, there is no way you will be disappointed in this particular Emerson.

product_title: 4X1 HD Component Av Selector (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
I am an audiophile who was looking to connect multiple devices to my single set of 5.1 channel inputs. I have several devices with 5.1 analog audio outputs. (Blu-ray, SACD, PC sound card) SACD can best be heard via these 5.1 analog connections. I wanted an inexpensive (but sound neutral) way of connecting my devices and this switch works nicely. Though it's a 4-way switcher, one of the inputs doesn't have all six of the input jacks needed for 5.1, so it is, for this purpose, a three-way switch.

This box simply connects the selected pairs of RCA jacks together. Simply designate and connect like-colored jacks together and the signal is passed through unaltered. As far as I can tell (and I'm a fairly critical listener) there's no attenuation from impedance-matching resistors (as would be found in electronic switches)or from Y-ing two outputs together. There's no hum from power supplies or hiss or other noise from electronics, since there's no electronics and no power supply. It needs neither batteries nor a power outlet. No status lights either. The unit selected is the button that's pushed down lower than the others. If you're willing to push a button on a box on top of your stack of players when you put in a disk, it's the solution of choice. I hardly miss remote control capability since I have to get up load media anyway.

I was also able to use 7.1 by direct connection of the SBR & SBL channels to their corresponding inputs on my preamp. Since generally only one 5.1 source device should be in operation at any time, my single 7.1 device works great as well. My connections were as follows:

FL - L - White
FR - R - Red
Sub - V - Yellow
Ctr - Y - Green
SL - Pb - Blue
SR - Pr - Red (Orange)
SBL - N/A - Direct Connection
SBR - N/A - Direct Connection

I've used this device for a little over a week now with fairly heavy usage and have experienced no problems. As an aside, it is nice to have my PC sound card hooked up. It allows me to listen to all things web related in full surround - a nice option. Highly recommended!all things web related in full surround - a nice option. Highly recommended!

product_title: Sony Walkman S-540 Series 8 GB Video MP3 Player
review_headline: The best of 'the other' MP3 players
review_body:
If Sony weren't so internally dysfunctional (as a company) they would have had the iPod+iTunes business years ago. As it is, Sony music sells through iTunes, and Sony Walkman ends up being one of the 'other' brand MP3 players.

Too bad.

This is a 1st rate music player, every bit as good as the iPod in interface and sound quality; and it is actually more versatile in functionality (music, videos, photos in any format, and a good FM radio). The UI is very fast and friendly. The case design is attractive -- I liked the red color, and it looks great in the flesh.

As other reviews note, the case and screen are plastic, so they may scratch, though their quality is good, and I think they could take significant abuse.

Overall, I am very very happy with this purchase. These Walkman players are excellent quality at their price point (I paid $79) a fraction of the price of comparable iPod (or now defunct Zune) with comparable music quality (DAC) and much more flexibility in media file formats (if they are not in a format that the Walkman can play directly, they will be converted as soon as you drop them in the folder)

Where the Walkman actually improves on the iPod is their software interface -- pure drag and drop, with automatic file conversion, leveling, etc. I would choose the Walkman over the iPod just because of this (and I did).

Funny, I used to aviod Sony because of their awful software (+bloatware). They seem to have gotten the message, and their software is IMHO, class leading.

product_title: Sony MDRNC200D Digital Noise-Canceling Headphones (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
OK, I have to admit that I usually buy cheap headphones, so there's probably a reason these are the best I've ever had. That said, my husband has a couple of pairs of noise cancelling headphones, and I don't like them at all. They work just fine, but they give me a hollow feeling in my head (no jokes, please). It just kind of feels like I'm in a bubble.

This pair doesn't have that effect! Yay! I've been listening to various kinds of music for the past hour or so, and the sound is really good! One Night In Bangkok by Murray Head is playing right now. I've listened to soft, hard, classical, and now classic 80's. Everything sounds very clear, so much so that I can now make out some of the words. \\"Siam's gonna be the witness to the ultimate test of cerebral fitness\\" - oh, that's what he's saying! I thought... uh, never mind.)

I don't hear any other noises from around the house, so the noise cancelling function seems to be working just fine. It takes a while to get used to the placement of the buttons, but that's no different than anything else. I'm glad that these headphones work just fine even if the battery dies, though the noise cancelling thing doesn't work then. The phone just rang, and the only reason I knew it was because I saw my husband pick it up. Cool! There's a button on the left can that says \\"monitor\\" and it's for shutting off the headphones if you want to listen to something without taking them off. Nice feature, but I would probably take them off if I needed to listen to someone just to be polite.

This actually came with a battery! Yay! It was in the top pocket of the case with the cord and the airplane adapter. I haven't tried it on an airplane yet, but considering how well these seem to work, I'm really looking forward to that in a few months.

I haven't cranked up the volume because I want my ears to work when I'm old, so I haven't noticed any of the distortion that other reviewers have mentioned. At midrange volume, the sound is wonderful, and since outside noise has been blocked so well, I don't need to crank it up any higher.

And lastly, these are very comfortable. And they haven't fallen off yet, despite the fact that Ricky Martin is Livin' La Vida Loca right now. You can't dance far when you're wired in to your laptop, but you can certainly get some good shaking going.is wonderful, and since outside noise has been blocked so well, I don't need to crank it up any higher. review_headline: Not fancy, but gets the job done
review_body: I purchased this converter to use with laptops (Dell Mini, Asus EP 121) and cell phone (Motorola Atrix) that have hdmi video output. I want to be able to display the screens using digital projection equipment that has a 15 pin DE-15 \\"VGA\\" input. The converter is packaged so simply it might cause initial concern about functionality. It came in a plain cardboard box with a single photocopied sheet of instructions, my first impression was \\"whoops\\". I hurried to test it out so that I could return it if necessary. The hdmi support in Windows 7 is MUCH better than Vista or XP, so no change in settings on the laptops was required. I plugged in the cables and it just worked. No problems. If you want to make use of a screen or projector that only accepts VGA input but have a laptop that only has hdmi video output, this converter should get the job done.

One other thing I do like about this is it is all one unit - in other words, there are not separate detachable speakers where you could possibly have the attaching bracket break: it is portable and we have moved it from one room to the back porch with no problem.

Overall, this is a very good value and appears to be of a better manufacturing quality than others out there. While a little more pricey, the quality of the sound outweighs (to me) those costs.

product_title: ClearStream 1 Convertible Indoor/Outdoor HDTV Antenna with Mount - 30 Mile Range
review_headline: Amazing product.  Save big bucks on cable bill.
review_body: Ask most people about television antennas and they'll think of old style rabbit ears, or a broken, rusty roof-top antenna.   But since the transition to digital television in June 2009, free over-the-air digital high definition TV has been available to 90% of Americans who have a newer flat panel TV.  (Older TV's require a box.)      I have two daughters in college who were expecting to pay for cable TV in their apartments.   I suggested that before sinking $60/mo for cable, that they try out \\"free wireless digital TV\\" as I called it.  They had no clue that it even existed.   I bought the Clearstream 1 from Amazon for my daughter in St. Louis.  She lives in the city in a ground floor apartment, next to a 3 story building.  Her window was not facing the direction of the towers, so I didn't have high hopes for any signal, let alone something that was reliable.   I unboxed the antenna.  The \\"convertible\\" model includes a mesh reflector and a bracket for an outside mast.  These are not used in the indoor configuration--either wall or desk mount.  The unit snaps together in a couple of seconds.  It is the perfect size to set inconspicuously behind the TV on the window sill.   The provided cable had the screw on F-connectors, and a very thin center conductor, which easily bends.  On my first attempt to screw on the cable, the center conductor bent flat rendering the cable useless.  Fortunately I had a spare push-on type cable.   It was MUCH easier to connect than the provided cable.  The screw type connectors were hard to turn since the connector was partially recessed on the antenna unit.  It can be done, but it takes smaller fingers and more patience than I have.      Once the cable was attached to the unit, I connected it to the antenna jack on the TV.  Again I set the unit in a window just behind the flat panel TV with no particular orientation.  The next step was to do the channel scan on the TV.   Amazingly, the scan resulted in 30+ channels.   Being next to a tallbuilding, I hadn't expected any.  Her Vizio TV was one of only a few models that does NOT have a signal strength meter in the menu.  There was no way to measure the signal intensity.  But the primary stations in St. Louis  (ABC, CBS, NBC, FOX and a couple of independents) came in perfectly, and in high definition.   No static.  No blockiness.   I was really amazed.   Later, I checked the signal strength with a tuner card that I had in my laptop computer, and the signal was acceptable on all of the channels, though not really strong.  Being about 8.5 miles from the towers, I suspect that we were getting a strong reflection from the adjacent building rather than a direct signal path.  Whatever works! Another thing working in our favor was the fact that all of the major TV stations in St. Louis are transmitting on the UHF band, and this is a UHF antenna.  UHF generally works better in a crowded area in part because it is not subject to as much interference (from neighboring hair dryers, etc.) as VHF transmissions.  With UHF stations, you usually either get them or you don't.  With VHF, you can be watching with a perfect picture that will all of a sudden disappear when interference occurs.  To find out if your local stations are UHF or VHF,  don't go by the channel numbers.   (In New York, channel 4 really broadcasts on channel 28 in the UHF band.  They just use the name 4.)  You really need to check the actual channel numbers with a website like [...] or [...]      To summarize, the Clearstream 1 Convertible worked perfectly, and my daughter and roommates are very happy--especially since there is no monthly cable bill.    Of course, they won't be able to watch CNN, ESPN, BRAVO, etc.  But a lot of television today is available over the internet, so they don't mind.   It is a very good, attractive, easy to set up antenna that will pull in reception from local TV stations and save you a ton of money each month.       My other daughter is in Chapel Hill NC where there is amix of UHF and VHF stations.  Again, she was not facing the towers, and further from the transmitter making reception more difficult.   I got her a \\"Clearstream 2\\" model similar to 2 Clearstream 1's  strapped together, with a single mesh reflector.   It's much more obtrusive as an indoor antenna, but does a pretty good job of pulling in the stations--much better than I had expected.   She discontinued her cable service and is very happy that she did so.   With the money saved, she added a Roku box and is now able to watch Netflix and many other shows, all for about $8/month, and still have all of the networks as well as local news weather and sports.

product_title: Philips SPP5035A/17 Home Theater Surge Protector with 3 Outlets and 1500J Wall Tap (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Shuts Down the Power. Jury is Out on the Picture Quality Improvement Claim.
review_body:
I have the 3 Outlet protector & chose this option because I wanted to at least up the number of outlets than I normally would have had with the standard wall outlet. There are 2 plugs on 1 side & 1 plug on the other. There is a phone jack insert that is obsolete.

The power protector covers the entire wall outlet - there is a 3 prong to fit in the upper plug & a support prong that fits in the lower plug to stabilize the protector for those of us who plug in heavy cords. The protector has a continuous on green & red light (as seen on the front of the box), and, if the protector is not covered by a TV, is bright enough to be easily seen in the dark.

We had a power surge shortly after I installed the protector and the protector did as advertised - completely shut down the things plugged into it (other household electronics glitched & came back on). The TV suffered no surge damage & continues to function.

I cannot tell if my picture quality has improved since installing the protector. If it has, it is so minute that it really makes no difference to me, an average electronics user.

This protector is good for a secondary TV with few \\"accessories\\". For the full home theater, you'll want more plug options (which means a big & bulky strip like [[ASIN:B000SXWGA6 Panamax M10-HT-PRO Home Theater Management]]).

By pointing this antenna in that direction from my attic room and inserting an inline powered signal booster that is capable of sending signal to four different T.V. sets I now have 3 T.V. sets hooked up and receiving signals from 15 HDTV stations in the St. Louis metropolitan area. product_title: iHome iP39 Kitchen Timer and Alarm Clock Radio Speaker System for iPhone/iPod
review_body:
Sound quality is fine for its size. I was hoping to use this for an alarm clock in my bedroom, and it works for that, but I am disappointed about a few features:

* The iPod must be PLAYING music when you insert it into the dock for it to play through the speakers. You can't insert it first and then choose your music.
* Though iHome peddles its alarm software in the user guide, the software is not compatible with this product. That is, it doesn't communicate with the clock radio. The advantage of the software is that you can set the alarm to play a specific tune. Since the clock radio does not have that feature, if you set the alarm to play the iPod, it plays whatever was last up on the iPod. I'd rather not wake to punk if that's the last thing I was listening to. So I just wake up to the radio. Bummer. The whole reason I bought this was to be able to charge my iPod and wake to music from it. Oh well, it does charge.
* Some users complained about the brightness of the display. It can be turned down, but it's pretty dim. Another step in the dimness setting would have helped.
* The remote claims to have a magnet on the back, but that seems to be untrue. That magnet won't stick to metal. I think it's just a piece of metal that sticks to the speaker on the side of the unit(as pictured). It's the SPEAKER that's magnetic, not the remote. What good is sticking the remote to the side of the unit? It's not really a remote then, is it?

While it's okay for what it does, I'd have returned it if I hadn't waited too long to do so. I didn't have time last month to monkey with that. Oh well.

review_headline: Terrific solution to stream audio in my car! Audio guy WIN!!
review_body: I've used an 3.5mm (1/8\\") cable and the aux input for 10 years to play music off a portable device in my vehicles since FM transmitters compress audio so drastically.  A cable has always been ok but never as simple as I would have liked.  It's a nuisance to be tethered to a short cable especially when playing music from my phone and a long cable gets in the way when not in use.  This problem grew to be an even bigger pain when I purchased a LifeProof case (waterproof, sleeker version of the Otterbox) for my iPhone 4S which requires a screw-on plug be removed from the case to allow access to the headphone jack.  Solution? The Britelink Bluetooth Audio Receiver. I was skeptical but now totally sold on this method.  I used some velcro-stickies to mount the unit (surprisingly small) next to my car stereo on the dash.  It stays unseen by most passengers and never gets in the way.  The audio quality is near perfect.. as a full-time audio engineer this was very important.  It's not by any means reference quality but definitely good enough for general listening.  The battery lasts longer than expected somewhere around 14 hours of playback... For me that means I charge the device once every week or so.  The ONLY con I have with the receiver is that you have to hold the power button for a few more seconds than I would have liked.  To me a simple press would be sufficient but instead you hold for about 5 seconds before the device powers up (about 15 seconds to pair to a device but you only do that once per device/phone/ipod).  I am very pleased with this product.

review_body:
I've gotta say, buying mid-range headphones is pretty pointless. Either you deal with \\"okay\\" sound with cheap ones (like I put at the end of my review), or you shell out a few bucks and get the best.

I tried these headphones on my computer (imac 27 in, 2.7 ghz), my phone (evo shift), and my ipod (classic 60 gb).
As others have pointed out, the construction is sound; the fabric cables are a huge bonus, I'm not worried I'll bust them in a month or two. That's really the best part about these. They are comfortable, but fall out easily (making using them for anything besides sitting impractical).
Another reviewer also said they have flat sound. That is certainly true, aside from the bass. They sounded alright with The Beatles, but some modern hip hop sounded almost too muddled to listen to. Reverend Horton Heat sounded like the bass had been brought way up in an (unsuccessful) attempt to \\"fill out\\" the sound.
Additionally, they have REALLY bad white noise. From the moment I plugged them in, there was a soft woosh constantly running through them. Likely interference, as it lessened with my ipod (was worst on the computer), but the level of extra noise is unacceptable for me.
As far as sound, the Apple earbuds are probably better. These are far more comfortable though.
Keep looking. These[...]preferable if you're not looking for top-of-the-line.

product_title: XtremeMac Tango TRX Bluetooth 30-Pin iPod/iPhone/iPad Speaker Dock
review_headline: XtremeMac Tango: Good Product for the Price
review_body:
XtremeMac Tango TRX 2.1 Wireless is a small Speaker with iPod capabilities and it satisfies in most respects. It can be used with devices that have Bluetooth connectivity, like a Smartphone, or with iPods or MP3 players, for a full sound experience.

I have a Smartphone and while I don't use it for listening purposes very frequently, I still access it on occasion and the XtremeMac Tango has proven itself an effective means to better sound. Hooking up the Bluetooth to the XtremeMac is about as simple as it can be and in very little time, you can be listening to your favourite tunes with better sound than you would normally experience.

XtremeMac Tango has many positive qualities and the first is the one you notice when you open the box. This device is compact and has a slick, modern, high- tech appearance. It looks sharp on your desktop or most anyplace else. And it is compact enough to setup just about anyplace. Just move a few books aside and you should have no problem setting up your XtremeMac Tango. The remote control is nice, too. It offers volume control, pause, skip, and other functions with the press of a button.

Most qualities of the XtremeMac Tango are positive, but one that will concern some is the quality of the sound. I consider it acceptable and it is certainly much better than listening to music straight from my Smartphone. But I know that those who demand near- perfect sound will find XtremeMac Tango inferior to other, more sophisticated devices. This appears to be a common concern, judging by other reviews, and I must agree that the sound is less than perfect, even though certainly better than the sound you get when you utilize the built- in speaker on your Smartphone.

Having a quick, simple way to listen to music from a phone, Ipod, or MP3 is a nice convenience and the XtremeMac Tango TRX 2.1 offers exactly that. The unit is sharp in appearance and the device can be hooked up and ready to use in minutes. There are better devices out there for optimal sound quality, but they cost much more and when all factors are considered, the XtremeMac Tango ranks as a good speaker system overall.re are better devices out there for optimal sound quality, but they cost much more and when all factors are considered, the XtremeMac Tango ranks as a good speaker system overall.

product_title: MAXIMO Enhanced Definition Isolation Earphones
review_headline: It worked well, while it lasted...
review_body: Some things to note:  -It came with a lot of accessories. It had tips of sizes, allowing me to find a good fit for my ears.  -It comes with a carrying case! I cannot stress how important it is to have a carrying case for IEMs such as this one. You'll get much more life out of your IEMs when you care for them properly.  -It comes with a clip for you clip the cord against your shirt to minimize microphonic sounds (rubbing of the cord will produce loud sounds in your ear for most IEMs).    Regarding the sound quality:   -I found the sound quality to be pretty good for a ~50 dollar IEM. Personally, I prefer a neutral, natural sound from my headphones (a flat, realistic sound). In comparison to the Head-Direct RE0's, the music doesn't sound as clear. The Im-590 is still up there in sound quality, though. Don't get me wrong; it's leaps and bounds ahead of anything SkullCandy has to offer. It's just that nothing sounds muddied with the RE0's. Where the Im-590's shine, though, is the full base response. After obtaining a good seal with the flanges(VERY IMPORTANT with any IEM), I heard a nice, rich base response with the Im-590's without any bloated bass.     What REALLY bugged me was the build quality of these headphones. I'm very careful with anything I own, yet, after wearing these headphones for ~5 hours, the sound suddenly disappeared in the left driver. I heard intermittent crackling sounds for a few minutes; then, the sound completely disappeared from the left driver. I RMA-ed these to Amazon.    It was good was it lasted. Maybe it was just my bad luck, but I didn't want to take another chance with headphones of questionable build quality.    Hope this helps...

product_title: V-MODA Remix M-Class Earbuds
review_headline: These are the worst things I have ever purchased! DO NOT BUY!!!
review_body: I had purchased these earbuds because I had lost my old earbuds.  V-Moda is a company I trust because my previous earbuds were V-Moda Vibes, and they were equal, or possibly better than the Skull Candy 50/50 earbuds I had (possible because they are the same price). I thought, since these V-Moda Remix M-class earbuds were $50 when they came out, as well as the vibes, they must be pretty good, but boy, was I wrong.     Pros: high quality material (aluminum), sticks in your ears, and very nice treble.     Cons: NO bass or mid (crackly and such), fell apart in a week, the holes where the music comes out are in the worst places.     Yes, the metal is very nice, and the rubber used for the chord is high quality and easy to untangle. The little rubber length adjuster is just a thick, cheap, piece of fat rubber, that you rap your chord around to make it shorter, which sucks if you are trying to listen to music when walking, or exercising. It bounces around, and gets stuck to your clothes! Then, when you take the adjuster off, the chord makes a spring shape for at least the next few times you use them... The problem is that I took it out of my ear by lifting up the bottom of the bud, and the back snapped off! The two pieces separated! I was confused, so i pulled the other earbud from the back, and that snapped off with a light tug! What crap.     Next, like I said, the treble is great, but the bass is horrible. If you put on bass booster, the music sounds like fuzz and crackles. If you keep an equalizer off, the bass just sounds like... Well, it sounds like there is no bass. You can buy bass less earbuds, but they are high quality. One of the features of these earbuds has to do with its high quality bass. (False)...     Finally, the driver (or speaker) is in the back of an earbud. Then there are holes where the sound travels to reach your ear. On these earbuds, the holes are very tiny circles, that create a circle around the inside of your ear. The problem is, sound goes through the bottom/middle of your ear, not the outskirts... That is why the earbuds are very quite, and you don't get the sound you could possible receive... I recommend more in-ear earbuds, instead of the round circle ones that just sit on the shape of the ear.    Altogether, these are the worst purchase I have ever made when it comes to music! If you want reasonably priced earbuds, I recommend Skullcandy, Coby, Sony, or of you are willing to spend more money, Bose are really nice. The Apple ones that come with an i-pod are great, or even another pair of V-Moda earbuds, like the vibe, the vibe 2, or the bass freq. Just not the Remix M-class!

review_body: These sound amazing.  I wore them in a loud airplane (louder than a commercial airliner) and they blocked out plenty of noise.  However, These headphones did not fit my ear very well. review_headline: Nice scanner for the average listener
review_body: I bought this scanner for an employee who likes listening to radio traffic.  I paid $89 through Amazon and I see it is a few dollars less today.. Uniden makes good products.. I had one question on programming and they responded to me very promptly and professionally.  It isn't too complicated to program or operate, if you've owned a scanner before.. If you are new to scanners, you will probably have to read the manual good.  Like I said, there tech support is really good.  This model scanner covers the basics.. It does not do 800 MHZ though.. This may be important in your area.. 800 mhz is getting more and more popular with all lines of two-way radio.. Also, this does not do Digital formatting of radio.. You will spend $400 to $500 for one of those scanners.. Some departments are running digital.. My best advice is to check your area to see what is being used before you purchase a scanner.. The internet is a good place to search for radio info.. FCC has a website for radio license, but not user friendly..  I believe the scanner just above this one in price ( + $40 ) does 800 mhz.  This is a 100 channel scanner, which should be more than adequate for the average listener.. I bought a scanner 20 years ago that was a 10 ch and paid the same price back then as this one is now.. It is also an am-fm radio, as well as an alarm clock.. I would certainly recommend this model if you do not need 800 mhz coverage.

After reading through all the reviews, I noticed references to problems with the adapter. I purchased a $2 replacement 75/300 ohm TV Antenna Transformer Adapter from Menard's. product_title: iHome Rechargeable Mini Speakers (Black & Grey)
review_headline: The Most Amazing Portable Electronics Product I've Ever Owned
review_body:
I was skeptical when I first saw these. I expected tinny sound, minimal volume, and short battery life. I was as wrong as it is possible to be.

First, the engineering is very clever. The speakers are so compact that when collapsed and put together (they have magnetic bases), they fit in one hand. The speakers use a single cable for both charging and sound. The end that goes to into each speaker is a mini-USB connector. The end that plugs to your audio device is a standard headphone jack. A standard USB connector Ys off of that and is used to charge the speakers from your laptop or power to USB adapter.

Connected to an iPhone 4 at 2/3 volume the speakers were clearly audible 25 feet away. When cranked all the way up it was painful to sit right in front of them. I used a tone generator app to check the frequency response. They produce sound all the way down to 18Hz and all the way up to 20KHz. The volume is not even across the entire frequency range (no surprise), but it's quite solid between 60Hz and 4Khz (where most music and all speech recordings live).

I haven't succeeded in finding out how long the battery life is, because I haven't had a chance to sit in one spot long enough to run it completely down. The longest I have used them on battery is 2 hours and 45 minutes, at which point they were still going strong. If I could give this product 6 stars, I would.

product_title: Audio Unlimited Premium 900MHz Wireless Indoor/Outdoor Speakers withRemote and Dual Power Transmitter
review_headline: Perfect! Up and running in five minutes!
review_body: I was a bit skeptical about these, but i really needed a set of wireless speakers! I own a business and have several people working using sewing machines in a 1200 sq ft space. we all love to listen to music. since customers are also in the same area, i didnt want people using headphones and not being able to interact with them. Anyway, so although it seemed like the reviews weren't all that great, i really couldnt find much else anywhere near this price range that could be plugged directly into a computer or ipod. So i figured in a worst case scenario id wind up returning these speakers if they really sucked.    I cant tell you how pleased i am with these things! when they arrived, seriously it probably takes longer to remove them from the packaging than it does to set them up. take out the speakers, plug each one into a wall outlet. plug the main transmitter into a wall outlet. plug one of the included cables into the sound source (they include pretty much every type of cable(s) youd need to attach to receivers, ipods, etc). turn on your music. thats it! i had ZERO problems. I have several networked computers, wireless phones, a wireless printer, routers, all within 10 feet of the transmitter. there is no interference! the farthest speaker away from the transmitter is about 100 feet away.    the quality of the speakers is pretty good. its true the bass isnt amazing, but its more than sufficient. we listen to a mix of hip hop, rock, and spoken podcasts. everything is still clear, even when turned up loud enough to be heard over the noise of the machines. i havent had any situation where ive had to turn up the speakers more than a few clicks.     The only time ive heard feedback/interference is when ive turned off the music/sound source but left the transmitter and speakers turned on. as soon as you either turn music back on or turn off the transmitter, the feedback is gone. oh, or if by chance you havent fully connected the transmitter to the sound source (not fully plugged in), you'll hear some feedback.    probably the one and only gripe i have about this product is the cord that comes from the transmitter to the sound source itself. for some reason, audio unlimited decided to use possibly the thinnest cord ever......im kinda worried about it pulling out or something. its attached inside the transmitter so theres no real way to remove or replace it without opening that up. seems like a horrible decision to forego a regular cord here. seriously, the thing is probably less than 25% as thick as most audio cords.    ive only had this system about a month, but assuming it continues to work as it does now, im VERY happy with this purchase!

review_body: Pros: Plays games REALLY well in 2d and 3d modes  Great on battery life 5.5hours MAX personally tested.   Excellent loud crisp speakers. Great highs and mids  Sharp clean display. Not full HD but Blurays and games look Excellent  Bright illuminated keyboard. Cons: Textured finish feels REALLY plasticy but it beats the super glossy fingerprint magnets like HP laptops. The minimal glossy portions do look really nice though. Would prefer a matte finish   Backlit keyboard could be a little too bright at times. The raised keys bleed a lot of the white led light especially when looking at in from an angle.   ANNOYINGLY LOUD beeps when you adjust the volume. It not only beeps when you tap the volume button but will continue to beep as it raises and lowers the volume NOTE: its not Toshiba its the Realtek soundcard that makes the beep noise which can be muted in the volume mixer. Doesn't affect the functionality just the overall solid feel of the laptop.   Tons of inflated pre loaded software!    Other Thoughts: I've been using this laptop for 2 weeks straight now and i absolutely love it!   The Eco mode button is truly amazing. It shuts off the backlit keyboard, cuts power to the bluray drive, de-tunes the processor,and actually shows you your power consumption essentially bringing up your battery life to 5 hrs.   i got max about 5.5 with no wifi just photo editing. 4.5 hours of netflix streaming. 2-2.5 hours of playing need for speed hot pursuit with an xbox360 wireless remote plugged in. Also in Eco mode the laptop is almost silent. Right now the CPU fan is off and the hard drive is pretty inaudible.   The 5400rpm hd is pretty fast. i swapped in an old 7200 WD Scorpio Black and using ATTO the 5400 hd blows it away.   I've played Batman Arkham Asylum, NFS Hot Pursuit, and Civilization 5 on high to max settings in 2d and 3d and the GT540m kills!  This is the best 3d, Bluray Burning, Gaming, gen2 i7, laptop on the market Price vs Performance vs Feature wise.

product_title: iLuv Modern Sound 30-Pin Stereo Speaker Dock
review_headline: A good, inexpensive iPhone/iPod speaker that lives up to its price.
review_body:
I've been using the iLuv iMM288 for about a month. My reaction is that it good, but doesn't exceed what I expected. (In this review I would have preferred to give it 3.75 stars instead of 4 to capture my full impression. It was either 3 or 4 though, and it deserves more than 3.) The good part is that it works well as a way to amplify the music from your iPhone. I've used it with iTunes music as well as other iPhone applications. I listen to Spotify, via the app on my iPhone, with no problem.

I also like the companion software that you can add to your iPhone, an iPhone 4, in my case, to work with the unit. The software wasn't the most intuitive software I've used, but it does allow you to set up sleep timers, which I used a number of times. It also allows you to use your iPhone to turn the iLuv into an clock radio.

I've tried using it with 2 old iPods as well, the iPod Classic and an iPod Nano that's at least 3 years old. Both worked well.

The biggest compromise is the quality of the sound it actually produces. The sound isn't amplified to a 'big' sound, even at the highest volume level. The sound overall reminded me of the sound that comes from a decent laptop computer, which I would describe as 'a bit thin'. That might scare you off, but it's not meant to. The iLuv iMM288 works nicely as a small music listening solution on an office desk or a nightside table, where you're looking for a lower level amplification. Basically, you're not paying for a $400 sound system and you're not getting one.

product_title: Onkyo HT-S3400 5.1 Channel Home Theater (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Nice system with two small problems
review_body: I have had the Onkyo HT-S3400 system for about a month now. I am very happy with the look and sound of the system. The bass is surprising strong and the system set-up screens and adjustments are easy to access and operate.     I have two small criticisms:    1. The front speakers are not designed for use with speaker stands. I would suspect that most people use stands for the front speakers and mount the rear speakers on a wall. Obviously, Onkyo does not agree. I was able to mount the front speakers on stands using keyholes but it is not an ideal way to do this and the speakers are a little off-center on the stands.    2. I use Comcast for my cable TV service. After contacting both Comcast and Onkyo to try and get the correct codes to operate the Onkyo system using my Comcast remote I was told that the system was not compatible with the Comcast (Motorola) remote. Using the Code Search function I was finally able to locate a code that allowed me to turn on and operate the volume using the Comcast remote, but not turn it off. Other codes would turn the system off but not on. Seems strange to me. I have had 2 other surround sound systems and I was able to operate the receiver with the Comcast remote.    Other than the two above detailed issues I am very happy with the Onkyo HT-S3400 system.

product_title: DeoxIT® FaderLube Liquid, squeeze tube 100% solution 2 mL
review_body:
Squirted a tiny drop in each pot of a guitar tube distortion pedal and it works like new again. The pedal was only 3-4 years old but was known for having sub-standard pot quality, so it started crackling and cutting out when turning the knobs. But now it's back, working perfectly for the past two weeks.

The tube is tiny but I used so little in each of the six pots that indeed this will last me a year or two of occasional random use, hence the price is reasonable. Also I didn't need the DeOxit cleaner sprays or liquid either, just the Fader Lube, which is good because the cleaner line can shorten the life of pots by eating away their carbon tracks.

So if you're dealing with crackly pots on guitars, amps, pedals, etc... give this a try, it worked for me. But you don't have to take my word for it, da-dun-DUN!

review_body:
My family has opted to use a WIRED ear bud for our mobile phones, rather than blue-tooth (concerns about radio/microwave issues and so forth). My ears were not created to hold an ear-bud. As I tried various manufacturers, buds were too small, large, or sound far too soft. Buttons didn't work, etc. Jlab's wired mobile-device bud fits my ear perfectly. The bud has a soft tip conforms to your ear's contours, and is smaller to nestle firmly and comfortably (it's unlikely to hassle you by constantly falling out).

My wife is harder to \\"fit\\" than I. She tried my Jlab bud, loved it, and we ordered another. The device comes with several sized soft-rubber tips to accommodate most. A smaller tip was ideal for her ear. Sound is clear and sharp. Answer/end/and voice-command work smoothly with push of the in-line button (sits around collar bone on cord). review_body: These headphones were my third pair, having worn out two other brands. I was hoping to get a top quality product from Sennheiser. My Sharp headphones were the best that I ever owned, great fit and sound quality with ear covering cushions. These Sennheiser units work well have OK sound but are lacking much bass response. They are ill fitting and I too, have had trouble with them falling off my head with the slightest downward movement. In all fairness, I am bald and that may affect the fit as my son, with a full head of hair, has no trouble keeping them on his head. If the Sennheiser RS120 units had over the ear cushions and better ergonomics I would rate them as 4-5 star. I wish they had a LED indicating whether on or off it would also be nice. All in all, I give them an OK rating but not as great as Sennheiser's reputation.

product_title: iHome Color Changing 30-Pin iPod/iPhone Alarm Clock Speaker Dock
review_headline: great to look at, not so good to listen to
review_body:
The iHome iA17WZC is a nifty gadget that puts a smile on my face. Poor sound quality proves to be the Achilles' heal of this otherwise promising product.

PROs
+ Interesting round shape- fits great in a corner of a countertop.
+ Colorful built-in LED lights up the entire body of the clock in millions of colors.
+ Remote control.
+ Great integration with the iPhone/iPod. Syncs time with the push of a button.
+ Has a free iPhone/iPod app that could develop into something really neat.
+ iPhone 4 fits great on dock, even with iPhone bumper installed.

CONs
- Has an ugly DC power converter brick attached to the plug.
- Muddy, mediocre sound quality from the built-in speaker.
- Not terribly loud.

iPhone 4
---------------
My iPhone 4 docked beautifully, even with the bumper installed. The phone charged while in the dock and any music I played through the iPhone played to the clock-radio's speaker.

I played local MP3 music and also ran both the Pandora and SiriusXM apps on my phone. Everything worked great and played as expected. Overall, I think this product integrates beautifully with the iPhone/iPod.

iPod Touch
---------------
My iPod Touch worked perfectly with the iHome iA17WZC. The iHome app installed and worked the same as it did with my iPhone. Charging works great. Basically it is the same as the behavior of the iPhone 4 described above.

iPad 2
---------------
This dock does not support the iPad. It doesn't claim to so that isn't really a problem.

Speakers
---------------
The speakers on this clock are fairly mediocre. I'm not impressed with the muddy sound. Also, when you crank them up, they don't get very loud. In my opinion, I think only a young kid or someone listening to talk radio would be pleased with the quality of the speaker. Speakers alone make this a 3-star product. With better sound quality, this would be 5 stars.

Clock
---------------
The clock display on the iHome iA17WZC is bright and easy to read from any viewing angle. Even better, the color of the clock changes to exactly match the LED inside the \\"orb\\" of the clock. Everything changes in perfect sync.

Miscellaneous
---------------
The absolute coolest feature of this product is the infinite color display of the internal light. This color glows through the body of the clock and can be configured to be a solid color, to slowly transition through the entire spectrum of colors, or to pulse to the beat of the music you have playing. This feature brings such a big grin to my face and if the unit only had decent sound, this would be a slam-dunk 5 star product.

Summary
---------------
I really wish there was a way to upgrade the speaker quality of this product. The ability to control the clock from an iPhone/iPod app gives a world of possibilities and the colorful LED backlight adds a lot of character to any room. I think this is a great product for a 1-14 year old (because I don't think they'll be as discriminating on sound quality).ewing angle. This little device has ended all of that. I've been using it for almost a year now, and our problems have disappeared. We use a similar device where we have the digital cable service coming in, and we no longer suffer pixelation of our HDTV shows.

Honestly, for the price these little devices really do the job. Do not buy the simple amplifiers that you see at big box stores, they are inferior and a waste of money.

review_body: At first I was very excited, this is such a great price for banana plugs.  Beware, you get what you pay for. These are the worst I have ever used.  First of all, one of the plugs was missing a hole. It must have missed a step in the assembly line.  When I told amazon about it I was offered a $5 refund.  I was happy with that.  A few months later my center channel started acting up.  I went to swap it out for a different speaker to see if it was the speaker or the receiver, and I found that somehow the speaker wire had come loose from one of the banana plugs.  I tightened it up and it works fine.  How the does this happen?  I checked and the majority of the plugs had become slightly loose!  I have NEVER had to re-tighten any of my other banana plugs before.  I still do not understand how that happened, but I suppose they are just cheap and poorly designed.  This was not user error.   I would never recommend these to anyone.  I had a lot more success with monoprice closed screw type.

review_headline: Good for music but not for transcription.
review_body: I had high hopes for these earbuds, but for the price I paid they don't quite cut it. The sound is pretty good for music, but for use in transcription, which is what I use them for, they're marginal. The same holds true for movie dialog. They cancel noise pretty well, but things as mundane as keystrokes and outside conversations still get in and can be intrusive. They also tend to slip out and make my ears itch. When the battery gets low they start to make popping and high-pitched feedback noises.    The controller is bulky, especially if you're carrying them around on an iPod or MP3 player, and the cord isn't quite long enough if you're listening to audio on a laptop, especially if you're using an external keyboard. They have two volume choices, either high or low, which isn't bad, but depending on the volume controls of the player, it could be too much or not enough.
