product_title: Maha PowerEx MH-C9000 WizardOne Charger-Analyzer for 4 AA/AAA Batteries
review_headline: Still trying to figure this thing out, but works very well
review_body: Rechargeable batteries are the way to go.  Problem is that without the proper charger, you can drastically shorten the life of your batteries.  And that's all I know about batteries and battery chargers.  Apparently there is a lot more to know, which I found out the hard way when the Maha Powerex MH-C9000, recommended by a friend, arrived.  My research confirmed that this is the battery charger to own (I think there's another by LaCrosse Technologies that's pretty good too).  Other reviewers have mentioned that the instructions leave something to be desired, and I can certainly agree with that.  The instructions are next to useless for us non-techies, e.g. references to measurements and settings that don't appear on the LCD screen, arcane modes of operation, etc.  The Web site's FAQ is better, but not by a whole lot.  So I called Maha's customer service number.  Got right through to Eric who patiently answered my questions and explained some things I need to know about batteries and charging.  Turns out that the MH-C9000 is a very versatile and handy little item.  It does a lot and doesn't beat on your batteries       I'd ordinarily take away a star for the lack of good documentation, but I'm giving it back because Maha's customer support was so helpful.  The charger works very well too.

product_title: BIC America DV62si Bookshelf Speakers (Pair, Black)

Just my opinion, but vocals seems more realistic and they are just a bit more punchy.  No contest with rock tracks.  The BICs are flat and just miss the punch needed for r&r.  Most things sound great on the BICs (country, blues, soft rock, etc.) but for hard rock, they just don't work for some reason.  I am keeping the Entras for mains and using one of the BICs for a center (which works great by the way).  Still a steal for two awesome center channel speakers.

product_title: Pioneer VSX-1021-K 7.1 Home Theater Receiver, Glossy Black (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Good Receiver for the money. But...
review_body: It was with MUCH research that took me to finally choose this unit - I was looking at an Onkyo, Denon and the Pioneer. I had an older Pioneer receiver with no HDMI and based on my satisfaction with that kept me towards this model. Being that it was going to be installed in a cabinet I wanted to try Onkyo but their constant heat reports concerned me. That and I liked the features offered for apple integration. I only have 1/2 of my 7.1 speaker setup completed and with just the front channel, I connected my ipod touch and was shortly playing my Iron Movie video from my iPod Touch with acceptable quality.    Now - on to what they don't tell you in the review - 7.1 as per DOLBY's own site (check if you don't believe me)  7.1 setup is FRONT(left,center,right), CENTER(LR), REAR(LR) and SUB!  That's it - where did Pioneer all of a sudden decide that \\"THEIR\\" 7.1 setup actually put's 5 speakers up front and includes FRONT HIGH left and right.  Their manual almost implies that by doing the \\"dolby\\" method isn't optimal.    One of the main selling points on this receiver is for 'stand-by hdmi pass-thru\\" - well what again is not explained is this apparently called \\"HDMI Control\\" - but what they don't tell you is that it sounds like it's not a standard. I spoke to a Support person and basically he said that you enable it on the receiver, but then you must also have devices that allow you to enable it on the DEVICE side as well - which means probably my older 50\\" Samsung DLP won't have it.  And what that means is now I need to have the receiver turned on if I want audio AND video to process to the TV. I hope when I try later that their suggestion to allow Audio pass through to work will work as shown so I don't need to be blasting all speakers, just the TV in normal use.  After a day's research, it seems like this HDMI Control is about 3 years too early, and most people that finally get it working turn it off because it causes other issues. I wished there was support for 2 HDMI outputs and I have the DLP TV and an overhead front projector. I had to buy an Splitter box to run that, now it sounds like with this HDMI Control \\"feature\\" I should reconnect the external HDMI Switch.    That being said - so far these are the main drawbacks of the unit - and a few items that can no be accessed (system setup) from the front panel and instead you have to use the remote.

product_title: Tripp Lite Power Cord Extension Cable
review_headline: Only Saving Grace is TrippLite will replace it, but it will COST
review_body: I have had this unit for about a year, then it began to do strange things. Would shut off without any warning, pushing the test button would shut it off. After lengthy discussions with Tripp Lite it was returned for warranty. Yes YOU pay for the return (about $40.00 for return, Be aware you must protect it very well for shipping or they will deny the warranty)it took about four weeks to receive the warranty replacement. IT WAS BAD also. I did my own testing and discovered that if one of the batteries are bad (will show close to right voltage but still has a cell fault)the unit will either show half capacity on the display, and when the test button is pressed (4 seconds) the unit will fail. The PowerAlert software doesn't work on my Windows 7 Pro 64bit OS, by the way. I again emailed Tripp Lite describing the entire testing that I did and that there is a battery fault (I hooked it up to a laptop with Windows 7 Pro 32bit system, installed the PowerAlert software [it went in fine on the 32bit system] it showed the voltage lower than it should have been 22volts as opposed to 24-26volts) To Tripp Lite credit this time they sent another unit (second unit) with a label for return of the first warranty replacement (they did charge me [on credit, no card needed]the full retail price to ensure the return). This took about three more weeks (total without the unit seven weeks) This time the unit worked as it should, display showed full charge, and with a two hour power failure earlier this week it ran gave me time to shut the system down. The PowerAlert software NEVER did work with Windows 7 Pro 64bit (yes I did do all the usual things [shut off firewall, and anti-virus]) Tripp Lite says that it works with the 64bit system however I NEVER have been able to get it to work. Tripp Lite simply stops responding when I attempted to troubleshoot with them, they want you to call. When I called they walk you through the same ole thing and never did resolve it, claiming they would escalate it. NEVER heard from them again. I have moved it from my main system (can't trust it) and use it to keep clocks and unimportant things running with very little load. I have TWO Ultimate 1000va UPS (aka CyberPower) units that work Superb. I would not recommend this for anything that you depend on for serious use.  Jones9999

review_body: The price was right for this amazingly long (50') cable.  This Toslink fiber optic cable is very fine, and ,while not delicate, needs more care in avoiding damage than copper cables. product_title: V-MODA Bass Freq Earbuds
review_body: Considering these are averaging around $12-20 on amazon they really are super cheap. Also for that price they provide the deepest bass of any earbud I've ever heard under $80. The main problem is they just dont last. Over the last 4 years I've gone thru probably 5 pairs of these things. So yes less than 12 months average life span and I use these exclusively at the gym. So they get maybe 5-6 hours use per week and after lets call it 40 weeks they are done, usually one ear bud shorts out due to weak wiring. Now Im not saying after 200-300 hours use they stop. No. Im sure part of it is that I dont take pristine care of them. That is wrapping them around my mp3 player and throwing them in my bag at the gym when Im done. However, no matter how careful I am the longest pair maybe lasted a year and a few months and the shortest maybe 6-7 months. Why do I keep coming back? Honestly the sound is that good. They usually qualify for free shipping if you get two pair and exceed the $25 price point total. Thats what I just did. I got two for like $26. I figure that should last me a good 18 months and for the sound quality I figure its worth $1.50 a month. Besides at $13 a pair and even now buying a total of 6-7 pair Im still not at the price of one pair from Bose or Dre.    Might seem like a lot of criticism for a 4 star overall rating. As long as any prospective buyer has their eyes open and expects these to last just a year I do recommend these. If you like Bass, which I do especially when working out at the gym, these cannot be beat. I wish they lasted twice as long even if they doubled the price. As is I think I found the solution; just buy two pair at a time.

review_body: So people don't really understand how to review certain items. These guys are loud, really make it so you can't hear other people talk (you can still get the sense that they are talking but it doesn't interfere with the listening).  And the quality of the sound and bass are both very good.    Price is amazing.  We are talking $6 with prime shipping.  Forget about it.    Comfort is amazing. product_title: MartinLogan Motion 10 Floorstanding Speaker (Black Ash, each) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: Now I know that most reviews on Amazon state that the product they are reviewing is \\"best for the price\\".  This is particularly common with speakers.  Don't let this fool you.  Martin Logan has ultimately hit the pinnacle of speaker performance-to-value with the stunning Motion 10's.  To start, I purchased these speakers about a month and a half ago from a certified reseller on Amazon for about $225.00 each.  The shipping was great and the customer service was also at the five star mark.  The speakers arrived in some large boxes filled with styrofoam molds and elegant covers for the speakers themselves.  Not long after hooking up the speakers and setting the impedance on my receiver to 4 ohms, I played the first track and immediately was in disbelief.  The music (Maroon 5, in my case) sounded spectacular.  The bass was excellent for speakers with such a small footprint, and the highs/midrange was truly something special.  Keep in mind that in the owner's manual, there is a small excerpt stating that there is a 70 hour \\"burn in\\" period during which the speakers get accustomed and begin to sound much better.  This could be noticed after about 30 minutes of listening!  Fast-forward to today, and the 70 hours have been achieved.  I am speechless to how well these speakers actually play!  Being a 16 year-old, most kids my age fail to appreciate clarity or the stereo imaging created by a speaker.  I for one, found it to be something quite overlooked in speakers at this price point.  Not only is this a great value, but also a product that will keep serving you for years to come.  Pros: Great sound, small footprint, elegant design, great cable hookups, ribbon tweeter, magnetic grille, bragging rights for owning MartinLogan  Cons: Easy to topple over by small children, could use a better low-frequency extension  Don't waste your time looking for other speakers that cost hundreds more; the real deal are these Motion 10's

product_title: Midland WR120 series
review_body:
I have been dreading purchasing a weather radio for some time because they all seem too expensive for just a radio that receives the weather band. But, I figured out that it is time to take this out of the \\"family\\" budget. I literally looked at every single weather radio on Amazon. I found out that I want a radio with SAME (Specific Area Message Encoding) so it will alert for inclement weather. (tornadoes at night are an issue where I live) Most other radios seem to have issues with reliability, reception, or construction--issues I want to avoid. So, I narrowed it down to the Midland radios: WR-100, WR-120, and WR-300.

I was leery of purchasing this at first because of the limited review at the time. I found at that this is just the updated model of the WR-100, which seems to be one of the more popular weather radios. I went to Midland's website(to lookup the WR-120) and saw that the item was just released, hence the limited info.

I would consider this a great standard/staple alert weather radio. The SAME technology lets you setup your county, or multiple counties. You can find your county codes online at NOAA (search: national weather service radio codes to be taken there directly).

I really like the backlight on the display--a nice cool blue with easy to read lettering. The interface itself is great, it lets me flip through all current alerts with the up/down buttons, so I don't even have to listen to the radio to get the most up to date status. It is simple enough that my 4 year old could easily figure it out.

The alarm has 3 settings-tone, voice, and display.
-The tone alarm is loud! -- Which is great, not an annoying sound, just loud. It will wake you up. We can hear it all through our house.

-The voice alarm plays the loud tone for about 5 seconds and then goes into the radio broadcast(at the volume you set). I wish that the voice setting played just the radio, as I am used to a clock-radio alarm clock. The loud alert startles me out of sleep! I want the alarm to wake me, not scare me.

-The display just illuminates the backlight. Not useful for me at night, as I would not wake up to a soft blue, glowing light. I am sure this is plenty useful for some, and I will probably change the radio to this once we are out of tornado season.

Personally, I have not seen the multiple alert lights (5 for each-alert, watch and warning) to be all that useful because every message that my local weather service puts out does not code to the varying degree levels. I am sure this is useful for some, but I live right next to the NOAA station and they do not take advantage of this feature.(more a complaint against my local NOAA than the radio) -- ps the reception is great....because I live right next to the NOAA station, so my review of that is biased. :)

The radio runs on three AA batteries for backup. Not sure how long they last. There was no difference in reception, backlight, and radio functions when I unplugged it. This seems like this might be a great radio to do some light traveling.

I could not justify spending the extra on the WR-300 to get any additional features. (Maybe Midland can include a tone volume option in the next release model that lets you choose between several volume levels for any alert? Then the radio would be perfect.) I would have rated this 4.5 stars because the voice alert is not pure voice, but half stars are not an option, so I rounded up. Midland's Research and Product Development team seems to listen to customer reviews, so maybe the voice alarm can be fixed.

Definitely a must have family radio for safety, and the best value out there--I am glad I purchased it.

product_title: Archos Vision 24b 4 GB Video MP3 Player with 2.4-Inch Screen and FM Radio (Black)
review_headline: Decent unit, but a bit cheap
review_body:
I wasn't a huge fan of this player, although some of the features intrigued me, so I picked it up. The interface is a bit cloogy (I'm sure that's a technical term) and has animations that run a bit choppily. The construction feels kind of cheap, and it's difficult to navigate with one hand (I know that sounds silly, but I was using this while I was working out).

Moving files to and from the unit was a snap. I plugged it in on both a Mac and a PC, and it was just as easy with either platform by dragging and dropping the files in the appropriate folders. The unit uses a standard USB input (which is nice - proprietary ports suck) and the unit charges the same way.

The sound quality is great. The music is clear with good bass response. You might want to think about picking up another set of headphones, however; the ones that come with the unit are only so-so quality and don't do justice to the player's capabilities. The radio function is a nice-to-have. I used it a few times, but not very often, as I'm not a big fan of terrestrial radio. However, the tuning capabilities are nice, and there was very little static with most local radio stations.

The video playback was a bit choppy, both with the included video and with any videos I uploaded to the player. It's not so bad that it's distracting, but if you intend to get this for heavy video playing, I'd recommend going elsewhere.

The battery life is outstanding. I had a hard time draining the player - it just kept going and going. I was able to work out with it for over a week before it needed to be charged, and that includes my daughter watching videos.

This will likely become my 7 year old's mp3 player, as she's in love with it. If you're looking for a good low-cost all-around media player solution, this might be the unit for you. If you're a stickler for an iPod-like interface, you might want to look elsewhere.

product_title: BIC America F12 12-Inch 475-Watt Front Firing Powered Subwoofer
review_headline: BIC F12 sub is a great value
review_body: I just recently picked up one of these BIC F12's from Amazon after my previous subwoofer's amp died on me..  My previous sub was a 10 inch Athena model, which I picked up about 4 years ago..  Not a bad subwoofer (in fact, pretty excellent for the price at the time..), but nothing the audiophile-types would write home about, either..  But if you ask me, it was just fine, which is why I initially planned  to buy a new amp rather than buy a whole new subwoofer.  However, the amps I looked at were just a bittt too big to fit in the subwoofer box, or cost too much money for what I would get out of them (why spend $150 just to drive a nothing-fancy 10 inch sub?  Really.. 10-inches is very limiting for how deep/low the subwoofer will go.  More on that below..)    Sooo, I decided I might as well upgrade to something better..  Either a better 10 inch sub, or go up in size to a 12 inch..  I did like the compact(ish)-ness of my 10 inch Athena.  But looking at fancier 10 inch subs, they weren't particularly the same-small-ish size.  I actually considered buying an SVS or equivalent sub, but then convinced myself otherwise.  Cost/value won me over, and I knew I really shouldn't be spending all that extra money.  Reading a bunch about this subwoofer convinced me it would work just fine for me.  And the price pretty much couldn't be beat.  And now that I have it set up, it is definitely great.    Before I get into more specifics, in terms of size (one of my concerns) this sub is pretty nice.  It is only 3 inches wider than my older 10-inch sub, and pretty much exactly the same dimensions otherwise.  It's pretty straight-forward shape wise..  rectangular, with a pretty no-frills-run-of-the-mill front grill/woofer protector.    As for sound, this sub is pretty strong.  In my TV room (about 15 feet x 20 feet), straight out of the box with the subwoofer's amp set to \\"4\\", the subwoofer had the same db level at 26 hz as it did at 80 hz, but below 26 hz, it dropped off pretty quick..  And this is in a room that's completely open at both ends to the whole first floor..  So the sub can definitely push some air.  (By comparison, my 10 inch sub, in a much smaller room, could only go down to about 32 hz straight out of the box..)  I did find the BIC to be a bit \\"loud\\" (unbalanced, compared to the lower hz range..) in the 40-70hz range, but later I discovered that the spot in the room I was making measurements from had a huge gain at 60hz, so perhaps it's flatter than I measured.    After I took initial measurements (using a program called Room EQ Wizard), I equalized the sub using my DSP1124P..  And it sounds (and feels) amazing.  With the sub's amp still on the \\"4\\" setting, It now goes down to 18hz +/- 2db..  And by that I mean from 18hz to 40 hz it's 76 db +/- 2db..  That's with my normal listening volume of 65 db..  (From 40hz to 80 hz, I have it drop from 76 db to 65 db to match my mains..).  Below 18hz, though, it drops pretty fast but it's still pretty good..  15 hz is 68db.  Playing those low tones makes the room throb.  My 10 inch subwoofer could neeeever do that.  Even equalized, that one couldn't really handle 20 hz..  and it was in a much smaller room.    Seeing as I already owned an \\"equalizer\\" (the DSP1124P is about 100 dollars..), this subwoofer was a STEAL for what I was able to get out of it.  If you plan to equalize your subwoofer, this one will make for an amazing set up, that is for sure!  Even if you don't plan to equalize your sub, you're still getting a great deal on a great sub, you just won't get the really low bass as you might from more expensive subs.

product_title: Bose CineMate Series II Digital Home Theater Speaker System (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Buy these with your eyes open, and you won't be disappointed!
review_body: Wow!  That is all I have to say.  First, let me say that I am NOT an audiophile (am I the only one that thinks that name sounds sleazy).  I enjoy good sound as much as the next guy, but I would not call myself a connoisseur by any stretch of the imagination.  With that context, here is my review:    We had gotten along well with our 10-year old 27\\" Sanyo, but I convinced the wife that with the impending football season, we \\"needed\\" to upgrade to a flat screen.  We got a Vizio XVT3D474SV and were absolutely blown away by the picture.  We cannot believe we didn't make the transition to a LCD TV earlier.  There was just one problem.  Although the television speakers were good, as television speakers go, they just didn't seem to compliment the great picture.  We needed something with some more \\"depth\\" to it.    I had purchased a Panasonic 5:1 Home Theater several years ago, but I had never been happy with it.  I should have taken it back, because, I was never able to get the sound to work properly.  In fact, the volume was so low that you couldn't even listen to it comfortably.  So, I knew what I wanted (something with good sound), but I also knew what I didn't want something complicated with wires everywhere.      I didn't exactly know what system would meet my needs though... that is until we walked through Best Buy and heard the Bose Cinemate system.  We were sold immediately.  We did take the time to listen to some soundbars, but they paled in comparison.  The only other option was to go with a 5:1 or 7:1 home theater system, which we knew we didn't want (even if the price was better), so we made the plunge on the Bose system.  We also listened to the GS series.  The sound appeared to be a little fuller with the GS system, but not enough to pay an extra $200, so we stayed with the Series II, not realizing that we could adjust the bass on the woofeer.  Even if there is a difference, it is so minimal, that you won't really miss it unless you had the two systems side by side, like they were in the store.    Set up, as everyone else said, was a breeze.  It literally takes about 15 minutes from the time I opened the box until I was ready to push play.  The sound is \\"out of this world.\\"  It is so clear, even at high levels and very full.    Even an untrained ear like mine realizes this is not surround sound.  Do not be fooled by anyone who says that it is.  However, what it is, is one of the best 2:1 systems you can.  You clearly hear a separation of the sounds between the speakers.  It was just what that beautiful TV needed to show off its capabilities.      In case that wasn't enough, we also bought a 3D Blueray player to take advantage of the 3D capability.  We weren't expecting what we got the first time we popped a DVD in.  The sound was like sitting in a movie theater.  We watched \\"Salt\\" with Angelina Jolie.  I tell you, these speakers were made for action movies!    The only downfall is that there aren't many options for adjusting sound levels (i.e. adjusting the treble).  Your only controls are the bass on the woofer and the sound on the remote.  Also, the Cinemate Series II comes with its own remote that can only be used to adjust the sound.  None of my other remotes work with it.  I will spring for a Harmony 650 Universal Remote that will allow me to control all my devices with one remote (including the sound on the Bose system).  I also plan to get a set of tabletop speaker stands to raise them off the shelf they are sitting on.  I understand the sound is even better then.    I totally get the people who say they are a bit pricy.  This is a 2:1 system, and it seems like the going rate for systems like this is about $300 - $400.  These are $600.  Pricy, but in my opinion, they are in a class by themselves.  I don't regret spending the extra money.    The bottome line is that as long as you realize that you are not getting a surround sound system, and you're okay with that, you won't be disappointed.

product_title: Philips GoGear Vibe MP3 Player
review_headline: Very Good For Music, But Not Pictures And Videos
review_body:
The Good:
* Good sound quality
* Intuitive navigation and controls
* Songbird media management software

The Bad:
* Small screen makes for poor video and picture experience
* Stock earbuds are uncomfortable
* No expandable storage

Overall:

Setup: Philips has taken an approach that is meant to save cost in including the Songbird software on the device itself. This is a good choice because it both saves the one time use CD and the hassle of having to download the software. However, once installed on your PC it would be a good idea to delete it from the player so that it will not take up space for your media. While you do not have to install the software, it does make upgrading the firmware on the Vibe a cinch. For media management you can always use WMP if that floats your boat instead. Songbird borrows heavily from iTunes for its design, and it is a fully functional media management program. Once you connect the Vibe for its initial charge and upgrade the firmware, you can load media.

Music Transfer: Songbird presents a drag and drop transfer capability that is similar to using Windows Explorer. Once Songbird recognizes your Vibe, you can drag music by artist, album, song, or playlist on the \\"Music\\" area on your Vibe. During transfer you will see a spinning circle until it is complete. I find this method more intuitive than WMP's \\"Transfer List\\" for syncing. That always seemed like a clunky intermediate step that shouldn't be necessary.

Video Transfer: This works much the same way as music transfer. I did find that some of my videos would not transfer to the device. It seems that Songbird will not let you transfer videos with a resolution higher than the Vibe's 320 x 240 resolution. It's nice that it prevents you from transferring unplayable videos, but it would be nice to give the user feedback rather than make them guess.

Music Playback: While I have sound quality listed as a positive for the Vibe there is a catch. The first thing that you will need to do is throw the earbuds that come with it in the trash. I have taken to the in-ear style earbuds, but the Vibe ships with earbuds that rest outside your ear. To me this style is horribly uncomfortable, and you lose so much of the sound.

So I popped in my V-Moda Vibe (purely coincidence in name) earbuds that I had as a spare set. Once doing this I put the Vibe through its paces with a variety of music. For rock I went with Guns `N Roses' Chinese Democracy and Alice in Chains' Black Gives Way to Blue. The Vibe doesn't quite match the Creative Zen X-Fi in capturing sound detail, but it is not bad. The dialog at the beginning of Chinese Democracy was audible but at a much lower level. For rap I tried the Beastie Boys' Hot Sauce Committee, Part 2 and K'Naan's Troubadour. The bass was ample without being muddy or overbearing. Rounding things out I went with Melody Gardot's My One And Only Thrill, Dido's Life For Rent, and Johnny Cash's American II: Unchained. Across all of these styles I was pleased with the Vibe's playback. Rather than using the Equalizer settings and having to change between genres I turned on the \\"FullSound\\" feature. I expect that this will be adequate for most users. True audiophiles will be looking for a higher class device.

Display: With a mere 1.5\\" screen video playback and picture viewing is more or less a lost cause. Videos were very grainy, and the storage is better used on music. Voice Recording: While I don't have a regular need for a voice recorder, I tested out this feature on the Vibe, and it does a good job. It will record up to 4 minutes at a time which should be adequate for most quick reminders.

Value: The two main competitors to the Philips GoGear Vibe are the Sandisk Sansa Fuze+ and the Creative Zen Mozaic EZ300 - both in comparable 8 GB the Vibe has the smallest screen at 1.5 \\" vs. 1.8\\" and 2.4\\" respectively. The Fuze+ also has a microSD card expansion slot. It really comes down to how important videos and microSD are to you. All things being equal you are probably safe making a price based decision.

Overall: The Philips GoGear Vibe is a solid mp3 music player. It is easy to use, and it comes with a solid media manager application in Songbird. product_title: Fatman iTube Valve Dock Mk. II
review_headline: Tiny HYBRID -- not Tube -- Amp with Decent Sound at a Premium Price
review_body: This attractive, compact amp is not a valve (or tube) amp, in the strictest sense of the word, but really a hybrid amp -- one that uses tubes in the preamp stage, but for its actual amplification relies on solid state technology.    There's nothing wrong with that, of course, but ads stressing the fact that it uses tubes seem to play on the current infatuation with tubes to lull ill-informed consumers into paying more than they should for this sort of amp.    For $450, please be aware you could get an actual tube amp -- one that will sound worlds better, have more power, and be more versatile.    A quick bit of googling for Dared MP5, Sonic Integrity, and the like will reveal that all these hybrids were built in the same place as the Fatman and just re-branded: in Asia, they are all quite inexpensive.    With some shopping around, you should be able to find one of these here in the US for around $200 -- still more than these cost in Asia, but much more in line with what the amp is probably worth in the US marketplace.      I paid less than $200 for a brand new one. I enjoyed it for a brief period of time, but never found its sound particularly engaging, either with speakers or with headphones. It didn't do anything glaringly wrong, but it didn't add the tube magic that I had hoped it would, even with high quality NOS tubes substituted for the low-quality stock tubes.     While well-built and quite attractive to look at, this amp is essentially a novelty, because it is not powerful enough to drive most mass market speakers: prospective purchasers should either be prepared to invest in some highly-efficient speakers to do it justice, or plan on just enjoying its adequate headphone output.     The matching docking station is very, very cheaply made -- lightweight and plasticky (unlike the amp itself) -- and the remote control is a joke.     Please do yourself a favor and shop around before considering pressing the \\"Add To Cart\\" button. There are many more sonically-satisfying and serious amps out there at its price point.    Happy listening!    PS -  The two tubes in the front are the preamp tubes: they can be easily swapped out to upgrade the sound of the amp. The larger one in the back merely provides a visual representation of how hard the amp is being driven/how close it is to clipping. (In other words, it does not influence the sound of the amp at all, so there is no point in trying to upgrade the larger rear tube.)

product_title: Maha PowerEx 950 mAh AAA IMEDION "Ready When You Are." Rechargeable Batteries, 4 Pack
review_body: If you find yourself going through Alkaline batteries and spending a fortune, it is time to convert to Hybrid NiMH. Imedion batteries are kind of a combination of Alkaline and Nickel Metal Hydride (NiMH). If you have used regular NiMH (not hybrid) in the past, you might have asked yourself why did I waste my money because they discharge so fast when not being used. Hybrid NiMH are completely different: they will hold a charge when not in use, so you can have spares ready to go into a device when you need them. These do not have memory effect like NiCd. All in all a good battery. Comparable to Eneloop, but cheaper and have more power. BE CAREFUL: there are some devices that require the full power of an Alkaline battery and won't work with these.

product_title: Acoustic Research Rotating Docking System for iPod
review_headline: Works Great and Easy To Use
review_body:
This speaker system is designed for the iPod, iPad, and iPhone. Basically you plug your iPod, iPad, or iPhone into the jack and you are ready to go. There is a special holder to support each item. There is great volume and a 3D option to make the music seem more real. If you have a newer iPod, iPad, or iPhone, I'm sure even the phones will work in it, you have the option of using the speakers as an alarm and as a radio. I have an older iPod so I couldn't tell you how well this feature works. You can also rotate the iPad or iPhone for viewing video. But, once again, I don't have one so I don't know how well this works.

I also plugged my computer into the speakers. It was really easy to do and I still had great sound. The speakers gave the computer a surround sound feeling. Since I used a audio jack, I'm sure you can use the speakers with other mp3 players or anything else that essentially has a head phone jack.

When I first used the speaker out of the box, the remote control was a little finicky. But I replaced the battery and that problem went away. The only other problem I had was the holder that you put your device into was just off enough that I couldn't use it. I'm sure that problem was that I have such an old ipod that it was not compatible. But it still works fine plugging my iPod into the jack without support. I rotated it and had no problem.

If you are looking for some speakers for your iPod, iPad, iPhone, mp3 players, or anything else that you need external speakers for, buy this. It is definitely worth the money. It's very easy to use and you get great sound quality.

Shawn Kovacich
Author of the Achieving Kicking Excellence book and DVD series.

product_title: Sony Dash Personal Internet Viewer
review_headline: Steer clear -- can't even get it to register
review_body: So, I bought it and was psyched because I figured it was a cool gadget to have.  Other reviewers said it streamed nicely with Netflix and Facebook.  I needed a new alarm clock and figured I'd give it a shot as, heck, it was about $99 (cheaper through other sellers, but shipping killed the deal with them).    So, it arrived and I was psyched.  Looked good.  Powered up and did all the fancy intro... Connected perfectly to my wireless network and immediately did a software update which seemed to go flawlessly.    Went to Sony's website to register the product because you can't load any apps or do anything with it until you register.  That's where it went wrong.  Went online, registered for the account, entered the registration code and their site clearly crashed.  Tried for several hours, same result.  \\"Sony can't complete your request at this time.  Try again later.\\"  So, I used the online chat support.. The tech asked me some basic questions -- \\"Have you tried other browsers\\" etc.  Then said the site is having a problem and to try later.  Great.    So, here I am several hours later and still nothing.  Can't load a single application on it.  Can't see anything other than what's loaded stock.  Tried going to the site again and same errors.    Great concept, but with support like this and clearly not having luck registering it, it's going back for a refund.  Let them work out the kinks and I might try again, but for now, I'll pass.

product_title: Cheetah Mounts APTMSB Flat Screen TV Wall Mount Bracket Designed for 32"-55" Plasma LED LCD TV (Actually Fits 20-55" TVs) Includes Free 10' Braided High Speed HDMI Cable With Ethernet
review_headline: Get your own wall anchors, included hardware is useless
review_body: The bracket itself is fine and very sturdy. The integrated level is a nice touch as is the included separate 3 direction level. Once you get the main bracket on the wall, all is good.    Pros:    1) Solid construction  2) Easy to put Flat Panel TV on or take off the bracket  3) If you can use the lag bolts to mount it into wall studs, those work fine  4) Inexpensive    Cons:    1) Other mounting hardware    My issue is that the way my daughters room wall studs are setup where I wanted to put the TV, I could only use one lag bolt. I needed to use wall anchors for the other three mounting points. It turns out that the toggle bolts that they include do not fit through the mounting holes of the wall bracket. Even if you unscrew the toggle bolts and then pre-screw them onto the bracket, you can't pound the toggle through the wall because there isn't enough clearance for the flaps to fully fold back and clear the back of the sheetrock.    Basically, the toggle bolts for drywall mounting are completely useless. The wall anchors they provide are not much better since they are too long for typical 1/2\\" sheetrock. The spines that hold them in place are too far down so that if you put them in flush to the wall, they spin in place when you try to tighten the lag bolts.    2) The tilt set screws use a dumbbell-like bar, but on one of the TV brackets tightening it had the bar in a 90 degree position relative to the back of the TV so it stuck out. Trouble is that this bracket is very close to the wall and there wasn't enough clearance. So, I had to really crank it down just to get it to an angle where the TV would go on the wall. I was afraid of stripping the set screw.     So, the long and short of it is that the bracket itself is OK, but go out and get several heavy duty drywall anchors at your local hardware store because the included drywall anchors and toggle bolts are useless.

product_title: BOQARI Q1 Metal Earbuds Headphones with Travel Case
review_headline: Much better than some reviewers would lead you to think
review_body: These earbuds had been in my saved shopping cart for a while, and previous to having finally purchased them I purchased the highly acclaimed Klipsch S-4's which haven't disappointed with their excellent fit and sound.  They are truly exceptional.  Well, when the price of the Boqari's dropped below $25.00 I had to bite, so-to-speak.  I thought, even if the negative reviews are supported (and some of them are scathing) then the Boqari's would be relegated to occasional use, like listening to a dialogue-filled movie or youtube video.  All they would need to do is have decent mid-range capability and feel comfortable.  Well, when they arrived in a very nice box, zippered leather case and replaceable buds to fit a child up to an elephant I thought, wow, now that's a nice presentation at least.  But it's the sound that was most surprising, even without the recommended burn-in period.  It's solidly coherent from top to bottom, and the midrange is clear.  If I could envision a frequency response curve it would be even and not ragged, with no discernable peaks over-emphasising one or another part of the sound spectrum, and as I said, this is my immediate impression after having used the klipsch S-4's few months.  Though I still prefer the Klipsch's--which have only gotten better with use--I am also mightily impressed with these Boqari's, especially at the price I paid.  I must admit, however, there aren't enough features which would warrant the MSRP of $299.00; that is, unless it was sold at an exclusive Beverly Hills or NYC Boutique, but even those who can afford to pay that much for earbuds would enjoy the sounds they produce.  At 1/3 the MSRP or lower, these are a great deal, and at 1/6th they are almost a no-brainer.

product_title: Apple iPod nano 16 GB Silver (6th Generation) Discontinued Model (in White Box)
review_body: I have had this nano for a little over a month now and haven't had any problems with it so far.  I have read many reviews about ppl complaining of the features that it lost to previous generations.  This nano was clearly made for those who wanted something compact like the shuffle and with a little more features.  It is perfect for those who are on the go.  I think it is perfect for exercise.  You can tap the sleep/wake button twice to shuffle to the next song and the volume controls are on the top also so you don't have to actually wake it up and skip to the next song.  The clip is great so you don't have to worry about an armband anymore which I was getting sick of using and constantly buying b/c they would wear out every couple months.  I don't know why so many people are worried about the lack of video camera or whatever it is lacking compared to the previous generation, but why would you want a nano if that is what you wanted.  It seems like it was pointless to even integrate that option on something that was meant to be small, that are much better options if that is what you wanted.  As long as the hinge on the clip doesn't wear out or come loose i will continue to be very happy with this product.  It does everything I was looking for in a nano.  It is small, easy to use, plenty of features, and great for exercise.

product_title: Philips HN 110 Folding Noise-Canceling Headphones
review_headline: I was surprised how well they worked
review_body: I bought these headphones just before I took a long flight to the South Pacific.  I had been told that that plane I was going to fly on would be very-very noisy and that I shouldn't count on getting much sleep.  To the contrary, once I turned my headphones on, all I remember was a low hum from the engines and I was able to sleep very well.  Further, during the subsequent month that I spent hopping from place to place on smaller planes (in one case I was on a prop plane) I was never more than just peripherally aware that the engines were making any noise at all.  I am not saying that the headphone completely cut out the noise around me, no headphones can do that, but they made the noise more tolerable and not as nerve jangling.  To be honest, I didn't comprehend just how loud some of the engines were until I took them off mid-flight and realized just how much noise had been masked.  This a wonderful product and I have recommended it to several of my friends.  They fold up very nicely so as not to take up much space, and they fit snuggly over my ears.  I know that others have stated that they were uncomfortable, but I didn't have any problems at all.

product_title: Terk VR1 Automatic TV Volume Controller
review_body: Around 2003 I purchased a \\"Terk VR-1\\" volume regulator. This unit used slick DSP technology and worked well.     I recently purchased five \\"Terk VR-1\\" units from Amazon.com for myslef and friends and received units with the same make and model number in an Audiovox cardboard box. A friend told me these were not the same, so I opened the new unit to discover that no original Terk DSP circuitry was used in the Audiovox-but Terk labeled-unit, but rather inexpensive and poorly operating analog circuitry is used now. To me this is misleading to downright illegal to use not only the same Terk name, but the same model number for a product that operates in an entirely different, much simpler (and in my opinion worse) principle.    While this may control volume, it is not nearly as good as the original DSP based \\"Terk VR-1\\" from years ago. The name and model number is misleading-kinda like asking for a hamburger and getting a hot-dog.    Dan  Natick, MA

review_body: I was hesitant to get these stands because of the negative reviews, but did not find anything else online that looked how I wanted.  I figured they were cheap enough to risk it. The biggest flaw is the interior design of the tubing; there are cross-welded bars that make feeding the wire down the tube an exercise in patience and anger management.    All said and done, they look fantastic and are very solid.  I'm using them with small speakers (Boston Acoustics CS2310B) so the plates are actually slightly larger than the speakers themselves.    I say go for it!

product_title: Jwin Jhv100B Closed-Type Pro Digital Studio Monitor Headphones
review_body: I'm not a fan of any type of earbud, so I got a set of these to listen to music in my cubicle at work...I gotta say, for ~$10, these things rock...I'm certainly no audiophile, but the sound on these is really good, there's a good amount of bass (which is what seperates great sound from the \\"just OK\\" sound - IMHO). I love the over-the-ear design as it blocks out almost all the external room noise, and they fit well with not too much pressure on the ole noggin, but still feel like they are not going to fall off your head. If I had to have one complaint it would be trying to adjust the volume using the two dials on each earpiece - you have to just rely on the sound in your head as opposed to having the dials in the same place on each.  anyways - I liked these so much I bought a second set for home!  seriously - for $10, how can you go wrong?

review_body: First, how can you not like a company named Jamo(YAH-MOE)? This is a Danish company better known in Europe(YURRUP). This has to be one of the best speaker deals on the planet at twice the price! The fronts have a 1\\" silk tweeter, two 5\\" mids, and an 8\\" side woofer. And what a range!  The Audessy set-up on my receiver set the crossover with these things at 50hz.  The systems mids are strong, the highs are sweet, and the lows leave little for the sub to do.  Although you will want to use a sub with movies.  It still has some work to do.  I bought a Polk PSW10 sub that works just fine for my set-up.  I'd call this a warm to neutral system.    When I opened the carton, I was astonished at how beautiful these speakers were.  Better looking than the pictures. product_title: Skullcandy SCS-SCBP3.5 Skullcrushers Subwoofer Stereo Headphones
review_body: I'll keep this simple:    1) They are good for bass, but little else. With even my untrained ears, I easily notice that the highs and mids are very unimpressive. They are very murky, not clear and crisp like they should be. If you look on the side of the box, you can see that the makers of these don't deny this--there is a graph showing the bass maxed out and the mids and highs suffering...    2) They are somewhat attractive and comfortable. I like the way they look. I have pretty big ears, and I barely notice these until a couple hours of listening. This being said they are also somewhat warm. As others have noticed, the bass amplifier on the cord is kind of annoying and heavy. I think just letting it hang there would eventually damage the product. So you constantly have to worry about it falling down and such.    In short, I wouldn't buy them if I had another chance. Instead, I would of bought the Audio-Technica ATH-M30 Professional Headphones. They're hardly more expensive, and are obviously of much higher quality. Rattling your head with dubstep music IS fun for a while (it makes your ears tickle, lol), but I listen to a wide variety of music. Genres such as blues don't sound nearly like they should.

product_title: Optoma 3D-XL Converter Box for 3D Video and Gaming (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: Without the 3D-XL i wouldn't be able to play High Def 3D movies from my PS3 to my projector (Optoma HD67). Or game in 3D.  Both 3D Blu-rays and SBS (Side-By-Side) files work flawlessly. There is only one alternative to this box, but i see this as the better option as it includes a pair of top quality 3D glasses, plus an additional HDMI input (total of 2) to allow multiple sources which you can switch between with a push of a button.  You must already have a \\"3D-ready\\" projector for the 3D-XL to work. \\"3D-Ready\\" just means that the picture refreshes at a 120 Hz rate as opposed to your typical 50 or 60Hz. Most PC's with an NVidia Graphics card will be able to play 3D content with a 3D ready projector without the 3D-XL, however the 3D-XL is required to use a blu-ray player or PS3 for 3D content.  I would definitely recommend this paired with a lower end 3D ready projector as a cheaper alternative to an expensive 3D projector.

product_title: Onkyo TX - NR609 7.2 Channel Network THX Certified A/V Receiver (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: Fairly easy to setup, rather confusing to operate.  I have 3 HDMI devices: Sony BD, Cable box (Scientific Atlanta 4250HDC), and a PC with HDMI out.    HDMI Passthru (when in Standby mode)  Default setting is not setup for HDMI passthru. You need to go to Hardware setup and then choose the HDMI option where you specify to turn on the \\"Passthru\\" function.  I did this and there was no sound from the TV.  I went back to the HDMI set up and there is an option to have \\"TV Audio\\" ON/OFF. I turned it ON.  The receiver would not detect the cable box all the time. (actually it does not detect it most of the time. I have to turn the receiver on, and then select cable.  It does detect the other two HDMI devices ok and the sound does come out of the TV.  However, the \\"TV Sound\\" option disables all digital sound. This means that even when you turn the receiver ON, it does not play the sound through the receiver. You need to go to \\"Hardware Setup\\" and turn OFF the \\"TV sound\\" in order for the receiver to produce sound.  What is even stranger is that, when \\"TV sound\\" is ON, even the music that comes through DLNA / Internet is played only through the TV and not the receiver.    Thus, the Passthru function is useless: in order to hear anything you need to turn \\"TV Audio\\" On, which in turns strips the receiver of all of its sound processing functionality!     DLNA  It does not play FLAC or Ogg Vorbis through the network. Only from a locally inserted USB device.    Telephone Support  I called Onkyo support to verify that I was not missing something. They confirmed that it is supposed to work like this.  The particular person I got on the phone was not helpfull, did not understand the issues (unless repeated 3 times), and not knowlegable about the product.

review_headline: Great sound... but too fragile! Recommend Miles Davis Tributes with better warranty
review_body: I've tried most high end headphones on the market and at first i thought these were the perfect pair but realized i was wrong...  I tried them for the first time and was sold since it was at the time the best pair of headphones I had heard. For some reason they picked up a weird buzzing sound on my samsung mp3 player and was the only pair of headphones it happened with. I eventually got a new Ipod touch which got rid of the buzzing but I lost the great bass I had from the Samsung player.   One of the other other selling points was the 1. Sound isolation, compact size, light weight, and overall comfort.  well the sound isolation is no where near as good as my Altec Lansing UHP606 or UHP 336 headphones which also do a claimed 26db. Also rarely does the size actually matter unless you are trying to wear them under a helmet like i was but due since the sound isolation was not up to par, I preferred the altec's when riding.   They are very comfortable but for some reason they seemed to really hurt my hears after about an hour or two. I'm not sure why since most other soft ear tips don't bother me but these do have a different shape than many of the other headphones I have.   Quality: after only a year of occasional use and being babied, the cord broke once after being snagged. Actually severed the wire in half. Every time this has ever happened with other headhphones they just pull out of the ear, but UE has a reputation for weak cords and that is Very TRUE. Read other reviews, these are very fragile. I called UE and they said i was out of luck.   To replace my high end headphones i bought a pair of Monster Miles Davis tribues and they sound amazing! Great highs and bass and the sound is controlled by the several different sets of tips. some create better highs while others better bass. PLUS a free replacement if YOU break them. They were on sale from amazon for $250 compared to the msrp of 400 and at that price its cheaper to buy one and break them and get a free replacement than to buy 2 pairs of UE 700's if you break them, which you eventually will.

review_body: I was referred to Ultimate Ears by a friend of mine after asking around for some quality earbuds. product_title: Logitech Harmony One Universal Remote with Color Touchscreen (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
The Harmony 1 remote is one of the higher end Harmony universal remotes with a nice touch sensitive screen. My gestalt is that it is built a but more durably than my old 880s (I've had 3, still use one that's on it's last legs that's about 4 years old, had one replaced and another that just died after a few years). My set up with the software transfered all my old 880 settings to my Harmony 1--that was a really nice surprise and it saved me a ton of time for setting up the new one.

I noticed right away, like with my 880 remotes, that the charging base was a bit finicky. I would have to wiggle the remote a bit to get it to finally lock in to the charging mode. I did get 2-3 full charges, but last night, despite fiddling with the thing for about 10 minutes, I couldn't get it to sustain contact adequate to charge the remote.

Today I called the remote customer support, for some reason the base issues are handled by a separate section (they're common enough for their own sub-department! Perhaps a design change is in order?) I ended up having to call a different number, then transfered to yet a 3rd person. Despite the obvious nature of the problem the tech guy was forced to work through an algorithm on his computer that kept telling him it was a battery problem when it clearly was an issue with the base making contact with the remote.

Ultimately he was able to get things entered properly and they are sending out a new base AND remote (not sure why both, seems an expensive waste to me) under my warranty. Hopefully the new one will work as designed. Honestly I'd rather have a regular plug-in charger for the reliability and to get the space occupying base out of the way. I believe a complete redesign is in order.

product_title: Sony RMNU1 HomeShare Universal Remote (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Not so good as a dedicated IR remote
review_body: I was really looking forward to receiving this remote as I had an RM-AV3000 and loved it (sadly it stopped working after several years).  However, after living with this remote for a few days, I'm very disappointed.  It is easy and somewhat intuitive to setup and start using, however, this remote lacks the ability to input a code specific to the device you're trying to program, like the RM-AV3000 did.  As an alternative, you choose a specific type ("type 1, type 2, etc.), after you choose the manufacturer of the device your programming, and rarely do all the functions work as they should, so you wind up using the learn feature anyway.  I would have liked to have the ability to input manufacturer specific codes into the remote.  My Plasma HDTV made by panasonic uses dedicated buttons for ON and OFF- this remote, as far as I can tell, does not have the ability use specific ON/OFF commands for powering up/down your device, rather it uses a generic 'power toggle', which is fine for most modern electronics, except those that use dedicated buttons for on and off.  The biggest problem I have with this remote is how slow it is.  Using the activity command (watch TV, for instance), it takes a full 15 seconds to turn on my TV, cable box and receiver (My harmony 880 does it in 1/4 the time- the RM-AV3000 was even faster)- this is completely unacceptable.  Not only that, but there's a lag-time after all components turn on, and when the volume control starts working.  One can adjust the delay between commands, but the fastest delay is 1 second, which by today's standards is terribly slow.  My other gripe was the very poor IR signal strength- you'd think this category of remote would provide a very strong IR signal, however, in my brief experience, it does not.  The final complaint- my AV receiver is made by Sony (a mere 2 years old), yet, upon programming the RMNU1 it didn't work!  I had to learn every function of my Sony receiver to the RMNU1, even though the instructions say it's 100% compatible with Sony electronics. I find it difficult to believe this is truly the case, so perhaps it was user error, although all my other devices seemed to work just fine.  Overall, I really liked the size, ergonomics, and weight of the RMNU1, but it has shortcomings that for me, make it a painful device to use.  I'll be returning this remote and searching for something different.  It's too bad, because I really wanted to like it.

product_title: Monster MCC AVL 200 Central and Lighting Control Revolution 200 (Black)
review_body: As someone who simply cannot step back from buying new remotes from time to time (women's shoes are my remotes) I was very happy to see that Monster's AVL200 is being sold at a reasonable price at last. I already used the AVL300 before I exchanged it for a Nevo Q50, so I've been familiar with Monster-remotes for a while.  Whereas the AVL300 was based on Harmony-technology and software the AVL200 was developed by Universal Electronics who are also responsible for the Nevo-range and the Acoustic Research ARRX18G Xsight (or the One4all Xsight Touch like it is called in Europe). Therefore it also uses the EZ-RC web-based configuration-tool and the Universal Electronic database of IR-codes.  So how do I like the AVL200 compared to the AVL300 and the Acoustic Research? To be honest not that much. The AVL200 has a very strong focus on the integration of Z-Wave-technologie for home-automization. It features dedicated buttons to select light-scenes for several situations which is nice as long as you are looking for a home-automization-controller.  However, as a regular universal remote that is supposed to replace all those separate remotes of all your home-theater devices it fails because of the absence of useful hard keys or a suitable display for putting functions on virtual keys. Yes, the AVL200 does have a display but it only displays 3 lines of text. Functions have to be chosen by scrolling up or down a command-list and selected by pressing OK. Please imagine all the functions that your AV-receiver has and then imagine how long you will have to scroll down if you simply would like to select the \\"THX\\"-mode etc. This is simply anything but comfortable.  So how does it compare to the AVL300 and the Acoustic Research? Well, to be honest, as a home-theater-controller both do a better job. They both come with a color-display that can be configured quite freely to display the buttons you use most often. They both can use RF-IR-transmitters so that you can control devices thatare hidden in closets. They also both come with rechargeable batteries and a charging cradle. And the AVL300 also offers Z-Wave-compatibility.  So what remains in favor of the AVL200? Not much I'm afraid to say. I ordered it because I like its console-like form-factor. However, on pictures it does look much better than in reality. The AVL200 is pretty small (could have been a little bit larger for me as it was supposed to stay on our couch-table) and the high-gloss surface is not really my cup of tea. It looks pretty pretty cheap but that's a matter of personal taste I guess.  Bottom-line: Would I buy the AVL200 again? I don't think so! Is it worth its original price of US$249? Definitely not! Is the AVL200 for you? Only if you like to use your Z-Wave-products with dedicated hard-buttons and controlling your home-theater properly has a low priority. Everyone else might be better off with a Harmony (or an AVL300 if you can still get it for a low price) or an Acoustic Research.

review_headline: The only speakers/dock I'll ever need.
review_body:
The Fidelio docking speaker for the iPad, iPod, iPhone, etc is a sleek little racetrack shaped set of rechargeable speakers with built in dock to support various other gadgets.

The controls are minimal. There is an on-off sliding switch at the back, a + and - button on the front for volume control, and a \\"connect\\" button with the bluetooth icon. As the gadgets you would dock in these speakers have their own play, ff, rw, pause, etc buttons you really don't need more than that. If you desire, you can download the Fidelio app from the App Store on any of your iApple devices that connect to the App Store. The Fidelio app is cool, and allows for different sound profiles to maximize sound quality. There is also a clock and the same types of controls that iTunes gives you. I find that I typically skip over the Fidelio app, as the sound out of the box is just fine with me- warm and rich and clear. My son likes the finer control offered by the app and when he has snagged the speakers and brought them to his room, he typically plays with the app.

What I really like about this is the size and portability. The weight isn't heavy but it definitely feels sturdy and won't tip over with the addition of an iPad. I keep the speakers/dock in my kitchen, plugged in and ready to go. However, when I'm at my work table and the boys are rowdy, I'll unplug it and put it right on the table. Going outside? I can take it with me so I can listen to music while puttering about on our patio tending to my container garden. It is very convenient. If toting it for longer trips, there is a cover which attaches to cover the dock connectors and speaker holes and keep them clean and functional.

Overall, I like that everyone in our family (each with a different iGadget) can use this. We were using an 11 year old Bose Wave CD/AM/FM monstrosity before this and one ipod would use the apple-made dock and another would need that unplugged and reconnected directly, and having the ipad just sitting on the counter, while we are busy in the kitchen baking and cooking, seemed like a disaster waiting to happen. This also conveniently has bluetooth connection, which is a definite plus as I'm forever needing my ipod touch in the middle of a song, while working on various projects. It's nice being able to pick it up and hold it in my hand, and even leave the room for a few minutes with it, without disrupting the music. The bluetooth is not something that was on my list of \\"needs\\" for new speakers, but it is definitely a handy feature, and the sound is equal (according to my ears) to the sound quality when it is directly docked.

I have tried other docks (I've tried a couple of the Philips ones) and this is the first one that really fits our needs for quality sound and portability and versatility without any negatives coming to mind. review_headline: Meh. I wouldn't buy them again
review_body: I bought these based on all of the positive reviews here on Amazon.    When i received the product, it appeared very nice. The packaging portrayed quality, and the fit and finish of the product itself is very nice. If you put these in a display case, you could easily fool your friends into thinking you paid $150+ for these headphones. But that's about where the excitement ends.    The hard-edged metal design causes the edge of the bud to dig into my ear lobe. Even though the rubber nub fits nicely into my ear, the chunky design of the bud body forces me to pull them out after every 1-2 hours to let the blood flow back through my earlobe (I can keep my old $40 philips headphones in all day).     The good news is that when they're in there, they stay pretty snug.     The cable used is thick and noisy. When the cable shifts around, you can hear it in the headphone -- I definitely don't plan on using these during any kind of running or jogging. If the cord wrapped behind the neck, that would be nice too.     As far as the sound, it's certainly not knock-your-socks-off good. The sounds is clear, but the lows are muddy/nonexistent/nonexciting and the mids are so-so. Not sure if I'm not sophisticated enough, but I just don't understand what is so great about this sound. I've had other headphones where I start uncontrollably bobbing my head to the music because the sound is just so good (one $40 and one $35), but I just don't see that happening with these.    As far as customer service goes, don't buy these if you plan on returning them. I started the process, but it seems like a pain (direct with the vendor. You have to log a \\"ticket\\" and then follow up, then ship the item). I just kept them for use as back-ups. product_title: Sennheiser Dynamic High Grade Performance Premiere Headphones
review_body: Take this review for what it's worth: I don't consider myself an audiophile but I do listen to a ton of music. After owning several pairs of cheapish Sony headphones for years I got tired of them always breaking and having to replace them once a year. After some research I settled on the 595s and I'm glad I did. They are without a doubt the best sounding headphones I've ever owned, and they are really comfortable to boot. The clarity of songs I'd been listening to for years is insane and it is easy to pick up very subtle details in songs. I don't know anything about if they are \\"warm\\" or lack bass or anything that other people have reviewed, I just know to me they sound damn good.  After owning the headphones for 2 years one side would randomly go out. Not sure what it was, definitely wasn't the cable as I tried every type of moving it around to try and reproduce the sound going out, it was always random. I never abused these or did anything crazy with them so this was kinda troubling to me. I sent them back to Sennheiser and they told me they were not repairable (but never told me what went wrong with them) and offered me a brand new pair for $60. I accepted that since I was kinda addicted to these. I only paid $150 for these to begin with (not from Amazon) so it was worth it to me.  2 years after that the second pair is still going strong after daily use (literally every day) so hopefully the first problem was just a fluke. Some people have commented that the build quality is somewhat cheap on them and I can kinda see that as they definitely couldn't stand up to being stepped on or something like that, but the occasional drop on the floor should be OK.  When I first got these I used them at work but I work in an area with other people and they definitely could hear what I was listening to, so eventually I bought a pair of Sennheiser 448s to use at work (since I needed something closed) The 448s are somewhat annoying to use since they aren't nearly as comfortable and they don't sound anywhere near as good. But that was to be expected. I suppose I need to find something comparable to the 595s that has closed ears (please comment with any recommendations!)  So if you are looking for a pair of headphones to use at home that isn't going to completely break the bank then I'd go ahead and pull the trigger. product_title: Sony Portable Heavy Duty CD Radio Boombox Speaker System
review_headline: Speaking softly not all it's cracked up to be
review_body:
\\"Speak softly and carry a big stick; you will go far.\\" - President Teddy Roosevelt

I've had the ZS-H10CP for a couple of years now, and am generally satisfied. It does look rugged, though I haven't dropped it onto the concrete slab of a building site to see what comes off. It does seem to be moisture resistant, though I haven't sprayed it with a high pressure nozzle. The tonal quality is satisfactory. The knobs and buttons are uncomplicated - suitable for even the most ham-fisted of operators wearing construction gloves. The radio - AM and FM - and the CD player both meet my requirements, especially during college football season when the USC Trojans are playing.

However ...

I never cease to be surprised by the highest sound level that I can achieve by turning the volume knob all the way up. It seems remarkably low, especially as the device is billed as a \\"jobsite boombox.\\" Oh, puhleeze.

Mind you, I use the device out in the yard as I water and trim the shrubbery and admire the koi fish in the pond. Under those circumstances, I can hear it perfectly well. I mean, however, that I can't imagine the Real Men on a construction site being able to hear their Mozart CDs over the bedlam din of power saws, drills, nail guns and cement mixers.

Look, I just want the ability to blow the neighbors' windows out with Neil Diamond's \\"Brother Loves Traveling Salvation Show\\" at 7:00 AM on a Sunday morning if I'm so inclined. But I can't, and the ZS-H10CP's deficiency in this regard makes me feel somewhat diminished.

review_headline: THE BEST I've found for the price.
review_body: Let me get this out of the way..the Metalix series is available in 5 or 6 colors and are all listed as seperate products on Amazon. I have the Black/Silver but just chose this product page since it only had 1 review.  When looking for an overall performance indicator ALL the reviews and ratings should be averaged together.    Ok now onto the review. Construction wise these buds are ALL METAL. The ENTIRE speaker housing, the lead in from the cord/housing, AND the plug. If all my full size headphones were made of 100% METAL I'd be a happy camper.....but plastic reigns supreme from a cost perspective on MOST headphone products.     For the street price of $5 at Big Lots these deserve at LEAST a 4 star rating. The only reason they don't get 5 stars is their lack of performance on Rock, Hard Rock, Jazz and...... Metal....this is the ironic part.     On everything else especially Rap and Electronic music they're EXCELLENT. With a 13 OHM impedance it doesn't take much to pound tremendous amounts of bass into your skull. Theres another review on Amazon that gave a 2 star rating because of the cord slipping off her MP3 player???? You should NEVER wrap a cord around an MP3 player or cell phone. If you need to keep the cord in check use a wire tie.     These are my go-to buds when it's T-Shirt time and I don't want to mess up the hair. I know high quality sound and if these are used for Rap(which IS NOT music), or any type of well recorded/mastered electronic music they are very satisfying. If anyones familiar with Dubstep genre of music some tracks contain some VERY powerful bass. The Metalix reproduce it all without missing a beat. The bass quality might not be as good as my Audio Technica ATH-A700 cans....but I'm NEVER left with the desire to change to another set of buds or cans. I'm amazed that these little things can produce so much bass!!!    Now on to my settings I use just for these buds. In Foobar2000 I lower all lower bands up to 880 hz and slightly boost the high frequencies from 10 khz and up.    The sound signature of these buds are VERY bass heavy which muddies the midrange and treble response. My EQ method gives a much flatter response.    So to sum up don't judge these buds by just plugging them into your MP3 player and hitting the loudness setting. Spend a bit of time EQing and you'll find as I have, that with some thoughtful EQing they can be a VERY satisfying set of buds.....all for $5.

product_title: Tecsun PL-606 Digital PLL Portable AM/FM Shortwave Radio with DSP, Black
review_headline: A great small radio, DSP is innovative!
review_body: I've had the Tecsun 606 for two weeks.  What I like is that it is a small design, uses two AA cells instead of 4, and has competent electronics and performance.  It wasn't until I read a review where a user said he liked the \\"ETM\\" feature that I decided to read the manual for the first time, and I agree.  The Tecsun ETM feature is very good.  You press down the ETM button once you are on SW, AM or FM, and the radio will scan the entire range and find stations with enough signal to be useable.  On SW this means the radio starts at about 2.3 MHz and goes to the end of the 21. MHz band.  Once it finishes, taking on SW about 2 minutes, you then use the tuning dial to select the stations that ETM found.  My experience is that ETM finds stations that you would stop on if you were band scanning, and that it does not skip over useable signals.  The manual of course suggests you use the ETM scan several times a day on SW to compensate for reception conditions, and this is what all of us SW listeners do anyway.    The sound of the radio is not hi fi, but its performance is excellent.  On AM it does a very good job, but sure with a longer AM bar antenna it could do better.  On FM it is fine and SW is very good to excellent.  No SSB.  There is no keypad tuning on the radio, so if you don't want to use ETM, you need to band select and then use the tuning knob on the side to get the frequency you want.  The bandwidths of 1 3 and 6 khz are fine.    I've found I'm using ETM all the time now since I have gained confidence that ETM will indeed find listenable signals.  You have to try it to convince yourself that ETM is credible and not some kind of cheesy scanning scheme.  I think ETM is well done.  If I had an issue, it is this:  the whip antenna will become lose and will need to be tightened using a very small phillips screwdriver.  At least on my radio this happens.  Time will tell if this radio's tuning and volume dials will survive hundreds of uses per day, but overall, I thinkthis is a great small two battery radio and for new shortwave listeners especially, as well as us old crusty ones, ETM is a nice gift!   Fidelity will not blow you away, but the performance is great, with low power consumption and a competent design using the latest DSP technology from a US company.  It's a buy in my view and a great emergency radio in a pinch.

review_body: I've been using this for the past month now, and I've gotten more and more pleased with it as time goes on. Externally, it's a very simple device: the single port (headphone jack with threads to screw into the base of the cord) accommodates either the headphones or the USB-to-headphone-jack charging and data cord. The power button on the side also serves to switch between shuffle and linear modes (songs are stored by the date they were transferred onto the player). A short press of the button changes modes and toggles the button's LED from blue to red; a long press turns it off. The five other buttons control volume, change the track, and play/pause. It's worthwhile to learn the position of the buttons by memory, so you can adjust it without looking.     They recommend you thread your goggle strap through the brackets but I haven't gotten that to work very well. Instead, I attach it to the shoulder strap of my swimsuit. Sometimes one end still pops off. It might be less of a problem if the brackets were not in the same plane as the main body, but sort of sticking out to the back instead. review_body:
I have long been a fan of Cambridge Soundworks and Klipsch for my speaker needs. I wasn't able to find anything at Cambridge Soundworks that I liked, and I really didn't want to spend $1,500 on my game room for speakers and a receiver. I bought these based on the high reviews here, and overall I think this is a great value.

My only gripe is the center channel speaker should, IMO, be a bit bigger to handle the amount of sound that center channels need for most movies and TV. I ended up using an older Cambride center channel, which measurably improved the dialogue in movies.

The satellites are about what you would expect. They are bright, don't have a ton of mid-range, but are more than serviceable for a system at this price. They obviously aren't going to perform as well as large speakers that cost 10x as much, but they are excellent for this price point.

The sub-woofer is why I am giving this 5 stars. You can easily spend more on a subwoofer alone that doesn't sound as good as this one. The bass is tight, it doesn't distort, and it doesn't overwhelm the satellites either when playing music or watching a bass-heavy movie like Avatar or most of what Hollywood puts out these days. The bass is there, but not overpowering.

I paired this with an inexpensive Yamaha receiver and my 7 year-old Panasonic plasma and I had my entire game room up and running for less than $1,000. Not bad at all.

These aren't going to satisfy the serious audiophile (or the poseur audiophile who thinks they need really expensive and exotic looking speakers). However, if you are looking to upgrade to surround sound and don't want to break the bank look no further.
