product_title: Omicron TURENO HDTV Speaker subwoofer
review_body: I am a self-proclaimed audiophile with a serious inclination towards VALUE. This, my friends, is a product that has immense value.    To give you an idea of what I mean by value, my previous set-up had KLH Subwoofers that were so under-rated and unknown that it wasn't until I spoke of them that people even considered them as KLH (being that KLH, for some unknown reason, has a bad name. Now, by no means would I consider myself cheap...I like value--inexpensive items that do as they say while preserving quality. Being that Matt Polk put the name of the Polk legacy on these, the quality should not be in question at any point.     I think the only reason that these are at such a reduced rate is because of their meager ratings (50-Watt amp and 10\\" woofer...something else that is unattractive is the front facing port--don't they know that most new speakers come with the port to the rear to avoid port noise??!!) and, even moreso, reviewing its bigger brothers and sisters with downward firing ports means that although this sub isn't in the same class, there are offerings for more discerning listeners. If I had a good $1000 to blow on subwoofers, I would have probably bought two of the PSW110s without question...    Ah, yes...TWO.    The biggest reason that I look for subwoofers of value is so that I can purchase more than one (if you were wondering why I keep using these nouns in the plural). Although I am still relatively young <30y/o, I've been into home theater since the days when there was no such thing as Home-Theater-In-a-Box and Definitive Technology illuminated the minds of young, aspiring audiophiles with diagrams of their BP3000s tower speakers with built in 300-Watt Amplifiers and 15\\" Sub-/Woofers. Ah yes...those good ol' days...    Now, Home Theater is the standard and it may be difficult to discern one product from another (trust me, most of it is trash--INCLUDING BOSE). The best way to go about building a theater system is not by adhering to the one-click feature-like HTiB. Piece by piece...step by step... It helps to buy speakers in a particular company's model family since they are normally making use of the same drivers and are normally tonally matched. Many companies claim their speakers as tonally matched without considering the effects of the difference in enclosure size and construction of a center channel and a satellite... Ah...that's info for you--but not why I'm writing this review...    This review is about the two Polk Audio 10PSWs sitting here in front of me.     They sound awesome for what they are. I'm glad that an earlier reviewer made it known that the 50w amplifier is continuously rated--not instantly...or even rated considering a massive amount of Total Harmonic Distortion--as many companies do and then say \\"@ 1KHz\\"...who sits home listening to 1KHz Sine signals?? At loud volumes even? Don't be fooled. Normally they follow that spec up with \\"30-20KHz +/-3db\\" As many of you probably know...that's HALF the power that they're quoting it at...3db = 1/2 Wattage (or twice the wattage considering the context...normally, it's LESS, not MORE).    Many of you, I'm sure, have bought one of these and are either loving it or hating it (most loving from what I can tell). Indeed, with the varying types of music and source program I use, these fit the bill nicely. The sound is present...strong...detailed. I haven't experienced the muddy sound as other people have noted. I'm sure that it's not just luck...I have two...surely, one would be muddy if this was prevalent.    Now, time for pointers (I love the reviewers who leave pointers...it's normally the nudge for most people to consider a truly awesome product--as this one is)    Pointer#1: Buy Two (2)    These are probably some of the least expensive, best sounding subs you can get right now. When in the market for a sub, you should at least have a budget of $200--$400 even...otherwise, you'll find yourself wondering what you paid for... Remember, there are materials(wood, cables), components (subwoofer driver, subwoofer amplifier), and labor that goes into that bass machine. If any of these things aren't optimally constructed, the overall device will suffer. You can understand this, I'm sure. The flip side of this, is that surely, there was a corner cut somewhere. Thus, why continue to hammer out your amplifier? The amp is often overlooked in all of this. Most people see the pretty cone of their subwoofer and totally disregard the reality that the real work horse of the build is the amplifier.     Having two subs is not for more bass...but to conserve the life of the subwoofers you have. In addition, when the time comes to party or watch a movie, you don't have to worry about your subs (the drivers themselves) bottoming out or sounding as if they're straining. Thus, with two, you get the benefit of both worlds (longevity, present sound quality). Electronics have limitations...use them wisely and they will perform AND last a very long time...    Pointer #2: Gain >1/2    You should never have to turn your amplifier gain past half. Past half is where distortion and clipping are introduced. Sure, depending on your source, this may not be prevalent, but if you have a good, strong signal, there will come a time when you hear artifacts that weren't intended for reproduction (e.g. distortion, clipping). As a rule, if you have to turn your sub past half, you might want to adjust your settings in your receiver or see Pointer #1 again... A benefit of two, is that the both of them can be readjusted lower to account for the assistance or each other. My Polks are each at about 1/3 (and that's only because I really enjoy the sound right now...so I'm excited...otherwise they would each be at 1/4). The reason you only want \\"enough\\" volume is because headroom is what you want... this is the power that is used during explosions, kick drums--sudden bursts...this is what you bought it for, right?      Yes, that's right. I know that there are manyother reviewers--bless their heart--who are praising having it just past half or 3/4 of the way up. Mine are at 1/3 and it was like that when I only had one connected. Now that I have both connected, I'll have to half the volume of both of them to equal the volume of the one (and no, the gain knob potentiometers are not linear, so it'll have to be by ear).     Pointer #3: Subs Fill, Not Dominate    Subwoofer modules are only meant to fill in where the other speakers in your system fail. My set-up has Mirage towers as my mains. However, the built in crossover of my Harmon/Kardon handles all bass traffic well--cut off at 60Hz (the point where bass can not be located by the human ear). Having the setting higher than this will not only put more stress on your sub but also the amplifier (lets not forget the amp). When adjusting the gain, you just want to ensure that the frequencies from the sub are at around the same volume as your main speakers. This will keep you from being bass hungry. That's not the point of a sub...this isn't a mobile system...this is home. The environment doesn't warrant that level of \\"hyper-bass\\"... If done this way, you will be able to reach higher sound pressure levels while retaining your dynamism...    These pointers should help with any sub...this sub is truly a great, great buy...    Hope this helps...

review_body: Quick delivery, low price of my Clarity C120 is just what I needed.  I'm very happy with this product.

product_title: Jensen 3-Speed Stereo Turntable with AM/FM Stereo Radio (Silver)
review_body:
I bought the record player to play some old 78 records that I have. I bought a ton of records recently at a storage auction. I am selling them on Ebay, but I needed to check the condition of some of the older records and I didn't have a turntable that would play the 78's.
Overall, I am pleased with it. I'm glad it came with internal speakers, but like some of the other reviewers, I connected a spare pair of external speakers to it. The AM/FM Stereo function was a bonus, but I find I use the FM Stereo quite a bit and it sounds great through the external speakers. The record player is okay and functions as designed. For what I needed, it does just fine.
As far as what I might change, it doesn't have the connections to connect to my stereo system, and that would have been nice. It is meant to be a standalone system and that's okay. And the overall quality is what you might expect in a lower priced item, plastic everything and fake woodgrain. And last, the AM/FM dial is not digital, so you have to fiddle with it to get the channel you want.
But overall, for a $50 or so item, it does what I needed at a reasonable price.

review_body: We were disappointed with this radio.  It took a while to setup.  However, we did like the vast number of HD radio stations that we had access to.    The biggest disappointment was that after we setup our radio stations and playlists, we found that once we powered the unit off and then turned it back on, it would just sit there saying \\"Connecting\\"!      We found that we had to unplug the unit and plug it back in for it to reset and then reselect our stations.  This is very irritating, especially if you want to use the remote control.  Unplugging and plugging in the unit whenever you power it off is unacceptable.    I do not recommend this radio.    TW

product_title: Yamaha RX-V667 7.2-Channel Home Theater Receiver (OLD VERSION) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: This is my third Yamaha AV receiver, and each one is better than the last.  Primary differences from my old Yamaha RXV-659 are:  1. The sound quality is much better, due to the newer decoders. 2. Surround is more seamless and center channel dialog is cleaner.  3.  Auto speaker setup with the remote microphone is more accurate -- no need to tweak with my sound meter. 4. On-screen display made it much easier to set up and change input labels.    I replaced my old receiver with this one only because I wanted to go to HDMI instead of component video connections to my new TV.  I connect the following devices to the receiver: Blu-Ray, cable box/DVR, CD/SACD/DVD Audio player and an old VCR (all different brands).  This receiver accommodates them all, from 6-channel analog input to the latest HDMI.  All the video inputs up-convert with no issues.  Setup with the on-screen display was easy.  The only complaint I have is that the user manual, which I needed to refer to every so often, is provided only on a CD.  I had to print it out and mark a few pages with post-it notes.

product_title: iHome iHM9BC Portable Stereo System for iPod, iPhone and MP3 Players
review_headline: Good sound quality, great value, but...
review_body: Got these for my 9-year-old daughter for christmas. I should've read the product description more closely... The portability- it's lightweight and can go anywhere    Cons: Her iPod is an older one and doesn't hold its charge very long. I mistakenly thought this charged the iPod while it was playing, but it doesn't.  Also, there's no AC adapter-it only runs on 4 AA batteries. GREAT for portability. That's why I gave this product 4 stars instead of 5.     My daughter's happy with them, so that's the important thing. Just wish I'd read the product description and noticed these missing features.

product_title: Altec Lansing Ultra High Def Sound Headphones with iPhone Control
review_headline: Decent sound as long as you get a good fit
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:mo2JBWAG0DRFLP7]]I felt the Altec Lansing MZX606 Ultra High Def headphones provided a decent sound quality, although not the best I've heard. As I point out in the video review, these are not \\"noise-cancelling\\" headphones, rather they are \\"noise-isolating\\" headphones. The former are designed to mask ambient noise via electronics while the latter are designed to prevent unwanted noise from getting into your ear via a tight fit in the ear canal. That is the biggest problem with these headphone. If you use them during working-out, as I do, you may find them continually slipping out of your ear because the perspiration causes them to loose their snugness in the ear canal and they slip out. This is a huge nuisance. The other issue is that since they fit so tightly in your ear, inserting them actually creates an unpleasant air pressure situation on my ear drum as I insert them. Some people may not find this as much of a problem, but I did.

The in-line control for iPods is nice but I rarely use it simply because I'm not used to using an in-line control.

The cord has an isolation loop that helps prevent cord noise (if the cord is rubbing on clothing for instance) for being transmitted to your ear. The little plastic pouch is handy for storing your headphone but I think it's rather humorous that they call it PVC Leather. It's not real leather so it should not be called leather at all. The assortment of tips will help to ensure you get a good fit in your ear taking into consideration the concern I voiced earlier. If you aren't using them for working out but in other situations where sweating isn't an issue, you may not have the same fitting issues that I had and they may be a better choice for you.

product_title: Denon DHT-591BA Home Theater System with Denon AV Receiver and Boston Acoustics 5.1 Speaker Package (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: This is a \\"Home Theater in a box\\": and it is a pretty big box (around 70 lbs).  As this was sold for what I consider a very modest price and included free shipping (which was a sweet deal considering the weight) I was not expecting much.  I had auditioned some other setups from Bose and Klipsch prior to purchasing this.  Those systems cost more money and had limitations that I found troubling.  I was in for quite a surprise.  This little setup rocks.  You can't expect miracles with such small speakers and subwoofer, but this thing way over-delivers.  We had it set up in a fairly large room (> 300 square feet) with over 20' ceilings and it had no problem filling the room with sound.  Surprisingly good value.  Another plus was that the packaging was sturdy enough to stand up to being shipped twice.

product_title: Ultra High Performance HDMI Switcher, 3to1 Switch
review_body: The setup is easy and it is simple to operate. The remote control works well. Switching is easy. I use the remote, as i do not power off my Apple TV. If you power off devices you should be able to forgo the remote and the device will choose the correct port. The picture and sound is played true through the device. It has a DC power port, but I found no need for it as it is powered when the HDMI cables are attached. There is no power adapter, but again it is not needed. I have a blue ray/VHS player, a DVD player, and an Apple TV playing through this device. It is connected to a Sony Bravia HD TV. Very pleased.

product_title: Clip Plus 4 GB MP3 Player (Black)
review_body: I own several MP3 players. My iPod Classic, with its massive 160GB storage, is an iconic staple. My Zune 120GB syncs beautifully with my notebook computer. I enjoy running long distances and my iPod Shuffle clips nicley to the band of my shorts. So what's special about this little unit, the Sansa Clip Plus? Like the Shuffle, the Clip is the size of a tiny box of matches and also clips nicely to my shorts. I can't say that for the Classic or the Zune. The Clip is solidly built with a tiny LED screen and offers features such as voice recorder and FM radio. It also has twice the storage (4GB) as the Shuffle's (2GB). Battery life is nice. What peaked my interest in this player was another feature; the Micro SD card slot. Insert a tiny card in this slot and your media has just been increased exponentially. Not bad for something so tiny. It has software, but for those that don't want to go that route, you can also drag and drop music right off Windows Media Player. Niice! And the sound? Very good for this unassuming MP3. The deal-breaker for me was the price. Forty dollars? Are you kidding? I have come to the conclusion that good things do indeed come in small packages. This little contender scores big without breaking the bank.

product_title: TechCraft Wide Flat Panel TV Stand - Black
review_body: The TechCraft HBL60 is a MUST BUY for a 55/60\\" TV. It takes 2 people to bring in the box...it's that heavy! It is well designed, the glass shelves are all tempered glass, and did I mention: heavy!! Took me about 1/2 hour to assemble...and looks GREAT. You CAN NOT beat the price. This is being used for a Sony 60\\" TV and is just...pardon me...AWESOME!! Everything came well packed in cardboard and strategically packed in surrounded Styrofoam. I kept the core glass box and materials, because if I move, it's how I want the glass packed for moving!!    You can't beat the look...and yes, it is a dust magnet...but that's why they make `Swiffers'! Get plastic, studded carpet savers for the feet so you can level the table with the included screw-in leg levelers, on carpet.    `Nuff said!    R.

product_title: PSWI225 Polk Wireless Subwoofer (Black)
review_body: Bought this subwoofer because we liked the wireless aspect.  Set up was confusing and is still not entirely right.  We get weird popping/knocking sounds sometimes. review_body: Ideal for under the kitchen cabinets for small tv.  Easy to install and really likes that it folds the tv up when not in use.  Exactly what we wanted.

review_headline: Easy to set up and easy to use

review_body: Cable works great, I using it to connect a Panasonic DVD player to my Panasonic LCD TV. Panasonic's Viera Link works great with this cable also. You got to wonder what the profit margin really is with those cables sold be local retailers.

product_title: Sony NWZS544 8 GB Walkman MP3 Video Player
review_headline: You can't queue up songs! Or create/organize playlists from the device itself!
review_body: I bought this player, tried it for one day, and immediately returned it the next.    An mp3 player that can't queue up songs on the go or let you create/organize playlists from the device itself completely DEFEATS THE PURPOSE of having 8Gs of portable music!  It's absurd that it can hold such a large number of songs, but you can't exert any specific control over what selection of songs get played or in what order.  This oversight is something you would expect from a much cheaper player.    Yes, you can make a playlist in Windows Media Player beforehand and quite easily upload it to the player. Yes, you can set it to play a shuffle on all songs, a previously uploaded playlist, or a single album or artist.  BUT assuming I even had the time to constantly be making and uploading new playlists on my computer in preparation for my daily commute, what about the ability to spontaneously choose a list of songs in the moment based on my mood?  I found I had to constantly be perusing my song library and waiting until a song finished, then selecting the next one I wanted because there's no \\"play next\\" or \\"queue\\" option.  Too much work!  It takes the pleasure out of just sitting back with your music.    It's a shame, because aside from this, the interface, sound, and other features (especially the radio) are all quite satisfactory for the price that you pay. However, without playlist editing capabilities, the price is definitely too high.    If you want to spend the extra time on your computer to use the playlists, and be extremely limited by what you can listen to while out and about, you might not mind this mp3 player.

review_body: So I purchased these headphones in Electric Blue. So I figured my luck was terrible and I got rejects but my third pair is showing signs of breaking after 8 weeks of safe use, this time being in my pocket in the format that the manual suggests, meaning you wrap your earphones separate of your music player which I have done for every earphone. product_title: Siege Audio CODEC Ear Bud
review_body: So I saw these at a local Sun and Ski for 20 bucks.  I'm going snowboarding in Colorado in January and wanted a set of headphones that have an inline volume control so I don't have to keep pulling my gloves off to adjust volume on my ipod. I thought these would be a perfect fit.  They are similar to Skullcandy (which is what I usually buy, but the cheapo skullcandy doesn't have volume control)     I thought for $20, why not?  They couldn't be too bad, right?  WRONG!!  I opened the package and realized problem 1 immediately-the piece that is intended to minimize cord movement at the plug slides up and down the cable, effectively rendering it useless.  So now the cable is free to bend and break inside the insulation, thus cutting audio for one or both ears.  This is my major problem with Skullcandy also.  Either way, I took some electrical tape and remedied the issue with copious tape.  Problem 2 came shortly after opening when I was trying to find the right earpiece for my ear...there isn't one.  This is probably not as big of a problem for most folks, as I'm sure the majority of people will not have an issue finding the right size, as they do come with 4 different sizes.  No worries, though!  I'll just use the earpieces from my old Skullcandy pair.  Well...then I plugged them into my ipod thinking FINALLY...they'll work!  Well, they did, but the sound was very muted, kind of like a very poor quality MP3 was being played.  I don't have any poor quality mp3 recordings on my computer.  Well, maybe it's the ipod, then...after all-it is about 3 or 4 years old.  Maybe it just doesn't put out decent sound.      So, I plugged these suckas into my phone (Samsung Captivate-GREAT audio sound)  Well, even out of my phone the sound quality sucked.  I've played with the equalizer, adjusted various volume levels, and still can't get a decent sound out of these headphones. They would get 1 star, but I feel that should be reserved for products that just don't work period.  These work, and the inline volume control works, so that's what gets these a second star, but above and beyond that, these are worthless. Crappy build quality (maybe poor assembly or quality control?) and poor sound = bad headphones.

product_title: Panamax M10-HT-PRO Home Theater Management (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Enormous Power Conditioner Strip. Does What it is Suppose to Do.
review_body:
Yes, it is big. Really, really big. My spouse loves it.

We have power surges on our lines, so this surge protector/conditioner was a nice addition to our home theater system. The conditioner is suppose to clean out the \\"noise\\" to the TV too. The family vote is that the TV picture is nicer using this product.

We replaced 2 power strips with this one strip and have multiple items and a cable line plugged into the strip.

Panamax says that this strip is specifically designed for HD Flat Panel Display Systems & is suppose to do the following:
1. Improve Picture & Sound;
2. Surge Protection;
3. Coax/Sat Protection;
4. Telephone Line Protection;
5. Automatic Voltage Monitoring;
6. Premium Filtration;
7. 12 Volt Trigger Input;
8. Isolated Banks.

Does it protect against surges? We haven't been subjected to a power outage or power surge since installing this strip. However, I am comforted to know that it is there just in case. Panamax offers a limited guarantee on the strip in case of power failure.

product_title: LAVA HD-2805 UHF/VHF Outdoor HDTV Antenna
review_body: OK, I bought this antenna for the specific purpose of receiving stations 45 miles from me. I got the antenna connected to my coax cable on the roof, and set it down inside the window next to the mount (wanted to make sure it was getting signal before I fully installed it). I scanned for channels, and was THRILLED to get 21 stations (I only got 7 with my homemade antenna). I was getting the exact stations I was hoping for, so all was well. Fast forward 2 weeks. The advertisements claim it is \\"perfect for snow and icy climates\\". Ummmmm....YEAH RIGHT! It was out in the freezing weather for two weeks, and could no longer receive the stations 45 miles away, and barely the ones that were 15. I bought a separate antenna as a backup thank goodness (for the sake of not missing the Superbowl - GO PACKERS!!), and now this one acts as my backup, and the backup is now my main antenna.    I would HIGHLY recommend my \\"backup\\" BTW....the AntennaCraft HBU33 with RCA pre-amp (its in my attic).    I now just have this antenna pointed towards the local stations 15 miles away, and my other pointed to the longer distance ones. I am a little upset that I paid $60 and put in a couple hours mounting time for an antenna that does not perform better than a $10-20 indoor antenna.    I would venture to guess that this antenna would perform well in warmer climates. It does feel very cheaply made, so perhaps its not as weather resistant as the company would have you believe.    I would return it, but I just don't want to go through the hassle. And it works for its new purpose (as the backup), its just too bad it fell short of its original purpose.

Only negative that I can come up with is that it does not have an On/Off switch so power goes to the unit at all times and the blue lights on the unit are bright enough to light up a whole room in the dark. product_title: Belkin Micra Digital HDMI to Mini-HDMI Cable (6ft)
review_headline: Micra Digital HDMI to Mini-HDMI Cable (6 Feet)
review_body:
The Micra Digital HDMI to Mini-HDMI Cable is used to connect a device with an HDMI port to another device with a Mini-HDMI (also known as a Type C HDMI) port. HDMI, which stands for High-Definition Multimedia Interface, is a connector that is capable of transmitting high volumes of digital video and audio signals. HDMI ports are found on TV's and DVD players (all new TV's and DVD players come with at least one). Mini-HDMI, on the other hand, are found on HD camcorders, DSLR cameras, and other portable devices that are capable of high definition video and audio.

Note, that there is another type of HDMI called Micro-HDMI (Type D HDMI), which is a 19-pin HDMI connector. To connect an HDMI device to a device with a Micro-HDMI, you will need a [[ASIN:B003UH0Z9Q HDMI to Micro-HDMI Cable]]. Make sure you're getting the right kind of cable.

The connectors on the Micra cable are not gold-plated to prevent oxidation, which can degrade signal transmission. You can get HDMI to Mini-HDMI cables with gold-plated connectors for less. Check out these very favorably-rated cables made by [[ASIN:B000TT80DG TripLite]] and [[ASIN:B003ES5ZR8 AmazonBasics]].

product_title: TechCraft Wide Flat Panel TV Stand - Black
review_headline: There is a reason this stand is top rated
review_body: When I browse on Amazon, the first thing I usually do on a product page is look at the user review. They are really helpful, insightful, and usually gives you a glimpse of what you can expect from the product yourself. After buying this stand, I felt I had to help out my fellow shoppers!    First things first, the stand is heavy. I am in the military and in pretty good shape, but I still needed one of my buddies to help me transport it to my place.          The next thing is the assembly. When you first look at the pieces and the instruction manual, you may think that assembling the stand will be hard work, but it really isn't. One thing you will need that is not included in the package is a simple phillips screwdriver. Other than that, everything you need is in the box. And trust me, assembly is really not as hard as it looks. Everything is clearly marked with numbers and the pieces fit logically, so it is kinda hard to get confused setting it up. I had a buddy help me out and it took us 15 mins to put everything together. You can do it by yourself no problem, but if you have a friend close, might as well have them help!        Now, when the stand is assembled, it is simply beautiful. It looks much better than it does in the pictures, which is crazy because it already looks good! I have a PS3 and a Xbox 360 and they both fit comfortably on one of the shelves. However, my receiver did not fare as well. it is possible I could have squeeze it in on the bottom shelf, but I really didn't feel like trying to make it work. So if you have a large receiver, that may be a sticking point for you; wasn't for me. The stand also has holes in the back in order to route your cables through them to eliminate clutter, which is useful, but since i don't have many things hooked up, i haven't utilized that feature.    All in all, this is a great TV stand. It looks classy, is very sturdy, and has plenty of space horizontally for a variety of components. The only knock I can think of, isagain, the vertical space between shelves, but as long as you don't have a large receiver, you will be fine. And even with that said, I can't knock it down a star because it is so wonderful.    If you are on the fence about this stand, don't be. This purchase is worth it and the price is definitely right.

review_headline: Does the job but really not for heavier televisions!
review_body:
I bought this item after doing much searching for the wall mount of my needs. I found this mount and read the reviews so I knew what I might get.

I have a Hitachi 55\\" LCD and have it mounted on a wall which is angled so I could swivel it if needed. My order was received promptly. I wouldn't recommend this mount if you have a television heavier than 85 lbs. because the weight of my television seems to be the limit that this mount will handle. If you are not mechanically inclined...do not depend on the one sheet directions to help you understand how to install the mount...they are very vague and poorly explain how each part is utilized. The lag bolts are not top quality but should work for smaller televisions. I added my own quality bolts to give me a piece of mind and are a low cost item at your hardware store/ It would have been nice to have a template included so that you could make your layout easier. The wall I installed my television on would not allow me to center the television where I wanted (studs were off centered) so I went online and found some information that might be helpful to anyone who reads my review. I cut a piece of 3/4\\" plywood (34\\" x 20\\") and used 12-4\\" cabinet screws to secure to the center of the studs then secured the back plate of the mount to the plywood with the lag screws that I purchased where it would be centered on the wall. Then I just made sure the bracket was level and secure before mounting the television to the mount. Probably took me about 35-45 minutes to install once I made all my marks and located the studs.

Overall, this is a good mount for the money... and for being made in China! I will definitely buy another one of these for the 32\\" in my bedroom so if your looking to save some $$ and need a mount that will do the job, I would recommend this mount for your television.

Additionally, there was a 5v female power outlet on the device itself, but no power adapter in the packaging. Given the wording in the instructions I was afraid this power was needed for the automatic switching I wanted.    Eventually I ignored all the instructions and just plugged it in as I was planning:  1) Xbox  2) Extra Cable (For Nikon DSLR etc.)  3) Mac mini (always on)    This device just works. Whenever a higher priority device turns on the switch switches. It only takes a second or so but it works great. There is is an included remote and IR receiver but I haven't bothered with it. The automatic switching was what I was after and all my devices appear to work well with it. If I really need to switch manually, there is a select button on the device itself.    I can only assume the powered outlet it present if your devices don't transmit enough power for the auto detection/switching. I'm sure the remote functionality is handy if you need it. But the bottom line is this works well. The instructions could be drastically reduced and seem to imply this is more complicated than it actually is. Plug in your devices and go. While I'd love to dock a star for that, the device is exactly what I needed and didn't cost a ton.

product_title: Sony MDR-XD200 Stereo Headphones
review_body: My previous pair of headphones were Rosewill RMH-556 (not on Amazon anymore, thankfully),[...]so this isn't the first pair of headphones.  In a nutshell, everything I hated about the Rosewill is fixed with the Sony pair.    Sound quality: I'd say overall it's more crisp, but one thing that's a bit more tangible is bass output.  The Rosewill's are supposed to be 10Hz-25kHz vs the Sony's 10Hz-22kHz, however, I'd say that that's not quite accurate.  I had VLC tuned to maximize the bass output of the Rosewill headphones, and the moment I switched over to the Sony's I noticed I could raise the bass slider a whole lot more without distorting the audio.    Ergonomics:  The Rosewill is supposedly around-the-hear.  It isn't.  It touches your earlobe, which doesn't bother you at first, but after you wear them for a quite a few hours, your earlobe will start aching.  The Sony headphones are much larger completely touch the sides of my head all the way around.  I have a larger than average head (my caps/hats are 8\\") and this fits over my head with room to spare, whereas the Rosewill just barely made it.    These are much, much sturdier (I ended up breaking the Rosewills because they were so flimsy) and at the same time are incredibly lightweight.  When I pick them up I'd expect them to way at least 3 times as much, so I guess that would make it less noticeable that you're wearing them.    The audio cable is plenty long for what I need, but I guess it could be a bit more insulated. Still at the same time it's snug and solid while still being lightweight (whereas the Rosewill's cord was loose against the earphone it connected to).    Without a doubt, these are worth the extra $6.  Quite inexpensive and I'd probably be happy paying even $30-40 for these, but $20 is also fine with me :).    I did like having the little hardware volume-control dial on the Rosewill, but I guess that reduces the number of points of failure and I don't mind reaching an extra inch to adjust the volume of the device it's plugged in to I guess.  No big deal there.    I would buy it again. And again.

However, Microsoft also offers a dock for the HD player that is a gem.  It connects to your TV and allows you to control playback with a handy remote.  Most significantly, the dock features a digital, optical out that can be used to feed the digital out to a third party DAC.  This means that if you have invested in a great audio system you can enjoy the convenience of the 64 gigs of music available at one time, the remote, and full CD quality audio.  No settling for MP3 or any other compressed formats for playback.  Anyone who is serious about listening to music should jump on this unique capability. product_title: QUANTUM FX ANT-105 TV Remote-Controlled Rotating Antenna - DTV and HDTV Ready
review_body: This antenna is incredibly cheaply made - aluminum soda cans have better quality control.  All the sheet metal screws were loose - necessary because there isn't enough metal there to tighten them.  The rotor head flops around 20 degrees horizontally and 7 degrees vertically.    Outdoors?  Forget about it.  Steel zinc plated cheap hardware in contact with bare aluminum will rust out in no time.  It couldn't stand a direct hit from a pine cone. The reflector dish is cheap steel mesh.    Mine was well packed, but the reflector dish was dented in two places and one director loop was very badly mangled. (and probably went into the box that way)    The one saving grace is that it is almost omnidirectional so if the useless rotor chooses to quit working, and it works when it feels like it, it doesn't really matter.    Rabbit ears are cheaper and about as effective.    My 10 cent bow-tie coathanger bits and pieces antenna outperforms this one and is more directional. (only cost 10 cents because it was cheaper to punch holes in pennies than truck to the store to buy washers)    Edited:  I took the rotor apart and found the motor was not fastened in place - there is a place for screws but it wasn't screwed down - so the whole motor flopped around and would jamb up when it reached the end of its travel.  I put in two screws and the \\"dead band\\" went from plus and minus 20 degrees to 3 degrees.  Signal improved a bit also - perhaps the high and low bands were reversed (the case goes together either way - not keyed so I had a 50% chance of getting it right) Rotor works great now.    The 4 screws holding the rotor case on only catch one or two threads and they were stripped out so I used electrical tape as a back-up.  I need a better method because the tape will soften in summer and I want to hang it upside down from the roof ridge in the attic.    $25 bucks is too much for this much hassle - wait till you see it at the 99 cent store.

review_body: I had never put much stock in to sound quality on my computer until recently.  I decided it was about time to get a decent pair of headphones, and so I did.  I loved them, the music sounded so great compared to what I was used to.  I felt it was near perfect until I decided I wanted to get a Zo, because of all the positive reviews I had read.  I put it on orange and when I listened to my music I couldn't believe the bass response -- Not only that but the mids and the highs sounded so much better as well.  My near perfect headphones were now nothing without my Zo.      They say on their site it is like having a 12\\" subwoofer in your headphones, and if you have speakers / headphones that can handle the frequencies that is definitely true.  I went from hearing a light hit on the bass to FEELING it.  I even went as far as to get a car CD player with aux out so I could take it on the road with me, and have been impressed with how it makes my stock speakers sound there as well.  Of course I don't get the pounding bass like my headphones, but they are still able to shake the truck a little bit with no distortion.  Even the systems built in bass boost got distorted on higher settings -- this simply isn't the case with the Zo. My wife watched a movie on her laptop with headphones and Zo and now wants one -- I have yet to see or hear a negative review on this thing.    I must point out the flaws: No power indicator, it will simply cut out and you have to charge it.  If using on the computer you can charge it while listening to it but it has an annoying buzz while plugged in so I just do without for an hour (and don't really listen to music). product_title: Microsmith Hlp Hot Link Pro(tm) Remote Ir Booster System (6 Emitters)
review_body: I purchased this product after agoning over the decision made more difficult by the reviews good and bad. Whether offering help or advice it told me they were passionate about thier product and opinions of said product.  None of the other big vendors did anything of the sort. Probably a small company which means even more when they can provide feedback but the big names cannot devote anyone to the same percieved level of service. Works like a charm.  My eqipment is in a closet just behind the wall where the TV mounts, drilled throught the wall with grommets and into the coat closet, cables were plenty long enough.  I do not have any latency like described in some posts.  Don't need to be a sys engineer to get this to work, just need to be able to read. Hid the IR sensor behind the TV as directed where it is not flooded with light or inteference from the room or TV itself.... I cannot get it to fail any time of day.  Very happy with this purchase and if I had another use for another I would buy one.  One post stated it seemed cheaply put together, I did not think so, although it did not have embossments or logos all over it it looked and felt pretty solid to me. Another said the emitters came of the ribbon, mine are solidly attached.  Anothe said the ribbon split wrong revealing bare wire, I carefully seperated mine with no issues. I would recommend they make the box so it could be wall mounted with the oblong keyhole so it could hang on a screw but other than that....I liked the ribbon style cable for the emitters that could be split and routed as needed, Sticky stuff worked just fine if you find the eye first and don't have to remove it.  Can you really expect it to stick if you remove it half a dozen time before you find the IR reciever on your remote equip because you did not read the instructons first. I think I recall another post saying it got hot, I have not noticed this and frankly don't recall feeling for it but have touched it since it has been on and no heat issues jump out at me. product_title: JVC Air Cushion Headphone
review_body: I was going to wait at least another week or so to do this review, but I couldn't wait any longer....    The earphones that came with my iPod Nano was losing low-end frequency and all I got was tinny telephone-quality audio...even on max volume level. That's when I took the time and searched through almost every earbuds costing between the $20-$50 range. The list calls for JLab, Sony, Skullcandy, V-Moda, Panasonic, JVC, Q-Electronics....you name it, I've read just about every single brand, including Bose, JBL and others. After combing through all the pros and cons, the final three came down to Sony, JLab and JVC.    I chose JVC over the other two for the following reasons:  Sony: Although I owned a pair of DJ set, I find that the Bass from Sony is a bit too much and overpowering. Also, the Sony buds are bigger in comparison.  JLab: Too many reviewers complained about the cords being too sensitive and racking up movement noise. Also, many claimed that the Bass is good but also muddled.      Now, the JVC:  I've been a JVC loyalist since the 80s and all I can say is I've never owned a bad product from this manufacturer. Along with the reviews I can pretty much expect to get the same result, and indeed I did. For the money, the JVC HA-FX67 is as good as any $200 earpiece...and I mean it! I can hear details that I've never heard of from my Sony. The Bass is rich, tight and solid, the Mid is perfect and the Highs are very clean, yet subtle and not too overly bright. The overall balance on these phones are just too amazing and they are VERY comfortable to wear. As you can see, the housing is also silicone-wrapped so that it can rest comfortably in your ear cups. In addition, it comes with three different size interchangeable silicone earpieces and one set of memory foam (total of 4 sets). I use the largest one and they do a fabulous job of blocking outside noise. Once I put them on, they are snug fit. The noise is so blocked up that I felt like I'm underwater in a swimmingpool, and I hear nothing but the full nuance of sweet music to my ears. These phones delivered sounds at a much higher decibel due to their excellence of filtering outside noise, and along, can be achieved with at a much lower volume setting (25% compared to 45-50%) than what it used to be. Not only I get better sound, but I'm also gaining battery life.    PROS:  Good tight and very solid Bass, excellent Mid and Trebles. Overall sound is well-balanced.  Cord Clip  Small/Medium/Large Silicone Earpiece Set  Memory Foam Earpiece Set  Air cushioned/silicone surround housing for extra comfort and sound isolation  Friction Noise Reduction Cord (this was one of the selling point for me)    CONS:  No case (to store the rubber buds)       Anyway, I can't seem to part with it for the moment. Again, the sound is just too amazing and I love the rich tight solid bass that it puts out.

product_title: iDesign Slimline Music System for iPod and iPhone Devices
review_headline: Good, but not quite what it claims to be
review_body: Setup is a snap, the sound is terrific, and it does indeed work by a remote that synchs immediately with your iPod. Click on \\"iPod\\" and then on \\"Music\\" and you are presented with a broad selection of choices: Playlists, Artists, Albums, Composers, Genres, etc (ending in Videos and Audiobooks). From that point, however, a very big problem emerges. In contrast to the rapid iPod click-wheel that allows one to find and play particular items quickly and easily, this small remote operates by push-buttons that advance its tiny, dull and too-briefly illuminated screen one item or short screen at a time. Each item is arranged alphabetically, and if you have a few thousand items it will take forever to get all the way down just to the halfway point, and forget ever making it all the way down to Y. Beyond this problem, the way the device gathers items into categories seems eccentric if not sometimes entirely arbitrary - as one example, it gathered only two items under \\"Genres\\" > \\"Alternative\\": Tom Waits, who is quite happy there; and the classical cellist Janos Starker, who is spinning in his grave. (Maybe it mistook the work \\"stark\\" for \\"punk\\"). Only these two items in spite of the fact that I have several hundred items in this category on my iPod (but then I'm not good about managing \\"Genres\\" on my iTunes). Another problem is that very little information about each item can be seen on the tiny screen, so that my entire collection of Albums > Bach Cantatas shows up only as screen after screen of \\"Bach Cantat\\" and I can't see which one I'm selecting until it's actually playing and the title starts scrolling across the screen. The same items do show up differently on different lists, so that I may get Composers > Bach > Cantata 78. And I will end by reporting one last and very annoying shortcoming: once a particular item has been playing for a few minutes it shows up on the remote screen from then on only as \\"now playing,\\" and although it will continue to play all the tracks for that item, once that registers it is impossible ever to return to other items or categories at all, so that to do anything one must start all over again from the very beginning: iPod > Music > Album (or whatever), yadda yadda. The only possible fix around these shortcomings would seem to be to create special short Playlists on iTunes to transfer to your iPod and be used only for this particular device for particular purposes: sleep/wake, workout, Baby Einstein, etc.

product_title: RCA DH24SPF Two Way 3 Ghz Bi-Di Splitter
review_headline: It's a SPLITTER, not a TAP !!
review_body:
This is an excellent product when used PROPERLY -- and as intended.
This is a SPLITTER, which means that BOTH of the \\"OUT\\" terminals should be connected to cables of the SAME, or nearly the SAME Length in order for your equipment to receive an equal share of the signal.
In other words -- the RCA splitter has 1 \\"IN\\" and 2 \\"OUT\\" terminals -- and the cables attached to the terminals must be the SAME or nearly the SAME length so that the signal loss in each cable run will be the same for both components.
Example: If you have one cable coming off the Splitter that's 60 feet long but the other one is only 6 feet long, they'll be way out of \\"balance\\", and certain equipment (such as a cable modem) will not function the same on either length of cable. Internet connection speeds are very sensitive to signal imbalance, so it's important to keep your cable modem on the shortest possible cable run, and NEVER on the \\"long side\\" of a junction !!
Under those circumstances, a SPLITTER is the WRONG CHOICE -- and a \\"TAP\\" must be used !!
A \\"TAP\\" looks a lot like a SPLITTER, but works differently -- the TAP has 1 \\"IN\\" and 1 \\"OUT\\" terminal, with the 3rd terminal \\"unmarked\\". -- With a TAP, the longer 60-foot run would be connected to the \\"OUT\\" terminal, and the shorter 6-foot run would go to the \\"unmarked\\" terminal.
Note that the DH24SP is a \\"2-way\\" splitter, which means that the high-frequency signal can pass freely in BOTH directions, which is critical for high-speed internet's need for bi-directional, hi-speed transfer of data \\"packets\\" to and from your server/tester/ISP.
Some reviewers have claimed that a cheapo splitter from the dollar store is \\"just as good\\" -- but that's just crazy talk !! And those gold-plated ones from \\"the shack\\" are NOT APPROVED by COX Cable, either !! I thought they were jackin' me around, but the COX Tech replaced my \\"golden\\" splitter with a SV2G 5-1000 MHz splitter and my internet connection speeds improved quite a bit !!
Anyways, if you need a SPLITTER for high bandwidth applications, such as Satellite, Cable Internet, Digital Cable, or HDTV -- this is it !!
Just remember to keep your cables as close to the same length as possible, and if you CAN'T, get a TAP for that long run !!!
One other thing -- for absolute best performance and a strong, steady signal, place your Modem and your Wireless Router about 4 feet apart to prevent radio frequency interference. Electrical interference of any kind drives Wireless Routers crazy, which is why I use and recommend Category 7 (double-shielded) Ethernet cables !!
The RCA (Audiovox) DH24SP gave a noticable improvement in the picture quality of our 52\\" Samsung LCD HDTV and to the 20\\" Standard TV on the other leg. It replaced an SV2 Splitter @5-1000 Hz. and -3 db drop per leg.
Great product when used as intended, and well worth the money - especially since Amazon.com cut the price IN HALF of what I paid here just a few weeks ago !!
The most important thing to remember is that this is NOT a signal BOOSTER, and it CANNOT make a weak signal stronger !!
What it WILL do is divide a high-frequency signal into 2 separate but equal parts by using intelligent circuitry combined with quality components and excellent workmanship.
The Bi-Directional capability MAY improve your computer's UPLOAD speeds, but that will depend on other factors.
My own personal install (outdoors) yielded an average Upload Speed increase of about 275 % over the old ISP-provided splitter -- (it wasn't bi-directional)

UPDATE: 21 January, 2015
The RCA 2.4 GHz splitter has been going strong for four (4) years now, delivering internet speeds as high as 131 Mbps Download, and 30 Mbps Upload (Top 12% of the world), and excellent audio-video quality from Samsung 52-inch HDTV.
Thanks to Amazon Customer Frostarix, I was made aware that an upgraded (3.0 GHz) model is now available from RCA-Audiovox. Based onthe excellent service life and performance of the 2.4 GHz model, I would highly recommend the newer model to any and all who demand the absolute best performance from their equipment.
Don't be fooled into buying the cheaper splitters, thinking that they are \\"just as good\\" -- or that they are \\"good enough\\" -- or that they are \\"a best seller\\" -- because there is no substitute for the economy of quality performance !!

review_headline: You get what you pay for
review_body: I replaced a 2 year old Onkyo TX-8555 receiver after a lightning strike with a Yamaha RX-497. The Yamaha has excellent sound, more power, and much better base response. Even though the Yamaha is rated at 75 watts per channel and the Onkyo at 100, the Yamaha will blow the socks off the Onkyo. The Onkyo lacked bass. I am not a bass freak but I do like a little depth. Even with the bass cranked up all the way, it never gave me as much bass as my 30 year old Technics. I had to add a subwoofer to get as much bass as before with just my Bose 501 speakers. With the Yamaha RX-497 I have all the bass I want without the subwoofer. It also has a Loudness feature to boost the bass at lower volumes. An excellent buy.

product_title: Sony BRAVIA DAV-HDX589W 5.1-Channel Theater System (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: The biggest worry I had when buying this product was setting it up.  I wanted to be able to use the system will watching TV as well as DVDs/Radio/music inputs/etc.  The basic set up of the system was very easy and I had no problem.  Even callibrating the speakers was easy.  However, at first the speakers did not appear to work with the cable channels even though I followed all of the instructions.  After talking to a friend I found out the problem lay in what type of audio output my TV had.  Apparently it only had Digital output RCA cables and not a coaxial option.  Not a big deal because I found an optical digital cable on Amazon for $2.12 new with no shipping and handling, but I wish that the manual for the system had mentioned that there are different types of outputs.  I would have been really upset if it wouldn't have worked with my cable.

product_title: Mount-It! Tilting Mount For 30"- 56" Displays - Black
review_body: Fast Shipping. I had a couple questions before and after purchase. Both were answered quickly and completely.  The Mount is strong and the hardware is packaged in a way that makes it easy to assemble.    The instructions that came with the mount are for mounting on a concrete wall. I would have liked to see instructions for other surfaces like drywall studs.  But if you've ever hung something on studs in a wall you'll have no problem.    Great Price  Great Product    Thanks!

product_title: Apple 16 GB iPod nano 6G - Graphite OLD MODEL
review_headline: They've added A LOT of features...
review_body: to the iPod Shuffle. They have added touch screen functionality, picture browsing, the ability to select your song (I'm sure they've still retained the ability to shuffle through all tracks), and an FM radio.  They've killed the nano and have introduced a shuffle with a touch screen at the same price point and the same name as an iPod nano. That's all the nano 6g really is. It's a cute little mp3 player that lets you touch navigate through music and pictures, and that's it. Radio's been included in every player but the iPod, so its hard to give them much credit for that. This appears to be a huge step back for the nano. The removal of features cannot be justified at the same price point.

product_title: Sangean DT-210 FM-Stereo/AM PLL Synthesized Pocket Receiver
review_body: I wanted to listen to an FM radio at work.  I work in a cubicle around a lot of computers.  This device did not perform well.  I have an MP3 player that I have been using but was looking for something with a longer battery life.  This did not work out for me at all.

product_title: Cable 6 Feet Extension USB Male to USB Female Cable
review_body: Well made product.  Does exactly what it is suppose to do.  Which in my case was allow me to relocate the wireless transceiver for my keyboard. Great price! I appreciate the fast service.

product_title: iLive Stereo Speaker System with iPod Dock
review_body: I've owned this speaker/docking station for 2 years now, and I was surprised to see all the negative or poor reviews!  I haven't had any problems with this product.  These speakers aren't nowhere near Bose but it has decent speakers which are more for a bedroom than a living room.  I have to take my case off of my 4 gen. ipod nano to dock.  I set my alarm on my nano and the docking station will sync with the nano and turn on my music or turn off my music (depending on my settings).  I love the night light on the docking station since it lights up enough for me to see my baby sleeping or for me walk in and out the bedroom without bumping into anything.  Setting the clock is very easy.  The remote is tiny and I used it once in awhile.  Overall, I like this product and purchased it cheap at Toysrus for the same price listed here on Amazon.  It works and serves the purpose in my bedroom.  Too bad so many other customers didn't have the same great experience that I have with this product.

product_title: Mediabridge Toslink Cable - Optical Digital Audio Cable
review_body: This is the first optical cable I have purchased from Mediabridge but have used 3 of their HDMI cables in various lengths and have had no problems with them.  I have had a few different makes of Toslink cables, but always settled for the lower end versions because of the high cost of name-brand cable. Like almost everything- you get what you pay for- very thin sheathing over the fiber optic and just felt like they would snap at any minute. I had a couple of failures due to moving a component and the cat pulled on one and the fiber snapped inside.  This cable's sheathing is easily 3 times thicker than the low-cost cables and compared to my most expensive cable it is noticeably thicker and also the Toslink connectors seem to be of a higher quality.  I use this between my old DVD player which doesn't have HDMI to connect to my receiver to listen to CDs. I know- why would anyone use that when they have a Blu ray player, XM radio, and their home PC all connected to their home theater system? I'm not sure..cause it still works and I hate to throw it away, maybe.  If you need a digital optical solution to connect your xbox360, your TV if the HDMI doesn't support audio return, or an older CD/DVD/SAT component to your receiver this is what you need.[[ASIN:B004LSNF04 Mediabridge - Toslink Cable - Optical Digital Audio Cable - 6ft]]

review_body: The smaller end is too big for making a solid connection with a bumper-equipped iPhone4.  Otherwise, nice idea and seems to be well-made.

product_title: Conair Shower Radio
review_body: This radio was exactly what I was looking for: cheap & simple. I was a little annoyed that it took a whopping 4 AA batteries, but was fine with that so long as it worked well, which it did, for about a year. Then the volume started to go and I had to blast the thing just to have it play loud enough over the shower head. Now it only plays sound at an inaudible level. It lasted a year. If you want something that will last longer than that, I guess you'll have to cough up more dough.

product_title: Polk Audio RC60i 2-Way In-Ceiling  Speakers (Pair, White)
review_body: I bought these for my wife to use in the kitchen and installed them in the cabinets. They work great for ambient background music. I liked that they're flat all the way across and blend in unlike the Pyle PDIC80 I was considering. At 9in from edge to edge they were overall a little bit bigger than I was expecting. I paired them with the AudioSource AMP-100 2-Channel Amplifier. I don't know if it's the amp or the speakers but while they're loud enough for the kitchen I do have to have them turned up almost full blast. I don't know what the RMS is but peak is rated at 40 watt and the amp is rated at 50 watt RMS per channel.    [Edit] I did some more listening today and the quietness was due to the source. They're plenty loud now and they sound fantastic.

product_title: Sony MDR-IF240RK Wireless Headphone System
review_body: I could not find any position for the base that did not cause a buzzing noise in the headphones that was anywhere from low, but definitely noticeable, loudness to very loud. Overall, this looks like a cheap product.

review_body:
This is a well-made cable, noticeably thicker than cheaper cables. This cable is the right length to connect my wall-mounted television to the recessed box behind it without excess cable to deal with, and connects solidly to the television and the [[ASIN:B002OFWQ24 HDMI coupler for wallplate]] I mounted in the recessed box.

review_body: I ordered two of these cables at the same time I ordered my Sony TV.  I received the TV on a Friday, but no cables, and needed the cables to complete the setup.  Guess what, no setup over the weekend.  Also, the tracking number for the shipment was supplied to me via Amazon email message.  My understanding is that UPS picks up the package, and delivers it to the US postal service for shipment.  The tracking number was not in either system through the whole time it was in transit.  I sent an email to the shipper through Amazon asking for assistance (Amazon sent me a confirmation of my sent message), and I never received a reply from the shipper.  It was poor performance all the way around.  I think that there is no excuse for this substandard performance considering the high tech communication environment that we now have in the electronic business marketplace.

product_title: Sony RMVLZ620 Universal Remote Control (Black)
review_body: I bought this remote to replace the SONY RM-V302 I had previously, which worked like a champ for a decade.  When I was in the market for a replacement, I figured logically that a newer Sony remote would have a minimum of equivalent compatibility with my Zenith tv.      Apparently logic does not apply to Sony as this absolutely does NOT work with Zenith tv's with any supplied codes.  After that did not work, I used the feature that tries all TV codes.  Amazingly, NONE of them worked.  It's not as if programming a remote is even remotely close to the realm of difficult.  I went through this process twice more in addition just to verify I had not hit a wrong key inadvertently.  I had not.        I did some searching, including viewing Sony's website for this, and there is a nice little disclaimer at the bottom saying if the manufacturer's code does not work, you may be required to try all TV codes until you find one that works.  Given that there's 100,000 combinations and a large subset of that devoted to TV's, there is no way in hell I am spending the time to go through every possible combination.  Purely ridiculous.      I could buy an $8 RCA remote that would be guaranteed to work, but I went with Sony due to brand-name recognition and previous relatively positive experiences with similar products.  In the end, this remote is literally useless to me for it's primary function, and given that returning it would be more trouble than it's worth, I broke it intentionally out of spite.  It's functionality remains about the same.  So, I am going back to the previous remote I had which I've located for sale on ebay.  This remote ate a portion of my wallet and, more importantly, my time.      Proceed with caution and make sure returning is an easy option if you go with this remote.  As I found out, there are no guarantees.    Update :  I purchased a Sony RMVZ320 from the local Best Buy on the basis that returning would be cake, and this is my synopsis :   - It has nearly thesame design as this *but* with GREATER compatibility with legacy products and at $10+ less cost.      - It still did not work 100% on my Zenith tv.  The number buttons did not work, though everything else did.      - Unless you absolutely need the 1 extra device to go from 7 to 8 max and the learning capability, which is stated to be flakey in it's reliability, I would recommend the Sony RMVZ320 emphatically over this.  Far better value per dollar.

product_title: Philips HTS3450 DVD/5.1 Surround Home Theater with USB Direct
review_body: So everyone who buys this speaker set ends up with the same complaint. After owning it for roughly a year, the subwoofer will stop functioning (either slowly or instantly). This is due to two bad capacitors on the subwoofer's power supply board. You can fix it yourself for relatively cheap (about $3 for parts if you already have the tools and solder).    Either way, this is really unacceptable. I guess Philips really is just going downhill.

product_title: Cheetah APTMM2B TV Wall Mount for 20-75" TVs up to VESA 600 and 165lbs, and fits 16” And 24” Wall Studs, and includes a Tilt TV Bracket, a 10' Twisted Veins HDMI Cable and a 6" 3-Axis Magnetic Bubble Level
review_body: I was on the fence about buying this product but after purchasing and receiving it and realizing what a great buy it was I just had to come back and share my thoughts.  This is one great buy, no kidding. It was simple to hang (although I did purchase my own toggle bolts instead of using the bolts supplied) and it is SOLID. Using the built in level I was able to align the bracket, mount it, and hang the TV all within 20 minutes, including drilling the toggle bolt holes, and with only the assistance of my 13yr old.    If you are considering buying this mount stop thinking about it and DO IT!

product_title: Sony ICFC717PJ Nature Sounds Clock Radio
review_body: I purchased this item because it met all the requirements my wife was looking for   1.) Projection of the time  2.) Nature Sounds  3.) MP3 capability.    The only thing missing was an outside temperature sensor, but that wasn't a show stopper.  When the unit arrived, it was as advertised...sharp looking item from Sony.  Appeared to work great.  The only issue I found was in the quality of the nature sounds.  They appeared very computer generated.  We had another machine from Homedics that was not reliable, but the sounds were great and realistic.  It was that units lack of reliability that drove us to the Sony name.  After listening to the sounds, that's as far as we went with the unit...repackaged and returned it.  For the cost (~$60) I expected a higher quality sound output from Sony...I had found similar quality in less expensive units from other manufacturers...get the sound right, and this would be worth the price.

product_title: Bose QuietComfort 3 Acoustic Noise Cancelling Headphone
review_body: I received the Bose QuietComfort 2 acoustic noise cancellation headphones as a gift. After 14 months the left phone had lower volume, verified by Bose store staff. Bose only offered that I buy new headphones for $89 because their warranty is one year. Eighteen months later the left phone is dead; the right phone is barely audible. Clearly the headphones are flawed in design. Bose advertises that its products should give users years of enjoyment; I got 14 months. I cannot recommend Bose products.

product_title: Logitech Pure-Fi Anywhere 2 Compact Docking Speakers for iPod and iPhone
review_headline: Great for camping!  A little heavy for the backpack.
review_body: My husband and I are thrilled with this little power house.  Music is one of the most important things to him and we have killed more than one truck battery playing music when we are in the back country.  We did a fair amount a research of portable units and the sound quality is great especially at this price. So far it also seems pretty indestructable  We plan on getting a second one for my office.

review_body: HAVE NEEDED ONE OF THESE FOR THREE YEARS---FINALLY FOUND IT ON AMAZON OF COURSE.  WORKS GREAT

product_title: iHome iP9 Clock Radio for iPod and iPhone
review_body:
I iHome iP9SR radio is a great radio. It is to be used with any iPod, or iPhone. It has some great features to go along with it. I bought this radio to replace a small stero that I had. However, it has an alarm clock on it that most people will probably use it for. You can wake up to your playlist different days of the week at different times! It will also wake you up gradually and/or put you to sleep gradually, which is nice if you have a spouse who doens't want to listen to music all night. If only I could get 2!

I got this item for Christmas and have not stopped playing with it since then. The sound quality is great with it's 3-D sound. My radio stations come in crisp and clear and my iPod sounds beautiful. This radio also comes with a remote control that can change your settings, control volume, switch songs, etc. The radio is also nice because it charges your iPod/iPhone as it sits in the dock. you can choose to have it plugged it or run on batteries as well.

The other nice feature is that it's small and doesn't take up a lot of room. Perfect to fit in any space you need it to.

review_body: Yes this product is well worth the money I'm using a double monitor set up and one of my monitors doesn't have a hdmi connection just dvi and vga so I wanted the digital performs so I found this cord.. Its well worth the money..

product_title: TEAC CD-P650-B Compact Disc Player with USB and iPod Digital Interface (Black)
review_body: I still have an old school rack mounted stereo system with individual components. After the death of my CD player I was looking for a single play CD player. The Teac CD-P650 was my choice due to the USB interface. In addition to great Audio CD playback, this unit adds the dimension of plugging in an MP3 player or a thumb drive and being able to enjoy music from those sources. I am a volunteer DJ for CJAM 99.1 FM and I often use thumb drives to preview new releases. The CD player displays the artist and title from the MP3 source, so I can quickly review new music. Overall the unit was eay to set up and works great!

product_title: 19"(50cm) 7 Pin SATA Right Angle to Straight DATA HDD Hard Drive Cable
review_body: The cable itself is good quality and works fine.    However, potential buyers should take note, as one of the prior reviews points out (I wish I had seen it before purchasing) - the right angle connector is upside down. The notch forces you to route the cable from the other direction, opposite of what everyone would expect. This means it may not allow you to use what your case provides for securing cables (definitely with Dell cases). I don't understand why a manufacturer would do this.    Since SATA cables are commodity items, I'd recommend going with some other.

product_title: iHome iP11 Spacesaver Alarm Clock for iPod and iPhone
review_body: We bought this alarm clock for our daughter for Christmas, to use with her 3rd-gen iPod Touch 8Gb.  It's impossible to get the alarm clock to wake to the iPod, even after updating the iPod software (per the iHome support site instructions), and turning off the passcode and auto-lock feature.  If the iPod is turned off (per the instructions), the alarm clock will power up the iPod, but it won't play any music.  Sometimes it won't even do that; sometimes it wakes to the beeper, even if the iPod is docked and Wake-To is set to iPod.    I sent an email to iHome support several days ago, but haven't gotten a reply.  I'm ready to return it to swap for another brand.

product_title: SoundRacer SRV8 Realistic SuperCar V8 Engine Sound Effects
review_body: Seems to be well built.  Works ok.  If you leave it plugged in all the time you have to reset it every time you start your car.  The sounds are pretty good.  It seems like it doesn't match up with my engine just right.  They say in the instructions to set it at a different number of rpms if it doesn't.  I did that but when I slow down to a stop it sometimes goes a little wild.  It is to be understood though, being that it picks up your alternator.      It also faded out very quickly.  It seemed fun for the first 1/2 hour or so I had it.  Now it just lives in my glove box.  Great technology but for the price I wish I hadn't bought it.  I could have bought something else that I would have gotten more use out of.      I guess in all, if you have a lot of money and nothing to do with it, or you need a gift for someone and have no other ideas of what to get them this would be a good buy.  It does bring a few giggles when someone hears it for the first time.

product_title: Sennheiser Premium Earphones -
review_headline: WOW. Audiophiles, you will not be disappointed.
review_body: UPDATE: 2/1/11    I have learned couple things from burning these headphones for almost 24 hours.    1.) Unless the bass really stands out for you, do NOT adjust the bass to the max! To me, I like to listen to a lot of rock, but with the bass on max, my ears begin to hurt after 30 minutes. I prefer almost max, perhaps 3 tick marks. Just a quick tip.    2.) The earbuds fit, but you should possibly get some Comply foam buds if possible! If you find the stock foam earbuds good, you'll find the Comply foam incredible. I currently have some.  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------  Original Review:    I have been an owner of other sets of HiFi headphones, Ultimate Ears (Found not snug within my ears) and Etymotics (More bass please).    But one pair of equipment is different from another. And this is one that will shock you from the minute you click the play button on your iPod or MP3 player.    Some very basic background of me: I am an audiophile. I am willing to find an excellent set of hifi headphones that meet my needs of bass, lyric and instrument clarity. Price is not an option as long as it fulfills my music needs.    These satisfy me and my conditions 3000%! This pair is my new set of headphones I will use to replace my Klipsch S2's.    Pros:  Tunable bass, a plus for me.  Many eartips to try.  Clarity is excellent!    Cons:  Biggest one here: Price (Everyone's saying this. Think about how much money you will put to listen to music in incredibly high quality. If you feel it is worth every penny that your music should sound excellent, this pair of headphones will not disappoint. As another reviewer has said, if you use it over a range of couple years, the price doesn't seem to be too big of a concern.)    Overall, the BEST HiFi headphones I have ever used! Highly recommended for audiophiles!

product_title: Coby Jammerz Platinum High-Performance Isolation Stereo Earphones
review_body: I was searching for good earphones that were cheap and possibly looked nice and stylish, and of course sounded good. I began searching here at Amazon because I know many earphones can be found here. There were many good looking earphones but they were way too expensive and then I saw these Coby Jammerz earphones for a very low price, but then I saw that they were Coby and thought maybe they weren't good quality since most people only trust big name brands like Sony, Philips, Panasonic and many more. But then I decided to give Coby and these earphones a try since they had a very good low price. I purchased these and they arrived when Amazon said they were going to arrive, I guess I can kind of trust Amazon a little bit again since I got an item one day late one time. I opened the package and started to examine them, they did look good and feel good quality. I tried them on my Philips GoGear Vibe (Newer Model) and WOW! they did sound very good with good crisp sound and very good bass. I think they have a little more bass than my other earphones JBuds by JLab even though the JBuds are more famous. If I were to get picky I would want the cord to be a little more longer since my JBuds have a longer cord. From now on I'm going to give other brands a try, sometimes other brands have very good stuff and they don't have to be Sony, Philips, Panasonic or others to have good quality stuff.

product_title: JBL Balboa SUB 10 - 10-Inch Powered Subwoofer (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: I love this sub-woofer, but I had to rate it one star less due to the automatic shutoff causes it to thump a lot. Doesn't seem to make sense that it turns on and off while the Amplifier is still on. Sound quality is great and it really makes a difference when watching action movies, etc. Maybe when I upgrade to a new amplifier the thumping will end, but I don't think it'll make a difference. It is a Sony STR-DG500 amp. If I were to shop for another powered sub-woofer I would not look for and specifically purchase an auto-shutoff version due to this thumping problem.

product_title: Creative Labs Zen Mozaic EZ300 MP3 Player (Black)
review_body: I bought this because I needed an MP3 player that would sync with a Linux, and this is the easiest MP3 player I have used. I had previously used a Zune which is unfortunately forever stuck with Windows. When I first put music on it, I couldn't believe that it was as easy as it was. I literally put my music in the music folder... and that was it. It was on the Zen. Easy. Simple. Not to mention features that the Zen has that you have to pay extra for if you want on a Zune or iPod. Speaker, microphone, more than just English and Spanish languages. Not to mention that for the price I get double the gigs for half the price. This is great. You're getting a superior device and paying less because you are buying the iPod or Zune brand name.

product_title: Yamaha RX-A1000 7.1-Channel Home Theater Receiver (OLD VERSION) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: I haven't had a receiver since my old Denon got stolen... but I'm using the RX-A1000 with 2x Klipsch WF-35 floor standers, 2 x Klipsch WB14 Bookshelves, the Klipsch WC24 center, and 2x Klipsch WS24 surrounds for a 7.1 experience and let me say the Aventage is AWESOME! The sound is so CLEAN. The features are ROBUST. Can you say WEB CONTROL via the web browser on the laptop and streaming FLAC? Fully lossless audio playback is so nice and the sound is amazing. Yamaha didn't overhype this, they outdid themselves and it is trully high fidelity in my opinion. Sounds orgasmic. Would highly reccomend it! Never had the need to turn it into the positive dbs, usually keep it about -17db and -6db when I'm really jammin. Super loud on these Klipsch W series.

product_title: Coby Deep Bass Headphones with Stereo Earphones
review_body: Absolutely adore these headphones. The sound is wonderful and they're incredibly stylish. I didn't, however, care for the earbuds. They don't stay in my ears very well. :(

product_title: JBuds Rugged Metal In-Ear Earbuds Style Headphones with Travel Case
review_headline: Great alternative earbuds @ a great value!!!!
review_body: I know the earphones market is over saturated! Its so overwhelming trying to find the right pick with so many choices and advertising being jammed down our.... Needless to say I am VERY VERY PLEASED with my JLab J4m earbuds. I had looked into all the major brands but I try to stay away from the commercial pricing as much as possible. I was thinking about the Dr Dre beats and such, but based on other's reviews I opted to go more on value and quality over name brand. Their other ear bud lineup seems to also carry higher esteem than most. I like the fact they are flat line cables and also have Kevlar re-enforced material. Whats even better is that have a variety of rubber plugs for your personalized fit. I also like the fact they came with a neat carrying case. Lastly I sided with the J4M style because of the inline mic. I haven't used that much so far but the standard audio jack plug ensures I won't have to worry about taking calls or keeping other audio sounds private when needed!
