product_title: Timex T065S Solar Powered Radio Controlled Atomic Alarm Clock (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Shoddy Construction, okay for the price
review_body: I bought this clock because I wanted a \\"set-and-forget\\" clock that also had a thermometer. My major complaint about this clock is that in the two weeks that I've owned it, it's never been able to sync with the atomic clock! It keeps trying every night and never succeeds. Since returning it is not worth the hassle, I decided to open it up and look inside. (I'm an engineer, with some knowledge of how these circuits work) I was surprised to find that the the circuits inside looked EXTREMELY cheap. There was a dry solder where the battery wire connected to the circuit board. The antenna (for the radio) had its wires shorted. Everything looked very sloppy in general. I then managed to separate the short on the antenna, hoping that it would make the radio work. No luck. The radio sync still doesn't work. Which is hardly surprising considering that the antenna itself is not cleanly wound! It's unevenly wound by hand! Not machine wound. Did I mention that the build quality is horrible?    I don't know if the clock's circuitry has support for managing daylight savings or I have to reset it twice a year. I'll find out in about 4 months I guess. But for the price, I guess it's a decent enough clock. It serves my purpose: Maintains time fairly accurately and has a thermometer. I'd really like to have the clock sync with the atomic clock via the radio though.    Edit (17-Jan-2010): Okay, so the radio feature FINALLY worked out, but it's still kind of flaky, works sometimes, doesn't sometimes. I'm willing to now give this product the benefit of the doubt: Maybe it's my location or something about the construction of my apartment that's the problem. I've revised the rating to 4 stars now. Would give it five stars if only I had not opened up the clock and seen the shoddy construction.

product_title: Sony Ear Clip
review_body: I bought these headphones quite a while ago and after a long period of owning them realized how awful some other headphones really are in comparison. I love these things.  In regards to the sound quality, these are excellent. I use them almost exclusively for my iPod and they are the best I've come across.  A lot of other headphones are horribly tinny but the high end here is bright, crisp and detailed. There's bass here too, but not too much. It's just right. It's subtle and enhances the experience, as opposed to being overly loud and distorted. The balance is almost perfect. I can listen to a wide variety of genres and they all sound equally as good. I don't have to mess with EQ or anything else to get a good sound. It's naturally there.  The design could also be a bit better. The headphones are very comfortable and don't feel like they're crushing your ears, but the problem is that the over the ear design leaks some sound and makes some of the elements sound lower (and annoys anyone standing next to you). The clips are spring clips, which I never found to be a problem. They don't feel durable though (even though they are) and contribute to the sound leakage. Not awful, but not ideal. The interchangeable headphone caps also aren't really a huge draw. I've had them fall off the headphones a few times. The cord is also long, which could be a good or bad thing, depending upon what you're using them for. I'm 5' 5\\" and the cord extends from my toe to forehead, to give a general idea. I don't think these are huge drawbacks but they can be for some so it's worth mentioning.  Despite some of those design flaws the headphones are quite durable and I'm not exactly delicate with them. I've fallen asleep with them. I've tossed them around.  I don't recommend doing any of that but I've had these since June 2009 and they broke a few days ago (November 2010). That's what sparked the review. I realized I was upset they broke and immediately came to Amazon to purchase another pair. I'll probably stick with these for a long as I can imagine.

review_headline: Good for frequent fliers only, if you're lucky enough to get a unit that works
review_body: I bought this product ahead of an international flight. Product claims to reduce \\"environmental noise by up to 85%\\" on the box. Initial impression was that the noise cancelling did an excellent job of cutting out white noise, and high-frequency background noise (eg. aircraft noise, background machinery) but did a poor job of cutting out any external noise within the human vocal range (eg. people talking, other music playing, etc.). Not quite the complete \\"cone of silence\\" I was hoping for but still specifically suitable for air travel. Sound quality was fine for the money, but not audiophile-perfect. The form-factor of the ear-cups was smaller than I expected but they were nonetheless comfortable - I had to fully extend both arms to fit the cups over my ears properly, and even then it was still touching the top of my head. I have a large but not huge head, so if you wear a hat bigger than 7 5/8 these headphones may simply be too small for you.    Follow-up comment: the noise-canceling stopped functioning after only four hours of use. The power light no longer turns on, and I know it's not the batteries fault - I tried four different ones, all of which work fine in a torch, and the unit still doesn't function. Disappointed, as I had high hopes for these - returning for a refund.    Only recommended for frequent fliers with small heads, and even then only if you're lucky enough to get a non-defective unit.

first, this would've gotten 5 stars had it not been for the fact that i couldn't access online features until i performed a usb firmware up date out of the box. granted, it was an easy process. my only other issue is it seems as the volume doesn't go that high. however, that may be in part related to my dated speakers. nevertheless, this system is spectacular and very much upgrade proof. as an aside, the remote is fantastic too in that i was able to ditch all of me other remotes (including my xbox 360 remote) and can now navigate my tv (toshiba 55\\" LED tv), xbox 360, tuner, cable (time warner), and blu-ray player (toshiba) all with my onkyo remote! awesome. i'm overall extremely satisfied. highly recommended purchase. feel free to post questions and i'll be happy to reply.

UPDATE 25 APR 2011: i have upgraded my review to 5 stars as i continue to learn more and more about this system. first off, following some tinkering with the speaker set up menu, the sound volume is now booming. love it. recommend that buyers who utilize the auto configuration microphone incorporated with the tuner consider reviewing and manually modifying the auto configured settings (speaker calibration levels) as this can increase to volume output significantly. this is a VERY easy process that simply involves a few clicks in the menu set up screen. additionally, in retrospect, performing the out of box usb firmware up date was painless as well and shouldn't have detracted from my initial rating. anyway, as above, highly recommend!

product_title: Logitech Squeezebox Boom All-in-One Network Music Player / Wi-Fi Internet Radio (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: A great idea, but so-so execution
review_body: As someone who lives in a hilly, rural area, I'm used to counting myself lucky when I can tune in two or three different radio stations at home. So of course I've found the breadth of content available on the squeezebox to be pretty jaw dropping--it gets practically any radio station in the world or on the internet, and even made it easy to locate my puny little local stations. But once I got over the thrill of listening to Australian morning shows while getting ready for bed in the US, it became clear there are some fairly serious problems here. The sound isn't consistently great: some stations come in well, but others sound tinny and tiny. (This is presumably the station's problem, but it's still an annoyance.) The remote is so small it's guaranteed to be lost or thrown into the wash with my sheets in no time flat. The menu structure requires eye contact with the squeezebox, so there's no easy way to station-surf, even in your favorites list. And the documentation provided with the unit is pretty laughable, so if you're not someone who deals well with the vagaries of unknown technology, you're probably going to find the squeezebox a hassle to set up and use. On the other hand, I'm optimistic that future software updates will address some of these annoyances and that I'll be using my squeezebox boom semi-happily for years to come.

I bought [[ASIN:B001GUPEMW Altec Lansing UHP326 BackBeat Titanium noise-isolating earphones]]which have wonderful sound, but wouldn't stay in my ears and hurt. I'll stick with them, but I wish they had more boom boom pow :(

product_title: Apple iPod touch 8GB (4th Generation)
review_body:
After saving up and waiting for this cool little toy to come out, I finally got it in yesterday. As soon as I got it opened up, I looked at the hardware of it all. I first noticed the slimness of the device which is real nice, then the two camera front and back, my name imprinted on the device (from Apple), the on/off button being switched onto the right side from left, and finally the volume buttons being separated instead of just being a rocker.
After I got all my data synced to the Ipod Touch, I begin playing with it for a few hours. I notice that the battery seemed to drain fast when having wifi on. The device got rather warm on my hands and they began to sweat. My hands sweating lead to having my device all greasy and oily which is BAD. I hate that this device gets so warm, because my device is encoded with finger prints and smudges. Besides that when I was playing with device, it took me a second to getting used to because I'm new to apple products. It is very fast to scroll though the apps, wonderful retina display, and I love how it loads everything up so fast! I had already downloaded apps onto my Itunes before I got my device, so I was all set. The games took a few seconds to load and depending on what game you get, the graphics are gold. It's fast in frame rate and I never experienced a lag when I was multitasking as well in the back round. When you are viewing the screen, it's rare to even notice the pixels. The only time when you do is when you mostly do is when you load up a low resolution app/movie/video or zoom in on a picture. When I was hearing the audio though the internal speakers, it got kind of rough when you begin to turn it up all the way. I didn't like that it didn't have crisp high quality audio when full blast, but then that's why you put on head phones. I just think Apple could of made the speakers a little nicer, since it is an MP4 player at heart...
The Apps that Apple were bragging about such as Facetime or Game center, I haven't tried out yet and there isn't much to it yet. All I know is that the camera will be great for video chatting, but it's not really great for taking pictures. Picture taking is one of the down sides to this product, it has very low resolution and you always have to manually fix the focus and always find a spot with really good light. The videos aren't half bad, but it could be better. It would be nice to at least have the option of auto focus...

Overall this product is amazing, like Apple said it's like the Iphone 4 without the phone...and the quality of it as well. It's very fun to play with for hours on end, great for listening to your music and watching movies/TV shows. It gets rather hot and makes your palm sweat which will make your device look like crap. It has a wonderful display and the speakers are good with the volume turn down. It's great for people of all ages, even people with a hard time with technology.

product_title: Logitech Speaker for iPod and iPhone
review_headline: Press firmly down on the "kickstand" to secure the speaker!
review_body:
It is amazing to me how many people write bad reviews for products when the actual problem is user error. This speaker system is fantastic considering portability, price, sound, and design. I would estimate that more than half of the negative reviews that I have read about the Logitech S715i on this site and others is due to the inability of consumers to read instructions or properly use the product. The dock cover that converts into a very sturdy stand is actually quite secure. The kickstand has a metal screw that fits quite firmly into a rubber gasket on the back of the speaker, creating a very secure and level platform which also prevents any rattling that may occur with moving parts like this on light-weight speaker. Yes, you must press firmly on the stand so that it seats properly, so I can understand some confusion right out of the box. However, a simple inspection of the speaker should alleviate any frustration. Its also hard to miss the factory installed yellow sticker attached to the dock cover/kickstand with a barney-style diagram on how to press firmly down in order to secure the stand. Some reviewers actually returned this speaker because it \\"did not support the weight of their iPhone.\\" I read one review where someone actually recommended leaning the speaker against a wall to support it. Please learn how to use a product before you waste your energy writing a negative review.

I just received the speaker today, so I cannot comment on the battery life yet. It is frustrating that I must remove my iPod case in order to connect it. The remote is also disappointing. These two issues preclude me from giving it 5 stars. However, its difficult not to say that the Logitech S715i performs very well for a compact and very STURDY speaker system!

product_title: Goldsource STU-750 Step Up/Down Voltage Transformer Converter - AC 110/220 V - 750 Watt
review_headline: does exactly what I bought it for
review_body:
I moved to the US from the UK, and took my PS3 and some other small electrical items with me. The PS3 won't work with a simple plug adaptor (the green light came on, but nothing happened), so I found out that I needed a voltage transformer. I bought this size (750W) because it has enough voltage to spare (apparently this is recommended).

The unit is smaller than I expected - I plugged it into the mains, plugged the PS3 into the UK power socket on the front, switched it on, and it all works

I leave it on for a few hours at a time and it runs very quietly (a very faint hum). I left it on overnight once while the PS3 downloaded content, and it was still running fine in the morning.

We have also used this with a food mixer we brought over from the UK.

Instructions were very clear - when it arrived I had to set it to transform from 110 to 240 - it was a simple matter of moving a pin on the back of the box.

It also came with 2 spare fuses

UPDATE - TWO YEARS LATER

This is still running really well. We switch it on every morning and then off again at night, but I don't think that's really necessary. If the house is absolutely silent you can notice a slight hum from this unit but otherwise no complaints. The UK PS3 is still using it every day as is our UK wireless router.

They aren't showing up in the library, they don't seem to be on the device at all until I attach it to my computer where I can find them easily.

product_title: Sony MDR-XB500 40mm XB Diaphragm Driver Extra Bass Headphones
review_body: Yep, these things bump.  Highs are recessed, mids are recessed, and the bass is cranked--and it goes all the way down.  (Oh yeah!)  But the \\"lows\\" do include a bit of low mids.  The \\"bass\\" boost seems to go as high as ~300 Hz.  (I think anything over ~150Hz isn't true \\"bass,\\" but that's just me.)  This seems to make the bass a bit less clean and more bloated.  Whale-ish, even.  Not that that's necessarily a bad thing...      As for comfort, they fit my tall-narrow head just fine.  The pads are wonderfully soft, but they can get sweaty and stifling after a while.  Clamping pressure is a bit higher than I like, which seems to induce fatigue after an hour or so.  What I wouldn't give for some puffy velour pads on these!  (Sony, are you listening?)    All in all, they're among the best basshead cans for the buck.

product_title: C2G/Cables to Go 27028 - Firewire 6-Pin Female 4-Pin Male Adapter
review_body: Does exactly as advertised, takes the 6-pin firewire to a 4-pin firewire to connect to my computer.  Delivered extremely fast and in new condition.

product_title: Antennas Direct
review_body: I had been looking at antennas for the lo9ngest time, always circling back to this one, but never pulled the trigger. Moving into a new house, and wanting to finally watch an NFL game, I pulled the trigger on this one, and went with the pole and preamp package. So glad I did.    The antenna itself is easy to put together - and take portions apart if not put together correctly. It mounts on the pole perfectly, and you need this because it cannot stand on its own.    So I set the antenna up on the first floor of my home first, complete with preamp booster. It pulled in a few channels, but not all the ones I wanted. SInce that was a test, the next thing I did was put the antenna in my walk-up attic, essentially a third floor. Without the preamp, it pulled in a couple more channels, but with the preamp, it yanked down twice as many, and crystal clear too. Despite being listed as a one directional outside antenna, this is great multidirectional unit.    I am 85 miles away from the stations I am pulling in.

I saw these cables on Amazon.com and admit that I was skeptical since all the cables at the stores were anywhere from $50 - >$100. I decided to try it based on a majority of reviews being 5 star.  I am NOT disappointed, what a great purchase! We have a 3D Samsung system and the cable works flawlessly. product_title: Panasonic Lightweight Headphones with XBS Port
review_body: I bought these to use on a recent trip.  I didn't want to risk expensive headphones getting lost, so I was excited to find well-reviewed headphones at such an awesome price.  They are worth every penny!  I will confess that I am not an audiophile, but not once did I notice a lack of sound quality whether listening to movies or music.  I have used them every day since in a number of situations and they have proven themselves to be very durable.  I also love that they are comfortable and low-profile.  Not a fashion statement per se, but they don't draw attention either.  Buy buy buy!

product_title: Sony Docking System for iPod with Wireless Subwoofer
review_body: I listened to a lot of Ipod docking systems at local electronic retailers in the area I live in, but when I listened to the Sony with the wireless subwoofer I knew that it was the one I was going to buy. Like a lot of other reviews here,I was thinking about buying the Bose system until I listened to this one.The subwoofer just fills out the sound of the music.I bought the Sony for a $100 less than the cheapest Bose system.I have been listening to the Sony system for two weeks now and love it!!!!!!!!!!!

product_title: APC Back-UPS Pro
review_body: I am returning this unit. The noise level is unacceptable.  It is high time APC starts paying attention to noise.  Their new models are noisier than the older ones.

product_title: Onkyo HT-S5300 7.1-Channel Home Theater Receiver and Speaker Package with iPod Dock (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Great Product, Great Sound, Easy Setup!
review_body: This is a great product, and a great value! Packaging was very solid. And setup was easy, wires are color coded and everything, so you know which are the longer ones. when using the HDMI love the menu on screen. The worst part about this is the remote.. Kind of crappy, and doesnt fit into the look if you have a high end setup. The one thing that bothers me that I was unaware of is that it if you are using a component input, then you must also run a secondary component input to the TV... I was under the impression that the receiver would transmit and incoming component video signal to the TV through the HDMI output. 1 more cable to run but other than that it is a great system and sound is awesome. The subwoofer is big, and self powered so it gets a lot of punch, but it is bigger than I expected.

product_title: Apple iPod touch 8GB (4th Generation)
review_body: This device is fast, feature-rich, clear, and incredibly thin. It is easy reading ebooks -- I have put all my Kindle books on it, no extra charge. Apps work great: sketching with Sketchbook Mobile (virtually instant response), watching Netflix or PBS shows, no hitches in the streaming, even making music (if my efforts can be called music) with a keyboard app. I sync calendar and contacts with MS Office Outlook, and songs and photos with iTunes. I haven't tried loading movies yet.  I have a Nokia E71 (also thin) and carry it and the iPod, the Nokia for phoning, typing, some ebooks already on it, email, and web. I have a $12.27 app on the Nokia that makes it a portable router, so the iPod Touch, which has WiFi, can even surf the web and check email with its bigger screen anywhere my Nokia can.  I learned of the iPod Touch from my grandkids, so I knew what I was getting before I ordered. The Amazon site was quite accurate.  The only downside I can think of is the typing, which is slower than a keypad because it's so easy to hit the wrong character on the touchscreen.  Great device.

product_title: Belkin 6-Outlet Home and Office Power Strip Surge Protector with 4-Foot Power Cord, 720 Joules (BE106000-04)
review_body:
Great product. This is my 3rd one. Just plug everything in and your covered. Several years ago I lost a TV and a Surround Sound Amp to power surges. Sense then I have been building up 3 Home Theater and Computer Systems. At the top of the list for each system is a Belkin surge protector.

The area I live in, in Phoenix is prone to power surges, and I have never lost a piece of equipment that was plugged into the Belkins.

Belive me, power surges are VERY BAD THINGS. The power surge that killed my old SS Amp caused a BANG to emit from the speakers, that was so loud, my first thought was, someone had fired a weapon outside my bedroom window. But then I smelled the arcid odor of burnt up electronics.

Do yourself a favor and plug your valuable electronics into one or more of these surge protectors.

product_title: Timex Expedition Trail Series Mens Chrono/Alarm/Timer Black
review_body:
For more years then I can remember I have been using two old Timex watches (an Ironman and an Ironman Tirathalon)to tell time. Although adequage at first, an irritating phenomon began to occur. As my eyes got older and older the numbers on both watches got smaller and smaller. Things got so bad I was required to use 2.50 power off-the-shelf Walgreen glasses just to read the time. Bummer! So when the batteries finally died, rather then buy two new batteries, it made more sense to me to spend money on a new watch, preferrably one that could be read without glasses. After all, the right watch is one that can be read whether or not eye glasses are handy or not.

A Google search for watches with large letters lead me to some exceptionally fine looking watches that were also exceptionally expensive and far too nice looking for the rough treatment my watches receive. So, I began pouring over reviews of watches on Amazon.com and bingo! the $30 \\"Times T49750 Expedition\\" appeared and looked like what I needed. But looks on a computer page can be deceiving. Although I worried the watch might disappoint me, Amazon's great return policy gave me the confidence to take a chance and buy it. I am glad I did.

The watch is plain looking, which suits me fine. It possesses numerous features such as: time, date, hourly chimes if desired. three alarms, a timer, 12 or 24 hour display, a chrono mode for recording lap times or sprints, plus more. For me, it is enough just to be able to read the time and date. By my measurement the time numbers stand about 8-9mm high, more then tall enough for my eyes to see without the need to use 2.50 X glasses. The band is slightly wider and seems more sturdy then other bands I've had, a good thing. I also like that the watch can be laid flat on a surface. The band also can be folded on the watch and itself so the watch can be held in one hand as a stop watch. So far, I'm enjoying this watch. When the battery on this baby dies, I'll definitely replace the battery.ly replace the battery.

review_body: This is one of the lowest-profile wall mounts I could find.  It's great.  Easy to install and mount the TV. We installed the TV only to realize when we sit on our sofa, the ceiling fan light reflects off the TV right in the middle of the TV.  We ended up ordering another mount that can tilt. It doesn't look as slick, but is necessary.

product_title: Coby Dynamic Digital Stereo Mini Ear-bud
review_body: I ordered these headphones after my JVC headphones broke. I just needed a temporary pair until I returned the school where the sell the JVC ones for really cheap. I ordered these and was very disappointed. One headphone arrived damage which already made me upset and to top it off the sound quality was HORRIBLE. The headphones that came with my blackberry had much better sound quality. These headphones kind of remind of the ones you find in a dollar store and clearly cost em more than one dollar. Even for a temporary pair, these headphones were not worth the price.

product_title: ASUS RT-N16 - Wireless router - 4-port switch - Gigabit Ethernet - 802.11b/g/n (draft) - desktop
review_body: This router has been my worst and I've owned d-link (power supply died) and belkin (radio card died and got unreliable).  I have also delt with netgear (plain died) and linksys (couldnt handle bandwidth/users on first one, second one overheaded and burned out the radio card) dying on me at friend's houses.      This was my first foray into trying ASUSTek routers and it was a mistake.  I picked this one because of the price and the features and that a friend had suggested it was a brand he has used and was very happy with.  For me, I'm not so happy.    The stock oem firmware was bad.  Uptimes of about 5 days.  I updated the firmware twice with asus's firmwares and now longest uptime run has been around 30 hours before some failure.  Either the router loses it's ip to the modem and wont reconnect or the thing freezes up completely and wont answer any dhcp requests from clients.    One day I was backing up my g wireless laptop to the 100mbit wired desktop, moving about 35 gigs of files over the wireless, yea excessive when I could use wired but it needed testing.  Transfer went along just fine so I went back to my main pc with 1000mbit wired connection to continue browsing the internet.  I have a 6mb dsl line and the router managed to eek out barely enough packets from the lan to the wan connection to complete a dns lookup and download the header of one page.  It was like dialup all over again.  I killed the transfer on the laptop and speed on the main desktop went to normal.  Not good.    Unit runs hotter than previous routers.  I've had to put a fan on it which helped the stability a bit.    Cant say much for the usb features.  I tried it with ntfs and ext3 formatted drives, which it read ok.  But with the instability I havent left a drive connected on it for very long.  I'll keep my nas.

product_title: JLab JBuds Hi-Fi Noise-Reducing Ear Buds (Purple)
review_body: I have been trying to find a pair of earbuds for my ipod that were inexpensive, good quality and comfortable.  I found them !  These are a great value for the money, I was told by my wife that she wants a pair now.

product_title: Polk Audio PSW505 12-Inch Powered Subwoofer (Single, Black)
review_body:
This is a wonderful \\"consumer\\" piece of sound equipment for your home theater and it is phenomenal at that. If you're in a band and need an industrial subwoofer for your concerts, forget this product (try something like these: [[ASIN:B0033WMNZW Peavey PV 118 300W Powered 18 Inch Subwoofer]] or a [[ASIN:B00318D4XI Mackie HD1801 18-inch Powered Subwoofer]]) --- as this Polk is out of your league and not what this product is intended for. Also, if you've just spent $5,000 on an Pioneer ICE amp, this product is probably not for you either: you're too discriminating or just have money to blow and you'll probably wind up with something in a different league.

If on the other hand, you have an amp like a Pioneer VSX-1120, and a 55\\" to 60\\" TV with in-wall speakers, this subwoofer is right up your alley. It looks good in a living room and just fits with the decor. Also you get great subwoofer performance. And definitely if you don't have a subwoofer with your in-wall sound system, you're probably missing something. I know I was. I was missing this PSW505. Adding the subwoofer entirely transformed my listening experience and mind you I have 7 in-wall high powered surround loudspeakers wiht 8\\" woofers but there was a \\"fullness\\" missing from the music. This subwoofer did the trick on my reasonably sized family room.

Here are some answers to questions I had:

So what does long-throw mean? It means that the subwoofer cone moves a lot to reproduce the sounds. This is good but requires a big amp, which this thing has 300watts of continous and 460 peak (WOW!).

It has speaker outputs (screw post) for speaker pass through
It has has RCA inputs with a crossover turn knob.
It has an LFE in (some people hate and some people love). For me not being a huge audiophile, the LFE is great because my AMP has an LFE out.

It has an on/off/standby switch. In standby the unit powers on by itself when you system does and goes to sleep when not in use. Great feature.

At the moment this product is very hard to find right now and is going for near $500. This is the old model and the new models from Polk don't appear to have as much power so this is a high demand product right now. If you can find it, get it. You will not be dissappointed. It will shake your floors and I only have it at 50%.At the moment this product is very hard to find right now and is going for near $500. (our old one had that)  both ends connect securely and are not loose.  got it in a very timely manner too.

product_title: Next Generation Remote Control Extender
review_body: After extensive searching for a solution for my bedroom tv I found this on Amazon.  I initially looked for a name brand like Logitech but due to reviews went with this instead.  After a month of use it has continued to work perfectly.  I have it set up under the bed with the tv receiver and it is absolutely hidden.  This allows me to use the remote as normal with the LCD tv on the wall.  Couldn't ask for more.  No comment yet on battery life but hopefully it lasts awhile as well.

product_title: Philips Fidelio SBD7500 30-Pin iPod/iPhone Speaker Dock
review_headline: Day one here, but a very happy camper....
review_body: Let me first say that shipping speed with Amazon can be amazing at times. The email said that I should expect this on 4/1 and it arrived today at work! Under promise and over deliver!     Have my Amazon stuff delivered to work, since we were slow I could not wait to open it up and try it out based on my previous purchase recently of the DS3000 for my better half. And this one is IMO even better sounding than the DS3000! Connected my iPhone 4 with a bumper attached and the sound was great. Rich in bass, which is missing in small speaker systems sometimes. My boss walked by and liked the sound, and asked how I was planning on using it. Said I got it for those times I am stuck off the sales floor for hours on end a day or two each week. She said... great now every one will be wanting to spend time off the sales floor working in the back areas. LOL Told her not to worry, it was designed for the iPod and iPhone; not telling her that it included a cable to connect the DS7500 to headphone jacks. May have to charge rent to my co-workers to use it.     What I like about the DS7500 so far:    - Relatively small and compact. Something I can see traveling with.     - With the above, it comes with a nice travel case.     - The sound is close to awesome IMO.    What I dislike so far with the DS7500:    - Batteries are a bit hard to get to fit right at times. Very tight space given my large fingers to get them to pop in.     - The flip-out stand seems to be flimsy, not solid feeling. Along with the above I had to go back and make sure that I could closed the battery cover properly to allow the flip-out stand to close properly.     - The case includes a detachable side-pocket for what I would think would be the AC adapter. I be darned to figure out how to get the AC adapter to fit and still be attached to the main case. Note to Philips - make the AC adapter one of those with flip-out prongs. (though it does appear that the prongs can detach, but none of us were able to figure it out at work! LOL) .    The form factor seems to beg for iPad compatibility - but the kick-out stand is the limiting factor. Have yet tried my iPad with this dock - but can see why iPad owners want to use this speaker dock with the iPad - seems to beg for iPad usage.     For me I went with the DS7500 over the DS7550 because I did not want to be locked in to their rechargeable battery system. Looking at Philip's website I could not see a clear reason to spend more....    In the end I am so far happy with my purchase....

product_title: PYLE PT260A 200-Watt Digital AM/FM Stereo Receiver
review_body: This is a great deal. I recommend it highly. The only drawbacks are that you don't get an input for a headphone jack (just 2 inputs for microphones). You get an input for CD/DVD and Auxillary and you can also play your IPOD/MPG3 on it, so everything goes. The AM antenna isn't so easy to hook up but the FM works great with your own antenna. Also on my particular unit, the input selector button doesn't always work but the remote does it anyway, so no big deal. Overall, great sound, 200 watts for great money. If they only had such a deal when I was younger and I could get away with blasting my stereo.

product_title: Sennheiser Closed Circumaural Hi-Fi Headphone
review_body: I bought this product because of the price, the brand and the rave reviews here at Amazon.    Pros  -Good price  -Good sound  -Good durability    Cons  -Burn in time required  About 24 hours I think is sufficient  -Low bass  Others say the sound that the headphones make is more natural. That could be true, but I personally would have liked more bass.  -Low volume  I am primarily using my PC to push these headphones but I did try it on my nokia phone. For both applications I thought the volume response could have been better. I have to tune to almost full volume to get the same volume I would get on other headphones at half volume.  -Cord too long and thin    All in all a good buy for the low price.   But if I had another chance, I'd probably skip these and try another.

product_title: Sennheiser Professional Headphones with Sound Channeling
review_headline: Amazing Sound Quality, But Impractical For Mobile Use
review_body: I owned these headphones and was thoroughly blown away by the clarity of the music. Personally, the sound was much more \\"true\\" than can be heard in any other brand such as Bose, Beats, Sony, or Shure. I felt as if I were in a studio listening to the music. Very great experience.     Please understand that these open, dynamic headphones allow you to enjoy the music and also everyone else around you. I actually got complaints that everyone else could hear my music clearly. It didn't matter how loud I had the music, the sound resonated to those around me.     A con to me was the stereo jack and the headphone adapter. I hated that I had to have an adapter just to plug the headphones into my computer or mp3 device. The stereo jack should not have been the primary jack, but the adapter.     Since I personally did not care for everyone else listening to my music and the annoying stereo jack, I have decided to switch to the Sennheiser HD448 Closed headphones.

product_title: Shure E3g Gaming Edition Sound Isolating Earphones for Portable Gaming Devices
review_headline: Last forever with a great sound
review_body: I bought these bad boys in the summer of 2004 and they're still going strong. I use them every single day for working out and around the house as well as at the office. They have clear sound with great separation. Most people think they're not bass-heavy enough, but I think they're giving a nice, tight, flat bass that is really what studio monitors are all about. They don't boom or reverberate, but that's really not what they're supposed to do. If you want great, clear sound that will outlast you, get these buds.

product_title: Sony Walkman NW-S706F - Digital player
review_headline: By far, this is the BEST mp3 player I've ever owned!
review_body:
I was up in Canada visiting an ex-girlfriend and the 256MB Philips Nike PSA player I had for the trip just died on me while lifting one day so I had to purchase a new one until I could get the Nike PSA repaired back home. We went to Future Shop where I saw a sweetheart of a deal on this (it was marked down to $79) and because of the convenient size (trust me, it's small) and being that I am and always have been an audiophile so the 4GB flash memory would allow me to load a considerable amount of lossless files (I won't listen to mp3s because it's a lossy format stripped of the highs and lows that give music its depth, thus making it sound three-dimensional),I went ahead and bought it. For about eight months, I had amazing performance with absolutely no problems whatsoever. During a 10-day sojourn to my vacation house on the Outer Banks, the noise canceling aspect of the headphones stopped working. AAAARRRRRGHHHHHHH!

Well, that was a long time ago and I couldn't pull myself to spending more on a set of noise cancelling headphones that I had originally spent on the player, so I just listened with the ambient noise creeping in through my Shure earbuds (even though they are great headphones, they aren't noise cancelling).

On the bright side of this dark and dreary occurrence, Sony.ca has put me in touch with their parts dealer so I could purchase the original set of earbuds that came with the player and I was finally able to get back to listening! Also, the ATRAC codec has somewhat gone by the wayside and there aren't many converters for Windows 7 to convert my FLAC and Apple Lossless music collection into ATRAC Lossless, so I will be trying to convert the flash-based memory to exFAT or FAT32 at the very least.

I apologize to digress the way that I did, but even though I have had problems, that is the story of my life and I'm sure you won't have similar problems. While this unit is no longer available through Amazon, I have seen it at several other sites. So if you see it, BUY IT! You won't be sorry...So if you see it, BUY IT! You won't be sorry...

review_body: I purchased the X-Mini II previously and the Satechi SD offers the same great amazing sound in such a portable product. The ability to use SD cards to listen to your music is awesome. Great value for the price so highly recommended.

product_title: ESQ35 ES90VI Headset
review_headline: Outstanding mids, weak highs, booming bass.
review_body:
I ordered these as a gold box deal for $58. At that price, these are hard to beat.

I currently own 8 pairs of cans ranging from JBuds J2's all the way to the Shure SE530's. I owned a mobile DJ business for several years and am very particular about audio quality. These buds perform extremely well with Rap/R&B, female vocalists, and audio books. They do not perform as well as I would like for classical music and classic rock. The mids and bass can be overwhelming with certain types of music. If you listen to a lot of Rap and/or Pop music, these should work very well for you.

Something to keep in mind with these buds is the type of tips you use. I am a big fan of Comply foam bud tips on the vast majority of my buds. I do not recommend using them with this set. The foam tips are notorious for absorbing some of the highs while enhancing the bass. These buds need no enhancement on the mids and lows. I highly recommend using a silicon based bud tip to get the best audio quality out of these buds.

Last but not least, I would recommend keeping an eye out for the Ultimate Ears SuperFi5's. I have seen them as a gold box deal and I think they are better overall sound quality for the same price.

This machine was less than $29 delivered to my front door. Outstanding value if you want to play all DVD formats. It is also one of the smallest players that I have ever seen.

review_body:
Initially I was quite displeased with this product. It took me awhile to figure out the product but the effort seems to be worth it. It's definitely not use out of the box product like an Ipod. It's a completely different type of music player.

I was expecting it to use Windows Media Player to upload the music on to it. From the manufacture's website I found out that it only sometimes works with WMP and certainly on with Windows XP. My Devise will not use WMP for my MicroSD card but the internal memory it works just fine. The XP part was a surprise for me because I had thought the world was beginning to move on from XP. However, the best way to put music onto the device is to simply drag and drop the music files onto it (here the OS doesn't matter anymore :)

What I'm getting at is that this MP3 acts a lot more like a computer does when it handles these files. It allows you to go to the different folders and find the \\"album\\" or more accurately: folder/directory that you are looking to listen to. This means that if you use a MicroSD card, all of your music will not be together and you will need to remember in which area you put the file you want. I would call this a plus and minus(really more of a minus). The problem with this quicker and easier way of putting music on the devise is that it assumes that your file paths are named in such a way that if you had to you could find the music file which is certainly not always the case because WMP and Itunes do all of that work behind the scenes. Also, it assumes you have well named files. The plus is that making a playlist is super easy, just put all of those songs in the same folder.

From what I have found, this devise eliminates the need for computer-based media software. Which is very cool in my book. It's literally a USB storage device that plays the files that you can navigate to just like in windows. It is however very nice to still use WMP for the internal memory due to the XML file that gives us the Album, song names, artist, and so on. in this way it's so much more like a computer then it's competitors.

product_title: Apple iPod touch 8GB (4th Generation)
review_body:
I have this iPod since 2 weeks. Everything works fine except it has issues with WiFi connection.
It does not work properly with many routers. I tested it with 4 different routers in 4 locations and there is always the same problem. The connection is very slow and the application which needs strong connection do not work well. I searched in Internet and found out that many iPod users have the same problem. Actually the only website who does not mention this problem with iPod, is the Apple website. I went to Apple store and the Apple-guy tested it with their WiFi in store and, no wonder, everything was fine. Because I assume they have routers which are optimized on Apple products. I believe Apple knows about this problem but does not speak about it. I am very disappointed with this product.

Update: I found out that IPod WiFi does not work properly with 802.11g and older versions. This is a shame. I have to upgrade my router to solve the problem.

product_title: Philips in-Ear Headphones Comfort Plus
review_body: Some reviewing this product say the cable is too short or just adequate, but I found it to be just right with not hanging down and getting caught up while using the headphone. From the plug-in to the ear buds, the cable measures exactly 4'. With the 3 different size ear buds that are provided, you're sure to find a good fit; and I love both the sound quality as well as the volume.  I wear hearing aids and have had a problem with both hearing and comfort using other headphones.  These can be worn for hours with no discomfort and they pump stereo sound out like you would not believe! Naturally I can't wear my hearing aids and the ear buds at the same time.  Yet with wearing only the ear buds I've had to reduce the volume on my PC...and the clarity is crystal-clear.    Also, if you're fortunate in finding Beach Audio has the Philips SHE9750 available (or any other audio device you're looking for), I strongly recommend purchasing from them. Not only do they offer the lowest price and fastest delivery, they're also very helpful, professional, and courteous.

product_title: Logitech Harmony One Universal Remote with Color Touchscreen (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Great Way to Clear the Coffee Table
review_body: I received the Harmony One as a gift this past Christmas. Initially, I was leery of another universal remote and didn't necessarily believe that this remote would function well, if fact I anticipated returning the remote. However, after two weeks of flawless use, I doubt I'll ever buy a non-Logitech remote. The pc/internet installation program provided worked great and I had my entire system programmed and running within three hours--most of my time was spent entering and downloading my favorite channels list.     The only drawbacks I encountered were the repositioning of custom buttons within the Logitech installation program--the user is forced to click an arrow up or down at each position (think Netflix queue rank ordering without any option to type position number)--and the fact that an additional adapter ($40) is needed for the remote to work with a PS3, though that's an issue with Sony and not Logitech.    Overall, I'm very satisfied and would recommend this remote anyone trying eliminate the remote control pile on the coffee table.

product_title: Onkyo HT-S6300 7.1-Channel Home Theater Receiver and Speaker System (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: I recently had a Panasonic home theater in the box system die on me that was 5 years old.  Because it was a 5 DVD disc system that used a special cable to send both power and signal to the sub, once the DVD player was toast, the sub was also toast. After this experience, I decided it would be best to get a receiver and then begin acquiring pieces for a system so that if anything ever went wrong again, I would only need to replace the malfunctioning component itself. I saw this unit at $500 and thought if I buy this receiver that already comes with speakers and sub, then I won't need anything else. I was a little wary about buying another in the box system, but after reading all the reviews, I decided to go ahead and do it.      I just got the system set up recently so I can't speak on durability, but the speakers and sub sound absolutely excellent. I have the sub volume control only up a quarter and it's booming.  Setup was a breeze. I'm using the 22 gauge cable that was already in place from the last system(which is the same gauge that comes with it) while I wait for the more expensive cable to arrive. Looking forward to seeing how it sounds with thicker cable.      The Ipod Dock is a little touchy but is still a great feature. It played a video from my Ipod on the TV with no trouble at all, which I didn't even know it could do. So far so very good!

product_title: Speaker Brackets
review_headline: Looks ugly with speakers using only one mounting screw.
review_body: I bought these for my Take 5 speakers. They do not fit. Period. Nor will they fit any speaker with a single mounting hole.    These are designed for speakers with two mounting holes. The Energy speakers have one 1/4-20 threaded mounting hole and one keyed hole for easy hanging. Unless you're willing to fabricate a bracket to go between this mount and the Energy speakers these will not fit...  Unless you're happy with sloppy work.    I even tried removing the bracket that mounts on the wall so I could use these backwards, ie. screw the bracket into the speaker. No go. The threaded portion is metric. The Energy speakers have 1/4-20 thread.     If you have speakers that use a single 1/4-20 threaded mounting hole buy something else.    ----------------  Amended comment...    Bren McRae made a comment to another review in response to a comment I made. These will work with the Energy speakers. When I opened the box, I saw no instructions. They were buried, I had removed one bracket and the mounting hardware and didn't look any farther. If you buy these, instructions are included!     I followed Mr. McRae's suggestion and it works. But as others have noted, the result is ugly. Other brackets will look better.    I've changed my rating to four stars from two.

product_title: Onkyo TX-SR508 7.1-Channel Home Theater Receiver (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: Ordered this on a Sunday and showed up Friday, free super-saver shipping.  My system: this receiver, polk psw10, bose 301 mains, bose 100 surrounds, polk rm6752 center.  Inputs: DirecTV HD-DVR, AppleTV.    Lots of tweaking to get the sound right (due to inexperience) but it's fun to try out different settings.  Used the Audyssey set-up to start and then tweaked the speaker setup for my ears.  So far, this system sounds nice and clean.  The HDMI switching of sources is seamless and am not experiencing any handshake problems.  Surround sound is excellent.  I probably will replace the Bose 301 speakers with matching Polk versions since there are some balance issues between the center channel and the mains.  I've never really liked the 301s, but after 15+ years they are quite usable. Surprisingly, the Bose 100s sound pretty good with this receiver.  With an older Marantz, these speakers plain sucked.    I highly recommend this inexpensive solution, you will not be disappointed!

review_body: I purchased this from amazon in December, 2010 based on 10 reviews, all of which gave it 5 stars (today there are (12) 5-star reviews plus mine)!  (As far as I can tell, we can only get it from amazon in the US at this time).  Delivery was very prompt, and I received it today.  I listen mainly to classical music and to bluesy rock, and I've been trying it out on my Sansa mp3 player.  I'm VERY satisfied with the sound quality, which was my main concern, as I can't tolerate poor quality because that drives me nuts trying to imagine how the music SHOULD sound!  I wish I could get a little more volume out of it, and I plan a trip to Radio Shack tomorrow to look for an extender for what I estimate to be a 3-&-a-half-inch audio cable (if you pick up your mp3 player, you'll have this little thing dangling from the end of it). product_title: 2.4 Ghz Wireless Headphone
review_headline: This is an OK Product at Best
review_body:
The first problem that I encountered with this product is that the re-chargeable batteries that it came with were corroded. So before I could even get to use them, I had to purchase a fresh set of re-chargeable batteries. (This is evidence that either the product was in the warehouse a very long time, or they just installed the very, very cheapest batteries that they could have found!)

With that aside, the adventure of using this headphone began. Unless you want to get a loud shout in your ear drums, set the volume down before putting them on. The Range is not too bad, maybe around 20 feet or so, but if you are in an area with other wireless devices, you can experience weird side effects. Also there is an operational hum, this will only be heard between songs, or where there is supposed to be silence.

Because of the batteries and the transmitter, this is a big and heavy unit to carry on your head for an extended period of time. It maybe good if you want to strengthen your neck muscles.

Generally, the units are not defective per say, just poor workmanship, so if you need a top notch item, this is NOT it. For casual home use, it may be acceptable, only if you can get it at a bargain price.

product_title: JBuds Rugged Metal In-Ear Earbuds Style Headphones with Travel Case
review_headline: Right bud stopped working after less than 2 months
review_body: Loved the buds while they worked. I found them comfortable and the sound to be quite good, though I wouldn't call myself an audiophile. That's why I can't give them 1 star. That said, the main reason I wanted them was all the \\"durable/rugged\\" talk, my last $15 Skull Candy earbuds having failed after only a month or two. I used these a grand total of one time while running. The rest was study duty.  Just yesterday the right earbud decided it didn't want to work. It isn't quite dead but the sound is so low that it might as well be. JLabs are supposed to be good with exchanges so that doesn't concern me, but waiting however many weeks I have to wait for a replacement pair is little consolation with a big exam next week and knowing that I can't study properly without good tunes.  Being heavy and kevlar-reinforced and whatnot is all well and good until an earbud fails for no apparent reason. If you're looking for \\"rugged\\" in the sense that they keep working for a long time, look elsewhere. These just seem rugged on the outside.  UPDATE 1/19/12: Finally got around to filing a warranty claim and was very impressed to see that JLab didn't even want my broken set sent back. Got a new set in the mail a few days later. Phenomenal customer service for sure.

product_title: WeSC Oboe Headphone
review_body: PROS ----------->  1) They look great  2) Sound is pretty good. Bass has a nice strong boom but the mids/highs are pretty muddy.  3) Cord length is good. It's longer than average headphones allowing for extra movement/room - but not too long where it would get in the way or be too loose.      *this is WITH the extension cord though. The cord length without the extension is literally just over 12 inches or so.. so I have know idea what purpose/thinking behind that was.  4) Cord material is probably the one great thing about these headphones - it's very rough/durable compared to most headphone wires.   5) They cancel outside noise quite well!  CONS ---------->  6) THEY ARE SOO UNCOMFORTABLE!!! Sure, they're fine for 10min max - but after that I literally start getting a headache they're so gosh darn tight! (and you can't adjust em)        *the one advantage to this is that if you where them while skateboarding or any physical activity, they  certainly won't fall off.  7) Headphone jack = crap.  The way the little headphone jack/plugin is designed (similiar to ipod earphones where it's straight up with no 90 degree bend in it) makes it really hard not to bend that part of the wire (especially if your carrying your device in your pocket) which in turn causes the plastic outer-case to crack overtime.. eventually the entire headset is useless b/c of this tiny detail. Additionally the other end of the headphone wire (where they connect to the left side ear phone) is not great quality - I had my pair for about a year & now only the right ear phone works, and I traced the problem in the wire to that spot (when I move it a certain way the sound would come in/out for a bit in the left side).

review_headline: ER-102 Packs a big punch in a little package
review_body: This product is an extremely versatile little beast. It can be used for backpacking, at home, on the boat and at the camp.     Currently it is being used in our household and has proven itself to be very well worth the purchase. On top of being able to crank charge the radio in a situation where no outlet is available, it can be plugged in for 8-12 hours and the charge lasts for weeks; it can also be used with batteries. It picks up great reception, even in rural areas and comes with a variety of fantastic features. As soon as it arrived, everyone wanted to play with it because it offers so many features.    It comes with a wakeup alarm, cellphone charger, a flashlight, back light for poorly lit areas, a freeze alert and also acts as a fairly reliable thermometer.    It is a very impressive product, and although the speakers do not amplify to a very high volume it can be used with headphones. It has been dropped 3-4 times from a height of 5-6 ft and it has not affected the performance one bit.     I recommend this product, there are no other products that offer as much as this for such a low price.

product_title: Onkyo TX-NR3008 9.2-Channel Network Home Theater Receiver (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
I have been using a Yamaha DSP-A1 HT amp for 10+ years. It supports 7.1 channels when everyone else was making 5.1 channel receivers. The 2 additional channels are positioned as "front wide". So the 7 speakers in my family room are arranged to have have 3 in the front (left/right/center) and the other 4 placed close to the 4 corners. Yamaha's own Cinema DSP processing enhances the standard Dolby/DTS 5.1 sound and the improvement is readily audible. In recent years, other brands have added more channels and offered more features in handling video and digital sources. So I thought it may be time to replace the old amp. After looking online for reviews and prices, I decided on the Onkyo TX-NR3008 which purportedly supports up to 11.2 channels. It is apparently as good as it gets among the 2010 crop of HT receivers. Sound and Vision gave it a rating of 10/10 in both features and performance. Unfortunately it proved to be a disappointment and I had to return it for a refund, which is not something I like to do.

There are several factors in my decision and I thought it may be useful for other buyers to know.

(1) Onkyo, and perhaps most other brands as well, adheres to the industrial standard of speaker positions. For 5.1 channel, the surround speakers are supposed to be on the L/R sides of the listening, not in the back. For 7.1 channel, 2 more speakers are placed in the rear. This means I couldn't use my two "front wide" speakers. Even if I were to down grade to use only 5.1, my rear speakers are in the rear corners and not to the sides of the seats as they should be. I tried it anyway, and the surround effect was clearly not as good as my old amp.

(2) The inferior surround sound I heard from the Onkyo was perhaps in part due to the confusion in trying to find the right "listening mode." Every receiver uses digital processing to simulates different ambiance. Onkyo has some modes of its own ("orchestra", "TV Logic", etc.) and some industrial standards (THX Music, Prologic Movie, etc.) In order to find the appropriate one, one would have to read the explanation of each mode in the manual, e.g., what is the difference between "direct", "pure audio" and "stereo"? Even if one chooses a mode after reading, there is no quick way to turn the effect on and off to make an A/B comparison. instead, with each press of the button, one cycles through a sequence of modes, can't jump from one to the other. Yamaha uses its proprietary Cinema DSP with many more modes that the user can clearly understand and access by buttons marked concert hall, jazz club, movie theater, etc. There are several choices in each group based on the acoustics of real locations. There is button to turn the mode on/off so that one can quickly decide if the effect is desirable. This is a much more user friendly way to find the right mode that would enhance the listening experience.

(3) My old CD player and AM/FM tuner have manual power on/off switches. I leave them in the ON position but plug them into the switched outlets in the old amp. That way when I turn on/off the amp by remote, the devices are on/off as well. The Onkyo has no AC outlets to control any older devices with manual power switch, e.g., a turntable. It has an AM/FM tuner built in, but its audio quality is perhaps like that of a kitchen radio, does not compare with vintage tuners. I could connect an external tuner on an unused port (e.g., game) but I would have to manually it on and then select GAME from the receiver remote. Similarly, playing LP through the phono section led me to believe that the quality of the phono amp was not a priority in the design. So for people who still care about sound quality from FM and LPs, it can be a deal breaker.

The last point above is probably true of all modern A/V receivers where money is put into handling a variety of digital audio and video sources. The Onkyo's MSRP is actually lower than my old Yamaha amp. They are almost exactly the same size and weight. Something has to give. For people who have speakers laid out according to the "industrial standard," and do not care much about the old analog music sources, this is probably a very good receiver, but it did not work for me. After one day of trial, I put it back in the box.

After I restored my system back to its original configuration, I discovered deep in the Onkyo manual that the "speaker layout" button on the remote would allow an option to use 2 front wide speakers in 7.1 channel, but this is not discussed in the early pages on how to connect and position the speakers. It is unclear how it generates the signal for these front channels, but it's clearly done in a fixed way for each listening mode. Yamaha actually went to real locations to calibrate the acoustics to produce simulated sound. That's something that I have not seen in other brands. The Onkyo's simulation may do a good job as well, but I decided not to bother with all the trouble to find out.

Although this receiver did not work out for me, I decided to give a neutral 3-star rating to indicate that it's not a bad product. It just did not match my speaker lay-out and my listening habit. Had I done my research better, perhaps I would not have bought it. Thanks to Amazon's policy, returning was relatively painless and that deserves some stars. product_title: Woodees Laptop Adaptor
review_headline: PC Only - NOT Mac Compatible w/o amplifier
review_body:
Summary
The Woodees VOIPAD35 is a very nicely built \\"Y\\" adapter for channeling a four conductor 3.5mm mini audio plug from a cell phone head set to a PC or laptop that has a low level Mic input and a headphone output that are also 3.5mm mini audio. The item appears to be well built, is nice looking and works well for systems that fit the above description. It claims to work for Mac laptops, and this is just not true without adding a microphone pre-amplifier. Don't be deceived by the packaging claims - this unit will NOT replace the need for a USB or other powered headset for Mac users. It may have some utility for PC users, but you can find cheaper solutions on ebay.

Claims that are either overstated or plain wrong:
* The packaging claims that it adapts \\"Smartphone Headset to PC or Mac\\". This is only true for smartphones with 3.5mm (1/8\\") plugs. Some new phones come with a micro audio plug that is too small for the Woodees female plug. The requirement for a 3.5mm plug is buried in the text on the packaging. Fact is, there are a lot of folks who do not know the difference and this issue should be more clearly stated.
* The product does not adapt the microphone of a smartphone headset to a Macintosh. For some time, Macintosh laptops have not supported a non-powered microphone input. The input that many mistake for a mic input on the Mac is actually a \\"line\\" input that requires significantly more input signal level than a passive (non-powered) microphone can deliver. If any of you who use this product think you are getting it to work with the microphone, you are mistaken. What is happening is that sound is coming in via the built-in mic on the Mac, not the headset microphone. This is easy to verify by checking the sound settings in the \\"System Preferences\\" panel. in any case, I would judge this product NOT MAC COMPATIBLE. The claim to this effect should be removed from the packaging unless they are willing to qualify it with the additional requirements of a pre-amp or active mic.
* If you do have to carry a pre-amp to use this with your Mac, then the claim of \\"You no longer have to pack two headsets\\" is clearly offset by needing to bring along a pre-amp. In my case, I was already using a Griffin iMic, USB audio adapter to amplify my current headset that I use for VOIP. The iMic is pretty small, but it is \\"another thing\\" that is, frankly, fairly uncommon. I don't think the fact that you COULD get one to use the Woodees makes the Woodees Mac compatible.

Pros:
* Works fine with my PC on Skype using passive headset that came with my Blackberry.
* Good looking.
* Appears to be sturdy

Cons:
* NOT MAC COMPATIBLE (See above)
* Mic and Earphone labels hard to see.
* Kind of expensive
* Implies that it's more than it is - it claims it's compatible with all sorts of VOIP and chat programs, which it is, but it is NOT an enabler. It's an over-marketed Y adapter.

Conclusion
This was a very disturbing product in that a less technical person than I might be taken in by all the erroneous claims and waste a ton of time trying to get this to do things (e.g. attempting to get the Mac to accept the low level microphone input). If the packaging was more forthright in the claims made, it would be a nice product and I would put it in the same bin as Monster Cable: over-priced but well made wires. product_title: Next Generation Remote Control Extender
review_headline: Love it, solved my multi-room TV viewing problems!! :)
review_body: I live in a \\"shotgun\\" house in New Orleans...for those who don't know what that is, all the rooms are in a row, no real hallway (except by the bathroom)...you just walk thru each room to get to the next.  I was trying to figure out a way to watch in the last room of the house (kitchen) what I had recorded on my DVR, which is in the first room...AND change channels while in the kitchen.  For years I had a splitter off of the DVR and a cable(s) running along the baseboards thru the house...and if I wanted to change the channel, I had to go all the way to the front of the house to do it...what a pain!!  I couldn't do anything more permanent and hassle-free than that since I rent.  So, I found this on Amazon and for $42 and free shipping, I was MORE than willing to try it out!  It arrived, I charged it up the required 36 hours, plugged it all in in a matter of minutes...and voila, it WORKS.  I just works.  I unhooked the splitter and stashed the cables that previously draped thru my house.  I can take my DVR remote control through the house and watch my recordings in the kitchen (and the bedroom), which is approx. 40 feet away from the box and has 3 walls, a closet and a bathroom in-between.  My cables are run in such a way under the house that each secondary TV in the house is really a \\"dummy\\" that just plays what's on the living room TV (which has the DVR connected to it).  My problem was that I couldn't change channels without standing in front of the DVR...and pacing back/forth thru my house just to watch TV is not my idea of a good time.  So, I can't recommend this thing more...it just simply works.  The only thing I noticed which bugs me a tad bit is that if I'm in the living room where the device is, sometimes there is a delay in what I press on the remote and what gets transmitted to the DVR.  That's so odd because it's primarily when I'm in the room with the receiver, rather that in a different room.  However, all in all, I don't care.  The function of this device is to allow me to control a device in a different room which it does perfectly!! :)

product_title: TDK Life on Record 3-Speaker Boombox Audio System
review_headline: Puts the Boom in the Room!
review_body:
I just received this beautiful monster and I couldn't be more happy.

Upon arrival, the first thing you'll notice immediately is just how enormous and heavy this Boombox is; it feels solid and has an aura of quality (and it weighs like 30+ pounds!). From the wood handle to the silky-smooth rotation of the metal dial to the touch-screen panel controls, to the beautiful backlit displays (with good typography) it feels more like what you'd expect from Lexus, Leica or Bang and Olufsen than TDK, clearly their design team was trying to make a statement that TDK is back, and it appears they've succeeded with this stunning example.

iPod, iPhone and iPad integration all seems to work flawlessly with the supplied USB to 30-pin connector cable.

I've only been listening to it now for an hour or so, but the sound quality so far is phenomenal. I listen mostly to electronic music and indie rock, which the TDK handles without a hitch. The mids and highs are clear and the bass is full and solid without feeling boomy or hollow the way some less expensive systems can sound. Volume isn't an issue; sound quality remains good even turned up loud (I've gone half way up, it's so lound I feel like my neighbors will start complaining if I go louder).

I've owned many boom boxes and portable speaker systems and this blows them all away. In fairness, it's also more than twice as expensive as any boom box I've ever owned, too. Sound quality is more akin to a high-quality bookshelf stereo system than a portable.

If you're a lover of design, high-quality construction and full, balanced sound I recommend checking the 3-speaker boom box out for yourself.

product_title: Logitech Harmony 650 Remote (Silver) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
I struggled with trying to find a universal remote that would work with my home office Onkyo stereo, plus have the buttons that I need for our Cox DVR. I had resorted to just having two remotes because, although the Onkyo remote is pretty good, it lacked the buttons for the DVR guide and recorded shows. And hours spent on the Internet could not produce a reliable code for the Cox DVR remote to control the volume on the Onkyo stereo.

I had heard that the Harmony remotes were good, but I had no intentions of paying $70 or more for a universal remote when I can get one at Wal-Mart for $20. However, after purchasing another Onkyo for our main living room, I finally broke down and purchased the Logitech 650 for the living room.

The remote is great looking, and it's actually a little slimmer than the Cox DVR remote that we were used to using. I glanced through the manual (not much there), connected the remote to my computer, registered with Logitech, and downloaded the software. So far, pretty painless. I had already gathered the model numbers from the equipment I wanted to program in, so if you do this ahead of time it will let you focus on your remote instead of jumping up and down to go get it. So away I went, adding the devices. The software did a fantastic job of seeing what I put in, and even recognized the newly purchased Roku that Santa delivered for Christmas.

One thing to understand is that the remote does two things - it controls an activity, and it controls a device. The device is just that - a device (such as a TV, stereo, etc.). An activity is what you want to do, such as \\"watch a movie\\", or \\"watch TV\\". You create an activity by picking the devices that are involved, plus the settings that each should be turned to. For instance, if your TV needs to be on Input 1, and your stereo needs to be on Video 1, then you program the remote that way. So when you hit \\"watch TV\\", it automatically sets it for you.

Although I'm a computer geek, it took a little poking around to get what I needed set up. But the software is not that complicated, so don't be afraid of it. All in all, it was pretty easy to set up. After some final tweaking, I was satisfied that everything worked - including the audio on the Onkyo!

What I didn't really \\"get\\" is that you should primarily use the remote to control \\"activities\\". I was using it to control the \\"devices\\". So while I would use the device button to get to my DVR, then my volume wouldn't work until I went back and chose the Onkyo. Sure, the audio worked, but it was a bit frustrating clicking around just to turn the volume up and down! I finally got so frustrated that I started to fill out a return request from Amazon. However, I stopped to do some more research. \\"Why would they do this?\\" I thought. I came across a question in the Logitech forum that was similar to my issues. One of the people comments said to use the \\"Activities\\" on the remote 95% of the time, and the devices if you need something in particular. When I approached it that way, everything started making since. Using the software, you can actually take an activity and customize every single button on the remote to do what you want on whatever device you want it to - as long as you are using the remote to control an \\"Activity\\". And really, there is no reason not to use it that way. With the devices you have selected for the activity, you have a lot of different options for control!

Since figuring that out, I have fallen in love with this remote. Even my wife - who was very hesitant with using it - has now commented that even she loves it. Since this controlled my Onkyo stereo (which I struggled with for a long time), I decided to purchase another Harmony remote for my home office. This time, I chose the cheaper Logitech 300. That remote did not have the Activities feature like the 650, and instead relied more on the devices. While it controlled everything I had - including another Onkyo stereo, the Activities on the 650 really do make sense, and make things so much easier. So after 2 days with the Harmony 300, I DID return it to Amazon for a refund. And I turned right around and ordered a second Logitech 650.

This time, it took about 15 minutes to have everything up and running properly, including a Western Digital HD TV. Prior to that, I would need to \\"touch\\" 3 remotes to use it!

The next model higher was quite a bit more expensive, which is why I took a chance on this one (twice). And I'm not sorry I did. product_title: Sonos BU250 Multiroom Music System (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
[[ASIN:B001CROHX6 SONOS - CONNECT Wireless Streaming Music Stereo Receiver Component]]UPDATE Dec 2013: 5+ years of near daily use later... It still works as well as it did on day 1; periodic software updates have made it even better. Now I stream Spotify chief among other subscription services. I moved to a new house and in the main room now keep a large power amp out of sight and always on with a sonos box hooked to it, and no stereo components visible, just big awesome sound that I dial up through my phone or computer. I still have my geek stereo rig upstairs that also sounds great. Another zone in the bedroom, and I am getting a Play3 for the family for Christmas to put in a workshop or carry around to the garage or patio; I have no reservations about the expansion. I never use the remote included with the system anymore. I still love it. I still take pride in having the best (ie quality and functional)stereo setup around.

---from Sep 2010---
I have had a Sonos system in my home for 2 years now (Bundle with passive player, powered player and remote plus an extra passive player). It has never once failed or sounded bad. It plays what I want when I want it where I want it. It is simple and robust. Install was intuitive and took 30 minutes most of which was unpacking boxes and running patch cable. I have not had to tangle with any other technical issue at all.
I purchased an extra zone player for the garage downstairs and it works great. I have a networked hard drive with all my music, to which I shuttle files from whichever computer I use for a download or plug a flash drive into. One mouse click to update the music index, and theres the music, wherever I want.
When I dont know exactly what I want to hear, I use it to listen to the radio - a LOT. All kinds of radio, like KEXP Seattle, or Eastvillage radio, or WRVU Nashville or WFMU or KCRW or WWOZ New Orleans or any web radio station -all in the menu on the remote... or I can paste a weblink to a stream and listen to my favorite online streaming recording from any archive...
I stream Pandora for hours (ad free somehow). I don't have Rhapsody or sirius or xm, but they are all integrated into the system and I am inclined to think they work. Or I can play vinyl (or a CD or an ipod or whatever)in the main room and send the music out to the other zones during a party.
I can drive the system from my phone seamlessly. This system is what I thought the future would be like, and I am so glad it is here. I have meant to review this for a year now, but the stereo has always just been too loud.
