product_title: Skullcandy Headphone Earbud
review_headline: Good Value, but VERY muddy sound.
review_body: I saw the Skullcandy Dub earbuds at Target the other day on sale for $5. I was originally planning on getting the Ink'd (which I had used before and liked) as a temporary replacement pair for a much higher end pair that had lost sound in one ear, but they were $16 and, according to the sales clerk, the Dubs were better. So it was a no-brainer. I Bought two pairs of the Dubs. I wish I hadn't. Now I would much rather pay the extra $5 for just one pair of Ink'ds.   Heres why: The Dubs are muddy. They have lots of bass. Too much of it, actually. It made my ears hurt. And it really drowns out the mids, which sort of halfheartedly linger in the background. The highs are also quite muddy, except for the occasional \\"s\\", which produces a harsh sibilance that rattles your spine. There is almost no sound separation, and drums sound like they're coming out of the next room.   However, for $5 I really can't complain. But if you're paying any more than that I would NOT recommend buying this pair. Instead, go for the Ink'd, which have a much more balanced sound.

product_title: Universal Intelligent Battery Charger with LCD for NIMH/NICD AA/AAA/C/D/9V Batteries
review_headline: Only charges up to 1000mah AA batteries
review_body:
I bought this to go along with a bunch of high capacity 2600mah AA batteries that I bought. I had a couple other chargers that were more basic, and this one had delta-V cutoff, plus it charged a variety of battery sizes (up to 4), so I thought it would be ideal. I noticed quickly that my charged AA batteries weren't lasting very long at all, but until recently I didn't know why. I finally flipped the thing over and saw that it only supports up to 1000mah AA batteries, which is WAY below standard for rechargeable AA batteries nowadays. It was only charging my 2600 batteries to about 35%, which explains why they weren't lasting long at all.

My other huge complaint was the fan. It's on 100% of the time when it's plugged in, batteries in it or not. There is no on/off button, and the fan is loud, so much so that you wouldn't want this thing plugged in while you were in the same room, and certainly not in your bedroom. If you don't want to waste energy by powering the fan all the time you have to unplug the unit from the wall as soon as you're done charging, and plug it back in when you're ready to charge. In addition, the fan itself obviously uses more power than the unit would if it were just charging the batteries, so it begs the question of how cost effective it is to use this thing. It keeps batteries out of landfills of course and that's a great thing, but personally I would never buy this unit again or recommend it to anybody.

product_title: Apple iPod nano 8 GB 6th Generation
review_body: I made a huge mistake when I bought the 6th generation Nano. It was an impulse purchase because I was so excited about the clip and it was so darn cute. In fact, I thought it was so great that I decided to have it personalized. Another huge mistake on my part. As soon as I received the Nano and started playing around with it I realized that this new design might not be so great. The clip is a fabulous idea, but it's awkward to use at times and I will frequently hit the touch screen when I'm clipping the ipod on and it affects the song that is playing. The touchscreen is, in concept, very cool, and I like how they work on phones. The ipod Nano, however, has a very tiny touchscreen which is not fun to use.    I really like the idea behind the redesign. I use the nano just for music and to listen to podcasts. I don't need a camera or to be able to watch videos. However, this product doesn't work for me at all. I nearly killed myself at the gym when I had to look down and then reach down to hit the tiny sleep button to turn the touch screen on and then fumble around with the touch screen to change my music selection. Sweaty fingers do not work on a touch screen. Actually, I ended up getting a really great cardio workout because I was so angry with the ipod that it made me run extra fast!    Other things that I don't like are the size and the weight. I think it just too small and light. I used it at work one day and it went flying off my desk when I accidentally brushed by it. You can't turn the machine off and lock it like you could with previous generations. I have a 3rd generation nano and I love it. Unfortunately, it is a 4GB version and I have almost no storage space left. I can't recommend this new Nano to anyone - it is simply too expensive for what you get. I agree with all the folks who are saying that this is just an upgraded shuffle. And, to add insult to injury, I can't return it to Apple. The folks in the Apple customer service department told me that because I had personalized the product it was not eligible for being returned. AAGGGHH! I just went online and bought a 5th generation Nano and I'm going to give the 6th generation to my niece because she has a shuffle and I think this will work better for her.    My advice - don't purchase this generation. Either buy a 5th generation, wait until Apple comes out with the 7th generation or get a completely different MP3 player.

product_title: Sennheiser Ergonomic Earbuds with Basswind System Sound
review_headline: I know Sennheiser could do better.
review_body: My father is an audiophile and I've come to also have fine tastes when it comes to audio products. I needed headphones to use in the office with my Ipod. I couldn't do full over-the-ear kind because I need to hear my phone if it rings, so I knew I wasn't going to get top of the line quality sound from another Sennheiser product. I still thought that these in the ear models would be better than my Sony MDR-J10 pair. They fit very well and don't cause ear strain like the buds that come with the Ipod. However the sounds seems muffled. They have a better range than my Sony pair. I tried them with all different styles of music: Classical, heavy rock, techno, jazz, and country. I've never heard in-the-ear headphones give better sound from a violin! Like I said though, once there is an electric guitar with distortion it seems like I'm listening to it through a pillow. Drums seem flat and in the background. Vocals could have even been better. They are still good for the money for the quality of the contruction. Sennheiser just has such a good reputation I hate to see their name on this product. In short, I know I wasn't going to get the sound of $200 headphones for the price of $20, but I think Sennheiser has the technology to clear up the sound of these.

review_body: I am getting ready for deployment and was looking forward to this overall, well-reviewed item.  I have experience with ipod travel speakers, as well as having a nice Bose sounddock at home (love!).  Unfortunately,I did not realize that my ipod would not fit in the dock with its case on. I do not want to be limited to just using my new case, since my old one was more expensive, and seems to be a better case (one of the incipio brand).    So, the size of the speakers (not great for travel/deployment) coupled with the case issue, lead me to look elsewhere for speakers.  I have already processed the return, but if I cannot find one before I leave in a few days, I will probably have to keep these speakers.  Overall, not happy with this purchase.      ----update 8 Mar 11----    So, I am currently deployed, and wanted to say that I have changed my verdict on these speakers.  True, I had to abandon a case that I liked, in order to use it with my iPod.  I found a case that works great for my ipod Touch 3g, the Casecrown Glider.  The bottom pops off with no difficulty (though it does not slip off, mind you), and I love the color choices.  I realize that I have a now, older, iPod, so I just purchased 2 more cases so my touch will be good to go for the long-haul with these speakers.  The sound from these speakers are great, my coworkers love when I bring it to our PT sessions, and I've come to be known as 'iPod' because of it.  These travel in a suitcase well, and as another reviewer commented, they take up that dead space in your suitcase, unless you are travelling with a ton of socks.  Anyways, these are great speakers, you can't go wrong.  Of note, I did leave my remote at home, because I did not want to lose it while deployed.One area logitech could improve is to make a spot, similar to my last Altec Lansing speakers, where you can snap the remote when you are traveling/not using it.

product_title: Denon AVR2310CI 7.1-Channel Multi-Zone Home Theater Receiver with 1080p HDMI Connectivity (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Denon AVR2310CI Bit by HDCP Repeater Bug
review_body: I purchased this receiver to update my system and provide a central control center for all devices.  The abundance of connections allows multiple choices video connections (HDMI, Component Video and Composite Video) and Audio, (Digital and Analog).  In the process of setting up, everything seemed to work fine.  All connections worked properly and I ran the auto configuration wizard with the microphone.  Then I turned the system off (Receiver in Standby) and the next morning NOTHING WORKED.  The receiver had no video output and no audio.  Turning the power off and on didn't do any good. Resetting the microprocessor (lost all my settings) worked the first time but not subsequently.  Later in the day it the system turned on fine, but then it didn't work the following day.  I called Denon Customer support and they suggested the issue was the High Definition Copy Protection (HDCP) Repeater Bit. They suggested turning the equipment on in a specific order which didn't work.  The final solution was don't use the HDMI Cable from the Cable Box (Scientific Atlanta 8240HDC), but rather use the component video and the Optical Audio Connection.  This solution worked and since my Plasma TV is not 1080P capable, the HDMI connection isn't entirely necessary.  You can search \\"HDCP Repeater bit\\" for lots of info on this bug.  It bites even when there is no HD (1080P) content involved.  Bottom line is that the HDMI connections on this receiver may or may not be usable.

However, it is just OK in the middle register (the whole orchestra or an alto or tenor singer). Personally I am enough of an audiophile to be aware of the issue but not enough to care, as far as I am concerned it is great.    Blue tooth connection is clear and remarkably handy. No static sound as I have heard in other bluetooth audio devices.    The fact that the device will \\"walk\\" off your desktop is  tribute to the clever design -- the battery actually is the driver for the bass notes, but it is also a cheesy bit of physical design. Don't lose the rubber pad.     However, all complaints are minor. For $200 and the size nothing comes close.

That funny looking jacket on the outside will probably prevent the cable from being torn or punctured by protecting the plastic. The only downside is that the big ends, the thick cord, and the PVC layer make this cable pretty inflexible and hard to squeeze into tight spaces. I'm not the most technical when it comes to TV specs but I did a little research and this cable seems fairly future-proof. I definitely recommend this for the picture quality and price if you have the space for it. product_title: Gefen HDmi Detective Plus
review_body: I no longer see the blank screen, signal loss, or loss of audio problems I had switching my TV source over to my HTPC. With this device, my TV and HTPC can get on the same page in about 4 seconds, which is a huge improvement from the 10-20 seconds it took before, if I was lucky. Minus one star because the instructions were confusing. Its not clear enough which devices should be powered on or off at each stage. After 4-5 attempts, I found it worked if I followed this sequence exactly:    1. With your TV and your source/HTPC powered on and all working well, disconnect the HDMI cable between them.  2. Connect the TV to the HDMI Detective Plus output port.  3. Connect the HDMI Detective Plus power adapter. The light comes on.  4. Push the programming button. Wait for the blinking light to go solid green.  5. Unplug the power adapter. You don't need it anymore; it's just for programming.  6. Plug your source/HTPC into the HDMI Detective Plus input port. You're done.    Note that you never turn off your HTPC or TV. Don't power off or restart your source as the instructions say.

product_title: Klipsch IMAGE S4 -Ear Enhanced Bass Noise-Isolating Headphones
review_headline: Take your time, use them right
review_body: The Klipsch Image s4 are fantastic. If you're like me, you tend to abuse your electronics a little more than you should. These headphones have a nice solid build quality that will stand the test of pulling/tugging. Whenever they are first used, treble is a little high and bass too punchy. But these are high-quality headphones which means they need a break-in period. Over time they will even out into the nice, full sounding Klipsch products that everyone loves. I recommend using your iPod or computer and playing your music library overnight for a week for two. This allows the sound drivers to grow properly and create the best sound possible. The difference is quite amazing.    Sound isolation works extremely well and blocks out almost all outside noise. That being said, these aren't over-the-ear headphones and are not 100% effective at blocking every minuscule sound (no in-ear headphones are, sorry.) But they will block the noise of that person talking on their cell phone in the subway, or most of the noise from a jet engine on a plane. You won't be disappointed with the sound isolation.    Overall, a fantastic pair of headphones that I wouldn't hesitate to purchase again. Wearing them for hours at a time doesn't become uncomfortable. Sound isolation is superb, and will block much of outside noise. Build quality is sturdy and can take some abuse. For those who are saying sound quality is awful, they obviously haven't gone through the break-in period needed to make these sound like butter. They also probably haven't experiment with the different ear-tips to find the best fit for their specific ear-canal. Don't hesitate, buy the headphones that everyone who uses them correctly can't stop using.

product_title: Koss Porta Pro On Ear Headphones with Case
review_body:
Got these on Black Friday for around $15, but they're definitely worth the full $30~, if not more.

The moment I unboxed them, I tried all different kinds of music with them to see how they sounded, and they passed with flying colors on everything ranging from hardcore dance and metal to ambient and rock.
Sound quality is very high. Vocals stand out well and no particular frequency overrides or interferes with another. Bass is excellent, and a lot stronger than headphones usually deliver, but not overwhelming or unbalancing. I HAVE heard from people around me that the sound leaks outside some when the music is louder, but nobody has complained yet.

The design is simple but effective. There is a tab above each ear that lets the wearer adjust how tightly the headphones fit on the ears, and the headband itself is comfortable and strong.
Very comfortable. I determined this by wearing them for 12 straight hours during a LAN party, and at no point were my ears sore or uncomfortable.
(Protip: If you're going to wear them a while, make SURE you set the tightness tab to a lower setting or your ears might get sore. Otherwise, you'll be fine.)

Despite the name they aren't VERY portable, but they are easily worn about the neck or carried somewhere with the little pouch when not in use.

Also, and it might just be me, but these headphones seem to block outside sound somewhat when worn.

tl:dr

PROS
-Great sound
-Comfy!
-Easy to use

CONS
-Not super-portable, but not immovable

review_body: For quite a long time I have been debating (with myself) what new stereo system to buy. I've looked at plenty of them too... everything from a $100.00 Sherwood to a $3,000.00 Rega. I'm hoping to one day upgrade to Klipsch RF 62's with an RF series subwoofer, but for now, I'm hardly feeling deprived. The only odd thing about it is the mongo-ogrely-hairy-knuckle-dragging gigantic remote control. It's truly massive... If it was any bigger, it would take 2 hands to operate it. But hey, it works great. As far as the system itself goes, I only regret that I didn't come off the extra $40.00 it would have taken to get the 3490 that has 120 watts power per channel. So many newer systems out there are stuck on 5.1 or 7.1 and even 9.2 technology for watching movies. Bahhh!!! This thing is the littlest brother in the HK family and it ROCKS!! Its just 2 simple channels of pure clean power with 2 subwoofer outputs. What more could you ask for?? If you want to cave the ceiling in, all you have to do is pull the jumpers off the back and the 3390 instantly becomes a pre-amp that you can connect to your Crown PA amplifier and QSC 18\\" monitors and guess what...? Down comes an avalanche of sheetrock, insulation and rafters!! This thing is magnificent on its own, but its real magic to me is its versatility as an independent system or as a pre-amp. review_headline: Not worth spending any amount of money on. They will fall apart!
review_body: Six years ago, these were Sony's top-of-the-line in-ear headphones. There's lots to like with these headphones. Low-end bass was superb compared to stock headphones that came with your mp3 player or Walkman. The short length of the headphone cord was ideal if you wore your music player around your neck or on an armband in the gym. But who really does that? Sony packaged an extension cord with this product, but the extension cord made the headphones too long! I bought these from the Sony Store in San Francisco at the full retail price of $74.99. As of this writing, Amazon is selling it for the basement-bargain price of $13.66.     While it's a great deal, it's not worthy of purchase because these headphones will not last. After a few months of the purchase, I lost nearly almost every earbud that came with the headphones because they kept falling off. A few months later, the right speaker went mute (typical of other Sony in-ear headphones I've used in the past). The cord relief and plug cover started deteriorating and falling off. Why pay any amount of money for something that will turn to into garbage so quickly?    There are other in-ear headphones that are much more worthy of purchasing over these. Since the Creative EP-640 that Amazon used to sell for $13 isn't available anymore, might I suggest the similar Creative EP-630 which Amazon sells for $18? The bass response in these Creative earbuds are much better than that of these Sonys and other more expensive earbuds I've tried (including Monster and Ultimate Ears).    In summary, don't buy these headphones at any price. It's not worth your money.

Not all of the books I'd like to read are available in digital format, but there is a vast selection of available books. Certainly no lack of choice or variety. I have 14 books on my Reader so far and love that they take up less than an inch of space on the bookshelf.
The Reader isn't backlit so I can read all day and not get eye strain. I even forget sometimes it's not a book and reach up to turn the page. The pages are easy to turn using the stylus, or your thumb on the screen, or the navigation buttons on the bottom of the Reader.
I loaded some pictures on to it from my computer and they look great. They're not in color, but they're very sharp.
So far, I have to load music on to it, but it comes with two songs. The sound quality is very nice.
I have the Reader cover with built in light - the light's on a flexible arm that stows away neatly. Great for reading before bed. The Reader's not very heavy and together with the cover I can hold it very much like a regular book.
One of the other reviews mentions colour and yes, I agree. My Reader is also red and it makes a big difference. One of the things I didn't like about the Kindles I'd seen was how blah white they were. The red is vibrant and beautiful.

I checked out the library feature which allows you to borrow books for the reader from a library, but there weren't any libraries listed for my state. I'm not sure if I can borrow books from another state, but I hope so as there are books I'd be interested in reading, but don't want to buy. Right now, that's my only snag.

product_title: IOGEAR 4-Port HDMI Switch with Remote GHDMIS4 (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: Received this unit two nights ago from Amazon. Two positive comments and a warning to share.    1) It transmits 1080P beautifully on input1. Some reviewers believe that only input 1 will pass 1080P, so I put my BD player on this port.  The rest of my sources are 720p or 1080i anyway, so the [purported] lack of multiple 1080p ports was not an issue for me. I'm quite the gear-head, but I don't have two 1080p sources.  Do many people have two HD disc players (only subset I know of:  HD DVD early adopters, now forced to switch but don't want to re-purchase movies).    2) Unlike the 2-port switch I got at my local DIY store, the Iogear codes come right up on the Logitech site database.    3) The unit was behaving erratically at first, after I first programmed the Harmony to switch to DVD - The Iogear would switch to input #1, and then back to my Roku.  I finally realized that if you switch the unit to an input with no signal, it then auto-senses and switches to the next port with an active signal.  It takes 1-2 seconds for my BD player to boot up, so the switch would flip back to my Roku input (as many of you know, the Roku is a brilliant device, except for the unfashionably dumb absence of a power switch).      After realizing the problem, the solution is easy:  a) change the order of your Activity sequence so the Iogear is the last step; and 2) program in a delay before the Iogear actuates - 3000 msec worked fine for my BD player.    I am very pleased with the product - I finally can program the Harmony to start all my video gadgets.    DS

product_title: beyerdynamic DT 880 Premium 600 OHM Headphones
review_body:
These replaced a pair of AKG K240s that have simply disintegrated from old age. AKGs are my reference point for long-term wearing and listening comfort. So I was concerned that the 880s might not measure up in the long term. But they reproduce audio so well, I bought them anyway.

I use headphones as a reference when mixing music, for extended gaming sessions, for listening to music while working, for listening to music during extended gaming sessions...basically any time I can't have music on speakers, I have music on headphones. The 880s have moved right in where the AKGs used to be, and I was worried they would be clunky. I was wrong. They look heavy, but they are not. They look like they'd be hot, but they're not any worse than any other full-sized phones. (It's just the fuzzy pads that gives you that impression.) They have a nice long cord that leaves you plenty of room to arrange it out of the way.

In short, they are very comfortable.

Note: be sure to get the 30 Ohm version if you want high volume levels from portable devices...

[update] Has it really been four years? They still look almost new--the pads are compressed slightly, perhaps. The 880s simply beat everything for being a comfortable, unbiased way to listen. They're my default headphones for reference, for listening, for nearly everything. I did locate a replacement set of pads for the ancient AKG K240s, and they're sometimes useful for extended editing sessions where their bass roll-off makes them a bit less fatiguing, but the D880s are definitely my reference.

product_title: Sennheiser CX 300-II Precision - Headphones ( in-ear ear-bud ) - black
review_headline: Even better than the fantastic CX-300's
review_body:
I lost my Sennheiser CX-300's, so I got this updated model as a replacement.
I was happy to hear that the sound production of these is just as good as the CX-300's were, but these have a higher quality fit and finish. They still have the assymetric cable (which wraps around the back of the neck instead of dangling in front of you), and I know this is just my own preference. But I like to drape the headphones around my neck when I'm not listening. It's a useful feature.

Improvements of the CX-300II over the CX-300 are a longer cord, and a more durable L-shaped connector plug, and a much sturdier connection between the two cords that lead to the ear buds.
One nice thing to note about the quality of these, is that the opening canal of the earbud is covered with a metal mesh grate, which is a better idea than what Sony does... they cover the earbud opening with a piece of felt paper with a hold punched in it. This paper deteriorates over time, but the metal on the CX-300II's does not.
In my opinion, Sennheiser did the right thing by not messing with the sound of the CX-300s. They are almost legendary. All they improved was the finish and durability, and these were good improvements.
As far as comfort goes, this is very important to me, as I listen to audiobooks and podcasts, and can have my earbuds in for hours at a time while I'm working. The Sennheisers are one of the few models that never hurt my ears after prolonged listening. I don't even feel them in there. I use the largest size silicone flange (it comes with three sizes), and they fit snug and stay in. Very comfortable.
I might get another set of these in case they are discontinued at some point.

product_title: 32GB RunCore SATA 70mm Mini PCI-e PCIe SSD for ASUS EEE PC 900, 900A, 901 and S101
review_headline: Great improvement over the stock Eee PC 901 SSD, Pro IV even better
review_body: This is a great upgrade over the stock SSD. I replaced the 16 GB one in my Eee PC 901 with this, and I noticed a huge improvement in speed. The stock SSD got about 250 KB/sec with random 4k writes in CrystalDiskMark, whereas the RunCore gets about 1.8 MB/sec. In real world usage, it went from about 3 hours for Windows Updates on a fresh install of XP to under half an hour. Sequential/random reads are very nice as well.    However...    The standard 32 GB RunCore SSD uses a JMicron 602B controller, whereas the Pro IV models use an Indilinx Barefoot, which is a newer and much better controller. The Pro IV is only a few dollars more, but is quite a bit faster over the regular RunCore (approximately 14-19 MB/sec on 4k random writes). The Pro IV also has a manual TRIM utility for XP/Vista (and native support for 7), to help keep write speeds high over long term use. The regular one doesn't support TRIM, so write performance will degrade over time (secure erases/formats, or free space wipes in CCleaner may help).    I didn't know about the Pro IV version until after I purchased this one. If the Pro IV is in stock, I definitely recommend getting that one instead. Both are a huge upgrade over the horrible stock SSD.

product_title: Vuzix Wrap 310 Video Glasses
review_body: I really don't know what to say in regard to the other people who have reviewed this product.  Perhaps a newer model or other fixes have been made.  The bottom line, I like them, A LOT, and I'm very happy with most every aspect of this purchase.  These are reasonably priced and well-worth the money in my opinion.  I just spent a long weekend at the in-laws where there isn't TV in the bedrooms and, to be honest, a person could go nuts without some form of a diversion.  These glasses fit the bill very nicely. I watched a number of movies that I had digital copies for and had previously downloaded to my iPod.  Awesome.    Out of the box, these are extremely easy to setup and use.  My 13-year old son had these working in a matter of minutes (almost had them setup before the wrapping paper had hit the floor) and he didn't need the manual for any of the setup.  You just put in the batteries, plug them in, put them on, and start the movie.  That's it.  The sound is great and it is easily comperable to any of my more expensive ($60ish) earphones.  As you use these glasses, you will become more and more used to them and you will know how to wear them for the best picture.  I would estimate that it took me about an hour to really find the sweet-spot; my son seemed to instantly take to them.  Adjustments for video and audio are very easy and all on-screen.  I was amazed with the picture quality and sound while watching Star Trek, Up, Transformers.  I have showed these glasses to a number of people here at work and all were equally amazed with the quality and the entire experience.  When I could get my mother-in-law to shut her flap long enough to try them, she even liked them.  (If I thought this would shut her up for 10 minutes, I gladly buy her a couple of her own.  Hell - I'd even through in an iPod.)  I know that I have been responsible for at least 2 other purchases of these glasses... just because I let someone try them for a few minutes.      I would definitely recommend these to anyone looking for an excellent compact video solution.  These will be going with me on business flights and vacations from now on.  I didn't rate them as a 5-star device because the image quality is great but not HD.  I guess you can spend another $200 if you want HD quality.  Someone commented that there are a lot of wires.  Well, I hate to say it but I don't know how you could do it any differently unless you dropped another $200 for the wireless version.  To be honest, there aren't \\"a lot\\" of wires.  There is a wire to connect to your iPod (etc.) and this connects to your batter pack/controller unit.  This connects to your headset and there are two earphones that plug in there. I still have both ears so I need both earphones.  But that's it.  Pretty straight forward and very simple to use.      For reference only, I simply can not watch a movie if either the sound or picture is lacking.  I pride myself in having two very good 7.1 surround sound setups w/ 55\\" LCD TV's at home.  I also have a couple of Bose headsets (Quiet Comfort) and their earbuds.  My computer has (3) 24\\" HP displays (triple SLI) with 7.1 surround as well - primarily for video and graphic editing but also for MS Flight Sim.  I'm telling you this just so that someone doesn't think that I'm simply accepting these because I have a very low standard.  If they were crap - I'd tell you they were crap.    Hope this helps.

product_title: SONOS P5 Color
review_body: The S5 solves a number of problems for me and I am happy to recommend it. It is a tidy, attractive and successful product, which handily delivers what it promises. Having a full Sonos system already in place in my home for other applications made it easy to install the S5, so it was essentially a 'plug and play' matter, and the instructions seem simple enough that even a first time owner should not have real problems. This isn't a \\"stand alone\\" item in the sense that it does require that at least one other Sonos component exist in your home. It must be connected to a Zonebridge via your router, to serve as your source for the wireless signal. Once all the handshaking happens between the Sonos related devices, the rest is easy and you just establish the kind of programming you wish to feed your S5. I merely adjusted the equalization to please my listening tastes, which included a touch of bass and treble boost, then I set the S5 into its ultimate location and have been a very happy camper since. The sound is satisfying, but not equivalent to a component-based, serious audio system [which is to be expected]. I do think the audio is better and more accurate than the muddier sound Bose usually offers, so that is a big plus for me. One surprise is that it will play rather loudly without distortion, but I don't do that very much, other than to impress someone who asks \\"does it play loud?\\" I like the timer feature which makes using it for snoozing a sweet bonus. The other features such as Pandora or Rhapsody are not unique to the S5, but are part of the Sonos package at large, and it all works together well. I congratulate Sonos for putting together a comprehensive, intelligent, well constructed, nicely supported series of products and hope they continue that pattern for the future. Highly recommended.

product_title: Logitech Portable Speaker S125i
review_headline: Very nice for what it is
review_body:
I am quite pleased with this little speaker set. Recently, I had cause to go speaker shopping, looking for a good iPod speaker for my niece's graduation. She was very specific in what she wanted for her dorm: a lightweight, movable speaker that would charge with decent sound. This would have filled the bill beautifully.

Note that I'm not calling this \\"portable,\\" as it bills itself. It *is* portable...you can move it from one room to another...but for real portability, you'd want a sturdier unit for cradling your expensive iPod--a boombox with a good handle. A speaker set like this is best settled place to place for a while...parked in an office or bedroom and moved periodically, but not really carried around. The iPod isn't that secure (at least, mine isn't).

Also, the sound is not huge. The bass booster is a nice feature that makes this unit feel more powerful than it is, but it is really intended for small spaces. It's got decent volume, but in a large room it's going to get lost. It's not your party music player, either; just a nice, compact personal player.

For ease of use, I've got little cause to complain, but we had a bit of trouble settling the 80 gb iPod video we tested in it. In fact, for one disappointing moment, I thought we weren't going to be able to get it to work--no sound at all. We soon found that our iPod seated better without any adapter, and while it isn't as stable as I would like (again, if it were truly portable), it plays just fine.

If what you're looking for is a very compact, charger speaker that is well suited to small spaces, then this one could be a good contender. I believe it has decent sound in comparison to other units of its size and price point. If you're looking for true mobility, you should consider getting a boombox instead. And remember that sometimes you *do* get what you pay for. There are certainly units with better sound. My husband's Logitech Pure-Fi Anywhere 2 Compact Speaker system for iPod is undeniably better (though larger and more than twice the price). And my Altec Lansing inMotion portable system is an entirely different class...at many times the cost.

But for my 12 year old son, this is ideal. I suspect my college-bound niece would have been pleased as well.tter (though larger and more than twice the price). And my Altec Lansing inMotion portable system is an entirely different class...at many times the cost. But for my 12 year old son, this is ideal. product_title: Pioneer SC-25 140 Watt 7.1 Channel Home Theater Receiver
review_headline: Superior sound and Great Video Up Conversion
review_body: I have had this receiver up and running for a week now.  It is driving the 7.1 set-up in my family room with digital audio out to my old pioneer elite 72-txv, which is driving audio for the rest of the house and outside.    Pros:      1.  Network capability.  I have this hard wired to my LAN, but I think it has wireless capability.  Other the network you can stream from various internet radio stations and THX Neural.  On the neural site their are very few options now, but they are broadcast in THX surround and the sound is spectacular.  After a couple second buffer, the music is streamed and there wasn't a single hiccup the entire time I was listening    2.  Ipod interface.  Much improved from my old Elite.  Much faster and more intuitive.  Even displays album art on your TV.  I wasn't able to access videos on my Ipod, but not sure if it has this capability.    3.  Stunning sound.  This receiver matches well with my Boston Accoustics center and surround speakers.  Easiliy the best they have ever sounded.  Using the Advanced MCACC - Auto function, set-up was fairly straightforward.    4.  Video display.  I have an LG Blu-Ray and Bravia LED-LCD as part of my system.  The picture is awesome with vibrant, sharp colors.  Clearly the SC-25 isn't adversely impacting picture and may even be helping.    Cons:    1.  Size, it is a beast and 5 pounds heavier than my old Elite, which I thought was heavy.    2.  Remote - No LCD display so some functions may be hard to do if you aren't close enough to read the receiver itself and have your diplay off    I am very happy with my SC-25 purchase and highly recommend.

product_title: Cowon D2+ 16 GB MP3 Player (Black)
review_headline: A great sounding player with insanely good battery life.
review_body: I've had this device for almost two years now. The battery is rated for up to 52 hours of music playback. On a recent trip from San Francisco to New York, I listened to the D2 almost constantly and the battery gauge didn't go down at all.    The sound quality is great! There is a 5-band equalizer, so you can tweak the sound however you like. The bass can be loud and clean sounding without causing any distortion.    The D2 just shows up as a disk drive, so it will work with pretty much any modern operating system like Linux without any trouble. It also supports formats that many players don't like Ogg Vorbis and FLAC.    The device is amazingly small, and the storage can be upgraded with an additional memory card.

review_body: Just wanted a way to easily attach my Fuze to my stereo and charge it that was a little classier than leaving the wires hanging when my MP3 player wasn't there. No.  The blue light is too bright and lights up my whole living room if the other lights are out.  A dab of car touch up paint fixed that.  The bumper is too thin as well.  I cut the mounting nubs off of the thinest bumper and glued it to the fattest one, problem solved.  So for the price and a little work, I got what I wanted and am satisfied with the appearance and sound.  Now if this were a Sansa review I would have to rant endlessly on why you would build a descent MP3 player and then not have any accessories for the damn thing...

product_title: Creative Zen X-Fi Video MP3 Player with Wireless LAN and Built-In Speaker (Black/Silver)
review_headline: One year experience with my LAST Creative product
review_body: Pros: above average headphones, FM radio, SD slot, good sound.   Cons: faulty design and horrible repair service.  Design.  Within the very first week the player, after playing for about 10-20 minutes, sometimes even less, started either freezing or just simply shutting down and the only way to bring it back to life was to reset it. I used the tip of the headphone's plug to do that. I was hoping that at some point Creative would release firmware that would solve all of my and, judging by their own site, other customer's similar problems.  While patiently waiting for firmware upgrade and trying not to be too PO, I tried all possible and some impossible ways to fix Zen. Unfortunately firmware that would fix freezing problem never came and all the tricks I used also failed to fix my Zen.  Finally, a few months ago, before one year warranty expiration date, I decided to send my Zen to Creative to be fixed. When I got it back from Creative repair center and turned it on, hoping that my Zen headache and frustration are over, to my surprise, I found that my settings are still intact. I thought that in order to repair the player they would have to reset it to original default settings, run some tests, etc. I guess all they did in repair center was repackaged player and sent it back without even bothering to fix it, because it still freezes/shuts down and now it got even worth - it started sounding as if all my music was ripped from old scratched LPs.  While dealing with my Zen, I was wondering who runs this company that doesn't care weather their products are sold, because at least 5 of my non-iPod co-workers/friends at some point were considering buying Creative Zen, not any more. And now, after reading my review, how many of potential Creative customers will change their mind and buy Creative's competition mp3 players?

product_title: Wolfcom Hidden Spy Audio / Video USB 4gb Dvr w/ Pinhole Color camera & Pen Recorder
review_headline: The Real Deal -- getting the most from your pen despite challenging instructions
review_body: This product was much more than I expected! The resolution is exquisite and the audio is outstanding. It's extremely simple to record and download with the simple one touch recording and and built in USB plug.    In one of the other reviews,they complained of instructions being in Japanese, so here's some advice to get you started.    To record, simply press the top button, the blue button on the back of the pen will turn on, and you are now recording.  To stop recording press the top button again.    To download your videos, unscrew the middle of the pen, where you will find a USB plug. Plug it into your computer. The computer should respond by giving you a message saying,\\"New hardware found\\", give the computer a minute and it should say,\\"hardware installed and ready to use\\".    Go into \\"my computer\\"and open the external drive.  Find the file named \\"record,\\" click on it and a file named \\"video\\" should appear.    Click on this to view your videos.  (You probably already have Windows video software preloaded on your computer.)    Once you have done this, the next time you plug it in a menu will appear, click on \\"play\\" to play back your videos!    To charge the pen, take the usb cable and plug the slimmer end into the the charger. Unscrew the pen and attach the thicker end into the pen's USB plug. Insert the charger into an outlet and you will charge the pen. Charge for a few hours, then unplug the thicker end of the USB cable from the pen and screw the pen back together.          Good luck.  Have fun!

They also do an awesome job of blocking out surrounding noises. I know there are a lot of people who say these hurt your ears after wearing them for too long, don't worry about that too much. Just a simple readjustment will stop that from happening. The only thing that's a bad thing is that they do leak some sound. But that's not that big of a deal for me so to me, this product is flawless. Another thing: everyone is saying that these are made out of some cheap crappy material that breaks easily. Once again, wrong. If you don't yank them off your head & actually make an effort to take care of them, they should last a while. & even if they do break, Skullcandy will either replace it at no charge or replace it for 50% depending on what happened. So if you're not planning on buying these because of all those reviews that say this product sucks, you should just go ahead and buy them. You'd be surprised at how amazing they are & how all those reviews were just a bunch of bs. These headphones are just so amazing. My very first pair & I couldn't ask for anything better for such a cheap price. Oh yeah, they're also stylish as well (;

review_headline: Onkyo-"Get it right before you sell"

One was hooking up the speaker wires to surround inputs. The right and left were NOT beside it other but were at one end and the other end. This leaves wire management with wire ties a mess. It worked pretty good but time consumming. The great thing about the receiver was the 3D pass thru from my Samsung bluray player. I watched Monsters vs Aliens and Cloudy with a chance of Meatballs in 3D and was very impressed. With the new complaint (1.4A) for 3D content, it WILL catch on for the future. I just HOPE that this Onkyo will keep me smiling for years to come. Update: I had to return the receiver to Amazon today (07/14/10) because NO customer support other than ship it back to us for repair. I tried to MANY times on resolving the calibration with the microphone issue. I just received the 2nd one yesterday and the receiver still doesn't work. Onkyo says ship it back to us. It is $50 for UPS ground delivery. It might take 2 to 4 weeks. I said NO and returned it back to Amazon. GET IT RIGHT BEFORE YOU PUT IT ON THE MARKET. This receiver went from a FOUR STAR, to a ONE STAR RATING. TERRIBLE CUSTOMER SERVICE.

review_headline: Just doesn't work well enough to bother
review_body: On the positive side, the physical design and contruction are excellent. I tried the unit in a VW Jetta, Jeep Liberty, Honda CRV and Toyota Corolla and was never able to get acceptable sound. product_title: Onkyo HT-S7200 (B) 7.1-Channel Home Entertainment Receiver/Speaker Package with Dock for the iPod (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Almost, but needed some help - disappointing iPod dock
review_body:
Others have done a great job covering specifics, so I just want to talk about my experience with this system after two months.

I got everything set up and was generally pleased with the system. Early on, while listening to a variety of music to get an idea of the system's performance, I found a key weakness - midrange. I listen to a good bit of bluegrass and guitar music, and it just sounded like Alison Krauss' voice was...well...missing. I was also struggling with the layout of my TV room - my only option was going to be either hang the side surrounds from the ceiling (yuck) or invest $50 more in stands.

That's when the light came on. Installing this system, I had replaced an older hodge-podge set which included some Cerwin Vega full-range speakers I had picked up 5 years ago for $75 at a yard sale. I got the brilliant idea to try those out as front speakers on the new system and when I did, there was simply NO comparison! I hooked one Cerwin Vega up on the left front and the Onkyo tallboy on the right and switched balance left and right. Alison would disappear and reappear in the music as I did. Even better, I realized that I could use the Vegas as fronts, and move the tallboys back as sides - instant speaker stands! With the extra punch of full range speakers in front, the sub didn't have to do quite so much work. The system sounds awesome now. After calibration, I dare say it's almost perfect for my level of investment.

A couple of other items.

The subwoofer is great for most content, but it does struggle for low rumbling sounds like prolonged explosions, thunder, etc. I've turned it down 3 times in my two months and it still has this issue. Oh well, it's not very often. It has done very well with all the music I listen to.

I'm using HDMI for a BD player and my PC into this receiver, and one HDMI out to the TV. This has worked VERY well. I also have a record player, a cassette player, and a CD changer connected. The odd man out is the TV, which I run into the Onkyo receiver through S/PDIF. So far everything works great. I've been able to use the HT-S7200 remote control almost exclusively as it will control basic functions on my Onkyo CD changer, the Panasonic BD-160 blu-ray player, and my Samsung LN52B750 TV. All in all, I think the functionality is one of this system's strongest points. I do have to get the Samsung and Panasonic remotes out for special content on those devices and to change settings.

One major, though trivial disappointment is that I can't use my iPod Touch on the dock without removing the Touch's protective cover. I have a very low-profile cover (Belkin Grip Vue) and I can use my Touch on any other dock I've tried with the cover on. Onkyo has made the mating connector too shallow and the surrounding area of the base too tight to allow the Touch to dock without removing the cover. review_headline: WARNING: DO NOT BUY THIS DECEPTIVE ITEM:

I have Dish Network and you can only control one TV off of this remote because if you are running a 2 TV setup off a dish box, the ESPN Remote is not capable of transmitting UHF signals to control the second TV.  Next, I have an i-pod dock that uses RF technology to control it, again the ESPN remote is not capable of this technology either.  The programing is insanity causing and seems to never quite do what you wanted it to do.    Technical details aside, this remote is nothing special.  It was great when it was capable of doing all that was ADVERTISED, but now I'd rather go back to using the 5 individual remotes.  Thereis a reason they are offering this device at a drastically reduced price, because it's capabilities are drastically reduced too.    Ultimate remote...maybe 5 years ago it would have been, but with advances in touchscreen technology and above mentioned other issues, this remote should be renamed to the ESPN Snake-Oil Remote, cause it ain't going to do what it promises.  The worst part is, they subtly released this statement, that this would be affective October 26th, yet when promoting it, all the descriptions describe all the capabilities, even the ones no longer available.  Seems a little bit irresponsible on their part to allow such an inaccurate description to continue to entice potential buyers.  Caveat Emptor (buyer beware) And now you know.

product_title: Denon S-52 Wifi Internet/Radio Audio System
review_headline: Wide range of features but not for the inexperienced or inept
review_body:
I selected the Denon S-52 because of its extraordinarily broad feature set and despite its relatively high price. It offers AM, FM, and HD radio, CD capability, wired or wireless internet radio, Rhapsody, and playback from a PC or USB storage device, as well as satellite radio compatibility. This range of inputs in a tabletop system is unique in the American marketplace at this time.

Let me address a couple of the most discussed issues related to the S-52 and then wrap up with a quick summary. I'll try not to repeat too much of the material covered by other reviewers.

First, sound quality. I note for the record that I am a professional musician with excellent ears and a very high quality home sound system. Judged by that standard, the S-52 does not produce sound of extraordinary quality. It has substantial bass boost and the mid and upper ranges are forward and brilliant, tending toward harsh in a few instances. This choice was made, I suspect, to increase competitiveness with the various Bose systems that many consider to represent audio excellence. Those who hold the Bose sound in high esteem will likely find the S-52 sound familiar and satisfying. Those who adhere to a higher standard of reproduction will be disappointed if they compare the S-52 to a quality audiophile system.

But...how many people listen to a table radio with the critical attention that they bring to their music room or to the concert hall? If this is your sole music source, and you are a discriminating listener, you may want to invest in better sonic performance. But if you will use the S-52 in your kitchen or office or out on your deck, as I suspect most will, the sound is just fine. As noted above, if Bose defines audio excellence in your ears, you may be pleased with the S-52 in any setting.

Second, ease of connection to the internet/general software usability. In this area, I align myself with those who conclude that Denon has stumbled in their software design. This is not the easiest system to set up, especially for routers that require manual entry of addresses. Persons lacking experience and/or intrepitude (Is there such a word? If not, there should be.) may find the setup process frustrating and tedious. My advice is to take a few deep breaths, read the manual closely, and follow the steps carefully. If that fails, consult the nearest teenage gamer, who will efficiently, if perhaps patronizingly, take the necessary steps on your behalf. I do not say this in a condescending manner; those of us who have earned some gray hairs did not grow up with this stuff and we do not take it for granted as our children and grandchildren do.

Now the summary. This is a quality product from a solid mid-range audio manufacturer. Appearance is unobtrusive and attractive without being trendy. Materials are substantial and build quality is excellent. Feature range is extraordinary. Everything works as described. Subject to the caveats above, the sound quality should satisfy most users. Those who are unsatisfied probably need to consider a different level of hardware altogether. Software setup can be challenging for the inexperienced. The price is high but, if you insist on the full range of inputs, there is nothing out there that is cheaper and all-in-one-box. You could cobble something together that would do all these things but the price would likely be just as high, the aesthetics less pleasing, and the overall quality no better.

product_title: Nvidia GeForce FX 5500 256MB AGP 8x TV-Out S-Video DVI Graphics Card
review_body: I have an older Dell computer (bought in 2003) that had a previous GeForce 5200 AGP card in it.  The display went out one day and rebooting would show the garbled boot sequence text, but would halt before actually starting windows.  I figured it was the video card.    Because of its age and the fact that I wanted a new computer soon, I was looking for a cheap AGP card and found the GeForce FX5500 for $29 on Amazon.  I got the card in the mail about 5 days later and opened up the package.  Immediately, I saw the box read PCI Express and knew that would not work on my outdated computer.  The confusing part was that the box also said AGP, and it gave me hope that it might be OK after all.    I opened the box and examined the card, comparing the seating to the card that I took out of my PC.  It sure looks like an AGP type card.  I plugged the card into the AGP slot, plugged in the monitor cable, and started the computer.  The PC started, but there was no display.  The monitor light never turned green (stayed orange).  Tried plugging the old card in again to see if the monitor light turned green, and it did.  Re-tried the new card again with the same result.  No matter what I did, the monitor never recognized the card.  I started looking for answers on the internet.  Some suggested that other cards would not work because of an undersized power supply.  That may be the case here, but as I said, I don't want to put any more money into this machine than I have to.    I went down to the electronics store and bought a GeForce FX6200 card that clearly specified AGP 8x for about $40.  Installed it, plugged in the cable and booted the PC.  Works great.  Now I have this useless $30 card that aint even worth the trouble of returning.  I guess I learned my lesson here.  Don't buy this kind of stuff off the internet, no matter how cheap it is.

product_title: Sony BRAVIA DAV-HDX589W 5.1-Channel Theater System (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Buyers should be aware that this is DVD system, not a home theater system
review_body:
This system has some good features... it sounds great, it looks good with the piano black finish... its easy to use and to install, plus the wireless speakers are great but here's what I think of the little details that makes this thing deserve a 3 star review:
1.- Its not completely wireless: The front and center speakers hook up to the back of the receiver and then you have a small WIRELESS amplification module (called SAIR by sony) that syncs with the receiver and you hook up your TWO SURROUND SAT SPEAKERS to that module.
2.- I HATE that sony gives you a specific length speaker wire to use... what if I need more wire? Sony uses these colored plugs that hook to the amp... so you will end up splicing sony's original cable in order to hook everything up
3.- THIS IS BY FAR THE MOST ANNOYING. It is a 5 dvd changer which is ok if we lived in 1998... I bought a bluray player and sony decided to add ONE INPUT (just audio, no video) to the theater... what if you had a PS3, xbox360? you would only be limited by that input which sucks a lot!.
4.- Finally, the remote used for this... I bought this for my dad, he is 60 years old and If I gave him this remote his head would explode. Thank God I also bought a Harmony one remote... Sony could have decided to do a better job designing this theater.

product_title: ABLE PLANET True Fidelity Foldable Active Noise-Canceling Headphones
review_body:
I actually purchased these through a site called Lockerz. I don't want to go into the dynamics of the site but for reference, I purchased them for $52 USD ($57 USD with taxes). They came in the mail with good packaging and no noticeable blemishes/scuffs on the product box.

The headphones are totally worth what I paid for; they yield good sound quality and the noise canceling feature is good enough that when I use the apparatus, I can barely hear myself typing on my laptop. There is a slight \\"hissing\\" noise when the noise canceling is activated without music but when the music is playing, you can't hear the hissing. The headband is snug and could be a bit uncomfortable over long periods of time but I don't have a problem wearing them for 2 hours or more.

As people have mentioned before, the case does not protect the headphones at all so I recommend getting a better case. The cord has ample length and its own volume control which is really convenient for devices that have less precise volume meters. I definitely recommend these to anyone who wants noise canceling headphones without paying $300.

product_title: Panasonic RP-HC55-S Noise-Cancelling Earbud Headphones
review_headline: I gave it a good try
review_body: I purchased the ear buds in October 2009.  I experienced a couple of problems with the buds:    Unreliability:  Less than 1 month after my purchase, the silver volume control in the center of the cord went bad.  When I touched the controller, the sound popped.  Customer service was very responsive and helpful.  They sent me a replacement even though I did not keep the original packaging.  Now, 2 months after receiving the replacement, the controller started causing problems again.  Without warning, one of the buds will emit a high-pitch whining squeal.  If I take the battery out of the controller, jiggle things around a while, the squeal will stop.     Inconvenience:  The controller in the center of the cord is a huge inconvenience.  I clipped it to whatever I could, but it wouldn't stay.  And because of the added weight of the controller, when the cord became unclipped, it pulled the buds out of my ear.  This is a huge inconvenience for a commuter (fumbling with the cord while getting in/out of cars and buses is a pain).    I purchased the buds because of the rating and write up in Consumer Reports.  I've stopped using them.  The positive comments I have for these buds are that they were relatively comfortable, did a fantastic job of reducing outside noise, and when the buds did work, the sound was great.

product_title: Pioneer Electronics Audition Series Docking Station for iPod
review_headline: Jaw Dropping Sound In A Sleek, Sexy Design
review_body:
First, let me get one comment out of the way: this thing is sexy. That was my first thought when I opened the box and unwrapped this gorgeous, sleek black docking station. With its glossy black curved top and matte black face behind which sit two speakers and a sub-woofer, this baby looks good enough for any room in my house. That's important to me since it now means I can enjoy my favorite music even in my formal living room where other electronics are prohibited because they're so ghastly looking.

Second, I wish Pioneer hadn't limited the product's name by calling it a \\"Docking Station for iPod\\" because it works with my iPhone 3G *without* an adapter, as well as with my son's iPod Nano. That came as a wonderful surprise since the other two docking stations we own work fine with one but require an adapter to work with the other. Not so with this docking station from Pioneer which services both devices and delivers crystal clear sound free of the buzzing and resonance that most docking stations produce when you really crank it up. (And, frankly, if you can't crank it up why buy it, right?)

The gorgeous sound, incidentally, remained impressive even when we connected my husband's iPhone 3GS to the Pioneer XW NAS3-K Docking station using the [[ASIN:B002RAOCPK Pioneer Electronics AS-BT100 Bluetooth Adapter for Compatible Pioneer Products (Black)]]! In fact, the ability to play music from his iPhone around from across the room made my husband proclaim this as his favorite stereo system in the house. That's high praise from a man whose monolithic sound system occupies the majority of one wall in our rec room.

I haven't tried the video out connections on the back of the Pioneer because we'd first have to move my husband's stereo system to get to our TV connectors. That said, he's indicating that he's so impressed with the Pioneer's sound quality that he'd be willing to give it a try (and I need him to move the entertainment center, anyway, so I can clean behind it).

Before I sound like I'm gushing too much, let me just point out my one reservation about this device: the remote control feels rather flimsy in comparison with the sleek solidity of the docking station itself. That's not a star-killer, in my opinion, because I'm rather used to protecting remote controls from my kids and, besides, when using the Bluetooth adapter the remote's completely unnecessary. I'm just rather surprised Pioneer didn't encase the remote in a glossy black case similar to that of the docking station.

All of which is to say that, Pioneer has always made quality electronics, and the Audition Series XW_NAS3-K Docking Station proves they're still at the top of their game. While I realize the price may cause some to blink or even gasp, this is NOT a typical cheap-looking docking station putting out tinny music you can barely hear from across the room. With its rich sound, iPod and iPhone compatibility, video output and Bluetooth capability, this is essentially a top-end stereo for your portable music that will deliver big, gorgeous sound from a small cabinet while looking sexy in the process.it). product_title: AUDIOVOX FMM100 FM modulator with isolation transformer
review_headline: Overall, a great option for adding AUX to your car stereo
review_body: So basically this is a fantastic way to add an auxilliary device to your current car stereo with the most minor of modifications.  It's especially fantastic when you don't have any other way to wire things in, such as harness patches, aftermarket systems that replace the CD changer, or a new headunit.    This is the second unit I've installed.  The first was about 6 years ago in my '85 Mustang (keeping it all original).  This one went in a '98 BMW (essentially no other options at all).  Easy install each time.  Be aware that for non-domestic vehicles, you may need an antenna adapter.  My Mustang just plugged right in, but the BMW required antenna adapters.    Required for install: a 12v switched power source, a ground connection, and a 1/8\\" to RCA phono cable from RadioShack.  Plug the antenna into the modulator, plug the modulator in the back of your radio, and mount the on/off switch for the modulator somewhere accessible. Done.    Sound quality has always impressed me with these.  Sure it's not the same as a direct connection into your system, but for not having to hack anything up, lose your CD changer, or spend $$$ on a new headunit and install, it's great.  I get no hissing or extraneous noise whatsoever in either car.    Picky people and audiophiles will say that sound is decent, but lacks the full range and clarity that for instance you would hear out a CD in the car.  Also, like the radio, audio does sound a little muddled and not as crisp as a CD.  I agree.  But to put it in perspective, this modulator is 20 times better than a wireless FM transmitter (no noise, no batteries, better sound) and 100 times better than no iPod/mp3 player.    Overall, I feel the sounds is very good and I will be very happy with it for years to come.  I've been using it in my Mustang for years now, and will do the same in the BMW.  Don't forget you can tailor the sound for your system using the EQ on your iPod/mp3 player and adjustments on your headunit.  I put my iPod on TrebleBooster, bumped the treble and bass a little on the headunit and it sounds very very good.    I gave the sound quality 4 stars, but it deserves 4.5 (at least the way it is installed and adjusted for in my systems).  Overall, for $30, this thing gets 5 solid stars from me.

product_title: Skullcandy Aviator Black Headphones
review_body: I am a Skullcandy enthusiast.  I found the Roc Nation Aviator headphones a solid product, clean sound, rad design, but a little expensive.    I passed the headphones to several of my friends to get their feedback.  All liked the design and the clear aviator glass.  So it gets extra marks for that.    The cord is a reinforced nylon that resist tangling and crimping, a definite plus.  It was the right length for me.    The earcups are a triangle shape and reinforced with soft memory foam.  One of my friends complained about the triangle shape, but thought with enough time he could get use to it.  I felt it was a little small for me, but I was use to the oversize Sennheiser PXC-350.  It was definitely very comfortable and I could wear them for several hours on the first day.  Like all full-size earphone, they did eventually get warm (your own body heat) but nothing too unbearable.    I compared the sound quality of the Aviator- 40 mm drivers to my Hesh-50 mm drivers ($25 - $40 on Amazon), FMJ earbuds - 11mm drivers ($35 - $50 on Amazon) and Sennheiser PXC-350-40 mm drivers (purchased for $178 on Amazon but the prices may vary).  I didn't break in the Aviator headphones.  Normally I play them over 50 hours to break them in.    The Aviators sounded excellent, very crisp and clean.  They did have a thin or tinny feel to it but that may be because they weren't broken in.  The Hesh headphones were equally good and had a warmer fuller sound to it.  This may be due to it broken in or maybe due to the larger drivers which would allow a more full sound.  Maybe someone from Skullcandy can do this comparison.  The Sennheiser performed very well and was much more comfortable.  It had a comparable sound quality, but in a quiet environment, the large ear cups had and echoey feel to it.  I didn't compare the headphones in a noisy area but I already knew the Sennheiser reduced the sound a lot and the Aviators and Hesh phones would not be as effective.  Surprisingly, the FMJ Earbuds seem to have the best sound.  The Comfy phone tips isolate the sound very well allowing me to focus on the music better.  It worked well in a noisy or quiet environment.    Overall  If I use the phones to travel or commute I would stick with the FMJ or Sennheiser.  If I wanted a good sound in a relatively quiet environment I would use the Hesh or Aviators. If I wanted to do radical things while wearing headphones, I would use the Hesh because they are cheaper and I would be focused on my task anyway.    The Aviator seem to have a crisper, cleaner sound but I'm not sure if it is worth the $100 premium over the Hesh.  If the Aviator's came down in price (10 - 20%) for a $100 - $125 price range it would be a solid buy.

If you look very closely at the different colors you and see which colors come with the aluminum-braided cord and which have the white rubbery/soft cord. I'm not sure which are better - I was used to my aluminum-braided cord on my first set - even though it is stiff and doesn't fold up as small as the white cord. These speakers are really an anomaly to me, as you typically get what you pay for with speakers and budget speakers generally sound thin, overdrive easily, and have poor workmanship.  On all these accounts, these speakers deliver.       Highly recommended.

review_headline: One of the best sub-$1K SW
review_body:
Once out of the box and set up correctly for my space, I tested this box with wide variety of music genres. The fidelity and \\"musicality\\" of the sound amazed me, not having heard the same quality except in much more expensive SW. The low to medium price range SW (ie, some Polks I listened to) tend toward a \\"boomy\\" monotone quality lacking detail, so for this price I have yet to hear anything better.

Unfortunately my enthusiasm for rich wonderful bass was not shared by my wife; I sent this back after about a week and compromised for the SUB-10 which lacks the 12's transparency and richness. In retrospect, she was correct that with my current speakers (also Klipsch) the SUB12 was a bit overkill.

While most would use this for home theater setups, paired with the right mains and amp it offers superb bass sound for audiophiles on a budget, be it classical, techno, jazz- it'll throw it back at you without sweat. It delivers much more than just bass for bass's sake.

product_title: Heavyweight Classic Messenger Bag
review_headline: Perfect for What I Was Looking For
review_body: I purchased the Olive Drab version of this bag.  Even though it has not been a great deal of time since my purchase (only a few days, as a matter of fact), I was very pleased with what I received.  I was looking for simplicity:  something I could use as a means of carrying my school supplies around campus instead of dealing with an abysmal traditional backpack.  I can say that this bag fit my needs perfectly.  The simplicity of the design is wonderful and very functional for a carrying bag.  In fact, I would have been perfectly fine without a velcro strip, especially since I plan on avoiding it (however, those of you that are looking to use the velcro, the strips really only line up if the bag is rather full).  The full description of the bag may be found below.    The strap is nice and wide to allow as much comfort as possible.  There is one large main compartment for large items, with a small zipper pouch sewn in as an extra flap (a little pointless in my opinion, but still could be useful); two decent sized pockets on the front of the bag and two smaller compartments on the sides, all for convenient storage for \\"ready-at-hand\\" items; and, of course, the large flap that covers the large compartment and two front pockets.    Like I said, the only downside to be considered with this bag are the velcro strips, but I have no intention of using them.  That is only personal opinion, of course.  However, I find that this bag is perfect for any university student that is constantly moving from area to area of campus, especially since the bag is very lightweight for less burden while walking longer distances.  It was a fantastic buy and I recommend it to anyone looking to pick up a messenger bag.

product_title: iLuv Mini Portable Speaker for iPod and MP3 Players
review_body: The first thing anyone has to realize when buying itty-bitty, portable speakers for under $20 is that they aren't going to blow you away or replace a high-end, high-powered home system.  They probably won't satisfy any audiophiles or stereo snobs.      BUT, all things considered, they do a pretty darn good job of covering a wide range of sound, travel very easily, and the batteries seem to last quite a while.  It's a near-perfect solution to anyone who can't wear headphones (or doesn't want to) for whatever reason, and moves about from place to place (kitchen, garage, den, etc.).  I was happy enough to order a second set in case the spouse/kids are using the first set I bought.    Recommended!

product_title: Sennheiser Sports Earbud Headphones
review_headline: FINALLY - The perfect headphones for running!!!
review_body: I have had the PMX 80's for a while and really like them, with one exception.  The cord was way too long.  I run with a small mp3 player (no ipods!) strapped to my upper arm.  99.9% of all headphones have cords that are so long that you have to get creative to manage the cords.  I had always thought why some compmnay didn't realize this and make a headphone with a short cord.    Well, some actually did, but the headphones themselves sucked.    Then a few weeks ago my Mp3 player and my PMX 80's were stolen.  So I am back in the market.    I bought a Sandisk Clip+ and then found these.  Just like the pmx80's, but with a shorter cord.  Awesome.  Got them yesterday and went for a run this morning.  Absolutely perfect.  Comfy, sound great, cord is the perfect length.    I doubt I will ever use the extension cord with volume control, but it seems really solid.  It is lightweight and it too has a clip on it to attach to a waisteband.      In summary, if you are a runner and wear your headphones on your arm, these things are perfect.  Their marketing department sort of blows because it isn't obvious in the ad here on Amazon that the cord is short with an included extension cord to make it longer.  If I hadn't read the reviews, I would have passed these up.    Well worth what I paid for them (over $50).  I had thee pmx60's for 3 years and they still sounded great before they were stolen. I expect these to be just as durable.      Finally, these are a ta bit more comfortable then the pmx60's as well.  Just by a bit. They seem softer.

product_title: Yamaha YST-FSW050BL Advanced YST II Down-Firing Active Subwoofer (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: I was initially skeptical that a sub this small could produce the chest-thumping bass I craved with movies. But the Yamaha fit into the space where I had room, and I went for it.     Setup was a piece of cake. For some reason my Yamaha A/V reciever didn't have a place to hook the system connector (or at least I couldn't find it). I was disappointed. But as far as I know all that connection does is turn the subwoofer power on and off automatically with the receiver. I accomplished the same thing by plugging the subwoofer's power cord into the switched outlet on the back of my receiver.    For most of my listening to TV and movies, the subwoofer doesn't kick in because it doesn't need to. But when I put the Master and Commander DVD in my Blu-Ray player and cranked up the volume to a low-moderate level, my wife reported she felt the floor shaking at the opposite end of the house. There was absolutely no question that I had some new sounds.     My only wish is that this had a setting to adjust the low-pass filter so I could fine tune it with my main speakers. But I'm not at all sure I could improve the sound by doing that. It seems to work seamlessly.     In short, if space and budget are tight and you have only a modest listening area, this Yamaha does the job and does it without any drama.  (Drama supplied by your movies and music.)

product_title: Tenergy AAA Ready to Use NiMH Rechargeable Batteries (4 Pack)
review_body: I bought a large number of these in AA and AAA, and they have been very disappointing, even at their \\"bargain\\" price point.  Their self-discharge rate is much higher than any standard NiMH battery, and they arrived with little or no charge on them---so it is not appropriate to call them \\"pre-charged\\" or low-self-discharge.  They are also very inconsistent from one battery to another in their ability to hold a charge, which is an indication of their poor quality control.  Capacity is also grossly overstated; the AAAs only hold about 500 mAh, and the AAs only about 1200 mAh (but with a lot of variability there, too.)    I own many different brands of NiMH batteries, and all the others are much better than these.  Many of the others cost me significantly less, too.  Rayovac standard NiMHs now have very low self discharge, and sell for about $6 per 4-pack in most stores---way better value, and much better batteries!

product_title: Logitech Harmony 880 Advanced Universal Remote Control (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
I am a new ATT Uverse customer after years with Charter. I have long used Logitech Harmony 659 and 520 remotes with Charter equipment with total satisfaction. Much to my dismay, these two remotes work less well with ATT Uverse's Cisco set-top boxes. Specifically, trying to enter channels directly is an exercise in frustration (skipped numbers are very common) and often presses of command keys go ignored. This is with both 659 and 520 remotes.

On a whim, I picked up an 880 and I find that the ATT UVerse Cisco booxes respond crisply and reliably to the 880. Don't know why the 880 should work better than 659 and 520, but it does.

As to the remote itself, the hard buttons are very nice. The lay-out is OK, but some buttons are a bit crowded. Volume and channel control could be better shaped. The back-lighting on the keys is less than adequate in a dark room. The color LCD screen is nice, but really no better than the monochrome screens of earlier models in function. The rechargability is very nice, but you get to buy a $12 battery when it dies.

The shape is just like the classic 659 and it fits nicely in the hand.

Like all harmony remotes, the programming is the best there is of any remote.

Excellent remote, overall, downgraded from 5 stars because of poor back-lighting and some crowded buttons.
